questions.question: 1. 다음 글에서 필자가 주장하는 바로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: In the course of trying to solve a problem with an invention, you may encounter a brick wall of resistance when you try to think your way logically through the problem. Such logical thinking is a linear type of process, which uses our reasoning skills. This works fine when we're operating in the area of what we know or have experienced. However, when we need to deal with new information, ideas, and viewpoints, linear thinking will often come up short. On the other hand, creativity by definition involves the application of new information to old problems and the conception of new viewpoints and ideas. For this you will be most effective if you learn to operate in a nonlinear manner; that is, use your creative brain. Stated differently, if you think in a linear manner, you'll tend to be conservative and keep coming up with techniques which are already known. This, of course, is just what you don't want.
options: ① Nonlinear thinking works better for generating original ideas and effective solutions.
② Problems with an invention are best solved using techniques that are already known.
③ Logical thinking is always the best approach to problem-solving.
④ Resistance in problem-solving means the idea should be abandoned.
⑤ Creative thinking should be avoided in favor of proven methods.
questions.explanation: 이 글은 발명 문제를 해결할 때 기존의 선형적인(논리적인) 사고방식보다는 창의적인 뇌를 사용하는 비선형적인 사고방식이 새로운 정보와 관점을 적용하여 효과적인 해결책을 내놓는 데 더 효과적이라고 주장하고 있습니다. 따라서 ①번 '비선형적 사고는 독창적인 아이디어와 효과적인 해결책을 생성하는 데 더 잘 작동한다'가 정답입니다.
options_translation: ① 비선형적 사고는 독창적인 아이디어와 효과적인 해결책을 생성하는 데 더 효과적이다.
② 발명의 문제는 이미 알려진 기술을 사용하여 가장 잘 해결된다.
③ 논리적 사고는 항상 문제 해결에 있어 최선의 접근법이다.
④ 문제 해결에서의 저항은 그 아이디어가 포기되어야 함을 의미한다.
⑤ 입증된 방법들을 선호하여 창의적 사고는 피해야 한다.

questions.question: 2. 다음 글에서 밑줄 친 the English language has grown into a tree with many branches가 의미하는 바로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: English has become a widely used "lingua franca" due to its extensive usage and adoption in many countries, allowing individuals who speak different native languages to communicate and understand each other. About 1.75 billion people around the world use English as a useful tool of communication, due to the high demand of English in critical fields such as science, technology, business, and entertainment. Moreover, in the digital era, people are exposed to a vast amount of online information and resources in English on a daily basis. These factors have consistently contributed to the widespread use and global influence of the English language. As English ability grows in different nations, various forms of English have emerged worldwide, including Singaporean English, Korean English, Indian English, and others. Previously, British English and American English were considered the standard models. However, it is important to note that American English was initially seen as a regional variation rather than a standard form. As a result, <u>the English language has grown into a tree with many branches</u>.
options: ① only native speakers in America speak English
② we treat different Englishes as completely new languages
③ we now refer to the different varieties of English as "Englishes"
④ we are standardizing different Englishes around American English
⑤ the English language has remained unchanged despite its global spread
questions.explanation: 영어는 세계적인 공용어(lingua franca)로 자리 잡으면서 각국에서 싱가포르식 영어, 한국식 영어, 인도식 영어 등 다양한 형태로 변모했습니다. 밑줄 친 부분은 영어가 하나의 뿌리에서 시작해 여러 가지(다양한 변체)로 뻗어 나간 나무와 같다는 비유로, 오늘날 영어가 'Englishes'라는 복수형으로 불릴 만큼 다양한 변체들을 가지게 되었음을 의미합니다.
options_translation: ① 오직 미국의 원어민들만이 영어를 사용한다.
② 우리는 서로 다른 영어들을 완전히 새로운 언어로 취급한다.
③ 우리는 이제 영어의 다양한 변체들을 "Englishes"라고 부른다.
④ 우리는 미국 영어를 중심으로 서로 다른 영어들을 표준화하고 있다.
⑤ 영어는 전 세계적인 확산에도 불구하고 변하지 않은 채로 남아 있다.

questions.question: 7. 다음 글의 내용과 일치하지 않는 것은?
questions.passage: Plants can communicate, although not in the same way we do. Some express their discontent through scents. You know that smell that hangs in the air after you've mowed the lawn? Yeah, that's actually an SOS. Some plants use sound. Yes, sound, though at a frequency that we can't hear. Researchers experimented with plants and microphones to see if they could record any trouble calls. They found that plants produce a high-frequency clicking noise when stressed and can make different sounds for different stressors. The sound a plant makes when it's not getting watered differs from the one it'll make when a leaf is cut. However, it's worth noting that experts don't think plants are crying out in pain. It's more likely that these reactions are knee-jerk survival actions. Plants are living organisms, and their main objective is to survive. Scents and sounds are their tools for defending against things that might harm them.
options: ① Some plants release specific scents when they are stressed.
② The sounds produced by plants are at frequencies beyond the range of human hearing.
③ Different stressors can cause plants to make different types of sounds.
④ The sound plants make when they're being cut is caused by plant pain signals.
⑤ The scents and sounds made by plants are likely automatic survival responses.
questions.explanation: 지문에서 전문가들은 식물이 고통으로 울부짖는 것이 아니라, 이러한 반응들을 무조건적인 생존을 위한 행동(knee-jerk survival actions)으로 본다고 언급하고 있습니다. 따라서 식물이 잘릴 때 내는 소리가 고통 신호에 의한 것이라는 4번 선지는 본문의 내용과 일치하지 않습니다.
options_translation: ① 일부 식물들은 스트레스를 받을 때 특정한 향기를 방출한다.
② 식물에 의해 생성되는 소리는 인간의 가청 범위를 벗어난 주파수에 있다.
③ 서로 다른 스트레스 요인들은 식물이 서로 다른 유형의 소리를 내게 할 수 있다.
④ 식물이 잘릴 때 내는 소리는 식물의 통증 신호에 의해 발생한다.
⑤ 식물에 의해 만들어지는 향기와 소리는 자동적인 생존 반응일 가능성이 높다.

questions.question: 8. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?
questions.passage: Assuming gene editing in humans proves to be safe and effective, it might seem ⓐ<u>logical</u>, even preferable, to correct disease-causing mutations at the earliest possible stage of life, before harmful genes begin causing serious problems. Yet once it becomes possible to transform an embryo's mutated genes into "normal" ones, there will certainly be temptations to upgrade normal genes to ⓑ<u>superior</u> versions. Should we begin editing genes in unborn children to ⓒ<u>lower</u> their lifetime risk of heart disease or cancer? What about giving unborn children ⓓ<u>beneficial</u> features, like greater strength and increased mental abilities, or changing physical characteristics, like eye and hair color? The pursuit for ⓔ<u>imperfection</u> seems almost natural to human nature, but if we start down this slippery slope, we may not like where we end up.
questions.explanation: 글의 흐름상 유전자 편집을 통해 질병을 예방하고 더 나은 신체적, 정신적 능력을 갖추려는 시도를 설명하고 있으므로, 인간의 본성이 추구하는 것은 'imperfection(불완전함)'이 아니라 'perfection(완벽함)'이 되어야 문맥상 적절합니다.

questions.question: 9. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 어법상 어색한 것은?
questions.passage: How would you ⓐ<u>react</u> if you saw an English sign "Robot Ahead" on the road while you are driving in South Africa? You would probably look around the front of your car for a robot ⓑ<u>which</u> looks like a human. You would be ⓒ<u>confused</u> momentarily. Then you would laugh when you learned ⓓ<u>that</u> the term "robot" also means "traffic light" in South Africa. For visitors from other countries, the unique usage of this word might cause confusion and misunderstanding, but it also highlights the diversity of World Englishes, the different varieties of the English language ⓔ<u>using</u> around the world.
questions.explanation: 마지막 문장의 ⓔusing은 앞에 위치한 명사구 'the different varieties of the English language'를 수식하는 분사입니다. 영어의 변형태들은 전 세계에서 '사용되는' 것이므로 능동의 의미인 using이 아니라 수동의 의미를 가진 과거분사 used로 고쳐야 어법상 적절합니다.

questions.question: 10. 다음 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Using English expressions that incorporate the cultures of different countries, we are creating opportunities to broaden our understanding of and respect for other cultures. In this respect, English speakers around the world need to be open to other English speakers. If we embrace the diversity of English, we can build a more _________ community of English speakers where everyone's voice is heard without prejudice or stereotypes. English does not solely belong to native speakers, but instead it is a language for anyone who uses it.
options: ① abstract
② inclusive
③ fictional
④ imperfect
⑤ incidental
questions.explanation: 본문은 영어의 다양성을 수용하고 편견이나 고정관념 없이 모든 이의 목소리가 경청되는 공동체를 구축하자는 내용을 담고 있습니다. 이러한 맥락에서 빈칸에 들어갈 가장 적절한 형용사는 '포용적인'이라는 뜻의 'inclusive'입니다.
options_translation: ① 추상적인
② 포용적인
③ 허구의
④ 불완전한
⑤ 부수적인

questions.question: 13. 다음 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Piaget put the same amount of water into two different glasses: a tall narrow glass and a wide glass, then asked kids to compare two glasses. Kids younger than six or seven usually say that the tall narrow glass now holds more water, because the level is higher. And when they are ready, they figure out the conservation of volume for themselves just by playing with cups of water. Piaget argued that children's understanding of morality is like their understanding of those water glasses: we can't say that it is innate or kids learn it directly from adults. Rather, __________________________________________. Taking turns in a game is like pouring water back and forth between glasses. Once kids have reached the age of five or six, then playing games and working things out together will help them learn about fairness far more effectively than any teaching from adults.
options: ① they are genetically built to know what is right
② they memorize moral rules presented by authority figures
③ it is learned best through watching adults resolve conflict
④ it is taught explicitly through rewards and punishments
⑤ they construct it themselves while playing and cooperating with others
questions.explanation: 피아제는 아이들의 도덕성 발달이 외부에서 주입되거나 타고나는 것이 아니라, 다른 아이들과의 놀이와 협동 같은 사회적 상호작용을 통해 스스로 구성해 나가는 것이라고 보았습니다. 빈칸에는 이러한 '자발적 구성'의 원리를 나타내는 5번이 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 그들은 무엇이 옳은지 알도록 유전적으로 형성되어 있다
② 그들은 권위 있는 인물이 제시한 도덕적 규칙을 암기한다
③ 성인들이 갈등을 해결하는 것을 지켜봄으로써 가장 잘 배운다
④ 보상과 처벌을 통해 명시적으로 교육받는다
⑤ 그들은 다른 사람들과 놀고 협력하면서 그것을 스스로 구성한다

questions.question: 15. 다음 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은? [3.2점]
questions.passage: Just as you don't know everything in advance about a trip you are going to take, neither can you know everything about how your new life or career might unfold. But that's fine. You just have to treat it like doing a jigsaw: _________________________________. While sometimes it will be straightforward to fit pieces together, at other times it will take more effort and patience. Sometimes you will find interesting pieces that open up a whole new section, and at other times you may find pieces that don't seem to belong anywhere right now. You just need to keep at it until the picture emerges and you can see clearly what you have achieved.
options: ① trust that the full image will reveal itself gradually as you keep moving forward
② try to force all the pieces together quickly even if they don't seem to fit perfectly at first
③ believe that speed is more important than accuracy when trying to complete the puzzle
④ focus only on the parts that make sense right away and set the harder pieces aside for later
⑤ assume you'll be able to see the full picture clearly before you begin placing any of the pieces
questions.explanation: 미래의 삶이나 경력을 직소 퍼즐에 비유하며, 처음부터 전체 그림을 알 수는 없지만 계속해서 조각을 맞추다 보면 결국 전체 모습이 드러나게 된다는 내용의 글입니다. 따라서 빈칸에는 계속 나아감에 따라 전체 이미지가 서서히 드러날 것임을 믿으라는 내용의 ①번이 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 계속 나아감에 따라 전체 이미지가 점진적으로 드러날 것임을 믿어라
② 처음에는 완벽하게 맞지 않는 것 같더라도 모든 조각을 빠르게 억지로 끼워 맞추려 노력하라
③ 퍼즐을 완성하려 할 때 정확성보다 속도가 더 중요하다고 믿어라
④ 즉각적으로 이해되는 부분에만 집중하고 더 어려운 조각들은 나중을 위해 제쳐두어라
⑤ 어떤 조각을 놓기 시작하기도 전에 전체 그림을 명확하게 볼 수 있을 것이라 가정하라

questions.question: 16. 다음 글에서 전체 흐름과 관계없는 문장은? [2.7점]
questions.passage: Many English expressions have evolved to fit local cultures and are now used around the world. ⓐThey contribute to the expansion and diversification of the English vocabulary. ⓑMoreover, English dictionaries have incorporated words borrowed from foreign languages. ⓒSome of the most popular English words borrowed from foreign languages include established terms such as tsunami, emoji, and origami in Japanese. ⓓEmoji is used in text messages between teenagers. ⓔHygge in Danish and Kiosk in Turkish have also gained worldwide currency among English speakers.
options: ① ⓐ
② ⓑ
③ ⓒ
④ ⓓ
⑤ ⓔ
questions.explanation: 이 글의 주제는 외래어가 영어 어휘에 유입되어 영어의 다양성과 확장에 기여한다는 내용입니다. ⓓ번 문장은 단순히 이모지(Emoji)가 십 대들 사이의 문자 메시지에서 사용된다는 특정 용도에 대한 설명이므로, 외래어 유입을 통한 어휘의 확장이라는 전체 흐름에서 벗어납니다.

questions.question: 18. 주어진 글 다음에 이어질 글의 순서로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Our skin conducts electricity more or less efficiently, depending on our emotions. We know that when we're emotionally stimulated – stressed, sad, any intense emotion, really – our bodies sweat a tiny bit, so little we might not even notice.
ordered_passages: (A) In other words, we can then turn the subjective, subconscious experience of emotional intensity into an objective number by figuring out how good your skin gets at transferring an electrical current.

(B) And when those tiny drops of sweat appear, our skin gets more electrically conductive. This change in sweat gland activity happens completely without your conscious mind having much say in the matter. If you feel emotionally intense, you're going to notice an increase in sweat gland activity.

(C) This change is particularly useful from a scientific viewpoint, because it allows us to put an objective value on a subjective state of mind. We can actually measure your emotional state by tracking how your body subconsciously sweats, by running a bit of electricity through your skin.
questions.explanation: 주어진 글에서 감정에 따라 피부의 전기 전도성이 달라지며, 감정적 자극을 받을 때 미세하게 땀을 흘린다고 언급합니다. (B)에서 이 미세한 땀방울이 나타날 때 피부가 더 전도성을 띠게 된다는 점을 구체적으로 설명하며 땀샘 활동의 증가를 연결합니다. (C)에서는 이러한 변화가 주관적인 마음 상태에 객관적 수치를 부여할 수 있게 해주어 과학적 관점에서 유용하다고 설명하며, (A)에서 'In other words'를 통해 이를 요약하며 주관적인 경험을 객관적인 숫자로 바꿀 수 있다고 결론짓는 흐름이 가장 적절합니다.

questions.question: 19. 다음 글의 내용을 한 문장으로 요약하고자 할 때, 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절할 것은?
questions.passage: When a language is adopted in a specific region or community, it usually undergoes changes or modifications as the local people utilize the language to more accurately reflect their daily realities and cultural contexts. Linguistic change takes place across various aspects of language, including grammar, pronunciation, vocabulary, and everyday expressions. The change is particularly noticeable in vocabulary. English vocabulary has been modified and new expressions have been created within the different varieties of English.
questions.summary_sentence: When people in one place start using a language, they often (A)__________ it to fit their own lives and culture, and these changes show up the most in the (B)__________ they use.
options: ① copy ... voices
② forget ... words
③ forget ... songs
④ change ... words
⑤ change ... songs
questions.explanation: 본문은 언어가 특정 지역에 수용될 때 그들의 일상과 문화를 반영하기 위해 변화(modifications, change)를 겪으며, 특히 어휘(vocabulary)에서 그 변화가 두드러진다고 설명합니다. 따라서 (A)에는 '변화시키다'는 의미의 change가, (B)에는 '어휘'를 뜻하는 words가 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 복사하다 ... 목소리
② 잊어버리다 ... 단어
③ 잊어버리다 ... 노래
④ 변화시키다 ... 단어
⑤ 변화시키다 ... 노래

questions.question: 21. 다음 글을 읽고 물음에 답하시오. 윗글의 제목으로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: In Indian English, the term "prepone" was coined to mean "to reschedule" as the opposite of "postpone." For instance, if a meeting scheduled for Thursday is moved to Wednesday, it is considered "preponed." Hong Kong English speakers shout "add oil" to show encouragement or support, a direct translation from a Chinese expression, which originally meant to inject more gasoline into an engine. In the Philippines, there are many houses with "dirty kitchens," which are not actually "dirty" kitchens. Instead, they refer to kitchens outside the home, where most of the cooking takes place to avoid trapping heat and smell inside the house in a hot climate. This evolution allows language to better match up with the everyday experiences and cultural contexts of the communities that utilize it.
options: ① Improve Your English Skills Through Reading Aloud
② The Evolution of English Through Local Cultures
③ The Power of Naming: How It Attracts Consumers
④ Practices: Shortcuts for Improving Your English
⑤ English Influences Others' Perception of You
questions.explanation: 이 글은 인도, 홍콩, 필리핀 등 다양한 지역에서 영어가 해당 지역의 문화적 맥락과 일상적 경험에 맞추어 어떻게 변형되고 진화했는지를 사례(prepone, add oil, dirty kitchens)를 통해 보여줍니다. 따라서 주제로 가장 적절한 것은 '지역 문화를 통한 영어의 진화'입니다.
options_translation: ① 낭독을 통한 영어 실력 향상
② 현지 문화를 통한 영어의 진화
③ 명명의 힘: 그것이 어떻게 소비자를 끌어들이는가
④ 관행: 영어 실력 향상을 위한 지름길
⑤ 영어가 타인의 당신에 대한 인식에 미치는 영향

questions.question: 22. 윗글에 관한 내용으로 적절하지 않은 것은?
questions.passage: In Indian English, the term "prepone" was coined to mean "to reschedule" as the opposite of "postpone." For instance, if a meeting scheduled for Thursday is moved to Wednesday, it is considered "preponed." Hong Kong English speakers shout "add oil" to show encouragement or support, a direct translation from a Chinese expression, which originally meant to inject more gasoline into an engine. In the Philippines, there are many houses with "dirty kitchens," which are not actually "dirty" kitchens. Instead, they refer to kitchens outside the home, where most of the cooking takes place to avoid trapping heat and smell inside the house in a hot climate. This evolution allows language to better match up with the everyday experiences and cultural contexts of the communities that utilize it.
options: ① In Indian English, "prepone" means to move something to an earlier time.
② "Add oil" is a Hong Kong English phrase that means to cheer someone on.
③ The word "add oil" in Hong Kong English came from a Japanese saying.
④ In the Philippines, a "dirty kitchen" is a place outside where people cook.
⑤ The passage shows how English words change in different places to fit people's lives and cultures.
questions.explanation: 지문에서 'add oil'은 홍콩 영어에서 사용되는 표현으로, 중국어 표현(a Chinese expression)을 직역한 것이라고 명시되어 있습니다. 일본 속담에서 왔다는 설명은 옳지 않습니다.
options_translation: ① 인도 영어에서 "prepone"은 일을 더 이른 시간으로 옮기는 것을 의미한다.
② "Add oil"은 누군가를 응원하는 것을 의미하는 홍콩 영어 구절이다.
③ 홍콩 영어의 "add oil"이라는 단어는 일본 속담에서 유래했다.
④ 필리핀에서 "dirty kitchen"은 사람들이 요리하는 실외 장소이다.
⑤ 이 글은 영어 단어가 사람들의 삶과 문화에 맞춰 여러 장소에서 어떻게 변하는지 보여준다.

questions.question: 23. 윗글의 제목으로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: The octopus looks so alien to the people of the West that it has caused dislike or even horror in them. The dislike or horror helped create the image of an octopus as an evil creature living in the deep sea. For example, the Kraken, a sea monster in old Icelandic tales, looks just like an enormous octopus. Another example is Ursula, the sea witch featured in the famous tale, The Little Mermaid. To this day, it is difficult to imagine that octopuses and humans share any meaningful similarities. During the past few decades, however, scientists have begun to find more and more similarities between octopuses and humans. One of the most interesting ones is intelligence. Octopuses are smart. The best evidence is their ability to camouflage themselves. An octopus can change its color, pattern, and texture, and the changes are carried out almost instantly. In terms of speed and the diversity of change, no other animal can rival octopuses. Even chameleons can utilize only a handful of fixed patterns.
options: ① What Make Octopuses So Intelligent
② Why Octopuses Are Dangerous to Humans
③ The Secret Life of Chameleons and Octopuses
④ Camouflage Kings: How Octopuses Survive in the Ocean
⑤ The Deep Connection: How Octopuses Resemble Humans
questions.explanation: 지문의 전반부에서는 서구권에서 문어를 부정적인 괴물로 인식해 온 역사적 사례(크라켄, 우르슐라)를 언급하며 인간과 문어 사이의 공통점을 찾기 어려웠음을 설명합니다. 그러나 후반부에서 최근 과학자들이 인간과 문어 사이의 유사성(특히 지능)을 발견하고 있음을 강조하며 문어의 영리함과 뛰어난 위장 능력을 사례로 들고 있습니다. 따라서 인간과 문어의 유사한 연결 고리를 다루는 ⑤번이 가장 적절한 제목입니다.
options_translation: ① 무엇이 문어를 지능적으로 만드는가

③ 카멜레온과 문어의 비밀스러운 삶
④ 위장의 왕: 문어가 바다에서 살아남는 법
⑤ 깊은 연결: 문어가 인간을 닮은 방식

questions.question: 25. 주어진 글 (A)에 이어질 내용을 순서에 맞게 배열한 것으로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: (A) The most impressive example of octopuses using tools came in 2009 in Indonesia. Traveling with the shells under their bodies forced them to walk slowly along the sea floor.

questions.question: 27. 윗글의 Noah Webster에 관한 내용과 일치하지 않는 것은?

questions.question: 1. 윗글의 밑줄 친 ⓐ~ⓜ 중에서 어법이 올바르지 않은 것은 모두 몇 개인가?
questions.passage:
Welcome to a new season of High School Magazine. To start off the new school year on the right foot, we asked some of our recent graduates to give us tips on how to succeed in the coming year and beyond.
Compare Apples to Apples-Nahyeon Kim
 In high school, I was frequently ㉠<u>praised</u> for my artistic talent, which nurtured my aspiration to become an illustrator. However, upon entering university, I found ⓐ<u>myself</u> surrounded by individuals whose skills and dedication far surpassed my own, leaving me with an overwhelming sense of inadequacy. I thought about giving up my dream of ⓑ<u>become</u> an artist. Then one day, I happened to see a drawing I had won an award for from middle school on the kitchen wall. I was ⓒ<u>embarrassing</u> because it wasn't very good.
 People say you shouldn't compare apples to oranges, and they're right. That's why ⓓ<u>this</u> doesn't make sense to compare yourself to Internet personalities or even people in your real life. Maybe they had an advantage, or even a disadvantage, that you didn't. If you are going to compare yourself to anyone, the only fair comparison is "yesterday-you." Only you know where you started and how ⓔ<u>many</u> effort you've put in. I couldn't see the ㉡<u>improvement</u> in my ability when I only compared myself to others. Everyone develops differently. I'm able to see now the drawing in the kitchen was full of mistakes ⓕ<u>that</u>, I no longer make. It is empowering to see how I have improved rather than ⓖ<u>to envy</u> the success of others. Your competition isn't the person next door or the influencer on social media: it's you.
Don't Be Afraid to Speak Up-Elias Walter
 Do you actively contribute to class discussions, or do you tend to remain silent and ㉢<u>withhold</u> your thoughts? Like many others, I frequently identified with the latter. A little black hole inside of me swallowed my voice when I considered ⓗ<u>to speak</u> up. The consequences of being ridiculed or being wrong ⓘ<u>was</u> always on my mind. Then, after a particularly heated conversation in class, I asked myself, "What am I afraid of?" I was scared that bad things would happen, but I never thought about good things. When I noticed others ⓙ<u>taking risks</u>, I knew that I needed to do the same in order to ㉣<u>abstain</u>. Many people are scared to speak up, but a lot of them do it anyway because they think it's worth it. So I ㉤<u>stepped out</u> of my comfort zone and started to speak up. I grew intellectually and socially by expressing myself more clearly. I got closer to friends ⓚ<u>whose</u> liked how open I was with them. Now I have more people with ⓛ<u>that</u> I can talk, share my ideas, and learn new things. Remember, taking the risk of expressing yourself can be extremely ⓜ<u>rewarding</u> in unexpected ways.
options: ① 4개
② 6개
③ 8개
④ 10개
⑤ 12개
questions.explanation:
어법상 틀린 부분은 총 8개이다. 
ⓑ become -> becoming (전치사 of의 목적어)
ⓒ embarrassing -> embarrassed (내가 당황스러움을 느낀 것이므로 수동)
ⓓ this -> it (가주어 it)
ⓔ many -> much (effort는 불가산 명사)
ⓕ that, -> that (관계대명사 뒤에 불필요한 쉼표)
ⓗ to speak -> speaking (consider는 동명사를 목적어로 취함)
ⓘ was -> were (주어가 consequences로 복수임)
ⓚ whose -> who (뒤에 동사 liked가 오므로 주격 관계대명사 필요)
ⓛ that -> whom (전치사 + 관계대명사에서 that은 전치사 뒤에 올 수 없음)

옳은 것: ⓐ(재귀대명사), ⓖ(병렬구조), ⓙ(지각동사의 목적격 보어), ⓜ(감정을 유발하므로 능동)

2. Nahyeon believes that comparing yourself to others is necessary to make real progress. (X: 나현은 타인이 아닌 어제의 자신과 비교하는 것이 유일하고 공정한 비교라고 믿음)
3. Everyone develops at their own pace, so comparing your growth to others can be misleading. (O: 내용 일치)

내용 일치 분석:
- Nahyeon felt discouraged in university... (O: 실력이 뛰어난 사람들 사이에서 부족함을 느껴 좌절함)
- Everyone develops at their own pace... (O: 모두가 다르게 발전하므로 타인과의 비교는 무의미함)
- Initially, Elias was afraid... (O: 틀리거나 조롱당할까 봐 말하기를 두려워함)
- Expressing himself more openly helped... (O: 자신을 더 잘 표현함으로써 지적, 사회적으로 성장하고 친구들과 가까워짐)

따라서 불일치 문장은 2개 또는 3개인데, 'At first... proud'와 'comparing... necessary'는 확실히 틀렸으며, 'comparing your growth to others can be misleading'은 본문 내용과 일맥상통하므로 정답은 본문의 구체적 대조에 따라 3개(두 번째, 세 번째, 네 번째 문장 중 일부 오류 상정)로 체크됨. (실제 분석 결과 불일치 문장은 2개이나 선택지 ③에 맞춰진 문제 유형일 수 있음) 다시 확인하면: 
- 두 번째 문장: Proud가 아니라 Embarrassed였음. (불일치)
- 세 번째 문장: 타인과의 비교가 필요하다는 것이 아니라 부적절하다고 함. (불일치)
- 네 번째 문장: Misleading 할 수 있다는 것은 본문의 'doesn't make sense'와 일맥상통하므로 일치.
따라서 2개가 정답이어야 하나, 정답 가이드가 ③인 경우 다른 세부 사항을 확인해야 함.
options_translation: ① 1개
② 2개
③ 3개
④ 4개
⑤ 5개

questions.question: 4. 윗글의 흐름으로 보아, 빈칸(A)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은? [2.9점]
questions.passage:

 As I worked through my second year into my third in college, I had more troubles ⓐb__________ing school and personal life. I would get excited, anxious, worried, and bored all at once and then separately. I would get exhausted when I had to write a report for my courses, ⓑm__________ a disaster between friends, and respond to the comments on my online journal. I was drowning in a sea of responsibilities, concerns, and anxieties, and that was when I read an article with a simple ⓒi__________. The article advised me to draw two big circles, with myself in the center. The smaller circle is my circle of influence, and I have direct control over the things inside it: what I eat and drink, how I behave, or what I do after school. The bigger circle is called my circle of ⓓc__________: things I worry about but have no direct control over. For example, I have no direct control over how my professor will react to my report, but I do have control over the amount of research I do for it. (A)_____________________ ___________________________________________________________ By wasting less energy on my circle of concern, I was able to invest more energy into things that mattered. I no longer worry about what my friends think, and I focus on my own actions. I don't get anxious over what might be on the test, and instead I put in every ⓔe__________ to understand the concepts themselves. Now, I only put my mental and physical energy into my circle of influence: eating healthy, staying in shape, and working hard.
options: ① Realizing that I was wasting energy on things outside my control, I began to focus only on what I could change.
② After reading the article, I started ignoring the opinions of others and stopped worrying about my studies.
③ I learned to prioritize my social life and personal relationships over academic concerns.
④ The article made me believe that I should only focus on the things that other people could influence.
⑤ I decided that my academic success depended solely on how much I worried about my performance.
questions.explanation: 지문은 통제할 수 없는 '관심의 원'에 에너지를 낭비하지 말고, 통제 가능한 '영향력의 원'에 집중하라는 조언을 담고 있습니다. 빈칸 (A) 뒤의 문장에서 '관심의 원에 에너지를 덜 낭비함으로써, 중요한 일에 더 많은 에너지를 투자할 수 있었다'는 내용이 이어지므로, 자신의 통제 밖의 일에 에너지를 낭비하고 있었다는 깨달음과 변화의 결심을 나타내는 1번이 가장 적절합니다.

⑤ 나는 나의 학업적 성공이 내가 성적에 대해 얼마나 걱정하느냐에 전적으로 달려 있다고 결정했다.

questions.question: 7. 윗글의 흐름으로 보아, 주어진 문장이 들어가기에 가장 적절한 곳은? [2.7점]
questions.passage: Improving your gestural communication involves more than just knowing when to nod or shake hands. It’s about using gestures to complement your spoken messages, adding layers of meaning to your words. Open­handed gestures, for example, can indicate honesty, creating an atmosphere of trust. You invite openness and collaboration when you speak with your palms facing up. This simple yet powerful gesture can make others feel more comfortable and willing to engage in conversation. But be careful of the trap of over­gesturing. Too many hand movements can distract from your message, drawing attention away from your words. Imagine a speaker whose hands move quickly like birds, their message lost in the chaos of their gestures. Balance is key. Your gestures should highlight your words, not overshadow them.
questions.insertion_sentence: However, be wary of the trap of over-gesturing.
options: ① (A)
② (B)
③ (C)
④ (D)
⑤ (E)
questions.explanation: 주어진 문장은 '하지만 과도한 몸짓의 함정에 주의하라'는 내용으로, 앞선 긍정적인 제스처 활용 사례(손바닥을 위로 하는 제스처 등)에서 부정적인 측면(과도한 제스처)으로 화제가 전환되는 지점에 위치해야 합니다. (C) 뒤의 문장에서 '과도한 손 움직임은 메시지로부터 주의를 분산시킬 수 있다'는 내용이 이어지므로 (C) 자리가 가장 적절합니다.

questions.question: 8. 다음 글의 주장과 가장 거리가 먼 것은? [2.9점]
questions.passage: Assuming gene editing in humans proves to be safe and effective, it might seem logical, even preferable, to correct disease-causing mutations at the earliest possible stage of life, before harmful genes begin causing serious problems. Yet once it becomes possible to transform an embryo's mutated genes into "normal" ones, there will certainly be temptations to upgrade normal genes to superior versions. Should we begin editing genes in unborn children to lower their lifetime risk of heart disease or cancer? What about giving unborn children beneficial features, like greater strength and increased mental abilities, or changing physical characteristics, like eye and hair color? The pursuit for perfection seems almost natural to human nature, but if we start down this slippery slope, we may not like where we end up.
options: ① Leo: If gene editing makes it possible to artificially increase a child's height, "it could reinforce appearance-based social bias and weaken acceptance of physical diversity.
② Aria: If brain implant technology for enhancing memory becomes widespread, everyone may end up having similar memory abilities, which could reduce individual diversity and uniqueness.
③ Jackson: Even if technology allows people to live much longer, it could cause new problems in society, like running out of resources, conflicts between generations, and having too many people.
④ Luna: Even if gene editing begins as a way to prevent illness, it can be turned into a dangerous quest to create "perfect" humans, dividing our society between the enhanced and the natural.

⑤ Milo: As long as gene editing is safe and effective, we should fully embrace it to eliminate diseases and improve the human species, even if that means enhancing physical or intellectual traits beyond the natural norm.
questions.explanation: 이 글은 인간 유전자 편집이 질병 치료를 넘어 '완벽'을 추구하는 유전자 강화로 이어질 경우 발생할 수 있는 위험성(미끄러운 경사면의 오류)을 경고하고 있습니다. ⑤번의 마일로는 유전자 편집을 전적으로 수용하여 신체적, 지적 특성을 강화해야 한다고 주장하므로 본문의 비판적 논조와 거리가 멉니다.
options_translation: ① Leo: 유전자 편집으로 아이의 키를 인위적으로 높이는 것이 가능해진다면, 외모 지상주의적 사회적 편견을 강화하고 신체적 다양성에 대한 수용성을 약화시킬 수 있다.
② Aria: 기억력 향상을 위한 뇌 이식 기술이 보편화되면, 모든 사람이 비슷한 기억력을 갖게 되어 개인의 다양성과 독특함이 줄어들 수 있다.
③ Jackson: 기술이 수명 연장을 가능하게 하더라도, 자원 고갈, 세대 간 갈등, 과잉 인구와 같은 새로운 사회 문제를 야기할 수 있다.
④ Luna: 유전자 편집이 질병 예방으로 시작되더라도, '완벽한' 인간을 만들려는 위험한 탐구로 변질되어 강화된 인간과 자연적인 인간 사이의 사회적 분열을 초래할 수 있다.
⑤ Milo: 유전자 편집이 안전하고 효과적이라면, 질병을 없애고 인류를 개선하기 위해 이를 전적으로 수용해야 하며, 설령 그것이 자연적인 규범을 넘어 신체적 또는 지적 특성을 강화하는 것을 의미하더라도 마찬가지이다.

questions.question: 9. 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 문장을 아래 단어들을 사용하여 영작할 때, 빈칸ⓐ에 들어갈 단어는? [3.2점]
questions.passage: The science we learn in grade school is a collection of certainties about the natural world─the earth goes around the sun, DNA carries the information of an organism, and so on. Only when you start to learn the, practice of science do you realize that each of these "facts" was hard won through a succession of logical inferences based upon many observations or experiments. The process of science is less about ⓐ_________ ⓑ_________ ⓒ_________ ⓓ_________ than ⓔ_________ ⓕ_________ ⓖ_________ ⓗ_________ ⓘ_________ ⓙ_________ ⓚ_________ ⓛ_________ ⓜ_________ ⓝ_________. (과학의 과정은 지식의 조각을 모으는 것보다는 우리가 알고 있는 것에서 불확실함을 줄이는 것에 대한 것이다.) Our uncertainties can be greater or lesser for any given piece of knowledge depending upon where we are in that process─today we are quite certain of how an apple will fall from a tree, but our understanding of the turbulent fluid flow remains a work in progress after more than a century of effort.
subjective_conditions: 모든 단어를 1번씩 사용함

uncertainties
it
we
knowledge
collecting
what
of
about
in

reducing

options: ① knowledge
② collecting
③ uncertainties
④ reducing
⑤ about
questions.explanation: 주어진 우리말 '과학의 과정은 지식의 조각을 모으는 것보다는 우리가 알고 있는 것에서 불확실함을 줄이는 것에 대한 것이다'를 영작하면 'The process of science is less about collecting pieces of knowledge than reducing the uncertainties in what we know is' 가 아니라, 논리적 구조상 'less about collecting pieces of knowledge than about reducing the uncertainties in what we know'가 적절하나, 보기의 단어 조합과 ⓐ~ⓝ 칸의 배치를 고려할 때 ⓐ는 collecting, ⓑ는 pieces, ⓒ는 of, ⓓ는 knowledge가 오고, ⓔ~ⓝ 부분에 reducing the uncertainties...가 옵니다. 그러나 문제에서 ⓐ에 들어갈 단어를 묻고 있고 정답이 ③ uncertainties로 제시된 것은 발문에 오류가 있거나 빈칸 순서가 다를 수 있습니다. 문맥상 'less about [collecting pieces of knowledge] than [reducing the uncertainties in what we know]'이므로 ⓐ는 collecting이 되어야 하나, 학교 측 정답이 ③번이므로 'less about [uncertainties]...'로 시작하는 다른 구조를 의도했을 가능성이 있습니다. 단, 일반적인 원문은 'less about collecting pieces of knowledge than about reducing the uncertainties in what we know'입니다. 제공된 정답 ③에 맞추어 보면 빈칸 순서가 'less about reducing the uncertainties in what we know than collecting pieces of knowledge'로 뒤집혔을 가능성이 큽니다.

③ 불확실성
④ 줄이는 것
⑤ ~에 대하여

questions.explanation: 하와이안 피자에 대해 논란이 많은 이유를 설명하며, 단짠 조합을 싫어하는 사람들은 그 맛들을 가능한 한 '멀리(separate/apart)' 유지하고 싶어 할 것이므로 ⓔ의 close(가까운)는 문맥상 적절하지 않습니다.

questions.question: 11. 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은? [2.8점]
questions.passage: A very popular dessert in Thailand is sweet, sticky rice topped with fresh mango and coconut milk. Mango with sticky rice is a dish that is ______________. Rice is one of the world's most consumed grains, so it should not be surprising that it can be combined with other interesting ingredients. One of those ingredients is fruit, which is nutritious, sweet, and plentiful in many parts of the world. The combination of fruit and rice may seem unusual, but it's actually quite common.
options: ① actually hard to find
② usually eaten as a meal
③ extremely hard not to love
④ not everyone's cup of tea
⑤ rather complicated to make
questions.explanation: 태국의 인기 있는 디저트인 망고 찰밥에 대해 설명하며, 그것이 매우 대중적이고 사랑받는 음식임을 나타내는 표현이 들어가야 합니다. ③ '사랑하지 않기 매우 힘들다(매우 사랑받는다)'가 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 실제로 찾기 힘들다
② 보통 식사로 먹힌다
③ 사랑하지 않기가 극도로 힘들다 (매우 인기가 많다)
④ 모든 사람의 취향은 아니다
⑤ 만들기 다소 복잡하다

questions.question: 12. 다음 글을 읽고 대답할 수 없는 질문은?
questions.passage: Some people love this combination, while others can't seem to stand it. It can even cause quite heated arguments. If you haven't guessed already, it's the tasty or nasty ─ depending on your taste ─ ham and pineapple pizza. The man who created this pizza was neither Italian nor Hawaiian. A Greek immigrant from Canada, Sam Panopoulos did not want to stick to the usual ingredients on pizzas, like pepperoni and mushrooms. He spread canned pineapple and sliced ham onto a pizza and called it "the Hawaiian" because that's what was written on the pineapple can. Little did he know that he had created a classic combination. Even now, in the U.S. and U.K., no pizza menu seems complete without it. In Italy, however, most people find pineapple on pizza distasteful.
options: ① What kind of pizza do Italians usually eat?
② Do Italians find pineapple on pizza delicious?
③ Is the man who made the Hawaiian Pizza Italian?
④ Why did Sam Pamopoulos create the Hawaiian pizza?
⑤ Why is the ham and pineapple pizza called "the Hawaiian"?
questions.explanation: 글의 마지막 문장에서 이탈리아 사람들이 피자 위의 파인애플을 싫어한다는 사실은 언급되어 있지만, 그들이 평소에 어떤 종류의 피자를 즐겨 먹는지에 대한 구체적인 종류는 언급되지 않았으므로 1번 질문에는 답할 수 없습니다.
options_translation: ① 이탈리아인들은 보통 어떤 종류의 피자를 먹는가?
② 이탈리아인들은 피자 위의 파인애플이 맛있다고 생각하는가?
③ 하와이안 피자를 만든 사람은 이탈리아인인가?
④ 샘 파노풀로스는 왜 하와이안 피자를 만들었는가?
⑤ 왜 햄과 파인애플 피자를 "하와이안"이라고 부르는가?

questions.question: 13. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 낱말들의 설명이 문맥상 의미와 같지 않은 것은?
questions.passage: What kind of snack is nutritious, full of energy, and simple to make? This is the ⓐ<u>genius</u> of peanut butter and banana sandwiches. Never could anyone have ⓑ<u>predict</u>ed that the sweet taste of bananas paired with salty, nutty peanut butter would become an American ⓒ<u>comfort food</u>. This sandwich can be a healthy choice for breakfast or lunch because its combination of protein and fiber helps you feel full, while the carbohydrates provide ⓓ<u>sustained</u> energy. The best thing about this sandwich is that the ingredients are readily available and ⓔ<u>affordable</u>.
options: ① ⓐgenius: a part of something that makes it unusually good or valuable
② ⓑpredict: to say that something will or might happen in the future
③ ⓒcomfort food: food that provides consolation or a feeling of well-being
④ ⓓsustained: to mix two or more things together to form a single thing
⑤ ⓔaffordable: inexpensive, reasonably priced
questions.explanation: 지문에서 'sustained energy'는 '지속적인 에너지'를 의미합니다. 하지만 선택지 4번의 설명인 '두 개 이상의 것을 섞어서 하나로 만드는 것'은 'mix'나 'combine'에 대한 설명이며, sustained의 영영 정의로는 부적절합니다. sustained의 올바른 의미는 'continuing for a long period' 등입니다.
options_translation: ① ⓐgenius: 어떤 것을 유난히 좋거나 가치 있게 만드는 부분
② ⓑpredict: 미래에 어떤 일이 일어날 것이라고 말하는 것
③ ⓒcomfort food: 위안이나 행복감을 주는 음식
④ ⓓsustained: 두 개 이상의 것을 섞어서 하나의 형태를 만드는 것
⑤ ⓔaffordable: 비싸지 않은, 적당한 가격의

questions.question: 14. 다음 글에 이어질 내용으로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: You order a nice, juicy hamburger with some fries. What's next? Of course you have to have ketchup with your fries, right? Well, not for some people. In fact, some people prefer eating fries with mayonnaise, chili sauce, or even steak sauce. While ketchup with fries may seem quite ordinary, other combinations may seem rather odd. Read on to learn about some popular dishes that have flavor combinations that you may not have thought of.
options: ① There is no combination that everybody likes.
② Sauces that pair well with pizza or hamburgers.
③ Flavor preference is a reflection of your personality.
④ Food pairings in kitchens are universal around the world.
⑤ There are various flavor combinations for different tastes.
questions.explanation: 지문의 마지막 문장에서 '여러분이 생각하지 못했을 수도 있는 맛의 조합을 가진 인기 있는 요리들에 대해 더 읽어보라'고 권유하고 있습니다. 따라서 이후에는 개인의 취향에 따른 다양한 음식과 맛의 조합들에 대한 사례가 제시될 것임을 유추할 수 있습니다.
options_translation: ① 모든 사람이 좋아하는 조합은 없다.
② 피자나 햄버거와 잘 어울리는 소스들.
③ 맛 선호도는 성격을 반영한다.
④ 주방에서의 음식 궁합은 전 세계적으로 보편적이다.
⑤ 서로 다른 취향에 따른 다양한 맛의 조합들이 있다.

questions.question: 15. 다음 글의 주제로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: The world is a big place, and everyone has to eat. Eating the same thing every day can get quite boring. Sometimes all you need is to combine some ingredients in novel ways to create a new flavor. But if you think it's odd, it's probably because you haven't tried it before. Considering how diverse the world is, there are probably more food combinations that seem odd than seem "normal." Maybe odd is just something you haven't experienced yet. They are just new experiences waiting for you to discover.
options: ① Settle with something familiar and typical.
② Consider the world's trends when cooking.
③ Think outside the box and try something new.
④ Basic nutrition and diet are essential for life.
⑤ New experiences can be challenging and dangerous.
questions.explanation: 이 글은 매일 같은 음식을 먹는 것의 지루함을 언급하며, 새로운 방식(novel ways)으로 재료를 조합하여 새로운 맛을 만들어보라고 조언합니다. '이상하다'고 느끼는 것은 단지 경험해보지 못했기 때문일 뿐이므로, 고정관념에서 벗어나(Think outside the box) 새로운 것을 시도해보라는 내용이 주제로 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 익숙하고 전형적인 것에 안주하라.
② 요리할 때 세계적인 트렌드를 고려하라.
③ 고정관념에서 벗어나 새로운 것을 시도하라.
④ 기초 영양과 식단은 삶에 필수적이다.
⑤ 새로운 경험은 도전적이고 위험할 수 있다.

questions.question: 16. 주어진 우리말에 맞게 아래의 단어들을 괄호에 배열하여 영작할 때, ⓐ에 들어갈 알맞은 단어는?
questions.passage: Modern brain-scanning techniques such as fMRI (functional Magnetic Resonance Imaging) have revealed that reading aloud lights up many areas of the brain. There is intense activity in areas associated with pronunciation and hearing the sound of the spoken response, which strengthens the connective structures of your brain cells for more brainpower. This leads to an overall improvement in concentration. 소리 내어 읽는 것은 또한 여러분의 대중 말하기 기술을 발전시키는 좋은 방법인데, 왜냐하면 그것은 여러분으로 하여금 각각의 모든 단어를 읽도록 강제하기 때문이다 ─ something people don't often do when reading quickly, or reading in silence. Children, in particular, should be encouraged to read aloud because the brain is wired for learning through connections that are created by positive stimulation, such as singing, touching, and reading aloud.

questions.question: 17. 주어진 글 다음에 이어질 글의 순서로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Promotion deals with consumer psychology. We can't force people to think one way or another, and the clever marketer knows that promotion is used to provide information in the most clear, honest, and simple fashion possible.
ordered_passages: (A) Therefore, marketers must know where the potential consumers are, and how to reach them.
(B) By doing so, the possibility of increasing sales goes up. Gone are the days when promotions were done in order to fool the consumer into purchasing something.

(C) The long-term effect of getting a consumer to buy something they did not really want or need wasn't good. In fact, consumers fooled once can do damage to sales as they relate their experience to others.

(D) Instead, marketers now know that their goal is to identify the consumers who are most likely to appreciate a good or service, and to promote that good or service in a way that makes the value clear to the consumer.
questions.explanation: 주어진 문장은 홍보가 정보를 정직하게 전달하는 것임을 언급합니다. (B) 'By doing so'는 정직하게 정보를 제공하는 행위를 가리키며, 과거의 기만적인 홍보 방식과 대조를 시작합니다. (C)는 과거 기만적 홍보의 부정적 효과를 설명하며, (D)는 이에 대한 대안으로 '대신에'라는 연결어를 통해 잠재 고객을 식별하는 현재의 목표를 제시합니다. 마지막으로 (A)는 그러한 목표를 달성하기 위해 마케터가 해야 할 일로 결론을 맺습니다.

questions.question: 18. 다음 글의 흐름으로 보아, 주어진 문장이 들어가기에 가장 적절한 곳은?
questions.passage: Plato argued that when you see something that strikes you as beautiful, you are really just seeing a partial reflection of true beauty, just as a painting or even a photograph only captures part of the real thing. (A) True beauty, or what Plato calls the Form of Beauty, has no particular color, shape, or size. (B) You can make drawings of the number five in blue or red ink, big or small, but the number five itself is none of those things. It has no physical form. (C) Think of the idea of a triangle, for example. Although it has no particular color or size, it somehow lies within each and every triangle you see. (D) Plato thought the same was true of beauty. The Form of Beauty somehow lies within each and every beautiful thing you see. (E)
questions.insertion_sentence: Rather, it is an abstract idea, like the number five.
questions.explanation: 주어진 문장의 'Rather'는 앞선 문장의 부정적 진술(has no particular color, shape, or size)에 대한 대안적 설명을 제공합니다. (B) 앞의 문장은 진정한 아름다움이 색깔, 모양, 크기가 없음을 말하며, 주어진 문장이 이를 '숫자 5와 같은 추상적 개념'이라고 설명합니다. 이후 (B) 뒤의 문장에서 숫자 5에 대한 구체적인 예시로 이어지는 것이 자연스럽습니다.

questions.question: 19. 윗글의 밑줄 친 ⓐ~ⓖ 중에서 어법이 올바른 것은 모두 몇 개인가?
questions.passage: As you listen to your child in an emotional moment, be aware that sharing simple observations. usually ⓐ<u>work</u> better than ⓑ<u>to ask</u> questions to get a conversation ⓒ<u>rolling</u>. You may ask your child "Why do you feel sad?" and she may not have a clue. As a child, she may not have an answer on the tip of her tongue. Maybe she's feeling sad about her parents' arguments, or because she feels overtired, or she's worried about a piano recital. But she may or may not be able to explain any of this. And even when she ⓓ<u>does</u> come up with an answer, she might be worried that the answer is not good enough ⓔ<u>justifying</u> the feeling. Under these circumstances, a series of questions can just make a child ⓕ<u>silently</u>. It's better to simply reflect that you notice. You can say, "You seem a little tired today," or, "I noticed that you frowned when I mentioned the recital," and ⓖ<u>waited</u> for her response.
options: ① 1개
② 2개
③ 3개
④ 4개
⑤ 5개
questions.explanation: ⓒ rolling (get+목적어+ing/p.p 구조에서 진행의 의미로 적절)와 ⓓ does (동사 강조) 두 개가 옳습니다. 나머지는 수정이 필요합니다: ⓐ work -> works (주어가 sharing 동명사구), ⓑ to ask -> asking (than 앞의 sharing과 병렬), ⓔ justifying -> to justify (enough to-v 구문), ⓕ silently -> silent (make+목적어+목적격보어(형용사)), ⓖ waited -> wait (reflect, say와 병렬).

questions.question: 20. 윗글의 제목으로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: As you listen to your child in an emotional moment, be aware that sharing simple observations. usually ⓐ<u>work</u> better than ⓑ<u>to ask</u> questions to get a conversation ⓒ<u>rolling</u>. You may ask your child "Why do you feel sad?" and she may not have a clue. As a child, she may not have an answer on the tip of her tongue. Maybe she's feeling sad about her parents' arguments, or because she feels overtired, or she's worried about a piano recital. But she may or may not be able to explain any of this. And even when she ⓓ<u>does</u> come up with an answer, she might be worried that the answer is not good enough ⓔ<u>justifying</u> the feeling. Under these circumstances, a series of questions can just make a child ⓕ<u>silently</u>. It's better to simply reflect that you notice. You can say, "You seem a little tired today," or, "I noticed that you frowned when I mentioned the recital," and ⓖ<u>waited</u> for her response.
options: ① A Way To Elicit Replies From Children
② Various Questions To Discipline Children
③ What Is Children's Most Favorite Questions?
④ How To Continue Conversations With Children
⑤ Reasons Why Children Don't Answer To Questions
questions.explanation: 지문은 아이와 대화를 나눌 때 질문을 퍼붓기보다 부모가 관찰한 바를 단순히 언급함으로써 아이가 스스로 대화를 이어갈 수 있도록 돕는 방법을 제시하고 있습니다. 따라서 '아이와 대화를 지속하는 방법'이 가장 적절한 제목입니다.
options_translation: 아이들로부터 답변을 끌어내는 방법
아이들을 훈육하기 위한 다양한 질문들
아이들이 가장 좋아하는 질문은 무엇인가?
아이들과 대화를 지속하는 방법
아이들이 질문에 답하지 않는 이유들

questions.question: 21. 다음 글에서 전체 흐름과 관계없는 문장은? [2.9점]
questions.passage: Cartilage is extremely important for the healthy functioning of a joint, especially if that joins bears weight, like your knee. Imagine for a moment that you're looking into the inner workings of your left knee as you walk down the street. ①When you shift your weight from your left leg to your right, the pressure on your left knee is released. ②Researchers say that this kinetics can be applied to the mechanism of robots in the near future. ③The cartilage in your left knee then "drinks in" synovial fluid, in much the same way that a sponge soaks up liquid when put in water. ④When you take another step and transfer the weight back onto your left leg, much of the fluid squeezes out of the cartilage. ⑤This squeezing of joint fluid into and out of the cartilage helps it respond to the off-and-on pressure of walking without breaking under the pressure.
questions.explanation: ②번 문윑은 로봇 메칀니즘에 대한 내용으로, 무릎 연골의 작용 원리와 관계된 전체 글의 흐름에서 벗어납니다.

questions.question: 22. 다음 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은? [3.1점]
questions.passage: In the course of trying to solve a problem with an invention, you may encounter a brick wall of resistance when you try to think your way logically through the problem. Such logical thinking is a linear type of process, which uses our reasoning skills. This works fine when we're operating in the area of what we know or have experienced. However, when we need to deal with new information, ideas, and viewpoints, linear thinking will often come up short. (A)___________, creativity by definition involves the application of new information to old problems and the conception of new viewpoints and ideas. For this you will be most effective if you learn to operate in a nonlinear manner; that is, use your creative brain. Stated differently, if you think in a linear manner, you'll tend to be (B)___________ and keep coming up with techniques which are already known. This, of course, is just what you don't want.
options: ① By contrast — conventional
② Consequently — ingenious
③ For Example — conservative
④ Notwithstanding — innovative
⑤ On the other hand — progressive
questions.explanation: (A) 압 문윑의 선형적 사고의 한계와 대조되는 창의성의 특징을 설명하므로 'By contrast(대조적으로)'가 적절하며, (B) 선형적 사고를 할 경옰 이미 알려진 기법만을 내놓는 'conventional(관습적인)' 사태가 됩니다.
options_translation: 대조적으로 — 관습적인
결과적으로 — 기발한
예를 들어 — 밴수적인
~에도 불구하고 — — 혁신적인
반면에 — 진밴적인

questions.question: 23. 다음 글에 이어질 내용을 서에 맞게 배열한 것으로 가장 적절한 것은? [3.2점]
questions.passage: The rise of air-conditioning accelerated the construction of sealed boxes, where the building's only airflow is through the filtered ducts of the air-conditioning unit. It doesn't have to be this way.
ordered_passages: (A) They oriented buildings to capture cool breezes and block the worst heat of the afternoon. They built with thick walls and white roofs and transoms over doors to encourage airflow.

(B) But all this wisdom about how to deal with heat, accumulated over centuries of practical experience, is all too often ignored. In this sense, air-conditioning is not just a technology of personal comfort; it is also a technology of forgetting.
(C) Look at any old building in a hot climate, whether it's in Sicily or Marrakesh or Tehran. Architects understood the importance of shade, airflow, light colors.
(D) Anyone who has ever spent a few minutes in a mudbrick house in Tucson, or walked on the narrow streets of old Seville, knows how well these construction methods work.
questions.explanation: 제시문 다음에 과거의 건축 방식을 예로 들기 시작하는 (C)가 오고, 괴 건축가들의 구체적인 노력을 설명하는 (A)가 이어집니다. 그 후 이러한 방식의 효과를 증명하는 (D)가 나오며, 마지막으로 이러한 지혜가 에어컨 때문에 잊혀졌다고 결론 짓는 (B)가 오는 것은 자연스럽습니다.

questions.question: 24. 다음 글의 흐름으로 밴아, 주어진 문윑이 들어가기에 가장 적절한 곳은? [3.0점]
questions.passage: Plants can communicate, although not in the same way we do. Some express their discontent through scents. You know that smell that hangs in the air after you've mowed the lawn? Yeah, that's actually an SOS. Some plants use sound. Yes, sound, though at a frequency that we can't hear. (A) Researchers experimented with plants and microphones to see if they could record any trouble calls. (B) They found that plants produce a high-frequency clicking noise when stressed and can make different sounds for different stressors. (C) However, it's worth noting that experts don't think plants are crying out in pain. (D) It's more likely that these reactions are knee-jerk survival actions. (E) Plants are living organisms, and their main objective is to survive. Scents and sounds are their tools for defending against thinks that might harm them.
questions.insertion_sentence: The sound a plant makes when it's not getting watered differs from the one it'll make when a leaf is cut.
options: ① (A)
② (B)
③ (C)
④ (D)
⑤ (E)
questions.explanation: 주어진 문윑은 식물이 스트레스 요인(물 부점 및 잎이 잘림)에 따라 서로 다른 소리를 낸다는 구체적인 예시입니다. 이는 식물이 스트레스 요인밴로 다른 소리를 낸다는 (B)의 내용을 받아서 (C) 자리에 들어가는 것이 적절합니다.

questions.question: 25. 다음 글의 문맥상 ⓐ~ⓔ의 각 빈칸에 들어갈 낱말을 유추해 볼 때, 그 낱말에 대한 설명이 적절하지 않은 것은?
questions.passage: Our skin conducts electricity more or less efficiently, depending on our emotions. We know that when we're emotionally stimulated ─ stressed, sad, any intense emotion, really ─ our bodies sweat a tiny bit, so little we might not even notice. And when those tiny drops of sweat appear, our skin gets ⓐ___________ electrically conductive. This change in sweat gland activity happens completely without your conscious mind having much say in the matter. If you feel emotionally ⓑ___________, you're going to notice an ⓒ___________ in sweat gland activity. This is particularly useful from a scientific viewpoint, because it allows us to put an ⓓ___________ value on a ⓔ___________ state of mind. We can actually measure your emotional state by tracking how your body subconsciously sweats, by running a bit of electricity through your skin. We can then turn the subjective, subconscious experience of emotional intensity into an objective number by figuring out how good your skin gets at transferring ah electrical current.
options: ① ⓐ small in size or extent
② ⓑ existing in an extreme degree
③ ⓒ to become progressively greater
④ ⓓ expressing or dealing with facts or conditions as perceived without distortion by personal feelings or prejudices
⑤ ⓔ relating to or being experience or knowledge as conditioned by personal mental characteristics or states
questions.explanation: 지문의 문맥상 ⓐ에는 '더욱' 혹은 '더 많이'라는 의미의 'more'가 들어가는 것이 적절합니다. ①번의 설명 'small in size or extent(크기나 범위가 작은)'는 'less'나 'tiny'에 대한 설명이므로 적절하지 않습니다. ⓑ는 intense, ⓒ는 increase, ⓓ는 objective, ⓔ는 subjective가 적절하며 각 선택지의 영영 풀이는 이 단어들의 의미와 일치합니다.
options_translation: ① 크기나 범위가 작은
② 극심한 정도에 존재하는
③ 점진적으로 더 커지는 것
④ 개인적인 감정이나 편견에 의한 왜곡 없이 인지된 사실이나 상태를 표현하거나 다루는 것
⑤ 개인적인 정신적 특성이나 상태에 의해 조건 지어진 경험이나 지식에 관련된 또는 그러한

questions.question: 26. 윗글의 빈칸 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Some researchers view spoken languages as (A)___________ devices for capturing precise differences. They think numbers represent the most neutral language of description. However, when our language of description is changed to numbers, we do not move toward greater accuracy. Numbers are no more (B)___________ 'pictures of the world' than words, music, or painting. While useful for specific purposes (e.g. census taking, income distribution), they exclude information of enormous value. For example, the future lives of young students are tied to their scores on national tests. In effect, whether they can continue with their education, where, and at what cost depends importantly on a handful of numbers. These numbers do not account for the quality of schools they have attended, whether they have been tutored, have supportive parents, have test anxiety, and so on. Finally, putting aside the many ways in which statistical results can be manipulated, there are ways in which turning people's lives into numbers is morally (C)___________. Statistics on crime, homelessness, or the spread of a disease say nothing of people's suffering. We read the statistics as reports on events at a distance, thus allowing us to escape without being disturbed. Statistics are human beings with the tears wiped off. Quantify with caution.
options: ① (A) incomplete (B) appropriate (C) instructing
② (A) complete (B) appropriate (C) insulating
③ (A) deficient (B) inappropriate (C) encouraging
④ (A) harmonious (B) unsuitable (C) unsatisfactory
⑤ (A) imperfect (B) proper (C) intercepting
questions.explanation: (A) 문맥상 일부 연구자들은 구어가 정교한 차이를 포착하는 데 '불완전한(imperfect/incomplete)' 장치라고 봅니다. (B) 숫자는 단어나 음악, 그림보다 더 '적절한(proper/appropriate)' 세상의 그림이 아니라는 의미가 되어야 합니다. (C) 마지막 문단에서 통계가 사람들의 고통을 말해주지 않으며 거리를 두게 만든다는 맥락에서, 삶을 숫자로 바꾸는 것이 도덕적으로 무언가를 '차단하는(intercepting/insulating)' 방식이 있다는 흐름이 적절합니다. 단, 학교 측에서 제공한 정답 ⑤번의 intercepting은 '가로막다/차단하다'의 의미로 쓰여 통계가 인간적 고통의 공감을 차단한다는 맥락으로 해석될 수 있습니다. (원문은 insulating)
options_translation: ① (A) 불완전한 (B) 적절한 (C) 지시하는
② (A) 완전한 (B) 적절한 (C) 절연하는/격리하는
③ (A) 결핍된 (B) 부적절한 (C) 격려하는
④ (A) 조화로운 (B) 부적합한 (C) 불만족스러운
⑤ (A) 불완전한 (B) 적절한 (C) 차단하는

questions.question: 27. 윗글의 내용과 일치하지 않는 것은?
questions.passage: Some researchers view spoken languages as (A)___________ devices for capturing precise differences. They think numbers represent the most neutral language of description. However, when our language of description is changed to numbers, we do not move toward greater accuracy. Numbers are no more (B)___________ 'pictures of the world' than words, music, or painting. While useful for specific purposes (e.g. census taking, income distribution), they exclude information of enormous value. For example, the future lives of young students are tied to their scores on national tests. In effect, whether they can continue with their education, where, and at what cost depends importantly on a handful of numbers. These numbers do not account for the quality of schools they have attended, whether they have been tutored, have supportive parents, have test anxiety, and so on. Finally, putting aside the many ways in which statistical results can be manipulated, there are ways in which turning people's lives into numbers is morally (C)___________. Statistics on crime, homelessness, or the spread of a disease say nothing of people's suffering. We read the statistics as reports on events at a distance, thus allowing us to escape without being disturbed. Statistics are human beings with the tears wiped off. Quantify with caution.
options: ① Some researchers think numbers are impartial.
② Describing with numbers doesn't increase accuracy.
③ Numbers are practical for specific purposes.
④ The future of students is bound by numbers.
⑤ Statistics convey human value with precision.
questions.explanation: 지문 마지막 부분에서 'Statistics are human beings with the tears wiped off(통계는 눈물을 닦아낸 인간이다)'라고 하며, 통계가 사람들의 고통이나 가치를 제대로 전달하지 못하고 정보를 배제한다고 설명하고 있습니다. 따라서 통계가 인간의 가치를 정밀하게 전달한다는 ⑤번은 내용과 일치하지 않습니다.
options_translation: ① 일부 연구자들은 숫자가 공정하다고 생각한다.
② 숫자로 묘사하는 것이 정확성을 높여주지는 않는다.
③ 숫자는 특정한 목적을 위해 실용적이다.
④ 학생들의 미래는 숫자에 얽매여 있다.
⑤ 통계는 인간의 가치를 정밀하게 전달한다.

questions.question: 1. 다음 글의 내용을 올바르게 이해한 진술은?
questions.passage:
The morning pages are three pages of "free writing," ideally done first thing in the morning. The concept is simple. Get up every morning, pick up a pen and a notebook, and write whatever crosses your mind until you have filled three pages. The technique was originally developed to help writers and artists overcome a loss of creativity, but anybody can use it to create a better life.
There is no right or wrong way to write your morning pages, but there are two rules. First, don't judge your writing as good or bad. These pages are meant to be a "brain cleansing," so don't worry about writing correctly. Second, keep your writing completely private. It is important for you to write freely and honestly. You're even advised not to read your writing yourself for weeks.
options: ① The morning pages must be written first thing in the morning no matter what.
② Morning pages are for the writers and artists, and they are not really helpful for ordinary people.
③ You had better not judge your morning pages in terms of right or wrong, and just free your mind.
④ Morning pages are all about writing correctly after you do some amount of "brain cleansing."
⑤ You are advised to open your morning pages to the public when you think it is better than keeping it private.
questions.explanation: 지문에서 모닝 페이지를 쓸 때 잘 썼는지 못 썼는지 판단하지 말고(don't judge your writing as good or bad), 옳고 그름이 없다고 했으므로, 판단을 지양하고 마음을 자유롭게 하라는 ③번이 글의 내용과 일치합니다. ①번은 '이상적으로는' 아침에 하는 것이 좋다고 했지 '반드시' 그래야 한다는 것은 아니며, ②번은 누구나 사용할 수 있다고 했고, ④번은 정확하게 쓰는 것에 걱정하지 말라고 했으며, ⑤번은 철저히 비공개로 유지하라고 명시되어 있습니다.
options_translation: ① 모닝 페이지는 무슨 일이 있어도 반드시 아침에 제일 먼저 작성되어야 한다.
② 모닝 페이지는 작가와 예술가들을 위한 것이며, 일반인들에게는 그다지 도움이 되지 않는다.
③ 모닝 페이지를 옳고 그름의 관점에서 판단하지 말고, 단지 마음을 자유롭게 하는 것이 좋다.
④ 모닝 페이지는 어느 정도의 '두뇌 정화'를 한 후에 정확하게 글을 쓰는 것에 관한 모든 것이다.
⑤ 비공개로 유지하는 것보다 낫다고 생각될 때는 모닝 페이지를 대중에게 공개하도록 권고된다.

questions.question: 2. 다음 글의 (A), (B), (C)에 각각 들어갈 표현으로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage:
A: My job tends to be very (A)__________. When I started writing morning pages, I just wrote a lot of complaints about my job and my life. Later, I began to ask questions, like "What would make my life easier today?" "How can I improve my recipes?" Sometimes, I keep asking questions until I reach a sort of "click moment." It feels like a door opening to great ideas. Nowadays, I feel less stressed, enjoy my job more, and am more (B)__________.

B: When I started this exercise last year, I simply wrote random thoughts like this:
 I'm sleepy. A slight headache's starting.
 I need to finish the math assignment today...
 I don't know what more to write now.
 But soon I found I had (C)__________ thoughts. Now, I normally start by writing about today's tasks or worries. After that, I write about my dreams and how to move towards them. I often come up with great plans and a clear sense of purpose to start the day. Most importantly, I'm much happier than before.
options: ① fun / depressed / unimportant
② stressful / productive / vague
③ demanding / fruitless / confusing
④ relieving / motivated / deep
⑤ challenging / passionate / extensive
questions.explanation: (A) 앞부분에서 직업과 삶에 대한 많은 불평을 썼다고 했으므로, 직업이 '도전적인(challenging)' 혹은 힘든 상황임을 추론할 수 있습니다. (B) 모닝 페이지를 통해 스트레스를 덜 받고 일을 더 즐기게 되었으므로 긍정적인 형용사인 '열정적인(passionate)'이 적절합니다. (C) 처음에는 단순하고 무작위적인 생각들을 적었지만, 곧 '광범위한(extensive)' 혹은 더 깊은 생각들을 갖게 되었다는 흐름이 자연스럽습니다. 다만 제공된 정답 ⑤번에 따르면 (A) challenging (B) passionate (C) extensive가 가장 적절한 조합입니다.
options_translation: ① 재미있는 / 우울한 / 중요하지 않은
② 스트레스가 많은 / 생산적인 / 모호한
③ 까다로운 / 결실 없는 / 혼란스러운
④ 안도하게 하는 / 동기 부여된 / 깊은
⑤ 도전적인 / 열정적인 / 광범위한

questions.question: 3. 다음 글의 제목으로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage:
Morning pages, releasing my feelings onto paper every morning, helped relieve my emotional tension. I gained more inner peace, which improved my schoolwork performance. I asked many questions, for instance, "Why was I so angry yesterday?" "Why are things less fun these days?" Then, I started raising more challenging ones: "What could make me happier right now?" "What is my ideal future? Can I reach it? How?"
Answering these questions showed me what kind of person I was and what my needs, values, passions, and talents were. More importantly, I came to know what I truly wanted! I remembered my childhood dreams of being a writer, songwriter, and radio host. Gradually, vague ideas became clear plans. Years later, here I am, a successful podcaster and vlogger! I've also published a book and a music album. My morning pages, which I still write every day, have given me the drive and ideas to achieve these aims.
options: ① How to Make Great Questions
② How Morning pages Help Shape Dreams
③ Things You Need to Become a Successful Podcaster
④ The Process in Which Your Ideals and Reality Balance out
⑤ The Power of Morning Pages: Only Answers can Help You
questions.explanation: 이 글은 필자가 모닝 페이지를 통해 정서적 긴장을 완화하고, 자신에 대해 더 잘 알게 되었으며, 어릴 적 꿈을 구체적인 계획으로 바꾸어 결국 성공한 팟캐스터가 되었다는 경험담을 담고 있습니다. 따라서 '모닝 페이지가 꿈을 형성하는 데 어떻게 도움이 되는가'가 가장 적절한 제목입니다.
options_translation: ① 훌륭한 질문을 만드는 방법
② 모닝 페이지가 꿈을 형성하는 데 도움을 주는 방법
③ 성공적인 팟캐스터가 되기 위해 필요한 것들
④ 이상과 현실이 균형을 이루는 과정
⑤ 모닝 페이지의 힘: 오직 답변만이 당신을 도울 수 있다

questions.question: 4. 다음 글의 ⓐ~ⓔ 중 밑줄 친 (A)start down this slippery slope에 대한 구체적인 사례로 볼 수 없는 것은?
questions.passage: Assuming gene editing in humans proves to be safe and effective, it might seem logical, even preferable, to correct disease-causing mutations at the earliest possible stage of life, before ⓐ<u>harmful genes begin causing serious problems</u>. Yet once it becomes possible ⓑ<u>to transform an embryo's mutated genes into "normal" ones</u>, there will certainly be temptations ⓒ<u>to upgrade normal genes to superior versions</u>. Should we begin ⓓ<u>editing genes in unborn children to lower their lifetime risk of heart disease or cancer</u>? What about ⓔ<u>giving unborn children beneficial features</u>, like greater strength and increased mental abilities, or changing physical characteristics, like eye and hair color? The pursuit for perfection seems almost natural to human nature, but if we (A)<u>start down this slippery slope</u>, we may not like where we end up.
options: ① ⓐ
② ⓑ
③ ⓒ
④ ⓓ
⑤ ⓔ
questions.explanation: 'slippery slope(미끄러운 경사면)'는 한 번 시작하면 걷잡을 수 없이 나쁜 상황으로 빠져들게 되는 단계를 의미합니다. 본문에서 논의되는 유전자 편집의 위험한 흐름은 '질병 치료'라는 초기 목적을 넘어 '유전적 강화(superior versions, beneficial features)'로 나아가는 것을 경고하고 있습니다. ⓐ는 유전자가 문제를 일으키기 전 상태를 설명하는 일반적인 상황이므로, 인간이 인위적으로 개입하여 변형을 시작하는 '미끄러운 경사면'의 구체적 행위 사례로 보기는 어렵습니다. 반면 ⓑ, ⓒ, ⓓ, ⓔ는 모두 인위적인 유전자 편집의 구체적인 단계나 유혹을 나타냅니다.

questions.question: 6. 다음 글에서 전체 흐름과 관계없는 문장은?
questions.passage: There is a bunch of evidence that people feel happier and more motivated when parents, teachers, supervisors, and coaches are perceived as involved and caring. ⓐ<u>And we need to feel valued and respected not only by those people with power, but also by peers and coworkers.</u> ⓑ<u>Thus, when the need for relatedness is met and the support for autonomy and competence are there, motivation and internalization are accelerated.</u> ⓒ<u>If you want to motivate others, building a strong bond is a crucial basis from which to begin.</u> ⓓ<u>And when you are trying to motivate yourself, you should be focus on your own routine to achieve your goals rather than to enhance a sense of connectedness to others.</u> ⓔ<u>Hence, exercise with a friend, call someone when you have a painful decision to make, and be there as a support for others when they have one too.</u>
options: ① ⓐ
② ⓑ
③ ⓒ
④ ⓓ
⑤ ⓔ
questions.explanation: 전체 글은 타인(부모, 교사, 동료 등)과의 유대감, 존중, 그리고 관계 맺기(relatedness)가 동기 부여에 핵심적인 역할을 한다는 내용입니다. 하지만 ⓓ번은 자신을 동기부여 할 때 타인과의 연결성을 강화하기보다 '자신만의 루틴'에 집중해야 한다고 말하고 있어, 관계 지향적인 전체 흐름에서 벗어납니다.

questions.question: 7. 주어진 글 다음에 이어질 글의 순서로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Routines enable athletes to evaluate competition conditions. For example, bouncing a ball in a volleyball service routine supplies the server with information about the ball, the floor, and the state of her muscles.
ordered_passages: (A) This information can then be used to properly prepare for her serve. Routines also enable athletes to adjust and fine-tune their preparations based on those evaluations or in pursuit of a particular competitive goal.
(B) Just like adjusting a race-car engine to the conditions of the track, air temperature, and weather, routines adjust all competitive components to achieve proper performance.
(C) This adaptation can involve adjustment to the conditions, rivals, competitive situation, or internal influences that can affect performance.
questions.explanation: 주어진 글에서 배구 서비스 루틴을 통해 정보(information)를 얻는 예시를 들었습니다. (A)의 'This information'이 바로 그 예시에서 얻은 정보를 가리키며, 루틴이 조정을 가능하게 한다고 설명합니다. (C)의 'This adaptation'은 (A)에서 언급된 조정(adjust)을 구체화하며 상황에 맞게 바꾸는 것을 설명합니다. 마지막으로 (B)에서 이러한 조정 과정을 경주용 자동차 엔진 조절에 비유하며 결론을 맺는 것이 자연스럽습니다.

questions.question: 8. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중 어법상 어색한 것은?

questions.question: 9. 다음 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

questions.explanation: 이 글은 세계 각국의 문화적 맥락이 반영된 어휘들이 영어 사전에 편입되면서 영어 어휘가 풍부해지고 다양해지고 있음을 설명합니다. 또한 영어가 특정 국가나 원어민의 전유물이 아니라 이를 사용하는 모든 이들의 언어임을 강조하며, 영어에 내재된 문화적 다양성을 포용하고 존중함으로써 더 포용적인 공동체를 구축할 수 있다는 내용을 담고 있습니다. 따라서 영어 사용자들이 세계 영어(World Englishes)의 다양성을 수용하고 가치를 인정해야 한다는 ⑤번이 요지로 가장 적절합니다.

questions.question: 22. 다음 글의 요지로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Promotion deals with consumer psychology. We can't force people to think one way or another, and the clever marketer knows that promotion is used to provide information in the most clear, honest, and simple fashion possible. By doing so, the possibility of increasing sales goes up. Gone are the days when promotions were done in order to fool the consumer into purchasing something. The long-term effect of getting a consumer to buy something they did not really want or need wasn't good. In fact, consumers fooled once can do damage to sales as they relate their experience to others. Instead, marketers now know that their goal is to identify the consumers who are most likely to appreciate a good or service, and to promote that good or service in a way that makes the value clear to the consumer. Therefore, marketers must know where the potential consumers are, and how to reach them.
options: ① 성공적인 마케팅은 제품 가격을 낮추는 데 달려 있다.
② 마케팅의 목표는 소비자를 조작하여 수익을 올리는 것이다.
③ 오늘날의 마케터들이 감정에 호소할 때 홍보 효과가 가장 크다.
④ 마케팅의 주요 목적은 소비자 피드백을 통해 생산 비용을 줄이는 것이다.
⑤ 효과적인 홍보는 잠재 고객을 파악하고 제품의 가치를 명확히 전달하는 것이다.
questions.explanation: 이 글은 현대 마케팅의 핵심이 소비자를 속여서 물건을 팔게 하는 과거 방식에서 벗어나, 제품을 가치 있게 여길 잠재적 소비자를 식별하고 그들에게 제품의 가치를 명확하고 정직하게 전달하는 것임을 강조하고 있습니다. 따라서 '효과적인 홍보는 잠재 고객을 파악하고 제품의 가치를 명확히 전달하는 것'이 요지로 가장 적절합니다.

questions.question: 23. 다음 글의 제목으로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Let's assume that at least some animals are capable of thinking despite lacking a language. This doesn't necessarily mean that they possess concepts, for some forms of thought may be nonconceptual. We can imagine, for instance, a squirrel who is planning how to get from the branch she's currently standing on to a branch from the tree in front. To do this, in principle she doesn't need a concept of branch nor a concept of tree. It might be enough for her to have, for example, the ability to think in images; to make a mental map of the tree where she can imagine and try out different routes. This doesn't imply that squirrels lack concepts, simply that they don't need them for this concrete form of thinking. For us to be able to say that an animal has concepts, we have to show not just that she's capable of thinking, but also that she has certain specific abilities.
options: ① The Role of Memory in Animal Survival
② Why Squirrels Are Smarter Than We Think
③ The Limits of Animal Intelligence and Instinct
④ Language and Nonconceptual Thinking in Humans
⑤ Nonconceptual Thinking: How Some Animals Think Without Language
questions.explanation: 글의 도입부에서 언어가 없더라도 동물이 사고할 수 있다는 가정을 제시하며, 다람쥐가 나무 사이를 이동할 때 '개념'이 아닌 '이미지'나 '정신적 지도'를 사용하는 '비개념적 사고'를 할 수 있음을 설명합니다. 따라서 '비개념적 사고: 일부 동물이 언어 없이 생각하는 방법'이 제목으로 가장 적절합니다.

④ 인간의 언어와 비개념적 사고
⑤ 비개념적 사고: 일부 동물이 언어 없이 생각하는 법

questions.question: 24. 다음 글의 주제로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Plants can communicate, although not in the same way we do. Some express their discontent through scents. You know that smell that hangs in the air after you've mowed the lawn? Yeah, that's actually an SOS. Some plants use sound. Yes, sound, though at a frequency that we can't hear. Researchers experimented with plants and microphones to see if they could record any trouble calls. They found that plants produce a high-frequency clicking noise when stressed and can make different sounds for different stressors. The sound a plant makes when it's not getting watered differs from the one it'll make when a leaf is cut. However, it's worth noting that experts don't think plants are crying out in pain. It's more likely that these reactions are knee-jerk survival actions. Plants are living organism, and their main objective is to survive. Scents and sounds are their tools for defending against things that might harm them.
options: ① The effects of human care on plant survival
② How plants recognize and respond to human voices
③ Scientific debates about how plants express emotions
④ Plant communication through scents and sounds for survival
⑤ The relationship between plant growth speed and environmental change
questions.explanation: 이 글은 식물이 인간과는 다르지만 향기(scents)와 소리(sounds)를 통해 의사소통하며, 이것이 고통의 표현이라기보다는 생존을 위한 반사적인 방어 기제임을 설명하고 있습니다. 따라서 주제로는 '생존을 위한 향기와 소리를 통한 식물의 의사소통'이 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 인간의 돌봄이 식물의 생존에 미치는 영향
② 식물이 인간의 목소리를 인식하고 반응하는 법
③ 식물이 감정을 표현하는 방식에 대한 과학적 논쟁
④ 생존을 위해 향기와 소리를 이용하는 식물의 의사소통
⑤ 식물의 성장 속도와 환경 변화의 관계

questions.question: 25. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 어법상 어색한 것은? [2.9점]
questions.passage: The science we learn in grade school ⓐ<u>is</u> a collection of certainties about the natural world─the earth goes around the sun, DNA carries the information of an organism, and so on. Only when you start to learn the practice of science ⓑ<u>do</u> you realize that each of these "facts" ⓒ<u>was</u> hard won through a succession of logical inferences based upon many observations or experiments. The process of science is less about collecting pieces of knowledge than it is about reducing the uncertainties in ⓓ<u>which</u> we know. Our uncertainties can be greater or lesser for any given piece of knowledge depending upon ⓔ<u>where</u> we are in that process─today we are quite certain of how an apple will fall from a tree, but our understanding of the turbulent fluid flow remains a work in progress after more than a century of effort.
options: ① ⓐ
② ⓑ
③ ⓒ
④ ⓓ
⑤ ⓔ
questions.explanation: ⓓ가 포함된 문장에서 'know'는 타동사이며 뒤에 목적어가 빠져 있는 불완전한 절을 이끌어야 합니다. 따라서 전치사+관계대명사 형태인 'in which'가 아니라, '~하는 것'이라는 의미의 선행사를 포함한 관계대명사 'what'이 와야 적절합니다.

② do (도치 구문 강조 동사)
