④ which (관계대명사/전치사구)
⑤ where (의문부사/관계부사)

questions.question: 26. 주어진 글 다음에 이어질 글의 순서로 가장 적절한 것은? [3.2점]
questions.passage: As you listen to your child in an emotional moment, be aware that sharing simple observations usually works better than asking questions to get a conversation rolling. You may ask your child "Why do you feel sad?" and she may not have a clue.
ordered_passages: (A) But she may or may not be able to explain any of this. And even when she does come up with an answer, she might be worried that the answer is not good enough to justify the feeling.
(B) As a child, she may not have an answer on the tip of her tongue. Maybe she's feeling sad about her parents' arguments, or because she feels overtired, or she's worried about a piano recital.
(C) Under these circumstances, a series of questions can just make a child silent. It's better to simply reflect what you notice.
questions.explanation: 주어진 문장에서 아이가 슬픈 이유를 모를 수도 있다는 내용이 나온 뒤, (B)에서 아이가 답을 바로 떠올리지 못할 수 있는 구체적인 예시들(부모님의 다툼, 피로, 피아노 발표회 걱정 등)이 나옵니다. (A)에서는 그러한 이유들을 'this'로 받으며 설명하지 못할 수도 있다는 점을 덧붙입니다. 마지막으로 (C)에서는 이러한 상황(Under these circumstances)에서 질문 세례가 아이를 침묵하게 하니 관찰한 것을 반영해주는 것이 낫다는 결론을 내립니다.

questions.question: 27. 다음 글의 내용과 일치하는 것은? [2.9점]
questions.passage: Piaget put the same amount of water into two different glasses: a tall narrow glass and a wide glass, then asked kids to compare two glasses. Kids younger than six or seven usually say that tall narrow glass now holds more water, because the level is higher. And when they are ready, they figure out the conservation of volume for themselves just by playing with cups of water. Piaget argued that children's understanding of morality is like their understanding of those water glasses: we can't say that it is innate or kids learn it directly from adults. Rather, it is self-constructed as kids play with other kids. Taking turns in a game is like pouring water back and forth between glasses. Once kids have reached the age of five or six, then playing games and working things out together will help them learn about fairness far more effectively than any teaching from adults.
options: ① 여섯 살 미만의 아이들은 이미 부피 보존 개념을 완전히 이해하고 있다.
② 아이들은 어른의 직접적인 가르침을 통해 공정성을 가장 잘 배운다.
③ 피아제는 도덕적 이해가 인간에게 타고나는 것이라고 보았다.
④ 아이들은 또래와의 놀이를 통해 도덕적 사고를 발달시킨다.
⑤ 규칙을 엄격히 가르치는 것이 아이들에게 도덕성을 키우는 가장 효과적인 방법이다.
questions.explanation: 본문에서 피아제는 아이들의 도덕적 이해가 선천적인 것이거나 어른에게 직접 배우는 것이 아니라, 아이들이 다른 아이들과 함께 놀면서 '자기 구성되는(self-constructed)' 것이라고 주장했습니다. 특히 게임을 하며 순서를 지키는 등의 활동이 공정성을 배우는 데 효과적이라고 언급했으므로 4번이 일치합니다.

questions.question: 28. 다음 글의 흐름으로 보아, 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은? [3.2점]
questions.passage: Some researchers view spoken languages as incomplete devices for capturing precise differences. They think numbers represent the most neutral language of description. However, when our language of description is changed to numbers, we do not move toward greater accuracy. Numbers are no more appropriate 'pictures of the world' than words, music, or painting. While useful for specific purposes (e.g. census taking, income distribution), they (A)____________ information of enormous value. For example, the future lives of young students are tied to their scores on national tests. In effect, whether they can continue with their education, where, at what cost depends importantly on a (B)____________ of numbers. These numbers do not account for the quality of schools they have attended, whether they have been tutored, have supportive parents, have test anxiety, and so on. Finally, putting aside the many ways in which statistical results can be manipulated, there are ways in which turning people's lives into numbers is (C)____________. Statistics on crime, homelessness, or the spread of a disease say nothing of people's suffering. We read the statistics as reports on events at distance, thus allowing us to escape without being disturbed. Statistics are human beings with the tears wiped off. Quantify with caution.
options: ① leave out	    lot		completely false
② translate into	    total set	emotionally rich
③ delete	    few		ethically cold
④ carry over	    handful	less sensitive
questions.explanation: 본문은 숫자가 세상을 묘사할 때 인간적인 고통이나 맥락을 담아내지 못한다는 점을 비판하고 있습니다. (A)에서는 숫자가 엄청난 가치를 지닌 정보를 '삭제(delete)'하거나 '누락(leave out)'한다는 맥락이 적절합니다. (B)에서는 소수의(few) 숫자에 따라 학생들의 미래가 결정됨을 의미하며, (C)에서는 숫자로 치환된 통계가 사람들의 고통을 보여주지 못해 '윤리적으로 차갑다(ethically cold)'는 점을 시사합니다. 따라서 가장 적절한 것은 3번입니다.
options_translation: ① 누락하다 - 많은 - 완전히 거짓인
② 번역하다 - 전체 세트 - 감정적으로 풍부한
③ 삭제하다 - 소수 - 윤리적으로 차가운
④ 이어지다 - 소수 - 덜 민감한

questions.question: 1. 윗글의 주제로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: The responsive behavior of dogs also caught the attention of an evolutionary anthropologist, Brian Hare. He conducted an experiment to see how dogs would respond to human gestures compared to wolves, who share the same common ancestor. He placed two cups on the ground with food hidden under only one of them. When he pointed to the cup with the food, the dogs found it easily. The wolves, (A)____________, struggled and chose cups at random, paying no attention to his gestures. Dr. Hare concluded that the dogs' ability to read human gestures allowed them to perform better than the wolves. He explained that dogs, unlike wolves, have developed communicative skills with humans and a sense of friendliness. This explanation sounds reasonable according to several evolutionary biologists. They say that from the common ancestors of these two species, those that acted friendly toward humans evolved into dogs, and those that didn't became wolves. (B)____________, Dr. Hare suggested that the friendly nature of dogs probably provided them a survival advantage that allowed their population to grow larger than that of wolves.
options: ① The history of dog training by humans
② The hunting strategies of wolves and dogs
③ Comparing the intelligence of dogs and wolves
④ How animals use their sense of smell to find food
⑤ How dogs developed better communication skills than wolves
questions.explanation: 개와 늑대의 반응 행동을 비교한 실험을 통해, 개가 인간의 제스처를 읽고 소통하는 능력을 어떻게 발달시켰으며, 이것이 생존에 어떤 이점을 주었는지 설명하는 글입니다. 따라서 주제로 가장 적절한 것은 '개가 늑대보다 더 나은 의사소통 능력을 발달시킨 방법'입니다.
options_translation: ① 인간에 의한 개 훈련의 역사
② 늑대와 개의 사냥 전략
③ 개와 늑대의 지능 비교
④ 동물들이 음식을 찾기 위해 후각을 사용하는 방법
⑤ 개가 늑대보다 더 나은 의사소통 능력을 발달시킨 방법

questions.question: 2. 윗글의 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: The responsive behavior of dogs also caught the attention of an evolutionary anthropologist, Brian Hare. He conducted an experiment to see how dogs would respond to human gestures compared to wolves, who share the same common ancestor. He placed two cups on the ground with food hidden under only one of them. When he pointed to the cup with the food, the dogs found it easily. The wolves, (A)____________, struggled and chose cups at random, paying no attention to his gestures. Dr. Hare concluded that the dogs' ability to read human gestures allowed them to perform better than the wolves. He explained that dogs, unlike wolves, have developed communicative skills with humans and a sense of friendliness. This explanation sounds reasonable according to several evolutionary biologists. They say that from the common ancestors of these two species, those that acted friendly toward humans evolved into dogs, and those that didn't became wolves. (B)____________, Dr. Hare suggested that the friendly nature of dogs probably provided them a survival advantage that allowed their population to grow larger than that of wolves.
options: ① nonetheless --- In other words
② however --- Furthermore
③ that is --- Namely
④ for example --- Nonetheless
⑤ otherwise --- In contrast
questions.explanation: (A) 앞 문장에서 개는 음식을 쉽게 찾았다고 언급한 반면, 뒤 문장에서는 늑대는 어려움을 겪었다고 대조되는 내용이 나오므로 역접의 접속사 however가 적절합니다. (B) 앞 문장에서 개의 진화적 설명을 제시한 후, 뒤 문장에서 개의 우호적 성격이 생존상의 이점을 제공했다는 추가적인 내용을 덧붙이고 있으므로 첨가의 접속사 Furthermore가 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 그럼에도 불구하고 --- 다시 말해서
② 그러나 --- 게다가
③ 즉 --- 즉 다시 말해
④ 예를 들어 --- 그럼에도 불구하고
⑤ 그렇지 않으면 --- 대조적으로

questions.question: 3. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 어법상 어색한 것은?
questions.passage: What does it mean for a character to be a hero as opposed to a villain? In artistic and entertainment descriptions, it's essential for the author ⓐ<u>to establish</u> a positive relationship between a protagonist and the audience. In order for tragedy or misfortune to draw out an emotional response in viewers, the character must be ⓑ<u>adjusted</u> so as to be recognizable as either friend or enemy. Whether the portrayal is fictional or documentary, we must feel that the protagonist is someone ⓒ<u>who</u> actions benefit us: the protagonist is, or would be, a worthy companion or valued ally. Violent action films are often filled with dozens of incidental deaths of minor characters ⓓ<u>that</u> draw out little response in the audience. In order to feel strong emotions, the audience must be ⓔ<u>emotionally</u> invested in a character as either ally or enemy.
options: ① ⓐ
② ⓑ
③ ⓒ
④ ⓓ
⑤ ⓔ
questions.explanation: ⓒ는 뒤에 actions benefit us라는 완전한 절(주어+동사+목적어)이 오고 있으며, '주인공의 행동'이라는 소유의 의미가 필요하므로 주격 관계대명사 who가 아니라 소유격 관계대명사인 whose로 고쳐야 합니다.

questions.question: 4. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 어법상 어색한 것은?
questions.passage: The rise of air-conditioning accelerated the construction of sealed boxes, ⓐ<u>where</u> the building's only airflow is through the filtered ducts of the air-conditioning unit. It doesn't have to be this way. Look at any old building in a hot climate, whether it's in Sicily or Marrakesh or Tehran. Architects understood the importance of shade, airflow, light colors. They oriented buildings to capture cool breezes and ⓑ<u>block</u> the worst heat of the afternoon. They built with thick walls and white roofs and transoms over doors to encourage airflow. Anyone who has ever spent a few minutes in a mud brick house in Tucson, or ⓒ<u>walk</u> on the narrow streets of old Seville, knows how well these construction methods work. But all this wisdom about how to deal with heat, ⓓ<u>accumulated</u> over centuries of practical experience, is all too often ignored. In this sense, air-conditioning is not just a technology of personal comfort; it is also a technology of ⓔ<u>forgetting</u>.
options: ① ⓐ
② ⓑ
③ ⓒ
④ ⓓ
⑤ ⓔ
questions.explanation: ⓒ는 앞의 spent와 병렬 구조를 이루어야 합니다. 'has ever spent ... or (has ever) walked'의 구조가 되어야 하므로 walk를 과거분사 형태인 walked로 고쳐야 합니다.

questions.question: 5. 다음 글의 제목으로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: As you listen to your child in an emotional moment, be aware that sharing simple observations usually works better than asking questions to get a conversation rolling. You may ask your child "Why do you feel sad?" and she may not have a clue. As a child, she may not have an answer on the tip of her tongue. Maybe she's feeling sad about her parents' arguments, or because she feels overtired, or she's worried about a piano recital. But she may or may not be able to explain any of this. And even when she does come up with an answer, she might be worried that the answer is not good enough to justify the feeling. Under these circumstances, a series of questions can just make a child silent. It's better to simply reflect what you notice. You can say, "You seem a little tired today," or, "I noticed that you frowned when I mentioned the recital," and wait for her response.
options: ① Avoiding Arguments in a Relationship
② Effective Ways of Coming up with Diverse Answers
③ How to Communicate with a Child in Emotional Moments
④ The Importance of Vivid Circumstances in Conversation
⑤ Observation: Creative Ways of Making Children Silent
questions.explanation: 아이가 정서적인 순간에 있을 때, '왜?'라는 질문을 던져 아이를 당황하게 하거나 침묵하게 만들기보다, 부모가 관찰한 바를 담담하게 전달함으로써 아이가 스스로 대화를 시작할 수 있게 도와주는 것이 효과적인 소통 방법이라는 내용을 담고 있습니다.
options_translation: ① 관계에서의 논쟁 피하기
② 다양한 답변을 생각해 내는 효과적인 방법들
③ 감정적인 순간에 아이와 소통하는 법
④ 대화에서 생생한 상황의 중요성
⑤ 관찰: 아이들을 침묵하게 만드는 창의적인 방법들

questions.question: 6. 다음 글의 제목으로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Routines enable athletes to evaluate competition conditions. For example, bouncing a ball in a volleyball service routine supplies the server with information about the ball, the floor, and the state of her muscles. This information can then be used to properly prepare for her serve. Routines also enable athletes to adjust and fine-tune their preparations based on those evaluations or in pursuit of a particular competitive goal. This adaptation can involve adjustment to the conditions, rivals, competitive situation, or internal influences what can affect performance. Just like adjusting a race-car engine to the conditions of the track, air temperature, and weather, routines adjust all competitive components to achieve proper performance.
options: ① The Various Roles of Routines in Sports
② How to Improve Muscle Strength for Sports
③ The Science Behind Fast Reflexes in Athletes
④ Why Strategy Matters More Than Physical Skill
⑤ Why Teamwork Is the Key to Winning Competitions
questions.explanation: 스포츠에서 루틴은 선수들이 경기 조건을 평가하고, 그에 맞춰 자신의 준비 상태를 미세하게 조정하며, 최적의 성과를 낼 수 있도록 돕는 다각적인 역할을 수행한다는 점을 설명하고 있습니다.
options_translation: ① 스포츠에서 루틴의 다양한 역할
② 스포츠를 위한 근력을 향상시키는 방법
③ 운동선수의 빠른 반사 신경 뒤에 숨겨진 과학
④ 왜 전략이 신체적 기술보다 중요한가
⑤ 왜 팀워크가 경기 승리의 핵심인가

questions.question: 7. 다음 글의 제목으로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Cartilage is extremely important for the healthy functioning of a joint, especially if that joint bears weight, like your knee. Imagine for a moment that you're looking into the inner workings of your left knee as you walk down the street. When you shift your weight from your left leg to your right, the pressure on your left knee is released. The cartilage in your left knee then "drinks in" synovial fluid, in much the same way that a sponge soaks up liquid when put in water. When you take another step and transfer the weight back onto your left leg, much of the fluid squeezes out of the cartilage. This squeezing of joint fluid into and out of the cartilage helps it respond to the off-and-on pressure of walking without breaking under the pressure.
options: ① Aging and Changes in Knee Cartilage
② Exercises to Reduce Knee Joint Pain
③ The Effect of Weight Loss on Joint Health
④ How Cartilage Handles Pressure While Walking
⑤ The Structure and Regeneration of Cartilage
questions.explanation: 연골이 걷는 동안 체중 이동에 따라 관절액을 흡수하고 배출하는 과정을 반복하며, 이러한 메커니즘을 통해 보행 시 발생하는 압력에 적절히 대응하고 관절 기능을 유지한다는 내용입니다.
options_translation: ① 노화와 무릎 연골의 변화
② 무릎 관절 통증을 줄이기 위한 운동들
③ 체중 감량이 관절 건강에 미치는 영향

questions.question: 8. 다음 글의 요지로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: There is a wealth of evidence that when parents, teachers, supervisors, and coaches are perceived as involved and caring, people feel happier and more motivated. And it is not just those people with power – we need to feel valued and respected by peers and coworkers. Thus, when the need for relatedness is met, motivation and internalization are fueled, provided that support for autonomy and competence are also there. If we are trying to motivate others, a caring relationship is a crucial basis from which to begin. And when we are trying to motivate ourselves, doing things to enhance a sense of connectedness to others can be crucial to long term persistence. So exercise with a friend, call someone when you have a difficult decision to make, and be there as a support for others as they take on challenges.
options: ① Making decisions alone is more effective than seeking advice from others.
② People must develop self-motivation without relying on external encouragement.
③ Coaches and teachers are the most important influences on a person's motivation and success.
④ Supportive relationships increase motivation and well-being by fulfilling the need for connection and encouragement.
⑤ Hard work and determination are the main factors in achieving success, regardless of social support.
questions.explanation: 타인과의 지지적이고 배려하는 관계가 인간의 유대감 욕구를 충족시키며, 이를 통해 동기 부여와 정서적 안녕감이 증진된다는 핵심 내용을 전달하고 있습니다.
options_translation: ① 다른 이에게 조언을 구하는 것보다 혼자 결정을 내리는 것이 더 효과적이다.
② 사람들은 외부의 격려에 의존하지 않고 자기 동기 부여를 발달시켜야 한다.
③ 코치와 교사는 개인의 동기 부여와 성공에 있어 가장 중요한 영향력이다.
④ 지지적인 관계는 유대감과 격려의 욕구를 충족시킴으로써 동기 부여와 안녕을 증가시킨다.
⑤ 사회적 지지와 관계없이, 고된 노력과 결단력이 성공을 거두는 주요 요인이다.

questions.question: 9. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?
questions.passage: Plato argued that when you see something that strikes you as beautiful, you are really just seeing a ⓐ<u>partial</u> reflection of true beauty, just as a painting or even a photograph only captures some of the real thing. True beauty, or what Plato calls the Form of Beauty, has no particular color, shape, or size. Rather, it is an ⓑ<u>abstract</u> idea, like the number five. You can make drawings of the number five in blue or red ink, big or small, but the number five itself is none of those things. It has no ⓒ<u>physical</u> form. Think of the idea of a triangle, for example. Although it has no ⓓ<u>particular</u> color or size, it somehow lies within each and every triangle you see. Plato thought the ⓔ<u>opposite</u> was true of beauty. The Form of Beauty somehow lies within each and every beautiful thing you see.
options: ① ⓐ
② ⓑ
③ ⓒ
④ ⓓ
⑤ ⓔ
questions.explanation: 글의 흐름상 플라톤은 삼각형의 관념이 각각의 삼각형 내부에 존재하는 것과 '마찬가지로' 아름다움의 형상 또한 모든 아름다운 것들 안에 존재한다고 주장했습니다. 따라서 '반대의(opposite)'가 아니라 '같은(same)' 혹은 '마찬가지의'라는 의미의 낱말이 문맥상 적절합니다.

questions.question: 10. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?
questions.passage: Assuming gene editing in humans proves to be safe and effective, it might seem logical, even preferable, to ⓐ<u>correct</u> disease-causing mutations at the earliest possible stage of life, before harmful genes begin causing serious problems. Yet once it becomes possible to transform an embryo's mutated genes into "normal" ones, there will certainly be temptations to ⓑ<u>upgrade</u> normal genes to superior versions. Should we begin editing genes in unborn children to ⓒ<u>lower</u> their lifetime risk of heart disease or cancer? What about giving unborn children ⓓ<u>beneficial</u> features, like greater strength and increased mental abilities, or changing physical characteristics, like eye and hair color? The pursuit for perfection seems almost natural to human nature, but if we start down this slippery slope, we may ⓔ<u>love</u> where we end up.
options: ① ⓐ
② ⓑ
③ ⓒ
④ ⓓ
⑤ ⓔ
questions.explanation: 글은 유전자 편집이 질병 예방을 넘어 우월한 형질을 만드는 쪽으로 변질될 수 있는 '위험한 비탈길(slippery slope)'에 대해 경고하고 있습니다. 이러한 위험한 상황이 초래할 결말에 대해서는 '좋아할(love)' 것이 아니라 '후회하거나(regret)' 두려워할 것이라는 문맥이 적절합니다.

questions.question: 11. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?
questions.passage: In the course of trying to solve a problem with an invention, you may encounter a brick wall of resistance when you try to think your way logically through the problem. Such logical thinking is a linear type of process, which uses our ⓐ<u>reasoning</u> skills. This works fine when we're operating in the area of what we know or have ⓑ<u>experienced</u>. However, when we need to deal with new information, ideas, and viewpoints, linear thinking will often come up ⓒ<u>short</u>. On the other hand, creativity by definition involves the application of new information to old problems and the conception of new viewpoints and ideas. For this you will be most effective if you learn to operate in a ⓓ<u>linear</u> manner; that is, use your creative brain. Stated differently, if you think in a linear manner, you'll tend to be ⓔ<u>conservative</u> and keep coming up with techniques which are already known. This, of course, is just what you don't want.
options: ① ⓐ
② ⓑ
③ ⓒ
④ ⓓ
⑤ ⓔ
questions.explanation: 글의 전반부에서 선형적 사고(linear thinking)는 새로운 아이디어를 다루는 데 한계가 있다고 설명하고 있습니다. 따라서 창의적인 뇌를 사용하여 효과적으로 문제를 해결하려면 선형적인 방식이 아닌 '비선형적인(non-linear)' 방식으로 작동해야 합니다.

questions.question: 12. 다음 글의 내용과 일치하지 않는 것은?
questions.passage: Plants can communicate, although not in the same way we do. Some express their discontent through scents. You know that smell that hangs in the air after you've mowed the lawn? Yeah, that's actually an SOS. Some plants use sound. Yes, sound, though at a frequency that we can't hear. Researchers experimented with plants and microphones to see if they could record any trouble calls. They found that plants produce a high-frequency clicking noise when stressed and can make different sounds for different stressors. The sound a plant makes when it's not getting watered differs from the one it'll make when a leaf is cut. However, it's worth noting that experts don't think plants are crying out in pain. It's more likely that these reactions are knee-jerk survival actions. Plants are living organisms, and their main objective is to survive. Scents and sounds are their tools for defending against things that might harm them.
options: ① Plants have ways of communicating, though not in the same manner as humans.
② Some plants release scents to indicate their dissatisfaction.
③ Certain plants produce sounds, but these occur at frequencies beyond human hearing.
④ Researchers found out stressed plants emit high-frequency clicking noises.
⑤ Experts discovered that plants shout when feeling pain in the same way animals do.
questions.explanation: 본문 하단에서 전문가들은 식물이 고통으로 울부짖는다고 생각하지 않으며, 이러한 반응은 생존을 위한 무조건적 반응(knee-jerk survival actions)일 가능성이 높다고 언급하고 있으므로 5번은 일치하지 않습니다.
options_translation: ① 식물은 인간과 같은 방식은 아니지만 소통하는 방법을 가지고 있다.
② 일부 식물은 불만을 나타내기 위해 향기를 방출한다.
③ 특정 식물은 소리를 내지만, 이는 인간이 들을 수 없는 주파수에서 발생한다.
④ 연구원들은 스트레스를 받은 식물이 고주파의 클릭 소리를 낸다는 것을 발견했다.
⑤ 전문가들은 식물이 동물과 같은 방식으로 고통을 느낄 때 소리를 지른다는 것을 발견했다.

questions.question: 13. 다음 글의 내용과 일치하는 것은?
questions.passage: The science we learn in grade school is a collection of facts about the natural world – the earth goes around the sun, DNA carries the information of an organism, and so on. Only when you start to learn the practice of science do you realize that each of these "facts" was hard won through a succession of logical inferences based upon many observations or experiments. The process of science is less about collecting pieces of knowledge than it is about increasing the uncertainties in what we know. Our uncertainties can be greater or lesser for any given piece of knowledge depending upon where we are in that process. For example, today we are quite certain of how an apple will fall from a tree, but our understanding of the turbulent fluid flow remains a work in progress after more than a century of effort.
options: ① Grade school science teaches us to deal with uncertainty in knowledge.
② All science facts are completely certain and never change.
③ Scientists no longer need to observe or experiment to find new facts.
④ Learning science means memorizing facts without thinking deeply.
⑤ We are more certain about falling apples than about turbulent fluid flow.
questions.explanation: 지문에 따르면 초등학교에서 배우는 과학은 단순한 사실의 집합으로 묘사되지만, 실제 과학 과정은 우리가 아는 것의 불확실성을 높이는 과정이라고 설명합니다. 필자는 예시를 통해 오늘날 우리가 사과가 나무에서 떨어지는 방식에 대해서는 상당히 확신하지만(quite certain), 난류 흐름에 대한 이해는 한 세기 이상의 노력 후에도 여전히 진행 중(work in progress)이라고 언급합니다. 따라서 '난류 흐름보다 사과가 떨어지는 것에 대해 더 확신한다'는 ⑤번이 내용과 일치합니다.
options_translation: 초등학교 과학은 우리에게 지식의 불확실성을 다루는 법을 가르친다.
모든 과학적 사실은 완전히 확실하며 절대 변하지 않는다.
과학자들은 새로운 사실을 찾기 위해 더 이상 관찰이나 실험을 할 필요가 없다.
과학을 배우는 것은 깊은 사고 없이 사실을 암기하는 것을 의미한다.
우리는 난류 흐름보다 사과가 떨어지는 것에 대해 더 확신한다.

questions.question: 14. 다음 글의 흐름으로 보아, 주어진 문장이 들어가기에 가장 적절한 곳은?
questions.passage: Let's assume that at least some animals are capable of thinking despite lacking a language. This doesn't necessarily mean that they possess concepts, for some forms of thought may be nonconceptual. (A) To do this, in principle she doesn't need a concept of branch nor a concept of tree. (B) It might be enough for her to have, for example, the ability to think in images; to make a mental map of the tree where she can imagine and try out different routes. (C) This doesn't imply that squirrels lack concepts, simply that they don't need them for this concrete form of thinking. (D) For us to be able to say that an animal has concepts, we have to show not just that she's capable of thinking, but also that she has certain specific abilities. (E)
questions.insertion_sentence: We can imagine, for instance, a squirrel who is planning how to get from the branch she's currently standing on to a branch from the tree in front.
questions.explanation: 주어진 문장은 언어 없이 사고할 수 있는 동물의 예시로 다람쥐가 나무 사이를 이동할 계획을 세우는 구체적인 상황을 제시합니다. (A) 뒤에 이어지는 문장에서 'To do this(이것을 하기 위해)'라는 지칭어가 다람쥐가 목표 지점까지 이동하는 행위를 가리키며, 그 뒤의 문장들 역시 다람쥐의 사례를 계속 설명하고 있으므로 주어진 문장은 (A) 위치에 들어가는 것이 가장 적절합니다.

questions.question: 15. 다음 글의 흐름으로 보아, 주어진 문장이 들어가기에 가장 적절한 곳은?
questions.passage: I decided to travel from his hometown, Waituhi, to Murupara with my grandfather to help complete the important whakapapa. (A) For some time, my grandfather had been busy writing down the village genealogy, known as the whakapapa. (B) The whakapapa had been in his old house. (C) But then came the night of the fire, which ran through the house and destroyed our past. (D) Trying to find a way out of the ashes of the past, Nani began to write the whakapapa again with his shaky hands, thanks to her. (E) He chanted the names of the ancestors, joining the past to the present once more.
questions.insertion_sentence: Suddenly, everything we knew was gone and Nani Tama, in despair, went to stay with his daughter, my Auntie Hiraina.
questions.explanation: (C) 문장에서 화재로 인해 집과 과거(whakapapa)가 소실되었다는 내용이 나옵니다. 주어진 문장은 그 화재의 결과로 모든 것이 사라져 절망한 Nani Tama가 딸의 집으로 옮겨가게 된 상황을 구체적으로 설명합니다. 그리고 (D) 문장의 'thanks to her(그녀 덕분에)'에서 'her'는 주어진 문장에 언급된 딸(Auntie Hiraina)을 지칭하므로, 주어진 문장은 (D) 위치에 들어오는 것이 논리적으로 타당합니다.

questions.question: 16. 다음 글의 요지로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Piaget put the same amount of water into two different glasses: a tall narrow glass and a wide glass, then asked kids to compare two glasses. Kids younger than six or seven usually say that the tall narrow glass now holds more water, because the level is higher. And when they are ready, they figure out the conservation of volume for themselves just by playing with cups of water. Piaget argued that children's understanding of morality is like their understanding of those water glasses: we can't say that it is innate or kids learn it directly from adults. Rather, it is self-constructed as kids play with other kids. Taking turns in a game is like pouring water back and forth between glasses. Once kids have reached the age of five or six, then playing games and working things out together will help them learn about fairness far more effectively than any teaching from adults.
options: ① Moral understanding is determined by genetic factors.
② Peer conflict has a negative impact on children's development.
③ Physical experiments have nothing to do with moral development.
④ Morality develops more effectively through peer interaction than through adult instruction.
⑤ Children learn all important concepts through formal education rather than experience.
questions.explanation: Piaget는 아이들의 도덕성 이해가 타고난 것이거나 어른에게 직접 배우는 것이 아니라, 아이들이 다른 아이들과 상호작용하며 '스스로 구성하는 것(self-constructed)'이라고 주장합니다. 특히 게임을 하며 순서를 지키고 문제를 함께 해결하는 과정이 어른의 가르침보다 공정성을 배우는 데 훨씬 효과적이라고 했으므로, 정답은 ④번입니다.
options_translation: 도덕적 이해는 유전적 요인에 의해 결정된다.
또래 갈등은 아동의 발달에 부정적인 영향을 미친다.
물리적 실험은 도덕성 발달과 아무런 관련이 없다.
도덕성은 성인의 훈육보다 또래 간의 상호작용을 통해 더 효과적으로 발달한다.
아이들은 경험보다는 정규 교육을 통해 모든 중요한 개념을 배운다.

questions.question: 19. 다음 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Promotion deals with consumer psychology. We can't force people to think one way or another, and the clever marketer knows that promotion is used to provide information in the most clear, honest, and simple fashion possible. By doing so, the possibility of increasing sales go up. Gone are the days when promotions were done in order to fool the consumer into purchasing something. The long-term effect of getting a consumer to buy something they did not really want or need wasn't good. In fact, consumers fooled once can do damage to sales as they relate their experience to others. Instead, marketers now know that their goal is to identify the consumers who are most likely to appreciate a good or service, and to promote that good or service in a way that makes the value clear to the consumer. Therefore, marketers ______________________.
options: ① take advantage of goods for fooling consumers
② impose a specific way of thinking on psychologists
③ have to rely on old-fashioned marketing strategies
④ find out the potential consumers and the strategies to access them
⑤ have to reach the top of the sales with reasonably priced products in the market
questions.explanation: 오늘날의 마케터들은 소비자를 속이는 것이 장기적으로 손해라는 것을 알고 있으며, 대신 제품의 가치를 알아줄 가능성이 높은 소비자를 식별하여 그들에게 가치를 명확히 전달하는 것을 목표로 합니다. 따라서 마케터는 잠재적 소비자를 찾아내고 그들에게 접근할 전략을 찾아야 한다는 ④번이 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: 소비자를 속이기 위해 제품을 이용한다
심리학자들에게 특정한 사고방식을 강요한다
구식 마케팅 전략에 의존해야 한다
잠재적 소비자와 그들에게 접근할 전략을 찾아낸다
시장에서 합리적인 가격의 제품으로 매출 정점에 도달해야 한다

questions.question: 20. 다음 글의 내용을 한 문장으로 요약하고자 할 때, 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Our skin conducts electricity more or less efficiently, depending on our emotions. We know that when we're emotionally stimulated – stressed, sad, any intense emotion, really – our bodies sweat a tiny bit, so little we might not even notice. And when those tiny drops of sweat appear, our skin gets more electrically conductive. This change in sweat gland activity happens completely without your conscious mind having much say in the matter. If you feel emotionally intense, you're going to notice an increase in sweat gland activity. This is particularly useful from a scientific viewpoint, because it allows us to put an objective value on a subjective state of mind. We can actually measure your emotional state by tracking how your body subconsciously sweats, by running a bit of electricity through your skin. We can then turn the subjective, subconscious experience of emotional intensity into an objective number by figuring out how good your skin gets at transferring an electrical current.
questions.summary_sentence: To sum up, our emotional state affects how much we subconsciously sweat, which changes our skin's ability to (A)_______________, allowing people to measure emotions (B)_______________.
options: ① (A) conduct a survey / (B) creatively
② (A) conduct electricity / (B) objectively
③ (A) conduct a survey / (B) logically
④ (A) conduct electricity / (B) subjectively
⑤ (A) continue to track / (B) neutrally
questions.explanation: 글의 내용은 감정 상태에 따라 무의식적으로 발생하는 땀이 피부의 전기 전도성(ability to conduct electricity)을 변화시키며, 이를 통해 주관적인 감정 상태를 수치화하여 '객관적으로(objectively)' 측정할 수 있다는 것입니다.
options_translation: (A) 설문 조사를 실시하다 / (B) 창의적으로
(A) 전기를 전도하다 / (B) 객관적으로
(A) 설문 조사를 실시하다 / (B) 논리적으로
(A) 전기를 전도하다 / (B) 주관적으로
(A) 계속해서 추적하다 / (B) 중립적으로

questions.question: 21. 주어진 글 다음에 이어질 글의 순서로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: When I arrived at Auntie's place, I was shocked to see how thin Nani Tama was. "Look, Nani," I said. "I'm not taking you anywhere. You could die on me!" Nani looked at me in anger. "You want me to die here in this room? Looking at these four walls? When the whakapapa is not yet finished?"
ordered_passages:
(A) We traveled all night, mostly in silence, listening to Nani chanting in the darkness. Sometimes, he burst into a song that he had taught Auntie. They sang together, lifting up their voices to send the song flying like a bird through the sky.
(B) Just before noon, we arrived in Murupara and met an old man. All afternoon and evening, two old men sat together, recalling missing names that had sang together with Auntie. When it was done, the old man whispered, "Goodbye, friend." Crying, they pressed their noses together in farewell.
(C) The old man held on tightly to the side of the bed and cried out as he stood up. Every slow, painful step hurt him, but he tried to walk. I could not help but carry him to the car, and we set off with Auntie.
questions.explanation: 제시된 글에서 Nani Tama가 whakapapa(족보)를 끝내야 한다며 나가기를 고집하는 상황이 나옵니다. (C)에서 노인이 침대 옆을 잡고 일어나 고통스러운 발걸음을 떼고 결국 차에 타서 출발하는 장면이 이어집니다. (A)에서 밤새도록 여행하며 Nani와 아주머니가 노래를 부르는 여정의 모습이 묘사되고, 마지막으로 (B)에서 정오 직전에 Murupara에 도착하여 다른 노인을 만나 작업을 마무리하고 작별 인사를 나누는 것으로 끝나는 것이 자연스럽습니다.

questions.question: 1. 윗글의 내용과 일치하지 않는 것은?
questions.passage:
This interactive map shows the location of every single tree in the city's parks and along its roads. It uses colors and symbols to indicate each tree's age and genus. Also, users can click on a tree to find out its species and even send it an email. At first, the "Email this tree" function had a specific purpose. It ⓐ<u>was designed</u> to allow people to easily inform council workers about trees that were damaged or in poor health.
After the map was posted online, ⓑ<u>unexpected something</u> happened. The trees started receiving thousands of emails, but many of them were not reports about damage or poor health. Instead, they were love letters, poems, greetings, and messages ⓒ<u>expressed</u> appreciation for the trees. One person wrote, "I love the way the light shines on your leaves and how your branches hang so low. It is almost like you are trying to hug me." The tree mail phenomenon quickly spread, and people all over the world started ⓓ<u>to send</u> messages.
A message that was sent all the way from Russia said, "When I read about this wonderful project, I was inspired to write to you, even though I live thousands of miles away. Although we are separated by a great distance, we share the same planet and the same environment. Perhaps one day we will meet. Until then, I hope you can stay healthy and strong."
The global popularity of the tree mail phenomenon reminds us ⓔ<u>what</u> we are all connected to nature, and we are all involved in building a more sustainable world. Without collective action from people across the globe, we would have little hope of saving our planet for future generations.
options: ① 세계 여러 지역의 사람들이 나무들에게 메시지를 보내기 시작했다.
② 그 상호작용형 지도는 사용자들이 도시 내 나무들의 위치, 나이, 그리고 속을 볼 수 있게 해준다.
③ “이 나무에게 이메일 보내기” 기능은 원래 사람들이 나무에게 사랑의 메시지를 보내도록 만들어졌다.
④ 한 러시아인이 멀리 떨어져 있음에도 불구하고 연결되어 있는 느낌이 든다고 메시지를 보냈다.
⑤ 나무에게 보내는 편지 현상은 자연과 지속 가능성의 중요성에 대한 인식을 높이는 데 도움을 주었다.

② 그 상호작용형 지도는 사용자들이 도시 내 나무들의 위치, 나이, 그리고 속을 볼 수 있게 해준다.
③ “이 나무에게 이메일 보내기” 기능은 원래 사람들이 나무에게 사랑의 메시지를 보내도록 만들어졌다.
④ 한 러시아인이 멀리 떨어져 있음에도 불구하고 연결되어 있는 느낌이 든다고 메시지를 보냈다.

questions.question: 3. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 어법상 옳은 것은?
questions.passage: Of all the challenges I chose for myself, the third one made me ⓐ<u>the most nervously</u>: changing my hairstyle. For many years, I had kept the same hairstyle because I had been worried about my forehead. I ⓑ<u>had always thought</u> it was large, and I didn't want to draw attention to it. Since I was feeling confident after the first two challenges, I went to a hair salon and talked to the stylist. He listened to my concerns and helped me ⓒ<u>finding</u> a shorter hairstyle that suited me. The next day at school, my classmates were a bit surprised. But overall, the reactions were positive. I realized that trying a different look wasn't as ⓓ<u>more difficult</u> as I thought it would be. In fact, it made me feel more confident about myself. I didn't expect that stepping out of my comfort zone would have such a positive effect on how I felt about ⓔ<u>me</u>.
options: ① ⓐ
② ⓑ
③ ⓒ
④ ⓓ
⑤ ⓔ
questions.explanation:
① ␖ the most nervous: make 동사의 목적격 보어 자리이므로 형용사가 와야 합니다.

③ ␘ find 또는 to find: help 동사의 목적격 보어로 원형부정사나 to부정사가 와야 합니다.
④ ␙ difficult: as ~ as 옠급 비교 구문이므로 비교급을 쓰지 않습니다.

questions.question: 4. 다음 글의 내용과 일치하지 않는 것은?
questions.passage: Plato argued that when you see something that strikes you as beautiful, you are really just seeing a partial reflection of true beauty, just as a painting or even a photograph only captures part of the real thing. True beauty, or what Plato calls the Form of Beauty, has no particular color, shape, or size. Rather, it is an abstract idea, like the number five. You can make drawings of the number five in blue or red ink, big or small, but the number five itself is none of those things. It has no physical form. Think of the idea of a triangle, for example. Although it has no particular color or size, it somehow lies within each and every triangle you see. Plato thought the same was true of beauty. The Form of Beauty somehow lies within each and every beautiful thing you see.
options: ① Each beautiful thing we see contains some part of the ideal Form of Beauty.
② Photographs show only a partial reflection of the complete essence of beauty.
③ What we perceive as beauty in the world is just an imperfect version of ideal beauty.
④ Every triangle we draw is a complete and perfect representation of the idea of a triangle.
⑤ Beauty exists as a concept that cannot be completely shown through any material object, just like a number.
questions.explanation: 본문에서 삼각형의 관념은 물체적인 형태가 없으며, 옰가 볼 수 읈는 개별적인 삼각형들에 내재해 읈다고 했습니다. 그리고 옰가 그리는 것은 그저 불완전한 투영일 봄이며, 완벽한 재현이 아닙니다.
options_translation: ① 옰가 볼 수 읈는 각각의 아름다운 것은 이상적인 '아름다움의 형상'의 일부를 포함한다.
② 사진은 아름다움의 완전한 불질의 부분적인 투영만을 보여준다.
③ 옰가 세사에서 아름다움으로 인식하는 것은 이상적인 아름다움의 불완전한 버전일 봄이다.
④ 옰가 그리는 모든 삼각형은 삼각형의 관념에 대한 완전하고 완벽한 표현이다.
⑤ 아름다움은 숫자와 마찬가지로 어떤 물질적인 대상을 통해서도 완전히 보여질 수 없는 개념으로 존재한다.

questions.question: 5. 다음 글의 흐름으로 보아, 주어진 문장이 들어가기에 가장 적절한 곳은?
questions.passage: Plants can communicate, although not in the same way we do. Some express their discontent through scents. You know that smell that hangs in the air after you've mowed the lawn? (A) Yeah, that's actually an SOS. Some plants use sound. Yes, sound, though at a frequency that we can't hear. (B) Researchers experimented with plants and microphones to see if they could record any trouble calls. (C) They found that plants produce a high-frequency clicking noise when stressed and can make different sounds for different stressors. (D) The sound a plant makes when it's not getting watered differs from the one it'll make when a leaf is cut. (E) However, it's worth noting that experts don't think plants are crying out in pain. It's more likely that these reactions are knee-jerk survival actions. Plants are living organisms, and their main objective is to survive. Scents and sounds are their tools for defending against things that might harm them.
questions.insertion_sentence: That's why researchers have begun to pay close attention to how plants respond to stress using various sensory mechanisms.
questions.explanation: 주어진 문장은 연구자들이 왜 식물이 다양한 감각 기제를 사용하여 스트레스에 어떻게 반응하는지에 주의를 기울이기 시작했는지에 대한 이유(That's why)를 설명하고 있습니다. (B) 앞 문장에서 식물이 우리가 들을 수 없는 주파수의 소리를 사용한다는 점이 언급되었으므로, 연구자들이 마이크를 사용하여 실험을 시작하게 된 계기로 연결되는 것이 가장 적절합니다.

questions.question: 6. 다음 글에서 필자가 주장하는 바로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Routines enable athletes to evaluate competition conditions. For example, bouncing a ball in a volleyball service routine supplies the server with information about the ball, the floor, and the state of her muscles. This information can then be used to properly prepare for her serve. Routines also enable athletes to adjust and fine-tune their preparations based on those evaluations or in pursuit of a particular competitive goal. This adaptation can involve adjustment to the conditions, rivals, competitive situation, or internal influences that can affect performance. Just like adjusting a race-car engine to the conditions of the track, air temperature, and weather, routines adjust all competitive components to achieve proper performance.
options: ① 루틴은 경기 중 선수의 집중력을 향상시키는 심리적 전략으로만 사용된다.
② 루틴은 선수들이 경기 조건을 파악하고 필요한 준비는 조정하는 데 도움을 준다.
③ 루틴은 선수의 신체적 한계를 극복하기 위해 훈련에서 강조되어야 하는 요소이다.
④ 루틴은 외부 조건에 영향을 받지 않도록 경기 전 상태를 완벽히 통제하는 방식이다.
⑤ 루틴은 운동선수에게 신체적 피로를 줄이고, 경쟁자들과의 긴장을 완화하는 데 도움을 준다.
questions.explanation: 본문은 루틴이 선수들로 하여금 경기 조건을 평가하게 하고(evaluate competition conditions), 그 평가를 바탕으로 준비 과정을 조정하고 미세하게 조정(adjust and fine-tune their preparations)할 수 있게 해준다고 설명하고 있습니다. 따라서 답은 2번입니다.

questions.question: 7. 다음 글의 제목으로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: The rise of air-conditioning accelerated the construction of sealed boxes, where the building's only airflow is through the filtered ducts of the air-conditioning unit. It doesn't have to be this way. Look at any old building in a hot climate, whether it's in Sicily or Marrakesh or Tehran. Architects understood the importance of shade, airflow, light colors. They oriented buildings to capture cool breezes and block the worst heat of the afternoon. They built with thick walls and white roofs and transoms over doors to encourage airflow. Anyone who has ever spent a few minutes in a mudbrick house in Tucson, or walked on the narrow streets of old Seville, knows how well these construction methods work. But all this wisdom about how to deal with heat, accumulated over centuries of practical experience, is all too often ignored. In this sense, air-conditioning is not just a technology of personal comfort; it is also a technology of forgetting.
options: ① The Myth of Cool: Why Traditional Buildings Were Never Truly Comfortable
② From Mudbrick to Metal: Evolution of Urban Building Techniques
③ Ancient Wisdom in Modern Design: The Return of Traditional Cooling
④ The Rise of Architecture: How Modern Buildings Reflect Efficiency and Elegance
⑤ The Comfort Trap: How Air Conditioning Made Us Forget Smarter Ways to Stay Cool
questions.explanation: 지문은 현대의 에어컨 보급이 과거의 지혜로운 냉방 건축 방식들을 잊게 만들었다는 내용을 담고 있습니다. 에어컨은 단순히 개인의 안락함을 위한 기술일 뿐만 아니라 과거의 지혜를 망각하게 하는 기술(technology of forgetting)이라는 점이 핵심입니다. 따라서 '안락함의 함정: 에어컨이 어떻게 우리를 시원하게 지내는 더 똑똑한 방법들을 잊게 만들었는가'를 의미하는 5번이 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 시원함의 신화: 전통적인 건물들이 결코 진정으로 편안하지 않았던 이유
② 진흙 벽돌에서 금속까지: 도시 건축 기술의 진화
③ 현대 디자인 속의 고대 지혜: 전통적 냉방의 회귀
④ 건축의 부상: 현대 건축물이 효율성과 우아함을 반영하는 방식
⑤ 안락함의 함정: 에어컨이 어떻게 우리로 하여금 시원함을 유지하는 더 똑똑한 방법들을 잊게 만들었는가

questions.question: 9. 다음 글의 주제로 가장 적절한 것은? [3.1점]
questions.passage: It is difficult for any of us to maintain a constant level of attention throughout our working day. We all have body rhythms characterised by peaks and valleys of energy and alertness. You will achieve more, and feel confident as a benefit, if you schedule your most demanding tasks at times when you are best able to cope with them. If you haven′t thought about energy peaks before, take a few days to observe yourself. Try to note the times when you are at your best. We are all different. For some, the peak will come first thing in the morning, but for others it may take a while to warm up.
options: ① Multitasking as a strategy for consistent productivíty
② The benefits of fixed work schedules for better focus
③ How environmental interruptions affect work efficiency
④ Maximizing efficiency by prioritizing morning productivity
⑤ Improving productivity by adjusting work schedules to personal energy rhythms
questions.explanation: 이 글은 사람마다 에너지와 집중력이 높은 시간대가 다르므로, 자신의 신체 리듬(에너지 정점)을 파악하여 가장 어려운 업무를 그 시간에 배치함으로써 생산성을 높일 수 있다는 내용을 담고 있습니다. 따라서 주제는 '개인적인 에너지 리듬에 업무 일정을 맞춤으로써 생산성 향상하기'가 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 일관된 생산성을 위한 전략으로서의 멀티태스킹
② 더 나은 집중력을 위한 고정된 업무 일정의 이점
③ 환경적 방해가 업무 효율성에 미치는 영향
④ 아침 생산성을 우선시함으로써 효율성 극대화하기
⑤ 개인의 에너지 리듬에 업무 일정을 조정하여 생산성 향상하기

questions.question: 10. 다음 글에서 전체 흐름과 관계없는 문장은? [3.0점]
questions.passage: As the social and economic situation of countries got better, wage levels and working conditions improved. Gradually people were given more time off. ⓐAt the same time, forms of transport improved and it became faster and cheaper to get to places. England's industrial revolution led to many of these changes. ⓑRailways, in the nineteenth century, opened up now famous seaside resorts such as Blackpool and Brighton. ⓒThe invention of the steam engine played a crucial role in the mechanization of agriculture. ⓓWith the railways came many large hotels. In Canada, for example, the new coast-to-coast railway system made possible the building of such famous hotels as Banff Springs and Chateau Lake Louise in the Rockies. ⓔLater, the arrival of air transport opened up more of the world and led to tourism growth.
questions.explanation: 이 글은 산업 혁명 이후 경제적 여건의 개선과 교통 수단의 발달(철도, 항공 등)이 관광 및 호텔 산업의 성장을 이끌었다는 내용입니다. 반면 ③(ⓒ)번 문장은 증기 기관 발명이 '농업의 기계화'에 기여했다는 내용으로, 전체적인 관광 산업의 발전이라는 흐름과 무관합니다.

questions.question: 11. 다음 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은? [3.3점]
questions.passage: As the parent of a gifted child, you need to be aware of a certain common parent trap. Of course you are a proud parent, and you should be. While it is very easy to talk nonstop about your little genius and his or her remarkable behavior, this can be very stressful on your child. It is extremely important to limit your bragging behavior to your very close friends, or your parents. Gifted children feel pressured when their parents show them off too much. This behavior creates expectations that they may not be able to live up to, and also creates a false sense of self for your child. You want your child to be who they are, not who they seem to be as defined by their incredible achievements. If not, you could end up with a driven perfectionist child or perhaps a drop­out, or worse.
options: ① excessive praise can place harmful pressure on gifted children
② students ought to be motivated to surpass their innate abilities
③ feeling proud of a kid's performance leads to future accomplishments
④ parents need to drive their talented kids to reach their maximum capacity
⑤ talking about a child's achievements with others helps build closer family bonds
questions.explanation: 이 글은 부모가 영재 자녀의 성취에 대해 지나치게 자랑하는 것이 아이에게 과도한 부담감을 주고, 부응하기 어려운 기대치를 형성하여 아이의 자아 정체성에 부정적인 영향을 줄 수 있음을 경고합니다. 따라서 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 '과도한 칭찬이 영재 아동에게 해로운 압박을 줄 수 있다'는 요약이 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 과도한 칭찬은 영재 아동에게 해로운 압박을 줄 수 있다
② 학생들은 자신의 타고난 능력을 뛰어넘도록 동기부여 되어야 한다
③ 아이의 성취에 대해 자부심을 느끼는 것은 미래의 성취로 이어진다
④ 부모는 재능 있는 아이들이 최대 역량에 도달하도록 몰아붙여야 한다
⑤ 타인과 아이의 성취에 대해 이야기하는 것은 더 긴밀한 가족 유대를 형성하도록 돕는다

questions.question: 12. 다음 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Let's assume that at least some animals are capable of thinking despite lacking a language. This doesn't necessarily mean that they possess concepts, for some forms of thought may be nonconceptual. We can imagine, for instance, a squirrel who is planning how to get from the branch she's currently standing on to a branch from the tree in front. To do this, in principle she doesn't need a concept of branch nor a concept of tree. It might be enough for her to have, for example, the ability to think in images; to make a mental map of the tree where she can imagine and try out different routes. This doesn't imply that squirrels lack concepts, simply that they don't need them for this concrete form of thinking. _______________________________________________________.
options: ① Thus, mental imagery must be regarded as a primitive version of verbal reasoning
② Consequently, we should treat all animal actions as instinctive rather than thoughtful
③ As a result, any form of problem-solving by animals should be interpreted as conceptual reasoning
④ In contrast, language use is the only reliable evidence of higher-order cognition in nonhuman species
⑤ Therefore, the presence of planning behavior alone cannot confirm the possession of conceptual thinking
questions.explanation: 이 글은 동물이 언어가 없어도 사고할 수 있으며, 특히 이미지를 통한 사고와 같은 비개념적 사고가 가능함을 설명하고 있습니다. 다람쥐가 나무 사이를 이동하는 계획을 세울 때 '나무'나 '가지'라는 언어적 개념이 반드시 필요한 것은 아니라는 예시를 통해, 계획하는 행동이 있다고 해서 반드시 '개념적 사고'를 소유하고 있다고 단정할 수는 없다는 결론이 도출됩니다.
options_translation: ① 따라서 정신적 이미지는 언어적 추론의 원시적 버전으로 간주되어야 한다
② 결과적으로 우리는 모든 동물의 행동을 사려 깊은 것이기보다 본능적인 것으로 취급해야 한다
③ 결과적으로 동물의 어떤 형태의 문제 해결도 개념적 추론으로 해석되어야 한다
④ 대조적으로 언어 사용은 인간 이외의 종에서 고차원적 인지의 유일한 신뢰할 수 있는 증거이다
⑤ 그러므로 계획하는 행동의 존재만으로는 개념적 사고의 소유를 확인할 수 없다

questions.question: 15. 주어진 글 다음에 이어질 글의 순서로 가장 적절한 것은? [2.9점]
questions.passage: Believe it or not, trees in Melbourne, Australia receive emails like this all the time.
ordered_passages: (A) The loss of canopy cover is a major threat to urban environments because it raises temperatures. Higher temperatures in cities can be dangerous for residents, as they increase the risk of heat exhaustion. They also lead to a rise in the use of air-conditioning. This speeds up climate change by increasing energy consumption and greenhouse gas emissions.

(B) How is it possible that trees have email addresses? And why are people sending them messages? The story behind these emails begins with Melbourne's Urban Forest Strategy plan, a response to Australia's millennium drought.

(C) This drought lasted from the late 1990s to 2010. By the time it ended, 40 percent of the city's 77,000 trees were in a state of declining health. Furthermore, the overall number of trees was decreasing. As a result, the amount of shade provided by trees within the city, also known as canopy cover, decreased.
questions.explanation: 멜버른의 나무들이 이메일을 받는다는 도입부의 내용 뒤에, 어떻게 그것이 가능한지 의문을 제기하며 그 배경이 되는 멜버른의 도시 숲 전략을 소개하는 (B)가 이어집니다. 그 다음 (B)에서 언급된 가뭄(millennium drought)에 대한 구체적인 설명과 그 영향으로 인한 수관 덮개(canopy cover)의 감소를 설명하는 (C)가 연결되고, 마지막으로 수관 덮개 감소가 도시 환경과 기후 변화에 미치는 위험성을 경고하는 (A)로 마무리되는 것이 가장 자연스럽습니다.

questions.question: 18. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은? [3.1점]
questions.passage: Some countries have proposed tougher guidelines for determining brain death when transplantation ― transferring organs to others ― is under consideration. In several European countries, there are legal requirements which specify that a whole team of doctors must agree over the diagnosis of death in the case of a potential donor. The reason for these strict regulations for diagnosing brain death in potential organ donors is, no doubt, to ease public fears of a premature diagnosis of brain death for the purpose of obtaining organs. But it is questionable whether these requirements reduce public suspicions as much as they create them. They certainly maintain mistaken beliefs that diagnosing brain death is an unreliable process lacking precision. As a matter of consistency, at least, criteria for diagnosing the deaths of organ donors should be exactly the same as for those for whom immediate burial or cremation is intended.
options: ① ⓐ
② ⓑ
③ ⓒ
④ ⓓ
⑤ ⓔ
questions.explanation: 지문은 뇌사 판정 기준이 장기 기증을 목적으로 할 때 더 엄격해지는 이유와 그 영향을 설명하고 있습니다. 문맥상 이러한 엄격한 요구 사항들이 오히려 대중의 의심을 불러일으킬 수 있다는 점을 시사하고 있으므로, 뇌사 진단이 정밀함이 부족하고 신뢰할 수 없다는 잘못된 믿음을 '강화(maintain 또는 reinforce)'할 수 있다는 흐름이 되어야 합니다. 따라서 '바로잡다(correct)'는 문맥상 적절하지 않습니다.

questions.question: 19. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은? [올림포스 기출1 Unit3 4번]
questions.passage: We are always teaching our children something by our words and our actions. They learn from seeing. They learn from hearing and from overhearing. Children share the values of their parents about the most important things in life. Our priorities and principles and our examples of good behavior can teach our children to take the high road when other roads look tempting. Remember that children do not learn the values that make up strong character simply by being told about them. They learn by seeing the people around them act on and uphold those values in their daily lives. Therefore show your child good examples of life by your action. In our daily lives, we can show our children that we respect others. We can show them our compassion and concern when others are suffering, and our own self-discipline, courage and honesty as we make difficult decisions.
options: ① share
② tempting
③ strong
④ uphold
⑤ negotiated
questions.explanation: ⑤번 자리에 'negotiated(협상된)'와 같은 단어가 오는 것은 문맥상 어색합니다. 부모가 말로 하는 가르침과 실제 행동이 일치하지 않으면 아이들은 그 가치들을 제대로 배우지 못하고, 부모의 가르침이 '훼손(undermined)'되거나 '약화'되기 쉽기 때문입니다. 따라서 문맥상 아이들이 부모의 가르침을 의심하게 만든다는 의미의 단어가 적절합니다.

questions.question: 20. 다음 글의 내용을 한 문장으로 요약하고자 한다. 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은? [올림포스 기출1 Unit11 1번]
questions.passage: From an organizational viewpoint, one of the most fascinating examples of how any organization may contain many different types of culture is to recognize the functional operations of different departments within the organization. The varying departments and divisions within an organization will inevitably view any given situation from their own biased and prejudiced perspective. A department and its members will acquire “tunnel vision” which disallows them to see things as others see them. The very structure of organizations can create conflict. The choice of whether the structure is “mechanistic” or “organic” can have a profound influence on conflict management. A mechanistic structure has a vertical hierarchy with many rules, many procedures, and many levels of management involved in decision making. Organic structures are more horizontal in nature, where decision making is less centralized and spread across the plane of the organization.
questions.summary_sentence: Conflicts within organizations can result not only from the (A)____________ perspectives of individual departments but also from the (B)____________ in how authority and decision-making are organized.
options: ① departmental ... similarities
② shared ... limitations
③ individual ... changes
④ unique ... differences
⑤ universal ... variations

questions.question: 23. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ⓐ~ⓖ 문장 중 어색한 부분 4개를 모두 찾아 바르게 작성하시오. (단, 반드시 고칠 부분의 문장 번호와 함께 바르게 고친 답을 함께 쓴 것만 정답으로 인정함. 4개 이상의 답을 쓸 경우, 앞에서 4개의 답만 인정) (ex: ⓗis → are)
questions.passage:
Ever since I was a child, I ⓐ<u>was</u> always afraid of water. So I have never enjoyed water activities or felt comfortable while ⓑ<u>doing</u> them. For the second challenge, I decided to try to overcome this discomfort. However, I wasn't sure ⓒ<u>what</u> to do at first. One day, I came across a video clip of my cousin surfing at an indoor pool on social media. It looked fun, and I liked the fact that it ⓓ<u>was taken place</u> in a shallow pool, not in the ocean. I messaged my cousin about it. She assured me that it wasn't too hard, so I signed up for a beginner course.
At the beginning of the lesson, it was hard just ⓔ<u>to stand up</u> on the board. After some help from the instructor, however, I learned how to balance properly and even managed to surf a few waves! It gave me such a rush of excitement. Being in the water wasn't as ⓕ<u>badly</u> as I had thought. While the experience didn't completely change my mind about water sports, it ⓖ<u>do helped</u> me discover my sense of adventure.
questions.answer:
ⓐ was → have been
ⓓ was taken place → took place
ⓕ badly → bad
ⓖ do helped → did help
questions.explanation:
ⓐ 'Ever since' 구문은 현재까지 이어지는 상태를 나타내므로 현재완료 시제(have been)가 적절합니다.
ⓓ 'take place'는 자동사로 수동태가 불가능하므로 능동태(took place)로 고쳐야 합니다.
ⓕ 형용사 'bad'는 보어 역할을 해야 하며, 'as ~ as' 원급 비교에서도 'was' 동사의 보어인 형용사가 필요합니다.
ⓖ 과거 시제의 동사를 강조할 때는 'did + 동사원형'을 사용하므로 'did help'가 적절합니다.

questions.passage: Assuming gene editing in humans proves to be safe and effective, it might seem logical, even preferable, to correct disease-causing mutations at the earliest possible stage of life, before harmful genes begin causing serious problems. Yet once it becomes possible to transform an embryo's mutated genes into "normal" ones, there will certainly be temptations to upgrade normal genes to superior versions. Should we begin editing genes in unborn children to lower their lifetime risk of heart disease or cancer? What about giving unborn children beneficial features, like greater strength and increased mental abilities, or changing physical characteristics, like eye and hair color? The pursuit for perfection seems almost natural to human nature, but if we start down this slippery slope, we may not like where we end up.

questions.question: 3. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은? [3.1점]
questions.passage: Plato argued that when you see something that strikes you as beautiful, you are not really seeing a whole reflection of true beauty, just as a painting or even a photograph only captures ⓐ<u>part</u> of the real thing. True beauty, or what Plato calls the Form of Beauty, has no particular color, shape, or size. Rather, it is an ⓑ<u>abstract</u> idea, like the number five. You can make drawings of the number five in blue or red ink, big or small, but the number five itself is none of those things. It has no ⓒ<u>specific</u> form. Think of the idea of a triangle, for example. Although it has ⓓ<u>particular</u> color or size, it somehow lies within each and every triangle you see. Plato thought the ⓔ<u>same</u> was true of beauty. The Form of Beauty somehow lies within each and every beautiful thing you see.
questions.explanation: 문맥상 플라톤의 '미의 형상(The Form of Beauty)'이나 '삼각형의 관념(idea of a triangle)'은 특정한 색깔이나 크기를 갖지 않는 추상적인 개념입니다. 따라서 ⓓ는 'particular(특별한/특정한)'가 아니라 'no particular' 또는 'no'와 어울리는 표현이 되어야 하거나, 문맥상 '특정한 색상이나 크기가 없음에도 불구하고(Although it has no particular color...)'라는 의미가 되어야 자연스럽습니다. 지문 원문상으로는 'no particular color'가 쓰여야 하므로 ⓓ가 적절하지 않습니다.

questions.question: 4. 다음 글의 목적으로 가장 적절한 것은? [2.8점]
questions.passage:
In the course of trying to solve a problem with an invention, you may encounter a brick wall of resistance when you try to think your way logically through the problem. Such logical thinking is a linear type of process, which uses our reasoning skills. This works fine when we're operating in the area of what we know or have experienced. However, when we need to deal with new information, ideas, and viewpoints, linear thinking will often come up short. On the other hand, creativity by definition involves the application of new information to old problems and the conception of new viewpoints and ideas. For this you will be most effective if you learn to operate in a nonlinear manner; that is, use your creative brain. Stated differently, if you think in a linear manner, you'll tend to be conservative and keep coming up with techniques which are already known. This, of course, is just what you don't want.
*linear: 선형의 **conservative: 보수적인
options: ① To describe the history of invention processes
② To prove that creativity is unrelated to logical thinking
③ To explain how linear thinking solves problems with inventions
④ To argue that logical reasoning is always effective for new ideas
⑤ To encourage the use of nonlinear thinking for creative problem-solving

questions.question: 6. 다음 글의 제목으로 가장 적절한 것은? [3.1점]
questions.passage: Promotion deals with consumer psychology. We can't force people to think one way or another, and the clever marketer knows that promotion is used to provide information in the most clear, honest, and simple fashion possible. By doing so, the possibility of increasing sales goes up. Gone are the days when promotions were done in order to fool the consumer into purchasing something. The long-term effect of getting a consumer to buy something they did not really want or need wasn't good. In fact, consumers fooled once can do damage to sales as they relate their experience to others. Instead, marketers now know that their goal is to identify the consumers who are most likely to appreciate a good or service, and to promote that good or service in a way that makes the value clear to the consumer. Therefore, marketers must know where the potential consumers are, and how to reach them.
options: ① The Challenges of Identifying Potential Consumers
② The Role of Consumer Feedback in Product Development
③ The Negative Effects of Advertising on Consumer Psychology

questions.question: 7. 다음 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은? [3.0점]
questions.passage: The science we learn in grade school is a collection of certainties about the natural world – the earth goes around the sun, DNA carries the information of an organism, and so on. Only when you start to learn the practice of science do you realize that each of these "facts" was hard won through a succession of logical inferences based upon many observations or experiments. The process of science is less about collecting pieces of knowledge than it is about reducing the ___________ in what we know. Our ___________ can be greater or lesser for any given piece of knowledge depending upon where we are in that process – today we are quite certain of how an apple will fall from a tree, but our understanding of the turbulent fluid flow remains a work in progress after more than a century of effort.
options: ① change
② uncertainties
③ verifications
④ probabilities
⑤ possibilities

questions.passage: The rise of air-conditioning accelerated the construction of sealed boxes, where the building's only airflow is through the filtered ducts of the air-conditioning unit. It doesn't have to be this way. Look at any old building in a hot climate, whether it's in Sicily or Marrakesh or Tehran. Architects understood the importance of shade, airflow, light colors. They oriented buildings to capture cool breezes and block the worst heat of the afternoon. They built with thick walls and white roofs and transoms over doors to encourage airflow. Anyone who has ever spent a few minutes in a mudbrick house in Tucson, or walked on the narrow streets of old Seville, knows how well these construction methods work. questions.question: 9. 다음 글의 요지로 가장 적절한 것은? [2.9점]
questions.passage:
Piaget put the same amount of water into two different glasses: a tall narrow glass and a wide glass, then asked kids to compare two glasses. Kids younger than six or seven usually say that the tall narrow glass now holds more water, because the level is higher. And when they are ready, they figure out the conservation of volume for themselves just by playing with cups of water. Piaget argued that children's understanding of morality is like their understanding of those water glasses: we can't say that it is innate or kids learn it directly from adults. Rather, it is self-constructed as kids play with other kids. Taking turns in a game is like pouring water back and forth between glasses. Once kids have reached the age of five or six, then playing games and working things out together will help them learn about fairness far more effectively than any teaching from adults.
*innate: 타고난 **conservation: 보존
options: ① Playing with water glasses teaches children the concept of fairness.
② Children learn morality directly from adults through direct teaching.
③ Morality in children is an innate trait that does not require social interaction.
④ Young children accurately understand volume conservation before the age of six.
⑤ Children's understanding of fairness develops through play with peers rather than adult instruction.

Some researchers view spoken languages as incomplete devices for ①<u>capturing</u> precise differences. They think numbers represent the most neutral language of description. However, when our language of description is ②<u>changed</u> to numbers, we do not move toward greater accuracy. questions.question: 15. 주어진 글 다음에 이어질 글의 순서로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: As you listen to your child in an emotional moment, be aware that sharing simple observations usually works better than asking questions to get a conversation rolling.
ordered_passages: (A) Maybe she's feeling sad about her parents' arguments, or because she feels overtired, or she's worried about a piano recital. But she may or may not be able to explain any of this. And even when she does come up with an answer, she might be worried that the answer is not good enough to justify the feeling.
(B) You may ask your child "Why do you feel sad?" and she may not have a clue. As a child, she may not have an answer on the tip of her tongue.

(C) Under these circumstances, a series of questions can just make a child silent. It's better to simply reflect what you notice. You can say, "You seem a little tired today," or, "I noticed that you frowned when I mentioned the recital," and wait for her response.

questions.question: 17. 다음 글의 내용과 일치하지 않는 것은?
questions.passage: Plants can communicate, although not in the same way we do. Some express their discontent through scents. You know that smell that hangs in the air after you've mowed the lawn? Yeah, that's actually an SOS. Some plants use sound. Yes, sound, though at a frequency that we can't hear. Researchers experimented with plants and microphones to see if they could record any trouble calls. They found that plants produce a high-frequency clicking noise when stressed and can make different sounds for different stressors. The sound a plant makes when it's not getting watered differs from the one it'll make when a leaf is cut. However, it's worth noting that experts don't think plants are crying out in pain. It's more likely that these reactions are knee-jerk survival actions. Plants are living organisms, and their main objective is to survive. Scents and sounds are their tools for defending against things that might harm them.

④ 식물의 소리는 사람 귀에는 들리지 않는다.

questions.question: 21. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?
questions.passage: Improving your gestural communication involves more than just knowing when to nod or shake hands. It's about using gestures to ⓐ<u>complement</u> your spoken messages, adding layers of meaning to your words. Openhanded gestures, for example, can indicate honesty, creating an atmosphere of ⓑ<u>trust</u>. You invite openness and collaboration when you speak with your palms facing up. This simple yet powerful gesture can make others feel more comfortable and willing to ⓒ<u>engage</u> in" conversation. But be careful of the trap of overgesturing. Too many hand movements can ⓓ<u>distract</u> from your message, drawing attention away from your words. questions.explanation: 문맥상 몸짓은 말하는 단어를 무색하게(overshadow) 만들지 않으면서 단어의 의미를 뒷받침하거나 강조해야 한다는 흐름입니다. 'understate(축소해서 말하다/절제하다)'는 뒤의 'not overshadow(무색하게 만들지 않다)'와 대조를 이루며 균형을 강조하는 맥락에서, 단어를 강화하거나 강조한다는 의미의 'accentuate'나 'support' 등의 표현이 적절합니다. 특히 마지막 문장에서 몸짓과 단어 사이의 조화를 강조하고 있으므로 'understate'는 적절하지 않습니다.

questions.question: 22. 다음 글의 흐름으로 보아, 주어진 문장이 들어가기에 가장 적절한 곳은?
questions.passage: Cartilage is a strong, flexible connective tissue that protects your joints and bones. questions.question: 23. 다음 글의 내용을 한 문장으로 요약하고자 한다. 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Our skin conducts electricity more or less efficiently, depending on our emotions. We know that when we're emotionally stimulated – stressed, sad, any intense emotion, really – our bodies sweat a tiny bit, so little we might not even notice. And when those tiny drops of sweat appear, our skin gets more electrically conductive. This change in sweat gland activity happens completely without your conscious mind having much say in the matter. If you feel emotionally intense, you're going to notice an increase in sweat gland activity. This is particularly useful from a scientific viewpoint, because it allows us to put an objective value on a subjective state of mind. We can actually do this by tracking how your body subconsciously sweats, by running a bit of electricity through your skin. We can then turn the subjective, subconscious experience of emotional intensity into an objective number by figuring out how good your skin gets at transferring an electrical current.

questions.question: 27. 다음 광에서 밑줄 친 This가 가리키는 것으로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Sunlight offers numerous health benefits. In small amounts, it boosts vitamin D levels, makes the bones stronger, prevents diseases, and heals skin conditions. questions.question: 28. 다음 광에서 필자의 주장을 가장 젘 나타낸 것은?
questions.passage:
Let's assume that at least some animals are capable of thinking despite lacking a language. This doesn't necessarily mean that they possess concepts, for some forms of thought may be nonconceptual. We can imagine, for instance, a squirrel who is planning how to get from the branch she's currently standing on to a branch from the tree in front. To do this, in principle she doesn't need a concept of branch nor a concept of tree. It might be enough for her to have, for example, the ability to think in images; to make a mental map of the tree where she can imagine and try out different routes. This doesn't imply that squirrels lack concepts, simply that they don't need them for this concrete form of thinking. For us to be able to say that an animal has concepts, we have to show not just that she's capable of thinking, but also that she has certain specific. abilities.
