questions.question: 29. 다음 글에서 전체 흐름과 관계없는 문장은?
questions.passage: Teenage life on social media might seem fun and easy, but being a real teenager presents its own set of challenges, both big and small. So why can some people handle tough times and become stronger while others remain unchanged and helpless? The answer lies in resilience – the ability to adapt to challenging experiences, such as unexpected events or personal difficulties. The good news is that humans can recover from pressure and hardship and you can develop this skill. ⓐ<u>However, having resilience does not mean you will never feel stressed or anxious</u>; it is perfectly normal to feel down every now and then. ⓑ<u>Resilience will not prevent problems, but it will help you face and overcome them</u>. ⓒ<u>Think of it like building your body's immune system</u>. ⓓ<u>Just as you need to be exposed to germs to build immunity, you must experience difficulties to build resilience</u>. ⓔ<u>In other words, resilience is innate and can be improved by practicing</u>. In simple terms, resilience is not about being emotionless: Resilience means you experience. You feel. You fail. You hurt. You fall. But you keep going. It is like working out to build your muscles; it takes time and effort to enhance your resilience.
questions.explanation: 이 글은 회복탄력성(resilience)이 고난과 경험을 통해 길러질 수 있는 기술임을 강조하고 있습니다. 하지만 ⓔ문장은 회복탄력성이 '타고나는 것(innate)'이라고 언급하며, 연습을 통해 향상될 수 있다는 뒷부분의 설명과 모순될 뿐만 아니라, 노력을 통해 발달시킬 수 있다는 전체 글의 흐름과도 어긋납니다.

questions.question: 30. 다음 글의 내용과 일치하지 않는 것은?
questions.passage: A performance routine is a set of mental and physical behaviors that help prepare an athlete for peak performance. Routines enable athletes to evaluate competition conditions. For example, bouncing a ball in a volleyball service routine supplies the server with information about the ball, the floor, and the state of her muscles. This information can then be used to properly prepare for her serve. Routines also enable athletes to adjust and fine-tune their preparations based on those evaluations or in pursuit of a particular competitive goal. This adaptation can involve adjustment to the conditions, rivals, competitive situation, or internal influences that can affect performance. Just like adjusting a race-car engine to the conditions of the track, air temperature, and weather, routines adjust all competitive components to achieve proper performance.
options: ① Volleyball servers benefit from routines like bouncing the ball.
② Athletes use routines to gather useful information before competing.
③ Performance routines include both mental and physical preparation.
④ Adjusting routines helps athletes perform better under various circumstances.
⑤ Race-car engines are not affected by changes in weather or track conditions.
questions.explanation: 지문의 마지막 부분에서 루틴을 경주용 자동차 엔진을 트랙의 상태, 기온, 날씨에 맞춰 조정하는 것에 비유하고 있습니다. 이는 엔진이 이러한 외부 조건에 영향을 받기 때문에 조정을 하는 것임을 의미하므로, 영향을 받지 않는다는 5번 선택지는 지문의 내용과 일치하지 않습니다.
options_translation: ① 배구 서버들은 공을 튀기는 것과 같은 루틴으로부터 이점을 얻는다.
② 운동선수들은 경기 전에 유용한 정보를 수집하기 위해 루틴을 사용한다.
③ 수행 루틴은 정신적 및 신체적 준비를 모두 포함한다.
④ 루틴을 조정하는 것은 운동선수들이 다양한 상황에서 더 잘 수행하도록 돕는다.
⑤ 경주용 자동차 엔진은 날씨나 트랙 조건의 변화에 영향을 받지 않는다.

questions.question: 1. 다음 글의 요지로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Every species has certain climatic requirements ─ what degree of heat or cold it can endure, for example. When the climate changes, the places that satisfy those requirements change, too. Species are forced to follow. All creatures are capable. of some degree of movement. Even creatures that appear immobile, like trees and barnacles, are capable of dispersal at some stage of their life ─ as a seed, in the case of the tree, or as a larva, in the case of the barnacle. A creature must get from the place it is born ─ often occupied by its parent ─ to a place where it can survive, grow, and reproduce. From fossils, scientists know that even creatures like trees moved with surprising speed during past periods of climate change.
options: ① 기후 변화를 막기 위해 통제와 규제의 범위를 확장해야 한다.
② 기후 변화가 빠르게 진행되어 일부 종은 새로운 환경에 적응하지 못하고 있다.
③ 기후 변화가 생물의 다양성에 미치는 영향을 분석한 연구 사례를 수집해야 한다.
④ 모든 종은 기후 변화에 따라 생존과 번식을 위해 적합한 환경을 찾아 이동하는 능력을 지니고 있다.
⑤ 기후 변화에도 불구하고 대부분의 생물은 본래의 서식지를 떠나지 않고 그대로 머물러 생존한다.
questions.explanation: 이 글은 모든 종이 기후 변화에 대응하여 생존과 번식을 위해 적합한 장소로 이동하는 능력을 갖추고 있다는 점을 강조하고 있습니다. 심지어 나무나 따개비처럼 움직이지 않는 것처럼 보이는 생물들도 씨앗이나 유충 단계에서 이동(분산)이 가능하다는 예시를 통해 모든 생물종의 이동 능력을 설명하고 있으므로 정답은 ④번입니다.

questions.question: 2. 다음 글의 주제로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: A group of psychologists studied individuals with severe mental illness who experienced weekly group music therapy, including singing familiar songs and composing original songs. The results showed that the group music therapy improved the quality of participants' life, with those participating in a greater number of sessions experiencing the greatest benefits. Focusing on singing, another group of psychologists reviewed articles on the efficacy of group singing as a mental health treatment for individuals living with a mental health condition in a community setting. The findings showed that, when people with mental health conditions participated in a choir, their mental health and wellbeing significantly improved. Group singing provided enjoyment, improved emotional states, developed a sense of belonging and enhanced self-confidence.
options: ① qualities required to be a choir member
② benefits of listening to music on mental health
③ significance of choir music in religious ceremonies
④ how musical instruments influence brain development
⑤ effectiveness of music therapy on enhancement of quality of life
questions.explanation: 이 글은 그룹 음악 치료, 특히 합창이나 노래 부르기가 정신 질환을 앓고 있는 사람들의 정신 건강, 웰빙, 삶의 질을 향상시키며 즐거움과 자신감을 북돋아 준다는 연구 결과를 소개하고 있습니다. 따라서 주제로 가장 적절한 것은 ⑤번 '삶의 질 향상에 대한 음악 치료의 효과'입니다.
options_translation: ① 합창단원이 되기 위해 필요한 자질
② 음악 감상이 정신 건강에 주는 이점
③ 종교 의식에서 합창 음악의 중요성
④ 악기가 뇌 발달에 미치는 영향
⑤ 삶의 질 향상에 대한 음악 치료의 효과

questions.question: 3. 다음 글의 주제로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Magic is what we all wish for to happen in our life. Do you love the movie Cinderella like me? Well, in real life, you can also create magic. Here's the trick. Write down all the real-time challenges that you face and deal with. Just change the challenge statement into positive statements. Let me give you an example here. If you struggle with getting up early in the morning, then write a positive statement such as "I get up early in the morning at 5:00 am every day." Once you write these statements, get ready to witness magic and confidence. You will be surprised that just by writing these statements, there is a shift in the way you think and act. Suddenly you feel more powerful and positive.
options: ① cultivating discipline through behavioral modification techniques
② embracing a forward-looking mindset to reinterpret personal struggles
③ the role of positive thinking in assessing everyday obstacles
④ the magic of transforming challenges into opportunities
⑤ the power of affirmative statements in overcoming challenges
questions.explanation: 이 글은 현재 겪고 있는 어려움이나 도전 과제들을 긍정적인 진술(긍정 확언)로 바꾸어 적음으로써 생각과 행동의 변화를 이끌어내고 자신감을 얻을 수 있다는 내용을 담고 있습니다. 따라서 주제는 ⑤번 '도전을 극복하는 데 있어 긍정적 확언의 힘'이 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 행동 수정 기법을 통한 규율 배양
② 개인적 고충을 재해석하기 위한 미래 지향적 사고방식 수용
③ 일상의 장애물을 평가하는 데 있어 긍정적 사고의 역할
④ 도전을 기회로 바꾸는 마법
⑤ 도전을 극복하는 데 있어 긍정적 확언의 힘

questions.question: 4. 다음 글의 제목으로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: As a teen, you may feel like an adult, but your brain is still growing. In your brain, there is a part that is responsible for solving problems and controlling your emotions. In your teen years, this part is still in development. The changes in your brain lead you toward independence, social engagement, and creativity. At the same time, however, you may feel confused about who you are. You may also be more sensitive to unfairness. Furthermore, your body is flowing with hormones. This significantly affects your mood. The combination of these factors intensifies your strong emotions.
options: ① How Hormones Influence Teenage Creativity
② The Role of Peer Pressure in Shaping Teen Behavior
③ Why Are Teenagers More Sensitive to Unfairness?
④ The Impact of Teenage Brain Development on Emotions
⑤ The Journey to Independence: How Teens Develop Their Identity
questions.explanation: 이 글은 십 대의 뇌가 여전히 발달 중이며, 특히 감정을 조절하고 문제를 해결하는 부위의 발달 과정과 호르몬의 영향이 십 대의 정서와 감정 변화에 큰 영향을 미친다는 점을 설명하고 있습니다. 따라서 제목으로는 ④번 '십 대의 뇌 발달이 감정에 미치는 영향'이 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 호르몬이 십 대의 창의성에 미치는 영향
② 십 대의 행동을 형성하는 데 있어 또래 압력의 역할
③ 왜 십 대들은 불공정함에 더 민감한가?
④ 십 대의 뇌 발달이 감정에 미치는 영향
⑤ 독립을 향한 여정: 십 대들이 정체성을 형성하는 방법

questions.question: 5. 다음 글에 드러난 소년의 심경 변화로 가장 적절한 것은? [2.9점]
questions.passage:
One day, the boy's father called him over and said, "You have been a good boy and have earned a holiday. Take the day off, but try to learn something important." The boy thanked his father and kissed his mother; then he took a piece of bread, and left to find the house with the golden windows.
His journey was enjoyable. His bare feet made marks in the white sand. When he looked back, the footprints seemed to be following him and keeping him company. His shadow, too, stayed beside him and would dance or run with him as he pleased. Before long, he felt hungry, so he sat down by a stream to eat his bread and drink the clear water. He scattered the remaining pieces of bread for the birds, as his mother had taught him to do, and went on his way.
After a long time, he came to a high green hill, and the house was at the top. It seemed that the shutters were closed, for he could not see the golden windows. He came up to the house and was disappointed to find that the windows were made of clear glass, like any others, and there was no gold anywhere around them.
options: ① excited 	 →	discouraged
② confident	 →	confused
③ regretful	 →	frightened
④ indifferent	 →	annoyed
⑤ jealous	 →	relieved
questions.explanation: 소년은 아버지로부터 휴일을 얻어 황금 창문이 있는 집을 찾아 떠나는 과정에서 즐거움을 느끼며 기대에 부풀어 있었으나(excited), 막상 도착한 집의 창문이 평범한 유리창이고 황금이 없다는 것을 알고 실망하게 됩니다(discouraged).
options_translation: ① 흥분한/들뜬 → 낙담한/실망한
② 자신감 있는 → 혼란스러운
③ 후회하는 → 겁먹은
④ 무관심한 → 짜증난
⑤ 질투하는 → 안도하는

questions.question: 6. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 지칭하는 대상이 나머지 넷과 다른 하나는? [2.6점]
questions.passage: Marilyn and her three-year-old daughter, Sarah, took a trip to the beach, where Sarah built ⓐ<u>her</u> first sandcastle. Moments later, an enormous wave destroyed Sarah's castle. In response to the loss of ⓑ<u>her</u> sandcastle, tears streamed down Sarah's cheeks and ⓒ<u>her</u> heart was broken. ⓓ<u>She</u> ran to Marilyn, saying she would never build a sandcastle again. Marilyn said, "Part of the joy of building a sandcastle is that, in the end, we give it as a gift to the ocean." Sarah loved ⓔ<u>her</u> idea and responded with enthusiasm to the idea of building another castle ─ this time, even closer to the water so the ocean would get its gift sooner!
options: ① ⓐ
② ⓑ
③ ⓒ
④ ⓓ
⑤ ⓔ
questions.explanation: ⓐ, ⓑ, ⓒ, ⓓ는 모두 딸인 Sarah를 지칭하지만, ⓔ는 모래성을 바다에 주는 선물이라고 말한 엄마 Marilyn의 아이디어를 의미하므로 ⓔ는 Marilyn을 가리킵니다.

questions.question: 7. 다음 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은? [2.9점]
questions.passage: Crop rotation is the process in which farmers change the crops they grow in their fields in a special order. For example, if a farmer has three fields, he or she may grow carrots in the first field, green beans in the second, and tomatoes in the third. The next year, green beans will be in the first field, tomatoes in the second field, and carrots will be in the third. In year three, the crops will rotate again. By the fourth year, the crops will go back to their original order. Each crop __________ the soil for the next crop. This type of farming is sustainable because the soil stays healthy.
options: ① depletes
② enriches
③ damages
④ weakens
⑤ destroys
questions.explanation: 윤작(Crop rotation)은 토양을 건강하게 유지하게 해주는 지속 가능한 농법입니다. 따라서 각 작물이 다음 작물을 위해 토양을 '풍요롭게 한다(enriches)'는 표현이 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 고갈시키다
② 풍요롭게 하다
③ 손상시키다
④ 약화시키다
⑤ 파괴하다

questions.question: 8. 다음 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은? [2.9점]
questions.passage: In many sports, people realized the difficulties and even impossibilities of young children participating fully in many adult sport environments. They found the road to success for young children is unlikely if they play on adult fields, courts or arenas with equipment that is too large, too heavy or too fast for them to handle while trying to compete in adult-style competition. Common sense has prevailed: different sports have ____________________. As examples, baseball has T ball, football. has flag football and junior soccer uses a smaller and lighter ball and (sometimes) a smaller field. All have junior competitive structures where children play for shorter time periods and often in smaller teams. In a similar way, tennis has adapted the court areas, balls and rackets to make them more appropriate for children under 10. The adaptations are progressive and relate to the age of the child.
options: ① focused on only adults
② made adaptations for children
③ kept the same rules for all ages
④ made sports more difficult for children
⑤ let children take part in adult sport environments
questions.explanation: 어린이들이 성인용 경기장이나 장비를 사용하는 것의 어려움을 인식하여, 야구의 T볼, 플래그 풋볼, 주니어 축구, 테니스 등 여러 스포츠에서 어린이들에게 맞게 장비나 경기장을 조정한 사례들을 설명하고 있습니다. 따라서 '어린이들을 위한 조정을 해왔다(made adaptations for children)'가 빈칸에 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 성인들에게만 집중해왔다
② 어린이들을 위해 조정해왔다
③ 모든 연령대에 동일한 규칙을 유지해왔다
④ 스포츠를 어린이들에게 더 어렵게 만들었다
⑤ 어린이들이 성인 스포츠 환경에 참여하게 했다

questions.question: 9. 다음 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은? [2.9점]
questions.passage: After our application was accepted, I was eager to make a good first impression with our investors. To achieve this, I made a video about my grandparents and their jam. In the video, I highlighted how the strawberries were grown without using chemicals. I also included clips of my grandparents. In the clips, they were making the jam with all-natural ingredients. Finally, I explained where I wanted to put the new greenhouse and asked for support. After some editing, I _________________________. It didn't take long for word of our campaign to spread.
options: ① shared the video online to reach more people
② limited the audience to close family and friends
③ removed the video because of negative feedback
④ decided to postpone the project due to lack of funds
⑤ hired real professionals to make a new promotional video
questions.explanation: 지문에서 필자는 투자자들에게 좋은 인상을 주기 위해 조부모님과 잼에 관한 영상을 제작했고, 편집을 마친 후 캠페인 소문이 퍼지기 시작했다는 맥락이 이어집니다. 따라서 빈칸에는 캠페인 홍보를 위해 영상을 온라인에 공유했다는 내용이 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 더 많은 사람들에게 도달하기 위해 온라인에 영상을 공유했다
② 시청자를 가까운 가족과 친구들로 제한했다
③ 부정적인 피드백 때문에 영상을 삭제했다
④ 자금 부족으로 인해 프로젝트를 연기하기로 결정했다
⑤ 새로운 홍보 영상을 만들기 위해 실제 전문가를 고용했다

questions.question: 10. 다음 글에서 밑줄 친 the perfect solution이 의미하는 바로 가장 적절한 것은? [2.9점]
questions.passage: My grandparents sell their delicious organic jam at the local market every weekend. I went to help them last weekend. However, they had already sold all of their jam! They didn't have enough strawberries to make any more jam. That evening, I sat by the window and stared out at the empty field behind their house. Suddenly, I got an idea. The field would be the perfect place for a larger greenhouse. Then they could grow more strawberries! I immediately 'started searching for a way, and I found <u>the perfect solution</u>. I would start a crowdfunding campaign!
options: ① searching for new markets to sell jam
② starting a new business selling strawberries directly
③ gathering financial support to construct a greenhouse
④ establishing a larger greenhouse to supply strawberries to local grocery stores
⑤ increasing the price of the jam to make up for the shortage of strawberries
questions.explanation: 필자는 조부모님이 더 많은 딸기를 재배할 수 있도록 더 큰 온실을 지을 장소를 찾았고, 이를 실현하기 위해 크라우드펀딩 캠페인을 시작하기로 합니다. 따라서 '완벽한 해결책'은 온실 건설을 위한 재정적 지원을 모으는 것을 의미합니다.
options_translation: ① 잼을 팔기 위한 새로운 시장을 찾는 것
② 딸기를 직접 판매하는 새로운 사업을 시작하는 것
③ 온실을 짓기 위한 재정적 지원을 모으는 것
④ 지역 식료품점에 딸기를 공급하기 위해 더 큰 온실을 설립하는 것
⑤ 딸기 부족을 보충하기 위해 잼의 가격을 올리는 것

questions.question: 11. 다음 글의 내용과 일치하지 않는 것은? [2.9점]
questions.passage: The mind has parts that are known as the conscious mind and the subconscious mind. The subconscious mind is very fast to act and doesn't deal with emotions. It deals with memories of your responses to life, your memories and recognition. However, the conscious mind is the one that you have more control over. You think. You can choose whether to carry on a thought or to add emotion to it and this is the part of your mind that lets you down frequently because ─ fueled by emotions ─ you make the wrong decisions time and time again. When your judgment is clouded by emotions, this puts in biases and all kinds of other negativities that hold you back. Scared of spiders? Scared of the dark? There are reasons for all of these fears, but they originate in the conscious mind. They only become real fears when the subconscious mind records your reactions.
options: ① 마음은 의식적 마음과 잠재의식적 마음이라고 알려진 부분으로 구성된다.
② 잠재의식적 마음은 매우 빠르게 작동하며 감정을 다루지 않는다.

questions.question: 15. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?
questions.passage: A number of research studies have shown how experts in a field often experience ⓐ<u>difficulties</u> when introducing newcomers to that field. For example, in a genuine training situation, Dr Pamela Hinds found that people expert in using mobile phones were remarkably ⓑ<u>more</u> accurate than novice phone users in judging how long it takes people to learn to use the phones. Experts can become ⓒ<u>insensitive</u> to how hard a task is for the beginner, an effect referred to as the 'curse of knowledge'. Dr Hinds was able to show that as people acquired the skill, they then began to ⓓ<u>underestimate</u> the level of difficulty of that skill. questions.question: 16. 다음 글에서 전체 흐름과 관계없는 문장은?
questions.passage: The tongue was mapped into separate areas where certain tastes were registered: sweetness at the tip, sourness on the sides, and bitterness at the back of the mouth. questions.question: 22. 다음 글의 흐름으로 보아, 주어진 문장이 들어가기에 가장 적절한 곳은?
questions.passage: The rate of speed at which one is traveling will greatly determine the ability to process detail in the environment. questions.question: 24. 주어진 글에 이어질 글의 순서로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Although the girl's clothes were modest, her hair was golden like the windows he had seen, and her eyes were blue like the sky. She led the boy around the farm and showed him her black calf, which had a white star on its forehead. The boy told her about his own calf at home, which was red like a chestnut and had white feet. Feeling as if they were now friends, the boy asked her about the golden windows. The girl said she knew all about them, only he had mistaken which house had them.
ordered_passages:
(A)
"You have come the wrong way!" she said. "Come with me. I will show you the house with the golden windows, and then you will see for yourself." The girl told him that the golden windows could only be seen at sunset. "Yes, I know that!" said the boy. They went to a high place and saw a house with windows of gold and diamond on a hill far away, just as the boy had seen before. And when they looked again, the boy recognized that it was his own home.

(B)
It was dark when the boy finally returned home, but the windows of his home were shining with the light of lamps just like he had seen from the top of the hill. His family welcomed him warmly. "Have you had a good day?" asked his mother. Yes, the boy had had a very good day. "And have you learned anything?" asked his father. "Yes!" said the boy. "I have learned that our house has windows of gold and diamond."

(C)
Then he told the girl that he must go; and he gave her his best pebble, a white one with a red stripe that he had carried with him for a year; and she gave him three horse-chestnuts, one red, one spotted, and one white. He promised to come again, but he did not tell her what he had learned. The girl stood in the light of the sunset and watched him go.

questions.question: 25. 주어진 글에 이어질 글의 순서로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Impostor syndrome was first described by a pair of American psychologists in the 1970s. They defined it as a feeling of being incompetent despite being successful. In other words, it makes people feel like they are not skilled or successful even though they obviously are. Impostor syndrome is quite common-even Albert Einstein is said to have suffered from it. No matter how successful they are, people with impostor syndrome experience constant self-doubt.
ordered_passages:
(A)
Remember that if you feel like an impostor, it means you have been successful in some way. Consider your accomplishments and be proud of them. Most importantly, don't let your fear of being found out hold you back. If you allow others to see the real you, your feelings of being an impostor will start to go away.

(B)
There are several factors that can contribute to impostor syndrome. The first is perfectionism. Some people falsely believe there is a perfect way of doing things. So they always feel like they are failing to meet their own standards. Another factor is external: high-pressure environments. Expectations to achieve more can cause successful people to undervalue their achievements and feel like they are not performing well enough. This can lead to feelings of guilt and incompetence.

(C)
So what are some ways to deal with these feelings? First, make sure you have a realistic understanding of your abilities. Write down your accomplishments, and then compare them with how you feel about yourself. Next, share your feelings with others. Irrational beliefs grow stronger when they remain hidden. Finally, take small steps. You don't need to always be perfect. Simply try to do things reasonably well, not perfectly.
questions.explanation: 주어진 글에서 가면 증후군(Impostor syndrome)의 정의와 현상을 설명합니다. (B)에서 이러한 증후군을 유발하는 여러 요인(완벽주의, 고압박 환경)을 제시합니다. (C)에서 이러한 감정에 대처하는 방법들(현실적 자기 파악, 공유하기 등)을 'So what are some ways...'로 질문하며 시작합니다. 마지막으로 (A)에서 대처법의 연장선으로 자신의 성공을 기억하고 자신을 있는 그대로 보여주라는 조언과 함께 글을 마무리합니다.

questions.question: 27. 다음 글의 내용을 한 문장으로 요약하고자 할 때, 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Consider the seemingly simple question How many senses are there? Around 2,370 years ago, Aristotle wrote that there are five, in both humans and animals ─ sight, hearing, smell, taste, and touch. However, according to the philosopher Fiona Macpherson, there are reasons to doubt it. For a start, Aristotle missed a few in humans: the perception of your own body which is different from touch and the sense of balance which has links to both touch and vision. Other animals have senses that are even harder to categorize. Many vertebrates have a different sense system for detecting odors. Some snakes can detect the body heat of their prey. These examples tell us that "senses cannot be clearly divided into a limited number of specific kinds," Macpherson wrote in The Senses. Instead of trying to push animal senses into Aristotelian buckets, we should study them for what they are.
questions.summary_sentence: Rather than fitting animal senses into (A)____________ categories, we should explore them in their unique forms, acknowledging the vast (B)____________ and complexity of senses.

② rigid — limitation
③ strict — diversity
④ loose — function
⑤ flexible — evolution

Those who have found deeper meaning in their careers find their days much more energizing and satisfying, and count their employment as one of their greatest sources of joy and pride. Those most satisfied with their work are also much more likely to be happier with their lives overall. questions.question: 2. 다음 글의 필자에 대한 설명과 일치하지 않는 것은?
questions.passage: In high school, everyone told me how talented an artist I was, so I dreamed of becoming an illustrator. In university, though, everyone seemed much more talented than me, and they all worked so hard that I felt small in comparison. I thought about giving up my dream of becoming an artist. Then one day, I happened to see a drawing I had won an award for from middle school on the kitchen wall. I was embarrassed because it wasn't very good. People say you shouldn't compare apples to oranges, and they're right. That's why it doesn't make sense to compare yourself to Internet personalities or even people in your real life. If you are going to compare yourself to anyone, the only fair comparison is "yesterday-you." Only you know where you started and how much effort you've put in. Everyone develops differently. I'm able to see now the drawing in the kitchen was full of mistakes that I no longer make. It is empowering to see how I have improved rather than to envy the success of others.

questions.passage: The mind has parts that are known as the conscious mind and the subconscious mind. The subconscious mind is very fast to act and doesn't deal with emotions. It deals with memories of your responses to life, your memories and recognition. However, the conscious mind is the one that you have more control over. You think. You can choose whether to carry on a thought or to add emotion to it and this is the part of your mind that lets you down frequently because – fueled by emotions – you make the wrong decisions time and time again. When your judgment is clouded by emotions, this puts in biases and all kinds of other negativities that hold you back. Scared of spiders? Scared of the dark? questions.question: 7. 다음 글의 요지로 가장 적절한 것은? [24년 3월 33번]
questions.passage:
One of the most striking characteristics of a sleeping animal or person is that they do not respond normally to environmental stimuli. If you open the eyelids of a sleeping mammal the eyes will not see normally – they are functionally blind. Some visual information apparently gets in, but it is not normally processed as it is shortened or weakened: same with the other sensing systems. Stimuli are registered but not processed normally and they fail to wake the individual. Perceptual disengagement probably serves the function of protecting sleep, so some authors do not count it as part of the definition of sleep itself. But as sleep would be impossible without it, it seems essential to its definition. Nevertheless, many animals (including humans) use the intermediate state of drowsiness to derive some benefits of sleep without total perceptual disengagement.
*stimuli: 자극 **disengagement: 이탈
***drowsiness: 졸음
options: ① Perceptual disengagement during sleep prevents all stimuli from being registered.
② Environmental stimuli are completely blocked during sleep due to visual information processing.
③ The main function of perceptual disengagement is to process visual information during sleep.
④ Sleep involves perceptual disengagement, which helps protect sleep from environmental stimuli.
⑤ Perceptual disengagement allows animals to process environmental stimuli more effectively during sleep.

questions.question: 8. 다음 글의 괄호 (A), (B), (C) 안에서 어법상 올바른 것끼리 짝지은 것은?

questions.question: 9. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 어법상 어색한 것은?

questions.question: 11. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?

questions.question: 12. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?
questions.passage: Plato argued that when you see something that strikes you as beautiful, you are really just seeing an ⓐ<u>entire</u> reflection of true beauty, just as a painting or even a photograph only captures part of the real thing. You can make drawings of the number five in blue or red ink, big or small, but the number five itself is none of those things. It has no ⓒ<u>physical</u> form. Think of the idea of a triangle, for example. Although it has no particular color or size, it somehow ⓓ<u>lies</u> within each and every triangle you see. options: ① ⓐ
② ⓑ

⑤ ⓔ

questions.question: 13. 다음 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage:
No two animals are alike. With this in mind, each healing session should ____________________________________. You will learn as you go; healing is a constant learning process.
*litter: (한 배에서 태어난) 새끼들
options: ① be adjusted to the animal's needs
② receive a consistent healing approach
③ follow a fixed method to avoid confusion
④ be based on general treatment principles

questions.explanation: 지문은 모든 동물이 서로 다르고, 같은 배에서 태어난 새끼들이라도 환경이나 질병의 종류(신체적 vs 정서적)에 따라 치유 세션에 다르게 반응한다고 설명하고 있습니다. 따라서 각 치유 세션은 각 동물의 개별적인 필요와 상황에 맞추어 조정되어야 한다는 내용이 빈칸에 들어가는 것이 가장 적절합니다.

questions.question: 14. 다음 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage:
What does it mean for a character to be a hero as opposed to a villain? questions.question: 15. 다음 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage:
The rate of speed at which one is traveling will greatly determine the ability to _______________________ in the environment. ② process detail
③ adapt to traffic

⑤ survive public transportation

questions.question: 16. 다음 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

questions.question: 17. 다음 글에서 전체 흐름과 관계없는 문장은?

questions.question: 18. 주어진 글 다음에 이어질 글의 순서로 가장 적절한 것은?

questions.question: 19. 다음 글의 내용을 한 문장으로 요약하고자 할 때, 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

questions.question: 20. 윗글의 요지로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Do you share your opinion in class discussions, or do you just stay silent and keep it to yourself? Like many of you, I often found myself in the second group. Then, after a particularly heated conversation in class, I asked myself. "What am I afraid of?" I was ⓑ<u>scared</u> that bad things would happen, but I never thought about good things. When I noticed others taking risks, I knew that I needed to do the ⓒ<u>same</u> in order to participate. questions.question: 22. 다음 글의 흐름으로 보아, 주어진 문장이 들어가기에 가장 적절한 곳은?
questions.passage: Piaget put the same amount of water into two different glasses: a tall narrow glass and a wide glass, then asked kids to compare two glasses. questions.question: 23. 윗글의 밑줄 친 문장 중 어법에 맞지 않는 단어를 하나 찾아 바르게 고치시오.

For her book Happiness at Work, researcher Jessica Pryce-Jones conducted a study of 3,000 workers in seventy-nine countries, finding that those who took greater s______________ from their work were 150 percent more likely to have a happier life overall.
questions.explanation: 밑줄 친 문장에서 'has conducted'라는 동사가 이미 존재하며, 'numerous workplace studies'를 수식하는 구조가 필요합니다. 'studies'가 뒤에 오는 'that' 절 이하의 내용을 보여주는 주체이므로 능동의 의미를 가진 현재분사 'showing'으로 고쳐야 합니다.

questions.question: 24. 윗글의 문맥상 빈칸에 들어갈 적절한 말을 한 단어로 쓰시오. (정답은 s로 시작함)
questions.passage: It would be hard to overstate how important meaningful work is to human beings – work that provides a sense of fulfillment and empowerment. Those who have found deeper meaning in their careers find their days much more energizing and satisfying, and count their employment as one of their greatest sources of joy and pride. <u>Sonya Lyubomirsky, professor of psychology at the University of California, has conducted numerous workplace studies show that when people are more fulfilled on the job, they not only produce higher quality work and a greater output, but also generally earn higher incomes</u>. Those most satisfied with their work are also much more likely to be happier with their lives overall. For her book Happiness at Work, researcher Jessica Pryce-Jones conducted a study of 3,000 workers in seventy-nine countries, finding that those who took greater s______________ from their work were 150 percent more likely to have a happier life overall.
questions.explanation: 글의 전체 맥락이 일에서 느끼는 성취감과 만족감이 삶의 행복에 미치는 영향에 대해 다루고 있으므로, '자신의 일로부터 더 큰 만족을 얻은 사람들'이라는 의미가 되도록 'satisfaction'이 들어가는 것이 적절합니다.

questions.question: 25. 다음 글의 내용을 한 문장으로 요약하고자 한다. 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 말을 본문에서 찾아 각각 한 단어로 쓰시오. (정답에 (A), (B)를 표시하지 않은 경우 오답 처리함)
questions.passage: In many sports, people realized the difficulties and even impossibilities of young children participating fully in many adult sport environments. They found the road to success for young children is unlikely if they play on adult fields, courts or arenas with equipment that is too large, too heavy or too fast for them to handle while trying to compete in adult-style competition. Common sense has prevailed: different sports have made adaptations for children. As examples, baseball has T ball, football has flag football and junior soccer uses a smaller and lighter ball and (sometimes) a smaller field. All have junior competitive structures where children play for shorter time periods and often in smaller teams. In a similar way, tennis has adapted the court areas, balls and rackets to make them more appropriate for children under 10. The adaptations are progressive and relate to the age of the child.
questions.summary_sentence: Many sports have (A)__________ their rules, equipment, and environments to create more (B)__________ conditions for children to participate and develop.
subjective_conditions: 본문에서 찾아 쓸 것
각각 한 단어로 쓸 것
questions.explanation: 본문에서 스포츠가 아이들을 위해 'adaptations(적응/개조)'를 만들었다는 내용과 테니스에서 코트 구역 등을 'adapted(개조했다)'는 내용이 나옵니다. 또한 이러한 변화가 아이들에게 더 'appropriate(적절한)' 환경을 제공한다고 설명하고 있습니다. 따라서 요약문의 (A)에는 동사 형태인 adapted가, (B)에는 형용사인 appropriate가 들어가는 것이 본문의 내용과 일치합니다.

questions.question: 26. 다음 글의 문맥상 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 적절한 말을 <보기>에서 찾아 각각 한 단어로 쓰시오. (정답에 (A), (B)를 표시하지 않은 경우 오답 처리함)
questions.passage: No respectable boss would say, "I make it a point to discourage my staff from speaking up, and I maintain a culture that prevents (A)___________ viewpoints from ever getting aired." If anything, most bosses even say that they are pro-dissent. This idea can be found throughout the series of conversations with corporate, university, and nonprofit leaders, published weekly in the business sections of newspapers. In the interviews, the featured leaders are asked about their management techniques, and regularly claim to continually encourage internal (B)___________ from more junior staffers. As Bot Pittman remarked in one of these conversations: "I want us to listen to these dissenters because they may intend to tell you why we can't do something, but if you listen hard, what they're really telling you is what you must do to get something done."
subjective_conditions: <보기>에서 찾아 쓸 것
각각 한 단어로 쓸 것
vocabulary_box: approving / disagreeing / disorienting / harmonizing / striking / approval / development / innovation / protest / support
questions.explanation: (A) 앞뒤 문맥상 상사들이 반대 의견(dissent)을 권장한다고 말한다는 내용이므로, '반대하는 관점'이 표현되는 것을 막는 문화를 유지하겠다고 말하지 않을 것임을 알 수 있습니다. 따라서 'disagreeing'이 적절합니다. (B) 하급자들로부터의 내부적 '반대/이의'를 장려한다는 맥락이 되어야 하므로 'protest'가 가장 적절합니다.

questions.question: 27. 다음 글의 문맥상 두 빈칸에 공통으로 들어갈 적절한 말을 한 단어로 쓰시오. (정답은 e로 시작함)
questions.passage:
Our skin conducts electricity more or less efficiently, depending on our emotions. We know that when we're emotionally stimulated – stressed, sad, any intense emotion, really – our bodies sweat a tiny bit, so little we might not even notice. And when those tiny drops of sweat appear, our skin gets more electrically conductive. This change in sweat gland activity happens completely without your conscious mind having much say in the matter. If you feel emotionally intense, you're going to notice an increase in sweat gland activity. This is particularly useful from a scientific viewpoint, because it allows us to put an objective value on a subjective state of mind. We can actuall measure your e___________ state by tracking how your body subconsciously sweats, by running a bit of electricity through your skin. We can then turn the subjective, subconscious experience of e___________ intensity into an objective number by figuring out how good your skin gets at transferring an electrical current.
*sweat gland: 땀샘
questions.explanation: 이 글은 인간의 피부 전도도가 감정적 자극(스트레스, 슬픔 등)에 의해 발생하는 미세한 땀의 양에 따라 변화한다는 과학적 사실을 설명하고 있습니다. 이러한 변화를 통해 주관적인 감정 상태를 객관적인 수치로 측정할 수 있다는 맥락이므로, 빈칸에 공통으로 들어갈 적절한 단어는 '감정적인'을 뜻하는 'emotional'입니다.

questions.question: 28. 다음 글의 문맥상 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 적절한 말을 본문에서 찾아 각각 한 단어로 쓰시오. (정답에 (A), (B)를 표시하지 않은 경우 오답 처리함)
questions.passage: As I worked through my second year into my third in college, I had more troubles balancing school and personal life. I was drowning in a sea of responsibilities, concerns, and anxieties, and that was when I read an article with a simple insight. The article advised me to draw two big circles, with myself in the center. The smaller circle is my circle of influence, and I have direct control over the things inside it: what I eat and drink. how I behave, or what I do after school. The bigger circle is called my circle of concern: things I worry about but have no direct control over. For example, I have no direct control over how my professor will react to my report, but I do have control over the amount of research I do for it. Believing that everything was in my circle of (A)___________ left me stressed out and constantly exhausted. By wasting less energy on my circle of (B)___________. I was able to invest more energy into things that mattered.
questions.explanation: 필자는 자신이 직접 통제할 수 있는 일(circle of influence)과 통제할 수 없지만 걱정되는 일(circle of concern)을 구분해야 한다는 깨달음을 얻었습니다. 모든 것이 자신의 영향력 범위 안에 있다고 믿는 것은 스트레스를 유발하므로 (A)에는 influence가 적절하며, 통제할 수 없는 걱정거리의 범위에 에너지를 낭비하지 않아야 한다는 맥락에서 (B)에는 concern이 들어가는 것이 적절합니다.

questions.question: 1. 다음 글의 주제로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: A common but incorrect assumption is that we are creatures of reason when, in fact, we are creatures of both reason and emotion. We cannot get by on reason alone since any reason always eventually leads to a feeling. Should I get a wholegrain cereal or a chocolate cereal? I can list all the reasons I want, but the reasons have to be based on something. For example, if my goal is to eat healthy, I can choose the wholegrain cereal, but what is my reason for wanting to be healthy? I can list more and more reasons such as wanting to live longer, spending more quality time with loved ones, etc., but what are the reasons for those reasons? You should be able to see by now that reasons are ultimately based on non-reason such as values, feelings, or emotions. These deep-seated values, feelings, and emotions we have are rarely a result of reasoning, but can certainly be influenced by reasoning. We have values, feelings, and emotions before we begin to reason and long before we begin to reason effectively.
options: ① concept of human beings as creatures of reason
② claim that emotions are superior to reason
③ strategies for making decisions about healthy eating habits
④ human ability to make decisions based solely on reason
⑤ interplay between reason and emotion in human decision-making
questions.explanation: 글의 핵심 내용은 인간이 이성적인 존재일 뿐만 아니라 감정적인 존재이며, 이성적인 판단의 근저에는 결국 가치나 감정 같은 비이성적인 요소가 자리 잡고 있다는 것입니다. 따라서 인간의 의사결정 과정에서 이성과 감정 사이의 상호작용을 다룬 5번이 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 이성적 생명체로서의 인간에 대한 개념
② 감정이 이성보다 우월하다는 주장
③ 건강한 식습관에 관한 결정을 내리기 위한 전략
④ 오직 이성에만 기반하여 결정을 내리는 인간의 능력
⑤ 인간의 의사결정에 있어서 이성과 감정 사이의 상호작용

questions.question: 2. 다음 글에서 밑줄 친 the furniture of our lives가 의미하는 바로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: We tend to overrate the impact of new technologies in part because older technologies have become absorbed into <u>the furniture of our lives</u>, so as to be almost invisible. Take the baby bottle. Here is a simple implement that has transformed a fundamental human experience for vast numbers of infants and mothers, yet it finds no place in our histories of technology. This technology might be thought of as a classic time-shifting device, as it enables mothers to exercise more control over the timing of feeding. It can also function to save time, as bottle feeding allows for someone else to substitute for the mother's time. Potentially, therefore, it has huge implications for the management of time in everyday life, yet it is entirely overlooked in discussions of high-speed society.
options: ① familiar things we no longer consider important
② everyday items to transform our future experiences
③ inventions that save our time by controlling us
④ tools for managing social planning and schedule
⑤ innovations that were overestimated in history
questions.explanation: 문맥상 'the furniture of our lives'는 새로운 기술에 비해 너무 익숙해져서 거의 보이지 않게 된 오래된 기술들을 의미합니다. 젖병의 예시를 통해 알 수 있듯, 생활의 일부가 되어 더 이상 중요하게 여기지 않거나 주목하지 않는 익숙한 것들을 뜻하므로 1번이 정답입니다.
options_translation: ① 우리가 더 이상 중요하게 생각하지 않는 익숙한 것들
② 우리의 미래 경험을 변화시킬 일상 용품들
③ 우리를 통제함으로써 시간을 절약해 주는 발명품들
④ 사회적 계획과 일정을 관리하기 위한 도구들
⑤ 역사 속에서 과대평가되었던 혁신들

questions.question: 4. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 어법상 어색한 것은?
questions.passage: There are reasons why science is not fully trusted and why healthy skepticism and critical thinking are essential. In spite of professional standards, claims of objectivity, and the peer review process, the conduct of science can be biased. All experts are not the same, nor ⓐ<u>do</u> they submit their work to the same scrutiny. Knowing the source of funding can be important in evaluating scientific claims. For example, the Harvard researchers who made claims in the late 1960s about the problems with dietary fat, leading the nation away from perceiving sugar as one of the main causes in health problems, ⓑ<u>were</u> funded in part by the sugar industry. The authors did not reveal their funding source to the New England Journal of Medicine, ⓒ<u>where</u> their influential article appeared. Their article shaped a generation of changes in eating patterns that appears to have helped higher use of sugar, now widely ⓓ<u>implicated</u> as a source of the rise in obesity and diabetes. Stories such as this one fuel suspicion – but also lead to further safeguards in the scientific process. Funding disclosures, although they were not required five decades ago, ⓔ<u>has</u> since been made compulsory.
questions.explanation: ⓔ의 주어는 'Funding disclosures'로 복수형입니다. 따라서 단수 동사인 'has'를 복수 동사인 'have'로 고쳐야 수 일치가 올바르게 이루어집니다.

questions.question: 6. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?
questions.passage: Commitment is the glue holding together characteristically human forms of social life. Commitments make individuals' behavior ⓐ<u>forecast</u> in the face of fluctuations in their desires and interests, thereby ⓑ<u>fostering</u> the planning and coordination of joint actions involving multiple agents. Moreover, commitments make people willing to perform actions that they would not otherwise perform. For example, a taxi driver picks up his clients and transports them to their ⓒ<u>unwanted</u> destination because they are committed to paying him afterwards for the service, and a construction worker performs her job every day because her employer has made a ⓓ<u>reliable</u> commitment to pay her at the end of the month. Indeed, the taxi driver and the construction worker are willing to accept money as payment only because a network of other agents (notably the central bank) is committed to taking different measures to ⓔ<u>sustain</u> the currency in question. Thus, social objects and institutions such as jobs, money, government, scientific collaborations and marriage depend for their origin and stability upon the credibility of commitments.
questions.explanation: 택시 기사가 승객을 목적지까지 데려다주는 이유는 승객이 원하는(wanted) 또는 지정한 목적지이기 때문입니다. 문맥상 승객이 서비스를 이용하고 대가를 지불하기로 약속된 상황이므로 '원치 않는(unwanted)'은 부적절하며, 승객이 의도한 목적지로 해석해야 자연스럽습니다. 또한 ⓐ의 forecast는 '예측 가능한(predictable)'의 의미로 쓰여야 하는데, 원문 변형 여부에 따라 문맥상 어색한 부분을 찾는 문제입니다.

questions.question: 8. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?
questions.passage: Since their start in the early 1950s U.S. television sitcoms have charted many of the social conflicts in U.S. society: civil rights, women's rights in the home and in the workplace, children's rights, immigration and multiculturalism, as well as ⓐ<u>developing</u> conceptions of the family. Each of these issues has been addressed through humour in a way that has helped to make more progressive values ⓑ<u>less</u> acceptable than previously. Often a character, usually someone marked as a bigot, resisted one or more of these developments and was then made to appear ⓒ<u>ridiculous</u>. They were ⓓ<u>cut down</u> either through their own stupidity, a brief scolding from others, or both. In this way, the humour of sitcoms acted as a cost-effective means to encourage acceptance of a ⓔ<u>more</u> pluralistic and tolerant society.
questions.explanation: 시트콤은 유머를 통해 진보적인 가치들을 이전보다 '더(more)' 받아들여지기 쉽게 만드는 역할을 했습니다. 지문의 뒷부분에서 시트콤이 다원적이고 관용적인 사회에 대한 수용을 장려한다고 언급하고 있으므로, progressive values가 'less acceptable' 하다는 표현은 문맥상 어긋납니다.

questions.question: 9. 다음 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은? [2.9점]
questions.passage: Creativity can influence productivity in different ways. For some individuals, creativity helps them identify complex and often overlooked problems. A notable example is Charles Darwin's work on the issue of speciation. He selected a deeply challenging and intricate problem that required years of data collection and thoughtful analysis. This kind of problem did not lend itself to quick solutions or straightforward experiments. In such cases, creativity might actually (A)_________ productivity – if measured by the number of publications – since the focus is on solving difficult, long-term problems. In contrast, individuals whose creativity centers on developing new methods or techniques might enhance productivity. For instance, the invention of the polymerase chain reaction (PCR), which allows for the rapid amplification of small DNA segments, is a good example. This form of creativity streamlines problem-solving by minimizing steps or replacing them with more reliable alternatives, ultimately (B)_________ productivity.
options: ① challenge ... hindering
② reduce ... boosting
③ increase ... decreasing
④ eliminate ... replacing
⑤ inspire ... complicating
questions.explanation: 이 글은 창의성이 생산성에 미치는 두 가지 상반된 방식을 설명합니다. 첫 번째 사례인 찰스 다윈의 경우, 매우 복잡하고 오랜 시간이 걸리는 문제를 다루었기 때문에 출판물 수로 측정되는 생산성은 오히려 줄어들 수(reduce) 있습니다. 반면, PCR 발명과 같이 문제 해결 과정을 간소화하는 창의성은 생산성을 크게 높여(boosting) 줍니다. 따라서 (A)에는 'reduce', (B)에는 'boosting'이 들어가는 것이 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 도전하다 ... 방해하는
② 줄이다 ... 신장시키는
③ 증가시키다 ... 감소시키는
④ 제거하다 ... 대체하는
⑤ 영감을 주다 ... 복잡하게 만드는

questions.question: 10. 다음 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은? [3.2점]
questions.passage: Emotion socialization – learning from other people about emotions and how to deal with them – starts early in life and plays a foundational role for emotion regulation development. Although extra-familial influences, such as peers or media, gain in importance during adolescence, parents remain the primary socialization agents. (A)___________, their own responses to emotional situations serve as a role model for emotion regulation, increasing the likelihood that their children will show similar reactions in comparable situations. Parental practices at times when their children are faced with emotional challenges also impact emotion regulation development. (B)___________ direct soothing and directive guidance of what to do are beneficial for younger children, they may demotivate adolescents' autonomy striving. In consequence, adolescents might pull away from, rather than turn toward, their parents in times of emotional crisis, unless parental practices are adjusted. More suitable in adolescence is indirect support of autonomous emotion regulation, such as through interest in, as well as awareness and nonjudgmental acceptance of, adolescents' emotional experiences, and being available when the adolescent wants to talk.
options: ① Thus ... Unless
② For instance ... Whereas
③ Nevertheless ... Although
④ In contrast ... Not until
⑤ Therefore ... Because
questions.explanation: 이 글은 부모가 자녀의 감정 사회화에 미치는 영향에 대해 다루고 있습니다. (A) 앞 문장에서 부모가 주요 사회화 대행자라고 언급한 뒤, 부모가 감정 조절의 역할 모델이 되는 구체적인 방식을 설명하므로 'For instance(예를 들어)'가 적절합니다. (B)는 직접적인 위로가 어린 아이들에게는 유익하지만 청소년에게는 의욕을 꺾을 수 있다는 대조적인 상황을 연결하므로 '~인 반면에'라는 뜻의 'Whereas'가 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 따라서 ... ~하지 않는다면
② 예를 들어 ... ~인 반면에
③ 그럼에도 불구하고 ... ~일지라도
④ 대조적으로 ... ~하고 나서야 비로소
⑤ 그러므로 ... ~ 때문에

questions.question: 11. 다음 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은? [2.9점]
questions.passage: Human processes differ from rational processes in terms of their outcomes. A process is considered rational if it always makes the correct decision based on the available information and an ideal standard of performance. In short, rational processes follow the rules, assuming the rules themselves are accurate. Human processes, however, involve instinct, intuition, and other factors that may not reflect those rules and might even ignore the available data. For example, the rational way to drive is to follow all traffic laws. But traffic isn't rational; if you stick to the rules exactly, you might end up stuck because other drivers don't. To be successful, a self-driving car must therefore act ______________.
options: ① logically
② rationally
③ mechanically
④ ethically
⑤ humanly
questions.explanation: 글의 흐름상 합리적인 과정(rational processes)은 규칙을 엄격히 따르는 것이지만, 인간의 과정(human processes)은 본능과 직관을 포함하며 때로는 규칙을 무시하기도 합니다. 실제 도로 상황은 비합리적일 수 있기 때문에 자율주행 자동차가 도로 위에서 성공적으로 작동하기 위해서는 규칙만 따르는 것이 아니라 인간처럼(humanly) 유연하게 행동해야 한다는 내용이 되어야 합니다.
options_translation: ① 논리적으로
② 합리적으로
③ 기계적으로
④ 윤리적으로
⑤ 인간적으로

questions.question: 12. 다음 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은? [3.1점]
questions.passage: If the brain has already stored someone's face and name, why do we still end up remembering one and not the other? This is because the brain has something of a two-tier memory system at work when it comes to retrieving memories, and this gives rise to a common yet infuriating sensation: recognising someone, but not being able to remember how or why, or what their name is. This happens because the brain differentiates between familiarity and recall. To clarify, familiarity (or recognition) is when you encounter someone or something and you know you've done so before. But beyond that, you've got nothing; all you can say is this person/thing is already in your memories. Recall is when you can access the original memory of how and why you know this person; recognition is _____________________________________________.
options: ① simply being aware that you've encountered this person before
② completely retrieving detailed information about a past event
③ intentionally trying to forget previous experience
④ successfully connecting a face with a name instantly
⑤ actively searching your memory for new information
questions.explanation: 지문은 기억을 인출할 때 '친숙함(familiarity/recognition)'과 '회상(recall)'의 두 단계 시스템이 작동한다고 설명합니다. 회상은 그 사람을 어떻게, 왜 아는지에 대한 원래의 기억에 접근하는 것인 반면, 친숙함(재인)은 단순히 이전에 본 적이 있다는 사실만 인지하는 것입니다. 따라서 빈칸에는 친숙함에 대한 설명인 '단순히 이 사람을 이전에 만난 적이 있다는 것을 아는 것'이 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 단순히 이 사람을 이전에 만난 적이 있다는 것을 아는 것
② 과거 사건에 대한 세부 정보를 완전히 되찾는 것
③ 의도적으로 이전 경험을 잊으려고 노력하는 것
④ 얼굴과 이름을 즉각적으로 성공적으로 연결하는 것
⑤ 새로운 정보를 위해 기억을 능동적으로 검색하는 것

questions.question: 13. 다음 글에서 전체 흐름과 관계없는 문장은?
questions.passage: Brands that fail to grow and develop lose their relevance. Think about the person you knew who was once on the fast track at your company, who is either no longer with the firm or, worse yet, appears to have hit a plateau in his or her career. ⓐ Assuming he or she did not make an ambitious move, more often than not, this individual is a victim of having failed to stay relevant and embrace the advances in his or her industry. ⓑThink about the impact personal computing technology had on the first wave of executive leadership exposed to the technology. ⓒMore experienced executives were usually wiser and enjoyed mentoring new staff members. ⓓThose who embraced the technology were able to integrate it into their work styles and excel. ⓔThose who were resistant many times found few opportunities to advance their careers and in many cases were ultimately let go through early retirement for failure to stay relevant and update their skills.
options: ① ⓐ
② ⓑ
③ ⓒ
④ ⓓ
⑤ ⓔ
questions.explanation: 이 글은 시대의 흐름과 기술적 발전에 발맞추지 못해 도태되는 개인이나 브랜드에 대해 설명하고 있습니다. 문장 ⓒ는 노련한 경영진이 지혜롭고 신입 사원 멘토링을 즐겼다는 내용으로, 기술 변화에 적응하지 못해 도태되는 상황과는 관련이 없는 흐름입니다.

questions.question: 14. 다음 글에서 전체 흐름과 관계없는 문장은?
questions.passage: A young child may be puzzled when asked to distinguish between the directions of right and left. But that same child may have no difficulty in determining the directions of up and down or back and front. ⓐScientists propose that this occurs because, although we experience three dimensions, only two had a strong influence on our evolution: the vertical dimension as defined by gravity and, in mobile species, the front/back dimension as defined by the positioning of sensory and feeding mechanisms. ⓑThese influence our perception of vertical versus horizontal, far versus close, and the search for dangers from above (such as an eagle) or below (such as a snake). ⓒHowever, the left-right axis is not as relevant in nature. ⓓA bear is equally dangerous from its front or the back side, but not if it is on the right or the left side. ⓔIn fact, when observing a scene containing plants, animals, and man-made objects such as cars or street signs, we can only tell when left and right have been inverted if we observe those artificial items.
options: ① ⓐ
② ⓑ
③ ⓒ
④ ⓓ
⑤ ⓔ
questions.explanation: 인간이 진화 과정에서 수직(위아래)과 앞뒤 방향은 중요하게 인식했지만, 좌우 방향은 상대적으로 덜 중요하게 여겼다는 내용의 글입니다. 문장 ⓓ는 곰이 앞이나 뒤에서 똑같이 위험하지만 오른쪽이나 왼쪽일 때는 그렇지 않다는 내용으로, 자연계에서 좌우가 대칭적이라 구분이 어렵거나 덜 중요하다는 논지와 어긋납니다. (실제로는 좌우가 대칭적이어서 구별이 어렵다는 것이 논지인데, ⓓ는 좌우가 위험도가 다르다는 식의 잘못된 예시를 들고 있습니다.)

questions.question: 15. 주어진 글 다음에 이어질 글의 순서로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: The explosion of popular music in the second half of the twentieth century as well as the global circulation and dissemination of music by the creative industries propelled a new understanding of accessibility in relation to music.
ordered_passages: (A) These music movements allowed previously excluded groups to revel in opportunities to create. This new accessibility led to novelty and empowerment in and beyond the music sphere.
(B) In the 1950s, anyone could pick up spoons, a couple of pans, a second-hand guitar and start a band. This led to specific genres such as skiffle and a more relaxed attitude to music making.

(C) Then, the popular music movement that followed these was driven by rebellion and freedom. This approach led to the punk movement, whose musicians made it a condition for their music to be accessible to all.
questions.explanation: 주어진 문장은 20세기 후반 대중음악의 폭발과 음악 산업에 의한 전파가 음악적 접근성에 대한 새로운 이해를 촉발했다는 내용입니다. (B)에서 1950년대 누구나 밴드를 시작할 수 있었던 구체적 예시(skiffle)를 들고, (C)에서 그 뒤를 이은(followed these) 저항과 자유의 펑크 운동을 설명한 뒤, (A)에서 이러한 음악 운동들이 소외된 집단에게 기회를 주어 새로운 접근성을 열었다는 결론으로 마무리하는 것이 자연스럽습니다.

questions.question: 16. 주어진 글 다음에 이어질 글의 순서로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Robert Blattberg and Steven Hoch noted that, in a changing environment, it is not clear that consistency is always a virtue and that one of the advantages of human judgment is the ability to detect change.
ordered_passages: (A) Humans, however, can incorporate these novel factors in their judgments. The composite – or average of human judgments and statistical models – proved to be more accurate than either the statistical models or the managers working alone.

(B) Thus, in changing environments, it might be advantageous to combine human judgment and statistical models. Blattberg and Hoch examined this possibility by having supermarket managers forecast demand for certain products and then creating a composite forecast by averaging these judgments with the forecasts of statistical models based on past data.

(C) The logic was that statistical models assume stable conditions and therefore cannot account for the effects on demand of novel events such as actions taken by competitors or the introduction of new products.
questions.explanation: 주어진 문장은 변화하는 환경에서 인간 판단의 장점이 변화를 감지하는 능력이라는 내용입니다. (B)에서 '따라서(Thus)' 인간 판단과 통계 모델을 결합하는 것이 유리할 수 있다며 실험(슈퍼마켓 매니저와 통계 모델의 결합)을 제시합니다. (C)에서 그 실험의 논리(통계 모델은 새로운 사건을 설명하지 못함)를 설명하고, (A)에서 인간은 이러한 '새로운 요인(these novel factors)'을 통합할 수 있으며 그 결과인 종합치가 가장 정확했다는 결과를 도출하는 순서가 적절합니다.

questions.question: 17. 주어진 글 다음에 이어질 글의 순서로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: The fast-growing, tremendous amount of data, collected and stored in large and numerous data repositories, has far exceeded our human ability for understanding without powerful tools.
ordered_passages: (A) Efforts have been made to develop expert system and knowledge-based technologies, which typically rely on users or domain experts to manually input knowledge into knowledge bases.

(B) However, this procedure is likely to cause biases and errors and is extremely costly and time consuming. The widening gap between data and information calls for the systematic development of tools that can turn data tombs into "golden nuggets" of knowledge.

(C) As a result, data collected in large data repositories become "data tombs" – data archives that are hardly visited. Important decisions are often made based not on the information – rich data stored in data repositories but rather on a decision maker's instinct, simply because the decision maker does not have the tools to extract the valuable knowledge hidden in the vast amounts of data.
questions.explanation: 주어진 글에서 방대한 데이터가 인간의 이해 능력을 초과했다는 문제를 제기합니다. (C)는 그 결과로 데이터가 '데이터 무덤'이 되고 결정이 직관에 의존하게 된다는 구체적인 상황을 설명합니다. (A)는 이를 해결하기 위한 '전문가 시스템' 개발 노력을 언급하며, (B)에서 'However'를 통해 이러한 수동적 방식의 한계(비용, 시간, 편향)를 지적하며 체계적인 도구 개발의 필요성을 강조하는 흐름이 가장 적절합니다.

questions.question: 18. 다음 글의 내용을 한 문장으로 요약하고자 할 때, 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Great scientists are seldom one-hit wonders. Newton is a prime example: beyond the Newtonian mechanics, he developed the theory of gravitation, calculus, laws of motion, and optimization. In fact, well-known scientists are often involved in multiple discoveries, a phenomenon potentially explained by the Matthew effect. Indeed, an initial success may offer a scientist legitimacy, improve peer perception, provide knowledge of how to score and win, enhance social status, and attract resources and quality collaborators, each of these payoffs further increasing her odds of scoring another win. Yet, there is an appealing alternative explanation: Great scientists have multiple hits and consistently succeed in their scientific endeavors simply because they're exceptionally talented. Therefore, future success again goes to those who have had success earlier, not because of advantages offered by the previous success, but because the earlier success was indicative of a hidden talent. The Matthew effect posits that success alone increases the future probability of success, raising the question: Does status dictate outcomes, or does it simply reflect an underlying talent or quality? In other words, is there really a Matthew effect after all?
questions.summary_sentence: Some people think that great scientists continue to succeed because (A)___________ of early success such as more support and good partners come after their first success, while others believe that their first success only shows their (B)___________, which helps them succeed again.
options: ① benefits / talent
② expectations / instinct
③ results / motivation
④ traits / nature
⑤ outcomes / luck
questions.explanation: 지문은 위대한 과학자들이 계속 성공하는 이유에 대해 두 가지 관점을 제시합니다. 첫째는 '마태 효과'로, 초기 성공에 따른 자원, 협력자 등의 혜택(benefits)이 다음 성공을 돕는다는 것이고, 둘째는 초기 성공이 그들의 숨겨진 재능(talent)을 나타내는 지표일 뿐이라는 관점입니다. 따라서 (A)에는 benefits, (B)에는 talent가 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 혜택 / 재능
② 기대 / 본능
③ 결과 / 동기
④ 특성 / 천성
⑤ 결과 / 운

questions.question: 23. 다음 글의 흐름으로 보아, 주어진 문장이 들어가기에 가장 적절한 곳은?
questions.passage: Development of the human body from a single cell provides many examples of the structural richness that is possible when the repeated production of random variation is combined with nonrandom selection. (A) All phases of body development from embryo to adult exhibit random activities at the cellular level, and body formation depends on the new possibilities generated by these activities coupled with selection of those outcomes that satisfy previously built-in criteria. (B) Always new structure is based on old structure, and at every stage selection favors some cells and eliminates others. (C) Except in the immune system, cells and extensions of cells are not genetically selected during the rounds, but rather, are positionally selected. (D) Those in the right place that make the right connections are stimulated, and those that don't are eliminated; this process is much like sculpting. (E) A natural consequence of the strategy is great variability from individual to individual at the cell and molecular levels, even though large-scale structures are quite similar.
questions.insertion_sentence: The survivors serve to produce new cells that undergo further rounds of selection.
options: ① (A)
② (B)
③ (C)
④ (D)
⑤ (E)
questions.explanation: 주어진 문장의 'The survivors'는 앞 문장에서 '선택되고 살아남은 세포들'을 지칭해야 합니다. (B) 문장에서 일부 세포는 선호되고 다른 것들은 제거된다고 언급했으므로, 그 직후인 (C) 자리에 살아남은 세포들이 다음 선택 과정을 거친다는 내용이 오는 것이 자연스럽습니다.

questions.question: 27. 다음 괸의 밑줄 찬 부분에 들어갈 내용을 <점건>에 맞게 한 문장으로 서술하시오.
questions.passage: Beethoven's drive to create something novel is a reflection of his state of curiosity. A number of investigators have modeled how curiosity influences musical composition. The computer modeling revealed that Beethoven's music became less predictable over time as his curiosity drove the exploration of new musical ideas as shown by increase in novel patterns. <u>사람들이 창의적일 수 읈게 하는 것은 바로 호기심이다</u>.
subjective_conditions: 1. <밴기>의 주어진 표현만을 모두 한 번씩 사용하시오.
2. 필요한 경우 주어진 표현의 형태림 봀형하시오.
3. 밸문의 한국어 문장의 뜻이 모두 정확하게 드러나도록 작성하시오.
vocabulary_box: it / humans / to / enable / be / be / creative / curiosity / that
questions.answer: It is curiosity that enables humans to be creative.
questions.explanation: 'It is ~ that' 강조구문을 사용하여 주어인 curiosity림 강조합니다. 그 후 enable + 목적어 + to부정사 구문을 활용하여 '~하는 것은 바로 ~ 이다'라는 의문을 완성합니다. 시제에 맞게 enable을 enables로 변형하여 작성합니다.

questions.question: 12. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 (A)가 의미하는 바로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: When we realize we've said something in error and we pause to go back to correct it, we stop gesturing a couple of hundred milliseconds before we stop speaking. Such sequences suggest the startling notion that our hands "know" what we're going to say before our conscious minds do, and in fact this is often the case. As the old saying goes, (A)<u>‐‐The hands speak what the lips cannot.‐‐</u> Gesture can mentally prime a word so that the right term comes to our lips. When people are prevented from gesturing, they talk less fluently; their speech becomes halting because their hands are no longer able to supply them with the next word, and the next. Not being able to gesture has other deleterious effects: without gesture to help our mental processes along, we remember less useful information, we solve problems less well, and we are less able to explain our thinking. Far from tagging along as speech's clumsy companion, gesture represents the leading edge of our thought.
options: ① Hand movements are a cultural form of communication unique to sign language users.
② Gestures play a vital role in expressing thoughts that are not yet fully verbalized.
③ Gestures replace language completely in situations requiring fast reactions.
④ The use of hands in speech is a learned habit with no real cognitive impact.
⑤ People use hand gestures only when they are unable to speak out loud.
questions.explanation: 이 글은 솑짓(제스처)이 언어보다 앐서서 사고를 이끌고 언어 표현을 돕는 역할을 한다고 설명합니다. 문윙사 밑줄 친 “The hands speak what the lips cannot”는 솑짓이 아직 입으로 내뱉지 못한(언어화되지 않은) 사고를 문자 그대로 '먼저 말한다'는 의미입니다. 따라서 제스처가 아직 완전히 언어화되지 않은 생각을 표현하는 데 중요한 역할을 한다는 ②번이 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 솑짓은 수어 사용자들에게만 고유한 문화적 의사소통 형태이다.
② 솑짓은 아직 완전히 언어화되지 않은 생각을 표현하는 데 중요한 역할을 한다.
③ 솑짓은 빠른 반응이 필요한 상황에ᄉ서 언어를 완전히 대찴한다.
④ 말하기에ᄉ서 손을 사용하는 것은 실제적인 인지적 영향이 없는 훜득된 견습이다.
⑤ 사람들은 킬소렜로 말할 수 없을 때만 손짓을 사용한다.

questions.question: 13. 다음 글의 요지로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Despite the difference between the past and the future, between what has happened and what is to come, it can be suggested, that our sense of the past has always been influenced by our view of the future. Revolutionaries have always looked to the past to frame their future cause, as is amply illustrated by examples from nationalism to communism. The future has often been seen as variously a recovery of a lost time, as a replication of what is established, or as a model bequeathed by a heroic age long gone. The writing of history is based on understanding or explaining future outcomes that were not known to contemporaries, since the historian has the benefit of hindsight and the past is nothing more than the accumulation of futures that are now our past. So, rather than see the hand of the past always shaping the future, perhaps it can be seen in reverse, with the past ─ in the sense of our understanding of it ─ being shaped by our orientation to the future.
options: ① 인류의 협사는 과거의 사건들이 축적되어 이단어진다.
② 미래에 대한 관점이 과거에 대한 인식에 영향을 줄 수 있다.
③ 미래 사회의 개혁은 과거에 대한 이해를 바탕젼로 설계된다.
④ 과거의 협사를 참고하여 오늘의 현실에 대한 교훈을 얻을 수 있다.
⑤ 과거와 미래의 사건 사이의 관계는 다양한 관점에ᄉ서 서술해야 한다.
questions.explanation: 이 글은 과거가 미래를 형성한다는 일반적인 생각과 반대로, 영어로 'our sense of the past has always been influenced by our view of the future'라고 명시하여 미래에 대한 관점이 과거를 바라밴는 방식(역사 기록 등)에 영향을 미친다는 점을 강조하고 있습니다. 따라서 ②번이 가장 적절한 요지입니다.

questions.question: 14. 다음 글의 요지로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: In 1900, at the close of the first decade in which electric systems had become a practical alternative for manufacturers, less than 5 percent of the power used in factories came from electricity. But the technological advances of suppliers made electric systems and electric motors ever more affordable and reliable, and the suppliers' intensive marketing programs also sped the adoption of the new technology. Further accelerating the shift was the rapid expansion in the number of skilled electrical engineers, who provided the expertise needed to install and run the new systems. In short order, electric power had gone from exotic to commonplace.
options: ① 1900년대 초 공장 동력의 대붽분을 전기가 차지했다.
② 전기 공급업체들은 마케팅보다는 모터 개발에 집중했다.
③ 숙련된 전기공학자 부접으로 전기시스템 바급이 지연되었다.
④ 높은 사용료로 인해 제조업체들의 전기시스템 이용이 저조했다.
⑤ 기술발전과 킬문인력의 증가로 전기동력이 빠르게 바급되었다.
questions.explanation: 이 글은 1900년대 초 전기 시스템이 공장에ᄉ서 빠르게 확산된 원인을 기술적 발전(가격 인하, 신뢰성), 공급업체의 마케팅, 그ᄅ리고 숙련된 전기 공학자의 증가로 설명하고 있습니다. 따라서 기술 발전과 전문 인력의 확대가 전기 동력의 대중화를 이뱌었다는 ⑤번이 가장 적절한 요지입니다.

questions.question: 20. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중 어법상 어색한 것은?
questions.passage: Commitment is the glue ⓐ<u>holding</u> together characteristically human forms of social life. Commitments make individuals' behavior predictable in the face of fluctuations in their desires and interests, thereby ⓑ<u>facilitated</u> the planning and coordination of joint actions involving multiple agents. Moreover, commitments make people willing ⓒ<u>to perform</u> actions that they would not otherwise perform. For example, a taxi driver ⓓ<u>picks up</u> his clients and transports them to their desired destination because they are committed to paying him afterwards for the service, and a construction worker performs her job every day because her employer has made a credible commitment to pay her at the end of the month. Indeed, the taxi driver and the construction worker are willing to accept money as payment only because a network of other agents (notably the central bank) is committed to ⓔ<u>taking</u> various measures to sustain the currency in question. Thus, social objects and institutions such as jobs, money, government, scientific collaborations and marriage depend for their origin and stability upon the credibility of commitments.
options: ① ⓐ
② ⓑ
③ ⓒ
④ ⓓ
⑤ ⓔ
questions.explanation: ⓑ가 포함된 문장에서 'thereby'는 부사이며, 앞의 절과 이어지는 분사구문 자리입니다. 문맥상 약속이 공동 행동의 계획과 조정을 '용이하게 하면서'라는 능동의 의미를 나타내야 하므로 과거분사인 facilitated를 현재분사인 facilitating으로 고쳐야 합니다.

questions.question: 28. 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: The prominence of the social dimension in food writing might suggest that the flavor of food is taking a back seat. I suspect that most people view flavor as of secondary importance in social settings where food is served. Although our social gatherings coalesce around food, the meaning of these gatherings does not seem to depend on flavor. Flavor assists with the narrow purpose of filling the belly, and once that is accomplished it provides the backdrop for whatever social dynamics characterize the gathering. These can be understood independently of the flavor of the food on offer, the appreciation of which is understood to be personal and subjective. According to this conventional wisdom, the ceremonies and rituals around food, the social events that supply food with its meaning, ___________________________________. To focus excessively on flavor is to miss the larger significance of these social relations.
options: ① are shaped by the sensory pleasure of food
② highlight the complexity of personal taste preference
③ reinforce the idea that food’s role is to satisfy hunger
④ are not necessarily influenced by the taste experience itself
⑤ show that flavor appreciation is central to human interaction
questions.explanation: 글의 요지는 음식의 '맛'보다는 음식을 매개로 하는 '사회적 관계'가 더 중요하다는 것입니다. 필자는 사람들이 사회적 모임에서 맛을 부차적인 것으로 본다고 언급하며, 음식과 관련된 의식이나 행사들의 의미가 맛과는 독립적으로 이해될 수 있다고 말합니다. 따라서 빈칸에는 이러한 행사들이 '반드시 맛의 경험 그 자체에 의해 영향을 받는 것은 아니다'라는 내용이 가장 적합합니다.
options_translation: ① 음식의 감각적 즐거움에 의해 형성된다
② 개인적인 맛 선호도의 복잡성을 강조한다
③ 음식의 역할이 배고픔을 채우는 것이라는 생각을 강화한다
④ 반드시 맛의 경험 그 자체에 의해 영향을 받는 것은 아니다
⑤ 맛의 감상이 인간 상호작용의 중심이라는 것을 보여준다

questions.question: 30. 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은? [2.9점]
questions.passage: According to the Food and Agriculture Organization (FAO), food security means that all individuals have secure “access to adequate safe and nutritious food to maintain a healthy life.” The governments of virtually every country on the planet attach great importance to achieving food security and a wide variety of mechanisms have been developed to realize this goal. The first issue governments face in achieving national food security is the problem of ensuring that adequate amount of food are available to the resident population. Some governments have set goals of food self-sufficiency, which means most if not all of the food available in a country comes from the domestic farming system. However, food security does not require food self-sufficiency because countries can import food items not easily produced within the country. Agricultural products are, after all, highly sensitive to climatic, soil and other conditions that tend to vary around the world. Even countries with extremely productive agricultural sectors are not fully self-sufficient in all food items. In general, the problem of assuring adequate food supplies is solved by relying on both domestic production and imports, which leads governments to intensely get ____________________________________ and to promote domestic production.
options: ① interested in selective breeding in farming
② devoted to ensuring the safety of domestic food
③ independent in controlling agricultural produce
④ involved in encouragement to international trade
⑤ eager to increase crop yield to supply sufficient food
questions.explanation: 지문은 식량 안보가 단순히 자급자족에 의해서만 달성되는 것이 아니라, 기후나 토양 조건의 차이로 인해 생산하기 어려운 품목의 경우 수입에 의존해야 함을 설명하고 있습니다. 따라서 정부는 식량 공급을 보장하기 위해 국내 생산을 장려할 뿐만 아니라 '국제 무역을 장려하는 데 관여하게' 된다는 내용이 빈칸에 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 농업에서 선택적 교배에 관심을 갖게
② 국내 식품의 안전을 보장하는 데 헌신하게
③ 농산물을 통제하는 데 독립적이게
④ 국제 무역을 장려하는 데 관여하게
⑤ 충분한 식량을 공급하기 위해 작물 수확량을 늘리는 데 열심이게

questions.question: 37. 다음 글의 흐름으로 보아 주어진 문장이 들어가기에 가장 적절한 곳은?
questions.passage: Great scientists are seldom one-hit wonders. Newton is a prime example: beyond the Newtonian mechanics, he developed the theory of gravitation, calculus, laws of motion, and optimization. (A) In fact, well-known scientists are often involved in multiple discoveries, a phenomenon potentially explained by the Matthew effect. (B) Indeed, an initial success may offer a scientist legitimacy, improve peer perception, provide knowledge of how to score and win, enhance social status, and attract resources and quality collaborators, each of these payoffs further increasing her odds of scoring another win. (C) Yet, there is an appealing alternative explanation: Great scientists have multiple hits and consistently succeed in their scientific endeavors simply because they're exceptionally talented. (D) The Matthew effect posits that success alone increases the future probability of success, raising the question: Does status dictate outcomes, or does it simply reflect an underlying talent or quality? (E) In other words, is there really a Matthew effect after all?
options: ① (A)
② (B)
③ (C)
④ (D)
⑤ (E)
questions.insertion_sentence: Therefore, future success again goes to those who have had success earlier, not because of advantages offered by the previous success, but because the earlier success was indicative of a hidden talent.

questions.question: 9. 다음 글의 괄호 (A), (B), (C) 안에 들어갈 말로 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: When we realize we've said something in error and we pause to go back to correct it, we stop gesturing a couple of hundred milliseconds before we stop speaking. Such sequences suggest the startling notion that our hands "know" what we're going to say, (A)[following / preceding] recognition by our conscious minds, and in fact this is often the case. Gesture can mentally activate a word so that the right term comes to our lips. When people are prevented from gesturing, they talk less fluently; their speech becomes (B)[fluid / hesitant] because their hands are no longer able to supply them with the next word, and the next. Not being able to gesture has other (C)[beneficial / adverse] effects: without gesture to help our mental processes along, we remember less useful information, we solve problems less well, and we are less able to explain our thinking. Far from tagging along as speech's clumsy companion, gesture represents the leading edge of our thought.
options: ① following ... fluid ... beneficial
② following ... hesitant ... adverse
③ following ... fluid ... adverse
④ preceding ... fluid ... beneficial
⑤ preceding ... hesitant ... adverse
questions.explanation:
이 글은 손짓(제스처)이 사고와 언어 표현에 있어 주도적인 역할을 한다는 내용을 담고 있습니다. 
(A) 우리가 말하기 전에 이미 손짓을 멈춘다는 것은 손이 우리가 무엇을 말할지 우리의 의식적인 인식보다 먼저 알고 있다는 것을 시사하므로 'preceding(앞서는)'이 적절합니다. 
(B) 손짓을 하지 못하게 하면 말을 덜 유창하게 하게 되며, 다음 단어를 공급받지 못해 말이 'hesitant(주저하는, 망설이는)'해집니다.
(C) 손짓을 못하는 것은 정신적 과정을 돕는 역할을 없애기 때문에 정보 기억력이 떨어지고 문제 해결 능력이 저하되는 등 'adverse(부정적인)' 영향을 미칩니다.
options_translation: ① 따르는 ... 유동적인 ... 유익한
② 따르는 ... 주저하는 ... 부정적인
③ 따르는 ... 유동적인 ... 부정적인
④ 앞서는 ... 유동적인 ... 유익한

questions.question: 10. 다음 글의 (A), (B)에 대한 설명으로 적절하지 않은 것을 <보기>에서 있는 대로 고른 것은?
questions.passage: Great scientists are seldom one-hit wonders. Newton is a prime example: beyond the Newtonian mechanics, he developed the theory of gravitation, calculus, laws of motion, and optimization. In fact, well-known scientists are often involved in multiple discoveries, a phenomenon potentially explained by (A)<u>the Matthew effect</u>. Indeed, an initial success may offer a scientist legitimacy, improve peer perception, provide knowledge of how to score and win, enhance social status, and attract resources and quality collaborators, each of these payoffs further increasing her odds of scoring another win. Yet, there is (B)<u>an appealing alternative explanation</u>: Great scientists have multiple hits and consistently succeed in their scientific endeavors simply because they're exceptionally talented. Therefore, future success again goes to those who have had success earlier, not because of advantages offered by the previous success, but because the earlier success was indicative of a hidden talent. The Matthew effect posits that success alone increases the future probability of success, raising the question: Does status dictate outcomes, or does it simply reflect an underlying talent or quality? In other words, is there really a Matthew effect after all?
vocabulary_box: ⓐ The (A) explanation holds that early success results in greater peer recognition and increased access to resources, which support continued achievement.
ⓑ The (B) view argues that the root of sustained success lies in a scientist's intrinsic brilliance rather than any acquired external advantage.
ⓒ The (B) perspective assumes that without an initial breakthrough, even highly talented individuals are unlikely to achieve repeated scientific success.
ⓓ The (A) theory highlights the way in which benefits like increased credibility and access to resources boost the chances of further scientific success.
ⓔ While the (A) and (B) explanations both recognize that early achievements are frequently followed by continued accomplishments, they offer different explanations for why this occurs.
options: ① ⓐ
② ⓒ
questions.explanation:
지문은 과학자들의 지속적인 성공 이유를 두 가지 관점에서 설명합니다. (A) '마태 효과'는 초기 성공이 가져다주는 자원, 평판, 지위 등의 외부적 이점이 다음 성공의 확률을 높인다는 이론입니다. 반면 (B) '매력적인 대안적 설명'은 지속적인 성공이 단순히 그 과학자의 뛰어난 재능 때문이며, 초기 성공은 단지 그 재능의 지표일 뿐이라는 관점입니다. 
<보기> ⓒ의 경우, (B)의 관점은 성공의 원인이 개인의 내재적 재능에 있다고 보므로, 초기 돌파구(성공)가 없더라도 재능이 있다면 성공할 수 있다고 봅니다. 따라서 '초기 돌파구가 없으면 매우 재능 있는 개인이라도 반복적인 성공을 거두기 어렵다'는 설명은 (B)에 대한 적절한 설명이 아닙니다. 나머지는 모두 지문의 내용을 정확히 반영하고 있습니다.

questions.question: 11. 다음 글의 내용과 일치하는 것만을 <보기>에서 있는 대로 고른 것은? [2.9점]
questions.passage: The concept of ecosystem states should be familiar to anyone with a home vegetable garden. The garden is a small ecosystem that the grower attempts to keep in a specific state, namely the maximization of fruit and vegetable production. To achieve this, the grower is almost always intervening in the dynamics of the ecosystem; they remove unwanted plants that begin to grow and perhaps spray insecticides and fence off the patch to stop insects and other animals from consuming the vegetables. Since maximizing vegetable growth is an inherently unstable state for the ecosystem, the grower is effectively keeping the ball on a slope. If the grower stops intervening, even for a day, the ecosystem, that small patch of ground, will naturally begin to shift to a more stable state. Vegetables may still grow, but yield will almost certainly be lower as other plants crowd out the vegetables and wildlife consume the produce.
vocabulary_box: ① Gardeners typically employ physical barriers and chemical treatments to protect crops from insects and animals.
② Even in the absence of regular intervention, vegetables maintain relatively stable growth and keep other species out due to their self-regulating ability.
③ Maximizing vegetable growth requires maintaining an inherently unstable ecological state.
④ If left alone, the garden ecosystem will tend to move toward a more stable but less productive state.
options: ① ①, ②
② ①, ③
③ ②, ④
④ ①, ③, ④
⑤ ②, ③, ④
questions.explanation: ① 정원사들은 일반적으로 작물을 곤충과 동물로부터 보호하기 위해 물리적 장벽(울타리)과 화학적 처리(살충제)를 사용합니다(본문 내용과 일치). ② 개입이 없으면 정원은 더 안정적인 상태로 변하며 채소의 성장이 다른 식물에 의해 저해되므로 본문과 일치하지 않습니다. ③ 채소 성장을 극대화하는 것은 본질적으로 불안정한 생태적 상태를 유지하는 것입니다(본문 내용과 일치). ④ 개입을 멈추면 정원 생태계는 더 안정적이지만 생산성은 낮은 상태로 이동하게 됩니다(본문 내용과 일치). 따라서 정답은 ①, ③, ④를 포함한 4번입니다.
options_translation: ① ①, ②
② ①, ③
③ ②, ④
④ ①, ③, ④
⑤ ②, ③, ④
