questions.question: 8. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 어법상 어색한 것은? [2.9점]
questions.passage:
As a general rule, it's better if your definition corresponds as closely as possible to the way in which the term is ordinarily used in the kinds of debates to which your claims are pertinent. There will be, however, occasions where it is appropriate, even necessary, ⓐ<u>to coin</u> special uses through what philosophers call stimulative definition. This would be the case ⓑ<u>where</u> the current lexicon is not able to make distinctions that you think are philosophically important. For example, we do not have a term in ordinary language that describes a memory that is not necessarily a memory of something the person ⓒ<u>had</u> it has experienced. Such a thing would occur, for example, if I could somehow share your memories: I would have a memory-type experience, but this would not be of something ⓓ<u>that</u> I had actually experienced. To call this a memory would be ⓔ<u>misleading</u>. For this reason, philosophers have coined the special term 'quasi-memory' to refer to these hypothetical memory-like experiences.
*pertinent: 관련 있는
questions.explanation: ⓒ가 포함된 문장에서 'a memory of something the person had experienced'가 되어야 합니다. 'something'이 관계대명사절 내에서 'experienced'의 목적어 역할을 수행하므로, 별도의 대명사 'it'이 중복되어 쓰일 수 없습니다. 따라서 ⓒ의 'had it'에서 'it'을 삭제해야 올바른 문장이 됩니다.

questions.question: 9. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 어법상 어색한 것은? [2.9점]
questions.passage:
It is important to recognize that although science is a rule-based procedure, it is very much a creative process. A conjecture is a philosophical invention, cooked up rather ⓐ<u>mystically</u> by the mind through the mental computation we call careful contemplation. However, until the hypothesis ⓑ<u>is tested</u> against reality, it is not yet truly knowledge; it is just information that represents speculation. Knowledge is information ⓒ<u>demonstrating</u> its usefulness. It is what is left over after cycles of experimental testing ⓓ<u>has eliminated</u> false theories. As scientists continually test their hypotheses and modify their models to account for new and surprising data, a kind of "learning loop" emerges ⓔ<u>that</u> statisticians call Bayesian updating.
*conjecture: 추론 **contemplation: 숙고 
***speculation: 추측
questions.explanation: ⓓ가 포함된 문장의 주어는 'cycles of experimental testing'입니다. 전치사구 'of experimental testing'의 수식을 받는 핵(head)은 복수 명사인 'cycles'이므로, 이에 대응하는 동사는 단수형 'has'가 아니라 복수형 'have'가 되어야 합니다.

questions.question: 11. 다음 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은? [2.9점]
questions.passage:
Beethoven's drive to create something novel is a reflection of his state of curiosity. Our brains experience a sense of reward when we create something new in the process of exploring something uncertain, such as a musical phrase that we've never played or heard before. When our curiosity leads to something novel, the resulting reward brings us a sense of pleasure. A number of investigators have modeled how curiosity influences musical composition. In the case of Beethoven, computer modeling focused on the thirty-two piano sonatas written after age thirteen revealed that the musical patterns found in all of Beethoven's music decreased in later sonatas, while novel patterns, including patterns that were unique to a particular sonata, increased. In other words. Beethoven's music became less predictable over time as his curiosity drove the exploration of new musical ideas. Curiosity is a powerful driver of _________________________.
*sonata: 악곡의 한 형식
options: ① external reward
② musical pattern
③ human creativity
④ computer modeling
⑤ emotional regulation
questions.explanation: 글 전체의 내용은 베토벤의 호기심이 어떻게 새로운 음악적 아이디어를 탐구하게 하고, 그것이 음악적 패턴의 변화(예측 가능성 감소, 참신함 증가)로 이어졌는지를 설명하고 있습니다. 따라서 호기심은 새로운 것을 만들어내는 '인간의 창의성'의 강력한 원동력이라는 결론이 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 외부적 보상
② 음악적 패턴
③ 인간의 창의성
④ 컴퓨터 모델링
⑤ 정서 조절

questions.question: 12. 다음 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은? [2.9점]
questions.passage: There are reasons why science is not fully trusted and why healthy skepticism and critical thinking are essential. In spite of professional standards, claims of objectivity, and the peer review process, the conduct of science can be biased. All experts are not the same, nor do they submit their work to the same scrutiny. Knowing the source of funding can be important in evaluating scientific claims. For example, the Harvard researchers who made claims in the late 1960s about the problems with dietary fat, leading the nation away from perceiving sugar as one of the main causes in health problems, were funded in part by the sugar industry. The authors did not reveal their funding source to the New England Journal of Medicine, where their influential article appeared. Their article shaped a generation of changes in eating patterns that appears to have fostered higher use of sugar, now widely implicated as a source of the rise in obesity and diabetes. Stories such as this one fuel suspicion — but also lead to further safeguards in the scientific process. Funding disclosures, although not required five decades ago, have since been made compulsory.
options: ① be biased
② remain neutral
③ stay free from bias
④ avoid ethical concerns
⑤ adhere strictly to evidence
questions.explanation: 이 글은 과학이 왜 완전히 신뢰받지 못하는지, 그리고 왜 자금 출처를 아는 것이 중요한지를 설명하고 있습니다. 하버드 연구원들이 설탕 산업의 자금 지원을 받고 지방의 위험성을 강조하며 설탕의 책임을 회피했던 사례를 통해, 과학적 연구 과정이 자금 지원 등에 의해 편향될 수 있음을 시사합니다. 따라서 빈칸에는 '편향될 수 있다(be biased)'가 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 편향될 수 있다
② 중립을 유지할 수 있다
③ 편견으로부터 자유로울 수 있다
④ 윤리적 우려를 피할 수 있다
⑤ 증거를 엄격히 고수할 수 있다

questions.question: 13. 다음 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은? [3.1점]
questions.passage: Emotion socialization ─ learning from other people about emotions and how to deal with them ─ starts early in life and plays a foundational role for emotion regulation development. Although extra-familial influences, such as peers or media, gain in importance during adolescence, parents remain the primary socialization agents. For example, their own responses to emotional situations serve as a role model for emotion regulation, increasing the likelihood that their children will show similar reactions in comparable situations. Parental practices at times when their children are faced with emotional challenges also impact emotion regulation development. Whereas direct soothing and directive guidance of what to do are beneficial for younger children, they may intrude on adolescents' autonomy striving. In consequence, adolescents might pull away from, rather than turn toward, their parents in times of emotional crisis, unless parental practices are adjusted. More suitable in adolescence is _________________________, such as through interest in, as well as awareness and nonjudgmental acceptance of, adolescents' emotional experiences, and being available when the adolescent wants to talk.
options: ① avoidance of emotional risk-taking
② adolescents' dependence on societal norms
③ parental control over adolescents' autonomy
④ socialization through constant behavior guidance
⑤ indirect support of autonomous emotion regulation
questions.explanation: 청소년기에는 자율성을 추구하려는 경향이 강해지므로, 어린 시절과 같은 직접적인 달래기나 지시적인 지도는 오히려 부모로부터 멀어지게 만들 수 있습니다. 따라서 청소년기에는 청소년의 감정적 경험을 수용하고 그들이 원할 때 곁에 있어 주는 것과 같은 '자율적인 감정 조절에 대한 간접적인 지원'이 더 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 정서적 위험 감수 회피
② 청소년의 사회적 규범에 대한 의존
③ 청소년의 자율성에 대한 부모의 통제
④ 끊임없는 행동 지도를 통한 사회화
⑤ 자율적인 감정 조절에 대한 간접적인 지원

questions.question: 14. 다음 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은? [3.1점]
questions.passage: The governments of virtually every country on the planet attach great importance to achieving food security and a wide variety of mechanisms have been developed to realize this goal. The first issue governments face in achieving national food security is the problem of insuring that adequate amounts of food are available to the resident population. Some governments have set goals of food self-sufficiency, which means most if not all of the food available in a country comes from the domestic farming system. However, food security does not require food self-sufficiency because countries can import food items not easily produced within the country. Agricultural products are, after all, highly sensitive to climatic, soil and other conditions that tend to vary around the world. Even countries with extremely productive agricultural sectors are not fully self-sufficient in all food items. The United States, for example, depends on imports for its supply of coffee, tea, bananas and other tropical products. In general, the problem of assuring adequate food supplies is solved by __________________________________.
options: ① combining domestic production with food imports
② producing every kind of food only on local farms
③ storing enough grain to last the nation ten years
④ reducing nationwide consumption so supplies will last longer
⑤ maximizing export earnings by selling most staple crops overseas
questions.explanation: 글의 내용은 식량 안보가 반드시 식량 자급자족을 의미하는 것은 아니며, 기후나 토양 조건 때문에 모든 품목을 자국 내에서 생산할 수 없으므로 수입이 필요하다는 점을 강조합니다. 따라서 적절한 식량 공급을 확보하는 문제는 '국내 생산과 식량 수입을 결합하는 것'으로 해결됩니다.
options_translation: ① 국내 생산과 식량 수입을 결합하는 것
② 모든 종류의 음식을 오직 지역 농장에서만 생산하는 것
③ 국가에 10년 동안 지속될 만큼 충분한 곡물을 저장하는 것
④ 공급이 더 오래 지속되도록 전국적인 소비를 줄이는 것
⑤ 대부분의 주요 작물을 해외로 팔아 수출 수익을 극대화하는 것

questions.question: 15. 다음 글에서 전체 흐름과 관계없는 문장은?
questions.passage:
The prominence of the social dimension in food writing might suggest that the flavor of food is taking a back seat. I suspect that most people view flavor as of secondary importance in social settings where food is served. ① Although our social gatherings coalesce around food, the meaning of these gatherings does not seem to depend on flavor. ② Flavor assists with the narrow purpose of filling the belly, and once that is accomplished it provides the backdrop for whatever social dynamics characterize the gathering. ③ These can be understood independently of the flavor of the food on offer, the appreciation of which is understood to be personal and subjective. ④ According to this conventional wisdom, the ceremonies and rituals around food, the social events that supply food with its meaning, depend on the quality of sensations provided by the food. ⑤ To focus excessively on flavor is to miss the larger significance of these social relations.
*coalesce: 합쳐지다 **backdrop: 배경
questions.explanation: 이 글은 음식과 관련된 사회적 상황에서 음식의 '맛'보다는 '사회적 의미'와 '관계'가 더 중요하다는 점을 강조하고 있습니다. ①, ②, ③, ⑤번 문장은 모두 맛보다는 사회적 교류의 가치를 강조하는 흐름을 보이고 있으나, ④번 문장은 오히려 사회적 행사나 의식이 음식의 맛(감각의 질)에 달려 있다고 주장하므로 전체 흐름과 상반되는 내용을 담고 있습니다.

questions.question: 16. 글의 순서로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: It is a common assumption that most vagrant birds are ultimately doomed, aside from the rare cases where individuals are able to reorientate and return to their normal ranges.
ordered_passages: (A) However, there are many lines of evidence to suggest that vagrancy can, on rare occasions, dramatically alter the fate of populations, species or even whole ecosystems.

(B) This is undoubtedly true for the majority of cases, as the most likely outcome of any given vagrancy event is that the individual will fail to find enough resources, and/or be exposed to inhospitable environmental conditions, and perish.
(C) Despite being infrequent, these events can be extremely important when viewed at the timescales over which ecological and evolutionary processes unfold.
questions.explanation: 주어진 문장에서 떠돌이 새들의 운명에 대한 일반적인 통념을 언급합니다. (B)에서 이것이 사실임을 인정하고, 대부분의 개체가 죽는다는 구체적인 이유를 제시합니다. (A)에서 '그러나'라는 연결어를 통해 떠돌이 새들의 행동이 생태계에 큰 영향을 미칠 수도 있다는 반전의 내용을 제시합니다. 마지막으로 (C)에서 이러한 사건들이 드물지만 생태학적/진화적 관점에서 매우 중요할 수 있음을 강조하며 마무리합니다.

questions.question: 17. 글의 순서로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Great scientists are seldom one-hit wonders. Newton is a prime example: beyond the Newtonian mechanics, he developed the theory of gravitation, calculus, laws of motion, and optimization. In fact, well-known scientists are often involved in multiple discoveries, a phenomenon potentially explained by the Matthew effect.
ordered_passages: (A) Yet, there is an appealing alternative explanation: Great scientists have multiple hits and consistently succeed in their scientific endeavors simply because they're exceptionally talented.

(B) Therefore, future success again goes to those who have had success earlier, not because of advantages offered by the previous success, but because the earlier success was indicative of a hidden talent.

(C) Indeed, an initial success may offer a scientist legitimacy, improve peer perception, provide knowledge of how to score and win, enhance social status, and attract resources and quality collaborators, each of these payoffs further increasing her odds of scoring another win.
questions.explanation: 주어진 글에서는 위대한 과학자들이 다수의 발견을 하는 현상을 '마태 효과(Matthew effect)'로 설명할 가능성을 언급합니다. (C)에서는 마태 효과가 어떻게 초기 성공이 후속 성공의 확률을 높이는지 구체적인 이점들을 나열합니다. (A)에서는 마태 효과와는 다른 매력적인 대안적 설명으로서 과학자들의 탁월한 재능을 제시합니다. 마지막으로 (B)에서는 그 재능을 기반으로 한 미래의 성공이 초기 성공을 통해 입증된 잠재적 재능 덕분임을 언급하며 마무리합니다.

questions.question: 18. 글의 순서로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: If you had wanted to create a "selfdriving" car in the 1950s, your best option might have been to strap a brick to the accelerator. Yes, the vehicle would have been able to move forward on its own, but it could not slow down, stop, or turn to avoid barriers. Obviously not ideal. But does that mean the entire concept of the self-driving car is not worth pursuing?. No, it only means that at the time we did not yet have the tools we now possess to help enable vehicles to operate both autonomously and safely. This oncedistant dream now seems within our reach. It is much the same story in medicine. Two decades ago, we were still taping bricks to accelerators. Today, we are approaching the point where we can begin to bring some appropriate technology to bear in ways that advance our understanding of patients as unique individuals. In fact, many patients are already wearing devices that monitor their conditions in real time, which allows doctors to talk to their patients in a specific, refined, and feedback-driven way that was not even possible a decade ago.
ordered_passages: (A) In fact, many patients are already wearing devices that monitor their conditions in real time, which allows doctors to talk to their patients in a specific, refined, and feedback-driven way that was not even possible a decade ago.

(B) But does that mean the entire concept of the self-driving car is not worth pursuing? No, it only means that at the time we did not yet have the tools we now possess to help enable vehicles to operate both autonomously and safely.

(C) This once-distant dream now seems within our reach. It is much the same story in medicine. Two decades ago, we were still taping bricks to accelerators. Today, we are approaching the point where we can begin to bring some appropriate technology to bear in ways that advance our understanding of patients as unique individuals.
questions.explanation: 주어진 글에서 1950년대의 자율주행 자동차를 비유적으로 설명합니다. (B)에서 자율주행이라는 개념을 포기해야 하는 것은 아니며 당시에는 기술이 부족했을 뿐임을 설명합니다. (C)에서 그 꿈이 현재 현실화되고 있으며 의학 분야에서도 비슷한 상황이 벌어지고 있음을 언급합니다. (A)에서 실제 의학적 사례(환자 모니터링 기기)를 들어 구체적으로 기술 발전의 효과를 설명합니다.

questions.question: 19. 다음 글의 흐름으로 보아, 주어진 문장이 들어가기에 가장 적절한 곳은?
questions.passage: The concept of ecosystem states should be familiar to anyone with a home vegetable garden. (A) The garden is a small ecosystem that the grower attempts to keep in a specific state, namely the maximization of fruit and vegetable production. (B) He removes unwanted plants that begin to grow and perhaps sprays insecticides and fences off the patch to stop insects and other animals from consuming the vegetables. (C) Since maximizing vegetable growth is an inherently unstable state for the ecosystem, the grower is effectively keeping the ball on a slope. (D) If the grower stops intervening. even for a day, the ecosystem, that small patch of ground, will naturally begin to shift to a more stable state. (E) Vegetables may still grow, but yield will almost certainly be lower as other plants crowd out the vegetables and wildlife consume the produce.
questions.insertion_sentence: To achieve this, the grower is almost always intervening in the dynamics of the ecosystem.
questions.explanation: 주어진 문장의 'To achieve this'가 가리키는 내용은 앞 문장(A)에 언급된 '채소 및 과일 생산의 극대화(maximization of fruit and vegetable production)'를 의미합니다. (B) 뒤의 문장들은 재배자가 어떻게 생태계에 개입(intervening)하는지에 대한 구체적인 예시(원치 않는 식물 제거, 살충제 살포 등)를 설명하고 있으므로, 주어진 문장은 (B)의 자리에 들어가는 것이 가장 적절합니다.

questions.question: 20. 다음 글의 흐름으로 보아, 주어진 문장이 들어가기에 가장 적절한 곳은?
questions.passage: We are the only species that seasons its food, deliberately altering it with the highly flavored plant parts we call herbs and spices. (A) It's quite possible that our taste for spices has an evolutionary root. (B) Many spices have antibacterial properties ─ in fact, common seasonings such as garlic, onion, and oregano inhibit the growth of almost every bacterium tested. (C) And the cultures that make the heaviest use of spices ─ think of the garlic and black pepper of Thai food, the ginger and coriander of India, the chili peppers of Mexico ─ come from warmer climates, where bacterial spoilage is a bigger issue. (D) Our uniquely human attention to flavor, in this case the flavor of spices, turns out to have arisen as a matter of life and death. (E)
questions.insertion_sentence: In contrast, the most lightly spiced cuisines ─ those of Scandinavia and northern Europe ─ are from cooler climates.
questions.explanation: 문단 (C)에서는 따뜻한 기후의 지역들이 향신료를 많이 사용한다는 내용을 설명하고 있습니다. 주어진 문장은 'In contrast'를 통해 이와 대조적으로 추운 기후의 지역(스칸디나비아, 북유럽)은 향신료를 적게 사용한다는 내용을 담고 있으므로 (D)의 위치에 들어가는 것이 적절합니다. 그 뒤의 (D) 문장은 이러한 향신료의 사용이 생사의 문제(사멸 및 항균 효과)와 연관되어 발생했다는 전체적인 결론을 도출하고 있습니다.

questions.question: 21. 다음 글의 내용을 한 문장으로 요약하고자 할 때, 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 말은?
questions.passage: In order to bring the ever-increasing costs of home care for elderly and needy persons under control, managers of home care providers have introduced management systems. These systems specify tasks of home care workers and the time and budget available to perform these tasks. Electronic reporting systems. require home care workers to report on their activities and the time spent, thus making the distribution of time and money visible and, in the perception of managers, controllable. This, in the view of managers, has contributed to the resolution of the problem. The home care workers, on the other hand, may perceive their work not as a set of separate tasks to be performed as efficiently as possible, but as a service to be provided to a client with whom they may have developed a relationship. This includes having conversations with clients and enquiring about the person's well-being. Restricted time and the requirement to report may be perceived as obstacles that make it impossible to deliver the service that is needed. If the management systems are too rigid, this may result in home care workers becoming overloaded and demotivated.
questions.summary_sentence: Managers have introduced management systems to make time and budget more (A)____________ in home care, but their (B)____________ can turn these systems into obstacles that burden workers and weaken service quality.
options: ① controllable		creativity
② controllable		rigidity
③ complicated		strength
④ complicated		cooperation
⑤ random		balance
questions.explanation: 본문에서 관리자들은 시간과 예산을 'controllable(통제 가능한)' 상태로 만들기 위해 관리 시스템을 도입했습니다. 그러나 이러한 시스템이 너무 'rigid(경직된)'할 경우, 이는 돌봄 노동자들에게 장애물이 되어 서비스 품질을 약화시키고 노동자들을 지치게 만든다는 내용이 마지막 문장에 언급되어 있습니다.
options_translation: 통제 가능한 - 창의성
통제 가능한 - 경직성
복잡한 - 힘/강점
복잡한 - 협력
무작위의 - 균형

questions.question: 22. 다음 글의 내용을 한 문장으로 요약하고자 할 때, 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 말은?
questions.passage:
Dictionaries are relatively good resources for anyone interested in finding out what a word means. Using one set of words to define another word is called a lexical definition. But it's important to understand the limits of dictionary definitions. More often than not, a definition in a dictionary requires readers to have a fairly robust understanding of the language already at their disposal. In other words, a dictionary functions in many cases as a cross-reference or translator between words one knows and words that one doesn't yet know. Even the most obscure words in a dictionary, say, for example, "pulchritudinous" or "kalokagathia," must be defined using words that the reader already knows and understands.
*lexical: 어휘적인 **robust: 탄탄한 ***obscure: 난해한
questions.summary_sentence: While dictionaries are useful for defining words, they often rely on the reader's (A)____________ language knowledge to (B)____________ those definitions.
options: ① existing ... understand
② existing ... memorize
③ limited ... redefine
④ limited ... interpret
⑤ foreign ... translate
questions.explanation: 사전은 단어의 뜻을 정의할 때 이미 알고 있는 단어들을 사용하여 설명하기 때문에, 독자가 사전을 통해 뜻을 파악하려면 이미 갖추고 있는(existing) 언어 지식이 있어야 그 정의를 이해(understand)할 수 있다는 내용의 글입니다.
options_translation: ① 기존의 ... 이해하다
② 기존의 ... 암기하다
③ 제한된 ... 재정의하다
④ 제한된 ... 해석하다
⑤ 외국어의 ... 번역하다

questions.question: 23. 다음 글의 문맥상 빈칸(A)에 들어갈 한 단어를 <보기>의 사전적 의미를 참고하여 쓰시오. (단, (A)는 p로 시작하는 단어임)
questions.passage:
Too many times people, especially in today's generation, expect things to just happen overnight. When we have these false expectations, it tends to discourage us from continuing to move forward. Because this is a high tech society, everything we want has to be within the parameters of our comfort and convenience. If it doesn't happen fast enough, we're tempted to lose interest. So many people don't want to take the time it requires to be successful. Success is not a matter of mere desire: you should develop (A)p□□□□□□□ in order to achieve it. Great things take time to build.
*parameter: 매개 변수. 제한
subjective_conditions: (A)는 p로 시작하는 단어임
vocabulary_box: It is the ability to stay calm and accept a delay or something annoying without complaining.
questions.explanation: 글의 문맥상 성공을 거두기 위해서는 단기간에 이루어지는 것을 기대하기보다 시간이 걸리는 것을 견뎌내야 한다는 내용입니다. <보기>의 설명인 '불평 없이 지연이나 짜증나는 일을 받아들이고 침착함을 유지하는 능력'은 '인내(patience)'를 의미하므로 빈칸에 적절합니다.

questions.question: 24. 다음 글의 문맥상 빈칸(A)에 들어갈 한 단어를 <보기>의 사전적 의미를 참고하여, 지문에서 찾아 쓰시오. (단, 필요한 경우 단어의 형태를 바꿀 것)
questions.passage:
Commitment is the glue holding together characteristically human forms of social life. Commitments make individuals' behavior predictable in the face of fluctuations in their desires and interests, thereby facilitating the planning and coordination of joint actions involving multiple agents. Moreover, commitments make people willing to perform actions that they would not otherwise perform. For example, a taxi driver picks up his clients and transports them to their desired destination because they are committed to paying him afterwards for the service, and a construction worker performs her job every day because her employer has made a credible commitment to pay her at the end of the month. Indeed, the taxi driver and the construction worker are willing to accept money as payment only because a network of other agents (notably the central bank) is committed to taking various measures to sustain the currency in question. Thus, social objects and institutions such as jobs, money, government, scientific collaborations and marriage depend for their origin and stability upon the (A)□□□□□□□□□□□ of commitments.
*fluctuation: 동요
subjective_conditions: 지문에서 찾아 쓸 것
필요한 경우 단어의 형태를 바꿀 것
vocabulary_box: It is defined as the quality or characteristic of being trustworthy, believable, or reliable.
questions.explanation: 사회적 제도나 대상들의 안정성은 약속의 '신뢰성'에 달려 있다는 맥락입니다. <보기>의 '신뢰할 수 있고 믿을 수 있는 품질이나 특성'이라는 정의에 부합하는 단어는 'credibility'입니다. 본문의 'credible(신뢰할 수 있는)'을 명사형으로 변형하여 답을 작성합니다.

questions.question: 25. 다음 글의 문맥상 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 한 단어를 각각 본문에서 찾아 쓰시오.
questions.passage:
Since their start in the early 1950s U.S. television sitcoms have charted many of the social conflicts in U.S. society: civil rights, women's rights in the home and in the workplace, children's rights, immigration and multiculturalism, as well as evolving conceptions of the family. Each of these issues has been addressed through humour in a way that has helped to increase the acceptance of more progressive values compared to the past. Often a character, usually someone marked as a bigot, resisted one or more of these developments and was then made to appear ridiculous. They were cut down either through their own stupidity, a brief scolding from others, or both. In this way, the (A)□□□□□□ of sitcoms acted as a cost-effective means to encourage (B)□□□□□□□□□□ of a more pluralistic and tolerant society.
*bigot: 편견이 아주 심한 사람 **pluralistic: 다원적인
subjective_conditions: 본문에서 찾아 쓸 것
questions.explanation: 시트콤은 사회적 갈등을 유머(humor)를 통해 다룸으로써 진보적인 가치에 대한 수용(acceptance)을 높이는 역할을 했다는 내용입니다. 지문 내의 'humour(영국식 표기이나 지문 근거)' 또는 'humour', 'acceptance'가 빈칸에 들어갈 핵심어입니다. (단, 답안에는 지문의 철자를 따르는 것이 일반적이나 humor로 기재된 경우도 인정될 수 있음)

questions.question: 26. 다음 글을 한 문장으로 요약할 때, 빈칸 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 한 단어를 각각 지문에서 찾아 쓰시오.
questions.passage:
For years, many psychologists have held strongly to the belief that the key to addressing negative health habits is to change behavior. This, more than values and attitudes, is the part of personality that is easiest to change. Ingestive habits such as smoking, drinking and various eating behaviors are the most common health concerns targeted for behavioral changes. Process-addiction behaviors (workaholism, shopaholism, and the like) fall into this category as well. Mental imagery combined with power of suggestion was taken up as the premise of behavioral medicine to help people change negative health behaviors into positive ones. Although this technique alone will not produce changes, when used alongside other behavior modification tactics and coping strategies, behavioral changes have proved effective for some people. What mental imagery does is reinforce a new desired behavior. Repeated use of images reinforces the desired behavior more strongly over time.
*ingestive: (음식) 섭취의 **premise: 전제
questions.summary_sentence: Psychologists believe that changing (A)____________, especially through techniques like (B)____________ imagery and suggestion, can effectively help people improve (C)____________ health habits when combined with other strategies.
questions.explanation: 이 글은 부정적인 건강 습관을 해결하기 위해 행동을 변화시키는 것이 중요하며, 특히 정신적 이미지(mental imagery) 기법을 다른 행동 수정 전략과 병용할 때 효과적이라는 내용을 담고 있습니다. 요약문에서 (A)는 심리학자들이 변화시켜야 한다고 믿는 대상인 '행동(behavior)', (B)는 이미지 기법을 수식하는 '정신적인(mental)', (C)는 개선해야 할 대상인 '부정적인(negative)' 건강 습관이 적절합니다.

questions.question: 27. 다음 글의 문맥상 빈칸(A)에 들어갈 말을 <보기>의 단어들을 한 번씩 사용하여 배열하시오.
questions.passage:
We must explore the relationship between children's film production and consumption habits. The term "children's film" implies ownership by children ─ their cinema ─ but films supposedly made for children have always been consumed by audiences of all ages, particularly in commercial cinemas. The considerable crossover in audience composition for children's films can be shown by the fact that, in 2007, eleven Danish children's and youth films attracted 59 per cent of theatrical admissions, and in 2014, German children's films comprised seven out of the top twenty films at the national box office. This phenomenon corresponds with a broader, international embrace of what is seemingly children's culture among audiences of diverse ages. The old prejudice that children's film is some other realm, separate from (and forever subordinate to) a more legitimate cinema for adults is not supported by the realities of consumption: children's film sits __________ ________________________.
*subordinate: 하위의
subjective_conditions: 보기의 단어들을 한 번씩 사용할 것
vocabulary_box: of contemporary
at
popular
the center
culture
questions.answer: at the center of contemporary popular culture
questions.explanation: 이 글은 어린이 영화가 실제로는 모든 연령대의 관객에게 소비되고 있으며, 이는 어린이 영화가 성인 영화와 분리된 하위 영역이 아니라는 것을 보여준다고 설명합니다. 따라서 빈칸에는 어린이 영화가 현대 대중문화의 중심에 있다는 의미가 들어가야 합니다. 주어진 단어를 조합하면 'at the center of contemporary popular culture'가 됩니다.

questions.question: 28. 다음 글에서 밑줄 친 the leading edge of our thought가 의미하는 바를, <보기>의 단어들을 한 번씩 사용하여 배열하시오. (단, 필요한 경우 단어의 형태를 바꿀 것)
questions.passage:
When we realize we've said something in error and we pause to go back to correct it, we stop gesturing a couple of hundred milliseconds before we stop speaking. Such sequences suggest the startling notion that our hands "know" what we're going to say before our conscious minds do. Gesture can mentally prime a word so that the right term comes to our lips. When people are prevented from gesturing, they talk less fluently; their speech becomes halting because their hands are no longer able to supply them with the next word, and the next. Not being able to gesture has other deleterious effects: without gesture to help our mental processes along, we remember less useful information, we solve problems less well, and we are less able to explain our thinking. Far from tagging along as speech's clumsy companion, gesture represents <u>the leading edge of our thought</u>.
*startling: 놀라운 **deleterious: 해로운
subjective_conditions: 보기의 단어들을 한 번씩 사용하여 배열할 것
필요한 경우 단어의 형태를 바꿀 것
vocabulary_box: force in
processes
our
a guiding
think
questions.answer: a guiding force in our thinking processes
questions.explanation: 지문에서 제스처는 말보다 먼저 일어나고 단어를 떠올리게 하며 사고 과정을 돕는 역할을 한다고 설명합니다. 따라서 밑줄 친 '우리 사고의 선도적인 모서리'라는 표현은 제스처가 사고 과정에서 안내하는 역할을 하는 힘이라는 의미입니다. 'think'를 'thinking'으로 변형하여 'a guiding force in our thinking processes'로 완성할 수 있습니다.

questions.question: 29. 다음 글에서 어법상 어색한 한 부분을 찾아, 이를 바르게 고쳐 쓰시오.
questions.passage: Empathy is frequently listed as one of the most desired skills in an employer or employee. although without specifying exactly what is meant by empathy. Most businesses stress empathy, emphasizing the need for leaders to understand the perspective of employees and customers when negotiating deals and making decisions. When some consultants argue that successful companies foster empathy, what that translates to is that companies should conduct good market research. In other words, an "emphatic" company understands the needs and wants of its customers and seek to fulfill those needs and wants. When some people speak of design with empathy, what that translates to is that companies should take into account the specific needs of different populations ─ the blind, the deaf, the elderly, non-English speakers, the color-blind, and so on ─ when designing products.
questions.explanation: 이 문장의 주어는 'an "emphatic" company'로 3인칭 단수 형태입니다. 접속사 and에 의해 첫 번째 동사인 understands와 병렬 구조를 이루어야 하므로, 복수 동사 형태인 seek를 3인칭 단수 현재 시제에 맞는 seeks로 고쳐야 어법상 적절합니다.

questions.question: 1. 다음 글의 목적으로 가장 적절한 것은? [3.2점]
questions.passage: In our competitive society, many people believe that only the biggest or the strongest can survive and thrive. However, I propose an alternative view: kindness is the key to success. Isn't that a comforting thought? We can use the power of our natural kindness to communicate and cooperate with different individuals. We can all benefit from this instead of trying to be better than others. I'd like to end this talk with a message. Think of our society as a bouquet. Just as each flower adds to the beauty when it harmonizes with the others, each person can contribute to a more beautiful world when they cooperate. By being kind and working together, we can truly flourish. Thank you for your attention.
options: ① 친절과 협력의 중요성을 강조하려고
② 꽃다발을 구입할 때 주의점을 안내하려고
③ 강자만이 살아남을 수 있는 사회를 비판하려고
④ 경쟁적인 사회에서 생존하는 방법을 알려주려고
⑤ 강연에서 사용할 수 있는 적절한 비유법을 소개하려고
questions.explanation: 필자는 경쟁적인 사회에서 살아남기 위해 가장 크거나 강해야 한다는 일반적인 믿음 대신 친절이 성공의 열쇠임을 제안하고 있습니다. 사회를 꽃다발에 비유하며 사람들이 조화롭게 협력할 때 더 아름다운 세상을 만들고 함께 번영할 수 있음을 강조하고 있으므로 글의 목적으로 ①번이 가장 적절합니다.

questions.question: 3. 밑줄 친 <u>be emotionally invested in a character</u>가 다음 글에서 의미하는 바로 가장 적절한 것은? [4.3점]
questions.passage:
What does it mean for a character to be a hero as opposed to a villain? In artistic and entertainment descriptions, it's essential for the author to establish a positive relationship between a protagonist and the audience. In order for tragedy or misfortune to draw out an emotional response in viewers, the character must be adjusted so as to be recognizable as either friend or enemy. Whether the portrayal is fictional or documentary, we must feel that the protagonist is someone whose actions benefit us; the protagonist is, or would be, a worthy companion or valued ally. Violent action films are often filled with dozens of incidental deaths of minor characters that draw out little response in the audience. In order to feel strong emotions, the audience must <u>be emotionally invested in a character</u> as either ally or enemy.
* villain: 악당 ** protagonist: 주인공
options: ① be uninterested in the character's fate
② feel strong hostility toward the character's job
③ be indifferent to what happens to the character
④ feel connected to and care about the character
⑤ focus more on the author than on the character
questions.explanation: 글의 맥락에서 관객이 주인공의 비극이나 불행에 대해 감정적인 반응을 보이기 위해서는 해당 인물을 친구나 적과 같은 구체적인 대상으로 인식해야 한다고 설명합니다. 'be emotionally invested in a character'는 관객이 등장인물에게 감정적으로 몰입하는 것, 즉 인물과 정서적으로 연결되어 있다고 느끼고 관심을 갖는 것을 의미하므로 ④번이 정답입니다.
options_translation: ① 캐릭터의 운명에 무관심하다
② 캐릭터의 직업에 강한 적대감을 느낀다
③ 캐릭터에게 일어나는 일에 무관심하다
④ 캐릭터와 연결되어 있다고 느끼고 관심을 갖는다
⑤ 캐릭터보다 작가에게 더 집중한다

questions.question: [7~8] 다음 글의 제목으로 가장 적절한 것을 고르시오. [3.5점]
questions.passage: I'll give you another example of how friendliness is related to survival. Dr. Hare and his colleagues designed an experiment with chimpanzees and bonobos. Although the two are genetically similar, they are different in nature. To study their cooperative behavior, Dr. Hare's team set up a device which required two individuals to pull both ends of a rope at the same time in order to access food on a board. When placed with partners that the chimpanzees knew, they were able to work together to get the food. However, when paired with new partners, the chimpanzees usually failed to get the food, and when they occasionally succeeded, they did not share the food with their partner. The bonobos, on the other hand, got along much better than the chimpanzees. They solved the problem regardless of which individual they were paired with, and they were also more willing to share the food. This research shows that bonobos have a cooperative and friendly nature. Experts suggest that their nature has helped their species survive. Without these characteristics, they could have faced extinction.
options: ① Friendliness as a Survival Strategy: Lessons from Bonobos
② Why Chimpanzees Rule Where Bonobos Fail as a Species
③ Extinction of the Friendliest: Bonobos vs. Chimpanzees
④ Importance of Defeating Your Enemy at the First Opportunity
⑤ The Power of Aggression: How Chimpanzees Thrive Through Competition
questions.explanation: 이 글은 보노보의 우호적이고 협동적인 본성이 종의 생존에 결정적인 역할을 했음을 침팬지와의 실험 비교를 통해 설명하고 있습니다. 침팬지는 낯선 파트너와 협력하지 못하고 음식을 나누지 않은 반면, 보노보는 누구와도 잘 협력하며 음식을 나누는 모습을 보여주었습니다. 따라서 '생존 전략으로서의 우호성'을 다룬 1번이 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 생존 전략으로서의 우호성: 보노보에게서 얻는 교훈
② 보노보가 종으로서 실패하는 곳에서 침팬지가 지배하는 이유
③ 가장 친절한 자의 멸종: 보노보 대 침팬지
④ 첫 번째 기회에 적을 물리치는 것의 중요성
⑤ 공격성의 힘: 침팬지가 경쟁을 통해 번성하는 방법

questions.question: 10-11. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 어법상 틀린 것을 고르시오. 10. [3.3점]
questions.passage: The responsive behavior of dogs caught the attention of an evolutionary anthropologist, Brian Hare. He ① <u>conducting</u> an experiment to see how dogs would respond to human gestures compared to wolves, who share the same common ancestor. He placed two cups on the ground with food hidden under only one of them. When he pointed to the cup with the food, the dogs found it ② <u>easily</u>. The wolves, however, struggled and chose cups at random, paying no attention to his gestures. Dr. Hare concluded ③ <u>that</u> the dogs’ ability to read human gestures allowed them to perform better than the wolves. He explained that dogs, unlike wolves, have developed communicative skills with humans and a sense of friendliness. This explanation sounds ④ <u>reasonable</u> according to several evolutionary biologists. They say that from the common ancestors of these two species, those that acted friendly toward humans evolved into dogs, and those that didn’t became wolves. Furthermore, Dr. Hare suggested that the friendly nature of dogs probably provided them a survival advantage that allowed their population to grow larger than ⑤ <u>that</u> of wolves.
questions.explanation: 해당 문장의 주어는 He이며, 뒤에 이어지는 구절에서 본동사 역할을 할 단어가 필요합니다. 현재분사 형태인 conducting은 단독으로 동사 역할을 할 수 없으므로, 과거 시제 동사인 conducted로 고쳐야 어법상 적절합니다.

questions.question: 12-13. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것을 고르시오. 12. [3.7점]
questions.passage: Piaget put the same amount of water into two different glasses: a tall narrow glass and a wide glass, then asked kids to ① <u>compare</u> two glasses. Kids younger than six or seven usually say that the ② <u>taller</u> glass contains more water, due to its higher water level. And when they are ready, they figure out the conservation of volume for themselves just by playing with cups of water. Piaget argued that children’s understanding of morality is like their understanding of those water glasses: we can’t say that it is ③ <u>inherent</u> or kids learn it directly from adults. Rather, it is ④ <u>self-constructed</u> as kids play with other kids. Taking turns in a game is like pouring water back and forth between glasses. Once kids have reached the age of five or six, then playing games and working things out together will help them learn about fairness far ⑤ <u>less</u> effectively than any teaching from adults.
questions.explanation: 글의 맥락상 아이들의 도덕성 이해는 어른이 직접 가르쳐주는 것이 아니라 또래와 놀며 스스로 구성해가는 과정입니다. 따라서 또래와 함께 게임을 하고 문제를 해결하는 과정이 어른의 가르침보다 '더(more)' 효과적으로 공정함을 배우게 해준다는 내용이 적절하므로, less를 more로 고쳐야 합니다.

questions.question: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것을 고르시오. 13. [3.2점]
questions.passage: Now let’s turn our attention to ourselves, Homo sapiens. How have we managed to survive for so long? Neanderthals existed together with Homo sapiens until about 40,000 years ago, and they were known to be ① <u>unintelligent</u> and physically superior to Homo sapiens. Neanderthals were able to make tools and fire and had strong bodies with ② <u>well-developed</u> muscles and broad shoulders. ③ <u>Despite</u> the advantageous characteristics of Neanderthals, however, it was Homo sapiens who ultimately survived and thrived. One possible explanation is that our ancestors lived in larger communities that ④ <u>promoted</u> cooperation and the free exchange of knowledge, while Neanderthals tended to live in smaller groups. These social ⑤ <u>differences</u> may have given Homo sapiens a competitive advantage over Neanderthals, allowing them to adapt to an ever-changing environment.
questions.explanation: 네안데르탈인은 도구와 불을 사용할 수 있었으며, 신체적으로 매우 우수했습니다. 지문 전체의 논지는 네안데르탈인이 지능이 낮거나 신체적으로 열등해서 멸종한 것이 아니라, 사피엔스의 사회적 협력 능력이 더 우수했기 때문이라는 것입니다. 따라서 네안데르탈인이 단순히 'unintelligent(지능이 낮은)'하다고 설명하는 것은 글의 흐름상 어색하며, 보통은 '지능적이고 신체적으로 우수했음에도 불구하고'라는 대조의 맥락이 필요하므로 intelligent 등으로 고치는 것이 적절합니다.

questions.question: 14. (A), (B), (C)의 각 네모 안에서 문맥에 맞는 낱말로 가장 적절한 것은? [3.5점]
questions.passage: Recent brain imaging methods like fMRI (functional Magnetic Resonance Imaging) show that reading aloud (A) [ activates / disables ] multiple parts of the brain. When we speak and hear our own voice, the brain regions responsible for these tasks become highly active, helping brain cells form stronger connections and (B) [ undermining / boosting ] mental performance. This leads to an overall improvement in concentration. Reading aloud is also a good way to develop your public speaking skills because it forces you to read each and every word - something people don't often do when reading quickly, or reading in silence. It is especially important for children to read aloud, as their brains develop through (C) [ positive / negative ] interactions like singing, touching, and speaking, which create strong learning pathways.
options: ① activates ... undermining ... negative
② activates ... boosting ... positive
③ activates ... boosting ... negative
④ disables ... boosting ... positive
⑤ disables ... undermining ... negative
questions.explanation: (A) fMRI와 같은 뇌 영상 기술이 낭독이 뇌의 여러 부위를 활성화(activates)한다는 것을 보여주며, (B) 이러한 뇌 활동이 세포 간의 연결을 강화하여 정신적 성과를 증진(boosting)시키고, (C) 노래, 촉각, 말하기와 같은 긍정적인(positive) 상호작용을 통해 어린이의 뇌가 발달한다는 흐름이 적절합니다.

questions.question: 다음 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것을 고르시오. [3.7점]
questions.passage: There is a wealth of evidence that when parents, teachers, supervisors, and coaches are perceived as involved and caring, people feel happier and more motivated. And it is not just those people with power - we need to feel valued and respected by peers and coworkers. Thus, when the need for relatedness is met, motivation and internalization are fueled, provided that support for autonomy and competence are also there. If we are trying to motivate others, _________ is a crucial basis from which to begin. And when we are trying to motivate ourselves, doing things to enhance a sense of connectedness to others can be crucial to long-term persistence. So exercise with a friend, call someone when you have a difficult decision to make, and be there as a support for others as they take on challenges.
options: ① a caring relationship
② determination to succeed
③ recognition from their superiors
④ pushing them to their limits
⑤ internalization of their goals
questions.explanation: 글 전체적으로 타인과의 유대감(relatedness)과 보살핌(caring)이 행복과 동기부여에 큰 영향을 미친다고 설명하고 있습니다. 따라서 타인을 동기부여할 때 'a caring relationship(보살펴주는 관계)'이 시작을 위한 결정적인 토대가 된다는 것이 문맥상 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 보살펴주는 관계
② 성공하려는 결의
③ 상사로부터의 인정
④ 그들을 한계까지 몰아붙이는 것
⑤ 목표의 내면화

questions.question: 18. 다음 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은? [4.1점]
questions.passage:
The science we learn in grade school is a collection of certainties about the natural world - the earth goes around the sun, DNA carries the information of an organism, and so on. Only when you start to learn the practice of science do you realize that each of these "facts" was hard won through a succession of logical inferences based upon many observations or experiments. The process of science is more about reducing the uncertainties in what we know than __________________________. Our uncertainties can be greater or lesser for any given piece of knowledge depending upon where we are in that process - today we are quite certain of how an apple will fall from a tree, but our understanding of the turbulent fluid flow remains a work in progress after more than a century of effort.
* inference: 추론 ** turbulent fluid flow: 난류 유동
options: ① facing uncertainty with confidence
② gathering scattered pieces of knowledge
③ exploring the connections between pieces of knowledge
④ clearly defining the boundary between certainty and uncertainty
⑤ explaining and reasoning about observable phenomena using scientific knowledge
questions.explanation: 이 글은 초등학교에서 배우는 과학이 '확실성'의 집합체로 보이지만, 실제 과학의 과정은 우리가 아는 것 속에서 불확실성을 줄여가는 과정임을 설명하고 있습니다. 따라서 빈칸에는 과학의 일반적인 오해인 '확실한 지식을 단순히 수집하는 것'이라는 내용이 들어가는 것이 적절합니다. 'collection of certainties'와 유사한 의미를 지닌 ②번 '흩어진 지식의 파편들을 모으는 것'이 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 자신 있게 불확실성에 직면하는 것
② 흩어진 지식의 파편들을 모으는 것
③ 지식의 파편들 사이의 연결고리를 탐구하는 것
④ 확실성과 불확실성 사이의 경계를 명확하게 정의하는 것
⑤ 과학적 지식을 사용하여 관찰 가능한 현상을 설명하고 추론하는 것

questions.question: 19. 다음 글에서 전체 흐름과 관계 없는 문장을 고르시오. [3.4점]
questions.passage:
The rise of air-conditioning accelerated the construction of sealed boxes, where the building's only airflow is through the filtered ducts of the air-conditioning unit. It doesn't have to be this way. Look at any old building in a hot climate, whether it's in Sicily or Marrakesh or Tehran. Architects understood the importance of shade, airflow, light colors. They oriented buildings to capture cool breezes and block the worst heat of the afternoon. ① They built with thick walls and white roofs and transoms over doors to encourage airflow. ② Anyone who has ever spent a few minutes in a mudbrick house in Tucson, or walked on the narrow streets of old Seville, knows how well these construction methods work. ③ Air conditioners can reduce mortality rates due to higher temperature. ④ But all this wisdom about how to deal with heat, accumulated over centuries of practical experience, is all too often ignored. ⑤ In this sense, air-conditioning is not just a technology of personal comfort; it is also a technology of forgetting.
* accumulate: 축적하다 ** duct: (배)관 *** transom: 채광
questions.explanation: 이 글은 에어컨의 보급으로 인해 과거의 지혜로운 건축 방식(통풍, 그늘 등 자연 냉방 방식)이 잊히고 있다는 점을 비판적으로 다루고 있습니다. ③번 문장은 에어컨이 높은 기온으로 인한 사망률을 줄일 수 있다는 에어컨의 긍정적인 효과를 언급하고 있으므로, 과거의 건축적 지혜가 잊히고 있다는 전체 흐름과 관계가 없습니다.

questions.question: 20. 다음 글에서 전체 흐름과 관계 없는 문장을 고르시오. [3.4점]
questions.passage:
In the course of trying to solve a problem with an invention, you may encounter a brick wall of resistance when you try to think your way logically through the problem. Such logical thinking is a linear type of process, which uses our reasoning skills. ① This works fine when we're operating in the area of what we know or have experienced. ② However, when we need to deal with new information, ideas, and viewpoints, linear thinking will often come up short. ③ On the other hand, creativity by definition involves the application of new information to old problems and the conception of new viewpoints and ideas. ④ For this you will be most effective if you learn to operate in a nonlinear manner; that is, use your creative brain. ⑤ Using both linear and nonlinear thinking together is an effective way to engage the brain. Stated differently, if you think in a linear manner, you'll tend to be conservative and keep coming up with techniques which are already known. This, of course, is just what you don't want.
* linear: 선형의 ** conservative: 보수적인
questions.explanation: 이 글은 새로운 문제를 해결할 때 논리적이고 선형적인 사고의 한계를 지적하며 비선형적이고 창의적인 사고가 필요함을 강조하고 있습니다. ①~④번은 선형적 사고와 창의적 사고를 대조하며 창의적 사고의 필요성을 설명하고 있으며, 마지막 문장 또한 선형적 사고의 보수성을 경계하고 있습니다. 하지만 ⑤번 문장은 두 사고방식을 함께 사용하는 것이 효과적이라는 일반적인 뇌 활용법을 제시하고 있어 논점의 흐름을 벗어납니다.

questions.question: 21. 주어진 글 다음에 이어질 글의 순서로 가장 적절한 것을 고르시오. [3.2점]
questions.passage: For some time, my grandfather had been busy writing down the village genealogy, known as the whakapapa. The whakapapa had been in his old house.
ordered_passages: (A) Then his voice suddenly stopped in the middle of the chant. The village waited in worried silence until the next name burst out of his mouth. It took Nani Tama almost two years to gather most of the whakapapa, but there were still missing names he needed to fill in.

(B) But then came the night of the fire, which ran through the house and destroyed our past. In only one night, everything we knew was gone. Nani Tama, in despair, went to stay with his daughter, my Auntie Hiraina. Trying to find a way out of the ashes of the past, Nani began to write the whakapapa again with his shaky hands.

(C) He chanted the names of the ancestors, joining the past to the present once more. The village went quiet and listened to his chanting. His voice traveled along the lines of our genealogy, searching back across the centuries. Sometimes, there were lines that were difficult to remember.
questions.explanation: 주어진 글에서 할아버지가 마을의 족보(whakapapa)를 쓰고 있었고 그것이 옛집에 있었다고 언급됩니다. (B) 화재로 인해 집과 족보가 소실되었고, 할아버지는 딸의 집으로 옮겨 다시 족보를 쓰기 시작했다는 내용이 먼저 옵니다. (C) 할아버지가 조상들의 이름을 읊조리며 기억을 되살리고 마을 사람들이 이를 경청하는 장면이 이어집니다. (A) 읊조림 도중 기억이 나지 않아 잠시 멈췄다가 다시 이어가는 구체적인 상황과, 2년 후에도 여전히 빈 부분이 있다는 내용으로 마무리되는 것이 자연스럽습니다.

questions.question: 22. 다음 주어진 문장에 이어질 글의 순서로 가장 적절한 것은? [3.7점]
questions.passage: Promotion deals with consumer psychology.
ordered_passages: (A) In fact, consumers fooled once can do damage to sales as they relate their experience to others. Instead, marketers now know that their goal is to identify the consumers who are most likely to appreciate a good or service, and to promote that good or service in a way that makes the value clear to the consumer. Therefore, marketers must know where the potential consumers are, and how to reach them.
(B) We can't force people to think one way or another, and the clever marketer knows that promotion is used to provide information in the most clear, honest, and simple fashion possible.

(C) By doing so, the possibility of increasing sales goes up. Gone are the days when promotions were done in order to fool the consumer into purchasing something. The long-term effect of getting a consumer to buy something they did not really want or need wasn't good.
questions.explanation: 주어진 문장은 홍보가 소비자 심리를 다룬다는 도입부입니다. (B)는 영리한 마케터가 정직하고 명확한 정보 제공을 위해 홍보를 사용해야 함을 언급하며 생각을 강요할 수 없음을 설명합니다. (C)는 '그렇게 함으로써(By doing so - (B)의 정직한 방식)' 판매가 증가할 수 있다고 연결하며 과거의 기만적인 홍보 방식의 문제점을 지적합니다. (A)는 기만당한 소비자가 초래할 수 있는 손해를 언급하며 현대 마케터가 지향해야 할 목표(가치 전달 및 잠재 고객 도달)로 글을 마무리합니다. 따라서 적절한 순서는 (B)-(C)-(A)입니다.

23. 주어진 글 (A)에 이어질 내용을 순서에 맞게 배열한 것으로 가장 적절한 것은? [3.2점]
questions.passage:
(A)

When I arrived at Auntie's place, I was shocked to see how thin (a) <u>Nani Tama</u> was. "Look, Nani," I said. "I'm not taking you anywhere. You could die on me!" Nani looked at me in anger. "You want me to die here in this room? Looking at these four walls? When the whakapapa is not yet finished?" The old man held on tightly to the side of the bed and cried out as he stood up.
ordered_passages: (B) Just before noon, we arrived at a small town called Murupara. "Where do we go now?" I asked Nani. He did not reply, but he was searching inside (b) himself, staring at the small houses. Then, at a street corner, he told us to turn. After turning the corner, we saw an old man standing in front of a house. He welcomed Nani Tama with a gentle smile, but in his eyes, I saw the message, "We must hurry." Now that day seems like a dream to me.

(C) Every slow, painful step hurt him, but he tried to walk. I could not help but carry him to the car, and we set off with Auntie. We traveled all night, mostly in silence, listening to Nani chanting in the darkness. It was strange but wonderful to hear (c) him. Sometimes, he burst into a song that he had taught Auntie. They sang together, lifting up their voices to send the song flying like a bird through the sky.

(D) It was early morning and still dark when we returned to Auntie's place. All the lights were on, and the village people were waiting for us. Smiling, Nani Tama lifted up the whakapapa and offered it to the village. Our hearts were full because (d) our grandfather had saved our past for us. Our Nani Tama smiled again. His smile grew tired. He sighed. "At last, I may go now." Then, he closed his eyes. "No, Dad!" Auntie Hiraina cried. The sun burst across the hills.

(E) I remember the two old men sitting at the table and the soft sounds of the Maori words as they talked. All through the quiet afternoon and into the evening, they recalled missing names. I had a strange feeling that there were other people in the room. I felt as if people from the past were looking over the shoulders of the two old men to see if the work was correct. Finally, they stopped. It was done. After a moment of silence, (e) the old man whispered to Nani, "Goodbye, friend." Crying, they pressed their noses together to say goodbye.
questions.explanation: (A)에서 족보를 완성하기 위해 길을 떠나기로 결심한 후, (C)에서 차를 타고 밤새 이동하며 노래를 부릅니다. (B)에서 목적지에 도착해 한 노인을 만나고, (E)에서 두 노인이 함께 족보 작업을 마친 뒤 작별 인사를 나눕니다. 마지막으로 (D)에서 마을로 돌아와 완성된 족보를 전달하고 할아버지가 평온하게 숨을 거둡니다. 따라서 순서는 (C)-(B)-(E)-(D)가 가장 적절합니다.

questions.question: 1. 윗글의 ⓐ ~ ⓔ 중 어법상 적절하지 않은 것의 개수는? [3.5점]
questions.passage:
Noise-cancelling technology is not only used in music devices. Other fields also take advantage of this technology, such as ticket offices at tourist attractions which are often very noisy. Microphones are installed in ticket offices to detect external noise, and an opposite sound wave is generated and transmitted through a speaker, ⓐ <u>enabling the ticket agent to hear the customer's voice clearly</u>. Another area in which this technology is used is drive-through fast-food restaurants and coffee shops. They use noise-cancelling headsets to improve communication between employees and customers by eliminating vehicle noise. ⓑ <u>These noise-cancelling headsets help drive-through employees to take orders accurately.</u> The same technology is also used for cars, which audio systems generate waves to cancel out unpleasant sounds such as engine, wind, and road noise. Thanks to noise-cancelling devices, ⓒ <u>drivers can focus</u> on driving without being disturbed by distracting noises.
As technology advances, many people expect it will solve various social issues caused by noise pollution. A common source of these problems is noisy neighbors, as ⓓ <u>the noise that they make</u> can lead to conflict among residents. Noise-cancellation technology can help address these problems by reducing unwanted disturbances, allowing people to ⓔ <u>lead more peaceful and healthier lives</u>.

② 2개

④ 4개

questions.passage: No respectable boss would say, "I make it a point to discourage my staff from ⓐ <u>speaking up</u>, and I maintain a culture that prevents disagreeing viewpoints from ever ⓑ <u>getting aired</u>." If anything, most bosses even say that they are ⓒ <u>pro-dissent</u>. This idea can be found throughout the series of conversations with leaders. In the interviews, the featured leaders are asked about their management techniques, and regularly claim to continually ⓓ <u>encourage</u> internal protest from more junior staffers. As Bot Pittman remarked in one of these conversations: "I want us to listen to these dissenters because they may intend to tell you why we can't do something, but if you ⓔ <u>listen hard</u>, what they're really telling you is what you must do to get something done."
options: ① ⓐ: expressing opinions or ideas freely
② ⓑ: being kept private or hidden
③ ⓒ: not supportive of opposing ideas

questions.question: [서답형 2] 윗글의 밑줄 친 ⓐ를 <조건>에 맞게 변형하시오. [3.0점]
questions.passage:
Which is the better environment for studying: a noisy place or a quiet place? ⓐ People seldom want to put up with a lot of noise because it can be unpleasant and distracting. Fortunately, scientists have invented noise-cancelling technology, which is now being used across various fields to reduce unwanted noise. What is the scientific principle behind this achievement? To understand this, let's examine how sound travels.

Sound is produced through vibrations that occur from a sound source, when the strings of a guitar are played, for instance. The vibrations of the sound source cause the air to vibrate and the sound to travel as waves, similar to the ripples created in a lake when you throw a stone. When these sound waves reach our ears, the brain interprets them as sound. Just as different ripples in water might overlap if you throw two stones, sound waves can also interfere with each other when they meet. There are two types of interference: constructive and destructive. Constructive interference occurs when the peaks of two waves overlap, resulting in a bigger wave and a louder sound. Destructive interference, on the other hand, occurs when a peak of one wave overlaps with a valley of another wave, so they cancel each other out and produce a quieter sound, or no sound at all.

Destructive interference is used in the noise-cancelling feature of headphones when we listen to music. Inside the headphones are microphones and noise-cancelling circuitry. The microphones pick up sounds from the outside, and the circuitry analyzes them to produce opposite sound waves. For example, if outside noise has a value of +1, the circuitry will generate an opposite noise of -1 and transmit it to the speakers. ( ㉠ ) This cancels out the unwanted sound even in noisy surroundings, so you can hear the music sound clearly without turning up the volume. ( ㉡ ) However, it is not easy to entirely eliminate external noise with this technology. ( ㉢ ) To achieve full noise cancellation, the circuitry must convert the noise into digital data and instantly transmit the opposite sound to the speakers as soon as the noise reaches the microphones. ( ㉣ ) Therefore, this noise-cancellation technology is effective for predictable sounds like those of car engines and subways that occur regularly or over a period of time. ( ㉤ )

2. 4개의 단어로 작성할 것.
3. 주어를 대명사로 바꾸지 않을 것.
4. 대소문자 구분 없음.
5. 철자 오류 시 0점 처리하며 부분 점수 없음.
6. 조건을 어길 시 0점 처리함.

questions.passage: With no horses available, the Inca empire excelled at delivering messages on foot. The messengers were stationed on the royal roads to deliver the Inca king's orders and reports coming from his lands. Called Chasquis, they lived in groups of four to six in huts, placed from one to two miles apart along the roads. They were all young men and especially good runners who watched the road in both directions. If they caught sight of another messenger coming, they hurried out to meet them. The Inca built the huts on high ground, in sight of one another. When a messenger neared the next hut, he began to call out and repeated the message three or four times to the one who was running out to meet him so that the message would not be forgotten or misunderstood. The Inca empire could relay messages 1,000 miles (1,610 km) in three or four days under good conditions.

questions.passage:
Consider the seemingly simple question How many senses are there? Around 2,370 years ago, Aristotle wrote that there are five, in both humans and animals — sight, hearing, smell, taste, and touch. However, according to the philosopher Fiona Macpherson, there are reasons to doubt it. For a start, Aristotle missed a few in humans: the perception of your own body which is different from touch and the sense of balance which has links to both touch and vision. Other animals have senses that are even harder to categorize. Many vertebrates have a different sense system for detecting odors. Some snakes can detect the body heat of their prey. These examples tell us that "senses cannot be clearly divided into a limited number of specific kinds," Macpherson wrote in The Senses. Instead of trying to _________,
we should study them for what they are.
options: ① follow the lessons on senses from Aristotle
② compare animal senses with human senses
③ accept Fiona's ideas concerning human senses
④ keep a balanced view to understand real senses
⑤ sort a variety of animal senses into more than five categories

questions.passage: A number of research studies have shown how experts in a field often ⓐ struggle when introducing newcomers to that field. For example, in a genuine training situation, Dr Pamela Hinds found that people expert in using mobile phones were remarkably ⓑ less accurate than novice phone users in judging how long it takes people to learn to use the phones. Experts can become ⓒ insensitive to how hard a task is for the beginner, an effect referred to as the 'curse of knowledge'. Dr Hinds was able to show that as people acquired the skill, they then began to ⓓ overestimate the level of difficulty of that skill. Her participants even did not accurately ⓔ remember how long it had taken them to acquire that skill in an earlier session. <u>전문가들이 그것이 얼마나 어려웠는지를 잊어버린다는 것을 우리가 안다면</u> for them to learn, we can understand the need to look at the learning process through students' eyes, rather than making assumptions about how students 'should be' learning.

questions.question: 9. 다음 글을 읽고 한 학생이 글을 작성하였다. 밑줄 친 부분 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은? [4.0점]
questions.passage:
Norms are everywhere, defining what is "normal" and guiding our interpretations of social life at every turn. For example, there is a norm in Anglo society to say Thank you to strangers who have just done something to help, such as open a door for you, point out that you've just dropped something, or give you directions. There is no law that forces you to say Thank you. But if people don't say Thank you in these cases it is marked. People expect that you will say it. You become responsible. Failing to say it will be both surprising and worthy of criticism. Not knowing the norms of another community is the central problem of cross-cultural communication. To continue the Thank you example, even though another culture may have an expression that appears translatable (many don't), there may be different norms for its usage, for example, such that you should say Thank you only when the cost someone has caused is substantial. Otherwise, it might sound ridiculous in that cultural context.

After reading about cultural norms in communication -especially how they shape what is considered "normal" behavior-I learned that saying "thank you" is a ① <u>common</u> expectation in many Western societies. For example, as the passage explains, in Anglo cultures, people usually say "thank you" to strangers who do ② <u>small</u> helpful things like giving directions. Even though it's not ③ <u>required</u> by law, people still expect it, and not saying it might be seen as rude. The reading also pointed out that one of the biggest challenges in cross-cultural communication is not knowing the social norms of other communities, which can easily lead to ④ <u>misunderstandings</u>.
After reading this, I became curious and did some additional research about how gratitude is expressed in different countries. That's how I learned more about Japan and its unique thank-you culture. In Japanese society, people may not say "thank you" (arigatou gozaimasu) for small acts, such as someone holding a door open or pointing something out. Instead, gratitude is more often expressed when the other person has made a ⑤ <u>insignificant</u> effort or done something meaningful. Understanding this, I will be careful not to say "thank you" too casually or frequently, as I might do in my own culture.
questions.explanation: 글의 맥락상 일본 사회에서는 사소한 행동(small acts)에 대해서는 감사를 표하지 않을 수 있으며, 대신 상대방이 '의미 있는(meaningful)' 일을 했거나 상당한 노력을 기울였을 때 감사를 표한다고 설명하고 있습니다. 따라서 ⑤ 'insignificant(사소한, 하찮은)'는 'significant(상당한, 중요한)' 혹은 'substantial'과 같은 단어로 바뀌어야 문맥상 적절합니다.

questions.question: 10. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분에 해당하는 예시로 가장 적절한 것은? [3.9점]
questions.passage: One of the most striking characteristics of a sleeping animal or person is that they do not respond normally to environmental stimuli. If you open the eyelids of a sleeping mammal the eyes will not see normally - they are functionally blind. Some visual information apparently gets in, but it is not normally processed as it is shortened or weakened; same with the other sensing systems. Stimuli are registered but not processed normally and they fail to wake the individual. Perceptual disengagement probably serves the function of protecting sleep, so some authors do not count it as part of the definition of sleep itself. But as sleep would be impossible without it, it seems essential to its definition. Nevertheless, many animals (including humans) use the intermediate state of drowsiness to derive some benefits of sleep without <u>total perceptual disengagement</u>.
options: ① Cats often nap throughout the day. When they are in light sleep, they still may respond to some stimuli, but they often ignore minor environmental changes like background noise or movement.
② Some fish, like certain types of sharks, enter a deep sleep state where they are completely unresponsive to external stimuli. They may appear still or motionless while resting.
③ Bats often sleep hanging upside down in dark, quiet places. They are inactive during the day but are able to wake quickly when disturbed by movement or noise.
④ Giraffes often sleep while standing, and even when they lie down to sleep, they can quickly react to any potential danger from predators.
⑤ Many birds, such as pigeons, remain responsive to changes in their environment even during periods of sleep.
questions.explanation: 밑줄 친 'total perceptual disengagement(완전한 지각적 이탈)' 없이 잠의 이점을 얻는 상태는 수면 중에도 어느 정도 주변 환경에 대한 반응성을 유지하는 상태를 말합니다. 비둘기와 같은 많은 새들은 잠을 자는 동안에도 환경의 변화에 반응할 수 있는 상태(보통 반구 수면을 통해)를 유지하므로, 완전한 지각 차단이 일어나지 않은 예시로 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 고양이는 종종 하루 종일 낮잠을 잡니다. 얕은 잠을 잘 때 그들은 여전히 일부 자극에 반응할 수 있지만, 배경 소음이나 움직임과 같은 사소한 환경 변화는 종종 무시합니다.
② 특정 종류의 상어와 같은 일부 물고기는 외부 자극에 완전히 반응하지 않는 깊은 수면 상태에 들어갑니다. 그들은 휴식하는 동안 정지해 있거나 움직임이 없어 보일 수 있습니다.
③ 박쥐는 종종 어둡고 조용한 곳에서 거꾸로 매달려 잠을 잡니다. 그들은 낮 동안에는 활동하지 않지만 움직임이나 소음에 의해 방해를 받으면 빠르게 깨어날 수 있습니다.
④ 기린은 종종 서서 잠을 자며, 심지어 누워서 잠을 잘 때도 포식자의 잠재적인 위험에 빠르게 반응할 수 있습니다.
⑤ 비둘기와 같은 많은 새들은 수면 중에도 환경 변화에 계속 반응합니다.

questions.question: 11. 윗글의 ⓐ ~ ⓔ 중 어법상 적절한 것의 개수는? [3.4점]
questions.passage: The tongue was mapped into separate areas ⓐ <u>where</u> certain tastes were registered: sweetness at the tip, sourness on the sides, and bitterness at the back of the mouth. Research in the 1980s and 1990s, however, demonstrated ⓑ <u>that</u> the "tongue map" explanation of how we taste was, in fact, totally wrong. As it turns out, the map was a misinterpretation and mistranslation of research ⓒ <u>conducted</u> in Germany at the turn of the twentieth century. Today, leading taste researchers believe that taste buds are not grouped according to specialty. Sweetness, saltiness, bitterness, and sourness can ⓓ <u>be tasted</u> everywhere in the mouth, although they may be perceived at a little different intensities at different sites. In addition, the mechanism at work is not <u>  ㉠  </u>, but <u>  ㉡  </u>. It's not that you taste sweetness at the tip of your tongue, but rather that it's ⓔ <u>what</u> you perceive first.
options: ① 1개
② 2개
③ 3개
④ 4개
⑤ 5개
questions.explanation: ⓐ where: 관계부사로 뒤에 완전한 문장이 오므로 적절함. ⓑ that: 명사절 접속사로 뒤에 완전한 문장이 오며 demonstrated의 목적어 역할을 하므로 적절함. ⓒ conducted: research를 수식하는 과거분사로 '수행된'이라는 의미가 적절함. ⓓ be tasted: 주어(맛)가 맛보아지는 대상이므로 수동태가 적절함. ⓔ what: 선행사를 포함한 관계대명사로 perceive의 목적어 역할을 하므로 적절함. 따라서 5개 모두 적절하다.

questions.question: 12. 윗글의 빈칸 ㉠과 ㉡에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은? [3.1점]

options: ① time      ...      action
② time      ...      location

④ action    ...      time

questions.explanation: 글의 맥락상 혀의 '장소(place)'에 따라 맛이 결정되는 것이 아니라, 맛을 느끼는 '시간/순서(time)'의 문제라는 설명이 이어지므로(what you perceive first), ㉠에는 place, ㉡에는 time이 적절하다.

questions.question: 13. 윗글의 (a)~(e) 부분 중 어법상 틀린 것만을 고른 것은? [3.5점]
questions.passage: The responsive behavior of dogs also caught the attention of an evolutionary anthropologist, Brian Hare. He conducted an experiment to see how dogs would respond to human gestures compared to wolves, who (a) <u>share</u> the same common ancestor. He placed two cups on the ground with food hidden under only one of them. When he pointed to the cup with the food, the dogs found (b) <u>them</u> easily. The wolves, however, struggled and chose cups at random, paying no attention to his gestures. Dr. Hare concluded that the dogs' ability to read human gestures (c) <u>allowing</u> them to perform better than the wolves. He explained that dogs, unlike wolves, have developed communicative skills with humans and a sense of friendliness. This explanation sounds (d) <u>reasonable</u> according to several evolutionary biologists. They say that from the common ancestors of these two species, those that acted friendly toward humans evolved into dogs, and those that didn't became wolves. Furthermore, Dr. Hare suggested that the friendly nature of dogs probably provided them a survival advantage that allowed their population to grow larger than (e) <u>that</u> of wolves.
questions.explanation: (b) them: 가리키는 대상이 단수인 'the cup with the food'이므로 it으로 고쳐야 한다. (c) allowing: concluded 뒤에 이어지는 that절의 동사 자리이므로 allowed로 고쳐야 한다.

questions.question: 14. 윗글의 내용을 올바르게 이해하고 있지 않은 사람은? [2.8점]
questions.passage: The responsive behavior of dogs also caught the attention of an evolutionary anthropologist, Brian Hare. He conducted an experiment to see how dogs would respond to human gestures compared to wolves, who (a) <u>share</u> the same common ancestor. He placed two cups on the ground with food hidden under only one of them. When he pointed to the cup with the food, the dogs found (b) <u>them</u> easily. The wolves, however, struggled and chose cups at random, paying no attention to his gestures. Dr. Hare concluded that the dogs' ability to read human gestures (c) <u>allowing</u> them to perform better than the wolves. He explained that dogs, unlike wolves, have developed communicative skills with humans and a sense of friendliness. options: ① 인숙: Wolves selected cups at random, neglecting the human's gestures.
② 혜진: Dogs had no difficulty finding the cup by following the human's pointing gestures.
③ 진욱: The friendly nature of dogs enabled them to survive better than wolves.
④ 상혁: Dogs had a favorable attitude toward humans while wolves didn't have a good relationship with humans.
⑤ 상원: Dogs didn't share any resemblance with wolves about their ancestors.
questions.explanation: 지문 첫 부분에 개와 늑대가 같은 공통 조상을 공유한다고(share the same common ancestor) 언급되어 있으므로 조상에 대한 유사점이 전혀 없다는 상원의 말은 틀렸다.
options_translation: ① 인숙: 늑대들은 인간의 제스처를 무시하고 무작위로 컵을 선택했어.
② 혜진: 개들은 인간의 가리키는 제스처를 따라서 컵을 찾는 데 어려움이 없었어.
③ 진욱: 개의 친화적인 본성이 늑대보다 더 잘 생존할 수 있게 해주었어.
④ 상혁: 개는 인간에게 우호적인 태도를 가졌던 반면 늑대는 인간과 좋은 관계를 맺지 못했어.
⑤ 상원: 개는 조상에 있어서 늑대와 어떤 유사성도 공유하지 않았어.

questions.question: [서답형 4] 다음 글의 요지를 <보기>에서 주어진 단어를 사용하여 <조건>에 맞게 완성하시오. [5.0점]
questions.passage: Crop rotation is the process in which farmers change the crops they grow in their fields in a special order. For example, if a farmer has three fields, he or she may grow carrots in the first field, green beans in the second, and tomatoes in the third. The next year, green beans will be in the first field, tomatoes in the second field, and carrots will be in the third. In year three, the crops will rotate again. By the fourth year, the crops will go back to their original order. Each crop enriches the soil for the next crop. This type of farming is sustainable because the soil stays healthy.
subjective_conditions: 1. <보기>에 제시된 단어를 모두 사용하되, 1개의 단어의 형태를 변형하여 사용하여 총 8개의 단어로 작성할 것.
2. 대소문자 구분없음.
3. 철자 오류 시 0점 처리하며, 부분 점수 없음.
4. 조건을 어길 시 0점 처리함.
vocabulary_box: is / crop / soil / helpful / reinforce / in / health / rotation
questions.answer: Crop rotation is helpful in reinforcing soil health
questions.explanation: 글의 요지는 돌려짓기(crop rotation)가 토양 건강을 강화하는 데 도움이 된다는 것이다. 주어진 단어 중 'reinforce'를 'reinforcing'으로 변형하여 'in reinforcing soil health(토양 건강을 강화하는 데 있어서)'로 구성하는 것이 적절하다.

questions.question: 15. 윗글의 내용을 아래의 한 문장으로 요약하고자 한다. 빈칸 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은? [3.5점]
questions.passage: I'll give you another example of how friendliness is related to survival. Dr. Hare and his colleagues designed an experiment with chimpanzees and bonobos. Although the two are genetically similar, they are different in nature. To study their cooperative behavior, Dr. Hare's team set up _________ both ends of a rope at the same time in order to access food on a board. When placed with partners that the chimpanzees knew, they were able to work together to get the food. However, when paired with new partners, the chimpanzees usually failed to get the food, and when they occasionally succeeded, they did not share the food with their partner. On the other hand, the bonobos got along much better than the chimpanzees. They solved the problem regardless of which individual they were paired with, and they were also more willing to share the food. This research shows that bonobos have a cooperative and friendly nature. Experts suggest that their nature has helped their species survive even though they have lived in the flooded swamp forest. Without these characteristics, they could have faced extinction.
questions.summary_sentence: According the study conducted by Dr. Hare, bonobos were not (A)_____ to share food with strangers (B)_____ chimpanzees, which resulted in avoiding extinction despite the fact that they have had (C)_____ adversity.
options: ① willing like geographical
② reluctant unlike environmental
③ reluctant unlike physical
④ willing unlike occasional
⑤ unwilling like occasional
questions.explanation: 보노보는 침팬지와 달리 낯선 개체와도 기꺼이 음식을 나누었으므로 (A)에는 꺼려한다는 의미의 reluctant가 들어가야 'not reluctant' (꺼려하지 않는 = 기꺼이 하는)가 되며, 침팬지와 대조되므로 (B)에는 unlike, 침팬지가 처했던 늪지대 환경(flooded swamp forest)은 지리적이라기보다 환경적 조건에 가까우므로 (C)에는 environmental이 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 기꺼이 하는 - 처럼 - 지리적인
② 꺼려하는 - 와 달리 - 환경적인
③ 꺼려하는 - 와 달리 - 물리적인
④ 기꺼이 하는 - 와 달리 - 가끔의
⑤ 내키지 않는 - 처럼 - 가끔의

questions.question: [서답형 5] 윗글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말을 <보기>에 주어진 단어들을 사용하여 <조건>에 맞게 완성하시오. [4.0점]

subjective_conditions: 1. <보기>에 제시된 단어를 모두 변형 없이 사용하고, 1개의 단어를 추가하여 총 8개의 단어로 작성할 것. (※ a device는 두 단어임)
