questions.explanation: 주어진 단어들을 조합하여 '두 개체가 끌어야 하는 장치'라는 의미를 만들어야 합니다. 주격 관계대명사 which를 사용하고 'require A to B(A가 B하도록 요구하다)' 구문을 활용하여 'a device which required two individuals to pull'로 완성하며, to를 추가하여 총 8단어가 됩니다.

questions.question: 16. [2.5점] 글의 흐름으로 보아, 주어진 문장이 들어가기에 가장 적절한 곳을 고르시오.
questions.passage: It's good to see you, everyone! I'm Dr. Edward Wilson, an evolutionary biologist. ( ① ) Thank you for inviting me here today. ( ② ) On my way, I had trouble locating this room. Luckily, a friendly student came up to me and walked me here. ( ③ ) It's fascinating how, in situations like this, we want to help someone in need. ( ④ ) Now, this raises some interesting questions: where does our friendliness come from, and why is it important? ( ⑤ ) When we played with a ball, I noticed that responded well to my gestures.
questions.insertion_sentence: To answer these questions, I'd like to tell you about my childhood companion dog, Sparky.
questions.explanation: 주어진 문장의 'these questions'는 바로 앞 문장(④번 뒤)의 'where does our friendliness come from, and why is it important?'를 가리킵니다. 또한 주어진 문장의 'Sparky'에 대한 언급 이후 ⑤번 뒤의 문장에서 'When we played with a ball...'로 이어지며 Sparky와의 일화가 구체적으로 시작되므로 ⑤번 위치가 가장 적절합니다.

questions.question: 17. [2.6점] 글의 흐름으로 보아, 주어진 문장이 들어가기에 가장 적절한 곳을 고르시오.
questions.passage: When we think of leaders, we may think of people such as Abraham Lincoln or Martin Luther King, Jr. ( ① ) If you consider the historical importance and far-reaching influence of these individuals, leadership might seem like a noble and high goal. ( ② ) Through diligence and experience, they improved upon their ideas by sharing them with others. ( ③ ) In addition, they sought their opinions and feedback, looking for the best way to accomplish goals for a group. ( ④ ) We all have the potential to be leaders at school, in our communities, and at work, regardless of age or experience. ( ⑤ ) Therefore, we have sufficient qualifications for good leaders through endless refinement and continuous improvement.
questions.insertion_sentence: But like all of us, these people started out as students, workers, and citizens who possessed ideas about how some aspect of daily life could be improved on a larger scale.
questions.explanation: 주어진 문장의 'these people'은 링컨이나 킹 목사 같은 위대한 인물들을 가리키며, 그들도 우리처럼 평범한 학생이나 시민에서 시작했다는 역접의 내용입니다. ①번 다음 문장에서 리더십이 숭고하고 높은 목표처럼 보인다는 내용 뒤에, '하지만(But)'으로 시작하는 주어진 문장이 들어와 그들의 평범한 시작을 언급하고, ②번 뒤의 'they'가 주어진 문장의 'these people'을 받아 그들이 어떻게 아이디어를 발전시켰는지 설명하는 구조가 자연스럽습니다.

questions.question: 18. 다음 글의 주제로 가장 적절한 것은? [3.4점]
questions.passage: Magic is what we all wish for to happen in our life. Do you love the movie Cinderella like me? Well, in real life, you can also create magic. Here's the trick. Write down all the real-time challenges that you face and deal with. Just change the challenge statement into positive statements. Let me give you an example here. If you struggle with getting up early in the morning, then write a positive statement such as "I get up early in the morning at 5:00 am every day." Once you write these statements, get ready to witness magic and confidence. You will be surprised that just by writing these statements, there is a shift in the way you think and act. Suddenly you feel more powerful and positive.
options: ① difficulties of creating new magics
② necessary factors that improve writing skills
③ adverse effects of using challenge statements
④ necessity of using affirmative statements for a magical change
⑤ influence of converting difficult statements into easy ones
questions.explanation: 필자는 삶에서 마법 같은 변화를 일으키기 위해 자신이 직면한 도전 과제들을 긍정적인 문장(affirmative statements)으로 바꾸어 써 볼 것을 권장하고 있으므로, 주제는 ④ '마법 같은 변화를 위해 긍정적인 문장을 사용하는 것의 필요성'이 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 새로운 마법을 만드는 것의 어려움
② 작문 기술을 향상시키는 필수 요소들
③ 도전 문장을 사용하는 것의 부정적인 효과들
④ 마법 같은 변화를 위해 긍정 문장을 사용하는 것의 필요성
⑤ 어려운 문장을 쉬운 것으로 바꾸는 것의 영향력

questions.question: 20. Jaroslav Heyrovsky에 관한 다음 글의 내용과 일치하는 것은? [2.6점]
questions.passage: Jaroslav Heyrovsky was born in Prague on December 20, 1890, as the fifth child of Leopold Heyrovsky. In 1901 Jaroslav went to a secondary school called the Akademicke Gymnasium. Rather than Latin and Greek, he showed a strong interest in the natural sciences. At Czech University in Prague he studied chemistry, physics, and mathematics. From 1910 to 1914 he continued his studies at University College, London. Throughout the First World War, Jaroslav served in a military hospital. In 1926, Jaroslav became the first Professor of Physical Chemistry at Charles University in Prague. He won the Nobel Prize in chemistry in 1959.
options: ① 자연과학보다 라틴어와 그리스어에 흥미를 느꼈다.
② Czech University에서 화학과 생물학을 배웠다.
③ 1910년부터 1914년까지 군 병원에 복무했다.
④ Prague의 Charles University에서 최초의 물리화학 교수가 되었다.
⑤ 1959년에 노벨 물리학상을 수상했다.
questions.explanation: 지문에 "In 1926, Jaroslav became the first Professor of Physical Chemistry at Charles University in Prague."라고 명시되어 있으므로 ④번이 일치합니다. ①은 자연과학에 더 흥미를 느꼈고, ②는 화학, 물리, 수학을 공부했으며, ③은 1910~1914년은 런던에서 공부한 시기이고 ⑤는 노벨 화학상을 받았습니다.

questions.question: 21. [21 ~ 22] 다음 글에서 전체 흐름과 관계 없는 문장을 고르시오. [3.5점]
questions.passage: In many sports, people realized the difficulties and even impossibilities of young children participating fully in many adult sport environments. They found the road to success for young children is unlikely if they play on adult fields, courts or arenas with equipment that is too large, too heavy or too fast for them to handle while trying to compete in adult-style competition. Common sense has prevailed: different sports have made adaptations for children. One of the most famous examples is in football (soccer). ① <u>Instead of a full-sized field, young children play on a smaller field with fewer players.</u> ② <u>The ball is also lighter and smaller, making it easier for them to kick and control.</u> Tennis has also been adapted for young athletes. ③ <u>Rather than competing on a full-sized court with a rapidly moving ball, young players practice on a reduced court with specially designed balls that move at a slower speed.</u> ④ <u>Overall, while many sports have been adapted to be more accessible for young or new players, others have changed to be more demanding.</u> ⑤ <u>By making sports more child-friendly, we help young athletes develop their skills, build confidence, and enjoy their favorite games.</u>
questions.explanation: 전체 글은 어린아이들이 스포츠에 더 쉽게 참여할 수 있도록 필드 크기나 장비 등을 조정(adaptation)한다는 내용입니다. 그러나 ④번은 다른 스포츠들이 더 까다로워지거나 요구사항이 많아졌다는 내용을 담고 있어 흐름에서 벗어납니다.

questions.question: 22. 다음 글에서 전체 흐름과 관계없는 문장은? [3.4점]
questions.passage: Working around the whole painting, rather than concentrating on one area at a time will mean you can stop at any point and the painting can be considered "finished." ① Artists often find it difficult to know when to stop painting, and it can be tempting to keep on adding more to your work. ② It is important to take a few steps back from the painting from time to time to assess your progress because putting too much into a painting can spoil its impact and leave it looking overworked. ③ Artists are also required to work for a period of time in a low without any interruption to maintain concentration on the right track. ④ If you find yourself struggling to decide whether you have finished, take a break and come back to it later with fresh eyes. ⑤ Then you can decide whether any areas of your painting would benefit from further refinement.
questions.explanation: 이 글은 그림을 그릴 때 한 부분에만 집중하기보다 전체적으로 작업하고, 때때로 뒤로 물러나 진행 상황을 점검하며 휴식을 취하는 것이 중요하다는 내용을 담고 있습니다. 하지만 ③번 문장은 중단 없이 한동안 계속 작업하는 것이 집중력 유지에 필요하다는 내용이므로, 전체적인 흐름과 관계가 없습니다.

questions.question: 23. 다음 글의 내용을 요약한 아래의 글에서, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은? [3.8점]
questions.passage: Now let's turn our attention to ourselves, Homo sapiens. How have we managed to survive for so long? Neanderthals existed together with Homo sapiens until about 40,000 years ago, and they were known to be intelligent and physically superior to Homo sapiens. Neanderthals were able to make tools and fire and had strong bodies with well-developed muscles and broad shoulders. Despite these attributes, however, it was Homo sapiens who ultimately survived and thrived. One possible explanation is that our forefathers lived in larger communities that promoted cooperation and the free exchange of knowledge, while Neanderthals tended to live in smaller groups. These social differences may have given Homo sapiens a competitive advantage over Neanderthals, allowing them to adapt to an ever-changing environment.
questions.summary_sentence: Neanderthals who lived in ① the <u>same</u> period with Homo sapiens had greater ② <u>physical</u> capability over Homo Sapiens. However, they couldn't avoid extinction because they lived a relatively ③ <u>solitary</u> life. Compared with Neanderthals, Homo Sapiens ④ <u>forbade</u> themselves to cooperate with each other in larger communities. These significant ⑤ <u>distinctions</u> between Neanderthals and Homo Sapiens supplied Homo sapiens with a competitive advantage over Neanderthals.
questions.explanation: 본문에서 호모 사피엔스는 더 큰 공동체에서 협력(cooperation)을 촉진했다고 설명하고 있습니다. 따라서 요약문에서 호모 사피엔스가 서로 협력하는 것을 '금지했다(forbade)'는 표현은 적절하지 않으며, '장려했다' 또는 '허용했다' 등의 단어가 적절합니다.

questions.question: 24. 다음 글의 내용을 한 문장으로 요약하고자 한다. 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은? [3.5점]
questions.passage: The rate of speed at which one is traveling will greatly determine the ability to process detail in the environment. In evolutionary terms, human senses are adapted to the speed at which humans move through space under their own power while walking. Our ability to distinguish detail in the environment is therefore ideally suited to movement at speeds of perhaps five miles per hour and under. The fastest users of the street, motorists, therefore have a much more limited ability to process details along the street - a motorist simply has little time or ability to appreciate design details. On the other hand, pedestrian travel, being much slower, allows for the appreciation of environmental detail. Joggers and bicyclists fall somewhere in between these polar opposites; while they travel faster than pedestrians, their rate of speed is ordinarily much slower than that of the typical motorist.
questions.summary_sentence: According to the above passage, we can understand that moving speed has a(an) (A)_______ relationship with processing detailed information in the environment for travelers because moving fast (B)________ our capacity of addressing it.
options: ① positive ...... damages
② positive ...... undermines
③ negative ...... undermines
④ negative ...... improves
⑤ inverse ...... enhances
questions.explanation: 이동 속도가 빠를수록 주변 환경의 세부 정보를 처리하는 능력이 떨어지므로 이동 속도와 정보 처리 능력 사이에는 (A) 부정적인(negative) 혹은 역의(inverse) 관계가 성립합니다. 또한 빠르게 이동하는 것은 세부 정보를 처리하는 능력을 (B) 약화시키거나(undermines) 손상시키기(damages) 때문입니다. 따라서 가장 적절한 것은 ③번입니다.
options_translation: ① 긍정적인 ...... 손상시킨다
② 긍정적인 ...... 약화시킨다
③ 부정적인 ...... 약화시킨다

questions.passage: Mapping can also rally community members around the assets of their community such as libraries, community centers, and parks. Heritage and cultural attractions, like landmarks, museums, and public artworks, are also good sources for community mapping. Through marking assets on a map, people become aware of the strengths and resources of their own community and build a strong bond with it. Also, these maps can provide valuable data to be used for tourism or urban design. The mapping project Where in Wally (short for Walthamstow, UK) is a case in point. A team of architects undertook the project to find out what spots were loved by the locals. People told the team about their treasured places and the reasons why these places were special to them. The team then added the places to an online map and marked them in the real world with yellow tags. The map and tags invited people to go on a treasure hunt and told them colorful stories about the corners of Walthamstow.

questions.passage: The tongue was mapped into separate areas where certain tastes were registered: sweetness at the tip, sourness on the sides, and bitterness at the back of the mouth. Research in the 1980s and 1990s, however, demonstrated that the "tongue map" explanation of how we taste was, in fact, totally wrong. As it turns out, the map was a misinterpretation and mistranslation of research conducted in Germany at the turn of the twentieth century. Today, leading taste researchers believe that taste buds are not grouped according to specialty. Sweetness, saltiness, bitterness, and sourness can be tasted everywhere in the mouth, although they may be perceived at a little different intensities at different sites. Moreover, the mechanism at work is not place, but time. It's not that you taste sweetness at the tip of your tongue, but rather that you register that perception first.
options: ① A Tongue Map Misconception: Do Taste Buds Really Have Separate Areas on the Tongue?
② Taste Perception: Why People Usually Perceive Sweetness First
③ Time Is Less Important for Tastes Than Place
④ How Tastes Are Registered on the Tongue
⑤ Taste Bud Research in the Early 1900's
questions.explanation: 이 글은 과거에 알려졌던 혀의 부위별 맛 지도(tongue map)가 사실은 잘못된 해석과 오역에서 비롯된 오해였음을 설명하고 있습니다. 실제로는 혀의 모든 부위에서 모든 맛을 느낄 수 있으며, 장소가 아니라 시간적 인지 순서의 차이가 존재한다는 점을 강조하고 있으므로 ①번이 가장 적절한 제목입니다.

questions.question: 3.다음 글의 주제로 가장 적절한 것을 고르시오.
questions.passage: No respectable boss would say, “I make it a point to discourage my staff from speaking up, and I maintain a culture that prevents disagreeing viewpoints from ever getting aired.” If anything, most bosses even say that they are pro-dissent. This idea can be found throughout the series of conversations with corporate, university, and nonprofit leaders, published weekly in the business sections of newspapers. In the interviews, the featured leaders are asked about their management techniques, and regularly claim to continually encourage internal protest from more junior staffers. As Bob Pittman remarked in one of these conversations: “I want us to listen to these dissenters because they may intend to tell you why we can’t do something, but if you listen hard, what they’re really telling you is what you must do to get something done.”
options: ① CEOs' pro-dissent attitudes that are encouraged in the workplace
② necessity for respected members in times of crises
③ ideas that could shift leader's authoritarian thinking
④ importance of employers voicing disagreements
⑤ ways to improve employees' work performance
questions.explanation: 지문은 존경받는 리더들이 직원들의 반대 의견(dissent)을 장려하고 경청하는 태도를 가지고 있음을 설명하고 있으므로, ① '직장에서 장려되는 CEO들의 반대 찬성 태도'가 가장 적절합니다.

④ 고용주들이 불일치하는 의견을 내는 것의 중요성

questions.question: 4. 다음 글의 주제로 가장 적절한 것을 고르시오.
questions.passage: Assuming gene editing in humans proves to be safe and effective, it might seem logical, even preferable, to correct disease-causing mutations at the earliest possible stage of life, before harmful genes begin causing serious problems. Yet once it becomes possible to transform an embryo's mutated genes into "normal" ones, there will certainly be temptations to upgrade normal genes to superior versions. Should we begin editing genes in unborn children to lower their lifetime risk of heart disease or cancer? What about giving unborn children beneficial features, like greater strength and increased mental abilities, or changing physical characteristics, like eye and hair color? The pursuit for perfection seems almost natural to human nature, but if we start down this slippery slope, we may not like where we end up.
options: ① public opinion on cloning animals for scientific research
② ethical problems of using gene editing for human enhancement
③ medical benefits of gene editing for curing rare genetic diseases
④ how gene editing could help reduce healthcare costs in the future
⑤ the process scientists use to identify and fix faulty genes in embryos
questions.explanation: 지문은 인간의 유전자 편집이 질병 치료를 넘어 인간 강화(능력 향상, 외모 변경 등)로 이어질 때 발생할 수 있는 윤리적 위험성과 '미끄러운 경사면' 효과를 경고하고 있으므로, ② '인간 강화를 위해 유전자 편집을 사용하는 것의 윤리적 문제들'이 주제로 가장 적절합니다.

questions.question: 5. 윗글의 ⓐ~ⓔ 중 어법상 틀린 것은? [3.3점]
questions.passage: In the middle of a major disaster, community mapping can prove ⓐ <u>to be</u> a very effective and important tool. The first responders to a disaster are often ordinary citizens. They can use maps to create and update data on health facilities, shelters, or even public roads. When community members work together at the time of a disaster, the gathered information can be based on actual needs rather than guesses. This is particularly critical when every second ⓑ <u>counts</u>. For example, community mapping helped ⓒ <u>deal with</u> the impact of Hurricane Sandy, one of the most destructive hurricanes to hit the United States. One of its main effects ⓓ <u>was</u> energy failures. Residents in affected areas would wait for hours in line at gas stations, sometimes only to learn that they were out of gasoline. In response to this problem, a group of high school students in New Jersey worked together to create an online community map, ⓔ <u>published</u> information on open gas stations with available fuel. The students gathered information from personal observations, calls to local gas stations, and updates from other social media users. The live data streams filled a significant community information gap.
options: ① ⓐ
② ⓑ
③ ⓒ
④ ⓓ
⑤ ⓔ
questions.explanation: ⓔ가 포함된 문장에서 'published'는 주어 'a group of high school students'의 동작을 나타내는 분사구문 자리입니다. 학생들이 정보를 '게시하면서' 지도를 만들었다는 능동의 의미가 되어야 하므로 현재분사인 'publishing'이 적절합니다.

questions.question: 7. 수면에 관한 다음 글의 내용과 일치하는 것은? [3.7점]
questions.passage: One of the most striking characteristics of a sleeping animal or person is that they do not respond normally to environmental stimuli. If you open the eyelids of a sleeping mammal the eyes will not see normally — they are functionally blind. Some visual information apparently gets in, but it is not normally processed as it is shortened or weakened; same with the other sensing systems. Stimuli are registered but not processed normally and they fail to wake the individual. Perceptual disengagement probably serves the function of protecting sleep, so some authors do not count it as part of the definition of sleep itself. But as sleep would be impossible without it, it seems essential to its definition. Nevertheless, many animals (including humans) use the intermediate state of drowsiness to derive some benefits of sleep without total perceptual disengagement.
options: ① Unlike animals, humans do not respond to external stimuli during sleep.
② While sleeping, mammals can neither register nor process visual information as they are functionally blind.
③ It is hard to wake up sleeping mammals because all the sensory information is not registered.
④ Perceptual disengagement plays an important role in helping us to stay asleep without interruption.
⑤ Only humans deliberately use drowsiness as a substitute for sleep to rule out the effects of perceptual disengagement.
questions.explanation: 지문에서 지각적 단절(Perceptual disengagement)이 수면을 보호하는 기능을 한다고 언급하고 있으므로 ④번이 정답입니다. ① 수면 중 자극 반응은 동물과 인간 모두에게 해당되며, ② 자극이 등록은 되지만 정상적으로 처리되지 않는 것이며, ③ 정보가 등록은 되지만 약화되는 것이고, ⑤ 인간을 포함한 많은 동물이 졸음을 활용한다고 했습니다.
options_translation: ① 동물과 달리 인간은 수면 중에 외부 자극에 반응하지 않는다.
② 잠을 자는 동안 포유류는 기능적으로 눈이 멀기 때문에 시각 정보를 등록하거나 처리할 수 없다.
③ 모든 감각 정보가 등록되지 않기 때문에 잠자는 포유류를 깨우는 것은 어렵다.
④ 지각적 단절은 우리가 방해받지 않고 잠을 잘 수 있도록 돕는 데 중요한 역할을 한다.
⑤ 오직 인간만이 지각적 단절의 효과를 배제하기 위해 졸음을 수면의 대안으로 의도적으로 사용한다.

questions.question: 8. Inca 제국의 전령시스템에 관한 다음 글의 내용과 일치하지 않는 것은? [4점]
questions.passage: With no horses available, the Inca Empire excelled at delivering messages on foot. The messengers were stationed on the royal roads to deliver the Inca king's orders and reports coming from his lands. Called Chasquis, they lived in groups of four to six in huts, placed from one to two miles apart along the roads. They were all young men and especially good runners who watched the road in both directions. If they caught sight of another messenger coming, they hurried out to meet them. The Inca built the huts on high ground, in sight of one another. When a messenger neared the next hut, he began to call out and repeated the message three or four times to the one who was running out to meet him. The Inca empire could relay messages 1,000 miles (1,610 km) in three or four days under good conditions.
options: ① People in the Inca Empire preferred to deliver messages on foot even though they were able to ride horses.
② Chasquis refer to messengers living in huts along the royal roads.
③ The messengers in the Inca Empire were young and they were good at running.
④ The huts built on high ground helped the messengers to see if another messenger was coming.
⑤ It could take messengers three or four days to relay messages under good conditions.
questions.explanation: 지문 첫 문장에서 "With no horses available(사용 가능한 말이 없었기 때문에)"라고 명시되어 있으므로, 말을 탈 수 있었음에도 도보를 선호했다는 ①번은 내용과 일치하지 않습니다.
options_translation: ① 잉카 제국 사람들은 말을 탈 수 있었음에도 불구하고 도보로 메시지를 전달하는 것을 선호했다.
② Chasquis는 왕실 도로를 따라 오두막에 사는 전령들을 가리킨다.
③ 잉카 제국의 전령들은 젊고 달리기를 잘했다.
④ 높은 지대에 지어진 오두막은 전령들이 다른 전령이 오고 있는지 확인하는 데 도움이 되었다.
⑤ 좋은 조건 하에서 전령들이 메시지를 전달하는 데 3~4일이 걸릴 수 있었다.

questions.question: 9.다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것을 고르시오.
questions.passage: In many sports, people realized the difficulties and even impossibilities of young children participating fully in many adult sport environments. They found the road to success for young children is ① <u>unlikely</u> if they play on adult fields, courts or arenas. Since the equipment used for adult sports is too large, too heavy or too fast, they can ② <u>easily</u> handle while trying to compete in adult-style competition. Common sense has prevailed: different sports have made ③ <u>changes</u> for children. As examples, baseball has T ball, football has flag football and junior soccer uses a smaller and lighter ball and (sometimes) a smaller field. All have junior competitive structures where children play for ④ <u>shorter</u> time periods and often in smaller teams. In a similar way, tennis has adapted the court areas, balls and rackets to make them more ⑤ <u>suitable</u> for children under 10. The adaptations are progressive and relate to the age of the child.
questions.explanation: 성인용 스포츠 장비가 너무 크고, 무겁고, 빠르기 때문에 아이들이 이를 '쉽게(easily)' 다루는 것은 문맥상 어색합니다. '어렵게(hardly)' 또는 '간신히' 등으로 바뀌어야 적절합니다.

questions.question: 10. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것을 고르시오.[3.9점]
questions.passage: Our skin conducts electricity more or less efficiently, depending on our emotions. We know that when we're emotionally ① <u>stimulated</u> - stressed, sad, any intense emotion, really - our bodies sweat a tiny bit, so little we might not even ② <u>notice</u>. And when those tiny drops of sweat appear, our skin gets more electrically conductive. This <u>change</u> in sweat gland activity occurs ③ <u>automatically</u>, without significant involvement from the conscious mind. When emotional intensity rises, an increase in sweat gland activity can be observed. By tracking how your body ④ <u>consciously</u> sweats - through the application of a mild electrical current to the skin - scientists can accurately measure emotional states. Thus, the ⑤ <u>subjective</u> experience of emotional intensity can be transformed into a <u>quantifiable</u> value based on the skin's electrical conductivity.
questions.explanation: 글의 흐름상 땀샘 활동은 의식적인 마음의 개입 없이 자동으로(automatically) 일어난다고 언급되었으므로, 과학자들이 감정 상태를 측정할 때 몸이 '의식적으로(consciously)' 땀을 흘리는 것을 추적한다는 표현은 적절하지 않습니다. ④ consciously를 unconsciously 또는 automatically와 같은 의미의 단어로 바꾸어야 합니다.

questions.question:
11.다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 어법상 틀린 것을 고르시오.

11. [3.7점]
questions.passage: Plants can communicate, although not in the same way we do. Some express their discontent through scents. You know that smell ① <u>that</u> hangs in the air after you've mowed the lawn? Yeah, that's actually an SOS. Some plants use sound. Yes, sound, though at a frequency we can't hear. Researchers experimented with plants and microphones to see if they could record any trouble calls. They found that plants produce a high-frequency clicking noise when ② <u>stressed</u> and can make different sounds for different stressors. The sound a plant makes when it's not getting watered ③ <u>differ</u> from the one it'll make when a leaf is cut. However, it's worth ④ <u>noting</u> that experts don't think plants are crying out in pain. It's more likely that these reactions are knee-jerk survival actions. Plants are living organisms, and their main objective is ⑤ <u>to survive</u>. Scents and sounds are their tools for defending against things that might harm them.
questions.explanation: 문장의 주어는 'The sound (a plant makes when it's not getting watered)'에서 'The sound'입니다. 주어가 3인칭 단수이므로 동사 differ를 단수형인 differs로 고쳐야 합니다.

questions.question:
12. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 어법상 틀린 것을 고르시오.

12. [3.7점]
questions.passage: Every species has certain climatic requirements - what degree of heat or cold it can endure, for example. When the climate changes, the places ① <u>which</u> satisfy those requirements change, too. Species ② <u>are forced</u> to follow. All creatures are capable of some degree of movement. Even creatures that appear ③ <u>immobile</u>, like trees and barnacles, are capable of dispersal at some stage of their life - as a seed, in the case of the tree, or as a larva, in the case of the barnacle. A creature must get from the place it is born - often ④ <u>occupied</u> by its parent - to a place where it can survive, grow, and reproduce. From fossils, scientists know that even creatures like trees ⑤ <u>moving</u> with surprising speed during past periods of climate change.
questions.explanation: know의 목적어인 that절 내부를 보면, 'even creatures like trees'가 주어입니다. 따라서 문장의 구조상 동사가 필요하므로 현재분사인 moving 대신 과거 시제 동사인 moved로 고쳐야 합니다.

questions.question: 13.다음 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것을 고르시오.
questions.passage: The science we learn in grade school is a collection of certainties about the natural world - the earth goes around the sun, DNA carries the information of an organism, and so on. Only when you start to learn the practice of science do you realize that each of these "facts" was hard won through a succession of logical inferences based upon many observations or experiments. The process of science is less about collecting pieces of knowledge than it is about ________. Our uncertainties can be greater or lesser for any given piece of knowledge depending upon where we are in that process - today we are quite certain of how an apple will fall from a tree, but our understanding of the turbulent fluid flow remains a work in progress after more than a century of effort.
options: ① expanding our imagination
② maintaining what we believe
③ narrowing the gaps in our knowledge
④ decreasing our confidence in what we know
⑤ reducing the reliability of our understanding
questions.explanation: 과학적 지식은 관찰과 실험을 통한 논리적 추론의 과정을 통해 얻어지는 것이며, 과학의 과정은 단순히 지식을 수집하는 것보다 지식의 불확실성을 줄여나가는, 즉 지식의 격차를 좁혀나가는 과정임을 설명하고 있습니다. 따라서 ③ '지식의 격차를 좁히는 것'이 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 우리의 상상력을 확장하는 것
② 우리가 믿는 것을 유지하는 것
③ 우리 지식의 격차를 좁히는 것
④ 우리가 아는 것에 대한 확신을 줄이는 것
⑤ 우리 이해의 신뢰성을 감소시키는 것

questions.question: 14.다음 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것을 고르시오. [4점]
questions.passage: What does it mean for a character to be a hero as opposed to a villain? In artistic and entertainment descriptions, it's essential for the author to establish a positive relationship between a protagonist and the audience. In order for tragedy or misfortune to draw out an emotional response in viewers, the character must be adjusted so as to be recognizable as either friend or enemy. Whether the portrayal is fictional or documentary, we must feel that the protagonist is someone whose actions benefit us; the protagonist is, or would be, a worthy companion or valued ally. Violent action films are often filled with dozens of incidental deaths of minor characters that draw out little response in the audience. The audience must ____________________, recognizing a character as either ally or enemy, to feel powerful emotions.
options: ① form emotional bonds
② maintain a neutral view
③ express personal feelings
④ observe emotional reactions
⑤ pay attention only to the hero's actions
questions.explanation: 글의 핵심 내용은 관객이 주인공과 긍정적인 관계를 맺고 아군으로 인식해야 감정적 반응이 일어난다는 것입니다. 빈칸 앞뒤 문맥에서 '동지나 적으로 인식'하여 '강력한 감정을 느끼기' 위해 필요한 조건은 주인공과의 정서적 유대 형성입니다.
options_translation: ① 정서적 유대감을 형성하다
② 중립적인 관점을 유지하다
③ 개인적인 감정을 표현하다
④ 감정적 반응을 관찰하다
⑤ 영웅의 행동에만 주의를 기울이다

questions.question: 15.다음 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것을 고르시오. [3.6점]
questions.passage: It would be hard to overstate how important meaningful work is to human beings — work that provides a sense of fulfillment and empowerment. Those who have found deeper meaning in their careers find their days much more energizing and satisfying, and count their employment as one of their greatest sources of joy and pride. Sonya Lyubomirsky, professor of psychology at the University of California, has conducted numerous workplace studies showing that when ____________________, they produce higher quality work and a greater output. Those most fulfilled with their work are also much more likely to be happier with their lives overall. For her book Happiness at Work, researcher Jessica Pryce-Jones conducted a study of 3,000 workers in seventy-nine countries, finding that those who took greater satisfaction from their work were 150 percent more likely to have a happier life overall.
options: ① people get paid high salaries
② fulfillment conflicts with people's needs
③ workers are more satisfied with their jobs
④ bosses encourage their employees to work harder
⑤ happiness is of greater importance than job satisfaction.
questions.explanation: 전체 지문은 일에서의 의미와 만족감이 업무 성과와 삶의 행복에 미치는 긍정적인 영향에 대해 설명하고 있습니다. 빈칸은 업무 성과(생산성)가 높아지는 조건을 찾는 것이므로, 일에 더 만족할 때라는 내용이 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 사람들이 높은 급여를 받을 때
② 성취감이 사람들의 필요와 상충할 때
③ 노동자들이 자신의 직업에 더 만족할 때
④ 상사가 직원들에게 더 열심히 일하라고 격려할 때
⑤ 행복이 직업 만족도보다 더 중요할 때

questions.question: 16. [3.7점] 다음 글에서 전체 흐름과 관계 없는 문장을 고르시오.
questions.passage: How about making a map with your classmates? ① Each of you can trace routes that you frequently use and mark how comfortable or safe you feel on those routes. ② With group participation and feedback, an informative visual map of safe routes to school can be constructed. ③ This shows that there's just one reason for, and one method of, carrying out community mapping. ④ The process is defined by the community itself, depending on what issues are raised and how the community members decide to deal with them. ⑤ The most important thing in the process is that you have to work with others.
questions.explanation: 글 전체가 공동체 매핑(community mapping)의 참여적이고 다양한 목적을 가질 수 있는 과정을 설명하고 있는데, ③번 문장은 '단 하나의 이유와 방법만 있다'고 주장하며 글의 유연하고 공동체 중심적인 성격과 대조되어 흐름을 방해합니다.

questions.question: 17. [3.6점] 다음 글에서 전체 흐름과 관계 없는 문장을 고르시오.
questions.passage: Plato argued that when you see something that strikes you as beautiful, you are really just seeing a partial reflection of true beauty. ① Just as a painting or even a photograph captures only part of the real thing, beautiful objects reflect the Form of Beauty. ② This Form has no particular color, shape, or size — it's an abstract idea. ③ What one person finds beautiful, another might overlook entirely, showing how beauty is often judged by different standards. ④ Think of the idea of a triangle: although it has no particular color or size, it somehow lies within each and every triangle you see. ⑤ Plato thought the same was true of beauty — the Form of Beauty exists within every beautiful thing you see.
questions.explanation: 이 글은 플라톤의 '미의 형상(Form of Beauty)'이라는 추상적이고 보편적인 개념이 구체적인 사물 속에 존재한다는 철학적 주장을 설명하고 있습니다. 반면 ③번은 아름다움이 개인의 주관적 기준에 따라 다르다는 '미의 상대성'을 언급하고 있어, 객관적인 형상을 강조하는 플라톤의 생각과는 무관합니다.

questions.question: 18.제시된 글 다음에 이어질 글의 순서로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: A couple of weeks later, the class was given another speech assignment. I didn't want to drop the ball like the first time.
ordered_passages: (A) My heart began to race, and I took a deep breath to calm it down. While my voice trembled from time to time, I managed to get my whole message across. When I was done, I felt so proud of myself that I barely noticed how loudly everyone was clapping for me!

(B) I felt nervous again when the big day finally arrived. But when the teacher called my name, I noticed that my nerves had actually calmed down a bit. I felt way better than the last time, for sure! I walked up to the front of the class and looked out into the audience.

(C) So this time, I practiced delivering the speech. I stood in front of the mirror every day for a week and went over all the things I wanted to say. I used cue cards which contained key phrases about important facts. I rehearsed how I would stand, how I would make eye contact with the audience, and even when I would pause.
questions.explanation: 제시문에서 이번에는 실수하고 싶지 않다고 했으므로, 그에 따라 연습하는 내용인 (C)가 먼저 오고, 그 다음 발표 당일이 되어 무대로 나가는 상황인 (B)가 이어지며, 마지막으로 성공적으로 발표를 마치고 느끼는 (A)가 오는 것이 자연스럽다.

questions.question: 19. [3.7점] 제시된 글 다음에 이어질 글의 순서로 가윜 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: A number of research studies have shown how experts in a field often experience difficulties when introducing newcomers to that field.
ordered_passages: (A) This effect is referred to as the 'curse of knowledge'. Dr Hinds was able to show that as people acquired the skill, they then began to underestimate the level of difficulty of that skill. Her participants even underestimated how long it had taken themselves to acquire that skill in an earlier session.

(B) Knowing that even experts forget how hard it was for them to learn—as her research has shown—we can understand the need to look at the learning process through students' eyes, rather than making assumptions about how students 'should be' learning.

(C) For example, in a genuine training situation, Dr Pamela Hinds found that people expert in using mobile phones were remarkably less accurate than novice phone users in judging how long it takes people to learn to use the phones. Like this, experts can become insensitive to how hard a task is for the beginner.
questions.explanation: 제시문에서 전문가가 초밴자에겂 어려움을 겪는다는 내용이 나오고, (C)에서 그에 대한 구체적인 예시(Pamela Hinds의 연구) 시작된다. (A)에서는 이 효과를 '지식의 저주'라고 명명하며 추가 설명을 하고, 마지막으로 (B)에서 이러한 연구 결과를 바탕으로 학생들의 관점에서 바라봐야 한다는 결론을 내리고 읈다.

questions.question: 20. [3.7점] 글의 흐름으로 바와, 제시된 문장이 들어가기에 가장 적절한 곳은?
questions.passage: Routines helps athletes evaluate competition conditions. ( ① ) For example, bouncing a ball in a volleyball service routine supplies the server with information about the ball, the floor, and the state of her muscles. ( ② ) Routines also make it possible for athletes to adjust and fine-tune their preparations based on those evaluations or in pursuit of a particular competitive goal. ( ③ ) This adaptation can involve adjustment to the conditions, rivals, competitive situation, or internal influences that can affect performance. ( ④ ) Just as a race-car engine is adjusted to match the track conditions, air temperature, and weather, routines help athletes fine-tune all aspects of their performance to suit the competitive environment. ( ⑤ )
questions.insertion_sentence: This information can then be used to properly prepare for her serve.
questions.explanation: 제시된 문장의 'This information'은 ① 다음 문장에서 언급된 'information about the ball, the floor, and the state of her muscles'를 가리키므로, ② 위치가 가장 적절하다.

questions.question: 21. [3.7점] 글의 흐름으로 바와, 제시된 문윥이 들어가기에 가윜 적절한 갳은?
questions.passage: Consider the seemingly simple question How many senses are there? ( ① ) Around 2,370 years ago, Aristotle wrote that there are five, in both humans and animals — sight, hearing, smell, taste, and touch. ( ② ) For a start, Aristotle missed a few in humans: the perception of your own body which is different from touch and the sense of balance which has links to both touch and vision. ( ③ ) Other animals have senses that are even harder to categorize; for example, many vertebrates have a different sense system for detecting odors, and some snakes can detect the body heat of their prey. ( ④ ) These examples tell us that "senses cannot be clearly divided into a limited number of specific kinds," Macpherson wrote in The Senses. ( ⑤ ) Instead of trying to push animal senses into Aristotelian buckets, we should study them for what they are. ( ⑥ )
questions.insertion_sentence: However, according to the philosopher Fiona Macpherson, there are reasons to doubt it.
questions.explanation: 제시된 문윥의 'it'은 ① 다음 문윥에 나온 아리스토텔렙의 5감설을 의미한다. ② 이후봀터 그 가설에 대한 의문과 반박 사례들이 언급되므로 ②에 들어가는 것이 자연스럽다.

questions.question: 22. 밑줄 친 <u>focus on the one thing you can control</u>이 윗글에서 의미하는 바로 가장 적절한 것은? [3.4점]
questions.passage:
The next day, I met Ms. Harper after school to talk about the speech. I said, “I’m embarrassed about the speech. (A) _________. (B) _________.”
“It’s quite all right to fall short of your own expectations as long as you learn something from it,” she said in a warm voice. “What was bothering you the most while you prepared for the speech?”
“I was afraid the other students would laugh at me if my speech wasn’t good enough.”
She replied, “You certainly can’t control what others think about your speech. That means you should <u>focus on the one thing you can control.</u>” That woke me up from the depths of despair. Of course, that was it! It wasn’t possible to make my classmates like my message, so the better choice was to concentrate on how I delivered it.
options: ① memorize every word of a speech perfectly
② ask your classmate to work with you on the speech
③ expect everyone in the class to enjoy and agree with your message
④ do your best during the speech, instead of worrying about how others might react
⑤ believe speeches are only successful when no one in the audience laughs during them
questions.explanation: 필자가 타인의 반응(웃음이나 평가)은 통제할 수 없으므로, 스스로 통제할 수 있는 부분인 연설의 전달 방식이나 최선을 다하는 것에 집중해야 한다는 조언을 듣고 깨달음을 얻는 내용입니다. 따라서 타인의 반응에 걱정하기보다 연설에 최선을 다하라는 의미인 ④번이 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 연설의 모든 단어를 완벽하게 암기하다
② 반 친구에게 연설을 함께 준비해달라고 요청하다
③ 학급의 모든 사람이 당신의 메시지를 즐기고 동의할 것이라고 기대하다
④ 타인이 어떻게 반응할지 걱정하는 대신, 연설하는 동안 최선을 다하다
⑤ 청중 중 아무도 웃지 않을 때만 연설이 성공적이라고 믿다

questions.question: [서술형 1] 윗글의 빈칸(A), (B)에 들어갈 문장을 조건에 맞게 완성하시오. [총 4점]
questions.passage:
The next day, I met Ms. Harper after school to talk about the speech. I said, “I’m embarrassed about the speech. (A) _________. (B) _________.”
“It’s quite all right to fall short of your own expectations as long as you learn something from it,” she said in a warm voice. “What was bothering you the most while you prepared for the speech?”
“I was afraid the other students would laugh at me if my speech wasn’t good enough.”
She replied, “You certainly can’t control what others think about your speech. That means you should <u>focus on the one thing you can control.</u>” That woke me up from the depths of despair. Of course, that was it! It wasn’t possible to make my classmates like my message, so the better choice was to concentrate on how I delivered it.
subjective_conditions: 1. 조동사를 활용할 것
2. 문맥상 의미와 어법에 맞게 쓸 것
3. 철자 오류는 오답 처리함
4. <보기>에 주어진 단어를 활용(어형 변화 가능)하되, 단어 추가 가능
5. 해석: (A) 저는 바보처럼 보였음이 틀림없어요. (B) 저는 제가 더 잘할 수 있었다는 걸 알아요.
vocabulary_box: (A) look like / a fool
(B) know / good / do
questions.answer:
(A) I must have looked like a fool.
(B) I know I could have done better.
questions.explanation: (A) '과거의 확실한 추측'을 나타내는 조동사 'must have p.p.'를 사용하여 "I must have looked like a fool"을 완성합니다. (B) '과거에 할 수 있었지만 하지 못한 일'에 대한 후회나 가능성을 나타내는 'could have p.p.'를 활용하여 "I know I could have done better"를 완성합니다.

questions.question: [서술형 2] 다음 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 말을 아래 <보기>에 있는 단어들을 모두 활용하여 <조건>에 맞게 완성하시오. [총 6점]
questions.passage: (A) _________. In evolutionary terms, human senses are adapted to the speed at which humans move through space under their own power while walking. Our ability to distinguish detail in the environment is therefore ideally suited to movement at speeds of perhaps five miles per hour and under. The fastest users of the street, motorists, therefore have a much more limited ability to process details along the street — a motorist simply does not have enough time or ability to appreciate design details. (B) On the other hand, pedestrian travel allows for the _________. Joggers and bicyclists fall somewhere in between these polar opposites; while they travel faster than pedestrians, their rate of speed is ordinarily much slower than that of the typical motorist.
subjective_conditions: 소문항 (A)
1. <보기>의 (A)에 주어진 단어만을 모두 한 번씩만 사용하되, 1개의 단어 추가 및 1개의 단어를 변형할 것
2. 해석: 얼마나 빠르게 사람이 이동하는가가 환경 속 세세한 것을 처리하는 능력을 결정할 것이다.
소문항 (B)
1. <보기>의 (B)에 주어진 단어만을 모두 한 번씩만 사용하되, 2개의 단어를 변형할 것
2. 해석: 반면에, 보행자 이동은 훨씬 더 느려서, 보행자 이동은 환경의 세세한 것의 감상을 허용해 준다.
공통
1. 문맥상 의미와 어법에 맞게 쓸 것
2. 답안지에 소문항 (A), (B)를 명시해 작성할 것, 그렇지 않은 경우 순서대로 채점함.
3. 철자 오류는 오답 처리함
vocabulary_box: (A) determine / how / in the environment / process / be / fast / detail / traveling / will / one / the ability
(B) environmental detail / slow / appreciation of / because / be / much / it
questions.answer:
(A) How fast one is traveling will determine the ability to process details in the environment.
(B) appreciation of environmental detail because it is much slower.
questions.explanation:
(A) 'How fast one is traveling'을 주어절로 사용합니다. 'traveling'은 유지하고, 'is'를 추가하여 진행형을 만들며, 'details'로 복수형 변형을 주어 문장을 완성합니다.
(B) 'appreciation of environmental detail' 뒤에 이유를 나타내는 절 'because it is much slower'를 연결합니다. 'slow'를 'slower'로, 'be'를 'is'로 변형하여 완성합니다.

questions.question: [서술형 3] 다음 소문항 (A), (B)의 빈칸에 들어갈 말을 아래 <보기>에 있는 단어들을 활용하여 <조건>에 맞게 완성하시오. [총 4점]
questions.passage: (A) Everyone has unique experiences, but many people _____________________________________________ outside their lives. Community mapping helps people look outside of themselves, connect with other members of their communities, and share valuable experiences. Community mapping is a collective process. (B) It enables members of a community _____________________________________________________________________________. Community mapping is also a unique and valuable tool as it can be used in diverse ways.
subjective_conditions: 소문항 (A)
1. 해석: 모든 사람들이 독특한 경험을 하지만, 많은 사람들이 그들의 삶 밖에서 일어나는 일로부터 고립되고 단절된 채로 있다.
소문항 (B)
1. 관계부사를 생략하지 말고 활용할 것
2. 해석: 그것은 한 지역 사회의 구성원들이 그들이 사는 장소들의 세부 사항들을 지도로 만들 수 있게 한다.
공통
1. 문맥상 의미와 어법에 맞게 쓸 것
2. <보기>에 주어진 단어를 활용(어형 변화 가능)하되, 단어 추가 가능
3. 답안지에 소문항 (A), (B)를 명시해 작성할 것, 그렇지 않은 경우 순서대로 채점함.
4. 철자 오류는 오답 처리함
vocabulary_box: (A) isolate / remain / connect / go on / from / what
(B) map / the places / live / of / details
questions.answer:
(A) remain isolated and disconnected from what goes on
(B) to map the details of the places where they live
questions.explanation:
(A) '고립되고 단절된 채로 있다'는 상태 유지를 나타내는 remain 뒤에 수동 의미의 형용사 isolated와 disconnected를 병렬로 연결하여 완성합니다. '일어나는 일'은 what goes on으로 표현합니다.
(B) enable A to-v 구문을 사용하여 'to map'으로 시작하며, '그들이 사는 장소들'은 the places 뒤에 관계부사 where를 사용하여 where they live로 수식합니다.

questions.question: [서술형 4] 다음 소문항 (A), (B)의 빈칸에 들어갈 말을 아래 <보기>에 있는 단어들을 사용하여 <조건>에 맞게 완성하시오. [총 6점]
questions.passage: Promotion deals with consumer psychology. We can't force people to think one way or another, and the clever marketer knows that promotion is used to provide information in the most clear, honest, and simple fashion possible. By doing so, the possibility of increasing sales goes up. (A) _________________________ into purchasing something. The long-term effect of getting a consumer to buy something they did not really want or need wasn't good. In fact, consumers fooled once can do damage to sales as they relate their experience to others. Instead, marketers now know that their goal is to identify the consumers who are most likely to appreciate a good or service, and to promote that good or service in a way that makes the value clear to the consumer. (B) Therefore, marketers must know _____________________________________________________________________________.
subjective_conditions: 소문항 (A)
1. 도치 구문을 활용할 것
2. <보기>의 (A)에 주어진 단어만을 모두 한 번씩만 사용하되, 1개 단어만 변형할 것
3. 해석: 무언가를 구매하도록 소비자를 속이기 위해 프로모션이 행해졌던 시대는 갔다.
소문항 (B)
1. <보기>의 (B)에 주어진 단어만을 모두 한 번씩만 사용하되, 1개 단어만 변형할 것
2. 해석: 그러므로, 마케팅 담당자는 그 잠재적인 소비자들이 어디에 있는지, 그리고 어떻게 그들에게 도달해야 하는지 알아야 한다.
1. 문맥상 의미와 어법에 맞게 쓸 것
2. 답안지에 (A), (B)를 명시해 작성할 것, 그렇지 않은 경우 순서대로 채점함
3. 철자 오류는 오답 처리함
vocabulary_box: (A) fool / go / in order to / the consumer / were / when / done / the days / promotions / are
(B) how / them / be / the potential / where / reach / consumers / and / to
questions.answer:
(A) Gone are the days when promotions were done in order to fool the consumer
(B) where the potential consumers are and how to reach them
questions.explanation:
(A) 'The days when... are gone' 문장에서 보어인 gone을 문두로 보내 'Gone are the days when...'의 도치 구문을 만듭니다. go를 Gone으로 변형하여 사용합니다.
(B) 의문사절(간접의문문) 'where the potential consumers are'와 의문사+to부정사 'how to reach them'을 and로 연결합니다. be를 are로 변형하여 사용합니다.

questions.question: 5. 윗글의 제목으로 가장 적절한 것은? [3.7점]
questions.passage: The fast-growing, tremendous amount of data, collected and stored in large and numerous data repositories, (a) <u>have</u> far exceeded our human ability for understanding without powerful tools. As a result, data (b) <u>collected</u> in large data repositories become "data tombs" - data archives that are hardly visited. Important decisions are often made based not on the information-rich data stored in data repositories but rather on a decision maker's instinct, simply because the decision maker does not have the tools (c) <u>to extract</u> the valuable knowledge hidden in the vast amounts of data. Efforts have been made to develop expert system and knowledge-based technologies, (which typically (d) <u>rely</u> on users or domain experts to manually input knowledge into knowledge bases. However, this procedure is likely to cause biases and errors and is extremely costly and time consuming. The widening gap between data and information calls for the systematic development of tools (e) <u>which</u> can turn data tombs into "golden nuggets" of knowledge.
options: ① Why Data Tombs Should Remain Untouched
② The Urgent Need for Tools to Transform Data into Knowledge
③ Research Data Repositories and Long-term Digital Preservation
④ The Rise of Artificial Intelligence and Big Data in Modern Society
⑤ Manual Maintenance: A Crucial Element in Knowledge-Based Data Services
questions.explanation: 방대한 데이터(data tombs)를 가치 있는 지식(golden nuggets)으로 변환할 수 있는 도구 개발의 필요성을 강조하는 글입니다.
options_translation: ① 왜 데이터 무덤이 손대지 않은 채로 남아있어야 하는가
② 데이터를 지식으로 변환하기 위한 도구의 시급한 필요성
③ 연구 데이터 저장소 및 장기 디지털 보존
④ 현대 사회에서 인공지능과 빅데이터의 부상
⑤ 수동 유지관리: 지식 기반 데이터 서비스의 핵심 요소

questions.question: 6. 밑줄 친 (a)~(e) 중 어법상 틀린 것은? [3.2점]
questions.passage: The fast-growing, tremendous amount of data, collected and stored in large and numerous data repositories, (a) <u>have</u> far exceeded our human ability for understanding without powerful tools. As a result, data (b) <u>collected</u> in large data repositories become "data tombs" - data archives that are hardly visited. Important decisions are often made based not on the information-rich data stored in data repositories but rather on a decision maker's instinct, simply because the decision maker does not have the tools (c) <u>to extract</u> the valuable knowledge hidden in the vast amounts of data. Efforts have been made to develop expert system and knowledge-based technologies, (which typically (d) <u>rely</u> on users or domain experts to manually input knowledge into knowledge bases. However, this procedure is likely to cause biases and errors and is extremely costly and time consuming. The widening gap between data and information calls for the systematic development of tools (e) <u>which</u> can turn data tombs into "golden nuggets" of knowledge.
options: ① (a)
② (b)
③ (c)
④ (d)
⑤ (e)
questions.explanation: (a) 문장의 주어는 'The fast-growing, tremendous amount of data'로 'amount'가 핵심 주어이므로 단수 동사인 'has'를 써야 합니다.

questions.question: 8. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 어법상 틀린 것을 고르시오.
questions.passage: Quite often the interaction between groups is socially unequal, and this is reflected in the fact that in many cases borrowing of words or constructions ① <u>goes</u> mostly or entirely in one direction, from the more powerful or prestigious group to the less favored one. The languages of socially subordinated groups may from quite an early period of contact provide terminology for objects or practices ② <u>with which</u> speakers of the more powerful group were previously unfamiliar, but the effects of contact in that direction may not progress any further than this. In some cases, as with the Dharug language of Sydney, Australia, the source of some of the earliest loans from Indigenous Australian languages into English, the fate of the language system is extinction after the obliteration of many of ③ <u>its</u> speakers. The remainder shifted to varieties of English, the language of the people who ④ <u>had suppressed</u> them. In conclusion, language borrowing from dominant to subordinate groups reflects social inequality, ⑤ <u>which</u> the language systems of the latter often vanish even though they may have provided some terms, as exemplified by Dharug in Australia.
questions.explanation: ⑤번 뒤의 문장 구조(the language systems of the latter often vanish)는 완전한 문장이므로, 관계대명사 which는 올 수 없습니다. 맥락상 '그러한 불평등한 상황에서'라는 의미를 나타내는 관계부사 where나 'in which' 등으로 바꾸어야 합니다.

questions.question: 9. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 어법상 틀린 것을 고르시오.
questions.passage: Everyone's heard the expression don't let the perfect become the enemy of the good. If you want to get over an obstacle ① <u>in order for your idea to become</u> the solution-based policy you've long dreamed of, you can't have an all-or-nothing mentality. You have to be willing to alter your idea and allow others ② <u>to influence</u> its outcome. You have to be okay with the outcome being a little different, even a little less, than you wanted. Say you're pushing for a clean water act. Even ③ <u>if</u> what emerges isn't as well-funded as you wished, or doesn't match what you originally conceived the bill to be, you'll have still succeeded in ensuring that kids in troubled areas ④ <u>access</u> to clean water. That's what counts, that they will be safer because of your idea and your effort. Is it perfect? No. Is there more work to be done? Absolutely. But in almost every case, helping move the needle forward is ⑤ <u>much</u> better than not helping at all.
questions.explanation: ④번 'access'는 이 문장에서 동사로 쓰이거나 'have access'의 형태가 되어야 합니다. 'access'가 타동사로 쓰이면 뒤에 'to'가 오지 않으며, 'access'가 명사로 쓰였다면 그 앞에 동사가 필요합니다. 여기서는 ensuring that절 내의 동사가 필요한 자리이므로 'have access' 또는 타동사 'access' 단독으로 쓰여야 하는데, 'access to'라고 되어 있으므로 어법상 틀립니다.

questions.question: 10. 다음 글에서 전체 흐름과 관계 없는 문장은? [3.6점]
questions.passage: Despite the difference between the past and the future, between what has happened and what is to come, it can be suggested that our sense of the past has always been influenced by our view of the future. ① In fact, physics does not distinguish between the past and future, because physically speaking, it is just as likely for time to move backwards as it is for it to move forwards. ② Revolutionaries have always looked to the past to frame their future cause, as is amply illustrated by examples from nationalism to communism. ③ The future has often been seen as variously a recovery of a lost time, as a replication of what is established, or as a model bequeathed by a heroic age long gone. ④ The writing of history is based on understanding or explaining future outcomes that were not known to contemporaries, since the historian has the benefit of hindsight and the past is nothing more than the accumulation of futures that are now our past. ⑤ So, rather than see the hand of the past always shaping the future, perhaps it can be seen in reverse, with the past — in the sense of our understanding of it — being shaped by our orientation to the future.
questions.explanation: 이 글은 과거에 대한 우리의 이해나 역사가 미래에 대한 전망이나 결과론적인 시각에 의해 형성된다는 내용을 담고 있습니다. ①번 문장은 물리학적으로 시간의 방향성에 차이가 없다는 과학적 사실을 언급하고 있어, 역사의 기술과 과거에 대한 인식이라는 글의 주제에서 벗어납니다.

questions.question: 12.다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것을 고르시오.
questions.passage: Creativity can have an effect on productivity. Creativity leads some individuals to recognize problems that others do not see, but which may be very ① <u>complex</u>. Charles Darwin's approach to the speciation problem is a good example of this; he chose a very difficult and tangled problem, speciation, which led him into a long period of data collection and deliberation. This choice of problem ② <u>hindered</u> a quick attack or a simple experiment. In such cases creativity may actually ③ <u>boost</u> productivity (as measured by publication counts) because effort is focused on difficult problems. For others, whose creativity is more focused on methods and technique, creativity may lead to solutions that ④ <u>radically</u> reduce the work necessary to solve a problem. We can see an example in the development of the polymerase chain reaction (PCR) which enables us to amplify small pieces of DNA in a short time. This type of creativity might reduce the number of steps or substitute steps that are ⑤ <u>reliable</u>, thus increasing productivity.
questions.explanation: 어렵고 복잡한 문제를 선택하여 오랜 시간이 걸리는 경우, 논문 편수로 측정되는 생산성은 오히려 '감소(decrease/lower)'하게 되므로 boost는 적절하지 않습니다.

questions.question: 13. 다음 글의 주제로 가장 적절한 것은? [3.5점]
questions.passage: Scholars of myth have long argued that myth gives structure and meaning to human life; that meaning is amplified when a myth evolves into a world. A virtual world's ability to fulfill needs grows when lots and lots of people believe in the world. Conversely, a virtual world cannot be long sustained by a mere handful of adherents. Consider the difference between a global sport and a game I invent with my nine friends and play regularly. My game might be a great game, one that is completely immersive, one that consumes all of my group's time and attention. If its reach is limited to the ten of us, though, then it's ultimately just a weird hobby, and it has limited social function. For a virtual world to provide lasting, wide-ranging value, its participants must be a large enough group to be considered a society. When that threshold is reached, psychological value can turn into wide-ranging social value.
options: ① need for a sufficient group size to uphold the social value of a myth
② importance of keeping a virtual world small to maintain its uniqueness
③ role of individual imagination in the creation of virtual worlds and myths
④ virtual worlds that can thrive without any need for collective participation
⑤ how myths can be effective with only a few people who believe in them
questions.explanation: 이 글은 가상 세계나 신화가 사회적 가치를 지니고 지속되기 위해서는 충분히 큰 규모의 참여자 집단이 필요하다는 내용을 다루고 있습니다.
options_translation: ① 신화의 사회적 가치를 유지하기 위한 충분한 집단 크기의 필요성
② 독특함을 유지하기 위해 가상 세계를 작게 유지하는 것의 중요성
③ 가상 세계와 신화 생성에 있어 개인적 상상력의 역할
④ 집단적 참여의 필요 없이 번성할 수 있는 가상 세계
⑤ 믿는 사람이 소수일 때 신화가 효과적일 수 있는 방법

questions.question: 14. 글의 흐름으로 보아, (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은? [3.4점]
questions.passage: The governments of virtually every country on the planet attach greater importance to achieving food security and a wide variety of mechanisms have been developed to realize this goal. The first issue governments face in achieving national food security is the problem of insuring that adequate amounts of food are available to the resident population. Some governments have set goals of food self-sufficiency, which means most if not all of the food available in a country comes from the domestic farming system. (A) _________, food security does not require food self-sufficiency because countries can import food items not easily produced within the country. Agricultural products are, after all, highly sensitive to climatic, soil and other conditions that tend to vary around the world. Even countries with extremely productive agricultural sectors are not fully self-sufficient in all food items. The United States, (B) _________, depends on imports for its supply of coffee, tea, bananas and other tropical products. In general, the problem of assuring adequate food supplies is solved by relying on both domestic production and imports. (C) _________, food security could exist without a high level of self-sufficiency, if trade were stable and provided a population with safe and nutritious food. However, food security is much more complicated than this due to climatic, economic and political risks, and disruptions to the supply chain.
options: ① However   ...   in fact        ...   Sequentially
② However   ...   for instance   ...   Technically
③ Therefore ...   however       ...   Consequently
④ Therefore ...   hence         ...   Conversely
⑤ Therefore ...   in sum        ...   Occasionally
questions.explanation: (A) 앞 문장에서 식량 자급자족을 목표로 한다는 내용을 언급하고, 뒤에서는 식량 안보에 자급자족이 반드시 필요한 것은 아니라는 대조적인 내용을 제시하므로 However가 적절합니다. (B) 미국이 커피, 차 등을 수입에 의존한다는 구체적인 사례를 들고 있으므로 for instance가 적절합니다. (C) 무역이 안정적이라면 기술적으로(이론적으로) 자급자족 없이도 식량 안보가 가능함을 설명하므로 Technically가 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 그러나 ... 사실은 ... 순차적으로
② 그러나 ... 예를 들어 ... 엄밀히 말하면
③ 그러므로 ... 하지만 ... 결과적으로
④ 그러므로 ... 따라서 ... 반대로
⑤ 그러므로 ... 요약하자면 ... 가끔

questions.question: 15. 다음 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것을 고르시오.
questions.passage: Intuition is valuable, but only when _________. Only then are they able to act quickly in accordance with their internalized expertise and evidence-based experience. Experts, for example, are able to think on their feet because they've invested thousands of hours in learning and practice: their intuition has become data-driven. Yet most people are not experts, though they often think they are. Most of us, especially when we interact with others on social media, act with expert-like speed and conviction, offering a wide range of opinions on global crises, without the substance of knowledge that supports it. And thanks to AI, which ensures that our messages are delivered to an audience more inclined to believing it, our delusions of expertise can be reinforced by our personal filter bubble. We have an interesting tendency to find people more open-minded, rational, and sensible when they think just like us.
options: ① it sounds plausible
② it contradicts the facts
③ instinct takes precedence over expertise
④ it's earned through effort and experience
⑤ the voices of non-experts are taken seriously
questions.explanation: 지문은 전문가들의 직관이 가치 있는 이유는 그것이 수천 시간의 학습과 연습을 통해 데이터화된 전문성 및 증거 기반의 경험에서 나오기 때문이라고 설명합니다. 따라서 빈칸에는 직관이 '노력과 경험을 통해 얻어질 때' 가치가 있다는 내용이 들어가는 것이 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 그것이 그럴싸하게 들릴 때
② 그것이 사실과 상충할 때
③ 본능이 전문성보다 앞설 때
④ 그것이 노력과 경험을 통해 얻어질 때
⑤ 비전문가의 목소리가 진지하게 받아들여질 때

questions.question: 16. 다음 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것을 고르시오.
questions.passage: Beethoven's drive to create something novel is a reflection of his state of curiosity. Our brains experience a sense of reward when we create something new in the process of exploring something uncertain, such as a musical phrase that we've never played or heard before. When our curiosity leads to something novel, the resulting reward brings us a sense of pleasure. A number of investigators have modeled how curiosity influences musical composition. In the case of Beethoven, computer modeling focused on the thirty-two piano sonatas written after age thirteen revealed that the musical patterns found in all of Beethoven's music decreased in later sonatas, while novel patterns, including patterns that were unique to a particular sonata, increased. In other words, Beethoven's music became less predictable over time as his curiosity drove the exploration of new musical ideas.
options: ① a key force behind creative exploration
② an outcome of mechanical musical training
③ a reaction to repeated exposure to familiar situations
④ an essential element in balancing mass appeal and musical quality
⑤ a strong driver of the increasing predictability of the commercial music industry
questions.explanation: 이 글은 베토벤의 음악적 창의성이 그의 호기심에서 비롯되었음을 설명하고 있습니다. 호기심이 새로운 음악적 아이디어를 탐구하게 만들고, 이것이 새로운 패턴의 증가로 이어졌다는 내용이므로 빈칸에는 '창의적 탐구의 핵심적인 힘'이라는 내용이 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 창의적 탐구 뒤에 있는 핵심적인 힘
② 기계적인 음악 훈련의 결과물
③ 친숙한 상황에 대한 반복적인 노출에 대한 반응
④ 대중적 매력과 음악적 질의 균형을 맞추는 필수 요소
⑤ 상업 음악 산업의 예측 가능성 증가의 강력한 동인

questions.question: 17. 다음 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것을 고르시오.
questions.passage: The concept of ecosystem states should be familiar to anyone with a home vegetable garden. The garden is a small ecosystem that the grower attempts to keep in a specific state, namely the maximization of fruit and vegetable production. To achieve this, the grower is almost always intervening in the dynamics of the ecosystem; they remove unwanted plants that begin to grow and perhaps spray insecticides and fence off the patch to stop insects and other animals from consuming the vegetables. Since maximizing vegetable growth is an inherently unstable state for the ecosystem, the grower is effectively keeping the ball on a slope. If the grower stops intervening, even for a day, the ecosystem, that small patch of ground, will naturally begin to __________. Vegetables may still grow, but yield will almost certainly be lower as other plants crowd out the vegetables and wildlife consume the produce.
options: ① remain intact and primitive
② attract more helpful microbes
③ get back to a more stable state
④ get uncontrollable with various weeds
⑤ be inhabited by some of the rare species
questions.explanation: 글의 맥락에서 채소 재배 상태는 인간의 개입으로 유지되는 '불안정한' 상태이며, 개입을 멈추면 생태계는 자연스럽게 (인간에게는 수확량이 적어 좋지 않지만) '안정적인' 상태로 돌아가려고 한다는 내용이 이어집니다. 따라서 '더 안정적인 상태로 돌아가다'가 정답입니다.
options_translation: ① 온전하고 원시적인 상태로 남다
② 더 도움이 되는 미생물을 끌어들이다
③ 더 안정적인 상태로 돌아가다
④ 다양한 잡초로 통제 불능이 되다
⑤ 몇몇 희귀종들이 서식하게 되다

questions.question: 18. 다음 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것을 고르시오.
questions.passage: A common but incorrect assumption is that we are creatures of reason when, in fact, we are creatures of both reason and emotion. We cannot get by on reason alone since any reason always eventually leads to a feeling. Should I get a wholegrain cereal or a chocolate cereal? I can list all the reasons I want, but the reasons have to be based on something. For example, if my goal is to eat healthy, I can choose the wholegrain cereal, but what is my reason for wanting to be healthy? I can list more and more reasons such as wanting to live longer, spending more quality time with loved ones, etc., but what are the reasons for those reasons? You should be able to see by now that __________. These deep-seated values, feelings, and emotions we have are rarely a result of reasoning, but can certainly be influenced by reasoning. We have values, feelings, and emotions before we begin to reason and long before we begin to reason effectively.
options: ① logic entirely precedes emotion for us
② reason is the sole foundation of all our actions and beliefs
③ emotions have little impact on our decision-making process
④ our decisions are always based purely on scientific evidence
⑤ the reasons we give are often just a rationalization of deeper, emotional impulses or values
questions.explanation: 이 글은 인간이 이성적인 존재일 뿐만 아니라 감정적인 존재이며, 이성은 결국 깊은 감정이나 가치에 기반을 두고 있다는 것을 설명합니다. 우리가 제시하는 이유들은 결국 더 깊은 감정적 충동이나 가치를 합리화하는 것일 뿐이라는 결론이 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 논리가 우리에게 전적으로 감정에 앞선다
② 이성이 우리 모든 행동과 믿음의 유일한 토대이다
③ 감정은 우리의 의사 결정 과정에 거의 영향을 주지 않는다
④ 우리의 결정은 항상 순수하게 과학적 증거에 근거한다
⑤ 우리가 제시하는 이유는 종종 더 깊은 감정적 충동이나 가치에 대한 합리화일 뿐이다

questions.question: 19. 주어진 글 다음에 이어질 글의 순서로 가장 적절한 것을 고르시오. 19. [3.6점]
questions.passage: We are the only species that seasons its food, deliberately altering it with the highly flavored plant parts we call herbs and spices.
ordered_passages: (A) It's quite possible that our taste for spices has an evolutionary root. Many spices have antibacterial properties — in fact, common seasonings such as garlic, onion, and oregano inhibit the growth of almost every bacterium tested.

(B) In contrast, the most lightly spiced cuisines — those of Scandinavia and northern Europe — are from cooler climates. Our uniquely human attention to flavor, in this case the flavor of spices, turns out to have arisen as a matter of life and death.

(C) Consequently, the cultures that make the heaviest use of spices — think of the garlic and black pepper of Thai food, the ginger and coriander of India, the chili peppers of Mexico — come from warmer climates, where bacterial spoilage is a bigger issue.
questions.explanation: 인간이 음식에 양념을 하는 유일한 종이라는 도입부 뒤에, (A)에서 향신료에 대한 기호가 진화적 뿌리(항균 특성)를 가졌을 가능성을 언급합니다. (C)에서 그 결과(Consequently) 박테리아 부패가 큰 문제인 더운 지역에서 향신료를 많이 사용한다는 내용이 이어지며, (B)에서 이와 대조적으로(In contrast) 추운 기후인 북유럽 지역은 향신료를 적게 쓴다는 내용으로 마무리되는 것이 가장 적절합니다.

questions.question: 20. 주어진 글 다음에 이어질 글의 순서로 가장 적절한 것을 고르시오. 20. [3.8점]
questions.passage: Robert Blattberg and Steven Hoch noted that, in a changing environment, it is not clear that consistency is always a virtue and that one of the advantages of human judgment is the ability to detect change.
ordered_passages: (A) Humans, however, can incorporate these novel factors in their judgments. The composite — or average of human judgments and statistical models — proved to be more accurate than either the statistical models or the managers working alone.

(B) Thus, in changing environments, it might be advantageous to combine human judgment and statistical models. Blattberg and Hoch examined this possibility by having supermarket managers forecast demand for certain products and then creating a composite forecast by averaging these judgments with the forecasts of statistical models based on past data.

(C) The logic was that statistical models assume stable conditions and therefore cannot account for the effects on demand of novel events such as actions taken by competitors or the introduction of new products.
questions.explanation: 변화하는 환경에서 인간의 판단력이 변화를 감지하는 데 유리하다는 도입부 뒤에, (B)에서 따라서(Thus) 인간의 판단과 통계 모델을 결합하는 것이 유리할 수 있다는 점을 언급하며 Blattberg와 Hoch의 실험을 소개합니다. (C)에서 그 논리(The logic)는 통계 모델이 안정적인 조건을 가정하여 새로운 사건을 설명할 수 없다는 점임을 설명하고, (A)에서 그러나(however) 인간은 이러한 새로운 요소를 통합할 수 있어 결합된 예측치가 더 정확했다는 결과로 이어집니다.

questions.question: 21. 다음 글의 내용을 요약하고자 한다. 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은? [3.8점]
questions.passage: The prominence of the social dimension in food writing might suggest that the flavor of food is taking a back seat. I suspect that most people view flavor as of secondary importance in social settings where food is served. Although our social gatherings coalesce around food, the meaning of these gatherings does not seem to depend on flavor. Flavor assists with the narrow purpose of filling the belly, and once that is accomplished it provides the backdrop for whatever social dynamics characterize the gathering. These can be understood independently of the flavor of the food on offer, the appreciation of which is understood to be personal and subjective. According to this conventional wisdom, the ceremonies and rituals around food, the social events that supply food with its meaning, do not depend on the quality of sensations provided by the food. To focus excessively on flavor is to miss the larger significance of these social relations.
questions.summary_sentence: In the social gatherings, the flavor of food plays a(n) (A) _________ role, and therefore, should not (B) _________ the primary goal or meaning of the social events.
options: ① ambiguous ... disclose
② eminent ... facilitate
③ leading ... generalize
④ subjective ... emphasize
⑤ supporting ... overshadow
questions.explanation: 이 글은 음식의 맛보다 사교적인 차원이 더 중요하게 여겨진다는 점을 설명하고 있다. 따라서 사회적 모임에서 음식의 맛은 (A) 보조적인(supporting) 역할을 하며, 사회적 행사의 주된 목표나 의미를 (B) 가리지(overshadow) 않아야 한다는 내용이 적절하다.
options_translation: ① 모호한 ... 드러내다
② 저명한 ... 촉진하다
③ 주도적인 ... 일반화하다
④ 주관적인 ... 강조하다
⑤ 보조적인 ... 가리다(무색하게 하다)

questions.question: 23. 다음 글의 내용을 가장 잘 나타내는 속담은? [3.3점]
questions.passage: Too many times people, especially in today's generation, expect things to just happen overnight. When we have these false expectations, it tends to discourage us from continuing to move forward. Because this is a high tech society, everything we want has to be within the parameters of our comfort and convenience. If it doesn't happen fast enough, we're tempted to lose interest. So many people don't want to take the time it requires to be successful. Success is not a matter of mere desire; you should develop patience in order to achieve it. Have you fallen prey to impatience?
options: ① Time is money.
② You snooze, you lose.
③ Rome wasn't built in a day.
④ Strike while the iron is hot.
⑤ The early bird catches the worm.
questions.explanation: 이 글은 성공을 위해서는 인내심을 갖고 시간이 필요하다는 점을 강조하고 있으므로 '로마는 하루아침에 이루어지지 않았다(Rome wasn't built in a day)'가 가장 적절한 속담입니다.
options_translation: ① 시간은 금이다.
② 졸면 기회를 놓친다.
③ 로마는 하루아침에 이루어지지 않았다.
④ 쇠뿔도 단김에 빼라.
⑤ 일찍 일어나는 새가 벌레를 잡는다.

questions.question: [서술형3] 다음 글의 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 말을 <보기>에 있는 단어들을 활용하여 <조건>에 맞게 문장을 완성하시오. [5점]
questions.passage: Human beings like certainty. This liking stems from our ancient ancestors who needed to survive alongside saber-toothed tigers and poisonous berries. Our brains evolved to help us attend to threats, keep away from them, and remain alive afterward. In fact, according to our experience, (A) _________, (B) _________. Is this berry the same shape as last time? The same size? If I know for certain it is, my brain will direct me to eat it because I know it's safe. And if I'm uncertain, my brain will send out a danger alert to protect me. The dependence on certainty all those millennia ago ensured our survival to the present day, and the danger-alert system continues to protect us. This is achieved by our brains labeling new, vague, or unpredictable everyday events and experiences as uncertain. Our brains then generate sensations, thoughts, and action plans to keep us safe from the uncertain element, and we live to see another day.
subjective_conditions: 1. 답안지에 (A), (B)를 명시해 작성할 것
2. 우리말 뜻: (A) 우리는 우리 자신이 무언가에 대해 더 확신할수록 (B) 옳은 선택을 할 가능성이 더 크다
3. 「the 비교급, the 비교급 구문」을 사용할 것
4. <보기>에 제시된 모든 단어 및 어구는 한 번씩만 사용할 수 있으며 모두 사용하여야 함
5. 의미와 어법에 맞게 <보기>에 제시된 단어 중 한 단어를 변형하고, <보기>에 제시되지 않았으나 문맥상 필요한 한 단어를 추가할 것
6. 철자 오류는 오답 처리함
vocabulary_box: (A) the / about / we / something / are / confidence
(B) have / of / possibility / great / we / make / the / the right choice
questions.answer:
(A) the more confidence we are about something
(B) the greater possibility we have of making the right choice
questions.explanation:
이 문제는 'the + 비교급, the + 비교급' 구문을 활용하여 문장을 구성하는 서술형 문제입니다.
(A) '우리는 우리 자신이 무언가에 대해 더 확신할수록'을 영작하면, 형용사 confident를 사용하여 'the more confident we are about something'이 되지만, 보기에는 명사 confidence가 주어졌으므로 이를 형용사 confident로 변형해야 합니다. (the more confident we are about something)
(B) '옳은 선택을 할 가능성이 더 크다'는 'the greater possibility we have of making the right choice'로 영작합니다. 보기의 great를 비교급 greater로 변형하고, 전치사 of 뒤에 동사 make를 동명사 making으로 변형하여 문맥과 어법을 맞춥니다. 또한 원문 흐름상 '더 크다'는 비교급의 의미를 위해 greater를 사용합니다.

questions.question: [서술형4] 다음 글의 주제를 <보기>의 단어들을 활용하여 <조건>에 맞게 문장으로 완성하시오. [6점]
questions.passage: It seems natural to describe certain environmental conditions as 'extreme', 'harsh', 'benign' or 'stressful'. It may seem obvious when conditions are 'extreme': the midday heat of a desert, the cold of an Antarctic winter, the salinity of the Great Salt Lake. But this only means that these conditions are extreme for us, given our particular physiological characteristics and tolerances. To a cactus there is nothing extreme about the desert conditions in which cacti have evolved; nor are the icy lands of Antarctica an extreme environment for penguins. It is lazy and dangerous for the ecologist to assume that all other organisms sense the environment in the way we do. Rather, the ecologist should try to gain a worm's-eye or plant's-eye view of the environment: to see the world as others see it. Emotive words like harsh and benign, even relativities such as hot and cold, should be used by ecologists only with care.
subjective_conditions: 1. 답안지에 (A), (B)를 명시해 작성할 것
2. 모든 단어 및 어구는 한 번씩만 사용할 수 있으며 모두 사용하여야 함
3. 단어 변형 및 추가 없음
4. 철자 오류는 오답 처리함
vocabulary_box: (A) human perspective / differently / depending on / perceived / environmental conditions / are
(B) the environment / understand / of / from / other / the viewpoint / organisms
questions.answer:
(A) environmental conditions are perceived differently depending on human perspective
(B) understand the environment from the viewpoint of other organisms
questions.explanation:
지문의 주제는 환경 조건이 인간의 관점에 따라 다르게 인식될 수 있으며, 생태학자는 다른 생물의 관점에서 환경을 이해해야 한다는 것입니다.
(A) 부분은 '환경 조건은 인간의 관점에 따라 다르게 인식된다'는 의미가 되도록 'environmental conditions are perceived differently depending on human perspective'로 배열합니다.
(B) 부분은 '생태학자들은 다른 유기체들의 관점에서 환경을 이해해야 한다'는 의미가 되도록 'understand the environment from the viewpoint of other organisms'로 배열합니다.

questions.question: 1. 다음 글의 주제로 가장 적절한 것은? [3.7점]
questions.passage: The responsive behavior of dogs also caught the attention of an evolutionary anthropologist, Brian Hare. He conducted an experiment to see how dogs would respond to human gestures compared to wolves, who share the same common ancestor. He placed two cups on the ground with food hidden under only one of them. When he pointed to the cup with the food, the dogs found it easily. The wolves, however, struggled and chose cups at random, paying no attention to his gestures. Dr. Hare concluded that the dogs' ability to read human gestures allowed them to perform better than the wolves. He explained that dogs, unlike wolves, have developed communicative skills with humans and a sense of friendliness. This explanation sounds reasonable according to several evolutionary biologists. They say that from the common ancestors of these two species, those that acted friendly toward humans evolved into dogs, and those that didn't became wolves.
options: ① role of human gestures in animal training
② similarities of biological evolution between dogs and wolves
③ benefits and drawbacks of dogs' friendliness toward humans
④ reason why different species came from the same ancestor
⑤ common belief that wolves struggle to understand human signals
questions.explanation: 이 글은 같은 조상에서 갈라져 나온 개와 늑대가 인간의 제스처에 다르게 반응하는 실험을 통해, 인간에 대해 우호적으로 행동한 종이 개로 진화하고 그렇지 않은 종이 늑대가 되었다는 진화론적 배경을 설명하고 있습니다. 따라서 '서로 다른 종이 같은 조상으로부터 나온 이유'를 다루고 있는 ④번이 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 동물 훈련에서 인간 제스처의 역할
② 개와 늑대 사이의 생물학적 진화의 유사성
③ 인간에 대한 개의 우호성의 장단점
④ 서로 다른 종이 같은 조상으로부터 나온 이유
⑤ 늑대가 인간의 신호를 이해하는 데 어려움을 겪는다는 일반적인 믿음

questions.question: 2. 다음 글의 제목으로 가장 적절한 것은? [3.5점]
questions.passage: No respectable boss would say, "I make it a point to discourage my staff from speaking up, and I maintain a culture that prevents disagreeing viewpoints from ever getting aired." If anything, most bosses even say that they are pro-dissent. This idea can be found throughout the series of conversations with corporate, university, and nonprofit leaders, published weekly in the business sections of newspapers. In the interviews, the featured leaders are asked about their management techniques, and regularly claim to continually encourage internal protest from more junior staffers. As Bob Pittman remarked in one of these conversations: "I want us to listen to these dissenters because they may intend to tell you why we can't do something, but if you listen hard, what they're really telling you is what you must do to get something done."
options: ① Promoting Dissent: The Value of Listening in Leadership
② Avoiding Conflict: The Secret to Successful Management
③ Limiting Voices: How Leaders Control Their Staff
④ The Power of Silence in Leadership
⑤ Leaders Who Force Their Staff
questions.explanation: 대부분의 리더들이 반대 의견(dissent)을 장려한다고 주장하며, 특히 마지막 문장에서 반대자들의 의견을 경청하는 것이 일을 완수하기 위해 무엇을 해야 하는지 알려준다는 점에서 리더십에서 반대 의견을 장려하고 경청하는 것의 가치를 다루고 있습니다.
options_translation: ① 반대 의견 장려하기: 리더십에서 경청의 가치
② 갈등 피하기: 성공적인 경영의 비밀
③ 목소리 제한하기: 리더들이 직원을 통제하는 방법
④ 리더십에서 침묵의 힘
⑤ 직원을 강요하는 리더들

questions.question: 3. 다음 글의 요지로 가장 적절한 것은? [3.1점]
questions.passage: Crop rotation is the process in which farmers change the crops they grow in their fields in a special order. For example, if a farmer has three fields, he or she may grow carrots in the first field, green beans in the second, and tomatoes in the third. The next year, green beans will be in the first field, tomatoes in the second field, and carrots will be in the third. In year three, the crops will rotate again. By the fourth year, the crops will go back to their original order. Each crop enriches the soil for the next crop. This type of farming is sustainable because the soil stays healthy.
options: ① 유기농 작물을 재배하기 위해서는 윤작이 필수적이다.
② 윤작에서는 세 가지 작물의 재배 순서가 가장 중요하다.
③ 토양을 비옥하게 유지하는 윤작은 지속가능한 농업 유형이다.
④ 특정 작물의 선택적 재배가 지속가능한 농업 환경을 결정한다.
⑤ 매년 다른 작물을 재배하는 것은 작물의 생산량 증가와 관련이 있다.
questions.explanation: 글의 마지막 부분에서 윤작(crop rotation)이 토양을 건강하게 유지하게 하여 지속 가능한 농법이라고 명시하고 있으므로 ③번이 정답입니다.

questions.question: 4. 다음 글의 분위기로 가장 적절한 것은? [3.1점]
questions.passage: It was early morning and still dark when we returned to Auntie's place. All the lights were on, and the village people were waiting for us. Smiling, Nani Tama lifted up the whakapapa and offered it to the village. My eyes were filled with tears as I saw the warmth in everyone's faces. Our hearts were full because our grandfather had saved our past for us. Our Nani Tama smiled again. His smile grew tired. There was a deep sadness in his eyes, but also a sense of peace. He sighed. "At last, I may go now." Then, he closed his eyes. "No, Dad!" Auntie Hiraina cried.
options: ① tired and hopeless
② scary and nervous
③ bright and excited
④ hopeful and energetic
⑤ sorrowful and touching
questions.explanation: 할아버지가 마을 사람들에게 유산을 전달하고 평화롭게 눈을 감는 장면으로, 고모의 울음과 사람들의 따뜻함이 교차하는 슬프면서도 감동적인(sorrowful and touching) 분위기이다.
options_translation: ① 피곤하고 절망적인
② 무섭고 긴장된
③ 밝고 신나는
④ 희망차고 활기찬
⑤ 슬프고 감동적인

questions.question: 5. 밑줄 친 <u>Each flower adds to the beauty when it harmonizes with the others</u>가 다음 글에서 의미하는 바로 가장 적절한 것은? [3.9점]
questions.passage: In our competitive society, many people believe that only the biggest or the strongest can survive and thrive. However, I propose an alternative view: kindness is the key to success. Isn't that a comforting thought? We can use the power of our natural kindness to communicate and cooperate with different individuals. We can all benefit from this instead of trying to be better than others. I'd like to end this talk with a message. Think of our society as a bouquet. <u>Each flower adds to the beauty when it harmonizes with the others</u>. Likewise, by being kind and working together, we can truly flourish. Thank you for your attention.
options: ① Individuals' distinct personalities are significant
② The more flowers there are, the more beautiful they are
③ Only the biggest and strongest can survive in a community
④ We can contribute to making a better world through cooperation
⑤ If we work together, the economic, social situation will grow worse
questions.explanation: 사회 전체가 꽃다발처럼 서로 조화를 이룰 때 아름다워진다는 비유는 협력을 통해 더 나은 세상을 만들 수 있다는 의미를 담고 있다.
options_translation: ① 개인의 뚜렷한 개성이 중요하다
② 꽃이 많을수록 더 아름답다
③ 공동체에서는 가장 크고 강한 자만이 살아남을 수 있다
④ 우리는 협력을 통해 더 나은 세상을 만드는 데 기여할 수 있다
⑤ 우리가 함께 일한다면 경제적, 사회적 상황은 더 악화될 것이다

questions.question: 6. 다음 글의 내용과 일치하지 않는 것은? [3.0점]
questions.passage:
We traveled all night, mostly in silence, listening to Nani chanting in the darkness. It was strange but wonderful to hear him. Sometimes, he burst into a song that he had taught Auntie. They sang together, lifting up their voices to send the song flying like a bird through the sky. Just before noon, we arrived at a small town called Murupara.
"Where do we go now?" I asked Nani.
