He did not reply, but he was searching inside himself, staring at the small houses. Then, at a street corner, he told us to turn. After turning the corner, we saw an old man standing in front of a house. He welcomed Nani Tama with a gentle smile, but in his eyes, I saw the message, "We must hurry."
options: ① 할아버지는 이동하면서 낭송하기도 했다.
② 할아버지는 고모와 함께 노래를 부르기도 했다.
③ 정오를 조금 지나 우리는 작은 마을에 도착했다.
④ 할아버지는 자신의 기억 속에서 길을 찾고 있었다.
⑤ 한 노인이 온화한 미소를 지으며 할아버지를 맞이했다.
questions.explanation: 본문에서 'Just before noon, we arrived at a small town(정오 바로 전에, 우리는 작은 마을에 도착했다)'이라고 언급되어 있으므로 '정오를 조금 지나' 도착했다는 ③번은 일치하지 않는다.

questions.question: 7. Messengers in the Inca empire에 관한 다음 글의 내용과 일치하지 않는 것은? [3.1점]
questions.passage: With no horses available, the Inca empire excelled at delivering messages on foot. The messengers were stationed on the royal roads to deliver the Inca king's orders and reports coming from his lands. Called Chasquis, they lived in groups of four to six in huts, placed from one to two miles apart along the roads. They were all young men and especially good runners who watched the road in both directions. If they caught sight of another messenger coming, they hurried out to meet them. The Inca built the huts on high ground, in sight of one another. When a messenger neared the next hut, he began to call out and repeated the message three or four times to the one who was running out to meet him. The Inca empire could relay messages 1,000 miles (1,610 km) in three or four days under good conditions.
options: ① 왕의 명령과 그의 영토에서 오는 보고를 전달하기 위해 배치되었다.
② 네 명에서 여섯 명의 집단으로 1~2마일 간격으로 떨어진 오두막에서 생활했다.
③ 모두 젊은 남성으로 한쪽 방향의 길만 주시하며 잘 달리는 사람들이었다.
④ 다른 전령이 오는 것을 보면 그들을 맞이하러 서둘러 나갔다.
⑤ 다음 오두막에 다가갈 때, 다음 전령에게 메시지를 서너 번 반복하여 소리쳤다.
questions.explanation: 본문에서 'watched the road in both directions(양쪽 방향의 길을 모두 주시했다)'라고 언급되어 있으므로 '한쪽 방향의 길만 주시하며'라는 ③번은 일치하지 않는다.

questions.question: 8. 밑줄 친 (a)~(e) 중 어법상 적절하지 않은 것은? [3.4점]
questions.passage: I'll give you another example of how friendliness is related to survival. Dr. Hare and his colleagues designed an experiment with chimpanzees and bonobos. (a) <u>Having</u> genetic similarities, they are different in nature. To study their cooperative behavior, Dr. Hare's team set up a device (b) <u>required</u> two individuals to pull both ends of a rope at the same time in order to access food on a board. When (c) <u>placed</u> with partners that the chimpanzees knew, they were able to work together to get the food. However, when paired with new partners, the chimpanzees usually failed (d) <u>to get</u> the food, and when they occasionally succeeded, they did not share the food with their partner. The bonobos, on the other hand, got along much better than the chimpanzees. They solved the problem regardless of which individual they paired with, and they were also more willing to the food. This research shows that bonobos have a cooperative and friendly nature. Experts suggest that their nature has provided them a(an) _________ . If it (e) <u>had not been</u> for these characteristics, they might have faced extinction.
options: ① (a)
② (b)
③ (c)
④ (d)
⑤ (e)
questions.explanation: (b)의 required는 앞에 있는 명사 a device를 수식하는 분사 자리인데, 장치가 두 개체를 '요구하는' 능동의 의미를 가져야 하므로 현재분사인 requiring 또는 주격 관계대명사+동사 형태인 that required로 고쳐야 합니다.

questions.question: 9. 윗글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은? [3.3점]
questions.passage: I'll give you another example of how friendliness is related to survival. Dr. Hare and his colleagues designed an experiment with chimpanzees and bonobos. (a) <u>Having</u> genetic similarities, they are different in nature. To study their cooperative behavior, Dr. Hare's team set up a device (b) <u>required</u> two individuals to pull both ends of a rope at the same time in order to access food on a board. When (c) <u>placed</u> with partners that the chimpanzees knew, they were able to work together to get the food. However, when paired with new partners, the chimpanzees usually failed (d) <u>to get</u> the food, and when they occasionally succeeded, they did not share the food with their partner. The bonobos, on the other hand, got along much better than the chimpanzees. They solved the problem regardless of which individual they paired with, and they were also more willing to the food. This research shows that bonobos have a cooperative and friendly nature. Experts suggest that their nature has provided them a(an) _________ . If it (e) <u>had not been</u> for these characteristics, they might have faced extinction.
options: ① physical defect
② biological diversity
③ aggressive instinct
④ genetic information
⑤ competitive advantage
questions.explanation: 글 전체의 맥락이 친화력(friendliness)이 생존(survival)과 관련이 있으며, 보노보의 협력적이고 우호적인 성격이 멸종을 면하게 해주었다는 내용이므로, 이러한 성격이 그들에게 '경쟁 우위(competitive advantage)'를 제공했다고 보는 것이 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 신체적 결함
② 생물학적 다양성
③ 공격적 본능
④ 유전 정보
⑤ 경쟁 우위

questions.question: 10. 다음 글에서 밑줄친 he가 가리키는 대상이 나머지와 다른 것은? [3.5점]
questions.passage:
The phone rang, and it was my dad calling from my hometown, Waituhi.
"Can you take a week off?" ① <u>he</u> asked. "Your Nani Tama wants you here."
"But Dad!" I answered. "My boss won't let me take any more time off."
The phone went silent, and then I heard my grandfather say faintly, "I need your help, Grandson. Drive me there. Hurry, I may not have much time."
I just knew I had no choice. When I arrived at Auntie's place, I was shocked to see how thin ② <u>he</u> was.
"Look, Nani," I said. "I'm not taking you anywhere. You could die on me!"
③ <u>He</u> looked at me in anger.
The old man held on tightly to the side of the bed and cried out as ④ <u>he</u> stood up. Every slow, painful step hurt him, but ⑤ <u>he</u> tried to walk. I could not help but carry him to the car, and we set off with Auntie.
questions.explanation: ①번의 he는 주인공에게 전화를 건 '아버지(Dad)'를 가리키며, 나머지 ②, ③, ④, ⑤는 주인공의 할아버지(Nani Tama)를 가리킵니다.

questions.question: 11. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 어법상 적절하지 않은 것은? [4.1점]
questions.passage: For some time, ① <u>my grandfather had been busy recording our genealogy</u>, which is known as whakapapa. Nani Tama had been in his old house for three nights, ②<u>destroying our past as he sang the names</u>. On the fourth night, everything stopped. Nani Tama, in despair, went to stay with his sister, Auntie Hiraina. ③ <u>While trying to recover the names of the past, Nani began to sing the names</u> with his shaky hands. He sang of our ancestors, joining the past to the present. The village went quiet and Nani Tama's voice traveled along the lines of our genealogy, searching back across the centuries. Sometimes, ④ <u>there were lines difficult to remember</u>. Then his voice suddenly stopped in the middle of the chant. The village waited in worried silence until the next name burst out of his mouth. It took Nani Tama almost two years to gather most of the whakapapa, ⑤ <u>but there were still missing names which needed to fill in</u>. Now, he wanted me to drive him to Murupara to finish his work.
questions.explanation: ⑤번에서 '채워져야 할' 이름들이라는 수동의 의미가 되어야 하므로 which needed to be filled in으로 고쳐야 어법상 적절합니다.

questions.question: 12. [3.7점] 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것을 고르시오.
questions.passage: One of the most striking characteristics of a sleeping animal or person is that they do not respond normally to environmental stimuli. If you open the eyelids of a sleeping mammal the eyes will not see normally - they are functionally ① <u>blind</u>. Some visual information apparently gets in, but it is not processed ② <u>properly</u> as it is shortened or weakened; same with the other sensing systems. Stimuli are ③ <u>registered</u> but not processed normally and they fail to wake the individual. Perceptual disengagement probably serves the function of protecting sleep, so some authors do not count it as part of the definition of sleep itself. But as sleep would be ④ <u>impossible</u> with it, it seems essential to its definition. Nevertheless, many animals (including humans) use the ⑤ <u>intermediate</u> state of drowsiness to derive some benefits of sleep without total perceptual disengagement.
questions.explanation: 잠을 자는 동안 감각적 이탈(perceptual disengagement)이 일어나 외부 자극에 반응하지 않게 되는데, 글의 흐름상 이러한 감각적 이탈 없이는(without it) 잠을 자는 것이 불가능하므로, 원문이나 문맥상 ④번의 impossible은 possible로 바뀌어야 자연스럽습니다. (또는 문맥상 'without it'이 되어야 하므로 'with it'이 포함된 문장에서 impossible은 부적절합니다.)

questions.question: 13. [4.1점] 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것을 고르시오.
questions.passage: A number of research studies have shown how experts in a field often experience difficulties when introducing newcomers to that field. For example, in a genuine training situation, Dr Pamela Hinds found that people ① <u>skilled</u> in using mobile phones were remarkably less accurate than novice phone users in judging how long it takes people to learn to use the phones. Experts can become ② <u>ignorant</u> to how hard a task is for the beginner, an effect referred to as the ‘curse of knowledge’. Dr Hinds was able to show that as people ③ <u>mastered</u> the skill, they then began to underestimate the level of difficulty of that skill. Her participants even ④ <u>minimized</u> how long it had taken themselves to acquire that skill in an earlier session. Knowing that experts ⑤ <u>perceive</u> how hard it was for them to learn, we can understand the need to look at the learning process through students' eyes, rather than making assumptions how students ‘should be’ learning.
questions.explanation: 이 글은 전문가들이 초보자의 입장을 이해하지 못하는 '지식의 저주'에 대해 설명하고 있습니다. 전문가들은 자신이 그 기술을 배우는 것이 얼마나 어려웠는지를 '망각'하거나 과소평가한다는 내용이 와야 하므로, '인지하다(perceive)'는 문맥상 적절하지 않으며 'forget' 또는 'ignore' 계열의 단어가 적절합니다.

questions.question: 14. [3.7점] 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것을 고르시오.
questions.passage: The rate of speed at which one is traveling will greatly determine the ability to process detail in the environment. In evolutionary terms, human senses are adapted to the speed at which humans move through space under their own power while walking. Our ability to distinguish detail in the environment is therefore ideally suited to movement at speeds of perhaps five miles per hour and under. The fastest users of the street, motorists, therefore have a much more limited ability to process details along the street - a motorist simply has little time or ability to appreciate design details. On the other hand, pedestrian travel, being much slower, allows for the _________ of environmental detail. Joggers and bicyclists fall somewhere in between these polar opposites; while they travel faster than pedestrians, their rate of speed is ordinarily much slower than that of the typical motorist.
options: ① perception
② devotion
③ preference
④ approval
⑤ confusion
questions.explanation: 속도가 느릴수록 환경의 세부 사항을 더 잘 파악할 수 있다는 내용이므로, 보행자의 이동은 환경적 세부 사항의 '지각(perception)'을 가능하게 한다는 ①번이 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 지각
② 헌신
③ 선호
④ 승인
⑤ 혼란

questions.question: 15. [3.5점] 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것을 고르시오.
questions.passage: Every species has certain climatic requirements - what degree of heat or cold it can endure, for example. When the climate changes, the places that satisfy those requirements change, too. Species are forced to follow. All creatures are capable of some degree of movement. Even creatures that appear immobile, like trees and barnacles, are capable of _________ at some stage of their life - as a seed, in the case of the tree, or as a larva, in the case of the barnacle. A creature must get from the place it is born - often occupied by its parent - to a place where it can survive, grow, and reproduce. From fossils, scientists know that even creatures like trees moved with surprising speed during past periods of climate change.
options: ① blending
② scattering
③ extinction
④ evaporation
⑤ collaboration
questions.explanation: 나무나 따개비처럼 움직이지 못하는 생물조차도 생애의 어느 단계(씨앗이나 유충 단계)에서는 이동이 가능하다는 내용입니다. 빈칸에는 이동이나 퍼짐을 의미하는 단어가 들어가야 하므로 '흩어짐, 분산'을 뜻하는 ②번 scattering이 가장 적절합니다. (원문은 dispersal/moving 등의 의미)
options_translation: ① 섞기
② 흩뿌리기(분산)
③ 멸종
④ 증발
⑤ 협력

questions.question: 16. 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것을 고르시오. [3.7점]
questions.passage: The mind has parts that are known as the conscious mind and the subconscious mind. The subconscious mind is very fast to act and doesn't deal with emotions. It deals with memories of your responses to life, your memories and recognition. However, the conscious mind is the one that you have more control over. You think. You can choose whether to carry on a thought or to add emotion to it and this is the part of your mind that lets you down eventually because — fueled by emotions — you ____________________________. When your judgment is clouded by emotions, this puts in biases and all kinds of other negativities that hold you back. Scared of spiders? Scared of the dark? There are reasons for all of these fears, but they originate in the conscious mind. They only become real fears when the subconscious mind records your reactions.
options: ① come to rational decisions
② frequently misjudge situations
③ often end up making sound actions
④ habitually delay what needs to be done
⑤ fail to distinguish between likes and dislikes
questions.explanation: 지문은 의식적인 마음이 감정에 휘둘릴 때 판단력이 흐려지고 부정적인 결과를 초래한다고 설명하고 있습니다. 빈칸 앞의 'fueled by emotions'와 빈칸 뒤의 'judgment is clouded by emotions'를 통해 감정 때문에 상황을 잘못 판단하게 된다는 흐름이 적절하므로 ②번이 정답입니다.
options_translation: ① 합리적인 결정에 도달한다
② 빈번하게 상황을 오판한다
③ 종종 결국 건전한 행동을 하게 된다
④ 습관적으로 해야 할 일을 미룬다
⑤ 좋아하는 것과 싫어하는 것을 구별하지 못한다

questions.question: 17. 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것을 고르시오. [3.8점]
questions.passage: A group of psychologists studied individuals with severe mental illness who experienced weekly group music therapy, including singing familiar songs and composing original songs. The results showed that the group music therapy improved the quality of participants' life, with those participating in a greater number of sessions experiencing the greatest benefits. Focusing on singing, another group of psychologists reviewed articles on the efficacy of group singing as a mental health treatment for individuals living with a mental health condition in a community setting. The findings showed that, when people with mental health conditions participated in a choir, their mental health and wellbeing significantly improved. In short, engaging in group singing __________________________________________________.
options: ① sparked creativity and inspired a love for music
② brought people together across different backgrounds and cultures
③ provided an opportunity to develop musical skills while having fun
④ created happiness, enhanced emotional well-being, and promoted belonging
⑤ developed a shared experience that discouraged communication skills and cooperation
questions.explanation: 지문은 집단 음악 치료와 합창 참여가 정신 질환을 앓는 사람들의 삶의 질과 정신 건강, 웰빙을 향상시킨다는 내용을 담고 있습니다. 따라서 결론(In short)으로 가장 적절한 것은 행복을 창출하고 정서적 안녕을 강화하며 소속감을 증진시킨다는 ④번입니다.
options_translation: ① 창의력을 불러일으키고 음악에 대한 사랑을 고취시켰다
② 다른 배경과 문화를 가진 사람들을 하나로 모았다
③ 즐기면서 음악적 기술을 개발할 기회를 제공했다
④ 행복을 창조하고, 정서적 안녕을 강화하며, 소속감을 증진시켰다
⑤ 의사소통 기술과 협력을 저해하는 공유된 경험을 발달시켰다

questions.question: 18. 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것을 고르시오. [3.8점]
questions.passage: In many sports, people realized the difficulties and even impossibilites of young children participating fully in many adult sport environments. They found the road to success for young children is unlikely if they play on adult fields, courts or arenas with equipment that is too large, too heavy or too fast for them to handle while trying to compete in adult-style competition. Common sense has prevailed: ____________________________. As examples, baseball has T ball, football has flag football and junior soccer uses a smaller and lighter ball and (sometimes) a smaller field. All have junior competitive structures where children play for shorter time periods and often in smaller teams. In a similar way, tennis has adapted the court areas, balls and rackets to make them more appropriate for children under 10. The adaptations are progressive and relate to the age of the child.
options: ① different physical activities have maintained adult-level standards for children
② various sports have modified their rules and equipment for children
③ the association has introduced a wider variety of sports for children
④ sports organizations have enforced strict adult rules for young players
⑤ guidelines for average athletes have been established
questions.explanation: 아이들이 성인용 경기장이나 장비를 사용하는 것이 부적절하다는 점을 인식하고, 야구의 T볼, 축구의 작은 공과 경기장, 테니스의 적응된 코트와 라켓 등을 예로 들며 아이들에게 맞게 스포츠가 변형되었다는 내용입니다. 따라서 '상식이 승리했다: 다양한 스포츠가 아이들을 위해 규칙과 장비를 수정했다'는 ②번이 정답입니다.
options_translation: ① 다른 신체 활동들이 아이들을 위해 성인 수준의 표준을 유지해왔다
② 다양한 스포츠들이 아이들을 위해 규칙과 장비를 수정했다
③ 협회가 아이들을 위해 더 다양한 종류의 스포츠를 도입했다
④ 스포츠 단체들이 어린 선수들에게 엄격한 성인 규칙을 강요했다
⑤ 평균적인 운동선수들을 위한 지침이 확립되었다

questions.question: 19. 다음 글에서 전체 흐름과 관계 없는 문장은? [3.3점]
questions.passage: No two animals are alike. Animals from the same litter will display some of the same features, but will not be exactly the same as each other; therefore, they may not respond in entirely the same way during a healing session. ① Environmental factors can also determine how the animal will respond during the treatment. ② For instance, a cat in a rescue center will respond very differently than a cat within a domestic home environment. ③ As the saying goes, "It is very difficult to find a black cat in a dark room, especially when there is no cat." ④ In addition, animals that experience healing for physical illness will react differently than those accepting healing for emotional confusion. ⑤ With this in mind, every healing session needs to be explored differently, and each healing treatment should be adjusted to suit the specific needs of the animal and you will learn as you go; healing is a constant learning process.
questions.explanation: 이 글은 동물마다 특성이 다르고 환경이나 질병의 종류에 따라 치유 세션에 대한 반응이 다르므로 개별적인 접근이 필요하다는 내용입니다. ③번 문장은 '검은 방에서 검은 고양이를 찾는 것은 어렵다'는 격언을 인용하고 있는데, 이는 글의 주제인 '동물의 개별성에 따른 치유 접근법'과 관계가 없는 내용입니다.

questions.question: 20. 글의 흐름으로 보아, 주어진 문장이 들어가기에 가장 적절한 곳은? [3.1점]
questions.passage: Now that day seems like a dream to me. I remember the two old men sitting at the table and the soft sounds of the Maori words as they talked. ( ① ) All through the quiet afternoon and into the evening, they recalled missing names. ( ② ) While they were doing the work, I had a strange feeling that there were other people in the room. ( ③ ) I felt as if people from the past were looking over the shoulders of the two old men to see if the work was correct. ( ④ ) After a moment of silence, the old man whispered to Nani, "Goodbye, friend." ( ⑤ ) Crying, they pressed their noses together to say goodbye.
questions.insertion_sentence: Finally, they stopped. It was done. The two old men sat quietly, feeling proud about what they had finally finished.
questions.explanation: 주어진 문장은 작업이 마침내 끝났음을 나타내며, 노인들이 조용히 앉아 자부심을 느꼈다는 내용을 담고 있습니다. ( ④ ) 앞부분까지는 과거의 인물들이 지켜보는 것 같은 느낌 속에서 이름을 소환하는 작업이 계속되는 과정을 묘사하고 있으며, ( ④ ) 뒷부분에서 '잠시 정적이 흐른 뒤(After a moment of silence)' 작별 인사를 나누는 장면으로 이어지므로, 작업 종료를 알리는 주어진 문장은 ④번에 위치하는 것이 가장 적절합니다.

questions.question: 21. [3.3점] 주어진 글 다음에 이어질 글의 순서로 가장 적절한 것을 고르시오.
questions.passage: Now let's turn our attention to ourselves, Homo sapiens. How have we managed to survive for so long?
ordered_passages: (A) These social differences may have given Homo sapiens having intelligence and bodies inferior to Neanderthals a survival advantage, allowing them to adapt to an ever-changing environment.

(B) Despite these attributes, however, it was Homo sapiens who ultimately survived and thrived. One possible explanation is that our ancestors lived in larger communities that promoted cooperation and the free exchange of knowledge, while Neanderthals tended to live in smaller groups.

(C) Neanderthals were known to be intelligent and physically superior to Homo sapiens, and they existed together with Homo sapiens until about 40,000 years ago. Neanderthals were able to make tools and fire and had strong bodies with well-developed muscles and broad shoulders.
questions.explanation: 주어진 글에서 호모 사피엔스의 생존 방식에 대한 질문을 던집니다. (C)에서 비교 대상인 네안데르탈인의 지적/신체적 우수성을 먼저 설명하고, (B)에서 '이러한 특성들에도 불구하고(Despite these attributes)' 호모 사피엔스가 생존했음을 밝히며 그 원인으로 사회적 협력을 제시합니다. (A)에서 (B)에 언급된 '사회적 차이(These social differences)'를 요약하며 마무리하는 (C)-(B)-(A) 순서가 가장 자연스럽습니다.

questions.question: 22. [3.3점] 주어진 글 다음에 이어질 글의 순서로 가장 적절한 것을 고르시오.
questions.passage: The tongue was mapped into separate areas where certain tastes were registered: sweetness at the tip, sourness on the sides, and bitterness at the back of the mouth.
ordered_passages: (A) Moreover, the mechanism at work is not place, but time. It's not that you taste sweetness at the tip of your tongue, but rather that you register that perception first.

(B) Research in the 1980s and 1990s, however, demonstrated that the "tongue map" explanation of how we taste was, in fact, totally wrong. As it turns out, the map was a misinterpretation and mistranslation of research conducted in Germany at the turn of the twentieth century.

(C) Today, leading taste researchers believe that taste buds are not grouped according to specialty. Sweetness, saltiness, bitterness, and sourness can be tasted everywhere in the mouth, although they may be perceived at a little different intensities at different sites.
questions.explanation: 주어진 글은 전통적인 '혀 지도'에 대해 설명합니다. (C)에서 오늘날의 연구자들이 맛봉오리가 전문 분야별로 나뉘지 않는다고 믿는다는 사실을 언급하며 혀 지도에 반하는 현대의 관점을 제시합니다. (B)에서 '그러나(however)' 1980~90년대 연구가 혀 지도가 오역에서 비롯된 잘못된 것임을 입증했음을 설명하고, (A)에서 '게다가(Moreover)' 작동 방식이 장소가 아니라 시간(반응 속도)의 문제임을 추가 설명하는 (C)-(B)-(A) 혹은 내용의 흐름상 (B)-(C)-(A)가 논리적이나, 제시된 선지 중 흐름이 가장 명확한 것은 ⑤번입니다. (다만 원문 맥락상 혀 지도의 잘못됨을 먼저 언급하는 (B)가 앞서는 것이 일반적이므로 정답은 ②번 (B)-(A)-(C) 또는 ⑤번 (C)-(B)-(A) 중에서 맥락을 재검토해야 하나, 일반적으로 잘못된 통념(주어진 글) -> 반박(B) -> 현재의 이론(C) -> 보충 설명(A) 순인 ③번 (B)-(C)-(A)가 가장 논리적입니다. 제공된 텍스트 흐름에 따라 ③번을 권장합니다.)

questions.question: 23. 다음 글의 내용을 한 문장으로 요약하고자 한다. 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것을 고르시오. [3.9점]
questions.passage: It would be hard to overstate how important meaningful work is to human beings - work that provides a sense of fulfillment and empowerment. Those who have found deeper meaning in their careers find their days much more energizing and satisfying, and count their employment as one of their greatest sources of joy and pride. Sonya Lyubomirsky, professor of psychology at the University of California, has conducted numerous workplace studies showing that when people are more fulfilled on the job, they not only produce higher quality work and a greater output, but also generally earn higher incomes Those most satisfied with their work are also much more likely to be happier with their lives overall. For her book Happiness at Work, researcher Jessica Pryce-Jones conducted a study of 3,000 workers in seventy-nine countries, knowing that those who took greater satisfaction from their work were 150 percent more likely to have a happier life overall.
questions.summary_sentence: (A)________ meaningful and fulfilling work not only increases job satisfaction and productivity but also significantly (B)_________ overall happiness in life.
options: ① Finding ...... undermines
② Pursuing ...... enhances
③ Performing ...... obstructs
④ Neglecting ...... worsens
⑤ Disregarding ...... promotes
questions.explanation: 의미 있고 성취감을 주는 일을 '추구하는 것(Pursuing)'이 직무 만족도와 생산성을 높일 뿐만 아니라 삶의 전반적인 행복을 상당히 '향상시킨다(enhances)'는 내용이 적절하다.
options_translation: ① 찾는 것 ...... 해친다
② 추구하는 것 ...... 향상시킨다
③ 수행하는 것 ...... 방해한다
④ 방치하는 것 ...... 악화시킨다
⑤ 무시하는 것 ...... 증진시킨다

questions.question: 24. 다음 글의 내용을 한 문장으로 요약하고자 한다. 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것을 고르시오. [4.0점]
questions.passage: Working around the whole painting, rather than concentrating on one area at a time, will mean you can stop at any point and the painting can be considered "finished." Artists often find it difficult to know when to stop painting, and it can be tempting to keep on adding more to your work. It is important to take a few steps back from the painting from time to time to assess your progress. Putting too much into a painting can spoil its impact and leave it looking overworked. If you find yourself struggling to decide whether you have finished, take a break and come back to it later with fresh eyes. Then you can decide whether any areas of your painting would benefit from further refinement.
questions.summary_sentence: By working on the entire painting rather than focusing on one area, stepping back to (A)_________ progress, and taking a break when uncertain, you can avoid overworking the piece and determine when it is truly (B)________ .
options: ① evaluate ...... completed
② accelerate ...... satisfying
③ interrupt ...... preservable
④ enhance ...... finished
⑤ assess ...... valuable
questions.explanation: 그림 전체를 작업하고, 진행 상황을 '평가하기(evaluate/assess)' 위해 뒤로 물러나며, 불확실할 때 휴식을 취함으로써 작품을 과하게 작업하는 것을 피하고 언제 그것이 진정으로 '완성되었는지(completed/finished)' 결정할 수 있다는 내용이다. (A)에는 evaluate와 assess가 모두 가능하지만, (B)에는 문맥상 completed가 가장 적절하다.
options_translation: ① 평가하다 ...... 완성된
② 가속하다 ...... 만족스러운
③ 방해하다 ...... 보존 가능한
④ 향상시키다 ...... 끝난
⑤ 평가하다 ...... 가치 있는

questions.question: 다음 글의 주제로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: 1. It is natural to feel angry from time to time; it doesn' t mean there is something wrong with you. Anger can sometimes be a useful tool. For example, an angry but open conversation can resolve a conflict between friends. The important thing is to manage your anger so that it does not turn into aggressive or violent behavior. This does not mean that you should stop yourself from feeling angry. Rather, you should express it in a productive way. Ask yourself some questions about your angry feelings. This can help you to better understand your anger.
options: ① Anger is an unnecessary emotion in life.
② Aggressive behavior is a natural outcome of anger.
③ Anger can be useful if managed and expressed properly.
④ Suppressing anger completely is the best way to avoid conflicts.
⑤ Anger should be avoided at all costs to maintain good relationships.
questions.explanation: 이 글은 분노가 때때로 유용한 도구가 될 수 있으며, 중요한 것은 분노를 관리하여 생산적인 방식으로 표현하는 것이라고 설명하고 있습니다. 따라서 '적절하게 관리되고 표현된다면 분노는 유용할 수 있다'는 내용의 ③번이 주제로 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 분노는 삶에서 불필요한 감정이다.
② 공격적인 행동은 분노의 자연스러운 결과이다.
③ 분노는 적절히 관리되고 표현된다면 유용할 수 있다.
④ 분노를 완전히 억제하는 것이 갈등을 피하는 최선의 방법이다.
⑤ 좋은 관계를 유지하기 위해 분노는 반드시 피해야 한다.

questions.question: 2. 다음 글의 제목으로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: We often try to make cuts in our challenges and take the easy route. When taking the quick exit, we fail to acquire the strength to compete. We often take the easy route to improve our skills. Many of us never really work to achieve mastery in the key areas of life. These skills are key tools that can be useful to our career, health, and prosperity. Highly successful athletes don' t win because of better equipment; they win by facing hardship to gain strength and skill. They win through preparation. It' s the mental preparation, winning mindset, strategy, and skill that set them apart. Strength comes from struggle, not from taking the path of least resistance. Hardship is not just a lesson for the next time in front of us. Hardship will be the greatest teacher we will ever have in life.
options: ① The Shortcut to Success
② Success Without Struggle
③ Winning is All About Good Luck
④ Growth Through Truth: The Hidden Secret
⑤ The Power of Hardship: Strength Through Struggle
questions.explanation: 이 글은 성취와 힘은 쉬운 길을 택하는 것이 아니라 고난(hardship)을 마주하고 분투(struggle)하는 과정에서 얻어진다는 점을 강조하고 있습니다. 따라서 ⑤번 '고난의 힘: 분투를 통한 힘'이 제목으로 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 성공으로 가는 지름길
② 투쟁 없는 성공
③ 승리는 전적으로 행운에 관한 것이다.
④ 진실을 통한 성장: 숨겨진 비밀
⑤ 고난의 힘: 분투를 통한 힘

questions.question: 3. 다음 글의 제목으로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Unfortunately, many people don' t take personal responsibility for their own growth. Instead, they simply run the race laid out for them. They do well enough in school to keep advancing. Maybe they manage to get a good job at a well-run company. But so many think and act as if their learning journey ends with college. They have checked all the boxes in the life that was laid out for them and now lack a road map describing the right ways to move forward and continue to grow. In truth, that' s when the journey really begins. When school is finished, your growth becomes voluntary. Like healthy eating habits or a regular exercise program, you need to commit to it and devote thought, time, and energy to it. Otherwise, it simply won' t happen — and your life and career are likely to stop progressing as a result.
options: ① Stop Learning After Graduation
② Follow the Path. Don' t Question It.
③ Why Hard Work in School Guarantees Success
④ Growth Beyond Graduation: The Real Journey Begins
⑤ Healthy Eating Habits and Regular Exercise: the Keys to a Successful Career
questions.explanation: 이 글은 많은 사람들이 대학 졸업과 함께 배움이 끝난다고 생각하지만, 사실 진정한 성장은 학교 교육이 끝난 뒤 자발적인 노력을 통해 이루어지며 이때부터 진짜 여정이 시작된다고 말하고 있습니다. 따라서 ④번 '졸업을 넘어선 성장: 진짜 여정이 시작된다'가 제목으로 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 졸업 후에는 배움을 멈춰라
② 길을 따르라. 의문을 갖지 마라.
③ 학교에서의 노력이 성공을 보장하는 이유
④ 졸업을 넘어선 성장: 진짜 여정이 시작된다
⑤ 건강한 식습관과 규칙적인 운동: 성공적인 경력의 열쇠

questions.question: 4. 다음 글에 관한 내용으로 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: As the parent of a gifted child, you need to be aware of a certain common parent trap. Of course you are a proud parent, and you should be. While it is very easy to talk nonstop about your little genius and his or her remarkable behavior, this can be very stressful on your child. It is extremely important to limit your bragging behavior to your very close friends, or your parents. Gifted children feel pressured when their parents show them off too much. This behavior creates expectations that they may not be able to live up to, and also creates a false sense of self for your child. You want your child to be who they are, not who they seem to be as defined by their incredible achievements. If not, you could end up with a driven perfectionist child or perhaps a drop-out, or worse.
options: ① Parents should frequently brag about their gifted child to boost the child' s confidence.
② A child' s identity should be based only on their academic achievements.
③ The best way to motivate a gifted child is by setting extremely high expectations for them.
④ Constantly showing off a child's giftedness has no negative effects on their development.
⑤ It is crucial for parents to avoid bragging excessively about their gifted child to support the child' s natural and healthy growth.
questions.explanation: 글의 핵심 내용은 영재 자녀를 둔 부모들이 아이의 성취를 과하게 자랑하는 것이 아이에게 스트레스를 주고 부정적인 영향을 미칠 수 있으므로, 이를 절제하고 아이가 있는 그대로의 모습으로 성장할 수 있도록 도와야 한다는 것이다. 따라서 5번이 가장 적절하다.
options_translation: ① 부모는 자녀의 자신감을 북돋우기 위해 영재 자녀에 대해 자주 자랑해야 한다.
② 아이의 정체성은 오직 학업적 성취에만 기반해야 한다.
③ 영재 자녀에게 동기를 부여하는 가장 좋은 방법은 매우 높은 기대를 설정하는 것이다.
④ 자녀의 영재성을 끊임없이 뽐내는 것은 발달에 부정적인 영향을 미치지 않는다.
⑤ 부모가 영재 자녀에 대해 과도하게 자랑하는 것을 피하는 것이 자녀의 자연스럽고 건강한 성장을 지원하는 데 중요하다.

questions.question: 5. 다음 글에 관한 내용으로 적절하지 않은 것은?
questions.passage:
Our emotions are thought to exist because they have contributed to our survival as a species. Fear has helped us avoid dangers, expressing anger helps us scare off threats, and expressing positive emotions helps us bond with others. From an evolutionary perspective, an emotion is a kind of "program" that, when triggered, directs many of our activities (including attention, perception, memory, movement, expressions, etc.). For instance, fear makes us very attentive, narrows our perceptual focus to threatening stimuli, will cause us either to face a situation (fight) or avoid
it (flight), and may cause us to remember an experience more acutely (so that we avoid the threat in the future). Regardless of the specific ways in which they activate our systems, the specific emotions we possess are thought to exist because they have helped us (as a species) survive challenges within our environment long ago. If they had not helped us adapt and survive, they would not have evolved with us.
options: ① Fear helps us avoid dangerous situations by increasing our awareness of threats.
② Positive emotions, like happiness, help us build social bonds and foster cooperation.
③ Human adaptation and survival have been little impacted by emotional responses to environmental threats.
④ Emotions influence many of our activities, including memory, attention, and movement.
⑤ Emotions triggering specific responses like fight or flight have assisted human survival and evolved with us.
questions.explanation: 글의 전체적인 요지는 인간의 감정이 생존과 적응에 큰 도움을 주었기 때문에 진화해 왔다는 것이다. 3번은 감정적 반응이 인간의 적응과 생존에 거의 영향을 미치지 않았다고 서술하고 있으므로 본문의 내용과 정반대된다.
options_translation: ① 공포는 위협에 대한 인식을 높임으로써 위험한 상황을 피하도록 도와준다.
② 행복과 같은 긍정적인 감정은 사회적 유대를 형성하고 협력을 촉진하도록 도와준다.
③ 인간의 적응과 생존은 환경적 위협에 대한 감정적 반응에 의해 거의 영향을 받지 않았다.
④ 감정은 기억, 주의력, 움직임을 포함한 우리의 많은 활동에 영향을 미친다.
⑤ 투쟁 혹은 도피와 같은 특정한 반응을 유발하는 감정은 인류의 생존을 도왔고 우리와 함께 진화해 왔다.

questions.question: 7. (A), (B), (C)의 각 네모 안에서 문맥에 맞는 낱말로 가장 적절한 것은? [2.9점]
questions.passage: Many people take the commonsense view that color is a(n) (A) [ subjective / objective ] property of things, or of the light that bounces off them. They say a tree' s leaves are green because they reflect green light — a greenness that is just as real as the leaves. Others argue that color doesn' t (B) [ prohibit / inhabit ] the physical world at all but exists only in the eye or mind of the viewer. They maintain that if a tree fell in a forest and no one was there to see it, its leaves would be colorless — and so would everything else. They say there is no such thing as color; there are only the people who see it. Both positions are, in a way, correct. Color is "the place," as Paul Cézanne put it, "where our brain and the universe meet." Color (C) [ emerges / fades ] when light from the world is registered by the eyes and interpreted by the brain.
options: ① objective ... inhabit ... emerges
② subjective ... prohibit ... fades
③ objective ... prohibit ... fades
④ subjective ... inhabit ... emerges
⑤ objective ... inhabit ... fades
questions.explanation: (A) 뒤의 문장에서 나뭇잎만큼이나 실재하는 초록색이라고 언급하므로 '객관적인(objective)'이 적절하다. (B) 색이 물리적 세계에 존재하지 않고 보는 이의 눈이나 마음에만 존재한다는 내용이므로 '거주하다/존재하다(inhabit)'가 적절하다. (C) 뇌에 의해 해석될 때 색이 나타난다는 맥락이므로 '나타나다(emerges)'가 적절하다.
options_translation: ① 객관적인 ... 존재하다 ... 나타나다
② 주관적인 ... 금지하다 ... 사라지다
③ 객관적인 ... 금지하다 ... 사라지다
④ 주관적인 ... 존재하다 ... 나타나다
⑤ 객관적인 ... 존재하다 ... 사라지다

questions.question: 9. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은? [3.3점]
questions.passage: Kids tire of their toys, college students get sick of cafeteria food, and sooner or later most of us lose interest in our favorite TV shows. The bottom line is that we humans are easily ① <u>bored</u>. But why should this be true? The answer lies buried deep in our nerve cells, which are designed to ② <u>decrease</u> their initial excited response to stimuli each time they occur. At the same time, these neurons ③ <u>strengthen</u> their responses to things that change — especially things that change quickly. We probably evolved this way because our ancestors got more survival value, for example, from attending to what was moving in a tree (such as a puma) than to the tree itself. Boredom in reaction to an unchanging environment turns down the level of neural excitation so that new stimuli (like our ancestor' s hypothetical puma threat) become more ④ <u>inconspicuous</u>. It' s the neural ⑤ <u>equivalent</u> of turning off a front door light to see the fireflies.
questions.explanation: 변하지 않는 환경에 대해 신경 자극 수준을 낮추는 이유는 새로운 자극이 더 '눈에 띄게(conspicuous)' 만들기 위함이다. 따라서 '눈에 띄지 않는'이라는 뜻의 inconspicuous는 적절하지 않다.

questions.question: 10. (A), (B), (C)의 각 네모 안에서 문맥에 맞는 낱말로 가장 적절한 것은? [3.3점]
questions.passage: The hunter-gatherer lifestyle, which can be described as "natural" to human beings, appears to have had much to (A) [ praise / criticize ] it. Examination of human remains from early hunter-gatherer societies has suggested that our ancestors enjoyed abundant food, obtainable without extreme effort, and suffered very few diseases. If this is true, it is not clear why so many humans settled in permanent villages and developed agriculture, growing crops and (B) [ taming / releasing ] animals: cultivating fields was hard work, and it was in farming villages that epidemic diseases first took root. Whatever its immediate effect on the lives of humans, the development of settlements and agriculture undoubtedly led to a high increase in population density. This period, known as the New Stone Age, was a major turning point in human development, (C) [ paving / hindering ] the way to the growth of the first towns and cities, and eventually leading to settled "civilizations."
options: ① praise ... taming ... paving
② praise ... taming ... hindering
③ praise ... releasing ... paving
④ criticize ... releasing ... hindering
⑤ criticize ... releasing ... paving
questions.explanation: (A) 수렵 채집 생활이 풍부한 음식과 질병이 거의 없었다는 긍정적인 맥락이 뒤따르므로 '칭찬할 만한(praise)'이 적절합니다. (B) 농경 사회의 발달과 관련하여 작물을 재배하고 동물을 '길들이는(taming)' 것이 문맥상 맞습니다. (C) 신석기 시대가 첫 마을과 도시의 성장에 길을 '열어주었다(paving)'는 표현이 자연스럽습니다.
options_translation: ① 칭찬하다 ... 길들이기 ... (길을) 닦다
② 칭찬하다 ... 길들이기 ... 방해하다
③ 칭찬하다 ... 풀어주기 ... (길을) 닦다
④ 비판하다 ... 풀어주기 ... 방해하다
⑤ 비판하다 ... 풀어주기 ... (길을) 닦다

questions.question: 11. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 어법상 틀린 것은? [3.4점]
questions.passage: Promotion deals with consumer psychology. We can' t force people ① <u>to think</u> one way or another, and the clever marketer knows that promotion is used to provide information in the most clear, honest, and simple fashion possible. By doing so, the possibility of increasing sales goes up. Gone ② <u>is</u> the days when promotions were done in order to fool the consumer into purchasing something. The long-term effect of getting a consumer to buy something they did not really want or need wasn' t good. In fact, consumers ③ <u>fooled</u> once can do damage to sales as they relate their experience to others. Instead, marketers now know that their goal is to identify the consumers ④ <u>who</u> are most likely to appreciate a good or service, and to promote that good or service in a way ⑤ <u>which</u> makes the value clear to the consumer. Therefore, marketers must know where the interested consumers are, and how to reach them.
questions.explanation: ②번 문장은 도치 구문입니다. 주어는 'the days'로 복수형이므로 동사는 'is'가 아니라 'are'가 되어야 합니다.

questions.question: 13. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 어법상 틀린 부분을 포함한 문장은? [3.5점]
questions.passage: AI image generators create images based on our text requests. ① <u>They do this by copying other images that were created by humans.</u> ② <u>The generators have the ability to analyze millions of images and their corresponding descriptions.</u> ③ <u>This allows them create works of art in a short time based on the provided instructions.</u> Moreover, AI programs can mix the styles of existing images upon request. For instance, you can blend a photograph of a cat with Johannes Vermeer' s Girl with a Pearl Earring. These two images have a few differences. However, ④ <u>the overall design, the eyes, and the scarf around the head are based on Vermeer' s painting.</u> ⑤ <u>A simple request was enough to create this complex and detailed image.</u>
questions.explanation: ③번 문장에서 'allow' 동사는 'allow + 목적어 + to부정사'의 형태를 취합니다. 따라서 'allow them create'는 'allow them to create'로 고쳐야 합니다.

questions.question: 16. 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은? [3.7점]
questions.passage: You need to learn how to deal with anger in a socially appropriate way. Remember: anger is a feeling, but behavior is a choice. The first step is recognizing the _________ signs of anger. It is possible to recognize those signs in advance. They include an increased heart rate, a flushed face, and the clenching of your fists. When these things happen, take action to reduce your anger. For example, you could try taking a break to organize your thoughts or ending a conversation before it gets too intense.
options: ① physical
② psychological
③ philosophical
④ financial
⑤ theoretical
questions.explanation: 빈칸 뒤에서 심박수 증가, 얼굴 붉어짐, 주먹 쥐기 등 신체적 증상들을 언급하고 있으므로 빈칸에는 '신체적인(physical)'이 가장 적절하다.
options_translation: ① 신체적인
② 심리적인
③ 철학적인
④ 재정적인
⑤ 이론적인

questions.question: 17. 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: By improving accessibility of the workplace for workers that are typically at a disadvantage in the labour market, AI can improve _________ in the workplace. AI-powered assistive devices to aid workers with visual, speech or hearing difficulties are becoming more widespread, improving the access to, and the quality of work for people with disabilities. For example, speech recognition solutions for people with dysarthric voices, or live captioning systems for deaf and hard of hearing people can facilitate communication with colleagues and access to jobs where inter-personal communication is necessary. AI can also enhance the capabilities of low-skilled workers, with potentially positive effects on their wages and career prospects. For example, AI' s capacity to translate written and spoken word in real-time can improve the performance of non-native speakers in the workplace. Moreover, recent developments in AI-powered text generators can instantly improve the performance of lower-skilled individuals in domains such as writing, coding or customer service.
options: ① inclusion
② flexibility
③ consistency
④ practicality
⑤ exclusiveness
questions.explanation: 이 글은 AI가 노동 시장에서 불리한 위치에 있는 사람들의 직장 접근성을 높임으로써 직장 내 '포용성(inclusion)'을 향상시킬 수 있다는 내용을 다루고 있습니다. 장애인, 저숙련 노동자, 비원어민 등의 업무 수행을 돕는 사례들을 제시하고 있으므로 빈칸에는 '포용성'이 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 포용성
② 유연성
③ 일관성
④ 실용성
⑤ 배타성

questions.question: 18. 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: It would be hard to overstate how important meaningful work is to human beings - work that provides a sense of fulfillment and empowerment. Those who have found deeper meaning in their careers find that _________. Sonya Lyubomirsky, professor of psychology at the University of California, has conducted numerous workplace studies showing that when people are more fulfilled on the job, they not only produce higher quality work and a greater output, but also generally earn higher incomes. Those most satisfied with their work are also much more likely to be happier with their lives overall. For her book Happiness at Work, researcher Jessica Pryce-Jones conducted a study of 3,000 workers in seventy-nine countries, finding that those who took greater satisfaction from their work were 150 percent more likely to have a happier life overall.
options: ① Flexibility should be valued over stability.
② Work is merely a means of earning a living.
③ Happiness at work has little to do with job satisfaction.
④ Financial rewards are the main motivation for most workers.
⑤ A meaningful career brings energy, satisfaction, and pride.
questions.explanation: 이 글은 의미 있는 일이 인간에게 얼마나 중요한지 강조하고 있습니다. 직업에서 깊은 의미를 찾은 사람들은 더 높은 업무 품질과 생산성을 보일 뿐만 아니라 전반적인 삶의 만족도도 높다는 연구 결과를 제시하고 있습니다. 따라서 빈칸에는 의미 있는 경력이 에너지, 만족감, 자부심을 가져다준다는 내용이 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 유연성은 안정성보다 중시되어야 한다.
② 일은 단지 생계를 꾸리기 위한 수단일 뿐이다.
③ 직장에서의 행복은 직무 만족도와 거의 관계가 없다.
④ 금전적 보상은 대부분의 근로자들에게 주된 동기이다.
⑤ 의미 있는 경력은 에너지, 만족감, 그리고 자부심을 가져다준다.

questions.question: 19. 다음 글에서 전체 흐름과 관계 없는 문장은?
questions.passage: Crop rotation is the process in which farmers change the crops they grow in their fields in a special order. For example, if a farmer has three fields, he or she may grow carrots in the first field, green beans in the second, and tomatoes in the third. ① The next year, green beans will be in the first field, tomatoes in the second field, and carrots will be in the third. ② In year three, the crops will rotate again. ③ By the fourth year, the crops will go back to their original order. ④ Surprisingly, some scientists argue that planting the same crop in the same field every year might actually boost soil fertility in ways we don' t yet understand. ⑤ Since each crop enriches the soil for the next, this type of farming is sustainable and keeps the soil healthy.
questions.explanation: 이 글은 윤작(crop rotation)의 개념과 그 이점(토양 건강 유지 및 지속 가능성)에 대해 설명하고 있습니다. 하지만 ④번 문장은 매년 같은 밭에 같은 작물을 심는 것(연작)이 토양 비옥도를 높일 수 있다는 내용으로, 윤작의 원리와 정반대되는 주장을 하고 있어 전체 흐름에서 벗어납니다.

questions.question: 20. 주어진 글 다음에 이어질 글의 순서로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Consider the seemingly simple question How many senses are there? Around 2,370 years ago, Aristotle wrote that there are five, in both humans and animals — sight, hearing, smell, taste, and touch.
ordered_passages: (A) Other animals have senses that are even harder to categorize. Many vertebrates have a different sense system for detecting odors. Some snakes can detect the body heat of their prey.

(B) However, according to the philosopher Fiona Macpherson, there are reasons to doubt it. For a start, Aristotle missed a few in humans: the perception of your own body which is different from touch and the sense of balance which has links to both touch and vision.

(C) These examples tell us that "senses cannot be clearly divided into a limited number of specific kinds," Macpherson wrote in The Senses. Instead of trying to push animal senses into Aristotelian buckets, we should study them for what they are.
questions.explanation: 주어진 글에서 아리스토텔레스의 5감에 대한 주장이 제시된다. (B)에서 'However'와 'it'을 통해 아리스토텔레스의 의견에 대한 반박과 그가 놓친 인간의 감각들을 설명하며 시작하는 것이 자연스럽다. 이어지는 (A)에서는 'Other animals'를 언급하며 인간 외 동물의 감각 예시를 들고, 마지막으로 (C)에서 'These examples'를 통해 앞선 사례들을 요약하며 결론을 맺는 순서가 가장 적절하다.

questions.question: 21. 주어진 글 사이에 이어질 글의 순서로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Many AI programs are open to the public, which means they are free and convenient to use.
ordered_passages: (A) They worry that AI will take the place of humans in more and more areas. There are also concerns that AI may replicate the styles of human artists without their consent.
(B) On the other hand, others think that AI cannot surpass human imagination and that it is not still independent on human assistance.
(C) However, these programs have stirred up controversy over their effect upon humans. Since AI has the potential to learn skills and perform them better than humans, some people view it as a threat.
(D) This is because the data that AI uses can have limitations. A dependence on flawed data with little diversity eventually limits the output of AI programs.

What kind of future do you think lies ahead of us? AI provides many benefits and new opportunities. What we need to do is figure out how to use AI tools ethically and think about how humans and AI can collaborate.
questions.explanation: 주어진 첫 문장에서 AI의 장점(무료, 편리함)을 언급한 뒤, (C)에서 'However'를 사용해 AI의 위협성과 논란을 제기한다. (A)는 (C)에서 언급된 위협에 대한 구체적인 걱정들(일자리 대체, 저작권)을 나열한다. (B)에서는 'On the other hand'를 통해 AI의 한계를 지적하며 인간을 능가할 수 없다는 반대 의견을 제시하고, (D)에서 그 이유(데이터의 한계)를 설명한다. 마지막으로 마무리 문단에서 AI와 인간의 협력과 윤리적 사용을 강조하며 끝맺는다.

questions.question: 22. 주어진 글 사이에 이어질 글의 순서로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: We all negotiate every day, whether we realize it or not. Yet few people ever learn how to negotiate.
ordered_passages: (A) This old-school, adversarial approach may be useful in a one-off negotiation where you will probably not deal with that person again.
(B) Those who do usually learn the traditional, win-lose negotiating style rather than an approach that is likely to result in a win-win agreement.

(C) However, such transactions are becoming increasingly infrequent, because most of us deal with the same people repeatedly — our spouses and children, our friends and colleagues, our customers and clients.

In view of this, it is crucial to achieve success while maintaining strong relationships with negotiating partners. In today' s interconnected business world, a win-win outcome is the preferred standard.
questions.explanation: 주어진 첫 단락에서 협상을 배우는 사람이 거의 없음을 언급한다. (B)에서 'Those who do(배우는 사람들)'를 통해 협상을 배우는 이들이 전통적인 '승-패' 방식을 배운다고 설명한다. (A)에서 'This old-school, adversarial approach'로 (B)의 '승-패' 방식을 지칭하며 일회성 협상에서의 유용성을 언급한다. (C)에서 'However'와 'such transactions'를 통해 일회성 거래가 점점 드물어짐을 지적하며, 마지막 마무리 문단에서 관계 유지와 '승-승' 결과의 중요성을 강조하는 흐름이 적절하다.

questions.question: 23. 글의 흐름으로 보아, 주어진 문장이 들어가기에 가장 적절한 곳은? [4.3점]
questions.passage:
Some researchers think numbers represent the most neutral language of description. However, when our language of description is changed to numbers, we do not move toward greater accuracy. ( ① ) While useful for specific purposes (e.g. census taking, income distribution), they exclude information of enormous value. ( ② ) For instance, the future lives of young students are tied to their scores on national tests. ( ③ ) In effect, whether they can continue with their education, where, and at what cost depends importantly on a handful of numbers. ( ④ ) Finally, putting aside the many ways in which statistical results can be manipulated, there are ways in which turning people' s lives into numbers is morally insulating. ( ⑤ ) Statistics on crime, homelessness, or the spread of a disease say nothing of people' s suffering. We read the statistics as reports on events at a distance, thus allowing us to escape without being disturbed. Statistics are human beings with the tears wiped off. Quantify with caution.
*statistical: 통계의 *manipulate: 조작하다 insulating:차단하는
questions.insertion_sentence: However, these numbers do not account for the quality of schools they have attended, whether they have been tutored, have supportive parents, have test anxiety, and so on.
questions.explanation: 제시된 문제의 'these numbers'는 ③ 뒤에 나오는 '국가 고사 점수(a handful of numbers)'를 가리킬다. ③ 문장은 학생들의 미래가 시험 점수에 의존한다는 내용이고, 제시된 문제은 이러한 학자들이 교육 환경이나 개인적 사정 등 중요한 질적 요소들을 반영하지 못한다는 내용이므로, ④에 들어가는 것이 가장 적절하다.

questions.question: 25. 밑줄 친 <u>when each tree thinks only of its own leaves, the forest loses its shape</u>이 다음 글에서 의미하는 바로 가장 적절한 것은? [4.4점]
questions.passage: From an organizational viewpoint, one of the most fascinating examples of how any organization may contain many different types of culture is to recognize the functional operations of different departments within the organization. The varying departments and divisions within an organization will inevitably view any given situation from their own biased and prejudiced perspective. A department and its members will acquire "tunnel vision" which disallows them to see things as others see them. The very structure of organizations can create conflict. The choice of whether the structure is "mechanistic" or "organic" can have a profound influence on conflict management. A mechanistic structure has a vertical hierarchy with many rules, many procedures, and many levels of management involved in decision making. Organic structures are more horizontal in nature, where decision making is less centralized and spread across the plane of the organization. <u>When each tree thinks only of its own leaves, the forest loses its shape.</u> Likewise, organizations that neglect to integrate the unique insights of their various departments often find themselves limited in overcoming challenges.
options: ① Organizations succeed when departments focus on their own specialized tasks.
② A rigid hierarchical structure is more effective than a horizontal one in problem-solving.
③ Each department within an organization should operate independently to maximize efficiency.
④ Conflicts between departments are necessary for the long-term growth of an organization.
⑤ If departments prioritize only their own interests without cooperation, the organization as a whole suffers.
questions.answer: ⑤ If departments prioritize only their own interests without cooperation, the organization as a whole suffers.
questions.explanation: 문맥상 각 부서가 자신들의 편협한 관점(tunnel vision)에만 치중하고 조직 전체의 관점을 통합하지 못하면 조직 전체가 어려움에 처한다는 의미이다.
options_translation: ① 부서들이 자신들의 전문화된 과업에 중심을 두면 조직은 강해진다.
② 경직된 계층 구조가 문제 해결에서 수평적 구조밴다 효과적이다.
③ 효율성을 극대화하기 윔해 조직 내 각 부서는 독립적으로 운영되어야 한다.
④ 부서 간의 갈등은 조직의 장기적 성장을 윔해 필요하다.
⑤ 부서들이 협력 없이 자신들의 이익만을 우선시하면, 조직 전체가 곤경에 찘한다.

questions.question: 27. 다음 글의 hanging out with the winners가 올바르게 적용된 사례만을 <보기>에서 있는 그대로 고른 것은? [4.6점]
questions.passage: One valuable technique for getting out of helplessness, depression, and situations which are predominantly being run by the thought, “I can’t,” is to choose to be with other persons who have resolved the problem with which we struggle. This is one of the great powers of self­help groups. When we are in a negative state, we have given a lot of energy to negative thought forms, and the positive thought forms are weak. Those who are in a higher vibration are free of the energy from their negative thoughts and have energized positive thought forms. Merely to be in their presence is beneficial. In some self­help groups, this is called “hanging out with the winners.” The benefit here is on the psychic level of consciousness, and there is a transfer of positive energy and relighting of one’s own latent positive thought forms.
vocabulary_box: ㄱ. In Alcoholics Anonymous, people struggling with alcohol addiction come together to share their experiences, support each other, and learn from those who have successfully stayed alcohol-free.
ㄴ. In Group Therapy Sessions, people are provided with emotional support that they need to overcome hardship, led by a licensed therapist or counselor.

ㄷ. Depression and Bipolar Support Alliance is a peer-led support group for people living with depression or bipolar disorder, providing a space to exchange coping strategies and receive emotional support from others who have overcome such challenges.
ㄹ. Motivational Seminars are events led by professional speakers who provide inspiration and advice to people in need of support.
options: ① ㄱ, ㄷ
② ㄱ, ㄹ
③ ㄴ, ㄹ
④ ㄱ, ㄷ, ㄹ
⑤ ㄴ, ㄷ, ㄹ
questions.explanation: ㄱ과 ㄷ은 전문가가 아닌 같은 문제를 겪는 동료들이 주도하는 지원 그룹(peer-led support group)에 대한 설명이며, ㄴ은 공인된 치료사(licensed therapist)에 의해, ㄹ은 전문 연설가(professional speakers)에 의해 주도되는 전문가 중심의 그룹이다.

questions.question: 28. 밑줄 친 (A), (B)가 다음 글에서 의미하는 바로 가장 적절한 것을 연결한 것은? [4.7점]
questions.passage: Whales are highly efficient at carbon storage. When they die, each whale sequesters an average of 30 tons of carbon dioxide, taking that carbon out of the atmosphere for centuries. For comparison, the average tree absorbs only 48 pounds of CO2 a year. <u>(A) From a climate perspective, each whale is the marine equivalent of thousands of trees.</u> Whales also help sequester carbon by fertilizing the ocean as they release nutrient-rich waste, in turn increasing phytoplankton populations, which also sequester carbon - <u>(B) leading some scientists to call them the "engineers of marine ecosystems."</u> In 2019, economists from the International Monetary Fund (IMF) estimated the value of the ecosystem services provided by each whale at over $2 million USD. They called for a new global program of economic incentives to return whale populations to preindustrial whaling levels as one example of a "nature-based solution" to climate change. Calls are now being made for a global whale restoration program, to slow down climate change.
options: ① (A) The impact of one tree in absorbing CO2 is much greater than that of individual whales. (B) Whales have a harmful effect on the development of beautiful marine environments.

② (A) A single whale absorbs and stores as much carbon dioxide as thousands of trees combined. (B) Similar to how engineers build and shape systems, whales influence the health of marine ecosystems in ways that support carbon sequestration.
③ (A) Thousands of whales absorb and sequester as much carbon dioxide as a single tree. (B) Whales play a crucial role in shaping and maintaining the health of ocean environments.

④ (A) The impact of one whale on reducing atmospheric CO2 is much less than that of individual trees. (B) By supporting the growth of marine life and helping regulate carbon levels, whales act as key contributors to the balance of ocean ecosystems.
⑤ (A) Whales play the huge role in helping combat climate change, just like forests do on land. (B) Whales contribute to the balance of ocean ecosystems by increasing carbon levels.
questions.explanation: (A)는 고래 한 마리가 대기 중의 이산화탄소를 흡수하고 저장하는 능력이 수천 그루의 나무와 맞먹는다는 의미이며, (B)는 고래가 해양 생태계의 건강에 영향을 주어 탄소 격리를 돕는 중추적인 역할을 한다는 의미이다. 따라서 2번이 가장 적절하다.
options_translation: ① (A) 이산화탄소를 흡수하는 데 있어 나무 한 그루의 영향이 개별 고래의 영향보다 훨씬 크다. (B) 고래는 아름다운 해양 환경의 발전에 해로운 영향을 미친다.
② (A) 단 한 마리의 고래가 수천 그루의 나무를 합친 것만큼 많은 이산화탄소를 흡수하고 저장한다. (B) 엔지니어가 시스템을 구축하고 형성하는 방식과 유사하게, 고래는 탄소 격리를 지원하는 방식으로 해양 생태계의 건강에 영향을 미친다.
③ (A) 수천 마리의 고래가 나무 한 그루만큼의 이산화탄소를 흡수하고 격리한다. (B) 고래는 해양 환경의 건강을 형성하고 유지하는 데 결정적인 역할을 한다.
④ (A) 대기 중 이산화탄소를 줄이는 데 있어 고래 한 마리의 영향은 개별 나무의 영향보다 훨씬 적다. (B) 해양 생물의 성장을 지원하고 탄소 수치를 조절하는 데 도움을 줌으로써, 고래는 해양 생태계 균형의 핵심 기여자로 작용한다.
⑤ (A) 고래는 육지의 숲처럼 기후 변화에 맞서 싸우는 데 거대한 역할을 한다. (B) 고래는 탄소 수치를 증가시킴으로써 해양 생태계의 균형에 기여한다.

questions.question: 1. 다음 글에서 필자가 주장하는 바로 가장 적절한 것은? [3점]
questions.passage: One valuable technique for getting out of helplessness, depression, and situations which are predominantly being run by the thought, “I can’t,” is to choose to be with other persons who have resolved the problem with which we struggle. This is one of the great powers of self-help groups. When we are in a negative state, we have given a lot of energy to negative thought forms, and the positive thought forms are weak. Those who are in a higher vibration are free of the energy from their negative thoughts and have energized positive thought forms. Merely to be in their presence is beneficial. In some self-help groups, this is called “hanging out with the winners.” The benefit here is on the psychic level of consciousness, and there is a transfer of positive energy and relighting of one’s own latent positive thought forms.
options: ① 부정적인 감정을 없애기 위해서는 운동이나 식단 조절이 가장 중요하다.
② 부정적인 생각에 지배당할 때는 문제를 극복한 사람들과 함께하는 것이 큰 도움이 될 수 있다.
③ 긍정적인 생각은 스스로 노력해서 만들어야 하며 타인의 감정이나 사고방식은 중요하지 않다.
④ 우울감은 신체적 원인에서 비롯되므로 약물치료나 운동을 통한 신체 리듬 회복이 효과적이다.
⑤ 개인의 전문성을 높이기 위해 문제를 해결한 사람들과 함께 어울리며 정보와 노하우를 공유해야 한다.
questions.explanation: 지문은 무력감이나 우울함 등 부정적인 생각에 사로잡혀 있을 때, 같은 문제를 이미 해결한 사람들과 함께 있는 것이 긍정적인 에너지 전이와 잠재된 긍정적 사고를 일깨우는 데 도움이 된다고 주장하고 있습니다. 따라서 정답은 ②번입니다.

questions.question: 2. 다음 글의 제목으로 가장 적절한 것은? [3.1점]
questions.passage: Many people take the commonsense view that color is an objective property of things, or of the light that bounces off them. They say a tree’s leaves are green because they reflect green light — a greenness that is just as real as the leaves. Others argue that color doesn’t inhabit the physical world at all but exists only in the eye or mind of the viewer. They maintain that if a tree fell in a forest and no one was there to see it, its leaves would be colorless — and so would everything else. They say there is no such thing as color; there are only the people who see it. Both positions are, in a way, correct. Color is objective and subjective — “the place,” as Paul Cézanne put it, “where our brain and the universe meet.” Color is created when light from the world is registered by the eyes and interpreted by the brain.
options: ① Color Illusions: Why We See What Isn’t Really There
② The Eye and Light: Discovering Human Vision and Biology
③ The Dual Nature of Color: Objective Light, Subjective Experience
④ Human Perception: The Brain’s Role in Creating Visual Illusions and Misconceptions
⑤ Why Leaves Are Green: A Scientific Explanation of Light and Reflection
questions.explanation: 지문은 색이 사물의 객관적인 특성이라는 견해와 관찰자의 눈이나 마음에만 존재하는 주관적인 것이라는 두 가지 견해를 모두 소개하며, 색이 객관적이면서도 주관적인 이중적 성격을 지님을 설명하고 있습니다. 따라서 정답은 ③번입니다.
options_translation: ① 색의 착각: 왜 우리는 실제로 존재하지 않는 것을 보는가
② 눈과 빛: 인간의 시각과 생물학 발견하기
③ 색의 이중적 본질: 객관적 빛, 주관적 경험
④ 인간의 지각: 시각적 착각과 오해를 만드는 뇌의 역할
⑤ 나뭇잎은 왜 초록색인가: 빛과 반사에 대한 과학적 설명

questions.question: 3. 다음 글의 빈칸에 공통으로 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은? [3.4점]
questions.passage: Why do you care how a customer reacts to a purchase? Good question. By understanding post-purchase behavior, you can understand the influence and the likelihood of whether a buyer will repurchase the product (and whether she will keep it or return it). You’ll also determine whether the buyer will encourage others to purchase the product from you. Satisfied customers can become unpaid ambassadors for your business, so _________ should be on the top of your to-do list. People tend to believe the opinions of people they know. People trust friends over advertisements any day. They know that advertisements are paid to tell the “good side” and that they’re used to persuade them to purchase products and services. By continually monitoring _________ after the sale, you have the sale, you have the ability to avoid negative word-of-mouth advertising.
options: ① brand loyalty
② social media
③ market trends
④ customer satisfaction
⑤ advertising strategy
questions.explanation: 지문은 구매 후 행동을 이해하는 것의 중요성을 강조하며, 만족한 고객이 무보수 홍보 대사가 되어 긍정적인 입소문을 낼 수 있음을 설명합니다. 따라서 빈칸에 공통으로 들어갈 말은 '고객 만족'이 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 브랜드 충성도
② 소셜 미디어
③ 시장 트렌드
④ 고객 만족
⑤ 광고 전략

questions.question: 4. 다음 글의 내용을 한 문장으로 요약하고자 한다. 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은? [3.7점]
questions.passage: Most people have no doubt heard this question: If a tree falls in the forest and there is no one there to hear it fall, does it make a sound? The correct answer is no. Sound is more than pressure waves, and indeed there can be no sound without a hearer. And similarly, scientific communication is a two-way process. Just as a signal of any kind is useless unless it is perceived, a published scientific paper (signal) is useless unless it is both received and understood by its intended audience. Thus we can restate the axiom of science as follows: A scientific experiment is not complete until the results have been published and understood. Publication is no more than pressure waves unless the published paper is understood. Too many scientific papers fall silently in the woods.
questions.summary_sentence: Scientific knowledge becomes (A) _________ only when research is not just shared, but also (B) _________ by its target audience.
options: ① authoritative ... debated
② pervasive ... interpreted
③ fruitful ... criticized
④ influential ... disapproved
⑤ significant ... comprehended
questions.explanation: 이 글은 과학적 논문이 출판되는 것만으로는 충분하지 않으며, 독자가 이를 이해해야만 비로소 의미가 있다는 점을 강조하고 있습니다. 따라서 과학 지식은 (A) 'significant(중요한/의미 있는)'해지며, 이는 대상 독자에 의해 (B) 'comprehended(이해되는)' 될 때만 가능하다는 5번이 정답입니다.
options_translation: ① 권위 있는 ... 토론되는
② 널리 퍼진 ... 해석되는
③ 결실 있는 ... 비판받는
④ 영향력 있는 ... 반대되는
⑤ 중요한 ... 이해되는

questions.question: 5. 다음 글에서 필자가 주장하는 바로 가장 적절한 것은? [3점]
questions.passage: Nearly everything has to go through your mouth to get to the rest of you, from food and air to bacteria and viruses. A healthy mouth can help your body get what it needs and prevent it from harm — with adequate space for air to travel to your lungs, and healthy teeth and gums that prevent harmful microorganisms from entering your bloodstream. From the moment you are created, oral health affects every aspect of your life. What happens in the mouth is usually just the tip of the iceberg and a reflection of what is happening in other parts of the body. Poor oral health can be a cause of a disease that affects the entire body. The microorganisms in an unhealthy mouth can enter the bloodstream and travel anywhere in the body, posing serious health risks.
options: ① 치아와 잇몸의 건강을 유지함으로써 외모와 자신감을 높여야 한다.
② 입은 신체의 건강과 직결되므로 구강 건강을 잘 유지해야 한다.
③ 질병 예방을 위해 꾸준한 운동과 식단 관리를 바탕으로 면역력 강화에 신경써야 한다.
④ 건강을 유지하기 위해 구강보다는 장기와 근육의 기능을 우선적으로 관리해야 한다.
⑤ 입을 통해 다양한 미생물이 유입되기 때문에 꾸준한 손씻기를 통해 질병을 예방해야 한다.
questions.explanation: 이 글은 구강 건강이 전신 건강에 미치는 영향을 강조하고 있습니다. 입을 통해 음식물뿐만 아니라 세균과 바이러스가 들어오며, 구강 건강이 좋지 않을 경우 미생물이 혈류를 타고 온몸으로 퍼져 심각한 건강 위험을 초래할 수 있다고 설명하므로 구강 건강 유지의 중요성을 주장하는 2번이 적절합니다.

questions.question: 6. 주어진 글 다음에 이어질 글의 순서로 가장 적절한 것은? [3.6점]
questions.passage: The interaction of workers from different cultural backgrounds with the host population might increase productivity due to positive externalities like knowledge spillovers.
ordered_passages: (A) They might even discriminate against other ethnic groups and they might fear that social conflicts between different foreign nationalities are imported into their own neighbourhood.

(B) This is only an advantage up to a certain degree. When the variety of backgrounds is too large, fractionalization may cause excessive transaction costs for communication, which may lower productivity. Diversity not only impacts the labour market, but may also affect the quality of life in a location.

(C) A tolerant native population may value a multicultural city or region because of an increase in the range of available goods and services. On the other hand, diversity could be perceived as an unattractive feature if natives perceive it as a distortion of what they consider to be their national identity.
questions.explanation: 주어진 글에서 다른 문화적 배경의 상호작용이 생산성을 높일 수 있다는 장점을 언급한 후, (B)에서 이것이 어느 정도까지만 장점이며 배경이 너무 다양하면 오히려 비용을 초래하고 생산성을 낮출 수 있다는 반전과 함께 삶의 질에 미치는 영향을 소개합니다. (C)에서는 삶의 질 측면에서 관용적인 원주민은 이를 가치 있게 여기지만, 반대로 국가적 정체성 왜곡으로 인식하면 부정적일 수 있음을 설명합니다. 마지막으로 (A)에서 부정적인 시각의 연장선으로 다른 민족 집단을 차별하거나 사회적 갈등을 우려하는 상황을 설명하는 순서가 가장 자연스럽습니다.

questions.question: 7. 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은? [3.3점]
questions.passage: We tend to believe that we _________________________ and that we are free of most of those that are socially undesirable. For example, a large majority of the general public thinks that they are more intelligent, more fair-minded, less prejudiced, and more skilled behind the wheel of an automobile than the average person. This phenomenon is so reliable and ubiquitous that it has come to be known as the "Lake Wobegon effect," after Garrison Keillor's fictional community where "the women are strong, the men are good-looking, and all the children are above average." A survey of one million high school seniors found that 70% thought they were above average in leadership ability, and only 2% thought they were below average. In terms of ability to get along with others, all students thought they were above average, 60% thought they were in the top 10%, and 25% thought they were in the top 1%!
options: ① view ourselves as below average in social skills
② become anxious when we outperform our friends
③ possess a host of socially desirable characteristics
④ treat everyone equally, regardless of their personal attributes
⑤ admire others who seem smarter and more capable than us
questions.explanation: 이 글은 사람들이 자신을 실제보다 더 긍정적으로 평가하는 '레이크 워비건 효과(Lake Wobegon effect)'에 대해 설명하고 있습니다. 빈칸 뒤의 예시들이 지능, 공정함, 운전 실력 등 사회적으로 바람직한 특성들을 평균 이상으로 가지고 있다고 믿는 경향을 보여주므로 정답은 ③ '사회적으로 바람직한 많은 특성들을 소유하고 있다'가 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 우리 자신을 사회적 기술에서 평균 이하로 본다
② 우리가 친구들보다 더 나은 성과를 낼 때 불안해진다
③ 사회적으로 바람직한 많은 특성들을 소유하고 있다
④ 개인적인 속성과 관계없이 모든 사람을 평등하게 대우한다
⑤ 우리보다 더 똑똑하고 유능해 보이는 타인들을 존경한다

questions.question: 8. 다음 글의 내용과 일치하지 않는 것은? [3점]
questions.passage: Whales are highly efficient at carbon storage. When they die, each whale sequesters an average of 30 tons of carbon dioxide, taking that carbon out of the atmosphere for centuries. For comparison, the average tree absorbs only 48 pounds of CO2 a year. From a climate perspective, each whale is the marine equivalent of thousands of trees. Whales also help sequester carbon by fertilizing the ocean as they release nutrient-rich waste, in turn increasing phytoplankton populations, which also sequester carbon - leading some scientists to call them the "engineers of marine ecosystems." In 2019, economists from the International Monetary Fund (IMF) estimated the value of the ecosystem services provided by each whale at over $2 million USD. They called for a new global program of economic incentives to return whale populations to preindustrial whaling levels as one example of a "nature-based solution" to climate change. Calls are now being made for a global whale restoration program, to slow down climate change.
options: ① 고래는 죽을 때 평균 30톤의 이산화 탄소를 격리하며, 수 세기 동안 대기로부터 그 탄소를 빼내어 둔다.
② 고래는 영양이 풍부한 배설물을 내보내면서 바다를 비옥하게 함으로써 탄소를 격리하는 데 도움을 준다.
③ 식물성 플랑크톤 개체수를 적절히 감소시키기 때문에 과학자들은 고래들을 '해양 생태계의 기술자'라고 부르게 되었다.
④ IMF의 경제학자들은 고래에 의해서 제공되는 생태계 서비스의 가치를 미화 200만 달러가 넘게 추정했다.
⑤ 기후 변화를 늦추기 위해 세계적인 고래 복원 프로그램에 대한 요구가 현재 제기되고 있다.
questions.explanation: 지문에서 고래는 영양이 풍부한 배설물을 통해 식물성 플랑크톤 개체수를 '증가시킨다(increasing)'고 언급되어 있습니다. 따라서 개체수를 '감소시키기 때문'이라는 ③번 선택지는 본문의 내용과 일치하지 않습니다.

questions.question: 9. 다음 글에서 전체 흐름과 관계 없는 문장은? [3.4점]
questions.passage: As the social and economic situation of countries got better, wage levels and working conditions improved. Gradually people were given more time off. ① At the same time, forms of transport improved and it became faster and cheaper to get to places. ② England's industrial revolution led to many of these changes, and railways, in the nineteenth century, opened up now famous seaside resorts such as Blackpool and Brighton. ③ With the railways came many large hotels. In Canada, for example, the new coast-to-coast railway system made possible the building of such famous hotels as Banff Springs and Chateau Lake Louise in the Rockies. ④ Due to their location near the railways, these hotels attracted numerous business travelers who prioritized quick access to transit networks. ⑤ Later, the arrival of air transport opened up more of the world and led to tourism growth.
questions.explanation: 이 글은 사회 경제적 발전, 노동 조건 개선, 교통 수단의 발달로 인해 관광 산업(seaside resorts, hotels, tourism growth)이 성장하게 된 배경을 설명하고 있습니다. ④번 문장은 호텔이 비즈니스 여행객을 유치했다는 내용으로, 여가와 관광 산업의 성장이라는 전체 흐름에서 벗어납니다.

questions.question: 10. 글의 흐름으로 보아, 주어진 문장이 들어가기에 가장 적절한 곳은? [3.6점]
questions.passage: Cartilage is extremely important for the healthy functioning of a joint, especially if that joint bears weight, like your knee. ( ① ) Imagine for a moment that you're looking into the inner workings of your left knee as you walk down the street. ( ② ) The cartilage in your left knee then "drinks in" synovial fluid, in much the same way that a sponge soaks up liquid when put in water. ( ③ ) When you take another step and transfer the weight back onto your left leg, much of the fluid squeezes out of the cartilage. ( ④ ) This squeezing of joint fluid into and out of the cartilage helps it respond to the off-and-on pressure of walking without breaking under the pressure. ( ⑤ )
questions.insertion_sentence: When you shift your weight from your left leg to your right, the pressure on your left knee is released.
questions.explanation: 주어진 문장은 왼쪽 다리에서 오른쪽 다리로 무게를 옮길 때 왼쪽 무릎의 압력이 해제된다는 내용입니다. ②번 뒤의 문장에서 왼쪽 무릎의 연골이 관절액을 '빨아들인다(drinks in)'고 설명하는데, 이는 압력이 해제되었을 때 일어나는 현상이므로 주어진 문장은 ②번에 들어가는 것이 가장 적절합니다.

questions.question: 11. 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은? [3.5점]
questions.passage: What does it mean for a character to be a hero as opposed to a villain? In artistic and entertainment descriptions, it's essential for the author to establish a positive relationship between a protagonist and the audience. In order for tragedy or misfortune to draw out an emotional response in viewers, the character must be adjusted so as to be recognizable as either friend or enemy. Whether the portrayal is fictional or documentary, we must feel that the protagonist is someone whose actions benefit us; the protagonist is, or would be, a worthy companion or valued ally. Violent action films are often filled with dozens of incidental deaths of minor characters that draw out little response in the audience. In order to feel strong emotions, the audience must _________ in a character as either ally or enemy.
options: ① accept the flaws
② be emotionally invested
③ trust and support a firm resolve
④ be indifferent to the bold actions
⑤ be attracted by the unexpected changes
questions.explanation: 글의 흐름상 관객이 주인공에 대해 강한 감정을 느끼기 위해서는 주인공에게 감정적으로 몰입(emotionally invested)되어야 한다는 내용이 가장 적절합니다. 본문에서 주인공과 관객 사이의 긍정적인 관계 수립 및 가치 있는 동료로서의 인식이 강조되고 있기 때문입니다.
options_translation: ① 결점을 받아들이다
② 감정적으로 몰입하다
③ 굳은 결의를 신뢰하고 지지하다
④ 대담한 행동에 무관심하다
⑤ 예기치 못한 변화에 매료되다

questions.question: 12. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 어법상 틀린 것은? [3.3점]
questions.passage: Piaget put the same amount of water into two different glasses: a tall narrow glass and a wide glass, and then asked kids ① <u>to compare</u> two glasses. Kids younger than six or seven usually say that the tall narrow glass now holds more water, because the level is higher. And when they ② <u>will be</u> ready, they figure out the conservation of volume for themselves just by playing with cups of water. Piaget argued that children's understanding of morality is like their understanding of ③ <u>those</u> water glasses: we can't say that it is innate or kids learn it directly from adults. Rather, it is self-constructed as kids play with other kids. Taking turns in a game ④ <u>is</u> like pouring water back and forth between glasses. Once kids have reached the age of five or six, then playing games and working things out together will help them ⑤ <u>learn</u> about fairness far more effectively than any teaching from adults.
questions.explanation: ②번의 'when'이 이끄는 부사절에서는 미래의 의미를 나타낼 때 현재 시제를 사용해야 하므로 'will be'는 'are'로 고쳐야 합니다.

questions.question: 13. 다음 글의 주제로 가장 적절한 것은? [3.1점]
questions.passage: Do you ever find yourself suddenly feeling angry? One moment you're fine, and the next moment you're slamming doors or rolling your eyes at your parents. Some people may think you just have a bad attitude or are getting too upset about a small problem. However, these feelings don't simply come from stress about everyday life. As a teen, you may feel like an adult, but your brain is still growing. In your brain, there is a part that is responsible for solving problems and controlling your emotions. In your teen years, this part is still in development. The changes in your brain lead you toward independence, social engagement, and creativity. At the same time, however, you may feel confused about who you are. You may also be more sensitive to unfairness. Furthermore, your body is flowing with hormones. This significantly affects your mood. The combination of these factors intensifies your strong emotions.
options: ① why teenagers experience intense emotions during adolescence
② the impact of social media on teenage mental health
③ ways for teens to resolve conflicts with their parents
④ significance of making a strong bond in teenagers
⑤ roles of friendships in shaping teenagers' identity
questions.explanation: 이 글은 십 대들이 강렬한 감정을 느끼는 이유가 뇌의 발달 과정과 호르몬의 변화 때문임을 설명하고 있으므로 주제로 ①번이 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 십 대들이 청소년기 동안 강렬한 감정을 경험하는 이유
② 소셜 미디어가 십 대의 정신 건강에 미치는 영향
③ 십 대들이 부모님과의 갈등을 해결하는 방법
④ 십 대들에게 강한 유대감을 형성하는 것의 중요성
⑤ 십 대의 정체성을 형성하는 데 있어서 우정의 역할

questions.question: 14. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은? [3.2점]
questions.passage: You need to learn how to deal with anger in a socially appropriate way. Remember: anger is a feeling, but behavior is a choice. The first step is recognizing the ① <u>physical</u> signs of anger. It is possible to recognize those signs in advance. They include an increased heart rate, a flushed face, and the clenching of your fists. When these things happen, take action to ② <u>alleviate</u> your anger. For example, you could try taking a break to organize your thoughts or ending a conversation before it gets too intense. In some cases, those strategies may not be ③ <u>insufficient</u>, so you may need to find proper coping skills for your personal situation. Without the right coping skills, you may find yourself becoming verbally or even physically ④ <u>aggressive</u>. Explore various strategies to ⑤ <u>determine</u> what is best for you, such as taking a walk, drawing a picture, or writing down things that come to your mind. You can also try to find possible solutions to a problem and then compare the advantages and disadvantages of each one.
questions.explanation: 맥락상 앞서 제시된 전략들이 충분하지 않을 수도 있다는 내용이 되어야 그 뒤의 '적절한 대처 기술을 찾을 필요가 있다'는 문장과 논리적으로 연결됩니다. 따라서 'insufficient(불충분한)'를 'sufficient(충분한)' 또는 'enough'로 고쳐야 '충분하지 않을 수도 있다(may not be sufficient)'가 되어 올바른 문맥이 됩니다.

questions.question: 15. 다음 글의 목적으로 가장 적절한 것은? [3.1점]
questions.passage:
It is natural to feel angry from time to time; it doesn't mean there is something wrong with you. Anger can sometimes be a useful tool. For example, an angry but open conversation can resolve a conflict between friends. The important thing is to manage your anger so that it does not turn into aggressive or violent behavior. This does not mean that you should stop yourself from feeling angry. Rather, you should express it in a productive way. Ask yourself some questions about your angry feelings. This can help you to better understand your anger.
Questions to Ask Yourself
• How often do I feel angry?
• What situations make me feel the most intense anger?
• Is my anger directed at anyone or anything in particular?
• Do I focus on the causes of my anger instead of solutions?
• Can I control my emotions when I get angry?
• How do I react and behave when I get angry?
options: ① 친구와의 갈등을 피하는 방법을 소개하려고
② 분노를 완전히 억제하는 방법을 제안하려고
③ 감정을 숨기는 것이 왜 중요한지를 강조하려고
④ 분노의 심리학적 원인을 과학적으로 분석하려고
⑤ 분노를 자기성찰의 기회로 삼을 수 있음을 알려주려고
questions.explanation: 이 글은 분노를 단순히 억제해야 할 부정적인 감정이 아니라, 생산적으로 표현하고 자신에게 질문을 던짐으로써 스스로를 더 잘 이해하고 성찰하는 기회로 활용할 수 있음을 조언하고 있습니다.

questions.question: 16. 글의 흐름으로 보아, 주어진 문장이 들어가기에 가장 적절한 곳은? [3.2점]
questions.passage: After our application was approved, I was eager to make a good first impression with our investors. ( ① ) To accomplish this, I made a video about my grandparents and their jam. ( ② ) In the video, I emphasized how the strawberries were cultivated organically, without the use of synthetic chemicals. ( ③ ) I also included clips of my grandparents. ( ④ ) Finally, I explained where I wanted to put the new greenhouse and asked for support. ( ⑤ ) After some editing, I posted the video on many social media sites.
questions.insertion_sentence: In the clips, they were making the jam using entirely natural ingredients.
questions.explanation: 주어진 문장의 'the clips'는 ③번 문장의 'clips of my grandparents'를 가리키며, 할아버지 할머니가 잼을 만드는 장면(clips)에서 천연 재료를 사용하고 있었다는 부연 설명이 이어지는 것이 자연스럽습니다. 따라서 ④번 위치가 가장 적절합니다.

questions.question: 17. 다음 글의 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은? [3.1점]
questions.passage:
My grandparents sell their delicious organic jam at the local market every weekend. I went to help them last weekend. (A) _________, they had already sold all of their jam! They didn't have enough strawberries to make any more jam. That evening, I sat by the window and stared out at the empty field behind their house. Suddenly, I got an idea. The field would be the perfect place for a larger greenhouse. Then they could grow more strawberries! I immediately started to search for a way, finding the perfect solution. I would start a crowdfunding campaign!
My grandparents were thrilled when I told them my idea. With the help of investors, we could build a large greenhouse and grow a lot more strawberries. (B) _________, we could reward the investors for their help by sending them jars of organic jam! With this plan in mind, the next step was to figure out the details.
options: ① However .... Furthermore
② However .... In other words
③ Instead .... Furthermore
④ Instead .... Therefore
⑤ Besides .... Therefore
questions.explanation: (A) 앞 문장에서 도와주러 갔으나, (A) 뒤에서 이미 잼이 다 팔렸다는 예상 밖의 상황이 나오므로 역접의 'However'가 적절합니다. (B) 앞뒤 내용은 투자자의 도움으로 딸기를 더 많이 키울 수 있다는 점에 이어, 투자자에게 보답할 수도 있다는 추가적인 장점을 나열하고 있으므로 첨가의 'Furthermore'가 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 그러나 .... 더욱이
② 그러나 .... 다시 말해서
③ 대신에 .... 더욱이
④ 대신에 .... 그러므로
⑤ 게다가 .... 그러므로

questions.question: 19. (A), (B), (C)의 각 네모 안에서 어법에 맞는 표현으로 가장 적절한 것은? [3.1점]
questions.passage:
Campaign Details
Before beginning your campaign, be sure to plan all the production details. How many products will you make? How long will it take to make the product? This planning is important (A) [because / because of] your potential investors will want to see a clear schedule. Once your plan is complete, remember (B) [setting / to set] your funding goal. It should be enough to complete the project and fulfill the rewards for the investors. Consider all the necessary costs before deciding on the amount.
Campaign Promotion and Communication
