questions.question: 21. 다음 글의 내용을 한 문장으로 요약하려 한다. 빈칸 (A), (B) 에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은? [3.9점]
questions.passage: Some researchers view spoken languages as incomplete devices for capturing precise differences. They think numbers represent the most neutral language of description. However, when our language of description is changed to numbers, we do not move toward greater accuracy. Numbers are no more appropriate 'pictures of the world' than words, music, or painting. While useful for specific purposes (e.g. census taking, income distribution), they eliminate information of enormous value. For example, the future lives of young students are tied to their scores on national tests. In effect, whether they can continue with their education, where, and at what cost depends importantly on a handful of numbers. These numbers do not account for the quality of schools they have attended, whether they have been tutored, have supportive parents, have test anxiety, and so on. Finally, putting aside the many ways in which statistical results can be manipulated, there are ways in which turning people's lives into numbers is morally insulating. Statistics on crime, homelessness, or the spread of a disease say nothing of people's suffering. We read the statistics as reports on events at a distance, thus allowing us to escape without being disturbed. Statistics are human beings with the tears wiped off. Quantify with caution.
questions.summary_sentence: While (A) _________ can be useful in certain contexts, they fail to fully capture human experiences and moral dimensions, which (B) _________ deeper truths through language and other expressive forms.
options: ① numbers ... reveal
② language ... conceal
③ numbers ... simplify
④ language ... reflect
⑤ statistics ... twist
questions.explanation: 글의 핵심은 숫자(또는 통계)가 특정 목적에는 유용할 수 있지만, 인간의 경험이나 고통과 같은 깊은 진실을 포착하지 못한다는 것입니다. 요약문에서 (A)에는 숫자(numbers)가 들어가고, (B)에는 언어와 다른 표현 형태를 통해 더 깊은 진실을 드러낸다는(reveal) 의미가 들어가는 것이 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 숫자 ... 드러내다
② 언어 ... 숨기다
③ 숫자 ... 단순화하다
④ 언어 ... 반영하다
⑤ 통계 ... 왜곡하다

questions.question:
[서답형 3(단답형)] Correct two grammatical errors.
[총 3점, 각 문제당 1.5점]
questions.passage: The best defence most species of octopus have is ⓐ <u>staying</u> hidden as much as possible and doing their own hunting at night. So to find one fully ⓑ <u>exposed</u> in the shallows in daylight was a surprise for two Australian underwater photographers. Actually, It was a flounder ⓒ <u>that</u> they saw at first. It was only when they looked again that they saw a medium-sized octopus. An octopus has an ability to change colour and pattern, which ⓓ <u>help</u> it become another creature. Many more of this species ⓔ <u>have found</u> since then, and there are now photographs of octopuses that could be said to be transforming into sea snakes.
questions.answer:
1) ⓓ help -> helps
2) ⓔ have found -> have been found
questions.explanation:
1) ⓓ: 관계대명사 which의 선행사는 앞 문장의 'an ability to change colour and pattern' 또는 'ability'이므로 단수 취급하여 help를 helps로 고쳐야 합니다.
2) ⓔ: 문맥상 이 종의 더 많은 개체들이 '발견되어 온 것'이므로 수동태인 have been found로 고쳐야 합니다.

questions.question: [서답형 4(단답형)] 다음 글에서 밑줄 친 (A), (B)에 해당하는 의미를 가진 문장을 주어진 <보기>의 단어들을 모두 사용하여 어법에 맞게 영작하시오. (단, 형태변화 가능, 스펠링 및 시제 주의)(각 1.5점, 총 3점, 부분점수 있음)
questions.passage:
What does it mean for a character to be a hero as opposed to a villain? In artistic and entertainment descriptions, <u>(A) 저자가 긍정적인 관계를 구축하는 것이 필수적이다</u> between a protagonist and the audience. In order for tragedy or misfortune to draw out an emotional response in viewers, the character must be adjusted so as to be recognizable as either friend or enemy. Whether the portrayal is fictional or documentary, we must feel that the protagonist is someone whose actions benefit us; the protagonist is, or would be, a wooden companion or valued ally. Violent action films are often filled with dozens of incidental deaths of minor characters that draw out little response in the audience. In order to feel strong emotions, the audience must be emotionally invested in a character as either ally or enemy. <u>(B) 관객의 관심을 끄는 가장 효과적인 방법들 중 하나는 명확한 설명이다</u> of whether the main characters are heroes or villains.
* villain: 악당 ** protagonist: 주인공
subjective_conditions: 주어진 <보기>의 단어들을 모두 사용하여 어법에 맞게 영작
형태변화 가능
스펠링 및 시제 주의
vocabulary_box: (A) : (be, it, to, for, the, author, establish, essential)
(B) : (an audience, be, of, to, one, the, way, most, engage, effective, )
questions.answer:
(A) : it is essential for the author to establish
(B) : One of the most effective ways to engage an audience is
questions.explanation: (A)는 가주어-진주어 구문인 'It is 형용사 for 의미상주어 to부정사' 구조를 활용합니다. (B)는 'One of the 최상급 복수명사' 주어와 단수 동사 'is'의 수 일치, 그리고 'ways'를 수식하는 to부정사(to engage)를 활용합니다.

questions.question: [서답형 5(단답형)] 다음 글의 문맥에 맞게, 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 단어를 주어진 본문에 있는 단어만을 사용하여 쓰시오. [단, 형태변화 가능, 각 1.5점, 총 3점 부분 점수 있음.]
questions.passage:
Modern brainscanning techniques such as fMRI (functional Magnetic Resonance Imaging) have revealed that (A) _________ (B) _________ lights up many areas of the brain. There is intense activity in areas associated with pronunciation and hearing the sound of the spoken response, which strengthens the connective structures of your brain cells for more brainpower. This leads to an overall improvement in concentration. To read words aloud is also a good way to develop your public speaking skills because it forces you to read each and every word - something people don't often do when reading quickly, or reading in silence. Children, in particular, should be encouraged to practice oral reading because the brain is wired for learning through connections that are created by positive stimulation, such as singing, touching, and oral reading.
* stimulation: 자극
subjective_conditions: 주어진 본문에 있는 단어만을 사용하여 쓰시오
형태변화 가능
각각 한 단어
questions.explanation: 글의 중반부와 후반부에서 'To read words aloud'와 'oral reading'이 뇌에 긍정적인 자극을 준다고 설명하고 있으므로, 빈칸에는 'oral reading'이 들어가는 것이 적절합니다.

questions.question: [단답형 6] 위 글의 빈칸 (A)~(D)에 들어갈 영어 단어를 주어진 조건에 맞게 쓰시오. [각 1점, 총 4점 부분 점수 있음.]
questions.passage:
Food security is a growing concern in the modern world, and Korea is no exception. Traditional farming methods alone may no longer be sufficient to meet the needs of a growing population, especially as arable land becomes more limited. To address this, there is a rising need to integrate smart farming technologies into Korean (A) ag _________.
Smart farms use artificial intelligence and automated systems to monitor crops, adjust environmental conditions, and optimize production. These technologies help growers make informed decisions in real time, reducing waste and increasing efficiency.
Consumers today are more aware of the origins of their food and expect consistent quality. Smart farming can meet these expectations by ensuring a stable supply of fresh produce, grown in controlled environments that limit exposure to pests and weather fluctuations. It also improves the ability to safely (B) di _________ food to various regions, reducing the risk of shortages.
By modernizing the farming industry through smart systems, Korea can take a critical step toward achieving long-term food security. It is essential for the country to actively (C) ad _________ these technologies to stay competitive and address future challenges. Investing in innovation not only supports local producers but also strengthens the nation's ability to sustainably produce and consume food in the years to come, helping to fulfill both national and global food (D) se _________ goals.
*arable land 경작지
subjective_conditions: 1. 주어진 영영 풀이에 해당하는 단어를 작성할 것.
2. 주어진 철자로 시작하는 영어 단어를 쓸 것.
3. 어법에 맞게 어형을 정확하게 작성할 것.
questions.subjective_answer_format:
<Answer>
(A) ag_________ : the science or practice of farming, including growing crops and raising animals for food, fiber, and other products.
(B) di_________ : to give something out to several people, or to spread or supply something.
(C) ad_________ : to start to use a particular method or to show a particular attitude towards somebody/something
(D) se_________ : the state of being protected from danger, risk, or lack of something essential.
questions.explanation: (A) 농업을 뜻하는 'agriculture', (B) 분배/유통하다를 뜻하는 'distribute', (C) 채택하다/도입하다를 뜻하는 'adopt', (D) 안보/안전을 뜻하는 'security'가 영영 풀이와 문맥에 적합합니다.

questions.question: 8.다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것을 고르시오. [4.2점]
questions.passage:
The concept of ecosystem states should be familiar to anyone with a home vegetable garden. The garden is a small ecosystem that the grower attempts to keep in a specific state, namely the maximization of fruit and vegetable production. To achieve this, the grower is almost always ① <u>intervening</u> in the dynamics of the ecosystem: they remove unwanted plants that begin to grow and perhaps spray insecticides and fence off the patch to ② <u>stop</u> insects and other animals from consuming the vegetables. Since maximizing vegetable growth is an inherently ③ <u>unstable</u> state for the ecosystem, the grower is effectively keeping the ball on a slope. If the grower stops intervening, even for a day, the ecosystem, that small patch of ground, will naturally begin to shift to a more ④ <u>unstable</u> state. Vegetables may still grow, but yield will almost certainly be lower as other plants ⑤ <u>crowd</u> out the vegetables and wildlife consume the produce.
* insecticide: 살충제
questions.explanation: 인위적인 개입을 통해 유지되는 채소밭(극대화된 생산 상태)은 본래 불안정한(unstable) 상태이다. 재배자가 개입을 멈추면 생태계는 자연스럽게 더 '안정적인(stable)' 상태, 즉 자연 상태로 되돌아가려 할 것이다. 따라서 ④의 unstable은 stable로 바뀌어야 문맥상 적절하다.

questions.question: 10. [3.7점] 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것을 고르시오.
questions.passage:
Quite often the interaction between groups is socially unequal, and this is reflected in the fact that in many cases borrowing of words or constructions goes mostly or entirely in one direction, from the more powerful or prestigious group to the less favored one. The languages of socially subordinated groups may from quite an early period of contact provide terminology for objects or practices with which speakers of the more powerful group were previously unfamiliar, but the effects of contact in that direction may not progress any further than this. In some cases, as with the Dharug language of Sydney, Australia, the source of some of the earliest loans from Indigenous Australian languages into English, the fate of the language system is _________ after the obliteration of many of its speakers. The remainder shifted to varieties of English, the language of the people who had suppressed them.
*prestigious: 권력을 가진 **subordinate: 종속된 ***obliteration: 소멸
options: ① extinction
② prosperity
③ variation
④ familiarity
⑤ continuity
questions.explanation: 글의 맥락상 사회적으로 힘이 약한 집단의 언어가 억압받고 사용자들이 사라짐(obliteration)에 따라 언어 체계가 겪게 될 운명은 '소멸(extinction)'이 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 소멸
② 번영
③ 변화
④ 친숙함
⑤ 지속성

questions.question: 14. 다음 글에서 전체 흐름과 관계 없는 문장은? [4.1점]
questions.passage: When we realize we've said something in error and we pause to go back to correct it, we stop gesturing a couple of hundred milliseconds before we stop speaking. ① An intended pause in speech enhances clarity and allows the audience time to reflect, making the message more impactful and memorable. ② Such sequences suggest the startling notion that our hands "know" what we're going to say before our conscious minds do, and in fact this is often the case. ③ Gesture can mentally prime a word so that the right term comes to our lips. When people are prevented from gesturing, they talk less fluently; their speech becomes halting because their hands are no longer able to supply them with the next word, and the next. ④ Not being able to gesture has other deleterious effects: without gesture to help our mental processes along, we remember less useful information, we solve problems less well, and we are less able to explain our thinking. ⑤ Far from tagging along as speech's clumsy companion, gesture represents the leading edge of our thought.
questions.explanation: 이 글은 제스처가 언어보다 앞서며 사고와 기억 과정을 돕는다는 내용입니다. ①번 문장은 연설 중 의도적인 일시 정지가 명확성을 높인다는 내용으로, 제스처가 사고를 주도한다는 핵심 주제와 무관합니다.

questions.question: 16.주어진 글 다음에 이어질 글의 순서로 가장 적절한 것을 고르시오. [3.9점]
questions.passage: Great scientists are seldom one-hit wonders. Newton is a prime example: beyond the Newtonian mechanics, he developed the theory of gravitation, calculus, laws of motion, and optimization.
ordered_passages: (A) Therefore, future success again goes to those who have had success earlier, not because of advantages offered by the previous success, but because the earlier success was indicative of a hidden talent.
(B) Yet, there is an appealing alternative explanation: Great scientists have multiple hits and consistently succeed in their scientific endeavors simply because they're exceptionally talented.

(C) Indeed, an initial success may offer a scientist legitimacy, improve peer perception, provide knowledge of how to score and win, enhance social status, and attract resources and quality collaborators, each of these payoffs further increasing her odds of scoring another win.
(D) In fact, well-known scientists are often involved in multiple discoveries, a phenomenon potentially explained by the Matthew effect.
questions.explanation: 위대한 과학자들이 반복적으로 성공하는 현상을 '매튜 효과'로 설명하는 (D)가 먼저 오고, 초기 성공이 가져다주는 구체적 보상들을 나열하는 (C)가 이어집니다. 이후 이에 대한 대안적 설명인 '재능'을 언급하는 (B)가 오고, 초기 성공이 숨겨진 재능의 지표이기 때문에 미래 성공으로 이어진다는 결론 (A)가 이어집니다.

questions.question: 17.주어진 글 다음에 이어질 글의 순서로 가장 적절한 것을 고르시오. [4.1점]
questions.passage: The explosion of popular music in the second half of the twentieth century as well as the global circulation and dissemination of music by the creative industries propelled a new understanding of accessibility in relation to music.
ordered_passages: (A) While ordinary people had always sung and made music, the popular music movement was driven by a spirit of rebellion and freedom.

(B) This approach led to the punk movement, whose musicians even made it a condition for their music to be non-virtuosic and accessible to all in the 1970s. Groups who had been entirely excluded from music revelled in opportunities to create. This led to a sense of novelty and empowerment in and beyond the music sphere.

(C) Suddenly, in the 1950s, anyone could pick up spoons, a couple of pans, a second-hand guitar and start a band. This led to specific genres such as skiffle, but also, more generally, reflected a much more relaxed and inclusive attitude to music making.
questions.explanation: 주어진 문장에서 대중음악의 폭발과 창조 산업에 의한 음악의 보급이 음악적 접근성에 대한 새로운 이해를 추진했다고 언급하고 있습니다. (C)에서 1950년대에 누구나 악기를 들고 밴드를 시작할 수 있게 된 구체적 예시와 포용적인 태도를 설명하고, (A)에서 이러한 대중음악 운동이 반항과 자유의 정신에 의해 주도되었음을 언급합니다. 마지막으로 (B)에서 '이러한 접근 방식(This approach)'이 1970년대 펑크 운동으로 이어졌다는 흐름이 가장 적절합니다.

questions.question:
18. 글의 흐름으로 보아, 주어진 문장이 들어가기에 가장 적절한 곳을 고르시오.

18. [4.0점]
questions.passage: There are reasons why science is not fully trusted and why healthy skepticism and critical thinking are essential. In spite of professional standards, claims of objectivity, and the peer review process, the conduct of science can be biased. ( ① ) All experts are not the same, nor do they submit their work to the same scrutiny. ( ② ) For example, the Harvard researchers who made claims in the late 1960s about the problems with dietary fat, leading the nation away from perceiving sugar as one of the main causes in health problems, were funded in part by the sugar industry. ( ③ ) The authors did not reveal their funding source to the New England Journal of Medicine, where their influential article appeared. ( ④ ) Their article shaped a generation of changes in eating patterns that appears to have discouraged higher use of sugar, now widely implicated as a source of the rise in obesity and diabetes. Stories such as this one fuel suspicion - but also lead to further safeguards in the scientific process. ( ⑤ ) Funding disclosures, although not required five decades ago, have since been made compulsory.
questions.insertion_sentence: Knowing the source of funding can be important in evaluating scientific claims.
questions.explanation: 주어진 문장은 자금 지원의 출처를 아는 것이 과학적 주장을 평가하는 데 중요하다는 내용입니다. ②번 뒤의 내용은 설탕 산업으로부터 자금을 지원받은 하버드 연구원들이 설탕의 유해성을 은폐하고 지방을 비판한 구체적인 사례를 들고 있으므로, 자금 출처의 중요성을 시사하는 주어진 문장이 ②번에 들어가는 것이 적절합니다.

questions.question: 20. 다음 글의 내용을 한 문장으로 요약하고자 한다. 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은? [4.3점]
questions.passage:
Dictionaries are relatively good resources for anyone interested in finding out what a word means. Using one set of words to define another word is called a lexical definition. But it's important to understand the limits of dictionary definitions. More often than not, a definition in a dictionary requires readers to have a fairly robust understanding of the language already at their disposal. In other words, a dictionary functions in many cases as a cross-reference or translator between words one knows and words that one doesn't yet know. Even the most obscure words in a dictionary, say, for example, "pulchritudinous" or "kalokagathia," must be defined using words that the reader already knows and understands. Otherwise, the dictionary isn't very helpful.
*lexical: 어휘적인 **robust: 탄탄한 ***obscure: 난해한
questions.summary_sentence: Dictionaries offer lexical definitions using (A)________ words, but their effectiveness relies on the reader's (B)_______ language knowledge, as even rare terms are explained through already understood vocabulary.
options: ① limited ...... creative
② novel ...... extended
③ familiar ...... existing
④ universal ...... hidden
⑤ specific ...... various
questions.explanation: 사전은 모르는 단어를 설명하기 위해 독자가 이미 알고 있는(familiar) 단어를 사용하여 정의를 내리며, 이러한 사전의 효과는 독자가 이미 가지고 있는(existing) 언어 지식에 의존한다는 내용이 적절하다.
options_translation: ① 제한된 ...... 창의적인
② 새로운 ...... 확장된
③ 친숙한 ...... 기존의
④ 보편적인 ...... 숨겨진
⑤ 특정한 ...... 다양한

questions.question: [서답형 3(단답형)] Place the words in the box in right order. [3점, 부분점수 없음]
questions.passage:
The governments of virtually every country on the planet attach great importance to achieving food security and a wide variety of mechanisms have been developed to realize this goal. The first issue governments face in achieving national food security is the problem of insuring that adequate amounts of food are available to the resident population. Some governments have set goals of food self-sufficiency, which means most if not all of the food available in a country comes from the domestic farming system. However, food security does not require food self-sufficiency because countries can import food items not easily produced within the country. Agricultural products are, after all, highly sensitive to climatic, soil and other conditions that tend to vary around the world. Even countries with extremely productive agricultural sectors are not fully self-sufficient in all food items. The United States, for example, depends on imports for its supply of coffee, tea, bananas and other tropical products. In general, <u>is solved by / relying on / domestic production / adequate food supplies / assuring / both / and / imports / the problem of</u>
→___________________________________________________________
questions.answer: the problem of assuring adequate food supplies is solved by relying on both domestic production and imports
questions.explanation: 주어 '적절한 식량 공급을 보장하는 문제(the problem of assuring adequate food supplies)' 뒤에 수동태 동사구 '해결된다(is solved by)'가 오고, 전치사 by의 목적어로 '국내 생산과 수입 모두에 의존함으로써(relying on both domestic production and imports)'가 오는 구조이다.

questions.question: 9. 다음 글에 드러난 'Nani Tama'의 심경 변화로 가장 적절한 것은? (2.2점)
questions.passage: When I arrived at Auntie's place, I was shocked to see how thin Nani Tama was. "Look, Nani," I said. "I'm not taking you anywhere. You could die on me!" Nani looked at me in anger. "You want me to die here in this room? Looking at these four walls? When the whakapapa is not yet finished?" The old man held on tightly to the side of the bed and cried out as he stood up. Every slow, painful step hurt him, but he tried to walk. I could not help but carry him to the car, and we set off with Auntie. We traveled all night, mostly in silence, listening to Nani chanting in the darkness. It was strange but wonderful to hear him. Sometimes, he burst into a song that he had taught Auntie. They sang together, lifting up their voices to send the song flying like a bird through the sky.
options: curious -> startled
excited -> touched
frightened -> relieved
upset -> disappointed
annoyed -> determined
questions.explanation: 글의 초반부에서 Nani Tama는 가지 말라는 말에 화가 났지만("looked at me in anger"), 이후 침대 옆을 꽉 잡고 일어서서 고통스러운 걸음을 걷는 노력을 보이며 노래를 부르는 등 의지적인 모습을 보여줍니다. 따라서 심경 변화로 'annoyed(짜증난) -> determined(단호한, 결연한)'가 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 호기심 있는 -> 깜짝 놀란
② 신이 난 -> 감동한
③ 겁에 질린 -> 안도한
④ 속상한 -> 실망한
⑤ 짜증이 난 -> 단호한

questions.question: [10~11] 다음 글의 주제로 가장 적절한 것을 고르시오. 11. (2.9점)
questions.passage: Assuming gene editing in humans proves to be safe and effective, it might seem logical, even preferable, to correct disease-causing mutations at the earliest possible stage of life, before harmful genes begin causing serious problems. Yet once it becomes possible to transform an embryo's mutated genes into "normal" ones, there will certainly be temptations to upgrade normal genes to superior versions. Should we begin editing genes in unborn children to lower their lifetime risk of heart disease or cancer? What about giving unborn children beneficial features, like greater strength and increased mental abilities, or changing physical characteristics, like eye and hair color? The pursuit for perfection seems almost natural to human nature, but if we start down this slippery slope, we may not like where we end up.
options: concerns over the misuse of gene editing technology in human embryos
genetic similarity between humans and other living organisms
the importance of early diagnosis in preventing genetic diseases
the reasons why gene editing is already widely accepted
how gene editing can eliminate all diseases in the future
questions.explanation: 글은 인간 배아의 유전자 편집이 질병 치료를 넘어 우월한 형질을 얻기 위한 수단으로 오용될 수 있다는 우려(slippery slope)를 다루고 있습니다. 따라서 '인간 배아 유전자 편집 기술의 오용에 대한 우려'가 주제로 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 인간 배아 유전자 편집 기술의 오용에 대한 우려
② 인간과 다른 생물 사이의 유전적 유사성
③ 유전 질환 예방에 있어 조기 진단의 중요성
④ 유전자 편집이 이미 널리 받아들여지고 있는 이유
⑤ 유전자 편집이 미래에 어떻게 모든 질병을 제거할 수 있는가

questions.question: 13. 다음 글의 요지로 가장 적절한 것은? (2.8점)
questions.passage: In our competitive society, many people believe that only the biggest or the strongest can survive and thrive. However, I propose an alternative view: kindness is the key to success. Isn't that a comforting thought? We can use the power of our natural kindness to communicate and cooperate with different individuals. We can all benefit from this instead of trying to be better than others. I'd like to end this talk with a message. Think of our society as a bouquet. Just as each flower adds to the beauty when it harmonizes with the others, each person can contribute to a more beautiful world when they cooperate. By being kind and working together, we can truly flourish.
options: ① 일상생활에서 진짜 친절함과 가짜 친절함을 구별해야 한다.
② 우리 사회를 더 아름답게 만드는 것은 친절함이다.
③ 경쟁 사회에서는 살아남고 번영하는 것이 핵심이다.
④ 살면서 다양한 사람과 소통하는 것이 중요하다.
⑤ 성공하기 위해서는 동기가 확실해야 한다.
questions.explanation: 이 글은 경쟁적인 사회에서 타인보다 우월해지려고 노력하기보다는 친절함과 협력을 통해 조화를 이루는 것이 중요하다고 강조합니다. 필자는 사회를 꽃다발에 비유하며 개개인이 협력할 때 세상이 더 아름다워지고 번영할 수 있다고 말하고 있으므로, 요지로는 2번 '우리 사회를 더 아름답게 만드는 것은 친절함이다'가 가장 적절합니다.

questions.question: 14. 다음 글의 제목으로 가장 적절한 것은? (3.2점)
questions.passage: In the course of trying to solve a problem with an invention, you may encounter a brick wall of resistance when you try to think your way logically through the problem. Such logical thinking is a linear type of process, which uses our reasoning skills. This works fine when we're operating in the area of what we know or have experienced. However, when we need to deal with new information, ideas, and viewpoints, linear thinking will often come up short. On the other hand, creativity by definition involves the application of new information to old problems and the conception of new viewpoints and ideas. For this you will be most effective if you learn to operate in a nonlinear manner; that is, use your creative brain. Stated differently, if you think in a linear manner, you'll tend to be conservative and keep coming up with techniques which are already known. This, of course, is just what you don't want.
options: ① Smart Ways to Find New ideas
② The Importance of Logical Thinking
③ How Logical Thinking Affects Creativity
④ Solving Problems: Through Familiar Experiences
⑤ Thinking Differently: The First Step Toward Creativity
questions.explanation: 이 글은 새로운 정보나 관점이 필요한 문제를 해결할 때 기존의 논리적이고 선형적인 사고 방식은 한계가 있다고 설명합니다. 대신 비선형적인 방식, 즉 창의적인 뇌를 사용하는 것이 효과적이라고 제안하며, 다르게 생각하는 것이 창의성의 핵심임을 강조하고 있습니다. 따라서 제목으로는 5번 '다르게 생각하기: 창의성을 향한 첫걸음'이 가장 적합합니다.
options_translation: ① 새로운 아이디어를 찾는 똑똑한 방법들
② 논리적 사고의 중요성
③ 논리적 사고가 창의성에 미치는 영향
④ 문제 해결하기: 친숙한 경험을 통해
⑤ 다르게 생각하기: 창의성을 향한 첫걸음

questions.question: 15. 다음 글의 내용과 일치하지 않는 것은? (2.9점)
questions.passage: The responsive behavior of dogs also caught the attention of an evolutionary anthropologist, Brian Hare. He conducted an experiment to see how dogs would respond to human gestures compared to wolves, who share the same common ancestor. He placed two cups on the ground with food hidden under only one of them. When he pointed to the cup with the food, the dogs found it easily. The wolves, however, struggled and chose cups at random, paying no attention to his gestures. Dr. Hare concluded that the dogs' ability to read human gestures allowed them to perform better than the wolves. He explained that dogs, unlike wolves, have developed communicative skills with humans and a sense of friendliness. This explanation sounds reasonable according to several evolutionary biologists. They say that from the common ancestors of these two species, those that acted friendly toward humans evolved into dogs, and those that didn't became wolves. Furthermore, Dr. Hare suggested that the friendly nature of dogs probably provided them a survival advantage that allowed their population to grow larger than that of wolves.
options: ① Brian Hare는 개와 늑대가 인간의 몸짓에 어떻게 반응하는지 실험을 했다.
② 음식이 담겨있는 컵을 가리킬 때 개는 쉽게 찾았지만 늑대는 찾는데 어려움을 겪었다.
③ 개는 늑대와 달리 인간과의 소통능력과 친근함에 대한 감각을 발달시켜왔다.
④ 개와 늑대는 조상이 같지만 인간과 친하지 않는 존재들은 늑대가 되었다.
⑤ 개의 친근한 특성 때문에 개의 개체 수는 점점 줄어들게 되었다.
questions.explanation: 지문의 마지막 문장에서 개의 친근한 본성이 개체 수를 늑대보다 더 크게 늘어나게(grow larger) 하는 생존상의 이점을 제공했을 것이라고 언급하고 있습니다. 따라서 개의 개체 수가 점점 줄어들게 되었다는 5번의 설명은 지문의 내용과 정면으로 배치됩니다.

questions.question: 【16~18】 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 어법상 틀린 것을 고르시오. 18. (3.5점)
questions.passage: Friction is a force between two surfaces that are sliding, or trying to slide, across each other. For example, when you try to push a book along the floor, friction makes this ① <u>difficult</u>. Friction always works in the direction opposite to the direction ② <u>which</u> the object is moving, or trying to move. Friction always slows a moving object down. The amount of friction ③ <u>depends</u> on the surface materials. The rougher the surface is, the more friction is ④ <u>produced</u>. Friction also produces heat. If you rub your hands together quickly, they will get warmer. Friction can be a useful force because it prevents our shoes from slipping on the pavement when we walk and stops car tires from skidding on the road. When you walk, friction is caused between the tread on shoes and the ground, acting to grip the ground and ⑤ <u>prevent</u> sliding.
questions.explanation: ② 뒤의 절 'the object is moving'은 move가 자동사로 쓰여 완전한 구조이므로, 관계대명사 which 대신 관계부사 where나 전치사+관계대명사인 in which를 사용해야 합니다.

questions.question: 【19~21】 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것을 고르시오. 19. (3.3점)
questions.passage: The basic science we learn in grade school is a body of ① <u>knowledge</u> about the natural world - the earth goes around the sun, DNA carries the information of an organism, and so on. Only when you start to learn the practice of science do you realize that each of these "facts" was hard won through a succession of ② <u>well-founded</u> inferences based upon many observations or experiments. The process of science is less about collecting pieces of knowledge than it is about ③ <u>worsening</u> the uncertainties in what we know. Our uncertainties can be greater or lesser for any given piece of ④ <u>finding</u> depending upon where we are in that process. Today, we are not ⑤ <u>uncertain</u> about how an apple will fall from a tree, but our understanding of the turbulent fluid flow remains a work in progress after more than a century of effort.
questions.explanation: 과학의 과정은 지식을 수집하는 것보다 우리가 아는 것 속의 불확실성을 '줄이는' 것 또는 '정제하는' 것에 더 가깝습니다. 따라서 worsening(악화시키는)은 문맥상 어색하며 refining 혹은 reducing 같은 단어가 적절합니다.

questions.question: 21. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은? [3.6점]
questions.passage: Our skin conducts electricity more or less efficiently, depending on our emotions. We know that when we're emotionally ① provoked - stressed, sad, any intense emotion, really - our bodies sweat a tiny bit, so little we might not even notice. And when those tiny drops of sweat appear, our skin gets ② less electrically conductive. This change in sweat gland activity happens completely without your conscious mind having much say in the matter. If you feel emotionally intense, you're going to notice a ③ growth in sweat gland activity. This is particularly useful from a scientific viewpoint, because it allows us to put an objective value on a subjective state of mind. We can actually measure your emotional state by tracking how your body ④ subconsciously sweats, by running a bit of electricity through your skin. We can then turn the subjective, subconscious experience of emotional intensity into an ⑤ objective number by figuring out how good your skin gets at transferring an electrical current.
questions.explanation: 감정적으로 자극을 받을 때 우리 몸에서는 미세하게 땀이 나는데, 이 땀 방울이 나타나면 피부의 전기 전도성이 낮아지는 것이 아니라 높아지게 됩니다. 땀(수분)은 전기를 잘 전달하기 때문입니다. 따라서 ②의 less는 more 또는 higher 등으로 고쳐야 문맥상 적절합니다.

questions.question: 25. 다음 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것을 고르시오. (4.3점)
questions.passage:
The rise of air-conditioning accelerated the construction of sealed boxes, where the building's only airflow is through the filtered ducts of the air-conditioning unit. It doesn't have to be this way. Look at any old building in a hot climate, whether it's in Sicily or Marrakesh or Tehran. Architects understood the importance of shade, airflow, light colors. They oriented buildings to capture cool breezes and block the worst heat of the afternoon. They built with thick walls and white roofs and transoms over doors to encourage airflow. Anyone who has ever spent a few minutes in a mudbrick house in Tucson, or walked on the narrow streets of old Seville, knows how well these construction methods work. Despite being the product of centuries of hands-on experience, ___________________________________________. In this light, air-conditioning isn't merely a tool for comfort - it also represents a kind of technological amnesia.

* amnesia: 기억상실
options: ① people have stopped using air-conditioning altogether
② modern architects always follow these traditional methods
③ this style of construction has recently become more popular
④ this ancient knowledge is still the basis of most new buildings today
⑤ this hard-earned knowledge about managing heat is frequently overlooked
questions.explanation: 이 글은 에어컨의 보급으로 인해 과거 사람들이 더운 기후에서 견디기 위해 고안해낸 건축학적 지혜(그늘, 통풍, 두꺼운 벽 등)가 잊히고 있다는 점을 지적하고 있습니다. 지문 마지막의 'technological amnesia(기술적 기억상실)'라는 표현은 과거의 유용한 지식이 더 이상 활용되지 않음을 의미하므로, 빈칸에는 열 관리와 관련된 힘들게 얻은 지식이 자주 간과된다는 내용의 ⑤번이 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 사람들은 에어컨 사용을 완전히 중단했다
② 현대 건축가들은 항상 이러한 전통적인 방식들을 따른다
③ 이러한 건축 양식은 최근에 더 인기를 얻고 있다
④ 이 고대 지식은 오늘날 여전히 대부분의 신축 건물의 기초가 된다
⑤ 열을 관리하는 것에 관한 이 힘들게 얻은 지식은 자주 간과된다

questions.question: 26. 다음 글에서 전체 흐름과 관계 없는 문장은? (3.9점)
questions.passage: As you listen to your child in an emotional moment, be aware that sharing simple observations usually works better than asking questions to get a conversation rolling. You may ask your child "Why do you feel sad?" and she may not have a clue. As a child, she may not have an answer on the tip of her tongue. ① Maybe she's feeling sad about her parents' arguments because she feels overtired, or she's worried about a piano recital. ② But she may or may not be able to explain any of this and even when she does come up with an answer, she might be worried that the answer is not good enough to justify the feeling. ③ Children develop better emotional regulation when their parents who do not tolerate unruliness model appropriate behavior. ④ Under these circumstances, a series of questions can just make a child silent. ⑤ It's better to simply reflect what you notice, such as "You seem a little tired today." or "I noticed that you frowned when I mentioned the recital." and wait for her response.
questions.explanation: 본문은 아이가 감정적인 상태일 때 질문을 퍼붓기보다 부모가 관찰한 내용을 단순하게 말해주는 것이 대화를 이끌어내는 데 더 효과적이라는 대화 기법에 대해 설명하고 있습니다. 반면 ③번 문장은 부모가 무질서함을 용인하지 않고 적절한 행동의 모범을 보일 때 정서 조절 능력이 발달한다는 내용으로, 대화의 기술이라는 중심 소재에서 벗어나 훈육과 정서 발달의 상관관계를 다루고 있으므로 흐름상 적절하지 않습니다.

questions.question: [31~32] 주어진 글 다음에 이어질 글의 순서로 가장 적절한 것을 고르시오. 31. (2.9점)
questions.passage: Just before noon, we arrived at a small town called Murupara. "Where do we go now?" I asked Nani. He did not reply, but he was staring at the small houses. Then, at a street corner, he told us to turn. After turning the corner, we saw an old man standing in front of a house.
ordered_passages: (A) I felt as if people from the past were looking over the shoulders of the two old men to see if the work was correct. Finally, they stopped. It was done. After a moment of silence, the old man whispered to Nani, "Goodbye, friend." Crying, they pressed their noses together to say goodbye.

(B) He welcomed Nani Tama with a gentle smile, but in his eyes, I saw the message, "We must hurry." I remember the two old men sitting at the table and the soft sounds of the Maori words as they talked. All through the quiet afternoon and into the evening, they recalled missing names. I had a strange feeling that there were other people in the room.

(C) It was early morning and still dark when we returned to Auntie's place. All the lights were on, and the village people were waiting for us. Smiling, Nani Tama lifted up the whakapapa and offered it to the village. Our Nani Tama smiled again. His smile grew tired. He sighed. "At last, I may go now."
questions.explanation: 박스 글에서 Murupara 마을에 도착하여 한 노인을 만나는 장면이 제시됩니다. (B)에서 그 노인이 Nani Tama를 환영하며 테이블에 앉아 마오리어로 이름을 기억해내는(족보 작업) 과정이 시작됩니다. (A)에서 이 작업이 마무리되고, 조상들이 지켜보는 듯한 느낌 속에서 작별 인사(hongi)를 나누는 장면으로 이어집니다. 마지막으로 (C)에서 다음 날 새벽 마을로 돌아와 완성된 whakapapa(족보)를 전달하고 안도하는 모습으로 끝나는 것이 논리적입니다.

questions.question: 32. (3.0점)
questions.passage: Plants can communicate, although not in the same way we do. Some express their discontent through scents. You know that smell that hangs in the air after you've mowed the lawn?
ordered_passages: (A) Yeah, that's actually an SOS. Some plants use sound. Yes, sound, though at a frequency that we can't hear. Researchers experimented with plants and microphones to see if they could record any trouble calls.

(B) However, it's worth noting that experts don't think plants are crying out in pain. It's more likely that these reactions are knee-jerk survival actions. Plants are living organisms, and their main objective is to survive. Scents and sounds are their tools for defending against things that might harm them.

(C) They found that plants produce a high-frequency clicking noise when stressed and can make different sounds for different stressors. The sound a plant makes when it's not getting watered differs from the one it'll make when a leaf is cut.
questions.explanation: (A)의 'Yeah, that's actually an SOS'는 주어진 글에서 언급된 잔디 깎는 냄새(smell)에 대한 직접적인 대답이며 소리(sound)를 통한 의사소통을 새로 소개한다. (C)는 (A)에서 언급된 실험의 구체적 결과(고주파 클릭 소리)와 스트레스 상황에 따른 다른 소리에 대해 설명한다. 마지막으로 (B)는 'However'를 통해 이러한 소리가 고통의 호소라기보다는 생존을 위한 본능적 방어 수단이라는 전문가들의 견해를 제시하며 내용을 마무리한다. 따라서 가장 적절한 순서는 (A)-(C)-(B)이다.

questions.question: 12. 밑줄 친 "<u>The hands speak what the lips cannot.</u>"가 다음 글에서 의미하는 바로 가장 적절한 것은? (3.1점)
questions.passage: When we realize we've said something in error and we pause to go back to correct it, we stop gesturing a couple of hundred milliseconds before we stop speaking. Such sequences suggest the startling notion that our hands "know" what we're going to say before our conscious minds do, and in fact this is often the case. As the old saying goes, "<u>The hands speak what the lips cannot.</u>" Gesture can mentally prime a word so that the right term comes to our lips. When people are prevented from gesturing, they talk less fluently; their speech becomes halting because their hands are no longer able to supply them with the next word, and the next. Not being able to gesture has other deleterious effects: without gesture to help our mental processes along, we remember less useful information, we solve problems less well, and we are less able to explain our thinking. Far from tagging along as speech's clumsy companion, gesture represents the leading edge of our thought.
options: ① Hand movements are a cultural form of communication unique to sign language users.
② Gestures play a vital role in expressing thoughts that are not yet fully verbalized.
③ Gestures replace language completely in situations requiring fast reactions.
④ The use of hands in speech is a learned habit with real cognitive impact.
⑤ People use hand gestures only when they are unable to speak out loud.
questions.explanation: 지문은 제스처가 우리가 말하고자 하는 것을 의식적으로 인지하기 전부터 알고 있으며, 적절한 단어가 입 밖으로 나오도록 돕는 역할을 한다고 설명합니다. 따라서 '손이 입이 할 수 없는 것을 말한다'는 의미는 아직 완전히 언어화되지 않은 생각을 표현하는 데 제스처가 중요한 역할을 한다는 ②번이 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 손 움직임은 수어 사용자들에게 고유한 문화적 의사소통 형태이다.
② 제스처는 아직 완전히 언어화되지 않은 생각을 표현하는 데 필수적인 역할을 한다.
③ 빠른 반응이 필요한 상황에서 제스처는 언어를 완전히 대체한다.
④ 말할 때 손을 사용하는 것은 실제적인 인지적 영향을 미치는 학습된 습관이다.
⑤ 사람들은 큰 소리로 말할 수 없을 때만 손동작을 사용한다.

questions.question: 13. (2.7점) 다음 글의 요지로 가장 적절한 것을 고르시오.
questions.passage: Despite the difference between the past and the future, between what has happened and what is to come, it can be suggested, that our sense of the past has always been influenced by our view of the future. Revolutionaries have always looked to the past to frame their future cause, as is amply illustrated by examples from nationalism to communism. The future has often been seen as variously a recovery of a lost time, as a replication of what is established, or as a model bequeathed by a heroic age long gone. The writing of history is based on understanding or explaining future outcomes that were not known to contemporaries, since the historian has the benefit of hindsight and the past is nothing more than the accumulation of futures that are now our past. So, rather than see the hand of the past always shaping the future, perhaps it can be seen in reverse, with the past - in the sense of our understanding of it - being shaped by our orientation to the future.
options: ① 인류의 역사는 과거의 사건들이 축적되어 이루어진다.
② 미래에 대한 관점이 과거에 대한 인식에 영향을 줄 수 있다.
③ 미래 사회의 개혁은 과거에 대한 이해를 바탕으로 설계된다.
④ 과거의 역사를 참고하여 오늘의 현실에 대한 교훈을 얻을 수 있다.
⑤ 과거와 미래의 사건 사이의 관계는 다양한 관점에서 서술해야 한다.
questions.explanation: 이 글은 과거가 미래를 형성하는 것뿐만 아니라, 미래에 대한 우리의 관점이 과거를 이해하고 구성하는 방식에 영향을 미친다는 역방향의 관계를 설명하고 있으므로 ②번이 요지로 가장 적절합니다.

questions.question: 14. (2.3점) 다음 글의 요지로 가장 적절한 것을 고르시오.
questions.passage: In 1900, at the close of the first decade in which electric systems had become a practical alternative for manufacturers, less than 5 percent of the power used in factories came from electricity. But the technological advances of suppliers made electric systems and electric motors ever more affordable and reliable, and the suppliers' intensive marketing programs also sped the adoption of the new technology. Further accelerating the shift was the rapid expansion in the number of skilled electrical engineers, who provided the expertise needed to install and run the new systems. In short order, electric power had gone from exotic to commonplace.
options: ① 1900년대 초 공장 동력의 대부분을 전기가 차지했다.
② 전기 공급업체들은 마케팅보다는 모터 개발에 집중했다.
③ 숙련된 전기공학자 부족으로 전기시스템 보급이 지연되었다.
④ 높은 사용료로 인해 제조업체들의 전기시스템 이용이 저조했다.
⑤ 기술발전과 전문인력의 증가로 전기동력이 빠르게 보급되었다.
questions.explanation: 글의 후반부에서 공급업체의 기술 발전, 마케팅, 그리고 숙련된 전기 공학자의 증가 덕분에 전기 동력이 생소한 것에서 흔한 것으로 빠르게 보급되었다고 설명하고 있으므로 ⑤번이 가장 적절합니다.

questions.question: 20. (3.1점) 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 어법상 틀린 것을 고르시오.
questions.passage: Commitment is the glue ① <u>holding</u> together characteristically human forms of social life. Commitments make individuals' behavior predictable in the face of fluctuations in their desires and interests, thereby ② <u>facilitated</u> the planning and coordination of joint actions involving multiple agents. Moreover, commitments make people willing ③ <u>to perform</u> actions that they would not otherwise perform. For example, a taxi driver ④ <u>picks up</u> his clients and transports them to their desired destination because they are committed to paying them afterwards for the service, and a construction worker performs her job every day because her employer has made a credible commitment to pay her at the end of the month. Indeed, the taxi driver and the construction worker are willing to accept money as payment only because a network of other agents (notably the central bank) is committed to ⑤ <u>taking</u> various measures to sustain the currency in question. Thus, social objects and institutions such as government, scientific collaborations, jobs, money and marriage depend for their origin and stability upon the credibility of commitments.
questions.explanation: ②번 facilitated는 분사구문의 역할을 하며 문맥상 '공동 행위의 계획과 조정을 용이하게 한다'는 능동의 의미를 나타내야 하므로 현재분사인 facilitating으로 고쳐야 합니다.

questions.question: 28. (3.1점) 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: The prominence of the social dimension in food writing might suggest that the flavor of food is taking a back seat. I suspect that most people view flavor as of secondary importance in social settings where food is served. Although our social gatherings come together around food, the meaning of these gatherings does not seem to depend on flavor. Flavor assists with the narrow purpose of filling the belly, and once that is accomplished it provides the backdrop for whatever social dynamics characterize the gathering. These can be understood independently of the flavor of the food on offer, the appreciation of which is understood to be personal and subjective. According to this conventional wisdom, the ceremonies and rituals around food, the social events that supply food with its meaning, __________________________________ . To focus excessively on flavor is to miss the larger significance of these social relations.
options: ① are shaped by the sensory pleasure of food
② highlight the complexity of personal taste preferences
③ reinforce the idea that food's role is to satisfy hunger
④ are not necessarily influenced by the taste experience itself
⑤ show that flavor appreciation is central to human interaction
questions.explanation: 이 글은 음식의 '맛'보다는 음식을 둘러싼 '사회적 차원'이 더 중요하게 여겨진다는 통념을 설명하고 있습니다. 맛은 단지 배를 채우는 좁은 목적을 도울 뿐이며, 음식과 관련된 의식이나 사회적 이벤트는 맛 그 자체와는 독립적으로 이해될 수 있다는 내용이므로 ④번 '반드시 맛 경험 자체에 의해 영향을 받는 것은 아니다'가 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 음식의 감각적 즐거움에 의해 형성된다
② 개인적 취향 선호도의 복잡성을 강조한다
③ 음식의 역할은 배고픔을 충족시키는 것이라는 생각을 강화한다
④ 반드시 맛 경험 자체에 의해 영향을 받는 것은 아니다
⑤ 맛 감상이 인간 상호작용의 중심이라는 것을 보여준다

questions.question: 30. (3.1점) 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: According to the Food and Agriculture Organization (FAO), food security means that all individuals have secure "access to adequate safe and nutritious food to maintain a healthy life." The governments of virtually every country on the planet attach great importance to achieving food security and a wide variety of mechanisms have been developed to realize this goal. The first issue governments face in achieving national food security is the problem of ensuring that adequate amounts of food are available to the resident population. Some governments have set goals of food self-sufficiency, which means most if not all of the food available in a country comes from the domestic farming system. However, food security does not require food self-sufficiency because countries can import food items not easily produced within the country. Agricultural products are, after all, highly sensitive to climatic, soil and other conditions that tend to vary around the world. Even countries with extremely productive agricultural sectors are not fully self-sufficient in all food items. In general, the problem of assuring adequate food supplies is solved by relying on both domestic production and imports, which leads governments to intensely get __________________________________ and to promote domestic production.
options: ① interested in selective breeding in farming
② devoted to ensuring the safety of domestic food
③ independent in controlling agricultural produce
④ involved in encouragement to international trade
⑤ eager to increase crop yield to supply sufficient food
questions.explanation: 식량 안보는 자국 내 생산(self-sufficiency)만으로는 달성하기 어려운데, 이는 농산물이 기후나 토양 등에 민감하여 모든 품목을 자급자족할 수 없기 때문입니다. 따라서 정부는 식량 공급을 보장하기 위해 국내 생산을 장려하는 동시에 '수입(imports)'에 의존하게 되며, 이는 국제 무역을 장려하는 결과로 이어집니다. 따라서 ④번 '국제 무역 장려에 참여하게 한다'가 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 농업의 선택적 육종에 관심을 갖게 한다
② 국내 식품의 안전성을 보장하는 데 헌신하게 한다
③ 농산물 통제에 있어 독립적이게 한다
④ 국제 무역 장려에 참여하게 한다
⑤ 충분한 식량 공급을 위해 작물 수확량을 늘리는 데 열성적이게 한다

questions.question: 37.글의 흐름으로 보아, 주어진 문장이 들어가기에 가장 적절한 곳을 고르시오.
questions.passage: Great scientists are seldom one-hit wonders. Newton is prime example: beyond the Newtonian mechanics, he developed the theory of gravitation, calculus, laws of motion and optimization. ( ① ) In fact, well-known scientists are often involved in multiple discoveries, a phenomenon potentially explained by the Matthew effect. ( ② ) Indeed, an initial success may offer a scientist legitimacy, improve peer perception, provide knowledge of how to score and win, enhance social status, and attract resources and quality collaborators, all of these payoffs further increasing her odds of scoring a later win. ( ③ ) Yet, there is an appealing alternative explanation: Great scientists have multiple hits and consistently succeed in their scientific endeavors simply because they're exceptionally talented. ( ④ ) The Matthew effect posits that success itself increases the future probability of success, raising the question: Does status dictate outcomes, or does it simply reflect underlying talent or quality? ( ⑤ ) In other words, is it really a Matthew effect after all?
questions.insertion_sentence: Therefore, future success again goes to those who have had success earlier, not because of advantages offered by the previous success, but because the earlier success was indicative of a hidden talent.
questions.explanation: 본문은 과학자의 지속적인 성공을 설명하는 두 가지 관점(마태 효과 vs. 타고난 재능)을 다룹니다. 주어진 문장은 성공이 이전의 이점 때문이 아니라 '숨겨진 재능'을 나타내기 때문이라는 결론을 담고 있습니다. 이는 ④번 문장에서 던진 질문(지위가 결과를 결정하는가, 재능을 반영하는가?)에 대한 후자의 답변에 해당하며, ⑤번 뒤의 '즉, 이것이 정말 마태 효과인가?'라는 의문과 논리적으로 연결됩니다.

questions.question: 8. 글의 흐름으로 보아, 주어진 문장이 들어가기에 가장 적절한 곳은? [3.9점]
questions.passage: Plants can communicate, although not in the same way we do. Some express their discontent through scents. You know that smell that hangs in the air after you've mowed the lawn? Yeah, that's actually an SOS. Some plants use sound. ( ① ) Yes, sound, though at a frequency that we can't hear. ( ② ) Researchers experimented with plants and microphones to see if they could record any trouble calls. ( ③ ) They found that plants produce a high-frequency clicking noise when stressed and can make different sounds for different stressors. ( ④ ) The sound a plant makes when it's not getting watered differs from the one it'll make when a leaf is cut. ( ⑤ ) It's more likely that these reactions are knee-jerk survival actions. Plants are living organisms, and their main objective is to survive. Scents and sounds are their tools for defending against things that might harm them.
questions.insertion_sentence: However, it's worth noting that experts don't think plants are crying out in pain.
questions.explanation: 주어진 문장은 식물이 고통으로 비명을 지르는 것은 아니라는 내용이다. ⑤번 뒤 문장에서 '이러한 반응들은 무릎 반사적인 생존 행동일 가능성이 더 높다'고 설명하며 삽입 문장의 내용을 뒷받침하고 있으므로 ⑤번 위치가 가장 적절하다.

questions.question: 9. 글의 흐름으로 보아, 주어진 문장이 들어가기에 가장 적절한 곳은? [3.9점]
questions.passage: Plato argued that when you see something that strikes you as beautiful, you are really just seeing a partial reflection of true beauty, just as a painting or even a photograph only captures part of the real thing. True beauty, or what Plato calls the Form of Beauty, has no particular color, shape, or size. ( ① ) Rather, it is an abstract idea, like the number five. ( ② ) You can make drawings of the number five in blue or red ink, big or small, but the number five itself is none of those things. ( ③ ) It has no physical form. ( ④ ) Although it has no particular color or size, it somehow lies within each and every triangle you see. ( ⑤ ) Plato thought the same was true of beauty. The Form of Beauty somehow lies within each and every beautiful thing you see.
questions.insertion_sentence: Think of the idea of a triangle, for example.
questions.explanation: 주어진 문장은 삼각형의 개념을 예로 들어보라는 내용이다. ④번 뒤의 문장에서 '그것은 특정한 색이나 크기가 없지만, 당신이 보는 모든 삼각형 내부에 존재한다'라고 언급하며 삼각형의 개념에 대해 설명하고 있으므로, 삼각형의 예시를 처음 도입하는 주어진 문장은 ④번에 들어가는 것이 가장 적절하다.

questions.question: 11. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은? [5.5점]
questions.passage: The rise of air-conditioning ① <u>accelerated</u> the construction of sealed boxes, where the building's only airflow is through the filtered ducts of the air-conditioning unit. It doesn't have to be this way. Look at any old building in a hot climate, whether it's in Sicily or Marrakesh or Tehran. Architects understood the ② <u>importance</u> of shade, airflow, light colors. They oriented buildings to capture cool breezes and block the worst heat of the afternoon. They built with thick walls and white roofs and transoms over doors to ③ <u>discourage</u> airflow. Anyone who has ever spent a few minutes in a mudbrick house in Tucson, or walked on the narrow streets of old Seville, knows how well these construction methods ④ <u>work</u>. But all this wisdom about how to deal with heat, accumulated over centuries of practical experience, is all too often ⑤ <u>ignored</u>. In this sense, air-conditioning is not just a technology of personal comfort; it is also a technology of forgetting.
questions.explanation: 더운 기후의 전통 건축가들은 그늘, 공기 흐름, 밝은 색상의 중요성을 이해하고 건물을 설계했다. 문 위의 환기창(transoms)은 공기 흐름을 막는(discourage) 것이 아니라 공기 흐름을 장려하거나 원활하게 하기 위한 것이므로 encourage 등의 단어가 적절하다.

questions.question: 12. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은? [4.2점]
questions.passage: Our skin conducts electricity more or less ① <u>efficiently</u>, depending on our emotions. We know that when we're emotionally stimulated-stressed, sad, any intense emotion, really-our bodies sweat a tiny bit, so little we might not even notice. And when those tiny drops of sweat appear, our skin gets more electrically ② <u>conductive</u>. This change in sweat gland activity happens completely without your conscious mind having much say in the matter. If you feel emotionally ③ <u>weak</u>, you're going to notice an increase in sweat gland activity. This is particularly useful from a scientific viewpoint, because it ④ <u>allows</u> us to put an objective value on a subjective state of mind. We can actually measure your emotional state by tracking how your body subconsciously sweats, by running a bit of electricity through your skin. We can then turn the subjective ⑤ <u>subconscious</u> experience of emotional intensity into an objective number by figuring out how good your skin gets at transferring an electrical current.
questions.explanation: 이 글은 감정적으로 자극을 받거나 강렬한 감정(intense emotion)을 느낄 때 피부의 전기 전도율이 높아진다는 내용이다. 따라서 ③번의 weak(약한)는 문맥상 적절하지 않으며, 'intense' 혹은 'stimulated'와 같이 감정적으로 고조된 상태를 나타내는 단어가 와야 한다.

questions.question: 13. 다음 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은? [4.2점]
questions.passage: Improving your gestural communication involves more than just knowing when to nod or shake hands. It's about using gestures to complement your spoken messages, adding layers of meaning to your words. Open-handed gestures, for example, can indicate honesty, creating an atmosphere of trust. You invite openness and collaboration when you speak with your palms facing up. This simple yet powerful gesture can make others feel more comfortable and willing to engage in conversation. But be careful of the trap of over-gesturing. Too many hand movements can distract from your message, drawing attention away from your words. Imagine a speaker whose hands move quickly like birds, their message lost in the chaos of their gestures. <u>Balance is key</u>. ___________ not overshadow them.
options: ① Your voices should match your gestures
② Your gestures should highlight your words
③ Your emotions should control the audience
④ Your imaginations should reflect your actions
⑤ Your appearances should match your profession
questions.explanation: 이 글은 효과적인 몸짓 의사소통을 위해서는 몸짓이 말을 보완하고 강조해야 하며, 말을 가리거나 방해해서는 안 된다는 균형의 중요성을 강조하고 있습니다. 빈칸 바로 뒤의 'not overshadow them(말을 가리지 않아야 한다)'과 조화를 이루면서 균형의 중요성을 설명하는 문구는 '제스처가 말을 강조해야 한다'는 ②번입니다.
options_translation: ① 목소리가 제스처와 일치해야 한다
② 제스처가 말을 강조해야 한다
③ 감정이 청중을 조절해야 한다
④ 상상이 행동을 반영해야 한다
⑤ 외모가 직업과 어울려야 한다

questions.question: 16. 다음 글에서 전체 흐름과 관계 없는 문장은? [4.2점]
questions.passage: Modern brain-scanning techniques such as fMRI (functional Magnetic Resonance Imaging) have revealed that reading aloud lights up many areas of the brain. ① There is intense activity in areas associated with pronunciation and hearing the sound of the spoken response, which strengthens the connective structures of your brain cells for more brainpower. ② This leads to an overall improvement in concentration. ③ Reading aloud is also a good way to develop your public speaking skills because it forces you to read each and every word-something people don't often do when reading quickly, or reading in silence. ④ Still many people prefer to listen to audiobook because it saves time. ⑤ Children, in particular, should be encouraged to read aloud because the brain is wired for learning through connections that are created by positive stimulation, such as singing, touching, and reading aloud.
questions.explanation: 이 글은 소리 내어 읽기(reading aloud)가 뇌 활동을 활성화시키고 집중력과 말하기 기술을 향상시킨다는 긍정적인 효과에 대해 설명하고 있습니다. 하지만 ④번 문장은 오디오북을 듣는 것이 시간을 절약해 주기 때문에 선호된다는 내용으로, 소리 내어 읽기의 뇌 과학적/교육적 이점이라는 전체 흐름에서 벗어납니다.

questions.question: 18. 다음 글에서 전체 흐름과 관계 없는 문장은? [2.8점]
questions.passage: <u>Promotion deals with consumer psychology. We can't force people to think one way or another, and the clever marketer knows that promotion is used to provide information in the most clear, honest, and simple fashion possible. By doing so, the possibility of increasing sales goes up. Gone are the days when promotions were done in order to fool the consumer into purchasing something.</u> ① The long-term effect of getting a consumer to buy something they did not really want or need wasn't good. ② In fact, consumers fooled once can do damage to sales as they relate their experience to others. ③ So, extreme promotional products are needed to meet the requirements of dissatisfied customers. ④ Instead, marketers now know that their goal is to identify the consumers who are most likely to appreciate a good or service, and to promote that good or service in a way that makes the value clear to the consumer. ⑤ Therefore, marketers must know where the potential consumers are, and how to reach them.
questions.explanation: 이 글은 현대의 판촉(promotion)이 소비자를 속이는 것이 아니라 정보를 정직하게 전달하고 적합한 소비자를 찾는 과정이어야 한다는 내용을 담고 있습니다. ③번 문장은 '불만족한 고객의 요구를 충족시키기 위해 극단적인 판촉 상품이 필요하다'는 내용으로 글의 흐름과 관련이 없습니다.

questions.question: 20. 주어진 글 다음에 이어질 글의 순서로 가장 적절한 것은? [3.9점]
questions.passage: There is a wealth of evidence that when parents, teachers, supervisors, and coaches are perceived as involved and caring, people feel happier and more motivated.
ordered_passages: (A) So exercise with a friend, call someone when you have a difficult decision to make, and be there as a support for others as they take on challenges.

(B) If we are trying to <u>motivate</u> others, a caring relationship is a <u>crucial basis</u> from which to begin. And when we are trying to motivate ourselves, doing things to enhance a sense of connectedness to others can be crucial to long-term persistence.

(C) And it is not just those people with power; we need to feel valued and respected by peers and coworkers. Thus, when the need for relatedness is met, motivation and internalization are fueled, provided that support for <u>autonomy</u> and competence are also there.
questions.explanation: 주어진 글에서 권위 있는 사람(부모, 교사 등)의 보살핌이 동기부여에 중요하다는 점을 언급한 후, (C)에서 권력자뿐만 아니라 동료들로부터 존중받는 것의 중요성을 이어받으며 관계 맺기(relatedness)의 필요성을 강조합니다. (B)에서 타인과 자신을 동기부여할 때 관계와 유대감이 중요함을 정리하고, (A)에서 이를 실생활에 적용하는 구체적인 행동 지침(친구와 운동하기 등)을 제시하며 마무리하는 것이 자연스럽습니다.

questions.question: 21. 주어진 글 다음에 이어질 글의 순서로 가장 적절한 것은? [3.9점]
questions.passage: Routines enable athletes to evaluate competition conditions.
ordered_passages: (A) For example, bouncing a ball in a volleyball service routine supplies the server with information about the ball, the floor, and the state of her muscles. This information can then be used to properly prepare for her serve.
(B) Just like adjusting a race-car engine to the conditions of the track, air temperature, and weather, routines adjust all competitive components to achieve proper performance.

(C) Routines also enable athletes to adjust and fine-tune their preparations based on those evaluations or in pursuit of a particular competitive goal. This adaptation can involve adjustment to the conditions, rivals, competitive situation, or internal influences that can affect performance.
questions.explanation: 주어진 문장에서 루틴이 선수들로 하여금 경기 조건을 평가하게 한다고 언급한 뒤, (C)에서 'also'를 통해 평가뿐만 아니라 조정을 가능하게 한다는 내용을 연결한다. (A)는 배구 서비스 루틴을 예로 들어 (C)의 평가와 준비 과정을 구체화하며, (B)는 경주용 자동차 엔진 조절에 비유하여 전체적인 요약을 제공하는 흐름이 적절하다.

questions.question: 22. 다음 글의 내용을 한 문장으로 요약하고자 한다. 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은? [5.5점]
questions.passage: Cartilage is extremely important for the healthy functioning of a joint, especially if that joint bears weight, like your knee. Imagine for a moment that you're looking into the inner workings of your left knee as you walk down the street. When you shift your weight from your left leg to your right, the pressure on your left knee is released. The cartilage in your left knee then "drinks in" synovial fluid, in much the same way that a sponge soaks up liquid when put in water. When you take another step and transfer the weight back onto your left leg, much of the fluid squeezes out of the cartilage. This squeezing of joint fluid into and out of the cartilage helps it respond to the off-and-on pressure of walking without breaking under the pressure.
questions.summary_sentence: When walking, knee cartilage act as a (A) _________ by absorbing and releasing synovial fluid which helps it respond to (B) _________ without damaging the knee.
options: ① window ...... impact
② filter ...... constant stress
③ grease ...... changing temperature
④ spring ...... explosion
⑤ sponge ...... repeating pressure
questions.explanation: 지문에서 연골이 활액을 흡수하고 방출하는 과정을 스펀지(sponge)에 비유하고 있으며, 이러한 작용이 걷기 시 가해지는 반복적인 압력(repeating pressure/off-and-on pressure)에 대응하도록 돕는다고 설명하고 있다.
options_translation: ① 창문 ...... 충격
② 필터 ...... 지속적인 스트레스
③ 윤활유 ...... 변화하는 온도
④ 스프링 ...... 폭발
⑤ 스펀지 ...... 반복되는 압력

questions.question: <서술형 2> 다음 글에서 문맥상 빈칸에 들어갈 내용을 <보기>에 주어진 어구를 사용하여 작성하시오. [4.5점]
questions.passage: Assuming gene editing in humans proves to be safe and effective, it might seem logical, even preferable, to correct disease-causing mutations at the earliest possible stage of life, before harmful genes begin causing serious problems. Yet once it becomes possible to transform an embryo's mutated genes into "normal" ones, there will certainly be temptations to upgrade normal genes to superior versions. Should we begin editing genes in unborn children to lower their lifetime risk of heart disease or cancer? What about giving unborn children beneficial features, like greater strength and increased mental abilities, or changing physical characteristics, like eye and hair color? The pursuit for perfection seems almost natural to human nature, but if _________ we may not like where we end up.
subjective_conditions: 1. <보기>의 주어진 단어를 모두 사용할 것(단어 변형 없음)
2. 추가로 사용되는 단어 없음
vocabulary_box: slippery / start / we / down / this / slope
questions.answer: we start down this slippery slope
questions.explanation: 이 글은 유전자 편집이 질병 치료를 넘어 우수한 능력을 갖추기 위한 수단으로 변질될 수 있음을 경고하고 있습니다. 빈칸에는 '한 번 시작하면 멈추기 어려운 위험한 상황'을 의미하는 관용적 표현인 'slippery slope'를 활용하여 'we start down this slippery slope' (우리가 이 위험한 비탈길을 내려가기 시작하면)라고 작성하는 것이 문맥상 가장 적절합니다.

questions.question: 2. 다음 글의 요지로 가장 적절한 것은? [3.2점]
questions.passage: Assuming gene editing in humans proves to be safe and effective, it might seem logical, even preferable, to correct disease-causing mutations at the earliest possible stage of life, before harmful genes begin causing serious problems. Yet once it becomes possible to transform an embryo's mutated genes into "normal" ones, there will certainly be temptations to upgrade normal genes to superior versions. Should we begin editing genes in unborn children to lower their lifetime risk of heart disease or cancer? What about giving unborn children beneficial features, like greater strength and increased mental abilities, or changing physical characteristics, like eye and hair color? The pursuit for perfection seems almost natural to human nature, but if we allow genetic alterations to upgrade humans, we may find ourselves facing a future we never intended, filled with unforeseen and devastating consequences.
options: ① Gene engineering promotes overall well-being, paving the way for a healthier and more advanced world.
② Human genes have been shaped by harsh environments over successive generations due to survival instincts.
③ Gene improvement should aim to create a society where individuals' potential and social status are determined by their DNA.
④ Genetic modification in humans could prevent disease but its potential misuse for enhancing human traits may lead to unexpected and disastrous outcomes.
⑤ Genetic editing has to be encouraged as a tool for societal control, where human traits and destinies are manipulated to serve a preset system.
questions.explanation: 이 글은 유전자 편집이 질병 예방에는 유용할 수 있지만, 인간의 특성을 강화하기 위한 용도로 남용될 경우 예상치 못한 비극적인 결과를 초래할 수 있다는 경고를 담고 있습니다.
options_translation: ① 유전 공학은 전반적인 웰빙을 증진하여 더 건강하고 진보된 세상을 위한 길을 열어준다.
② 인간의 유전자는 생존 본능으로 인해 여러 세대에 걸쳐 가혹한 환경에 의해 형성되어 왔다.
③ 유전자 개선은 개인의 잠재력과 사회적 지위가 DNA에 의해 결정되는 사회를 만드는 것을 목표로 해야 한다.
④ 인간의 유전자 변형은 질병을 예방할 수 있지만, 인간의 특성을 강화하기 위한 잠재적 오용은 예상치 못한 재앙적인 결과를 초래할 수 있다.
⑤ 유전자 편집은 인간의 특성과 운명이 미리 설정된 시스템에 봉사하도록 조작되는 사회적 통제의 도구로서 장려되어야 한다.

questions.question: 5. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중 어법상 틀린 것을 있는 대로 고른 것은? [3.8점]
questions.passage: The responsive behavior of dogs caught the attention of an evolutionary anthropologist, Brian Hare. To compare how dogs and wolves responded, he conducted an experiment with two cups ⓐ<u>placed</u> on the ground and food hidden under one of them. While the dogs responded to his gestures correctly, the wolves couldn't figure out ⓑ<u>what</u> he meant by them and just guessed randomly. ⓒ<u>Concluding</u> that dogs were better at reading human gestures, Dr. Hare argued that this ability gave them an advantage. He explained that dogs, unlike wolves, have developed communicative skills with humans and a sense of friendliness. This explanation sounds reasonable according to several evolutionary biologists. They say that it is friendliness toward humans that ⓓ<u>lead</u> some species to evolve into dogs, while others become wolves. Furthermore, Dr. Hare suggested that the friendly nature of dogs likely gave them a survival advantage, allowing their behaviors to differ from ⓔ<u>that</u> of wolves that lacked such friendliness.
questions.explanation: ⓓ it-that 강조 구문에서 강조되는 주어 'friendliness toward humans'가 단수이므로 동사는 leads가 적절합니다. ⓔ 비교 대상인 'their behaviors'가 복수이므로 대명사는 that이 아닌 those로 써야 합니다.

questions.question: 7. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중 어법상 틀린 것을 고르시오. [3.6점]
questions.passage: Promotion deals with consumer psychology. We can't make people ①<u>think</u> one way or another, and the clever marketer knows that promotion is used to provide information in the most clear, honest, and simple fashion possible. By doing so, the possibility of increasing sales ②<u>rises</u>. Gone are the days when promotions were done in order to fool the consumer into purchasing something. The long-term effect of getting a consumer to buy something they did not really want or need wasn't good. In fact, consumers ③<u>misleading</u> once can do damage to sales as they relate their experience to others. Instead, marketers now know that their goal is to identify the consumers who are most ④<u>likely</u> to appreciate a good or service, and to promote that good or service in a way that makes the value clear to the consumer. Therefore, marketers must know the places ⑤<u>where</u> the potential consumers can be found, and how to reach them.
questions.explanation: 주어인 'consumers'를 수식하는 분사 자리인데, 소비자가 '속임을 당한' 것이라는 수동의 의미가 되어야 하므로 현재분사인 misleading을 과거분사인 misled로 고쳐야 합니다.

questions.question: 8. 주어진 글 (A)에 이어질 내용을 순서에 맞게 배열한 것으로 가장 적절한 것은? [3.3점]
questions.passage: Human survival and success have long fascinated scientists and historians. One of the most important questions is how Homo sapiens, our species, managed to survive for so long. Both species lived at the same time until about 40,000 years ago, and in many ways, Neanderthals appeared to have the upper hand.
ordered_passages:
(B)
What truly distinguished Homo sapiens was their ability to build strong social connections. (a) <u>They</u> were better at cooperating, sharing food and knowledge, and helping one another in times of need, unlike Neanderthals. These social behaviors allowed them to adapt more quickly and effectively to changes in (b) <u>their</u> environment. Living in larger groups also encouraged communication and learning, which helped ideas spread and develop.

(C)
They were known to be intelligent and physically superior to Homo sapiens. Neanderthals were able to make tools and fire and had strong bodies with well-developed muscles and broad shoulders. These qualities made (c) <u>them</u> well suited for survival in harsh environments. However, physical strength and intelligence alone were not enough to ensure long-term survival.

(D)
Neanderthals, on the other hand, often lived in smaller and more isolated groups, which limited their ability to share ideas or support one another. These social differences may have given Homo sapiens a major advantage. Over time, (d) <u>they</u> were better able to survive challenges, pass on useful knowledge, and build more complex societies. In the end, it was this ability to live and work together that helped (e) <u>them</u> not just survive, but thrive.
questions.explanation: (A)의 마지막 문장에서 네안데르탈인이 우위에 있었다는 점을 언급하므로, 네안데르탈인의 강점을 설명하는 (C)가 오는 것이 적절하다. (C)의 마지막에서 육체적 힘과 지능만으로는 부족했다는 한계를 지적하고, (B)에서 호모 사피엔스의 차별점인 사회적 관계 능력을 소개한다. 마지막으로 (D)에서 네안데르탈인과 대조하며 호모 사피엔스의 승리 요인을 요약하며 마무리하는 것이 자연스럽다.

questions.question: 9. 주어진 밑줄 친 (a) ~ (e) 중에서 가리키는 대상이 나머지 넷과 다른 것은? [2.9점]

options: ① (a)
② (b)

questions.explanation: (a), (b), (d), (e)는 모두 Homo sapiens를 가리키지만, (c)는 맥락상 신체적으로 우월했던 Neanderthals를 가리킨다.

questions.question: 14. [3.7점] 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 문맥상 표현의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것을 고르시오.
questions.passage: Dr. Hare and his colleagues designed an experiment with chimpanzees and bonobos to examine how they behave in cooperative situations. Dr. Hare's team set up a device which required two individuals to pull both ends of a rope at the same time in order to access food on a board. Although the two species are genetically alike, they show clear ① <u>distinctions</u> in their behavior and approach to cooperation. Chimpanzees were usually successful only when working with familiar individuals, and they rarely ② <u>distributed</u> the food once they got it. On the other hand, the bonobos in the study were more willing to ③ <u>assist</u> each other and often shared the food with their partners. Their ability to work with both familiar and unfamiliar individuals showed strong social skills. Experts believe that this ④ <u>cooperative</u> behavior helped bonobos adapt more successfully to social challenges over time. This difference in behavior suggests how certain social traits, such as flexibility in interactions, can shape a species' progress in ways that ultimately lead to ⑤ <u>decline</u>.
questions.explanation: 보노보의 협력적인 행동과 상호작용의 유연성이 사회적 도전에 더 성공적으로 적응하게 도와주었다는 내용이므로, 이러한 특성이 종의 발전을 '쇠퇴(decline)'가 아닌 '번영'이나 '성공'으로 이끈다고 보는 것이 문맥상 적절합니다.

questions.question: 15. 주어진 글 (A)에 이어질 내용을 순서에 맞게 배열한 것으로 가장 적절한 것은? [3.3점]
questions.passage:
(A)
"The phone rang, and it was my dad calling from my hometown, Waituhi.
"Can you take a week off?" he asked. "Your Nani Tama wants you here."
"But Dad!" I answered. "My boss won't let me take any more time off."
The phone went silent, and then I heard my grandfather say faintly that (a) <u>he</u> needed my help. He said, "I must go to Murupara to finish the whakapapa. Drive me there. Hurry, I may not have much time."
I just knew I had no choice. "All right, Nani," I replied with a sigh. "I'll come."
ordered_passages:
(B)
Now that day seems like a dream to me. I remember the two old men sitting at the table and the soft sounds of the Maori words as they talked. All through the quiet afternoon and into the evening, they recalled missing names. I had a strange feeling that there were other people in the room. I felt as if people from the past were looking over the shoulders of the two old men to see if the work was correct.
Finally, they stopped. It was done. After a moment of silence, the old man whispered to Nani, "Goodbye, friend." Crying, they pressed their noses together to say goodbye.

(C)
When I arrived at Auntie's place, I was shocked to see how thin Nani Tama was.
"Look, Nani," I said. "I'm not taking you anywhere. You could die on me!"
Nani looked at me in anger.
"You want me to die here in this room? Looking at these four walls? When the whakapapa is not yet finished?"
The old man held on tightly to the side of the bed and cried out as (b) <u>he</u> stood up. Every slow, painful step hurt him, but he tried to walk. I could not help but carry him to the car, and we set off with Auntie.

(D)
We traveled all night, mostly in silence, listening to Nani chanting in the darkness. It was strange but wonderful to hear (c) <u>him</u>. Sometimes, he burst into a song that he had taught Auntie. They sang together, lifting up their voices to send the song flying like a bird through the sky.
Just before noon, we arrived at a small town called Murupara.
"Where do we go now?" I asked Nani.
He did not reply, but he was searching inside himself, staring at the small houses. Then, at a street corner, he told us to turn. After turning the corner, we saw an old man standing in front of a house. He welcomed Nani Tama with a gentle smile, but in (d) <u>his</u> eyes, I saw the message, "We must hurry."

(E)
It was early morning and still dark when we returned to Auntie's place. All the lights were on, and the village people were waiting for us. Smiling, Nani Tama lifted up the whakapapa and offered it to the village. Our hearts were full because our grandfather had saved our past for us.
Our Nani Tama smiled again. (e) <u>His</u> smile grew tired.
He sighed. "At last, I may go now."
Then, he closed his eyes.
"No, Dad!" Auntie Hiraina cried.
The sun burst across the hills.
questions.explanation: 글 (A)에서 화자가 할아버지(Nani Tama)의 요청에 따라 고향으로 가기로 결정한 후, (C)에서 고향집에 도착하여 할아버지의 쇠약한 모습을 보고 걱정하지만 할아버지의 강한 의지에 따라 길을 나서는 장면이 이어진다. (D)에서 밤새 이동하여 목적지인 Murupara에 도착하고 다른 노인을 만나는 과정이 서술되며, (B)에서 그 노인과 함께 족보(whakapapa) 작업을 완료하고 작별 인사를 나누는 장면이 이어진다. 마지막으로 (E)에서 마을로 돌아와 작업을 마을 사람들에게 전하고 할아버지가 평화롭게 숨을 거두는 결말로 마무리된다.
