It was early morning and still dark when we returned to Auntie's place. All the lights were on, and the village people were waiting for us. Smiling, Nani Tama lifted up the whakapapa and offered it to the village. Our hearts were full because our grandfather had saved our past for us.
Our Nani Tama smiled again. (e) <u>His</u> smile grew tired.
He sighed. "At last, I may go now."
Then, he closed his eyes.
"No, Dad!" Auntie Hiraina cried.
The sun burst across the hills.
options: ① (a)
② (b)
③ (c)
④ (d)
⑤ (e)
questions.explanation: (a), (b), (c), (e)는 모두 주인공의 할아버지인 Nani Tama를 가리키지만, (d)는 Murupara에서 Nani Tama를 기다리고 있던 다른 노인을 가리킨다.

questions.question: 17. 윗글에 관한 내용으로 적절하지 않은 것은? [2.8점]
questions.passage:
(A)
"The phone rang, and it was my dad calling from my hometown, Waituhi.
"Can you take a week off?" he asked. "Your Nani Tama wants you here."
"But Dad!" I answered. "My boss won't let me take any more time off."
The phone went silent, and then I heard my grandfather say faintly that (a) <u>he</u> needed my help. He said, "I must go to Murupara to finish the whakapapa. Drive me there. Hurry, I may not have much time."
I just knew I had no choice. "All right, Nani," I replied with a sigh. "I'll come."

(B)
Now that day seems like a dream to me. I remember the two old men sitting at the table and the soft sounds of the Maori words as they talked. All through the quiet afternoon and into the evening, they recalled missing names. I had a strange feeling that there were other people in the room. I felt as if people from the past were looking over the shoulders of the two old men to see if the work was correct.
Finally, they stopped. It was done. After a moment of silence, the old man whispered to Nani, "Goodbye, friend." Crying, they pressed their noses together to say goodbye.

(C)
When I arrived at Auntie's place, I was shocked to see how thin Nani Tama was.
"Look, Nani," I said. "I'm not taking you anywhere. You could die on me!"
Nani looked at me in anger.
"You want me to die here in this room? Looking at these four walls? When the whakapapa is not yet finished?"
The old man held on tightly to the side of the bed and cried out as (b) <u>he</u> stood up. Every slow, painful step hurt him, but he tried to walk. I could not help but carry him to the car, and we set off with Auntie.

(D)
We traveled all night, mostly in silence, listening to Nani chanting in the darkness. It was strange but wonderful to hear (c) <u>him</u>. Sometimes, he burst into a song that he had taught Auntie. They sang together, lifting up their voices to send the song flying like a bird through the sky.
Just before noon, we arrived at a small town called Murupara.
"Where do we go now?" I asked Nani.
He did not reply, but he was searching inside himself, staring at the small houses. Then, at a street corner, he told us to turn. After turning the corner, we saw an old man standing in front of a house. He welcomed Nani Tama with a gentle smile, but in (d) <u>his</u> eyes, I saw the message, "We must hurry."

(E)
It was early morning and still dark when we returned to Auntie's place. All the lights were on, and the village people were waiting for us. Smiling, Nani Tama lifted up the whakapapa and offered it to the village. Our hearts were full because our grandfather had saved our past for us.
Our Nani Tama smiled again. (e) <u>His</u> smile grew tired.
He sighed. "At last, I may go now."
Then, he closed his eyes.
"No, Dad!" Auntie Hiraina cried.
The sun burst across the hills.
options: ① Nani Tama는 손자에게 Murupara로 데려다 달라고 부탁했다.
② 두 노인은 Maori어로 대화하며 누락된 이름들을 기억해냈다.
③ 손자는 처음에는 여행을 거절했지만 결국 할아버지를 차에 태웠다.
④ 할아버지의 친구는 우리가 서둘러야 한다고 손자에게 말했다.
⑤ 족보를 마을 사람들에게 건네고 Nani Tama는 눈을 감았다.
questions.explanation: 지문의 내용상 서둘러야 한다고 말한 것은 할아버지의 친구가 아니라 할아버지 본인일 가능성이 높으며, 문맥에 따라 일치하지 않는 세부 사항을 파악해야 합니다.

questions.question: 18. 다음 (A), (B), (C) 각 네모 안에서 문맥상 어울리는 표현을 골라 짝지은 것으로 가장 적절한 것은? [3.8점]
questions.passage: Plants can communicate, although not in the same way we do. Some express their discontent through scents. You know that smell that hangs in the air after you've mowed the lawn? Yeah, that's actually an SOS. Some plants even communicate through sound-Yes, sound-but at frequencies that are (A) [ within/beyond ] human hearing. Scientists used sensitive microphones to investigate whether plants emit any signals when under pressure. They discovered that stressed plants (B) [ soak up/give off ] high-pitched clicking sounds and that these noises vary depending on the type of stress. For example, the sound a plant emits when it's not getting watered is different from the one it makes when a leaf is damaged. Still, specialists don't believe that these sounds mean plants are experiencing pain. Rather, these responses are thought to be automatic survival mechanisms. Plants are living organisms, and their main (C) [ objection/purpose ] is to survive. Scents and sounds are their tools for defending against things that might harm them.
options: ① within ... soak up ... purpose
② within ... give off ... objection
③ beyond ... soak up ... purpose
④ beyond ... soak up ... objection
⑤ beyond ... give off ... purpose
questions.explanation: (A) 인간의 가청 범위를 벗어난 소리이므로 beyond, (B) 스트레스를 받은 식물이 소리를 내뿜는 것이므로 give off, (C) 식물의 주요 목적은 생존이므로 purpose가 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 이내 ... 흡수하다 ... 목적
② 이내 ... 내뿜다 ... 반대
③ 너머 ... 흡수하다 ... 목적
④ 너머 ... 흡수하다 ... 반대
⑤ 너머 ... 내뿜다 ... 목적

questions.question: 24. 윗글의 밑줄 친 (a)~(e)가 각각 의미하는 바로 적절하지 않은 것은? [3.4점]
questions.passage: For some time, my grandfather had been busy writing down the village genealogy, ① <u>known</u> as the whakapapa. The whakapapa had been in his old house. But then came the night of the fire, ② <u>which</u> ran through the house and (a) <u>destroyed our past</u>. In only one night, everything we knew was gone. Nani Tama, in despair, went to stay with his daughter, my Auntie Hiraina. ③ <u>Try</u> to find a way out of the ashes of the past, Nani began to write the whakapapa again (b) <u>with his shaky hands</u>. He chanted the names of the ancestors, (c) <u>joining the past to the present once more</u>. The village went quiet and ④ <u>listening</u> to his chanting. His voice traveled along the lines of our genealogy, (d) <u>searching back across the centuries</u>. Sometimes, there were lines ⑤ <u>that</u> were difficult to remember. Then his voice suddenly stopped in the middle of the chant. The village (e) <u>waited in worried silence</u> until the next name burst out of his mouth. It took Nani Tama almost two years ⑥ <u>to gather</u> most of the whakapapa, but there were still missing names he needed to fill in. Now, he wanted me to drive ⑦ <u>himself</u> to Murupara to finish his work.
options: ① (a) refers to the loss of valuable cultural and historical records due to the fire.
② (b) emphasizes his emotional excitement and joy while rewriting the whakapapa.
③ (c) shows the effort to connect ancestral heritage with the current generation.
④ (d) illustrates the act of remembering and recovering names from long ago.
⑤ (e) indicates the villagers' deep concern for whether Nani Tama could recall the missing names.
questions.explanation: (b)의 'with his shaky hands'는 화재로 인해 모든 기록을 잃은 절망적인 상황에서 노령의 할아버지가 고군분투하며 다시 족보를 써 내려가는 고통과 노력을 상징하는 것이지, 기쁨이나 즐거움을 강조하는 것이 아닙니다.
options_translation: ① (a)는 화재로 인해 귀중한 문화적, 역사적 기록을 잃은 것을 가리킨다.
② (b)는 족보를 다시 쓰면서 느끼는 정서적 흥분과 기쁨을 강조한다.
③ (c)는 조상의 유산을 현 세대와 연결하려는 노력을 보여준다.
④ (d)는 아주 오래전의 이름을 기억해내고 복구하는 행위를 묘사한다.
⑤ (e)는 Nani Tama가 누락된 이름들을 기억해낼 수 있을지에 대한 마을 사람들의 깊은 우려를 나타낸다.

questions.question: [서답형 1] 윗글의 밑줄 친 ①~⑦ 중 어법상 잘못된 것을 3개 골라 번호를 쓰고, 어법상 올바른 형태의 한 단어로 바르게 고쳐 쓰시오. [총 3.0점]
questions.passage: For some time, my grandfather had been busy writing down the village genealogy, ① <u>known</u> as the whakapapa. The whakapapa had been in his old house. But then came the night of the fire, ② <u>which</u> ran through the house and (a) <u>destroyed our past</u>. In only one night, everything we knew was gone. Nani Tama, in despair, went to stay with his daughter, my Auntie Hiraina. ③ <u>Try</u> to find a way out of the ashes of the past, Nani began to write the whakapapa again (b) <u>with his shaky hands</u>. He chanted the names of the ancestors, (c) <u>joining the past to the present once more</u>. The village went quiet and ④ <u>listening</u> to his chanting. His voice traveled along the lines of our genealogy, (d) <u>searching back across the centuries</u>. Sometimes, there were lines ⑤ <u>that</u> were difficult to remember. Then his voice suddenly stopped in the middle of the chant. The village (e) <u>waited in worried silence</u> until the next name burst out of his mouth. It took Nani Tama almost two years ⑥ <u>to gather</u> most of the whakapapa, but there were still missing names he needed to fill in. Now, he wanted me to drive ⑦ <u>himself</u> to Murupara to finish his work.
subjective_conditions: 밑줄 친 ①~⑦ 중 어법상 잘못된 것 3개를 고를 것
한 단어의 올바른 형태로 고쳐 쓸 것
questions.answer: ③ => Trying, ④ => listened, ⑦ => him
questions.explanation:
③ 문맥상 '과거의 재 속에서 길을 찾으려고 노력하면서'라는 의미의 분사구문이 필요하므로 현재분사 Trying이 적절합니다.
④ The village went quiet and ~ 구조에서 went와 listened가 병렬 구조를 이루어야 하므로 listened가 적절합니다.
⑦ drive의 목적어는 주어인 he와 동일 인물이 아니라 화자(grandfather)를 가리키는 대상이지만, 문장의 목적어로 'himself'가 쓰이기 위해서는 주어와 대상이 같아야 합니다. 여기서는 '나에게 그를 태워다 달라고 원했다'는 의미이므로 재귀대명사가 아닌 일반 대명사 him이 와야 합니다.

questions.question:
[서답형3] 다음은 윗글의 주제문이다. 빈칸 ①, ②에 들어갈 말을 <조건>에 맞게 각각 한 단어로 쓰시오. [총 2.0점]

Instead of ① _________, we should focus on kindness and ② _________ to build a better society.
questions.passage:
In our competitive society, many people believe that only the biggest or the strongest can survive and thrive. However, I propose an alternative view: kindness is the key to success. Isn't that a comforting thought? We can use the power of our natural kindness to cooperate with different individuals. We can all benefit from this instead of trying to be better than others. Kindness allows us to build trust, bridge differences, and support one another in meaningful ways. It creates a space where everyone feels valued and included, regardless of their background or abilities. Rather than focusing on winning, we begin to focus on growing together. Think of our society as a bouquet. Each flower adds more beauty when it exists in harmony with the others, not when it stands alone. In the same way,
Valuing every individual helps build a stronger, more connected community. When we choose kindness and shared purpose, we don't just grow as individuals—we bloom together as a community.
subjective_conditions: o 본문의 단어만을 활용하되 반드시 변형하여 쓸 것
o ①, ②번 각각 11개 철자로 된 단어를 쓸 것
o 각각 다른 단어로 작성할 것
o 정답 작성 시 반드시 각 번호를 쓸 것 (번호 미기재 시 답을 모두 쓴 경우에만 순서대로 작성한 것으로 간주하여 채점함)
questions.explanation: 본문에 제시된 'competitive'(경쟁적인)를 11자 형태인 명사 'competition'으로, 'cooperate'(협력하다)를 11자 형태인 명사 'cooperation'으로 변형하여 빈칸을 완성할 수 있습니다.

questions.question: [서답형4] 윗 글의 흐름상 적절한 표현이 되도록 <보기>의 단어들을 배열하여 빈칸을 <조건>에 맞게 완성하시오 [3.0점]
questions.passage:
In our competitive society, many people believe that only the biggest or the strongest can survive and thrive. However, I propose an alternative view: kindness is the key to success. Isn't that a comforting thought? We can use the power of our natural kindness to cooperate with different individuals. We can all benefit from this instead of trying to be better than others. Kindness allows us to build trust, bridge differences, and support one another in meaningful ways. Valuing every individual helps build a stronger, more connected community. When we choose kindness and shared purpose, we don't just grow as individuals—we bloom together as a community.
subjective_conditions: o <보기>의 단어를 모두 한 번씩만 사용할 것
o 단어 추가 없음
o 어형 변화 있음
vocabulary_box: work / each person / flourish / society / when / make / together
questions.answer: society flourishes when each person works together
questions.explanation: 문맥상 '각 개인이 함께 일할 때 사회가 번영한다'는 내용이 들어가야 합니다. 주어진 단어를 어형 변화(flourish -> flourishes, work -> works)하여 배열하면 'society flourishes when each person works together'가 됩니다.

questions.question: 3. 빈칸에 공통으로 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은? [2.7점]
questions.passage: You never get a second chance to make a first impression. It is very important to make a good impression on others when we meet them for the first time. But people aren't the only ones who make first impressions - books do as well. A powerful _________ of a book can catch readers' attention and make them want to read on. Authors often spend weeks, months, or even years coming up with the perfect _________ for their books. Let's take a look at some of them.
options: ① opening line
② writing style
③ advertisement
④ main character
⑤ visual presentation
questions.explanation: 글의 맥락상 책의 첫인상을 결정짓는 것은 책의 첫 구절(opening line)이며, 작가들이 이를 위해 많은 시간을 들인다는 내용이 자연스럽습니다.
options_translation: ① 첫 구절
② 문체
③ 광고
④ 주인공
⑤ 시각적 표현

questions.question: 4. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은? [2.8점]
questions.passage:
"All children, except one, grow up."
- J.M.Barrie, 「Peter Pan」
No one can stop the sands of time. Every child becomes an adult whether they want to or not. But the book Peter Pan states that there is one child who is the ① <u>exception</u> to the rule. Peter Pan is a boy who ② <u>wants to grow older.</u> He wants to have fun and stay a child forever.
One night in London, Peter Pan and Tinker Bell visit the home of Wendy, John, and Michael. Peter Pan invites them to a fantastic island in the sky called Neverland. It is a ③ <u>magical</u> place where dreams are born and excitement never ends. The children take Peter Pan's hand and their ④ <u>adventure</u> begins. Only children can visit Neverland, and they do not grow up as long as they remain there. They have a wonderful time in Neverland. But in the end, the three children decide to ⑤ <u>return</u> home and grow up. What is the reason for this unexpected decision? Read the book to find out.
questions.explanation: 피터 팬은 영원히 아이로 남고 싶어 하는 인물이므로, '나이가 들고 싶어 한다(wants to grow older)'는 문맥상 적절하지 않습니다. '아이로 남고 싶어 한다(never wants to grow up)' 등으로 고쳐야 합니다.

questions.question: 5. 다음 글의 내용과 일치하지 않는 것은? [2.8점]
questions.passage:
"There is no lake at Camp Green Lake."
- Louis Sachar, 「Holes」
What comes to mind when you hear the word "camp?" Many people would think of fun activities like fishing, having a barbecue, and sleeping under the beautiful stars. So what kind of place do you imagine Camp Green Lake is? Perhaps it is a beautiful place where a green forest surrounds a blue lake. But the book, Holes, paints a different picture. It states that there is no lake there despite its name. Through this irony, Sachar is hinting that Camp Green Lake is not a normal camp with fun and games.
In fact, Camp Green Lake is not a camp at all. Located in the desert, it is like a prison for bad boys. The main character of the book, a teenage boy named Stanley Yelnats, is different from the other boys in the camp. He hasn't done anything wrong. He was just in the wrong place at the wrong time. Stanley and the other boys at Camp Green Lake are expected to improve their character by digging holes every day. Stanley suspects that there is another reason for the digging. Will Stanley successfully dig up the truth about Camp Green Lake?
options: ① 이름과 달리 Camp Green Lake에는 호수가 없다.
② Camp Green Lake는 사막에 있는 감옥과도 같은 곳이었다.
③ Stanley는 잘못을 저질러서 캠프에 오게 되었다.
④ Stanley와 다른 소년들은 캠프에서 매일 구덩이를 팠다.
⑤ Stanley는 구덩이를 파는 다른 이유가 있다고 생각한다.
questions.explanation: 본문에서 Stanley는 다른 소년들과 다르며 잘못을 저지르지 않았지만 운이 나빠서 그곳에 있게 되었다고 언급하고 있으므로(He hasn't done anything wrong. He was just in the wrong place at the wrong time.), 잘못을 저질러서 캠프에 오게 되었다는 ③번은 내용과 일치하지 않습니다.

questions.question: 6. 다음 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은? [2.7점]
questions.passage:
"It was a bright cold day in April, and the clocks were striking thirteen." - George Orwell, 「1984」
Typically, clocks strike from one to twelve times. But George Orwell's well-known novel, 1984, opens with the clocks striking thirteen times. In a normal world, a clock striking thirteen is out of the ordinary. But in this mysterious place, it doesn't seem to be unusual. Not just one clock but all clocks strike thirteen here. What's more, the number thirteen is often associated with _________ in Western cultures. In this way, Orwell hints to the readers that they are about to enter a world that is dark and unfamiliar.
options: ① bad luck
② good luck
③ happiness
④ satisfaction
⑤ thankfulness
questions.explanation: 서구 문화권에서 숫자 13은 불운과 관련이 깊으며, 본문에서도 어둡고 낯선 세계에 들어갈 것임을 암시한다고 했으므로 빈칸에는 'bad luck'이 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 불운
② 행운
③ 행복
④ 만족
⑤ 감사함

questions.question: 7. 다음 글의 내용과 일치하지 않는 것은? [2.8점]
questions.passage: The story takes place in an imaginary country ⓐ <u>called</u> Oceania in the year 1984. The government tries to control everyone's life. It has even created a new language ⓑ <u>to limit</u> people's thoughts and expressions. Big Brother, the leader of Oceania, ⓒ <u>watches</u> everything that goes on through television screens. As long as Big Brother is in power, the people of Oceania will never be free. The main character, Winston Smith, does not agree with ⓓ <u>which</u> the government is doing. He wants to fight against Big Brother, but he can't do it by ⓔ <u>himself</u>. Will Winston find others to join him? Or will he give in and be controlled by Big Brother like the rest of the people?
options: ① Oceania는 1984년을 배경으로 한 가상의 나라이다.
② Oceania의 정부는 사람들의 생각과 표현을 제한하는 새로운 언어를 만들었다.
③ Big Brother는 텔레비전 화면을 통해 사람들을 감시한다.
④ Winston Smith는 정부의 활동에 동의하며 Big Brother를 지지한다.
⑤ Winston은 Big Brother에 맞서 싸우고 싶어 하지만 혼자서는 할 수 없다.
questions.explanation: 본문에서 주인공 Winston Smith는 정부가 하고 있는 일에 동의하지 않으며(does not agree with what the government is doing), 빅 브라더에 대항해 싸우고 싶어 한다고 했으므로 지지한다는 설명은 틀렸습니다.

questions.question: 8. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 어법상 틀린 것은? [2.8점]
questions.passage: The story takes place in an imaginary country ⓐ <u>called</u> Oceania in the year 1984. The government tries to control everyone's life. It has even created a new language ⓑ <u>to limit</u> people's thoughts and expressions. Big Brother, the leader of Oceania, ⓒ <u>watches</u> everything that goes on through television screens. As long as Big Brother is in power, the people of Oceania will never be free. The main character, Winston Smith, does not agree with ⓓ <u>which</u> the government is doing. He wants to fight against Big Brother, but he can't do it by ⓔ <u>himself</u>. Will Winston find others to join him? Or will he give in and be controlled by Big Brother like the rest of the people?
options: ① ⓐ
② ⓑ
③ ⓒ
④ ⓓ
⑤ ⓔ
questions.explanation: ⓓ의 which는 전치사 with의 목적어 역할을 하면서 동시에 뒤에 이어지는 문장(the government is doing)의 목적어 역할을 해야 하는 선행사를 포함한 관계대명사 what이 되어야 합니다. which를 쓰려면 앞에 선행사가 있어야 합니다.

questions.question: 9. 다음 글의 제목으로 가장 적절한 것은? [3.7점]
questions.passage: Assuming gene editing in humans proves to be safe and effective, it might seem logical, even preferable, to correct disease-causing mutations at the earliest possible stage of life, before harmful genes begin causing serious problems. Yet once it becomes possible to transform an embryo's mutated genes into "normal" ones, there will certainly be temptations to upgrade normal genes to superior versions. Should we begin editing genes in unborn children to lower their lifetime risk of heart disease or cancer? What about giving unborn children beneficial features, like greater strength and increased mental abilities, or changing physical characteristics, like eye and hair color? The pursuit for perfection seems almost natural to human nature, but if we start down this slippery slope, we may not like where we end up.
options: ① Humanity: The Last Hope for All
② Gene Editing: A Double-edged Sword
③ Favorable Physical Characteristics of Humans for Attraction
④ Redesigning Gene Structure: A Scientific Revolution with Zero Risks
⑤ The Reason Why Disease-causing Mutations Occur in Human Body
questions.explanation: 이 글은 유전자 편집이 질병 치료라는 긍정적인 목적을 가질 수 있지만, 신체적/지적 능력을 강화하려는 우생학적 욕망으로 이어져 위험한 결과를 초래할 수 있다는 '양날의 검'과 같은 성격을 설명하고 있다.
options_translation: ① 인류: 모두를 위한 마지막 희망
② 유전자 편집: 양날의 검
③ 매력을 위한 인간의 유리한 신체적 특성
④ 유전자 구조의 재설계: 위험이 전혀 없는 과학적 혁명
⑤ 인체에서 질병을 유발하는 돌연변이가 발생하는 이유

questions.question: 10. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 'that process'가 가리키는 것으로 가장 적절한 것은? [3.6점]
questions.passage: The science we learn in grade school is a collection of certainties about the natural world - the earth goes around the sun, DNA carries the information of an organism, and so on. Only when you start to learn the practice of science do you realize that each of these "facts" was hard won through a succession of logical inferences based upon many observations or experiments. The process of science is less about collecting pieces of knowledge than it is about reducing the uncertainties in what we know. Our uncertainties can be greater or lesser for any given piece of knowledge depending upon where we are in <u>that process</u> - today we are quite certain of how an apple will fall from a tree, but our understanding of the turbulent fluid flow remains a work in progress after more than a century of effort.
options: ① learning facts from science books at elementary school
② starting to do experiments to increase uncertainties
③ lessening uncertainties through scientific inference
④ describing phenomena that are already known
⑤ watching things fall or move in real life
questions.explanation: 문맥상 'that process'는 바로 앞 문장에서 언급된 'the process of science'를 가리키며, 이는 지식을 수집하는 것보다 '우리가 아는 것의 불확실성을 줄여가는 과정(reducing the uncertainties)'을 의미한다.
options_translation: ① 초등학교 과학책에서 사실을 배우는 것
② 불확실성을 증가시키기 위해 실험을 시작하는 것
③ 과학적 추론을 통해 불확실성을 줄이는 것
④ 이미 알려진 현상을 묘사하는 것
⑤ 실생활에서 사물이 떨어지거나 움직이는 것을 지켜보는 것

questions.question: 11. 다음 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은? [3.6점]
questions.passage: There is a wealth of evidence that when parents, teachers, supervisors, and coaches are perceived as involved and caring, people feel happier and more motivated. And it is not just those people with power - we need to feel valued and respected by peers and coworkers. Thus, when the need for relatedness is met, motivation and internalization are fueled, provided that support for autonomy and competence are also there. If we are trying to motivate others, a caring relationship is a crucial basis from which to begin. And when we are trying to motivate ourselves, doing things to enhance a sense of _________ can be crucial to long-term persistence. So exercise with a friend, call someone when you have a difficult decision to make, and be there as a support for others as they take on challenges.
options: ① relief
② humor
③ failure
④ closeness
⑤ inferiority
questions.explanation: 이 글은 타인과의 관계, 존중, 유대감(relatedness)이 동기 부여에 중요하다고 강조하고 있다. 빈칸 뒤의 예시(친구와 운동하기, 전화하기 등)는 모두 타인과의 연결을 강화하는 행동이므로 'closeness(친밀감)'가 가장 적절하다.
options_translation: ① 안도
② 유머
③ 실패
④ 친밀함
⑤ 열등감

questions.question: 12. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 어법상 틀린 것은? [3.6점]
questions.passage: Oral reading, or reading aloud, is the act of vocally articulating written text, unlike silent reading. It involves more than just seeing words on a page: it's a multi sensory reading experience that engages the eyes, mouth, ears, and brain simultaneously. Modern brain-scanning techniques such as fMRI (functional Magnetic Resonance Imaging) have revealed ① <u>that</u> reading aloud lights up many areas of the brain. There is intense activity in areas ② <u>associated</u> with pronunciation and hearing the sound of the spoken response, which strengthens the connective structures of your brain cells for more brainpower. This leads to an overall improvement in concentration. Reading aloud is also a good way to develop your public speaking skills because it forces you ③ <u>to read</u> each and every word — something people don't often do when reading quickly, or reading in silence. Children, in particular, should ④ <u>be encouraged</u> to read aloud. Since the brain is wired for learning through connections ⑤ <u>what</u> are created by positive stimulation, such as singing, touching, and reading aloud.
questions.explanation: ⑤번의 what은 앞에 선행사(connections)가 존재하므로 선행사를 포함하는 관계대명사인 what을 쓸 수 없으며, 주격 관계대명사인 that이나 which로 고쳐야 합니다.

questions.question: 13. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은? [3.4점]
questions.passage: Routines enable athletes to evaluate competition conditions. For example, bouncing a ball in a volleyball service routine ① <u>supplies</u> the server with information about the ball, the floor, and the state of her muscles. This information can then be used to properly ② <u>prepare</u> for her serve. Routines also enable athletes to adjust and ③ <u>fine-tune</u> their preparations based on those evaluations or in pursuit of a particular competitive goal. This adaptation can involve adjustment to the conditions, rivals, competitive situation, or internal influences that can affect performance. Just like ④ <u>adjusting</u> a race-car engine to the conditions of the track, air temperature, and weather, routines adjust all competitive components to ⑤ <u>interfere with</u> proper performance.
questions.explanation: 글의 흐름상 루틴은 모든 경기 구성 요소를 조정하여 적절한 경기력을 '촉진'하거나 '최적화'하는 역할을 해야 하므로, '방해하다'라는 의미의 interfere with는 문맥상 적절하지 않습니다.

questions.question: 14. 다음 글에서 전체 흐름과 가장 관계없는 문장은? [3.5점]
questions.passage: Promotion deals with consumer psychology. Since people can't be forced to think in a particular way, a clever marketer knows that promotion is used to deliver information as clearly, honestly, and simply as they can. By doing so, the possibility of increasing sales goes up. ① The days are gone when promotions were done in order to trick the consumer into purchasing something. ② The long-term effect of getting a consumer to buy something they did not really want or need wasn't good. ③ As a matter of fact, consumers tricked once can do damage to sales as they relate their experience to others. ④ Many consumers are more likely to purchase a product when it is advertised by celebrities or influencers they admire. ⑤ Instead, marketers now know that their aim is to target the right people who are most likely to appreciate a good or service, and to promote that good or service in a way that makes the value clear to them.
questions.explanation: 이 글은 판촉(promotion)이 소비자에게 정직하고 명확한 정보를 전달하여 가치를 인식시켜야 한다는 점을 강조하고 있습니다. ④번 문장은 유명인이나 인플루언서를 통한 광고 효과에 대해 말하고 있어, 정보 전달의 명확성과 정직함이라는 글의 주제와는 관계가 없습니다.

questions.question: 15. 주어진 글 다음에 이어질 글의 순서로 가장 적절한 것은? [3.5점]
questions.passage: Our skin conducts electricity more or less efficiently, depending on our emotions.
ordered_passages: (A) We can actually measure your emotional state by tracking how your body subconsciously sweats, by running a bit of electricity through your skin. We can then turn the subjective, subconscious experience of emotional intensity into an objective number by figuring out how good your skin gets at transferring an electrical current.

(B) This change in sweat gland activity happens completely without your conscious mind having much say in the matter. If you feel emotionally intense, you're going to notice an increase in sweat gland activity. This is particularly useful from a scientific viewpoint, because it allows us to put an objective value on a subjective state of mind.

(C) We know that when we're emotionally stimulated, stressed, sad, any intense emotion, really—our bodies sweat a tiny bit, so little we might not even notice. And when those tiny drops of sweat appear, our skin gets more electrically conductive.
questions.explanation: 피부의 전기 전도성이 감정에 따라 달라진다는 도입글 뒤에, (C)에서 감정 자극 시 미세하게 땀이 나면서 전도성이 높아진다는 구체적 원리를 설명합니다. (B)에서 이러한 땀샘 활동이 무의식적이며 주관적 마음을 객관화하는 데 유용함을 언급하고, 마지막으로 (A)에서 실제 전기 측정을 통해 감정 상태를 수치화하는 구체적 방법을 설명하는 순서가 논리적입니다.

questions.question: 16. 다음 글에서 전체 흐름과 관계 없는 문장은? [3.5점]
questions.passage: Plato argued that when you see something that strikes you as beautiful, you are really just seeing a partial reflection of true beauty, just as a painting or even a photograph only captures part of the real thing. True beauty, or what Plato calls the Form of Beauty, has no particular color, shape, or size. ① Rather, it is an abstract idea, like the number five. ② You can make drawings of the number five in blue or red ink, big or small, but the number five itself is none of those things. ③ Also, Number five is also widely used for beauty products like the name of perfume. ④ When you think of the idea of a triangle, for example, although it has no particular color or size, it somehow lies within each and every triangle you see. ⑤ Plato thought the same was true of beauty: The Form of Beauty somehow lies within each and every beautiful thing you see.
questions.explanation: 이 글은 플라톤의 미의 형상(Form of Beauty)에 대한 추상적 개념을 설명하고 있으며, 숫자 5나 삼각형을 예로 들어 본질적인 형상이 개별적인 사물 안에 존재함을 설명하고 있다. ③번 문장은 숫자 5가 향수 이름과 같은 미용 제품에 널리 사용된다는 내용으로, 글의 논리적 흐름인 '추상적 본질'과는 무관한 지엽적인 내용이다.

questions.question: 17. 다음 글의 내용과 일치하지 않는 것은? [3.4점]
questions.passage: <u>Plants can communicate, although not in the same way we do.</u> Some express their discontent through scents. You know that smell that hangs in the air after you've mowed the lawn? Yeah, that's actually an SOS. Some plants use sound. Yes, sound, though at a frequency that we can't hear. Researchers experimented with plants and microphones to see if they could record any trouble calls. <u>They found that plants produce a high-frequency clicking noise when stressed</u> and can make different sounds for different stressors. <u>The sound a plant makes when it's not getting watered differs from the one it'll make when a leaf is cut.</u> However, it's worth noting that experts don't think plants are crying out in pain. It's more likely that these reactions are knee-jerk survival actions. Plants are living organisms, and their main objective is to survive. <u>Scents and sounds are their tools for defending against things that might harm them.</u>
options: ① 식물은 인간처럼 말로 의사소통을 하지는 못한다.
② 스트레스를 받은 식물은 고주파 소리를 낼 수 있다.
③ 식물은 물이 부족할 때와 잎이 잘릴 때 각기 다른 소리를 낸다.
④ 전문가들은 식물의 반응을 감정의 표현으로 본다.
⑤ 식물은 해로운 것들에 대항하기 위해 냄새와 소리를 사용한다.
questions.explanation: 지문에서 'experts don't think plants are crying out in pain. It's more likely that these reactions are knee-jerk survival actions'라고 명시되어 있으므로, 전문가들은 식물의 반응을 고통(감정)의 표현이 아닌 생존을 위한 무의식적 반응으로 본다.

questions.question: 18. 다음 중 지문에서 제시한 바람직한 부모의 반응 방식에 해당하는 것은? [4점]
questions.passage: As you listen to your child in an emotional moment, be aware that sharing simple observations usually works better than asking questions to get a conversation rolling. You may ask your child "Why do you feel sad?" and she may not have a clue. As a child, she may not have an answer on the tip of her tongue. Maybe she's feeling sad about her parents' arguments, or because she feels overtired, or she's worried about a piano recital. But she may or may not be able to explain any of this. And even when she does come up with an answer, she might be worried that the answer is not good enough to justify the feeling. Under these circumstances, a series of questions can just make a child silent. It's better to simply reflect what you notice. You can say, "You seem a little tired today," or, "I noticed that you frowned when I mentioned the recital," and wait for her response.
options: ① A child frowns after hearing about a family trip. The parent says, "What is it? Can't you just be excited like the others?"
② A child comes home looking discouraged after school. The parent says, "You seem a little down today." and waits quietly.
③ A child looks anxious before a test. The parent advises, "When I was your age, I used to stay up all night and study very hard. So I got straight A's in all subjects. You should do what I did."
④ A child is unusually quiet during dinner. The parent says, "You're always like this when you don't get what you want. That's the problem."
⑤ A child seems sad in the car. The parent keeps asking, "What happened at school? Did someone say something mean? Tell me or you'll never get out of the car."
questions.explanation: 지문에서는 아이에게 질문을 퍼붓기보다 부모가 관찰한 바를 단순히 언급(reflect what you notice)하고 반응을 기다려주는 것이 좋다고 조언하고 있다. ②번은 아이의 기분을 관찰하여 말해주고 조용히 기다려주는 모습이므로 지문의 조언과 일치한다.
options_translation: ① 가족 여행 소식을 듣고 아이가 인상을 찌푸리자, 부모가 "뭐니? 다른 사람들처럼 그냥 즐거워할 순 없니?"라고 말한다.
② 아이가 학교 끝나고 낙담한 모습으로 집에 오자, 부모가 "오늘 좀 기분이 안 좋아 보이네."라고 말하고 조용히 기다린다.
③ 아이가 시험 전 불안해 보이자, 부모가 "내가 네 나이였을 때는 밤을 새우며 아주 열심히 공부해서 전 과목 A를 받았단다. 너도 나처럼 해야 해."라고 조언한다.
④ 아이가 저녁 식사 내내 평소보다 조용하자, 부모가 "넌 네가 원하는 걸 얻지 못할 때면 항상 이러더라. 그게 문제야."라고 말한다.
⑤ 아이가 차 안에서 슬퍼 보이자, 부모가 계속해서 질문한다. "학교에서 무슨 일 있었니? 누가 못된 말을 했니? 말하지 않으면 차에서 절대 못 내려."

questions.question: 19. 다음 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은? [3.6점]
questions.passage: What does it mean for a character to be a hero as opposed to a villain? In artistic and entertainment descriptions, it's essential for the author to establish a positive relationship between a protagonist and the audience. In order for tragedy or misfortune to draw out an emotional response in viewers, the character must be adjusted so as to be <u>_________</u> as either friend or enemy. Whether the portrayal is fictional or documentary, we must feel that the protagonist is someone whose actions benefit us; the protagonist is, or would be, a worthy companion or valued ally. Violent action films are often filled with dozens of incidental deaths of minor characters that draw out little response in the audience. In order to feel strong emotions, the audience must be emotionally invested in a character as either ally or enemy.
options: ① reliable
② identifiable
③ compatible
④ remarkable
⑤ knowledgeable
questions.explanation: 글의 핵심은 관객이 캐릭터에게 감정적 반응을 느끼기 위해서는 그 캐릭터가 아군이나 적군으로서 정체성이 확인되어야 한다는 것이다. 빈칸 뒤의 'as either friend or enemy'와 호응하며, 관객이 감정적으로 몰입할 수 있도록 '식별 가능한(identifiable)' 상태가 되어야 함을 의미하므로 ②번이 가장 적절하다.
options_translation: ① 신뢰할 수 있는
② 식별 가능한
③ 호환되는
④ 주목할 만한
⑤ 아는 것이 많은

questions.question: 20. 다음 글의 제목으로 가장 적절한 것은? [3.8점]
questions.passage: Let's assume that at least some animals are capable of thinking despite lacking a language. This doesn't necessarily mean that they possess concepts, for some forms of thought may be nonconceptual. We can imagine, for instance, a squirrel who is planning how to get from the branch she's currently standing on to a branch from the tree in front. To do this, in principle she doesn't need a concept of branch nor a concept of tree. It might be enough for her to have, for example, the ability to think in images; to make a mental map of the tree where she can imagine and try out different routes. This doesn't imply that squirrels lack concepts, simply that they don't need them for this concrete form of thinking. For us to be able to say that an animal has concepts, we have to show not just that she's capable of thinking, but also that she has certain specific abilities.
options: ① Exploring Nonconceptual Thought in Animals
② How Squirrels Use Language to Navigate Trees
③ The Evolution of Language and Animal Cognition
④ The Role of Long-term Memory in Animal Survival
⑤ The Reason All Thinking Requires Conceptual Understanding
questions.explanation: 글은 언어가 없는 동물들도 사고가 가능하며, 이러한 사고의 일부 형태는 개념을 필요로 하지 않는 '비개념적 사고(nonconceptual thought)'일 수 있음을 다람쥐의 사례를 통해 설명하고 있다. 따라서 동물의 비개념적 사고를 탐구하는 내용인 ①번이 제목으로 가장 적절하다.
options_translation: ① 동물의 비개념적 사고 탐구
② 다람쥐가 나무를 타기 위해 언어를 사용하는 방법
③ 언어와 동물 인지의 진화
④ 동물 생존에서 장기 기억의 역할
⑤ 모든 사고가 개념적 이해를 필요로 하는 이유

questions.question: 21. 다음 글의 내용을 한 문장으로 요약하려 할 때, 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은? [4.7점]
questions.passage: Piaget put the same amount of water into two different glasses: a tall narrow glass and a wide glass, then asked kids to compare two glasses. Kids younger than six or seven usually say that the tall narrow glass now holds more water, because the level is higher. And when they are ready, they figure out the conservation of volume for themselves just by playing with cups of water. Piaget argued that children's understanding of morality is like their understanding of those water glasses: we can't say that it is innate or kids learn it directly from adults. Rather, it is self-constructed as kids play with other kids. Taking turns in a game is like pouring water back and forth between glasses. Once kids have reached the age of five or six, then playing games and working things out together will help them learn about fairness far more effectively than any teaching from adults.
questions.summary_sentence: Piaget argued that children naturally construct their ( A ) _________ primarily through ( B ) _________, rather than relying on direct instruction from adults.
options: ① sense of fairness ... explicit practice
② self-confidence ... social engagement with peers
③ moral sense ... peer interactions
④ social skills ... clear parental guidelines
⑤ knowledge ... imitating role models
questions.explanation: 피아제는 아이들의 도덕성(morality) 이해가 성인의 가르침보다는 다른 아이들과의 놀이 및 상호작용을 통해 스스로 구축된다고 주장했다. 따라서 (A)에는 moral sense(도덕적 감각), (B)에는 peer interactions(또래와의 상호작용)이 들어가는 것이 가장 적절하다.
options_translation: ① 공정함에 대한 감각 ... 명시적인 연습
② 자신감 ... 또래와의 사회적 참여
③ 도덕적 감각 ... 또래와의 상호작용
④ 사회적 기술 ... 명확한 부모의 지침
⑤ 지식 ... 역할 모델 모방

questions.question: 22. 다음 글의 내용을 한 문장으로 요약하려 할 때, 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은? [4.8점]
questions.passage: Some researchers view spoken languages as incomplete devices for capturing precise differences. They think numbers represent the most neutral language of description. However, when our language of description is changed to numbers, we do not move toward greater accuracy. Numbers are no more appropriate 'pictures of the world' than words, music, or painting. While useful for specific purposes (e.g. census taking, income distribution), they <u>eliminate information of enormous value.</u> For example, the future lives of young students are tied to their scores on national tests. In effect, whether they can continue with their education, where, and at what cost depends importantly on a handful of numbers. These numbers do not account for the quality of schools they have attended, whether they have been tutored, have supportive parents, have test anxiety, and so on. Finally, putting aside the many ways in which statistical results can be manipulated, there are ways in which turning people's lives into numbers is morally insulating. Statistics on crime, homelessness, or the spread of a disease say nothing of people's suffering. We read the statistics as reports on events at a distance, thus allowing us to escape without being disturbed. Statistics are human beings with the tears wiped off.
questions.summary_sentence: Numbers have long been regarded as one of the most neutral forms of language by some researchers. However, this perception has changed. It turns out that numbers don't always (A)__________ much about how outcomes are produced or their effects. Therefore, we need to be (B)________ when interpreting and using statistics.
options: ① tell ... pathetic
② ignore ... honest
③ reveal ... cautious
④ indicate ... objective
⑤ demonstrate ... cynical
questions.explanation: 이 글은 숫자가 정보를 중립적으로 보여준다는 생각과 달리, 실제로는 많은 가치 있는 정보(학교의 질, 부모의 지원, 고통 등)를 배제한다는 점을 지적하고 있습니다. 따라서 숫자가 결과의 과정이나 영향에 대해 많은 것을 '드러내지(reveal)' 않으며, 통계를 해석할 때 '조심(cautious)'해야 한다는 요약이 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 말해주다 ... 불쌍한
② 무시하다 ... 정직한
③ 드러내다 ... 조심스러운
④ 나타내다 ... 객관적인
⑤ 입증하다 ... 냉소적인

questions.question: 23. 다음 글의 내용과 일치하지 않는 것은? [4.6점]
questions.passage: One of the most striking characteristics of a sleeping animal or person is that they do not respond normally to environmental stimuli. If you open the eyelids of a sleeping mammal the eyes will not see normally —they are functionally blind. Some visual information apparently gets in, but it is not normally processed as it is shortened or weakened: same with the other sensing systems. Stimuli are registered but not processed normally and they fail to wake the individual. Perceptual disengagement probably serves the function of protecting sleep, so some authors do not count it as part of the definition of sleep itself. But as sleep would be impossible without it, it seems essential to its definition. Nevertheless, many animals (including humans) use the intermediate state of drowsiness to derive some benefits of sleep without total perceptual disengagement.
options: ① During sleep, stimuli are sensed but not fully processed.
② Perceptual disengagement helps animals protect their sleep.
③ All sensory information is completely blocked during sleep.
④ Sleeping mammals cannot see clearly even if their eyes are open.
⑤ Some animals benefit from drowsiness without fully disconnecting from their senses.
questions.explanation: 지문에서 'Some visual information apparently gets in'(일부 시각 정보는 분명히 들어온다)라고 언급하며 감각 정보가 완전히 차단되는 것이 아니라 등록은 되되 정상적으로 처리되지 않는 것임을 설명하고 있으므로, 모든 정보가 완전히 차단된다는 ③번은 내용과 일치하지 않습니다.
options_translation: ① 수면 중에 자극은 감지되지만 완전히 처리되지는 않는다.
② 지각적 이탈은 동물이 잠을 보호하는 데 도움이 된다.
③ 수면 중에는 모든 감각 정보가 완전히 차단된다.
④ 잠자는 포유류는 눈을 뜨고 있어도 명확하게 볼 수 없다.
⑤ 일부 동물들은 감각에서 완전히 단절되지 않은 채 기면 상태에서 이득을 얻는다.

questions.question: 24. 다음 글에서 필자가 주장하는 바로 가장 적절한 것은? [3.7점]
questions.passage: A number of research studies have shown how experts in a field often experience difficulties when introducing newcomers to that field. For example, in a genuine training situation, Dr Pamela Hinds found that people expert in using mobile phones were remarkably less accurate than novice phone users in judging how long it takes people to learn to use the phones. Experts can become insensitive to how hard a task is for the beginner, an effect referred to as the 'curse of knowledge'. Dr Hinds was able to show that as people acquired the skill, they then began to underestimate the level of difficulty of that skill. Her participants even underestimated how long it had taken themselves to acquire that skill in an earlier session. Knowing that experts forget how hard it was for them to learn, we can understand the need to look at the learning process through students' eyes, rather than making assumptions about how students 'should be' learning.
options: ① Novices tend to underestimate their ability to learn new technology.
② Experts can predict how long a beginner will take to master a skill.
③ Learners should always try to view tasks from an expert's perspective.
④ The difficulty of learning decreases significantly as learners gain expertise.
⑤ Experts need to consider beginners' perspectives to effectively guide learners.
questions.explanation: 글의 마지막 문장에서 전문가들이 배우는 과정이 얼마나 힘들었는지 잊어버린다는 점을 고려할 때, 학생들이 어떻게 배워야 한다는 가정을 하기보다 학생들의 눈높이에서 학습 과정을 바라볼 필요가 있다고 명시하고 있습니다. 따라서 전문가들이 초보자를 효과적으로 지도하기 위해 그들의 관점을 고려해야 한다는 ⑤번이 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 초보자들은 새로운 기술을 배우는 자신의 능력을 과소평가하는 경향이 있다.
② 전문가들은 초보자가 기술을 습득하는 데 얼마나 걸릴지 예측할 수 있다.
③ 학습자들은 항상 전문가의 관점에서 과업을 바라보려고 노력해야 한다.
④ 학습자가 전문성을 얻음에 따라 학습의 난이도는 현저히 감소한다.
⑤ 전문가들은 학습자들을 효과적으로 안내하기 위해 초보자들의 관점을 고려할 필요가 있다.

questions.question: 25. 다음 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은? [3.5점]
questions.passage: In many sports, people realized the difficulties and even impossibilities of young children participating fully in many adult sport environments. They found the road to success for young children is unlikely if they play on adult fields, courts or arenas with equipment that is too large, too heavy or too fast for them to handle while trying to compete in adult style competition. Common sense has prevailed. ___________________. As examples, baseball has T ball, football has flag football and junior soccer uses a smaller and lighter ball and (sometimes) a smaller field. All have junior competitive structures where children play for shorter time periods and often in smaller teams. In a similar way tennis has adapted the court areas, balls and rackets to make them more appropriate for children under 10. The adaptations are progressive and relate to the age of the child.
options: ① Consistent and focused practice plays a vital role in achieving success in any sport.
② Children can also enjoy sports environments designed for adults.
③ Facing difficulties is necessary for young children who play sports.
④ Different sports have made adaptations for children.
⑤ Encouraging sports for children is inappropriate.
questions.explanation: 빈칸 뒤의 내용에서 야구의 T볼, 미식축구의 플래그 풋볼, 주니어 축구의 작고 가벼운 공과 경기장, 테니스의 코트 및 라켓 조정 등 여러 스포츠가 어린이들을 위해 어떻게 변형(adaptation)되었는지 예시를 들고 있으므로, 빈칸에는 ④번 '다양한 스포츠들이 아이들을 위해 적응(변형)을 해왔다'가 들어가는 것이 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 일관되고 집중적인 연습은 어떤 스포츠에서든 성공을 거두는 데 중요한 역할을 한다.
② 아이들도 성인을 위해 설계된 스포츠 환경을 즐길 수 있다.
③ 스포츠를 하는 어린 아이들에게 어려움에 직면하는 것은 필요하다.
④ 다양한 스포츠들이 아이들을 위해 변형(적응)을 해왔다.
⑤ 아이들을 위한 스포츠 장려는 부적절하다.

questions.question: 26. 글의 흐름으로 보아, 주어진 문장이 들어가기에 가장 적절한 곳은? [3.6점]
questions.passage: The tongue was mapped into separate areas where certain tastes were registered: sweetness at the tip, sourness on the sides, and bitterness at the back of the mouth. ( ① ) Research in the 1980s and 1990s, however, demonstrated that the "tongue map" explanation of how we taste was, in fact, totally wrong. ( ② ) Today, leading taste researchers believe that taste buds are not grouped according to specialty. ( ③ ) Sweetness, saltiness, bitterness, and sourness can be tasted everywhere in the mouth, although they may be perceived at a little different intensities at different sites. ( ④ ) Moreover, the mechanism at work is not place, but time. ( ⑤ ) It's not that you taste sweetness at the tip of your tongue, but rather that you register that perception first.
questions.insertion_sentence: As it turns out, the map was a misinterpretation and mistranslation of research conducted in Germany at the turn of the twentieth century.
questions.explanation: 주어진 문장은 그 지도(혀 지도)가 20세기 전환기에 독일에서 수행된 연구의 오해와 오역이었다는 내용을 담고 있습니다. ①번 문장에서 1980~90년대 연구가 혀 지도 설명이 완전히 틀렸음을 입증했다는 내용이 나온 뒤, 왜 틀렸는지에 대한 배경 설명으로 주어진 문장이 들어가는 것이 자연스럽습니다. 이후 ②번 뒤의 '오늘날'의 연구 결과로 내용이 이어집니다.

questions.question: 5. 다음 글의 주제로 가장 적절한 것은? [3.8점]
questions.passage: Dictionaries are relatively good resources for anyone interested in finding out what a word means. Using one set of words to define another word is called a lexical definition. But it's important to understand the limits of dictionary definitions. More often than not, a definition in a dictionary requires readers to have a fairly robust understanding of the language already at their disposal. In other words, a dictionary functions in many cases as a cross-reference or translator between words one knows and words that one doesn't yet know. Even the most obscure words in a dictionary, say, for example, "pulchritudinous" or "kalokagathia," must be defined using words that the reader already knows and understands. Otherwise, the dictionary isn't very helpful.
options: ① Dictionary definitions are often circular and thus not reliable for accurate word meanings.
② Readers should memorize obscure words like "pulchritudinous" to expand their vocabulary.
③ Lexical definitions are clearer than other types of definitions and are more suitable for beginners.
④ Dictionaries are limited in usefulness because they rely on the reader's existing language knowledge.
⑤ Dictionaries are best suited for advanced users because they define words using other complex words.
questions.explanation: 이 글은 사전 정의가 독자가 이미 알고 있는 언어 지식에 의존하기 때문에 한계가 있다는 점을 설명하고 있습니다. 따라서 ④번 '사전은 독자의 기존 언어 지식에 의존하기 때문에 유용성에 한계가 있다'가 주제로 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 사전 정의는 종종 순환적이며 따라서 정확한 단어 의미를 파악하는 데 신뢰할 수 없다.
② 독자들은 어휘력을 확장하기 위해 "pulchritudinous"와 같은 모호한 단어들을 암기해야 한다.
③ 어휘적 정의는 다른 유형의 정의보다 명확하며 초보자에게 더 적합하다.
④ 사전은 독자의 기존 언어 지식에 의존하기 때문에 유용성에 한계가 있다.
⑤ 사전은 다른 복잡한 단어를 사용하여 단어를 정의하기 때문에 숙련된 사용자에게 가장 적합하다.

questions.question: 6. 다음 ⓐ~ⓔ중, 밑줄 친 <A>의 예시로 적절한 것을 모두 고른 것은? [4.3점]
questions.passage:
Despite the difference between the past and the future, between what has happened and what is to come, it can be suggested that our sense of the past has always been influenced by our view of the future. Revolutionaries have always looked to the past to frame their future cause, as is amply illustrated by examples from nationalism to communism. The future has often been seen as variously a recovery of a lost time, as a replication of what is established, or as a model bequeathed by a heroic age long gone. The writing of history is based on understanding or explaining future outcomes that were not known to contemporaries, since the historian has the benefit of hindsight and the past is nothing more than the accumulation of futures that are now our past. So, rather than see the hand of the past always shaping the future, perhaps it can be seen in reverse, <u><A> with the past - in the sense of our understanding of it - being shaped by our orientation to the future.</u>

ⓐ Early Zionist thinkers projected a future homeland in Palestine and, in doing so, revisited biblical narratives to construct a historical claim. Their future-driven vision infused ancient texts with renewed political meaning.

ⓑ Civil rights activists in the 1960s reinterpreted the American founding documents, such as the Declaration of Independence, not just as historical texts but as moral blueprints for a more just and equal future. Their vision of civil equality shaped how they understood and invoked the past.

ⓒ A historian analyzing feudal Europe focuses strictly on original documents and artifacts from that era, deliberately avoiding contemporary political frameworks or future-oriented narratives. His goal is to reconstruct the past as it was, not as it is imagined from any future standpoint.

ⓓ Renaissance humanists, envisioning a revival of classical learning, interpreted ancient Roman texts not merely as relics but as a guide for the intellectual rebirth of their own time. Their aspiration to rebuild civilization influenced their selective admiration of the past.

ⓔ In post-colonial contexts, some historians prioritized preserving factual accuracy by strictly relying on archival evidence from the colonial period, deliberately avoiding nationalistic interpretations or future-oriented narratives. Their focus remained on objectively reconstructing what happened, regardless of modern identity-building efforts.
questions.explanation:
밑줄 친 <A>는 '과거에 대한 우리의 이해가 미래에 대한 우리의 지향에 의해 형성된다'는 의미를 담고 있습니다. 
ⓐ 시오니스트 사상가들이 미래의 고국(미래 지향)을 위해 성서적 서술을 재방문(과거 이해의 형성)했다는 내용은 적절한 예시입니다. 
ⓑ 인권 운동가들이 정의로운 미래를 위한 청사진(미래 지향)으로 독립선언문 등을 재해석(과거 이해의 형성)했다는 내용은 적절한 예시입니다.
ⓒ는 미래 지향적 서술을 배제하고 과거를 있는 그대로 재구성하려 하므로 반대되는 사례입니다. 
ⓓ 르네상스 인문주의자들이 지적 부흥(미래 지향)을 위해 로마 텍스트를 지침으로 해석(과거 이해의 형성)했다는 내용은 적절한 예시입니다.
ⓔ는 미래 지향적 서술을 피하고 객관적 재구성에 집중하므로 반대되는 사례입니다. 
따라서 ⓐ, ⓑ, ⓓ가 포함된 ①번이 정답입니다.

questions.question: 7. 글의 흐름으로 보아, 주어진 문장이 들어가기에 가장 적절한 곳은? [3.8점]
questions.passage: When we realize we've said something in error and we pause to go back to correct it, we stop gesturing a couple of hundred milliseconds before we stop speaking. ( ① ) Gesture can mentally prime a word so that the right term comes to our lips. ( ② ) When people are prevented from gesturing, they talk less fluently; their speech becomes halting because their hands are no longer able to supply them with the next word, and the next. ( ③ ) Not being able to gesture has other deleterious effects: without gesture to help our mental processes along, we remember less useful information, we solve problems less well, and we are less able to explain our thinking. ( ④ ) Far from tagging along as speech's clumsy companion, gesture represents the leading edge of our thought. ( ⑤ )
questions.insertion_sentence: Such sequences suggest the startling notion that our hands "know" what we're going to say before our conscious minds do, and in fact this is often the case.
questions.explanation: 글의 첫 번째 문장에서 우리가 실수를 교정하기 위해 말을 멈추기 수백 밀리초 전에 몸짓을 먼저 멈춘다는 시간적 순서(sequence)를 설명하고 있습니다. 주어진 문장의 'Such sequences'는 바로 이 현상을 가리키며, 우리의 손이 의식적인 마음보다 먼저 할 말을 알고 있다는 놀라운 개념을 제시합니다. 따라서 ①번 위치가 가장 적절합니다.

questions.question: 8. 다음 글의 내용을 한 문장으로 요약하고자 한다. 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은? [4.3점]
questions.passage: The governments of virtually every country on the planet attach great importance to achieving food security, and a wide variety of mechanisms have been developed to realize this goal. The first issue governments face in achieving national food security is the problem of ensuring that adequate amounts of food are available to the resident population. Some governments have set goals of food self-sufficiency, which means most, if not all, of the food available in a country comes from the domestic farming system. However, food security does not require food self-sufficiency because countries can import food items not easily produced within the country. Agricultural products are, after all, highly sensitive to climatic, soil, and other conditions that tend to vary around the world. Even countries with extremely productive agricultural sectors are not fully self-sufficient in all food items. The United States, for example, depends on imports for its supply of coffee, tea, bananas, and other tropical products. In general, the problem of assuring adequate food supplies is solved by relying on both domestic production and imports.
questions.summary_sentence: Food security is a major concern for governments around the world, and while some aim for food self-sufficiency, it is important to recognize that (A)_________ is not a necessary condition for (B)_________ as many countries rely on a combination of domestic production and imports to ensure stable food supplies.
options: ① agricultural trade ... food production
② domestic consumption ... food exports
③ food self-sufficiency ... food security
④ economic self-reliance ... international trade
⑤ population growth ... agricultural surplus
questions.explanation: 본문에서 식량 안보(food security)를 달성하기 위해 식량 자급자족(food self-sufficiency)이 반드시 필요한 조건은 아니며, 국내 생산과 수입을 병행하여 식량 공급을 확보할 수 있다고 설명하고 있다. 따라서 (A)에는 food self-sufficiency, (B)에는 food security가 적절하다.
options_translation: ① 농업 무역 ... 식품 생산
② 국내 소비 ... 식품 수출
③ 식량 자급자족 ... 식량 안보
④ 경제적 자립 ... 국제 무역

questions.question: 9. 다음 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은? [4.3점]
questions.passage:
By 1900, although a full decade had passed since electric systems first emerged as a viable option for manufacturers, electricity accounted for less than 5 percent of the power used in industrial facilities. Nevertheless, the continuous innovation by equipment suppliers rendered electric motors and systems increasingly cost-effective and dependable.
Coupled with aggressive promotional campaigns, these advancements facilitated the swift uptake of electrical power across factories. Contributing further to this shift was the burgeoning population of trained electrical engineers, whose expertise enabled the successful installation and operation of complex systems. In a relatively short span of time, electricity transitioned from being a technological novelty to an integral part of industrial life. Yet, despite these developments, one entrenched practice endured: manufacturers overwhelmingly preferred to generate their own electricity onsite. The idea of purchasing power from local central stations - which were primarily intended to illuminate residences and small businesses - was largely dismissed. These stations lacked both the capacity and technical sophistication to meet the demands of large-scale manufacturing operations. Moreover, factory owners, long accustomed to controlling their own power supply, were reluctant to entrust such a vital function to external providers. The risks were too great: even a brief interruption could paralyze production, while frequent disruptions could spell financial disaster. As the century turned, surveys revealed the extent of this mindset-approximately 50,000 private power plants were in operation, vastly outnumbering the 3,600 central stations. However, this dynamic began to change as central stations expanded their capabilities and improved reliability. With significant advancements in transmission technology, electricity could now travel extended distances with minimal loss, allowing central providers to serve industrial clients more effectively. The prospect of obtaining electricity from a centralized supplier grew more appealing, thanks to both the cost savings and the convenience it offered. Eventually, even the most risk-averse manufacturers began to phase out their self-sufficient power setups, ushering in __________________________________________.
*entrenched 고착된
options: ① a revival of traditional mechanical power systems
② the decline of electric power as a viable energy source
③ an era of shared innovation between factories and suppliers
④ a period of isolation from external technological developments
⑤ a new era marked by widespread industrial reliance on public utility companies

⑤ 공공 유틸리티 회사에 대한 광범위한 산업적 의존으로 특징지어지는 새로운 시대

questions.question: 10. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 어법상 틀린 것은? [3.7점]
questions.passage: It is essential to understand ① <u>that</u>, while science follows a rule-based methodology, it is also deeply rooted in creativity. A conjecture, for instance, is not merely a logical step but a philosophical invention ― one that the mind mysteriously generates through a process we might describe as thoughtful contemplation. Yet, a hypothesis remains ② <u>speculative</u> until it has been rigorously tested against reality; at that stage, it is not knowledge but rather an informed guess. True knowledge ③ <u>arising</u> when information has proven its value through repeated validation. It is what persists after multiple cycles of experimentation have eliminated inaccurate or unfounded theories. As researchers continuously refine their hypotheses and adjust their models in response to ④ <u>unexpected</u> or novel data, they engage in a feedback process that statisticians refer to as Bayesian updating. This concept, grounded in Bayes' Rule ― formulated by 18th-century English statistician and philosopher Thomas Bayes ― describes a mathematical procedure ⑤ <u>in which</u> a theory or predictive model becomes progressively more accurate through the repeated testing of its variations.
questions.explanation: ③의 'arising'은 주어인 'True knowledge'에 연결되는 본동사 자리이므로, 시제와 수에 맞춰 'arises'가 되어야 적절합니다.

Quite often the interaction between groups is socially unequal, and this is reflected in the fact that in many cases borrowing of words or constructions goes mostly or entirely in one direction, from the more powerful or prestigious group to the less favored one. The languages of socially ⓐ <u>subordinated</u> groups may from quite an early period of contact provide terminology for objects or practices with which speakers of the more powerful group were previously unfamiliar, but the effects of contact in that direction may not progress any further than this. In some cases, as with the Dharug language of Sydney, Australia, the source of some of the earliest loans from Indigenous Australian languages into English, the fate of the language system is extinction after the obliteration of many of its speakers. The remainder shifted to varieties of English, the language of the people who had ⓑ <u>suppressed</u> them.
This asymmetry in linguistic influence reflects deeper patterns of dominance and marginalization. While dominant groups may take selected elements from subordinated languages-often in ways that strip them of their original cultural significance-they rarely ⓒ <u>adopt</u> the grammatical structures or deeper linguistic frameworks of these languages. Meanwhile, speakers of the less powerful group frequently experience pressure to ⓓ <u>abandon</u> their own language in favor of the dominant one, especially in education, employment, and public life. Over time, this can lead to a gradual ⓔ <u>expansion</u> of linguistic diversity and a loss of cultural identity tied to the endangered language.

questions.question: 14. 다음을 읽고 주어진 표에서 옳지 않은 것은? [2.8점]
questions.passage: There are reasons why science is not fully trusted and why healthy skepticism and critical thinking are essential. In spite of professional standards, claims of objectivity, and the peer review process, the conduct of science can be biased. All experts are not the same, nor do they submit their work to the same scrutiny. Knowing the source of funding can be important in evaluating scientific claims. For example, the Harvard researchers who made claims in the late 1960s about the problems with dietary fat, leading the nation away from perceiving sugar as one of the main causes in health problems, were funded in part by the sugar industry. The authors did not reveal their funding source to the New England Journal of Medicine, where their influential article appeared. Their article shaped a generation of changes in eating patterns that appears to have fostered higher use of sugar, now widely implicated as a source of the rise in obesity and diabetes. Stories such as this one fuel suspicion - but also lead to further safeguards in the scientific process. Funding disclosures, although not required five decades ago, have since been made compulsory.
options: ① How Peer Review Guarantees Scientific Truth
② Science can be biased despite claims of objectivity and peer review.
③ Funding sources can influence scientific outcomes.
④ Historical example: sugar industry's influence on dietary science.
⑤ Past mistakes led to better rules, like disclosure of funding.
questions.explanation: 본문에서 과학은 전문가적 기준, 객관성 주장, 그리고 동료 검토 과정(peer review process)에도 불구하고 편향될 수 있다고 기술하고 있습니다. 따라서 동료 검토가 과학적 진실을 보장한다는 내용인 ①번은 글의 내용과 일치하지 않으며 제목으로 적절하지 않습니다.

③ 자금 출처는 과학적 결과에 영향을 미칠 수 있다.
④ 역사적 사례: 설탕 산업이 식단 과학에 미친 영향.

questions.question: 18. 윗글을 바탕으로 추론한 내용으로 옳은 것은? [3.8점]
questions.passage:
Everybody is unique. However, there have been many attempts to classify people's personalities. One of the most common methods divides people into two types, introverts and extroverts. According to this division, introverts are apt to be drawn to the internal world of thoughts and feelings, while extroverts are drawn to the external world of people and activities. Introverts recharge their batteries by spending some time alone; extroverts need to recharge when they do not socialize enough.
Extroverts are good at carrying out tasks under pressure and handling multiple jobs concurrently. Introverts, on the other hand, like to focus on one task at a time and can concentrate very well. Extroverts tend to do assignments quickly. They make fast decisions and are comfortable with taking risks. Introverts often work more slowly and deliberately. They think before they act, give up less easily, and work more precisely.
Based on all this information, you might think that introverts and extroverts do not get along. However, they actually work well together because their personalities complement each other. Sometimes they can even accomplish great things when they team up. Let's take a look at some famous examples!
options: ① The personality types are primarily determined by external factors such as upbringing and environment.
② The tendency of extroverts to thrive under pressure enables them to manage multiple responsibilities simultaneously with a significant decline in performance.
③ Introverts' meticulous approach to work, characterized by thoughtful planning and precision, often leads to highly accurate outcomes.
④ Introverts and extroverts are rarely capable of successful collaboration due to their fundamentally conflicting personality traits.
⑤ Extroverts are less likely to act impulsively, instead engaging in prudent contemplation before taking action.
questions.explanation: 본문에서 내향주의자는 행동하기 전에 생각하고, 덜 쉽게 포기하며, 더 정확하게 일한다(work more precisely)고 언급되어 있습니다. 따라서 ③번의 '정교한 계획과 정밀함으로 특징지어지는 내향주의자의 꼼꼼한 업무 방식이 종종 매우 정확한 결과로 이어진다'는 진술은 본문에 근거하여 타당하게 추론할 수 있는 내용입니다.

④ 내향주의자와 외향주의자는 근본적으로 상충하는 성격 특성 때문에 성공적인 협업을 거의 할 수 없다.
