questions.question:
20. 주어진 글 다음에 이어질 글의 순서로 가장 적절한 것은?
[3.7점]
questions.passage: As a general rule, it's better if your definition corresponds as closely as possible to the way in which the term is ordinarily used in the kinds of debates to which your claims are pertinent.
ordered_passages: (A) For example, we do not have a term in ordinary language that describes a memory that is not necessarily a memory of something the person having it has experienced. Such a thing would occur, for example, if I could somehow share your memories: I would have a memory-type experience, but this would not be of something that I had actually experienced.
(B) To call this a memory would be misleading. For this reason, philosophers have coined the special term 'quasi-memory' to refer to these hypothetical memory-like experiences.

(C) There will be, however, occasions where it is appropriate, even necessary, to coin special uses through what philosophers call stimulative definition. This would be the case where the current lexicon is not able to make distinctions that you think are philosophically important.
questions.explanation: 주어진 글에서는 용어가 보통 사용되는 방식에 가깝게 정의하는 것이 좋다고 언급한다. (C)에서는 하지만 특별한 정의가 필요한 경우가 있으며, 기존 어휘로 구분할 수 없는 철학적으로 중요한 구분이 필요할 때라고 설명한다. (A)에서는 이에 대한 구체적인 예시로 본인이 경험하지 않은 기억에 대한 용어가 없음을 언급하고, (B)에서 이러한 것을 그냥 기억이라 부르는 것은 오해의 소지가 있으므로 철학자들이 'quasi-memory(준기억)'이라는 용어를 고안했음을 설명하며 마무리하는 것이 자연스럽다.

questions.question: 22. 주어진 글 다음에 이어질 글의 순서로 가장 적절한 것은? [2.8점]
questions.passage: Beethoven's drive to create something novel is a reflection of his state of curiosity. Our brains experience a sense of reward when we create something new in the process of exploring something uncertain, such as a musical phrase that we've never played or heard before.
ordered_passages: (A) In other words, Beethoven's music became less predictable over time as his curiosity drove the exploration of new musical ideas. Curiosity is a powerful driver of human creativity.
(B) When our curiosity leads to something novel, the resulting reward brings us a sense of pleasure. A number of investigators have modeled how curiosity influences musical composition.

(C) In the case of Beethoven, computer modeling focused on the thirty-two piano sonatas written after age thirteen revealed that the musical patterns found in all of Beethoven's music decreased in later sonatas, while novel patterns, including patterns that were unique to a particular sonata, increased.
questions.explanation: 주어진 글에서 불확실한 것을 탐구하는 과정에서 새로운 것을 창조할 때 보상을 느낀다고 설명한 뒤, (B)에서 그 보상이 즐거움을 주며 호기심이 음악적 구성에 어떻게 영향을 미치는지 모델링했다는 내용으로 이어진다. (C)에서는 베토벤의 소나타를 분석한 컴퓨터 모델링의 구체적인 결과(후기 소나타로 갈수록 새로운 패턴 증가)를 제시하고, (A)에서 '즉(In other words)'을 통해 베토벤의 음악이 시간이 지남에 따라 덜 예측 가능해졌으며 호기심이 창의성의 강력한 동력이라는 결론을 맺는 것이 자연스럽다.

questions.question: 23. 글의 흐름으로 보아, 주어진 문장이 들어가기에 가장 적절한 곳은? [2.8점]
questions.passage: Dancers often push themselves to the limits of their physical capabilities. But that push is misguided if it is directed toward accomplishing something physically impossible. ( ① ) For instance, a tall dancer with long feet may wish to perform repetitive vertical jumps to fast music, pointing his feet while in the air and lowering his heels to the floor between jumps. ( ② ) But a short-footed dancer may have no trouble! ( ③ ) Another dancer may be struggling to complete a half-turn in the air. ( ④ ) Understanding the connection between a rapid turn rate and the alignment of the body close to the rotation axis tells her how to accomplish her turn successfully. ( ⑤ ) In both of these cases, understanding and working within the constraints imposed by nature and described by physical laws allows dancers to work efficiently, minimizing potential risk of injury.
questions.insertion_sentence: That may be impossible no matter how strong the dancer is.
questions.explanation: 주어진 문장의 'That'은 ①번 문장에서 설명한 '긴 발을 가진 키 큰 무용수가 빠른 음악에 맞춰 반복적인 수직 점프를 하며 공중에서 발가락을 세우고 점프 사이에 뒤꿈치를 바닥에 내리는 동작'을 가리킨다. 이 동작은 무용수가 아무리 강하더라도 [물리적으로] 불가능할 수 있다는 내용이 들어가야 뒤에 나오는 '하지만 발이 짧은 무용수는 문제가 없을 수도 있다(But a short-footed dancer may have no trouble!)'라는 대조적인 내용과 자연스럽게 연결된다.

questions.question: 24. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 어법상 틀린 것은? [2.8점]
questions.passage: Fans who are inclined to spend a lot of time ① <u>thinking</u> about what athletes owe them as fans should also think about the corresponding obligations ② <u>that</u> fans might have as fans. One who thinks only about what they are entitled to receive from their friends without ever giving a moment's thought to what they owe their friends ③ <u>are</u>, to put it mildly, not exactly setting the best example. Similarly, fans who only think about what athletes owe them without ever thinking about what they owe to athletes have failed ④ <u>to take</u> the fan/athlete relationship all that seriously. As in nearly every other area of human life, whatever special rights fans may possess are limited by a corresponding set of obligations, and fans who never think about how they can be better fans even as they ⑤ <u>confidently</u> opine about what athletes owe them are hardly fulfilling their end of the bargain.
questions.explanation: ③번 문장의 주어는 'One'으로 단수 대명사이다. 따라서 동사인 'are'는 단수형인 'is'로 고쳐야 한다. 참고로 ①은 'spend time ~ing' 구문, ②는 목적격 관계대명사, ④는 'failed to부정사', ⑤는 동사 'opine'을 수식하는 부사로 모두 적절하다.

questions.question: 25. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은? [2.8점]
questions.passage: The ① <u>emphasis</u> on the social dimension in food writing might suggest that the flavor of food is taking a back seat. I suspect that most people view flavor as of ② <u>subordinate</u> importance in social settings where food is served. Although our social gatherings coalesce around food, the meaning of these gatherings does not seem to depend on flavor. Flavor assists with the ③ <u>limited</u> purpose of filling the belly. Once that is accomplished, it provides the ④ <u>context</u> for whatever social dynamics characterize the gathering. These can be understood ⑤ <u>depending</u> on the flavor of the food on offer, the appreciation of which is understood to be personal and subjective. According to this conventional wisdom, the ceremonies and rituals around food, the social events that supply food with its meaning, do not rely on the quality of sensations provided by the food. To focus excessively on flavor is to miss the larger significance of these social relations.
questions.explanation: 글 전체의 맥락은 음식의 맛보다는 사회적 관계가 더 중요하다는 통념을 설명하고 있다. 특히 뒤 문장에서 사회적 행사가 음식의 맛에 '의존하지 않는다(do not rely on)'고 언급하고 있으므로, 사회적 역동성은 음식의 맛에 '관계없이(independently of / regardless of)' 이해될 수 있다는 내용이 되어야 한다. 따라서 'depending'은 적절하지 않다.

questions.question:
26. 다음 밑줄 친 <A>에 대한 예시 중 적절하지 않은 것은?
[3.8점]
questions.passage: Technologists are always on the lookout for quantifiable metrics. Measurable inputs to a model are their lifeblood, and like a social scientist, a technologist needs to identify concrete measures, or "proxies," for assessing progress. This need for quantifiable proxies produces a bias toward measuring things that are easy to quantify. But simple metrics can take us further away from the important goals we really care about, which may require complicated metrics or be extremely difficult, or perhaps impossible, to reduce to any measure. And when we have imperfect or bad proxies, we can easily fall under the illusion that we are solving for a good end without actually making genuine progress toward a worthy solution. <A> <u>The problem of proxies results in technologists frequently substituting what is measurable for what is meaningful.</u> As the saying goes, "Not everything that counts can be counted, and not everything that can be counted counts."
options: ① A financial analyst used real-time market data and complex algorithms to predict stock trends, leading to more stable investment strategies.
② An educational platform designer used test scores as a measure of learning but found that students were memorizing answers without understanding concepts.
③ A social media company used time spent on the platform as a sign of success, but this led to designs that promoted addictive behavior rather than meaningful user engagement.
④ A health app developer focused on step count as a sign of user health but failed to consider that users could cheat the system or that steps alone don't represent overall wellness.
⑤ A climate data analyst relied on CO₂ levels as the only indicator of environmental health, but was criticized for ignoring biodiversity and ecosystem stability, which are less easily measured.
questions.explanation: 밑줄 친 <A>의 내용은 '측정 가능한 것(지표)'이 '의미 있는 것(본질)'을 대체하면서 발생하는 문제에 대한 설명입니다. ②, ③, ④, ⑤는 모두 수치화하기 쉬운 지표(시험 점수, 체류 시간, 걸음 수, CO2 농도)에 집중하다가 정작 중요한 본질적 가치를 놓치게 된 부정적인 사례들이나, ①번은 시장 데이터와 알고리즘을 활용해 안정적인 투자 전략이라는 긍정적인 결과를 도출한 사례이므로 적절하지 않습니다.
options_translation: ① 금융 분석가가 실시간 시장 데이터와 복잡한 알고리즘을 사용하여 주식 동향을 예측함으로써 더 안정적인 투자 전략을 이끌어냈다.
② 교육 플랫폼 설계자가 시험 점수를 학습의 척도로 사용했으나 학생들이 개념 이해 없이 답만 암기하고 있다는 것을 발견했다.
③ 소셜 미디어 회사가 플랫폼에서 보낸 시간을 성공의 신호로 사용했으나, 이것이 의미 있는 사용자 참여보다는 중독적 행동을 조장하는 디자인으로 이어졌다.
④ 건강 앱 개발자가 사용자의 건강 지표로 걸음 수에 집중했으나, 사용자들이 시스템을 속일 수 있다는 점이나 걸음 수만으로는 전반적인 건강을 나타내지 못한다는 점을 고려하지 못했다.
⑤ 기후 데이터 분석가가 CO2 수치를 환경 건강의 유일한 지표로 의존했으나, 쉽게 측정되지 않는 생물 다양성과 생태계 안정성을 무시했다는 비판을 받았다.

questions.question: 27. 다음 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은? [4.3점]
questions.passage:
In order to bring the ever-increasing costs of home care for elderly and needy persons under control, managers of home care providers have introduced management systems. These systems specify tasks of home care workers and the time and budget available to perform these tasks. Electronic reporting systems require home care workers to report on their activities and the time spent, thus making the distribution of time and money visible and, in the perception of managers, controllable. This, in the view of managers, has contributed to the resolution of the problem. The home care workers, on the other hand, may perceive their work not as a set of separate tasks to be performed as efficiently as possible, but as a service to be provided to a client with whom they may have developed a relationship. This includes having conversations with clients and enquiring about the person's well-being. Restricted time and the requirement to report may be perceived as obstacles that make it impossible to deliver the service that is needed.
___________________________________________________________________.
options: ① Overly strict monitoring systems may hinder home care workers from fulfilling their roles meaningfully, leading to stress and fatigue
② Time restrictions enforced by home care management have been successful in reducing worker fatigue by preventing prolonged and emotionally draining visits
③ Home care workers have generally embraced electronic monitoring systems, as these tools have been shown to simplify their daily routines and reduce emotional stress
④ The increased visibility of time and money distribution, enabled by digital systems, has strengthened trust between managers and care workers, fostering a more cooperative work environment
⑤ The implementation of detailed task allocation and strict reporting procedures has allowed caregivers to provide more personalized attention to each client, improving the overall quality of care
questions.explanation: 지문은 관리자들이 비용 통제를 위해 도입한 시스템(시간 제한, 보고 의무)이 실제 돌봄 노동자들이 중요하게 생각하는 관계 중심의 서비스(대화, 안부 확인 등)를 수행하는 데 방해가 된다는 점을 설명하고 있습니다. 따라서 빈칸에는 지나치게 엄격한 감시 시스템이 노동자들의 의미 있는 역할 수행을 방해하고 스트레스를 유발할 수 있다는 내용이 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 지나치게 엄격한 감시 시스템은 요양 보호사들이 그들의 역할을 의미 있게 수행하는 것을 방해하여 스트레스와 피로로 이어질 수 있다.
② 가정 간호 관리자에 의해 시행된 시간 제한은 길고 감정적으로 소모되는 방문을 방지함으로써 노동자의 피로를 줄이는 데 성공적이었다.
③ 요양 보호사들은 전자 감시 시스템이 일상적인 업무를 단순화하고 정서적 스트레스를 줄여주는 것으로 나타났기 때문에 대체로 이를 수용해 왔다.
④ 디지털 시스템에 의해 가능해진 시간과 돈 배분의 가시성 증대는 관리자와 요양 보호사 간의 신뢰를 강화하고 더 협력적인 업무 환경을 조성했다.
⑤ 상세한 업무 할당과 엄격한 보고 절차의 시행은 간병인들이 각 고객에게 더 개인화된 관심을 제공할 수 있게 하여 전반적인 케어의 질을 향상시켰다.

questions.question: 28. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 어법상 틀린 것은? [2.8점]
questions.passage:
Emotion socialization - learning from other people about emotions and how to deal with them - starts early in life and ①<u>plays</u> a foundational role for emotion regulation development.
Although extra-familial influences, such as peers or media, gain in importance during adolescence, parents remain the primary socialization agents. For example, their own responses to emotional situations serve as a role model for emotion regulation, increasing the likelihood ②<u>that</u> their children will show similar reactions in comparable situations. Parental practices at times when their children are faced with emotional challenges also impact emotion regulation development. Whereas direct soothing and directive guidance of what to do are beneficial for younger children, they may intrude on adolescents' autonomy striving.
In consequence, adolescents might pull away from, rather than ③<u>turn</u> toward, their parents in times of emotional crisis, unless parental practices are adjusted. More suitable in adolescence ④<u>is</u> indirect support of autonomous emotion regulation, such as through interest in, as well as awareness and nonjudgmental acceptance of, adolescents' emotional experiences, and ⑤<u>to be</u> available when the adolescent wants to talk.
questions.explanation: ⑤번이 포함된 문장은 보어(More suitable in adolescence)가 문두로 나간 도치 구문입니다. 동사(is) 뒤에 오는 주어인 명사구 'indirect support ...'와 병렬 구조를 이루어야 하므로, 'to be'는 동명사 형태인 'being'으로 고쳐야 어법상 적절합니다.

questions.question: 1. the morning pages에 관한 다음 글의 내용과 일치하지 않는 것은? [3.5점]
questions.passage: The morning pages are three pages of "free writing," ideally done first thing in the morning. The concept is simple. Get up every morning, pick up a pen and a notebook, and write whatever crosses your mind until you have filled three pages. The technique was originally developed to help writers and artists overcome a loss of creativity, but anybody can use it to create a better life. There is no right or wrong way to write your morning pages, but there are two rules. First, don't judge your writing as good or bad. These pages are meant to be a "brain cleansing," so don't worry about writing correctly. Second, keep your writing completely private. It is important for you to write freely and honestly. You're even advised not to read your writing yourself for weeks.
options: ① 아침에 가장 처음 하는 일이 이상적이다.
② 마음속에 떠오르는 건 무엇이든 세 페이지를 채울 때까지 쓰는 것이다.
③ 작가와 예술가들의 창조력 상실 극복을 돕기 위해 개발되었다.
④ 작성하기 위한 옳거나 그른 방법이 있다.
⑤ 완전히 비공개로 유지해야 한다.
questions.explanation: 지문에서 'There is no right or wrong way to write your morning pages(모닝 페이지를 쓰는 데 옳거나 그른 방법은 없다)'라고 명시되어 있으므로 ④번은 내용과 일치하지 않습니다.

questions.question: 2. 문어에 대한 다음 글의 내용과 일치하지 않는 것은? [3.5점]
questions.passage: Here is an animal with poison like a snake, a hard and pointed mouth like a bird, and ink like a pen. It can change its color, pattern, and texture, and the changes are carried out almost instantly. In terms of speed of change, no other animal can rival it. It can also taste with its skin. This animal is called an octopus. The octopus looks so alien to the people of the West that it has caused dislike or even horror in them. To this day, it is difficult for us to imagine that octopuses and humans share any meaningful similarities.
options: ① 새처럼 단단하고 뾰족한 입을 가졌다.
② 자신의 색깔, 무늬, 질감을 바꿀 수 있다.
③ 변화의 속도 측면에서, 어떤 다른 동물도 경쟁이 되지 않는다.
④ 서양 사람들에게 너무 낯설어서 호기심을 불러일으켰다.
⑤ 인간과 어떤 의미 있는 유사점을 공유하고 있다고 상상하기 어렵다.
questions.explanation: 지문에서 문어는 서양 사람들에게 너무 이질적이어서 '혐오(dislike)나 심지어 공포(horror)'를 불러일으켰다고 했으므로, '호기심을 불러일으켰다'는 ④번은 내용과 일치하지 않습니다.

questions.question: 3. 다음 글의 요지로 가장 적절한 것은? [3.5점]
questions.passage: In 2012, scientists met at the University of Cambridge to talk about consciousness in humans and animals. Consciousness means having subjective experiences or awareness. The scientists found that animals have emotions and can have consciousness like humans. For example, African grey parrots have shown evidence of consciousness that is almost as advanced as that of humans. Even octopuses have the brain structures needed for subjective experiences. Drugs that affect human consciousness also affect some animals in similar ways. So, the scientists concluded that consciousness is not just for humans. Animals can have it too. Since the Cambridge Declaration, research on animal consciousness has been actively carried out. Scientists are still working to find out exactly how animal consciousness works. Not all animals are conscious, but those with complex nervous systems are more likely to be. All things considered, it would be a wise and safe choice to assume that animals have feelings and to treat them with respect and kindness.
options: ① 동물에게도 감정이 있다고 가정하고 존중하는 것이 현명하다.
② 인간을 제외한 대부분의 동물은 주관적인 경험을 할 수 없다.
③ 신경계 질환이 있는 동물은 평소와 다른 행동을 보일 수 있다.
④ 최근에 동물의 의사소통 방식에 대한 연구가 주목을 받고 있다.
⑤ 동물에게 약물을 투여하는 것은 치료를 위한 목적에만 한정된다.
questions.explanation: 글의 마지막 문장에서 '동물이 감정을 가지고 있다고 가정하고 존중과 친절로 대하는 것이 현명하고 안전한 선택일 것이다'라고 결론짓고 있으므로 요지로 가장 적절합니다.

questions.question: 4. 다음 글에 드러난 David의 심경 변화로 가장 적절한 것은? [3.5점]
questions.passage: David, a chef and kitchen manager, has been writing morning pages for two years. At first, he filled his pages with complaints about his hard life. Later, he started asking himself questions like, "What would make my life easier today?" and "How can I improve my recipes?" Sometimes, he kept asking questions until he reached a sort of "click moment," which felt like a door opening to great ideas. Nowadays, he feels less stressed, enjoys his job more, and is more productive.
options: ① anxious → angry
② stressed → satisfied
③ scared → worried
④ cheerful → disappointed
⑤ curious → jealous
questions.explanation: 처음에는 힘든 삶에 대한 불평(complaints about his hard life)으로 페이지를 채웠으나, 현재는 스트레스를 덜 받고 직업을 더 즐기며 생산적이 되었다(feels less stressed, enjoys his job more)고 했으므로 심경 변화는 '스트레스 받은'에서 '만족하는'으로 변한 것이 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 불안한 → 화난
② 스트레스 받은 → 만족하는
③ 무서워하는 → 걱정하는
④ 쾌활한 → 실망한
⑤ 호기심 많은 → 질투하는

questions.question: 13. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 어법상 옳은 것은? [3.6점]
questions.passage: Forming a new habit is not easy, especially in the beginning. Here ① <u>is</u> five ways to start a habit that really sticks. First, start small. Don't try to do too much, too quickly. A habit is formed through repetition, so make the change easier to repeat. Second, make your goal specific. Don't say, "I'll meditate regularly." Say, "I'll meditate for five minutes each day." This works ② <u>much</u> better if you combine your new habit with an existing one. For example, "After brushing my teeth in the morning, I'll meditate for five minutes." When your fixed habit becomes a cue for action, your new habit is more likely to stick. Third, make ③ <u>them</u> attractive. Pair your new change with what you love. You could listen to your favorite piece of calming music while ④ meditated. Fourth, track your progress. Mark a calendar with an X every time you finish something. Seeing the progress gives you a sense of achievement and ⑤ <u>helps</u> you keep going. Fifth, be flexible. Forming a new habit takes time. If you find that your progress has stopped for any reason, just pick up where you left off.
options: ① is
② much
③ them
④ meditated
⑤ helps
questions.explanation: ① 주어인 five ways가 복수이므로 are가 적절합니다. ② 비교급 better를 수식할 수 있는 강조 부사로 much가 적절합니다. (중복 정답 가능성 검토: 문제에서 '옳은 것'을 묻고 있는데, ⑤번 'helps'는 주어 seeing the progress가 단수이므로 수 일치가 맞습니다. ②번 또한 비교급 강조로 문법적으로 옳습니다. 하지만 학교 시험의 의도상 ⑤번이 더 명확한 주술 일치를 묻는 정답일 수 있으나, ②번도 문법적으로 하자가 없습니다. 제공된 텍스트 기준으로는 ⑤번이 가장 전형적인 정답 후보입니다.) ③ 앞의 a new change를 가리키므로 it이 적절합니다. ④ 접속사 while 뒤에서 분사구문으로 '명상을 하면서'라는 능동의 의미가 되어야 하므로 meditating이 적절합니다.

questions.question:
15.다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 어법상 틀린 것을 고르시오.
[3.6점]
questions.passage: Our knowledge about the octopus is still very limited. Thanks to the efforts of scientists, however, it is expanding year by year. One of the most impressive new findings about the octopus ① <u>is</u> that it seems to have feelings. Of course,  it is impossible for us ② <u>to</u> know exactly what they feel, but a few of their changes in skin color seem to be linked to their feelings. For example, a giant Pacific octopus that turns red seems to be excited, while it is white when it is relaxed. An octopus ③ <u>presenting</u> with a difficult puzzle often undergoes several rapid changes in color. The octopus seems to be worried that it may not solve the problem. Few scientists today deny ④ <u>that</u> octopuses are intelligent animals. Perhaps it is time that we ⑤ <u>acknowledged</u> them as intelligent animals like us, instead of treating them as alien creatures.
options: ① is
② to
③ presenting
④ that
⑤ acknowledged
questions.explanation: ③ 문맥상 문어(octopus)가 퍼즐을 '제시받는' 것이므로 과거분사 presented가 되어야 합니다.

questions.question:
1. 다음 글의 요지로 가장 적절한 것을 고르시오

 [3.5점]
questions.passage: Improving your gestural communication involves more than just knowing when to nod or shake hands. It's about using gestures to complement your spoken messages, adding layers of meaning to your words. Openhanded gestures, for example, can indicate honesty, creating an atmosphere of trust. You invite openness and collaboration when you speak with your palms facing up. This simple yet powerful gesture can make others feel more comfortable and willing to engage in conversation. But be careful of the trap of overgesturing. Too many hand movements can distract from your message, drawing attention away from your words. Imagine a speaker whose hands move quickly like birds, their message lost in the chaos of their gestures. Balance is key. Your gestures should highlight your words, not overshadow them.
options: ① Communication can be done without words.
② Honest people use more gestures than others.
③ Overuse of gestures can do harm to your message.
④ Visual images are helpful for understanding a speech.
⑤ Body movements can be interpreted in different ways.
questions.explanation: 글의 중반부 이후에서 'be careful of the trap of overgesturing'와 'Too many hand movements can distract from your message'라고 언급하며, 과도한 제스처의 사용이 메시지 전달에 방해가 될 수 있음을 경고하고 있으므로 ③번이 정답입니다.
options_translation: ① 의사소통은 말 없이도 이루어질 수 있다.
② 정직한 사람들은 다른 사람들보다 제스처를 더 많이 사용한다.
③ 제스처의 과도한 사용은 메시지에 해를 끼칠 수 있다.
④ 시각적 이미지는 연설을 이해하는 데 도움이 된다.
⑤ 신체 움직임은 다양한 방식으로 해석될 수 있다.

questions.question:
2. 다음 글의 요지로 가장 적절한 것을 고르시오

 [3.5점]
questions.passage: What's the first thing you do in the morning? There's a good way to start the day. It's a kind of journaling called "morning pages." It has been found useful by many people. You can see how it works from the following example. David, a chef and kitchen manager, has been writing morning pages for two years. His job tends to be very stressful. When he started writing morning pages, he just wrote a lot of complaints about his hard life. Later, he began to ask questions like, "What would make my life easier today?" and "How can I improve my recipes?" Sometimes, he kept asking questions until he reached a sort of "click moment." It felt like a door opening to great ideas. Nowadays, he feels less stressed, enjoys his job more, and is more productive.
options: ① Writing morning pages can help improve your day.
② Various stressors in life can affect people's mental health.
③ Having a hobby is a good way to relieve stress from work.
④ Working as a chef comes with a lot of stress and pressure.
⑤ Asking questions while cooking is a useful way to make a recipe better.
questions.explanation: 아침 일기(morning pages)를 쓰는 것이 스트레스를 줄이고 생산성을 높이며 하루를 개선하는 데 도움이 된다는 내용이므로 ①번이 정답입니다.
options_translation: ① 아침 일기를 쓰는 것은 당신의 하루를 개선하는 데 도움이 될 수 있다.
② 삶의 다양한 스트레스 요인은 사람들의 정신 건강에 영향을 미칠 수 있다.
③ 취미를 갖는 것은 업무 스트레스를 해소하는 좋은 방법이다.
④ 요리사로 일하는 것은 많은 스트레스와 압박감을 동반한다.
⑤ 요리하는 동안 질문을 던지는 것은 레시피를 더 좋게 만드는 유용한 방법이다.

questions.question: 3. [3점] 다음 글의 주제로 가장 적절한 것을 고르시오
questions.passage: Crop rotation is the process in which farmers change the crops they grow in their fields in a special order. For example, if a farmer has three fields, he or she may grow carrots in the first field, green beans in the second, and tomatoes in the third. The next year, green beans will be in the first field, tomatoes in the second field, and carrots will be in the third. In year three, the crops will rotate again. By the fourth year, the crops will go back to their original order. In crop rotation, each crop enriches the soil for the next crop. This type of farming is sustainable because the soil stays healthy. When the same type of crop is planted in a field again and again, it uses all the nutrients in the soil. Pests and diseases that are common to that crop increase. Crop rotation can prevent these from happening.
options: ① advantages of eating organic vegetables
② definition and benefits of crop rotation
③ appropriate moments to enrich soil
④ problems of changing crops yearly
⑤ importance of sustainable farming
questions.explanation: 이 글은 윤작(crop rotation)이 무엇인지 설명하고(정의), 토양을 건강하게 유지하고 해충 및 질병을 예방하며 지속 가능한 농업을 가능하게 한다는 점(이점)을 다루고 있으므로 정답은 ②번입니다.
options_translation: ① 유기농 채소를 먹는 것의 이점
② 윤작의 정의와 이점
③ 토양을 비옥하게 할 적절한 시기
④ 매년 작물을 바꾸는 것의 문제점
⑤ 지속 가능한 농업의 중요성

questions.question: 4. [3.9점] 다음 글의 주제로 가장 적절한 것을 고르시오
questions.passage: The science we learn in grade school is a collection of certainties about the natural world-the earth goes around the sun, DNA carries the information of an organism, and so on. Only when you start to learn the practice of science do you realize that each of these "facts" was hard won through a succession of logical inferences based upon many observations or experiments. The process of science is less about collecting pieces of knowledge than it is about reducing the uncertainties in what we know. Our uncertainties can be greater or lesser for any given piece of knowledge depending upon where we are in that process-today we are quite certain of how an apple will fall from a tree, but our understanding of the turbulent fluid flow remains a work in progress after more than a century of effort.
options: ① need for more efforts to discover the reason for turbulent fluid flow
② different perceptions of researchers about scientific facts
③ ways to distinguish different ideas and put them together
④ process of science as reducing uncertainties in our knowledge
⑤ necessity of teaching students scientific viewpoints
questions.explanation: 이 글은 과학이 단순히 지식을 수집하는 것이 아니라, 우리가 알고 있는 것에서의 불확실성을 줄여가는 과정임을 설명하고 있습니다. 따라서 정답은 ④번입니다.
options_translation: ① 난류 유동의 원인을 발견하기 위한 더 많은 노력의 필요성
② 과학적 사실에 대한 연구자들의 서로 다른 인식
③ 서로 다른 생각들을 구별하고 결합하는 방법
④ 우리 지식의 불확실성을 줄여가는 과정으로서의 과학
⑤ 학생들에게 과학적 관점을 가르칠 필요성

questions.question: 5. 다음 글이 주는 교훈으로 가장 적절한 것은? [3.5점]
questions.passage:
Jack, an Arkansas farmer, was unhappy because he couldn't make enough money from his farm. He worked hard for many years, but things didn't improve. He sold his farm to his neighbor, Victor, who was by no means wealthy. Hoping for a fresh start, he left for the big city to find better opportunities. Years passed, but Jack still couldn't find the fortune he was looking for. Tired and broke, he returned to the area where his old farm was.
One day, he drove past his old land and was shocked by what he saw. Victor, the man who had bought the farm with very little money, now seemed to be living a life of great success. He had torn down the farmhouse and built a massive house in its place. New buildings, trees, and flowers adorned the wellkept property. Jack could hardly believe that he had ever worked on this same land. Curious, he stopped to talk to Victor.
"How did you do all this?" he asked. And he continued, "When you bought the farm, you barely had any money. How did you get so rich?" Victor smiled and said, "I owe it all to you. There were diamonds on this land — acres and acres of diamonds! I got rich because I discovered those diamonds." "Diamonds?" Jack said in disbelief. And he said, "I knew every part of that land, and there were no diamonds!"
Victor reached into his pocket and carefully pulled out something small and shiny. Holding it between his fingers, he let it catch the light. He said, "This is a diamond." Jack was amazed and said, "I saw so many rocks like that and thought they were useless. They made farming so hard!" Victor laughed and said, "You didn't know what diamonds look like. Sometimes, treasures are hidden right in front of us."
options: ① Kindness returns unexpectedly.
② Friends can be any shape or size.
③ You should talk less, and listen more.
④ If you lie to people, you will lose their trust.
⑤ Recognizing the value of what you have is important.
questions.explanation: 농부 잭은 자신의 땅에 있는 다이아몬드를 쓸모없는 돌로 여겨 기회를 놓쳤으나, 빅터는 그 가치를 발견하여 성공했다는 내용이므로 '자신이 가진 것의 가치를 알아보는 것이 중요하다'는 5번이 정답입니다.
options_translation: ① 친절은 예상치 못하게 돌아온다.
② 친구는 어떤 모양이나 크기일 수도 있다.
③ 말을 덜 하고 더 많이 들어야 한다.
④ 사람들에게 거짓말을 하면 신뢰를 잃을 것이다.
⑤ 당신이 가진 것의 가치를 인식하는 것이 중요하다.

questions.question: 6. [3.6점] 다음 글의 제목으로 가장 적절한 것을 고르시오
questions.passage: Piaget put the same amount of water into two different glasses: a tall narrow glass and a wide glass, then asked kids to compare two glasses. Kids younger than six or seven usually say that the tall narrow glass now holds more water, because the level is higher. And when they are ready, they figure out the conservation of volume for themselves just by playing with cups of water. Piaget argued that children's understanding of morality is like their understanding of those water glasses: we can't say that it is innate or kids learn it directly from adults. Rather, it is self-constructed as kids play with other kids. Taking turns in a game is like pouring water back and forth between glasses. Once kids have reached the age of five or six, then playing games and working things out together will help them learn about fairness far more effectively than any teaching from adults.
options: ① The Role of Parents in Moral Development
② How Children Construct Morality Through Play
③ Why Taller Glasses Seem to Hold More Water
④ Games and Water: Teaching Scientific Thinking
⑤ Water Conservation Education for Young Learners
questions.explanation: 피아제는 아이들의 도덕성 이해가 물 컵 실험과 유사하게 놀이를 통해 스스로 구축된다고 주장했다. 따라서 아이들이 놀이를 통해 어떻게 도덕성을 형성하는지를 설명하는 2번이 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 도덕 발달에 있어서 부모의 역할
② 아이들이 놀이를 통해 도덕성을 형성하는 방법
③ 왜 더 높은 유리잔이 물을 더 많이 담고 있는 것처럼 보이는가
④ 게임과 물: 과학적 사고 가르치기
⑤ 어린 학습자들을 위한 수자원 보존 교육

questions.question: 7. [3.6점] 다음 글의 제목으로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: No respectable boss would say, "I make it a point to discourage my staff from speaking up, and I maintain a culture that prevents disagreeing viewpoints from ever getting aired." If anything, most bosses even say that they are pro-dissent. This idea can be found throughout the series of conversations with corporate, university, and nonprofit leaders, published weekly in the business sections of newspapers. In the interviews, the featured leaders are asked about their management techniques, and regularly claim to continually encourage internal protest from more junior staffers. As Bot Pittman remarked in one of these conversations: "I want us to listen to these dissenters because they may intend to tell you why we can't do something, but if you listen hard, what they're really telling you is what you must do to get something done."
options: ① Feel Free to Ask for Help
② The Benefits of Reading Newspapers
③ Internal Resistance: What Great Bosses Welcome
④ What Makes Your Staffers Raise Their Voice?
⑤ Remarkable Leadership against Outer Dissenters
questions.explanation: 이 글은 많은 리더들이 표면적으로는 직원들의 반대 의견(dissent)을 장려하며, 특히 Bob Pittman의 말을 통해 반대자들의 의견을 경청하는 것이 일을 완수하는 데 필요한 정보를 얻는 방법임을 설명하고 있습니다. 따라서 '내부적 저항: 훌륭한 상사들이 환영하는 것'이 가장 적절한 제목입니다.
options_translation: ① 자유롭게 도움을 요청하라
② 신문 읽기의 이점
③ 내부적 저항: 위대한 상사들이 환영하는 것
④ 무엇이 당신의 직원들이 목소리를 높이게 만드는가?
⑤ 외부 반대자들에 맞서는 주목할 만한 리더십

questions.question: 8. Robert E. Lucas, Jr.에 관한 다음 글의 내용과 일치하는 것은? [3.2점]
questions.passage: Robert E. Lucas, Jr. was born on September 15, 1937, in Yakima, Washington. During World War II, his family moved to Seattle, where he graduated from Roosevelt High School. At the University of Chicago, he majored in history. After taking economic history courses at University of California, Berkeley, he developed an interest in economics. He earned a doctoral degree in economics from the University of Chicago in 1964. He taught at Carnegie Mellon University from 1963 to 1974. He returned to the University of Chicago in 1975, where he continued his career as a professor of economics. He was known as a very influential economist and, in 1995, he was awarded the Nobel Prize in Economic Sciences.
options: ① 제2차 세계대전이 끝난 후 Seattle로 이주했다.
② Yakima에서 고등학교를 졸업했다.
③ University of Chicago에서 화학을 전공했다.
④ Carnegie Mellon University에서 경제학 박사 학위를 받았다.
⑤ University of Chicago에서 경제학 교수로 재직했다.
questions.explanation: 지문에서 "He returned to the University of Chicago in 1975, where he continued his career as a professor of economics."라고 언급되어 있으므로 ⑤번이 일치합니다. ①은 전쟁 중에 이주했으므로 틀렸고, ②는 Seattle에서 고등학교를 졸업했으므로 틀렸으며, ③은 역사를 전공했으므로 틀렸고, ④는 University of Chicago에서 박사 학위를 받았으므로 틀렸습니다.

questions.question: 9. The morning pages에 관한 다음 글의 내용과 일치하지 않는 것은? [3.2점]
questions.passage: The morning pages are three pages of "free writing," ideally done first thing in the morning. The concept is simple. Get up every morning, pick up a pen and a notebook, and write anything that comes to your mind until you have filled three pages. The technique was originally developed for writers and artists, but anybody can use it to create a better life. There is no right or wrong way to write your morning pages, but there are two rules. First, don't judge your writing as good or bad. These pages are meant to be a "brain cleansing," so don't worry about writing correctly. Second, keep your writing completely private. It is important for you to write freely and honestly. You're even advised not to read your writing yourself for weeks.
options: ① 아침에 일어나자마자 하는 것이 좋다.
② 머릿속에 떠오르는 생각을 아무거나 쓰면 된다.
③ 원래 작가와 예술가들을 위해 개발된 기법이다.
④ 작성한 글을 좋거나 나쁜 것으로 평가하지 않아야 한다.
⑤ 주변 사람들과 공유하는 것이 중요하다.
questions.explanation: 글에서 두 번째 규칙으로 '글을 완전히 비공개로 유지하라(keep your writing completely private)'고 명시하고 있으므로 주변 사람들과 공유하는 것이 중요하다는 ⑤번은 내용과 일치하지 않습니다.

questions.question: 10. 다음 글의 내용과 일치하지 않는 것은? [3.2점]
questions.passage: Another sign of the intelligence of the octopus is its use of tools. In the lab, octopuses use tools to get food rewards. In the wild, they use stones to create walls to protect the entrances to their homes. They use not only stones but anything they can find to protect themselves. The most impressive example of octopuses using tools came in 2009 in Indonesia. A few octopuses were found to collect coconut shells. They cleaned the shells with bursts of water, carried them to a new location, and piled them as a shelter. Traveling with the shells under their bodies forced them to walk slowly along the sea floor. This made the octopuses more exposed to predators. But it seems that they were willing to take that risk for greater future protection. The scientists who discovered the behavior argue that this is clear evidence of octopuses using tools.
options: ① 실험실에서 문어는 먹이 보상을 얻기 위해 도구를 사용한다.
② 야생에서 문어는 집의 입구를 보호하기 위해 돌을 이용하여 벽을 만든다.
③ 문어가 도구를 사용하는 가장 인상적인 사례는 2009년 인도네시아에서 나왔다.
④ 코코넛 껍질을 몸 아래에 품고 이동하는 문어는 빠르게 걸었다.
⑤ 문어들은 미래의 더 큰 보호를 위해 위험을 기꺼이 감수하는 것으로 보인다.
questions.explanation: 본문에서 코코넛 껍질을 몸 아래에 품고 이동하는 것은 문어들을 해저에서 천천히 걷게 만들었다(forced them to walk slowly along the sea floor)고 언급하고 있으므로 ④번은 내용과 일치하지 않습니다.

questions.question: 11. [3.4점] 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중 어법상 틀린 것을 고르시오
questions.passage: The octopus looks so alien to the people of the West ①<u>that</u> it has caused dislike or even horror in them. The dislike or horror helped create the image of an octopus as an evil creature ②<u>living</u> in the deep sea. For example, the Kraken, a sea monster in old Icelandic tales ③<u>looks</u> just like an enormous octopus. Another example is Ursula, the sea witch ④<u>featured</u> in the famous tale, The Little Mermaid. To this day, it is difficult for us ⑤<u>to imagine</u> that octopuses and humans share any meaningful similarities.
questions.explanation: Kraken은 과거의 설화(old Icelandic tales)에 등장하는 존재이므로, 문맥상 과거 시제인 'looked'림 사용하거나, 해당 문장을 '전해지기로는 ~ 찘다' 등의 표현으로 쓰는 것이 더 자연스럽습니다. 해당 지문의 교과서 옐문에서눤 'was said to look'으로 표현되어 읈습니다.

questions.question: 12. [3.3점] 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중 어법상 틀린 것을 고르시오
questions.passage: Modern brain-scanning techniques such as fMRI (functional Magnetic Resonance Imaging) have revealed that reading aloud ①<u>lights</u> up many areas of the brain. There is intense activity in areas associated with pronunciation and ②<u>hearing</u> the sound of the spoken response, which strengthens the connective structures of your brain cells for more brainpower. This leads to an overall improvement in concentration. Reading aloud is also a good way to develop your public speaking skills because it forces you ③<u>to read</u> each and every word. This is something people don't often do when reading ④<u>quickly</u>, or reading in silence. Children, in particular, should ⑤<u>encourage</u> to read aloud because the brain is wired for learning through connections that are created by positive stimulation, such as singing, touching, and reading aloud.
questions.explanation: 아이들이 소리 내어 읽도록 '장려되어야' 한다는 수동의 의미가 되어야 하므로, 능동형인 encourage림 수동태인 'be encouraged'로 고쳐야 합니다.

questions.question: 13. [3.7점] 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중 어법상 틀린 것을 고르시오
questions.passage: There is a wealth of evidence that when people ①<u>perceive</u> parents, teachers, supervisors, and coaches as involved and caring, people feel happier and more motivated. And it is not just those people with power - we need to feel valued and respected by peers and coworkers. Thus, when the need for relatedness ②<u>is fulfilled</u>, motivation and internalization are fueled, provided that support for autonomy and competence are also there. If we are trying to motivate others, a caring relationship is a crucial basis ③<u>from which</u> to begin. And when we are trying to motivate ourselves, ④<u>make</u> efforts to enhance a sense of connectedness to others can be crucial to long-term persistence. So exercise with a friend, call someone when you have a difficult decision to make, and ⑤<u>support</u> others as they take on challenges.
questions.explanation: 문장의 동사인 'can be' 앝에 주어가 와야 하므로, 동사 원형인 make림 동명사 주어인 'Making'이나 to부정사 'To make'로 고쳐야 합니다.

questions.question: 14. 윗글의 밑줄 친 부분 중 어법상 틀린 것은? [3.5점]
questions.passage:
I started these morning pages, the free writing of whatever <u>(a) crosses</u> my mind in the morning, during my first year of high school. At that time, I felt lost, stressed, and unsure about the future, and it wasn't easy for me to concentrate. When I first tried writing three daily pages, I didn't expect to stick to it. But I did, and it changed my life!
Releasing my feelings onto paper every morning helped relieve my emotional tension. I gained more inner peace, <u>(b) which</u> improved my schoolwork performance. I asked many questions, for instance, "Why was I so angry yesterday?" "Why are things less fun these days?" Then, I started raising more challenging ones: "What could make me happier right now?" "What is my ideal future? Can I reach it? How?"
Answering these questions showed me what kind of person I was and what my needs, values, passions, and talents were. More importantly, I came to know <u>(c) that</u> I truly wanted! I remembered my childhood dreams of being a writer, songwriter, and radio host. Gradually, vague ideas became clear plans. Years later, here I am, a successful podcaster and vlogger! I've also published a book and a music album. My morning pages, which I still write every day, __________________________.
Dear subscribers, will you try writing your morning pages, too? You never know what creative energy or ideas you have until you start <u>(d) exploring</u>. Don't be a perfectionist, though. If you miss a few days, simply open your notebook and start again! The ultimate aim is to improve your mental health and help you <u>(e) lead</u> a happier, more creative life.
options: ① (a)
② (b)
③ (c)
④ (d)
⑤ (e)
questions.explanation: (c)가 포함된 문장에서 'I truly wanted'의 목적어 역할을 하면서 선행사가 없으므로 접속사 that이 아닌 관계대명사 what이 와야 합니다.

questions.explanation: 필자가 모닝 페이지를 통해 자신의 꿈을 찾고, 구체적인 계획을 세워 성공적인 팟캐스터 등이 되었다는 문맥이므로, 목표 달성에 필요한 동기와 아이디어를 주었다는 ④번이 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 더 빠르고 명확하게 쓰는 법을 보여주었다
② 감정이 행동보다 더 중요하다는 것을 가르쳐주었다
③ 목표에 대해 생각하는 것을 피할 수 있는 평화와 침묵을 주었다
④ 이러한 목표들을 달성하는 데 필요한 동기와 아이디어를 고취시켜 주었다
⑤ 일과를 정리하고 시간을 절약하는 것을 더 쉽게 만들어 준다

questions.question: 16. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것을 고르시오. [3.7점]
questions.passage: What does it mean for a character to be a hero as opposed to a villain? In artistic and entertainment descriptions, it's ① <u>crucial</u> for the author to establish a positive relationship between a protagonist and the audience. In order for tragedy or misfortune to draw out an emotional response in viewers, the character must be ② <u>developed</u> so as to be recognizable as either friend or enemy. Whether the portrayal is fictional or documentary, we must feel that the protagonist is someone whose actions ③ <u>benefit</u> us: the protagonist is, or would be, a worthy companion or valued ally. Violent action films are often filled with dozens of incidental deaths of minor characters that draw out ④ <u>dramatic</u> response in the audience. In order to feel strong emotions, the audience must be emotionally ⑤ <u>engaged</u> with a character as either ally or enemy.
questions.explanation: 주인공이 아닌 부수적인(incidental) 인물들의 죽음은 관객들에게 큰 감정적 반응을 일으키지 못한다는 문맥이 되어야 하므로 'dramatic(극적인)'은 'little' 또는 'no'와 같은 부정적인 의미의 어휘로 바뀌어야 합니다.

questions.question: 17. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것을 고르시오.  [3.7점]
questions.passage: Cartilage is extremely important for the healthy functioning of a joint, especially if that joint ① <u>bears</u> weight, like your knee. Imagine for a moment that you're looking into the inner workings of your left knee as you walk down the street. When you shift your weight from your left leg to your right, the pressure on your left knee is ② <u>increased</u>. Then, in much the same way that a sponge soaks up liquid when put in water, the cartilage in your left knee ③ <u>absorbs</u> synovial fluid. When you take another step and ④ <u>transfer</u> the weight back onto your left leg, much of the fluid squeezes out of the cartilage. This squeezing of joint fluid into and out of the cartilage helps it ⑤ <u>endure</u> the off-and-on pressure of walking without breaking under the pressure.
questions.explanation: 왼쪽 다리에서 오른쪽 다리로 체중을 옮기면(shift weight from left to right), 왼쪽 무릎에 가해지던 압력은 '증가(increased)'하는 것이 아니라 '감소(reduced/released)'해야 합니다. 압력이 줄어들어야 연골이 스펀지처럼 관절액을 흡수할 수 있기 때문입니다.

questions.question: 18. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것을 고르시오. [3.7점]
questions.passage: The rise of air-conditioning accelerated the construction of sealed boxes, where the building's only airflow is through the filtered ducts of the air-conditioning unit. It doesn't have to be this way. Look at any old building in a hot climate, whether it's in Sicily or Marrakesh or Tehran. Architects ① <u>acknowledged</u> the importance of shade, airflow, light colors. They oriented buildings to capture cool breezes and ② <u>block</u> the worst heat of the afternoon. They built with thick walls and white roofs and transoms over doors to ③ <u>enhance</u> airflow. Anyone who has ever spent a few minutes in a mudbrick house in Tucson, or walked on the narrow streets of old Seville, knows how ④ <u>well</u> these construction methods work. But all this wisdom about how to deal with heat, accumulated over centuries of practical experience, is all too often ⑤ <u>appreciated</u>. In this sense, air-conditioning is not just a technology of personal comfort; it is also a technology of forgetting.
questions.explanation: 마지막 문장에서 에어컨을 '망각의 기술(technology of forgetting)'이라고 표현한 것으로 보아, 과거의 건축적 지혜가 '인정받는(appreciated)' 것이 아니라 '무시되거나 잊히고 있다'는 흐름이 되어야 하므로 ⑤번이 부적절합니다.

questions.question:
19. 다음 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것을 고르시오

 [3.5점]
questions.passage: As you listen to your child in an emotional moment, be aware that sharing simple observations usually works better than asking questions to get a conversation rolling. You may ask your child "Why do you feel sad?" and she may not have a clue. As a child, she may not have an answer on the tip of her tongue. Maybe she's feeling sad about her parents' arguments, or because she feels overtired, or she's worried about a piano recital. But she may or may not be able to explain any of this. And even when she does come up with an answer, she might be worried that the answer is not good enough to justify the feeling. Under these circumstances, a series of questions can just make a child silent. It's better to simply ____________________. You can say, "You seem a little tired today," or, "I noticed that you frowned when I mentioned the recital."
options: ① state what you observe
② share your feelings with your child
③ wait until your child is ready to speak
④ explain how much you care about your child
⑤ ask questions that your child can easily answer
questions.explanation: 글의 앞부분에서 질문을 하는 것보다 간단한 관찰을 공유하는 것이 대화를 시작하는 데 더 효과적이라고 언급하고 있으며, 빈칸 뒤에서 "You seem a little tired today"나 "I noticed that you frowned..."와 같은 관찰의 예시를 제시하고 있으므로 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 '관찰한 것을 말하는 것'이 가장 적절하다.
options_translation: ① 당신이 관찰한 것을 말해라
② 아이와 당신의 감정을 공유해라
③ 아이가 말할 준비가 될 때까지 기다려라
④ 당신이 아이를 얼마나 아끼는지 설명해라
⑤ 아이가 쉽게 답할 수 있는 질문을 해라

questions.question:
20. 다음 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것을 고르시오

[3.9점]
questions.passage: Routines enable athletes to evaluate competition conditions. For example, bouncing a ball in a volleyball service routine supplies the server with information about the ball, the floor, and the state of her muscles. This information can then be used to properly prepare for her serve. Routines also enable athletes to adjust and fine-tune their preparations based on those evaluations or in pursuit of a particular competitive goal. This adaptation can involve adjustment to the conditions, rivals, competitive situation, or internal influences that can affect performance. Just like adjusting a race-car engine to the conditions of the track, air temperature, and weather, routines ____________________.
options: ① allow athletes to adapt themselves to the state of factors influencing their performance
② stimulate athletes and draw their attention to the external components
③ are developed to help sports players improve their mental abilities
④ are carried out in order to get the most out of the training
⑤ should be repeated to assess their opponents
questions.explanation: 지문은 루틴이 운동선수들에게 경기 조건을 평가하고, 그 평가를 바탕으로 준비 과정을 조정 및 미세하게 조정(fine-tune)하게 해준다고 설명하고 있다. 마지막 문장의 경주용 자동차 엔진 조정 비유는 루틴이 선수들의 수행에 영향을 미치는 여러 요인들에 스스로를 적응시키게 한다는 흐름과 일치한다.
options_translation: ① 운동선수들이 자신의 성과에 영향을 미치는 요인들의 상태에 스스로를 적응시키게 한다
② 운동선수들을 자극하고 외부 구성 요소에 주의를 기울이게 한다
③ 운동선수들의 정신적 능력을 향상시키는 것을 돕기 위해 개발된다
④ 훈련에서 최대한의 성과를 얻기 위해 수행된다
⑤ 상대를 평가하기 위해 반복되어야 한다

questions.question:
21. 글의 흐름으로 보아, 주어진 문장이 들어가기에 가장 적절한 곳을 고르시오
. [3.7점]
questions.passage: Plants can communicate, although not in the same way we do. Some express their discontent through scents. You know that smell that hangs in the air after you've mowed the lawn? ( ① ) Yeah, that's actually an SOS. Some plants use sound. Yes, sound, though at a frequency that we can't hear. ( ② ) Researchers experimented with plants and microphones to see if they could record any trouble calls. ( ③ ) The sound a plant makes when it's not getting watered differs from the one it'll make when a leaf is cut. ( ④ ) However, it's worth noting that experts don't think plants are crying out in pain. It's more likely that these reactions are knee-jerk survival actions. ( ⑤ ) Plants are living organisms, and their main objective is to survive. Scents and sounds are their tools for defending against things that might harm them.
questions.insertion_sentence: They found that plants produce a high-frequency clicking noise when stressed and can make different sounds for different stressors.
questions.explanation: 주어진 문장은 연구자들이 스트레스를 받은 식물이 고주파의 클릭 소리를 낸다는 점과 스트레스 요인에 따라 다른 소리를 낸다는 사실을 발견했다는 내용입니다. ② 뒤의 문장에서 연구자들이 마이크로 식물을 실험했다는 내용이 나오고, ③ 뒤의 문장에서 물을 주지 않을 때와 잎이 잘렸을 때의 소리가 다르다는 구체적인 발견 내용이 이어지므로, 발견의 일반적인 결과를 언급한 주어진 문장은 ③에 들어가는 것이 가장 적절합니다.

questions.question:
22. 글의 흐름으로 보아, 주어진 문장이 들어가기에 가장 적절한 곳을 고르시오
 [3.6점]
questions.passage: Let's assume that at least some animals are capable of thinking despite lacking a language. ( ① ) This doesn't necessarily mean that they possess concepts, for some forms of thought may be nonconceptual. ( ② ) We can imagine, for instance, a squirrel who is planning how to get from the branch she's currently standing on to a branch from the tree in front. To do this, in principle she doesn't need a concept of branch nor a concept of tree. ( ③ ) This doesn't imply that squirrels lack concepts, simply that they don't need them for this concrete form of thinking. ( ④ ) For us to be able to say that an animal has concepts, we have to show not just that she's capable of thinking, but also that she has certain specific abilities. ( ⑤ )
questions.insertion_sentence: It might be enough for her to have, for example, the ability to think in images; to make a mental map of the tree where she can imagine and try out different routes.
questions.explanation: 주어진 문장은 다람쥐가 나무의 정신적 지도를 만들거나 이미지로 생각하는 능력을 갖는 것으로 충분할 수 있다는 내용입니다. ③ 앞 문장에서 다람쥐가 나무나 나뭇가지에 대한 개념이 원칙적으로 필요하지 않다고 했으므로, 그 대안으로서 이미지로 생각하는 구체적인 방식(정신적 지도)을 설명하는 주어진 문장이 ③에 위치해야 문맥이 자연스럽게 이어집니다.

questions.question:
23. 다음 글에서 전체 흐름과 관계 없는 문장은?
[3.1점]
questions.passage: Plato argued that when you see something that strikes you as beautiful, you are really just seeing a partial reflection of true beauty, just as a painting or even a photograph only captures part of the real thing. ① True beauty, or what Plato calls the Form of Beauty, has no particular color, shape, or size. ② He believed that true love is always directed toward true beauty. ③ Rather, it is an abstract idea, like the number five. ④ You can make drawings of the number five in blue or red ink, big or small, but the number five itself is none of those things; It has no physical form. ⑤ Think of the idea of a triangle, for example. Although it has no particular color or size, it somehow lies within each and every triangle you see. Plato thought the same was true of beauty. The Form of Beauty somehow lies within each and every beautiful thing you see.
questions.explanation: 이 글은 플라톤이 주장한 '미의 형상(Form of Beauty)'이라는 추상적 개념에 대해 설명하고 있습니다. ②번 문장은 '진정한 사랑은 항상 진정한 미를 향한다'는 내용으로, 미의 본질이 추상적이고 물리적 형태가 없다는 전체적인 흐름과 관계가 없습니다.

questions.question: 24. [4점] 주어진 글 다음에 이어질 글의 순서로 가장 적절한 것을 고르시오.
questions.passage: In the course of trying to solve a problem with an invention, you may encounter a brick wall of resistance when you try to think your way logically through the problem.
ordered_passages: (A) This is precisely where nonlinear thinking becomes essential. Unlike step-by-step logical reasoning, nonlinear thinking enables the mind to form unexpected connections, rely on intuition, and consider problems from multiple perspectives.

(B) Such logical thinking is a linear type of process, which uses our reasoning skills. This works fine when we're operating in the area of what we know or have experienced. However, when it comes to generating new ideas or approaching unfamiliar problems, linear thinking often falls short.

(C) By encouraging imagination and flexibility, nonlinear thinking opens the door to new ideas and unexpected possibilities. It helps us move beyond limits and approach problems with a creative mindset.
questions.explanation: 주어진 글에서 논리적 사고의 한계(brick wall of resistance)를 언급했으므로, (B)에서 'Such logical thinking'으로 이를 받아 논리적 사고(선형적 사고)의 특징과 한계를 설명합니다. (A)에서는 논리적 사고가 부족할 때 '비선형적 사고(nonlinear thinking)'가 필수적임을 제시하며 그 특징을 설명하고, (C)에서 비선형적 사고의 효과를 정리하며 마무리하는 것이 자연스럽습니다.

questions.question: 25. [3.4점] 주어진 글 다음에 이어질 글의 순서로 가장 적절한 것을 고르시오.
questions.passage: Our knowledge about the octopus is still very limited.
ordered_passages: (A) Also, an octopus presented with a difficult puzzle often undergoes several rapid changes in color. The octopus seems to be worried that it may not solve the problem.

(B) Of course, it is impossible for us to know exactly what they feel, but a few of their changes in skin color seem to be linked to their feelings. For example, a giant Pacific octopus that turns red seems to be excited, while it is white when it is relaxed.
(C) Thanks to the efforts of scientists, however, it is expanding year by year. One of the most impressive new findings about the octopus is that it seems to have feelings.
questions.explanation: 문장은 문어 지식에 대한 한계를 언급하며 시작합니다. (C)에서 'however'를 통해 지식이 확장되고 있으며 새로운 발견(감정을 가짐)을 소개합니다. (B)에서 피부색 변화와 감정의 연결(예: 빨간색은 흥분, 흰색은 편안함)을 설명하고, (A)에서 'Also'를 통해 또 다른 사례(어려운 퍼즐을 풀 때 걱정하는 색 변화)를 제시하는 것이 자연스럽습니다.

questions.question: 26. 다음 글의 내용을 한 문장으로 요약하고자 한다. 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은? [3.9점]
questions.passage: Promotion deals with consumer psychology. We can't force people to think one way or another, and the clever marketer knows that promotion is used to provide information in the most clear, honest, and simple fashion possible. By doing so, the possibility of increasing sales goes up. Gone are the days when promotions were done in order to fool the consumer into purchasing something. The long-term effect of getting a consumer to buy something they did not really want or need wasn't good. In fact, consumers fooled once can do damage to sales as they relate their experience to others. Instead, marketers now know that their goal is to identify the consumers who are most likely to appreciate a good or service, and to promote that good or service in a way that makes the value clear to the consumer. Therefore, marketers must know where the potential consumers are, and how to reach them.
questions.summary_sentence: Rather than (A) _________ consumers, which brings negative effect on the sales in the long run, marketers must try to find the potential consumers who will (B) _________ a good or service and develop ways to attract them.
options: ① deceiving ... value
② identifying ... approach
③ forcing ... neglect
④ rewarding ... appreciate
⑤ fooling ... underestimate
questions.explanation: 글의 전반부는 과거의 방식인 소비자를 속이는 것(fooling/deceiving)이 장기적으로 부정적임을 설명하고, 후반부는 가치를 알아줄(appreciate/value) 잠재적 소비자를 찾는 것이 현대 마케터의 목표임을 설명하고 있습니다. 따라서 (A)에는 'deceiving', (B)에는 'value'가 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 속이는 것 ... 가치 있게 여기다
② 식별하는 것 ... 접근하다
③ 강요하는 것 ... 무시하다
④ 보상하는 것 ... 고마워하다
⑤ 속이는 것 ... 과소평가하다

questions.question: 27. 윗글을 읽고, ⓐ의 입장과 ⓑ의 입장에 대한 설명으로 옳은 것만을 <보기>에서 있는 대로 고른 것은? [4점]
questions.passage: Some researchers view spoken languages as incomplete devices for capturing precise differences. They think ⓐ <u>numbers represent the most neutral language of description</u>. However, when our language of description is changed to numbers, we do not move toward greater accuracy. Numbers are no more appropriate 'pictures of the world' than words, music, or painting. While useful for specific purposes (e.g. census taking, income distribution), they delete information of enormous value. For example, the future lives of young students are tied to their scores on national tests. In effect, whether they can continue with their education, where, and at what cost depends importantly on a handful of numbers. These numbers do not account for the quality of schools they have attended, whether they have been tutored, have supportive parents, have test anxiety, and so on. Finally, putting aside the many ways in which statistical results can be manipulated, there are ways in which turning people's lives into numbers is morally insulating. Statistics on crime, homelessness, or the spread of a disease say nothing of people's suffering. We read the statistics as reports on events at a distance, thus allowing us to escape without being disturbed. ⓑ <u>Statistics are human beings with the tears wiped off</u>. Quantify with caution.
summary_sentence:
< 보기 >
ㄱ ⓐ argues that using numbers is a clear and precise way to describe things.
ㄴ ⓑ suggests that numbers can make people's suffering seem distant, reducing our ability to empathize.
ㄷ. Both ⓐ and ⓑ say that numbers always tell the full truth.
ㄹ. While ⓐ trusts numbers, ⓑ questions their ability to represent real human lives.
options: ① ㄱ, ㄴ
② ㄴ, ㄷ
③ ㄷ, ㄹ
④ ㄱ, ㄴ ㄷ
⑤ ㄱ, ㄴ, ㄹ
questions.explanation: ㄱ: ⓐ는 숫자가 묘사의 가장 중립적인 언어라고 생각하므로 옳은 설명입니다. ㄴ: ⓑ는 숫자로 바뀐 통계가 고통을 멀게 느껴지게 하여 공감을 방해한다고 하므로 옳은 설명입니다. ㄷ: ⓐ는 숫자의 중립성을 믿지만 ⓑ는 숫자가 중요한 정보를 삭제하고 감정을 배제한다고 보므로 둘 다 전체 진실을 말한다고 보지 않습니다. ㄹ: ⓐ는 숫자를 신뢰하는 입장인 반면 ⓑ는 숫자가 실제 인간의 삶을 온전히 대변하는 능력에 의문을 제기하므로 옳은 설명입니다.

questions.question: 28. 윗글의 ⓐ와 ⓑ 중, 다음 글 <A>에 해당하는 입장과 그 근거로 적절한 것은? [4.1점]
