Finally, putting aside the many ways in which statistical results can be manipulated, there are ways in which turning people's lives into numbers is morally insulating. Statistics on crime, homelessness, or the spread of a disease say nothing of people's suffering. We read the statistics as reports on events at a distance, thus allowing us to escape without being disturbed. ⓑ <u>Statistics are human beings with the tears wiped off</u>. Quantify with caution.
summary_sentence: Measuring emotional intensity through skin conductance is particularly useful from a scientific viewpoint, because it allows us to put an objective value on a subjective state of mind. We can actually measure your emotional state by tracking how your body subconsciously sweats, by running a bit of electricity through your skin. We can then turn the subjective, subconscious experience of emotional intensity into an objective number by figuring out how good your skin gets at transferring an electrical current.
options: ① ⓐ … <A> argues that emotions are less important than numbers.
② ⓐ … <A> focuses on the moral risks of turning feelings into numbers.
③ ⓐ … <A> shows how numbers can be used to measure human emotions objectively.
④ ⓑ … <A> says turning emotions into numbers removes their meaning.
⑤ ⓑ … <A> warns that numbers ignore the emotional depth of human experience.
questions.explanation: <A>는 피부 전도도를 통해 주관적인 감정 상태를 객관적인 수치로 측정할 수 있다는 과학적 유용성을 강조하므로, 숫자를 중립적이고 정확한 묘사 도구로 보는 ⓐ의 입장에 해당합니다. ③번은 ⓐ의 입장과 부합하며 <A>가 감정을 객관적으로 측정하는 방법을 보여준다는 적절한 근거를 제시합니다.
options_translation: ① ⓐ … <A>는 감정이 숫자보다 덜 중요하다고 주장한다.
② ⓐ … <A>는 감정을 숫자로 바꾸는 것의 도덕적 위험에 집중한다.
③ ⓐ … <A>는 숫자가 인간의 감정을 객관적으로 측정하는 데 어떻게 사용될 수 있는지 보여준다.
④ ⓑ … <A>는 감정을 숫자로 바꾸는 것이 그 의미를 제거한다고 말한다.
⑤ ⓑ … <A>는 숫자가 인간 경험의 감정적 깊이를 무시한다고 경고한다.

questions.question: 1. 다음 글에서 필자가 주장하는 바로 가장 적절한 것은? [3.3점]
questions.passage: Despite the difference between the past and the future, between what has happened and what is to come, it can be suggested, that our sense of the past has always been influenced by our view of the future. Revolutionaries have always looked to the past to frame their future cause, as is amply illustrated by examples from nationalism to communism. The future has often been seen as variously a recovery of a lost time, as a replication of what is established, or as a model bequeathed by a heroic age long gone. The writing of history is based on understanding or explaining future outcomes that were not known to contemporaries, since the historian has the benefit of hindsight and the past is nothing more than the accumulation of futures that are now our past. So, rather than seeing the hand of the past always shaping the future, perhaps it can be seen in reverse, with the past — in the sense of our understanding of it — being shaped by our orientation to the future.
options: ① Each person who looks at the future should all be respected.
② Revolutionaries prepare for the future by analyzing the past objectively.
③ The perception of the future forms the understanding of the past.
④ Ideologies ranging from democracy to communism help us understand history.
⑤ Historians' evaluations of past events help to predict how the future will unfold.
questions.explanation: 이 글은 과거가 미래를 결정하는 것이 아니라, 미래에 대한 우리의 시각이나 지향점이 과거에 대한 이해를 형성한다는 주장을 담고 있습니다. 마지막 문장에서 '과거가 미래를 형성하기보다는 미래에 대한 지향점에 의해 과거가 형성된다'고 명시하고 있으므로 정답은 ③번입니다.
options_translation: ① 미래를 바라보는 각 개인은 모두 존중받아야 한다.
② 혁명가들은 과거를 객관적으로 분석함으로써 미래를 준비한다.
③ 미래에 대한 인식이 과거에 대한 이해를 형성한다.
④ 민주주의에서 공산주의에 이르는 이데올로기들은 우리가 역사를 이해하는 데 도움을 준다.
⑤ 과거 사건들에 대한 역사학자들의 평가는 미래가 어떻게 전개될지 예측하는 데 도움을 준다.

questions.question: 2. 밑줄 친 <u>gesture represents the leading edge of our thought</u>가 다음 글에서 의미하는 바로 가장 적절한 것은? [3점]
questions.passage: When we realize we've said something in error and we pause to go back to correct it, we stop gesturing a couple of hundred milliseconds before we stop speaking. Such sequences suggest the startling notion that our hands "know" what we're going to say before our conscious minds do, and in fact this is often the case. Gesture can mentally prime a word so that the right term comes to our lips. When people are prevented from gesturing, they talk less fluently; their speech becomes halting because their hands are no longer able to supply them with the next word, and the next. Not being able to gesture has other deleterious effects: without gesture to help our mental processes along, we remember less useful information, we solve problems less well, and we are less able to explain our thinking. Far from tagging along as speech's clumsy companion, <u>gesture represents the leading edge of our thought</u>.
options: ① gesture has nothing to do with thinking and speaking
② gesture and thoughts always react at the exact same rate
③ gesture appears before thought and plays a leading role in guiding it
④ speed of gesture that reflects thoughts varies from person to person
⑤ when the flow of conversation is disrupted, gesture can no longer provide any help
questions.explanation: 제스처가 말보다 먼저 멈추거나, 손이 의식적인 마음보다 먼저 말할 내용을 '안다'는 내용을 통해 제스처가 사고보다 앞서 나타나며 사고 과정을 돕고 이끄는 역할을 한다는 것을 알 수 있습니다. 따라서 '제스처가 사고의 앞서가는 선두를 나타낸다'는 말은 ③번 '제스처가 생각보다 먼저 나타나고 그것을 이끄는 주도적인 역할을 한다'는 의미가 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 제스처는 생각하고 말하는 것과 아무런 관련이 없다.
② 제스처와 생각은 항상 정확히 같은 속도로 반응한다.
③ 제스처는 생각보다 먼저 나타나며 그것을 안내하는 주도적인 역할을 한다.
④ 생각을 반영하는 제스처의 속도는 사람마다 다르다.
⑤ 대화의 흐름이 끊기면 제스처는 더 이상 어떤 도움도 줄 수 없다.

questions.question:
3. 다음 글의 요지로 가장 적절한 것을 고르시오
[3.8점]
questions.passage: The concept of ecosystem states should be familiar to anyone with a home vegetable garden. The garden is a small ecosystem that the grower attempts to keep in a specific state, namely the maximization of fruit and vegetable production. To achieve this, the grower is almost always intervening in the dynamics of the ecosystem: they remove unwanted plants that begin to grow and perhaps spray insecticides and fence off the patch to stop insects and other animals from consuming the vegetables. Since maximizing vegetable growth is an inherently unstable state for the ecosystem, the grower is effectively keeping the ball on a slope. If the grower stops intervening, even for a day, the ecosystem, that small patch of ground, will naturally begin to shift to a more stable state. Vegetables may still grow, but yield will almost certainly be lower as other plants crowd out the vegetables and wildlife consume the produce.
options: ① Growing crops in a small household patch tends to be more advantageous when the growing process is guided by sustainable practices.
② In order to support the development of vegetables in a household patch, the grower ought to preserve the area in a stable state.
③ A highly productive household garden created by the grower may persist in an unstable state even in the absence of continued intervention.
④ Human intervention in a household garden, driven by the desire to optimize crop yields, artificially alters the ecosystem, leading it toward a more stable state.
⑤ A home garden is an unstable ecosystem sustained by the grower's intervention to maximize production, and it shifts to a stable state when the intervention stops.
questions.explanation: 이 글은 가정 정원이 생산 극대화를 위해 경작자의 개입에 의해 유지되는 불안정한 생태계이며, 개입이 중단되면 더 안정적인 상태(생산량이 적고 다른 식물이 자라는 상태)로 변한다는 점을 설명하고 있습니다. 따라서 5번이 요지로 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 작은 가정 텃밭에서 작물을 기르는 것은 재배 과정이 지속 가능한 관행에 의해 안내될 때 더 유리한 경향이 있다.
② 가정 텃밭에서 채소의 발달을 지원하기 위해 재배자는 그 지역을 안정적인 상태로 유지해야 한다.
③ 재배자에 의해 만들어진 생산성이 높은 가정 정원은 지속적인 개입이 없는 상태에서도 불안정한 상태로 지속될 수 있다.
④ 농작물 수확량을 최적화하려는 욕구에 의한 가정 정원에 대한 인간의 개입은 인위적으로 생태계를 변화시켜 더 안정적인 상태로 이끈다.
⑤ 가정 정원은 생산을 극대화하기 위한 재배자의 개입에 의해 유지되는 불안정한 생태계이며, 개입이 멈추면 안정된 상태로 전환된다.

questions.question:
4. 다음 글의 요지로 가장 적절한 것을 고르시오
 [3.4점]
questions.passage:
In the 1950s, American sitcoms played a significant role in introducing progressive values to mainstream audiences. While these shows often appeared to reinforce traditional norms—centering on the nuclear family and domestic life—they also challenged certain social expectations through humor and character dynamics. For example, I Love Lucy portrayed a strong-willed, ambitious housewife who frequently subverted gender roles in pursuit of her own dreams. Father Knows Best and Leave It to Beaver, though presenting idealized family life, occasionally addressed moral dilemmas and emotional complexity that encouraged empathy and reflection. Workplace comedies like The Phil Silvers Show brought military and professional settings into the domestic sphere, expanding the scope of what could be considered "family-friendly" content. The humor, while generally light-hearted, often relied on misunderstandings that revealed deeper tensions around gender, class, and authority. Far from being mere entertainment, these sitcoms acted as agents of cultural change, helping mainstream audiences become more receptive to evolving social norms and values.

*subvert: 도전하다
options: ① American sitcoms that emerged in the 1950s emphasized patriarchal family structures and conventional norms.
② By negatively portraying socially taboo values in 1950s American sitcoms, conservative values of the time were reinforced.
③ American sitcoms have traditionally made the greatest contribution to shaping the foundation of modern television comedy.
④ Among the American sitcoms of the 1950s, the story of the daily life of the family in the suburbs received the most sympathy.
⑤ American sitcoms in 1950s questioned societal norms, playing a crucial role in shaping public acceptance of emerging progressive values.
questions.explanation: 이 글은 1950년대 미국 시트콤들이 겉으로는 전통적 규범을 따르는 듯 보였으나, 실제로는 유머와 캐릭터 역학을 통해 사회적 기대를 도전하고 진보적인 가치를 대중에게 소개하는 문화적 변화의 매개체 역할을 했음을 강조하고 있습니다. 따라서 5번이 요지로 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 1950년대에 등장한 미국 시트콤은 가부장적인 가족 구조와 관습적인 규범을 강조했다.
② 1950년대 미국 시트콤에서 사회적으로 금기시되는 가치들을 부정적으로 묘사함으로써 당시의 보수적 가치가 강화되었다.
③ 미국 시트콤은 전통적으로 현대 텔레비전 코미디의 토대를 형성하는 데 가장 큰 기여를 해왔다.
④ 1950년대 미국 시트콤 중 교외 가족의 일상 이야기가 가장 많은 공감을 얻었다.
⑤ 1950년대 미국 시트콤은 사회적 규범에 의문을 제기하며, 새로 떠오르는 진보적 가치에 대한 대중의 수용을 형성하는 데 중요한 역할을 했다.

questions.question: 7. [3.4점] 다음 글의 제목으로 가장 적절한 것을 고르시오
questions.passage: Stress not only affects physical disease but also the very structure of our brains, making us even more likely to experience a drained brain. A number of studies have been done to reveal what happens in healthy people's brains when they go through something stressful. One study demonstrated a link between a smaller hippocampus and people who had experienced long-lasting stress. Why does this matter? This part of the brain helps you remain resilient in the face of stress and is involved in mood regulation. It also helps you to monitor the safety of your environment and store dangerous images in your long-term memory so you can avoid them in the future. It does all these things as part of its duties of regulating your sympathetic and parasympathetic nervous systems. But chronic stress can confuse the hippocampus and lead to turning signals for cortisol "on" instead of "off," which can trap you in a constant state of fight, flight, or freeze.
options: ① Stress Reshapes Your Brain for the Better
② Chronic Stress: No Evident Link with the Hippocampus
③ Stress and the Shrunk Hippocampus: Non-Resilient Brain
④ How to Mitigate Stress and Attain Optimal Performance
⑤ Constructive Side of Stress: Transform Your Brain, Transform Your life
questions.explanation: 이 글은 만성적인 스트레스가 뇌의 구조, 특히 해마(hippocampus)의 크기에 영향을 미쳐 스트레스에 대한 회복력을 낮추고 기분 조절 능력을 저하시키는 과정을 설명하고 있다. 따라서 해마의 위축과 회복력 없는 뇌를 언급한 ③번이 제목으로 가장 적절하다.
options_translation: ① 스트레스는 당신의 뇌를 더 좋게 재구성한다
② 만성 스트레스: 해마와 명백한 연관성이 없음
③ 스트레스와 위축된 해마: 회복력이 없는 뇌
④ 스트레스를 완화하고 최적의 성과를 얻는 방법
⑤ 스트레스의 건설적인 측면: 뇌를 바꾸고 삶을 바꿔라

questions.question: 8. [3점] 다음 글의 제목으로 가장 적절한 것을 고르시오
questions.passage: There are reasons why science is not fully trusted and why healthy skepticism and critical thinking are essential. In spite of professional standards, claims of objectivity, and the peer review process, the conduct of science can be biased. All experts are not the same, nor do they submit their work to the same scrutiny. Knowing the source of funding can be important in evaluating scientific claims. For example, the Harvard researchers who made claims in the late 1960s about the problems with dietary fat, leading the nation away from perceiving sugar as one of the main causes in health problems, were funded in part by the sugar industry. The authors did not reveal their funding source to the New England Journal of Medicine, where their influential article appeared. Their article shaped a generation of changes in eating patterns that appears to have encouraged higher use of sugar, now widely implicated as a source of the rise in obesity and diabetes. Stories such as this one fuel suspicion — but also lead to further safeguards in the scientific process. Funding disclosures, although not required five decades ago, have since been made compulsory.
options: ① What is the Most Important Reason to Evaluate the Originality of Hypothesis?
② The Amount of Money that Goes into Sugar Production
③ The Need for Diversification of Experimental Methods
④ Reasons to Question the Credibility of Science
⑤ The Quickest Way to Become a Scientist
questions.explanation: 이 글은 과학적 연구가 자금 출처나 전문가의 편향성에 의해 영향을 받을 수 있음을 지적하며, 과학을 완전히 신뢰하지 말고 비판적 사고를 견지해야 할 이유(설탕 산업의 자금 지원 사례 등)를 설명하고 있다. 따라서 ④번이 가장 적절한 제목이다.
options_translation: ① 가설의 독창성을 평가하는 가장 중요한 이유는 무엇인가?
② 설탕 생산에 들어가는 자금의 양
③ 실험 방법의 다양화 필요성
④ 과학의 신뢰성에 의문을 제기해야 하는 이유들
⑤ 과학자가 되는 가장 빠른 방법

questions.question: 9. [3.4점] 다음 글의 밑줄 친 (a)~(e) 중, 어법상 틀린 부분이 있는 것의 개수를 고르시오
questions.passage: Since their start in the early 1950s U.S. television sitcoms have charted many of the social conflicts in U.S. society: civil rights, women's rights in the home and in the workplace, children's rights, immigration and multiculturalism, (a)<u>as well as evolving conceptions of the family</u>, (b)<u>Each of these issues has been dealt with through humour</u> in a way that has helped to make more progressive values more acceptable than previously. Often a character, usually someone marked as a bigot, resisted one or more of these developments (c)<u>and was then made to appear ridiculously</u>. That character (d)<u>was cut down either through one's own stupidity, a brief scolding from others, or both</u>. In this way, the humour of sitcoms acted as a cost-effective means (e)<u>that encouraged acceptance of a more pluralistic and tolerant society</u>.
options: ① 1개
② 2개
③ 3개
④ 4개
⑤ 5개
questions.explanation: (c)에서 appear는 2형식 동사로 쓰였으므로 주격 보어 자리에 부사 ridiculously 대신 형용사 ridiculous가 와야 합니다. (a), (b), (d), (e)는 어법상 적절합니다.

questions.question: 11. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 (a)~(e) 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것만은 있는 대로 고른 것은? [3.7점]
questions.passage:
Quite often the interaction between groups is socially unequal, and this is reflected in the fact that in many cases borrowing of words or constructions goes mostly or entirely in one direction, from the more (a)<u>dominant</u> group to the less favored one. This linguistic asymmetry mirrors social (b)<u>hierarchies</u>, where powerful cultures exert influence to others. The languages of socially subordinated groups may from quite an early period of contact provide terminology for objects or practices with which speakers of the more powerful group were previously unfamiliar, but the effects of contact in that direction may not progress any further than this. As the powerful groups language gains prestige, speakers of the less (c)<u>marginalized</u> language may gradually lose their native tongue. In some cases, as with the Dharug language of Sydney, Australia, the source of some of the earliest loans from Indigenous Australian languages into English, the fate of the language system is (d)<u>revitalzaion</u> after the obliteration of many of its speakers. The remainder shifted to varieties of English, the language of the people who had suppressed them. This case vividly illustrates that linguistic dominance often mirrors social (e)<u>inequality</u>.
* asymmetry: 비대칭, 불균형
questions.explanation: (c) marginalized: 문맥상 지배적인 언어가 위상을 얻음에 따라 원어민 언어를 잃게 되는 쪽은 '덜' 소외된 언어가 아니라 '더' 소외된 혹은 '지배적이지 않은' 언어의 화자들이다. (d) revitalzaion: 해당 문장은 많은 화자들이 말살된 후 언어 체계가 겪게 된 운명을 설명하고 있으며, 뒤에 남은 사람들이 영어로 전환했다는 점으로 미루어 '부활(revitalization)'이 아니라 '소멸(extinction/obliteration)'이 적절하다.

questions.question: 15. [2.9점] 다음 글에서 전체 흐름과 관계 없는 문장을 고르시오
questions.passage: It is important to recognize that although science is a rule-based procedure, it is very much a creative process. A conjecture is a philosophical invention, cooked up rather mystically by the mind through the mental computation we call careful contemplation. However, until the hypothesis is tested against reality, it is not yet truly knowledge; it is just information that represents speculation. Knowledge is information that has demonstrated its usefulness. It is what is left over after cycles of experimental testing have eliminated false theories. ① Many of the theories discarded during this process were later proven to be true. ② As scientists continually test their hypotheses and modify their models in response to new and surprising data, a process known as "learning loop" emerges, which statisticians refer to as Bayesian updating. ③ Based on Bayes' Rule, developed by eighteenth-century English statistician and philosopher Thomas Bayes, Bayesian updating is a mathematical process through which accepted theories or predictive models become increasingly accurate as they are repeatedly tested against competing variants. ④ In simple terms, it describes how scientists modify and refine their theories as more tests are performed. ⑤ Ultimately, science progresses through a dynamic interplay of creativity, testing, and continuous refinement.
questions.explanation: 이 글은 과학이 가설 설정과 실험적 검증 과정을 통해 지식으로 발전하며, 베이지안 업데이트와 같은 과정을 통해 이론이 정교화된다는 내용을 담고 있습니다. 하지만 ①번 문장은 '버려진 이론들이 나중에 사실로 입증되었다'는 내용으로, 가설이 검증을 통과하여 지식이 된다는 전체적인 논리적 흐름(수정 및 정교화 과정)에서 벗어납니다.

questions.question: 17. [2.8점] 다음 글에서 전체 흐름과 관계 없는 문장은?
questions.passage: If the brain has already stored someone's face and name, why do we still end up remembering one and not the other? ① <u>This is because the brain has something of a two-tier memory system at work when it comes to retrieving memories, and this gives rise to a common yet infuriating sensation: recognising someone, but not being able to remember how or why, or what their name is.</u> ② <u>This happens because the brain differentiates between familiarity and recall.</u> ③ <u>To clarify, familiarity (or recognition) is when you encounter someone or something and you know you've done so before.</u> But beyond that, you've got nothing; all you can say is this person/thing is already in your memories. ④ <u>Memories imprinted through the sense of smell affect adulthood.</u> ⑤ <u>Recall is when you can access the original memory of how and why you know this person; recognition is just flagging up the fact that the memory exists.</u>
questions.explanation: 이 글은 뇌가 기억을 인출할 때 '친숙함(익숙함)'과 '회상'이라는 두 단계 시스템을 사용한다는 점을 설명하며, 왜 얼굴은 알겠는데 이름은 기억나지 않는 현상이 발생하는지 다루고 있습니다. ④번 문장은 후각을 통해 각인된 기억이 성인기에 영향을 미친다는 내용으로, 기억 인출의 이중 구조라는 주제와 무관합니다.

questions.question: 19. 글의 흐름으로 보아, 주어진 문장이 들어가기에 가장 적절한 곳을 고르시오. [2.8점]
questions.passage: Great scientists are seldom one-hit wonders. Newton is a prime example: beyond the Newtonian mechanics, he developed the theory of gravitation, calculus, laws of motion, and optimization. ( ① ) In fact, well-known scientists are often involved in multiple discoveries, a phenomenon potentially explained by the Matthew effect. ( ② ) Indeed, an initial success may offer a scientist legitimacy, improve peer perception, provide knowledge of how to score and win, enhance social status, and attract resources and quality collaborators, each of these payoffs further increasing her odds of scoring another win. ( ③ ) Therefore, future success again goes to those who have had success earlier, not because of advantages offered by the previous success, but because the earlier success was indicative of a hidden talent. ( ④ ) The Matthew effect posits that success alone increases the future probability of success, raising the question: Does status dictate outcomes, or does it simply reflect an underlying talent or quality? ( ⑤ ) In other words, is there really a Matthew effect after all?
questions.insertion_sentence: Yet, there is an appealing alternative explanation: Great scientists nave multiple hits and consistently succeed in their scientific endeavors simply because they're exceptionally talented.
questions.explanation: 주어진 문장은 뛰어난 과학자들이 단순히 예외적으로 재능이 있기 때문에 지속적으로 성공한다는 '대안적인 설명'을 제시하고 있습니다. 본문 ( ③ ) 앞부분까지는 이전의 성공이 자원과 동료를 끌어들여 다음 성공 가능성을 높인다는 '매튜 효과(Matthew effect)'에 대해 설명하고 있으며, ( ③ ) 뒷부분의 'Therefore' 문장은 이전 성공의 이점 때문이 아니라 '숨겨진 재능(hidden talent)'을 나타내는 것이었기 때문에 성공이 이어진다고 결론짓고 있습니다. 따라서 재능에 기반한 대안적 설명을 도입하는 주어진 문장은 ( ③ )에 들어가는 것이 가장 적절합니다.

questions.question:
20. 다음 글의 내용을 한 문장으로 요약하고자 한다. 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것을 고르시오.
 [3.5점]
questions.passage: The explosion of popular music in the second half of the twentieth century as well as the global circulation and dissemination of music by the creative industries propelled a new understanding of accessibility in relation to music. Suddenly, in the 1950s, anyone could pick up spoons, a couple of pans, a second-hand guitar and start a band. This led to specific genres such as skiffle, but also, more generally, reflected a much more relaxed and inclusive attitude to music making. While ordinary people had always sung and made music, the popular music movement was driven by a spirit of rebellion and freedom. This approach led to the punk movement, whose musicians even made it a condition for their music to be non-virtuosic and accessible to all in the 1970s. Groups who had been entirely excluded from music revelled in opportunities to create. This led to a sense of novelty and empowerment in and beyond the music sphere.
questions.summary_sentence: In the mid to late 20th century, the rapid spread of popular music (A)________ accessibility of music, which in turn porivided chances for musically (B)__________ individuals to make music.
options: ① denied ... neglected
② fostered ... overlooked
③ promoted ... outstanding
④ facilitated ... innovative
⑤ integrated ... proficient
questions.explanation: 20세기 후반 대중음악의 확산은 음악에 대한 접근성을 높였으며(fostered/promoted/facilitated), 이는 이전에 음악 활동에서 배제되거나 소외되었던(overlooked/neglected) 사람들에게 기회를 제공했다는 내용입니다. 지문에서 'non-virtuosic(비거장적인)'과 'excluded(배제된)'라는 표현을 통해 전문적이지 않거나 간과되었던 사람들을 의미하는 (B)의 'overlooked'가 적절하며, 접근성을 촉진했다는 의미의 (A) 'fostered'가 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 부정했다 ... 무시된
② 촉진했다 ... 간과된
③ 증진시켰다 ... 뛰어난
④ 용이하게 했다 ... 혁신적인
⑤ 통합했다 ... 능숙한

questions.question: 21. [3.4점] 다음 글의 내용을 한 문장으로 요약하고자 한다. 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: The governments of virtually every country on the planet attach great importance to achieving food security and a wide variety of mechanisms have been developed to realize this goal. The first issue governments face in achieving national food security is the problem of insuring that adequate amounts of food are available to the resident population. Some governments have set goals of food self-sufficiency, which means most if not all of the food available in a country comes from the domestic farming system. However, food security does not require food self-sufficiency because countries can import food items not easily produced within the country. Agricultural products are, after all, highly sensitive to climatic, soil and other conditions that tend to vary around the world. Even countries with extremely productive agricultural sectors are not fully self-sufficient in all food items. The United States, for example, depends on imports for its supply of coffee, tea, bananas and other tropical products. In general, the problem of assuring adequate food supplies is solved by relying on both domestic production and imports.
questions.summary_sentence: Most governments' prime objective, (A)________ national food security, may be realized through both domestic production and the importation of food items that are not readily (B)________ within national borders.
options: ① attaining ... cultivable
② securing ... inaccessible
③ fulfilling ... spoiled
④ restraining ... producible
⑤ obstructing ... exploitable
questions.explanation: 이 글은 국가 식량 안보를 달성하기 위해 정부가 국내 생산과 수입을 병행한다는 내용을 담고 있습니다. 요약문에서 (A)는 식량 안보를 '달성하는 것(attaining)'이 정부의 주요 목표라는 흐름이 되어야 하며, (B)는 국경 내에서 쉽게 '경작될(cultivable)' 수 없는 품목을 수입한다는 내용이 적절하므로 정답은 ①번입니다.
options_translation: ① 달성하는 것 ... 경작할 수 있는
② 확보하는 것 ... 접근 불가능한
③ 충족시키는 것 ... 부패된
④ 억제하는 것 ... 생산 가능한
⑤ 방해하는 것 ... 개발 가능한

questions.question: 22. [3.5점] 다음 글의 내용을 한 문장으로 요약하고자 한다. 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Commitment is the glue holding together characteristically human forms of social life. Commitments make individuals' behavior predictable in the face of fluctuations in their desires and interests, thereby facilitating the planning and coordination of joint actions involving multiple agents. Moreover, commitments make people willing to perform actions that they would not otherwise perform. For example, a taxi driver picks up his clients and transports them to their desired destination because they are committed to paying him afterwards for the service, and a construction worker performs her job every day because her employer has made a credible commitment to pay her at the end of the month. Indeed, the taxi driver and the construction worker are willing to accept money as payment only because a network of other agents (notably the central bank) is committed to taking various measures to sustain the currency in question. Thus, social objects and institutions such as jobs, money, government, scientific collaborations and marriage depend for their origin and stability upon the credibility of commitments.
questions.summary_sentence: Commitment plays a crucial role in human social life by ensuring (A)_________ behavior, enabling cooperation, and thereby supporting the (B)_________ of social institutions.
options: ① resistible ... conformity
② incredible ... consistency
③ acceptable ... reconstruction
④ observable ... elasticity
⑤ foreseeable ... steadiness
questions.explanation: 이 글은 약속(Commitment)이 인간의 사회적 삶에서 행동을 예측 가능하게 하고 사회적 제도의 안정성을 유지해 준다는 내용입니다. 요약문에서 (A)는 행동을 예측 가능하게 한다는 'foreseeable(예측 가능한)'이 적절하며, (B)는 사회 제도의 'steadiness(안정성/안정성)'를 지지한다는 내용이 적절하므로 정답은 ⑤번입니다.
options_translation: ① 저항할 수 있는 ... 순응
② 믿을 수 없는 ... 일관성
③ 수용 가능한 ... 재건
④ 관찰 가능한 ... 탄력성
⑤ 예측 가능한 ... 안정성

questions.question: 26. 윗글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은? [3.8점]
questions.passage:
In 1900, at the close of the first decade in which electric systems had become a practical <u>(a)alternative</u> for manufacturers, less than 5 percent of the power used in factories came from electricity. But the technological advances of suppliers made electric systems and electric motors ever more <u>(b)affordable</u> and reliable, and the suppliers' intensive marketing programs also sped the adoption of the new technology. Further accelerating the shift was the rapid expansion in the number of skilled electrical engineers, who provided the <u>(c)expertise</u> needed to install and run the new systems. In short order, electric power had gone from <u>(d)exotic</u> to commonplace.
But one thing didn't change. Factories continued to build their own power-supply systems on their own premises. Few manufacturers considered buying electricity from the small central stations. Designed to supply lighting to local homes and shops, the central stations had neither the size nor the skill to <u>(e)serve</u> the needs of big factories. And the factory owners, having always supplied their own power, were reluctant to assign such a critical function to an outsider. They knew that a glitch in power supply would bring their <u>(f)operations</u> to a halt—and that a lot of glitches might well mean bankruptcy. As a result, a survey conducted at the beginning of the new century found that ____________________.
options: ① manufacturers considered private plants--more unaccustomed to themselves than central power plants
② the number of non--publicly operated power-supply facilities in service exceeded that of central power stations
③ numerous individuals recognized the efficacy of the government's initiative to broaden the provision of electricity to households
④ factory owners ceased independently generating the electricity needed to run their business and began relying on national power stations instead
⑤ large factories responsible for mass production experienced a decline, whereas smaller-scale enterprises specializing in limited production volumes began to emerge
questions.explanation: 본문은 공장들이 외부 중앙 발전소로부터 전기를 구매하는 것을 꺼려하고 자체 전력 공급 시스템을 유지했다는 내용을 다루고 있습니다. 따라서 새로운 세기 초의 조사 결과는 중앙 발전소보다 사설(비공공) 전력 공급 시설의 수가 더 많았다는 내용이 들어가는 것이 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 제조업자들은 중앙 발전소보다 개인 공장을 스스로에게 더 익숙하지 않은 것으로 간주했다
② 가동 중인 비공공 운영 전력 공급 시설의 수가 중앙 발전소의 수를 초과했다
③ 수많은 개인들이 가정에 대한 전기 공급을 확대하려는 정부 주도의 효능을 인식했다
④ 공장 소유주들은 사업 운영에 필요한 전기를 독립적으로 생산하는 것을 중단하고 대신 국가 발전소에 의존하기 시작했다
⑤ 대량 생산을 담당하는 대형 공장들은 쇠퇴한 반면, 제한된 생산량을 전문으로 하는 소규모 기업들이 나타나기 시작했다

questions.question: 27. <보기>에서 윗글의 밑줄 친 단어 (a)~(f)의 문맥상 영영 풀이로 적절한 것의 개수는? [3.5점]
questions.passage:
In 1900, at the close of the first decade in which electric systems had become a practical <u>(a)alternative</u> for manufacturers, less than 5 percent of the power used in factories came from electricity. But the technological advances of suppliers made electric systems and electric motors ever more <u>(b)affordable</u> and reliable, and the suppliers' intensive marketing programs also sped the adoption of the new technology. Further accelerating the shift was the rapid expansion in the number of skilled electrical engineers, who provided the <u>(c)expertise</u> needed to install and run the new systems. In short order, electric power had gone from <u>(d)exotic</u> to commonplace.
But one thing didn't change. Factories continued to build their own power-supply systems on their own premises. Few manufacturers considered buying electricity from the small central stations. Designed to supply lighting to local homes and shops, the central stations had neither the size nor the skill to <u>(e)serve</u> the needs of big factories. And the factory owners, having always supplied their own power, were reluctant to assign such a critical function to an outsider. They knew that a glitch in power supply would bring their <u>(f)operations</u> to a halt—and that a lot of glitches might well mean bankruptcy. As a result, a survey conducted at the beginning of the new century found that ____________________.
vocabulary_box: (a) something that can be chosen instead of something else; a different option or possibility
(b) inexpensive enough to be purchased or obtained without difficulty; reasonably priced
(c) professional skill or knowledge in a particular subject
(d) strikingly unusual or different in <u>appearance</u>, effect, or character; strange and unfamiliar
(e) to fulfill or meet the requirements of something or someone
(f) a medical procedure that involves cutting into someone's body in order to repair or remove a part that is damaged or diseased
options: ① 1개
② 2개
③ 3개
④ 4개
⑤ 5개
questions.explanation: (a) alternative(대안), (b) affordable(저렴한/구매 가능한), (c) expertise(전문 지식), (d) exotic(외래의/특이한), (e) serve(충족시키다)는 영영 풀이가 적절합니다. 그러나 (f) operations는 지문에서 '공장 운영/가동'을 의미하는데, 보기의 풀이는 '의학적 수술'을 설명하고 있어 부적절합니다. 따라서 적절한 것은 (a), (b), (c), (d), (e) 총 5개입니다.

questions.question: 1. 다음 글의 내용과 일치하지 않는 것은? [3.2점]
questions.passage:
In university, everyone seemed more talented than me, and they all worked so hard that I felt small in comparison. I thought about giving up my dream of becoming an artist. Then one day, I happened to see a drawing I had won an award for from middle school on the kitchen wall. I was embarrassed because it wasn’t very good.
People say you shouldn’t compare apples to oranges, and they’re right. So it’s unreasonable to compare yourself to others, whether online or in person. Maybe they had an advantage, or even a disadvantage, that you didn’t. If you are going to compare yourself to anyone, the only fair comparison is “yesterday-you.” Only you know where you started and how much effort you’ve put in. I couldn’t see the progress in my ability when I only compared myself to others. Everyone develops differently. I’m able to see now the drawing in the kitchen was full of mistakes that I no longer make. It’s empowering to focus on my own growth rather than envy the achievements of others. Your competition isn’t the person next door or the influencer on social media: it’s you.
options: ① I felt inferior to the university students, as they appeared more skilled and invested great effort in their field.
② I didn’t think the drawing that received an award in middle school looked very good.
③ It’s important to compare myself to others to see how much progress has been made.
④ Focusing on personal growth is more valuable than feeling envious of others’ successes.
⑤ The real competition isn’t others, but yourself.
questions.explanation: 지문에서 타인과 자신을 비교하는 것은 불합리하며(unreasonable), 자신의 성장에 집중하는 것이 타인의 성취를 부러워하는 것보다 힘을 준다(empowering)고 언급하고 있습니다. 따라서 타인과 비교하는 것이 중요하다는 3번 선지는 글의 내용과 일치하지 않습니다.
options_translation: ① 대학생들이 더 숙련되어 보이고 그들의 분야에 큰 노력을 쏟았기 때문에 나는 그들에게 열등감을 느꼈다.
② 나는 중학교 때 상을 받은 그림이 매우 훌륭해 보인다고 생각하지 않았다.
③ 얼마나 많은 진전이 이루어졌는지 확인하기 위해 나 자신을 타인과 비교하는 것이 중요하다.
④ 개인적인 성장에 집중하는 것이 타인의 성공을 부러워하는 것보다 더 가치 있다.
⑤ 진정한 경쟁 상대는 타인이 아니라 자기 자신이다.

questions.question: 2. 밑줄 친 <u>the greatest teacher</u>가 다음 글에서 의미하는 바로 가장 적절한 것은? [3.4점]
questions.passage: As we strive to grow, we often look for shortcuts and naturally move toward the path of least resistance. Yet in doing so, we lose valuable opportunities to develop the strength, self-control, and way of thinking needed to truly get better at something. We often take the easy route to improve our skills. Many of us never really work to achieve mastery in the key areas of life. These skills are key traits that aren’t developed through ease, but are shaped through challenge. Highly successful athletes don’t win because they have superior equipment; they win by facing hardship to gain strength and skill. They succeed by confronting challenges, practicing on purpose, and building a mindset focused on winning. It’s the mental preparation, winning mindset, strategy, and skill that set them apart. We grow stronger through difficulty, not through comfort or ease. Hardship is not just a lesson for the next time in front of us. Hardship will be <u>the greatest teacher</u> we will ever have in life.
options: ① a powerful force that ensures prosperity
② an experience that offers genuine and lasting growth
③ a source of wisdom gained through repeated success
④ a guide who shows the easiest path to improvement
⑤ a person who gives clear instructions and encouragement
questions.explanation: 글의 전체적인 흐름은 성장이 쉬운 길(ease, comfort)이 아니라 고난(hardship)과 도전(challenge)을 통해 이루어진다고 강조하고 있습니다. 따라서 '가장 위대한 스승'으로서의 고난은 진정하고 지속적인 성장을 제공하는 경험을 의미합니다.
options_translation: ① 번영을 보장하는 강력한 힘
② 진정하고 지속적인 성장을 제공하는 경험
③ 반복된 성공을 통해 얻은 지혜의 원천
④ 향상을 위한 가장 쉬운 길을 보여주는 안내자
⑤ 명확한 지시와 격려를 주는 사람

questions.question:
[3-4] 다음 글의 주제로 가장 적절한 것을 고르시오.

3. [3.3점]
questions.passage: Although efforts have been made to develop standards for digital information preservation, the needs of people with disabilities have largely been neglected, leaving many valuable digital resources inaccessible to those who are blind, deaf, or have other health conditions. While some progress has been made in educational and commercial technology, academic digital projects often fail to take care of these needs due to limited awareness or knowledge. As technology becomes increasingly central to education and communication, digital accessibility is more important than ever. Features like screen reader support and captions not only assist individuals with disabilities but also improve the user experience for everyone. To enhance digital accessibility, inclusive design should be prioritized from the outset of digital projects and incorporated into training and funding policies to ensure the needs of all users, including those with disabilities, are met.
options: ① the significance of inclusive design in ensuring digital accessibility for both people with and without disabilities
② the critical role of innovative design in creating environments that support only people with disabilities
③ specific methods for the social integration of people with and without disabilities
④ the importance of digital technology for physical recovery from a disability
⑤ an effective way to digitize information for people with health conditions
questions.explanation: 글의 후반부에서 디지털 접근성을 높이기 위해 장애인과 비장애인 모두를 위한 '포괄적 디자인(inclusive design)'의 중요성을 강조하고 있으므로 ①번이 주제로 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 장애인과 비장애인 모두를 위한 디지털 접근성 보장에 있어서 포괄적 디자인의 중요성
② 장애인만을 지원하는 환경을 조성하는 데 있어 혁신적 디자인의 결정적 역할
③ 장애인과 비장애인의 사회 통합을 위한 구체적인 방법들
④ 장애로부터의 신체적 회복을 위한 디지털 기술의 중요성
⑤ 건강 상태가 좋지 않은 사람들을 위해 정보를 디지털화하는 효과적인 방법

questions.question:
[3-4] 다음 글의 주제로 가장 적절한 것을 고르시오.

4. [3.4점]
questions.passage: Although praise is one of the most powerful tools available for improving young children's behavior, it is equally powerful for improving your child's self-esteem. Preschoolers believe what their parents tell them in a very profound way. They do not yet have the cognitive sophistication to reason analytically and reject false information. If a preschool boy consistently hears from his mother that he is smart and a good helper, he is likely to incorporate that information into his self-image. Thinking of himself as a boy who is smart and knows how to do things is likely to make him endure longer in problem-solving efforts and increase his confidence in trying new and difficult tasks. Similarly, thinking of himself as the kind of boy who is a good helper will make him more likely to volunteer to help with tasks at home and at preschool.
options: ① the power of frequent compliments to correct preschoolers' misbehavior
② preschoolers' stages of cognitive development enhanced by their parents' praise
③ preschoolers' confidence and self-esteem improved by their parental compliments
④ the negative impact of parent-child relationships on self-esteem in young children
⑤ the ability for young children to distinguish truth from false information
questions.explanation: 부모의 칭찬이 미취학 아동의 자아상에 통합되어 자신감과 자존감을 높여준다는 내용이므로 ③번이 주제로 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 미취학 아동의 잘못된 행동을 교정하는 빈번한 칭찬의 힘
② 부모의 칭찬으로 향상되는 미취학 아동의 인지 발달 단계
③ 부모의 칭찬으로 향상되는 미취학 아동의 자신감과 자존감
④ 부모-자녀 관계가 어린 자녀의 자존감에 미치는 부정적인 영향
⑤ 어린 아이들이 진실과 거짓 정보를 구별하는 능력

questions.question: 5. 다음 글의 요지로 가장 적절한 것은? [3.3점]
questions.passage: Advertisers often displayed considerable facility in adapting their claims to the market status of the goods they promoted. Fleischmann's yeast, for instance, was used as an ingredient for cooking homemade bread. Yet more and more people in the early 20th century were buying their bread from stores or bakeries, so consumer demand for yeast decreased. The producer of Fleischmann's yeast hired the J. Walter Thompson advertising agency to come up with a different marketing strategy to boost sales. No longer the "Soul of Bread," the Thompson agency first turned yeast into an important source of vitamins with significant health benefits. Shortly thereafter, the advertising agency transformed yeast into a natural laxative. Repositioning yeast helped increase sales.
options: ① Advertisers often modify how they present their products depending on their market status.
② The sales of a product are determined by its quantity rather than its marketing strategy.
③ To devise a marketing strategy, you don't need to know in detail the unknown characteristics of the product you want to promote.
④ Yeast was used in various ways according to the changes of the times.
⑤ Advertisers are willing to advertise exaggeratedly to boost sales.
questions.explanation: 광고주들이 시장 상황에 맞게 제품의 용도를 재포지셔닝하여 홍보 방식을 조정한다는 내용이므로 ①번이 요지로 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 광고주들은 종종 시장 지위에 따라 제품을 제시하는 방식을 수정한다.
② 제품의 판매는 마케팅 전략보다는 수량에 의해 결정된다.
③ 마케팅 전략을 세우기 위해, 홍보하고자 하는 제품의 알려지지 않은 특성을 자세히 알 필요는 없다.
④ 효모는 시대의 변화에 따라 다양한 방식으로 사용되었다.
⑤ 광고주들은 판매를 촉진하기 위해 기꺼이 과장 광고를 한다.

questions.question: 6. 밑줄 친 ①-⑤ 단어의 의미가 옳지 않은 것은? [3.3점]
questions.passage:
A very popular dessert in Thailand is sweet, ①<u>sticky</u> rice topped with fresh mango and coconut milk. Mango with sticky rice is a dish that is extremely hard not to love. Rice is one of the world's most ②<u>consumed</u> grains, so it should not be surprising that it can be combined with other interesting ingredients. Fruit is included as one of the ingredients, which is nutritious, sweet, and ③<u>plentiful</u> in many parts of the world. The combination of fruit and rice may seem unusual, but it’s actually quite common.
According to the Tourism Authority of Thailand, neither mango nor sticky rice is ④<u>native</u> to Thailand. Mangoes are native to Myanmar and India, and sticky rice is commonly eaten in Laos, which shares a border with Thailand. This suggests that the ⑤<u>roots</u> of the dish are probably a result of the mixing of cultures in Southeast Asia. Rice is usually thought of as a food that is eaten as a meal, but its use as a dessert shows how simple ingredients can create innovative, wonderful treats.
options: ① sticky: having a substance (such as glue or honey) on it that things easily attach to
② consume: to eat or drink something
③ plentiful: very small in amount or number
④ native: produced, living, or existing naturally in a particular region
⑤ root: the origin or basis of something
questions.explanation: 본문에서 plentiful은 '풍부한'이라는 의미로 쓰였으나, 영영 풀이 ③번의 'very small in amount or number'는 '매우 적은 양이나 수'를 의미하므로 옳지 않습니다. '풍부한'의 영영 풀이는 'existing in large amounts' 등이 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① sticky: 어떤 물건이 쉽게 달라붙게 하는 물질(풀이나 꿀 같은)이 묻어 있는
② consume: 무언가를 먹거나 마시다
③ plentiful: 양이나 수가 매우 적은
④ native: 특정 지역에서 자연적으로 생산되거나, 살거나, 존재하는
⑤ root: 무언가의 기원이나 기초

questions.question:
[7-9] 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 어법상 틀린 것을 고르시오.

7. [3.5점]
questions.passage: Someone else’s body language affects our own body, ①<u>which</u> then creates an emotional echo that makes us feel accordingly. As Louis Armstrong sang, “When you’re smiling, the whole world smiles with you.” If copying another’s smile lifts our mood, it means that their emotion has ②<u>been transmitted</u> through our body. ③<u>Unusual</u> as it may seem, experiments have shown that the way we use our body can affect how we feel. For example, our emotional state can be enhanced by ④<u>simply lifting</u> up the corners of our mouth. If people are asked to bite down on a pencil lengthwise, - ensuring it didn’t touch their lips, thereby copying a smile- they judge cartoons funnier than if they have been asked to frown. This idea ⑤<u>what</u> the body drives emotion is often summed up in the phrase, “I must be afraid, because I’m running.
questions.explanation: ⑤번의 what은 뒤에 'the body(주어) drives(동사) emotion(목적어)'라는 완전한 문장이 오고 있으며, 앞에 추상명사인 'This idea'가 있으므로, 이를 수식하는 동격의 접속사 that으로 고쳐야 합니다.

questions.question: 9. 다음 밑줄 친 부분 중, 어법상 틀린 것은? [3.5점]
questions.passage: Few people will be surprised to hear that poverty tends to create stress: a 2006 study published in the American journal Psychosomatic Medicine, for example, noted ①<u>that</u> a lower socioeconomic status was associated with higher levels of stress hormones in the body. Yet, stress is not only found in poorer communities - richer and more economically developed societies face a different kind of stress. One of the most significant factors ②<u>is</u> the pressure of time. According to a 1999 study ③<u>conducted</u> by American psychologist Robert Levine and Canadian psychologist Ara Norenzayan, which examined 31 countries, wealthier, more industrialized nations typically experience a faster pace of life. This contributes to an improved standard of living; nonetheless, it also results in populations that live with a persistent sense of urgency and ④<u>show</u> a higher risk of developing conditions like heart disease. In other words, the productivity that drives economic growth may enhance material wealth, but it simultaneously causes people ⑤<u>feel</u> “time-poor,” as they often struggle to find enough time to relax or enjoy themselves.
options: ① ①
② ②
③ ③
④ ④
⑤ ⑤
questions.explanation: ⑤번의 feel은 문장의 동사인 causes(5형식 동사)의 목적격 보어 자리입니다. cause는 목적어 뒤에 목적격 보어로 to부정사를 취하는 동사이므로, 동사원형인 feel을 'to feel'로 고쳐야 어법상 적절합니다.

questions.question: 10. 윗글의 제목으로 가장 적절한 것은? [3.2점]
questions.passage: How did the human mind evolve? One possibility is that competition and conflicts between human tribes played a crucial role in the development of human intelligence. A human tribe that could out-think its enemies, even slightly, possessed a vital advantage. A tribe with even a small intellectual advantage, such as (a) superior strategic thinking, foresight, and planning, was more likely to survive. This supports the notion that warfare and conflicts between groups served as selection pressures, giving an benefit to tribes (b) capable of strategizing and anticipating their enemies' actions. That is, the ability of your tribe to imagine and predict where and when a hostile enemy tribe might strike, and plan accordingly, gives your tribe a significant military (c) strength. The human mind became a weapon in the struggle for survival, a weapon far more decisive than any before it. Unlike claws, fangs, or brute strength seen in other species, intelligence functioned as humans' primary tool for (d) intensifying enemy threats. This suggests that mental warfare-anticipating attacks, strategizing defenses, and forming alliances- was crucial for survival. And this mental advantage was applied, over and over, within each succeeding generation. Tribes that were better at out-thinking their opponents won battles and thrived, passing on their intelligence-related genes to their offspring. You and I are the descendants of the winners: Modern human intelligence is a product of countless past conflicts where only the most strategically (e) skilled tribes survived.
options: ① The Development of Human Intelligence Driven by Struggle
② The Turning Point That Disrupted the Principle of Survival of the Fittest
③ The Necessity of Developing Various Types of Weapons to Defeat Enemies
④ Artifacts Passed Down by Ancestors for Future Generations
⑤ Optimal Methods for Enhancing Intelligence
questions.explanation: 이 글은 인간의 지능이 부족 간의 경쟁과 갈등(struggle) 속에서 생존 우위를 점하기 위해 발달해왔다는 내용을 다루고 있으므로 ① '투쟁에 의해 추동된 인간 지능의 발달'이 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 투쟁에 의해 추동된 인간 지능의 발달
② 적자생존의 원칙을 무너뜨린 전환점
③ 적을 물리치기 위한 다양한 유형의 무기 개발의 필요성
④ 미래 세대를 위해 조상들이 물려준 유물
⑤ 지능 향상을 위한 최적의 방법들

questions.question: 11. 밑줄 친 (a)~(e) 중에서 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은? [3.5점]

A human tribe that could out-think its enemies, even slightly, possessed a vital advantage. A tribe with even a small intellectual advantage, such as (a) superior strategic thinking, foresight, and planning, was more likely to survive. That is, the ability of your tribe to imagine and predict where and when a hostile enemy tribe might strike, and plan accordingly, gives your tribe a significant military (c) strength. The human mind became a weapon in the struggle for survival, a weapon far more decisive than any before it. Tribes that were better at out-thinking their opponents won battles and thrived, passing on their intelligence-related genes to their offspring.
