questions.explanation: 지능은 적의 위협을 '강화(intensifying)'하는 도구가 아니라, 적의 위협을 극복하거나 대응하기 위한 생존 도구로 사용되었습니다. 문맥상 적의 위협을 무력화하거나 완화(neutralizing/countering)하는 맥락이 되어야 합니다.

questions.question: 12. [3.6점] 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것을 고르시오.
questions.passage: Growing crops forced people to stay in one place. Hunter-gatherers typically moved around frequently, and they had to be able to carry all their possessions with them every time they moved. In particular, mothers had to carry their young children. As a result, hunter-gatherer mothers could have only one baby every four years or so, ① spacing their births to ensure they only needed to carry one young child at any given time. Farmers, in contrast, were able to remain in one location ② permanently and didn't need to be concerned with transporting young children long distances. Societies that settled down in one place could ③ lower the time between births from around four years to about two. So women in farming communities could have more children than those in hunter-gatherer groups, leading to a swift increase in population within agricultural communities. Larger families meant more help in the fields, making population growth ④ undesirable for agricultural societies. Interestingly, early farmers were often ⑤ less healthy than hunter-gatherers. Their diets became too grain-heavy, resulting in nutritional deficiencies, dental problems, and a higher spread of diseases in dense populations.
questions.explanation: 농경 사회에서는 대가족이 들판에서 더 많은 일손을 의미했으므로, 인구 증가는 '바람직하지 않은(undesirable)' 것이 아니라 '바람직한(desirable)' 것이었습니다.

questions.question: 13. [3.5점] 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것을 고르시오.
questions.passage: Restricting the number of items customers can buy ① promotes sales. Brian Wansink, Professor of Marketing at Cornell University, investigated ② the effectiveness of this tactic in 1998. He persuaded three supermarkets in Sioux City, Iowa, to offer Campbell's soup at a small discount: 79 cents rather than 89 cents. The discounted soup was sold in one of three conditions: a control, where there was no limit on the volume of purchases, or two tests, where customers were limited to either four or twelve cans. In the ③ <u>unrestricted</u> condition shoppers bought 3.3 cans on average, whereas in the scarce condition, there was a limit, they bought 5.3 on average. This suggests scarcity ④ <u>discourages</u> sales. The findings are particularly strong because the test took place in a supermarket with genuine shoppers. It didn't rely on claimed data, nor was it held in a laboratory where consumers might behave ⑤ <u>differently</u>.
questions.explanation: 희소성(제한 조건)이 있을 때 사람들이 더 많이 구매했다는 결과가 나왔으므로, 이는 희소성이 판매를 '저해한다(discourages)'가 아니라 '장려한다(encourages/promotes)'는 것을 의미합니다.

questions.question: 14. [3.5점] 다음 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것을 고르시오.
questions.passage: Spending time as children allows animals to learn about their environment. Young animals that spend more time with parents or in social groups often obtain skills and knowledge that are essential for survival in unpredictable environments. Without childhood, animals must rely more fully on hardware, and therefore be less flexible. For instance, some migratory birds are born knowing how to migrate, but they often follow inefficient routes because they cannot easily adapt to changes in the environment. By comparison, birds with the longest childhoods, and those that migrate with their parents, tend to have the most efficient migration routes. Similarly, young primates observe and imitate food-gathering skills or social cues from their group, giving them the tools to adapt to new situations. These learned behaviors are not instinctive but are passed down from generation to generation, forming a kind of animal culture. In this way, young individuals ___________________________________________ gain not only knowledge but also adaptability, especially in the face of rapid environmental change.
options: ① born with advanced natural abilities
② raised with their caregivers' care and involvement
③ that possess advantageous physical characteristics
④ that embrace cultural diversity
⑤ with strong genetic traits
questions.explanation: 이 글은 동물들이 부모나 사회 집단과 함께 어린 시절을 보내며 학습하는 것이 환경 적응력과 생존에 필수적임을 설명하고 있습니다. 빈칸은 이러한 학습을 통해 지식과 적응력을 얻는 주체를 설명해야 하므로 '양육자의 돌봄과 관여 속에서 자란' 개체들이 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 진보된 천부적인 능력을 가지고 태어난
② 양육자의 돌봄과 관여 속에서 자란
③ 유리한 신체적 특징을 소유한
④ 문화적 다양성을 포용하는
⑤ 강한 유전적 특질을 가진

questions.question: 15. [3.5점] 다음 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것을 고르시오.
questions.passage: Many human and nonhuman animals save commodities or money for future consumption. This behavior seems to reveal a preference of a delayed reward over an immediate one. However, in some cases the agents often choose a smaller, immediate reward over a larger, delayed one, even when they know the long-term option is better. For example, early in the year an employee might set aside money to buy Christmas presents but then spend it on a summer vacation instead. People act differently over time not because they lack knowledge, but because their sense of value changes. When a decision involves the distant future, people may plan rationally -for example, deciding to save money or eat healthy. But as the moment of choice approaches, the immediate option becomes more tempting, leading to a change in behavior. This illustrates ___________________________________________ as the timing of a decision comes closer. These cases may indicate a <u>weakness of will, often resulting in regret and missed goals.</u>
options: ① how people's intentions can shift
② how people's memory improves with time
③ how time pressure leads to better choices
④ how financial planning ensures long-term success
⑤ why immediate rewards are always more beneficial
questions.explanation: 사람들이 미래를 위해 계획을 세우지만 선택의 순간이 다가올수록 즉각적인 보상에 유혹되어 행동이 변하는 현상을 설명하고 있습니다. 따라서 빈칸에는 '사람들의 의도가 어떻게 변할 수 있는지'를 나타내는 표현이 들어가야 합니다.
options_translation: ① 사람들의 의도가 어떻게 변할 수 있는지
② 시간이 지남에 따라 사람들의 기억력이 어떻게 향상되는지
③ 시간적 압박이 어떻게 더 나은 선택으로 이어지는지
④ 재무 계획이 어떻게 장기적인 성공을 보장하는지
⑤ 왜 즉각적인 보상이 항상 더 유익한지

questions.question: 16. [3.5점] 다음 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것을 고르시오.
questions.passage: Why do you care how a customer reacts to a purchase? Good question. By understanding post-purchase behavior, you can understand the influence and the likelihood of whether a buyer will repurchase the product (and whether she will keep it or return it). You'll also determine whether the buyer will encourage others to purchase the product from you. Contented customers can be leading promoters who recommend your products to others without being paid, so ___________________________________________ . People tend to believe the opinions of people they know. People trust friends over advertisements any day. They know that advertisements are paid to tell the "good side" and that they're used to persuade them to purchase products and services. By continually monitoring your customer's satisfaction after the sale, you have the ability to avoid negative word-of-mouth advertising.
options: ① handling your customers' dissatisfaction doesn't matter
② it seems unimportant to emphasize how satisfied the customer will be
③ it's <u>meaningless</u> that you help customers deal with post-purchase discomfort
④ customer gratification should be a highest priority for your to-do list
⑤ it's very crucial to offer customers diversified products
questions.explanation: 만족한 고객이 자발적인 홍보대사가 되어 긍정적인 구전 효과를 일으킨다는 내용이므로, 기업 입장에서 고객 만족이 최우선 순위가 되어야 한다는 내용이 빈칸에 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 고객의 불만을 처리하는 것은 중요하지 않다
② 고객이 얼마나 만족할지를 강조하는 것은 중요하지 않아 보인다
③ 고객이 구매 후의 불편함을 처리하도록 돕는 것은 <u>의미 없다</u>
④ 고객 만족은 당신의 해야 할 일 목록에서 최우선 순위여야 한다
⑤ 고객들에게 다양한 제품을 제공하는 것은 매우 중요하다

questions.question: 17. [3.5점] 주어진 글 다음에 이어질 글의 순서로 가장 적절한 것을 고르시오.
questions.passage: The hunter-gatherer lifestyle, which can be described as “natural” to human beings, appears to have had much to recommend it.
ordered_passages: (A) In contrast, early farming required intense labor and brought new challenges, including malnutrition and the spread of infectious diseases due to increased population density. If this is true, it is not clear why so many humans settled in permanent villages and developed agriculture, growing crops and domesticating animals.

(B) Our ancestors in early hunter-gatherer societies often had access to a wide variety of natural foods, such as fruits, nuts, and wild animals, which provided them with a balanced diet. As a result, they were able to maintain relatively healthy lives, experiencing fewer diseases.

(C) Whatever its immediate effect on the lives of humans, agriculture made it possible to support larger populations and led to the rise of permanent settlements. This shift eventually gave rise to complex societies, cities, and what we now consider civilization.
questions.explanation: 주어진 글은 수렵 채집 생활의 장점을 언급하며 시작합니다. (B)에서 그 장점에 대한 구체적인 설명(균형 잡힌 식단, 건강한 삶)이 이어지고, (A)에서 'In contrast'를 통해 농경 생활의 단점(고된 노동, 질병)을 대조하며 농경의 시작에 대한 의문을 제기합니다. 마지막으로 (C)에서 농경이 인구 부양과 문명 발달로 이어졌음을 설명하며 마무리하는 것이 자연스럽습니다.

questions.question: 18. [3.5점] 주어진 글 다음에 이어질 글의 순서로 가장 적절한 것을 고르시오.
questions.passage: According to educational psychologist Susan Engel, curiosity begins to decrease as young as four years old.
ordered_passages: (A) By the time we are adults, we have fewer questions and more default settings. As Henry James put it, “Disinterested curiosity is past, the mental grooves and channels set.” The decline in curiosity can be traced in the development of the brain through childhood. Though smaller than the adult brain, the infant brain contains millions more neural connections.

(B) As children absorb more evidence from the world around them, certain possibilities become much more likely and more useful and harden into knowledge or beliefs. The neural pathways that enable those beliefs become faster and more automatic, while the ones that the child doesn’t use regularly are pruned away.

(C) The wiring, however, is a mess; the lines of <u>communication between infant neurons are far less efficient than between those in the adult</u> brain. The baby’s perception of the world is consequently both intensely rich and wildly disordered.
questions.explanation: 주어진 글은 유아기 호기심의 감소를 언급합니다. (A)에서 성인이 되며 질문이 줄어드는 현상과 유아기 뇌의 신경 연결이 더 많다는 특징을 설명합니다. (C)에서 'The wiring, however, is a mess'를 통해 앞서 언급된 유아기 뇌 연결의 특징(비효율성, 무질서)을 이어받고, (B)에서 아이들이 경험을 통해 특정 경로를 강화하고 쓰지 않는 경로를 제거(pruning)하며 지식이 굳어지는 과정을 설명하며 마무리됩니다.

questions.question: 19. [3.4점] 글의 흐름으로 보아, 주어진 문장이 들어가기에 가장 적절한 곳을 고르시오.
questions.passage: Do you share your opinion in class discussions, or do you just stay silent and keep it to yourself? Like many of you, I often found myself in the second group. A little black hole inside of me swallowed my voice when I considered speaking up. ( ① ) The consequences of being ridiculed or being wrong were always on my mind. ( ② ) Then, after a particularly heated conversation in class, I asked myself, “What am I afraid of?” ( ③ ) While reflecting on myself, I noticed others taking risks and realized I needed to do the same to truly participate. ( ④ ) By expressing myself more clearly, I grew intellectually and socially, which allows me to get closer to friends who liked how open I was with them. ( ⑤ ) Now I have more people with whom I can talk, share my ideas, and learn new things. Remember, taking the risk of expressing yourself can be extremely rewarding in unexpected ways.
questions.insertion_sentence: This led me to leave my comfort zone and start speaking up.
questions.explanation: 주어진 문장 'This led me to leave my comfort zone and start speaking up.'은 화자가 자신의 두려움을 돌아보고 다른 이들의 도전을 보며 깨달음을 얻은 결과로 이어지는 행동의 변화를 나타냅니다. ③번 뒤의 문장에서 화자가 다른 사람들을 보며 나도 참여해야겠다고 깨달은(realized I needed to do the same) 내용이 나오므로, 그 깨달음이 화자를 안주 지대에서 벗어나 말하게 했다는 주어진 문장은 ④번에 들어가는 것이 가장 적절합니다. 그 결과로 ④번 뒤의 내용인 지적, 사회적 성장과 친구들과 가까워진 사례가 이어지게 됩니다.

questions.question: 20. [3.5점] 다음 문장이 들어가기에 가장 적절한 곳은?
questions.passage: Up until about 6,000 years ago, most people were farmers. Many lived in different places throughout the year, hunting for food or moving their livestock to areas with enough food. ( ① ) There was no need to tell the time because life depended on natural cycles, such as the changing seasons or sunrise and sunset. ( ② ) For example, priests wanted to know when to carry out religious ceremonies. ( ③ ) This was when people first invented clocks - devices that show, measure, and keep track of passing time. ( ④ ) Clocks have been important ever since. ( ⑤ ) Today, clocks are used for important things such as setting busy airport timetables - if the time is incorrect, aeroplanes might crash into each other when taking off or landing!
questions.insertion_sentence: Gradually more people started to live in larger settlements, and some needed to tell the time.
questions.explanation: 주어진 문장은 사람들이 더 큰 정착지에 살기 시작하면서 시간을 알 필요가 생겼다는 내용을 담고 있다. ②번 앞까지는 자연의 주기에 의존하여 시간을 알 필요가 없었다는 내용이 나오고, ②번 뒤에는 시간을 알 필요가 생긴 구체적인 예시(사제들의 종교 의식 등)가 나오므로 ②번 위치가 가장 적절하다.

questions.question: 21. [3.5점] 다음 문장이 들어가기에 가장 적절한 곳은?
questions.passage: Managers are always looking for ways to increase productivity, which is the ratio of costs to output in production. Adam Smith, writing when the manufacturing industry was new, described a way that production could be made more efficient, known as the "division of labor." Making most manufactured goods involves several different processes using different skills. ( ① ) Smith's example was the manufacture of pins: the wire is straightened, sharpened, a head is put on, and then it is polished. ( ② ) One worker could do all these tasks, and make 20 pins in a day. ( ③ ) Because each worker specializes in one job, he or she can work much faster without changing from one task to another. ( ④ ) Now 10 workers can produce thousands of pins in a day - a huge increase in productivity from the 200 they would have produced before. ( ⑤ )
questions.insertion_sentence: But this work can be divided into its separate processes, with a number of workers each performing one task.
questions.explanation: 주어진 문장은 작업이 개별 공정으로 나뉘어 여러 노동자가 각각 하나의 작업을 수행할 수 있다는 내용이다. ②번 뒤 문장은 한 노동자가 모든 작업을 수행하여 하루에 20개의 핀을 만드는 비효율성을 설명하고 있으며, ③번 뒤 문장부터는 각 노동자가 한 가지 업무에 전문화되어 작업 속도가 빨라진다는 내용(분업의 결과)이 나오므로 그 전환점인 ③번이 적절하다.

questions.question: 22. [3.9점] 다음 글의 내용을 한 문장으로 요약하고자 한다. 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것을 고르시오.
questions.passage: As businesses shift some core business activities to digital, such as sales, marketing, or archiving, it is assumed that these changes reduce environmental harm by minimizing the use of consumable materials like paper and plastic. However, digital business activities can still threaten the environment. In some cases, the harm of digital businesses can be even more hazardous. A few decades ago, offices used to have much more paper waste since all documents were paper based. When workplaces shifted from paper to digital documents, invoices, and emails, it was a promising step to save trees. However, the hidden environmental costs of digitalization are frequently overlooked. For example, a single email may emit only a few grams of CO2, but this number rises dramatically with large attachments. Similarly, while online streaming appears to decrease waste associated with CDs or DVDs, it consumes massive amounts of electricity, particularly for high-resolution content.
questions.summary_sentence: While digital technologies may appear to be a greener option due to (A)__________ use of physical resources, their hidden environmental costs - from data storage to streaming - are not (B)_________ .
options: ① excessive ... enormous
② reduced ... insignificant
③ limited ... unreasonable
④ efficient ... considerable
⑤ minimal ... substantial
questions.explanation: 디지털 기술이 종이나 플라스틱 같은 물리적 자원의 사용을 줄였기 때문에 더 친환경적으로 보일 수 있지만(reduced), 데이터 저장이나 스트리밍으로 인한 숨겨진 환경적 비용(탄소 배출, 전력 소비 등)은 결코 사소하지 않다(not insignificant = 상당하다)는 내용이 되어야 한다.
options_translation: ① 과도한 ... 거대한
② 감소된 ... 사소한
③ 제한된 ... 불합리한
④ 효율적인 ... 상당한
⑤ 최소의 ... 실질적인

questions.question: 23. [3.7점] 다음 글의 내용을 한 문장으로 요약하고자 한다. 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: We tend to believe that we possess a host of socially desirable characteristics, and that we are free of most of those that are socially undesirable. For example, a large majority of the general public thinks that they are more intelligent, more fair-minded, less prejudiced, and more skilled behind the wheel of an automobile than the average person. This phenomenon is so reliable and ubiquitous that it has come to be known as the "Lake Wobegon effect," after Garrison Keillor's fictional community where "the women are strong, the men are good-looking, and all the children are above average." A survey of one million high school seniors found that 70% thought they were above average in leadership ability, and only 2% thought they were below average. In terms of interpersonal skills, all students thought they were above average, 60% thought they were in the top 10%, and 25% thought they were in the top 1%!
questions.summary_sentence: As shown in a survey of one million students, we tend to view ourselves as having more (A)________ traits than others, which reflects the common cognitive bias of (B)___________
options: ① problematic ... overestimating their knowledge
② unpleasant ... inflating their own abilities
③ desirable ... suspicion towards other
④ avoidant ... overconfidence in themselves
⑤ positive ... illusory superiority
questions.explanation: 사람들은 자신이 평균보다 더 나은 특성을 가지고 있다고 믿는 경향이 있으며, 이를 'Lake Wobegon effect'라고 부른다. 따라서 (A)에는 'positive(긍정적인)' 또는 'desirable(바람직한)'이 적절하고, (B)에는 자신을 타인보다 우월하다고 믿는 인지 편향인 'illusory superiority(허구적 우월감)'가 가장 적절하다.
options_translation: ① 문제가 있는 ... 그들의 지식을 과대평가하는 것
② 불쾌한 ... 그들 자신의 능력을 부풀리는 것
③ 바람직한 ... 타인에 대한 의심
④ 회피적인 ... 자신에 대한 과잉 확신
⑤ 긍정적인 ... 허구적 우월감

questions.question: [서답형 1] 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~⑤에서 어법에 맞지 않는 것을 3개 골라 바르게 고쳐 쓰시오.(빈칸을 모두 채워야 정답처리함. 즉 틀린 번호와 옳게 고친 단어 모두 써야 정답임. 고친 단어가 두 개의 단어를 초과 시 0점 처리함.) [6.0점]
questions.passage: The soil of a farm field is forced to be the perfect environment for monoculture growth. This is achieved by adding nutrients in the form of fertilizer and water by way of irrigation. Fertilizers provide essential nutrients like nitrogen and phosphorus, dramatically increasing crop yields and <u>① to allow</u> plants to grow in otherwise unproductive soils. At the same time, advanced irrigation systems have enabled farmers to supply water precisely and efficiently, reducing dependence on rainfall. <u>② That</u> these technologies have done is to significantly improve global food production and contribute to population growth. Nevertheless, they have also produced several unintended consequences. Because farm fields are loaded with nutrients and water relative to the natural land that surrounds them, they <u>③ desire</u> as luxury real estate by every random weed in the area. Farm fields filled with nutrients and water become <u>④ highly</u> attractive environments not just for crops but also for invasive weeds. These weeds compete with crops for resources and can lead to <u>⑤ increased</u> use of plant-killing chemicals, further impacting the environment.
subjective_conditions: 빈칸을 모두 채워야 정답 처리 (번호와 고친 단어 모두 작성)
고친 단어가 두 개의 단어를 초과 시 0점 처리
questions.explanation:
① increasing과 병렬 구조를 이루어야 하므로 분사 구문 형태인 allowing이 적절하다.
② 선행사를 포함하고 뒤에 목적어가 빠진 불완전한 문장을 이끌어야 하므로 What이 적절하다.
③ 농경지가 잡초들에 의해 '원해지는' 수동의 의미이므로 are desired가 적절하다.
④ 형용사 attractive를 수식하는 부사 highly는 적절하다.
⑤ 명사 use를 수식하는 분사 increased는 '증가된'이라는 의미로 적절하다.

questions.question: [서답형 4] <보기>에 제시된 설명에 해당하는 단어를 지문에서 찾아 변형없이 쓰시오. [4.0점]
questions.passage:
What kind of snack is nutritious, full of energy, and simple to make? This is the genius of peanut butter and banana sandwiches. Everyone was surprised that this sandwich would later become a comfort food for Americans. This sandwich can be a healthy choice for breakfast or lunch because its combination of protein and fiber helps you feel full, while the carbohydrates provide sustained energy. The best thing about this sandwich is that the ingredients are readily available and affordable.
Some people, however, like to take things to another level. Imagine a regular peanut butter and banana sandwich, and then add fried bacon to it. It has been said that the famous singer Elvis Presley loved this sandwich, which is why it's called, "The Elvis." Even though you may not want to eat the Elvis every day, there are many fans of this unconventional combination.
subjective_conditions: (A) very different from the things that are used or accepted by most people
(B) having substances that a person or animal needs to be healthy and grow properly; promoting good health and growth
(C) quickly and easily; in a way that shows you are willing to do something, without hesitation or complaint
(D) continuing for an extended period or without interruption
questions.explanation:
(A) 대다수의 사람들에 의해 사용되거나 받아들여지는 것들과 매우 다른: unconventional (독특한, 관습에 얽매이지 않은)
(B) 사람이나 동물이 건강하고 제대로 자라기 위해 필요한 영양소를 가진; 건강과 성장을 촉진하는: nutritious (영양가 있는)
(C) 빠르고 쉽게; 주저함이나 불평 없이 기꺼이 하려는 태도로: readily (손쉽게, 선뜻)
(D) 장기간 또는 중단 없이 지속되는: sustained (지속된, 일관된)

questions.question: 1. 다음 글에서 필자가 주장하는 바로 가장 적절한 것은? [3.2점]
questions.passage:
Fans who are inclined to spend a lot of time thinking about what athletes owe them as fans should also think about the corresponding obligations that fans might have as fans. One who thinks only about what they are entitled to receive from their friends without ever giving a moment's thought to what they owe their friends is, to put it mildly, not a very good friend. Similarly, fans who only think about what athletes owe them without ever thinking about what they owe to athletes have failed to take the fan/athlete relationship all that seriously. As in nearly every other area of human life, whatever special rights fans may possess are limited by a corresponding set of obligations, and fans who never think about how they can be better fans even as they confidently opine about what athletes owe them are hardly fulfilling their
end of the bargain.
options:
① Fans should consider athletes their most precious
friends.

② Fans should try to achieve self-fulfillment through
fan activities.

③ Fans should focus on the results rather than the
team's game process.

④ Athletes communicate with fans but do not have to
pay attention to their thoughts.

⑤ Fans should think about what they need to do, not
just what they want to receive from athletes.
questions.explanation: 글의 중반부와 마지막 부분에서 팬들이 선수들에게 무엇을 받을 권리만 생각할 것이 아니라, 좋은 팬으로서 선수들에게 어떤 의무를 가져야 하는지(상응하는 의무)를 생각해야 한다고 강조하고 있으므로 ⑤번이 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 팬들은 운동선수를 가장 소중한 친구로 여겨야 한다.
② 팬들은 팬 활동을 통해 자기 실현을 달성하려고 노력해야 한다.
③ 팬들은 팀의 경기 과정보다는 결과에 집중해야 한다.
④ 운동선수들은 팬들과 소통하지만 그들의 생각에 주의를 기울일 필요는 없다.
⑤ 팬들은 운동선수들로부터 받고 싶은 것뿐만 아니라 자신들이 해야 할 일에 대해서도 생각해야 한다.

questions.question:
2. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 <u>the flavor of food is taking a back
seat</u>이 의미하는 바로 가장 적절한 것은? [3.1점]
questions.passage: The prominence of the social dimension in food writing might suggest that <u>the flavor of food is taking a back seat</u>. I suspect that most people view flavor as of secondary importance in social settings where food is served. Although our social gatherings coalesce around food, the meaning of these gatherings does not seem to depend on flavor. Flavor assists with the narrow purpose of filling the belly, and once that is accomplished it provides the backdrop for whatever social dynamics characterize the gathering. These can be understood independently of the flavor of the food on offer, the appreciation of which is understood to be personal and subjective. According to this conventional wisdom, the ceremonies and rituals around food, the social events that supply food with its meaning, do not depend on the quality of sensations provided by the food. To focus excessively on flavor is to miss the larger significance of these social relations.
options: ① Nutrition is regarded as more important than taste.
② Emotional connections are weakened by tasteless food.

③ Modern cooking trends focus on bold and experimental
flavors.

④ People often choose food based on individual
preferences.

⑤ Social interaction is being emphasized more than the
flavor of food.
questions.explanation: 필자는 음식과 관련된 사회적 모임에서 음식의 맛은 부차적인 것이며, 사회적 관계나 상호작용이 더 중요하다고 주장하고 있습니다. 'take a back seat(뒷전이 되다)'는 의미는 맛보다 사회적 측면이 더 중시된다는 뜻이므로 ⑤번이 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 영양은 맛보다 더 중요하게 여겨진다.
② 정서적 연결은 맛없는 음식에 의해 약화된다.
③ 현대 요리 트렌드는 대담하고 실험적인 맛에 집중한다.
④ 사람들은 종종 개인적인 선호에 따라 음식을 선택한다.
⑤ 음식의 맛보다 사회적 상호작용이 더 강조되고 있다.

questions.question: 3. 밑줄 친 <u>children's film is some other realm</u>이 다음 글에서 의미하는 바로 가장 적절한 것은? [3.4점]
questions.passage: We must explore the relationship between children's film production and consumption habits. The term "children's film" implies ownership by children - their cinema - but films supposedly made for children have always been consumed by audiences of all ages, particularly in commercial cinemas. The considerable crossover in audience composition for children's films can be shown by the fact that, in 2007, eleven Danish children's and youth films attracted 59 per cent of theatrical admissions, and in 2014, German children's films comprised seven out of the top twenty films at the national box office. This phenomenon corresponds with a broader, international embrace of what is seemingly children's culture among audiences of diverse ages. The old prejudice that <u>children's film is some other realm</u>, separate from (and forever subordinate to) a more legitimate cinema for adults is not supported by the realities of consumption: children's film is at the heart of contemporary popular culture.
options: ① Children's movies are only for children.
② Adults should not be involved in making children's films.
③ Children's films should only be shown in exclusive movie theaters.
④ Children's movies are the areas where international acceptance is delayed.
⑤ The consumption of movies and that of other goods must be strictly distinguished.
questions.explanation: 밑줄 친 부분은 아동용 영화가 성인용 영화와는 분리된(별개의) 영역이라는 오래된 편견을 의미한다. 필자는 실제 소비 현실을 통해 아동용 영화가 모든 연령층에 의해 소비되며 현대 대중문화의 중심에 있다고 주장하므로, 밑줄 친 부분이 의미하는 바는 '아동 영화는 오직 아동만을 위한 것이다'라는 ①번이 가장 적절하다.
options_translation: ① 아동 영화는 오직 아동만을 위한 것이다.
② 성인들은 아동 영화를 제작하는 데 관여해서는 안 된다.
③ 아동 영화는 오직 전용 영화관에서만 상영되어야 한다.
④ 아동 영화는 국제적인 수용이 지연되는 영역이다.
⑤ 영화의 소비와 다른 재화의 소비는 엄격히 구별되어야 한다.

questions.question: 4. 다음 글의 요지로 가장 적절한 것은? [3.1점]
questions.passage: Too many times people, especially in today's generation, expect things to just happen overnight. When we have these false expectations, it tends to discourage us from continuing to move forward. Because this is a high tech society, everything we want has to be within the parameters of our comfort and convenience. If it doesn't happen fast enough, we're tempted to lose interest. So many people don't want to take the time it requires to be successful. Success is not a matter of mere desire; you should develop patience in order to achieve it. Have you fallen prey to impatience? Great things take time to build.
options: ① A simplified wish is the shortcut to success.
② It takes great deal of time and effort to accomplish great things.
③ Let's have a good expectation so as not to get disappointed.
④ You should be able to prepare important things even in a short time.
⑤ Technology is essential to expand situations where your determination is not being tested.
questions.explanation: 글의 후반부에서 '성공은 단순한 욕망의 문제가 아니며, 이를 달성하기 위해 인내심을 길러야 한다'고 언급하며, '위대한 일은 만드는 데 시간이 걸린다'고 결론짓고 있다. 따라서 요지로는 ②번 '위대한 일을 성취하는 데는 많은 시간과 노력이 필요하다'가 가장 적절하다.
options_translation: ① 단순화된 소망이 성공으로 가는 지름길이다.
② 위대한 일을 성취하는 데는 많은 시간과 노력이 필요하다.
③ 실망하지 않도록 좋은 기대를 갖자.
④ 짧은 시간 안에도 중요한 것들을 준비할 수 있어야 한다.
⑤ 당신의 결단력이 시험받지 않는 상황을 확장하는 데 기술이 필수적이다.

questions.question:
5. 다음 글의 주제로 가장 적절한 것을 고르시오.

 [3.3점]
questions.passage: Intuition can be great, but it ought to be hard-earned. Experts, for example, are able to think on their feet because they've invested thousands of hours in learning and practice; their intuition has become data-driven. Only then are they able to act quickly in accordance with their internalized expertise and evidence-based experience. Yet most people are not experts, though they often think they are. Most of us, especially when we interact with others on social media, act with expert-like speed and conviction, offering a wide range of opinions on global crises, without the substance of knowledge that supports it. And thanks to AI, which ensures that our messages are delivered to an audience more inclined to believing it, our delusions of expertise can be reinforced by our personal filter bubble. We have an interesting tendency to find people more open-minded, rational, and sensible when they think just like us.
options: ① the need to share diverse perspectives
② AI's ability to enhance intuitive learning
③ the usefulness of intuition in times of crisis
④ the emotional impact of social media on teenagers
⑤ the spread of unfounded confidence and false expertise
questions.explanation: 지문은 진정한 직관은 오랜 학습과 연습을 통해 얻어지는 것임에도 불구하고, 많은 사람들이 근거 없는 지식으로 전문가처럼 행동하며 소셜 미디어와 AI 알고리즘(필터 버블)에 의해 이러한 가짜 전문성과 근거 없는 확신이 강화되고 있음을 지적하고 있다. 따라서 주제는 ⑤번 '근거 없는 자신감과 가짜 전문성의 확산'이 가장 적절하다.
options_translation: ① 다양한 관점을 공유할 필요성
② 직관적 학습을 향상시키는 AI의 능력
③ 위기 시 직관의 유용성
④ 소셜 미디어가 십대들에게 미치는 정서적 영향
⑤ 근거 없는 자신감과 가짜 전문성의 확산

questions.question: 6. [3.4점] 다음 글의 주제로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: It's untrue that teens can focus on two things at once - what they're doing is shifting their attention from one task to another. In this digital age, teens wire their brains to make these shifts very quickly, but they are still, like everyone else, paying attention to one thing at a time, sequentially. Common sense tells us multitasking should increase brain activity, but Carnegie Mellon University scientists using the latest brain imaging technology find it doesn't. As a matter of fact, they discovered that multitasking actually decreases brain activity. Neither task is done as well as if each were performed individually. Fractions of a second are lost every time we make a switch, and a person's interrupted task can take 50 percent longer to finish, with 50 percent more errors. Turns out the latest brain research supports the old advice "one thing at a time." It's not that kids can't do some tasks simultaneously. But if two tasks are performed at once, one of them has to be familiar. Our brains perform a familiar task on "automatic pilot" while really paying attention to the other one. That's why insurance companies consider talking on a cell phone and driving to be as dangerous as driving while drunk - it's the driving that goes on "automatic pilot" while the conversation really holds our attention. Our kids may be living in the Information Age but our brains have not been redesigned yet.
options: ① benefits of growing up in a tech-rich environment
② value of managing attention during everyday tasks
③ role of automatic behavior in enhancing task efficiency
④ misconception about the cognitive benefits of multitasking
⑤ challenge of adapting brain function to digital-age demands
questions.explanation: 이 글은 십 대들이 한 번에 두 가지 일에 집중할 수 있다는 통념과 달리 실제로는 주의력을 전환하는 것이며, 멀티태스킹이 뇌 활동을 줄이고 작업 효율성을 떨어뜨린다는 연구 결과를 설명하고 있습니다. 따라서 '멀티태스킹의 인지적 이점에 대한 오해'가 주제로 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 기술이 풍부한 환경에서 자라는 것의 이점
② 일상 업무 중 주의력 관리의 가치
③ 작업 효율성을 높이는 자동화된 행동의 역할
④ 멀티태스킹의 인지적 이점에 대한 오해
⑤ 디지털 시대 요구에 뇌 기능을 적응시키는 과제

questions.question: 7. 다음 글의 제목으로 가장 적절한 것은? [3.3점]
questions.passage: The explosion of popular music in the second half of the twentieth century as well as the global circulation and dissemination of music by the creative industries propelled a new understanding of accessibility in relation to music. Suddenly, in the 1950s, anyone could pick up spoons, a couple of pans, a secondhand guitar and start a band. This led to specific genres such as skiffle, but also, more generally, reflected a much more relaxed and inclusive attitude to music making. While ordinary people had always sung and made music, the popular music movement was driven by a spirit of rebellion and freedom. This approach led to the punk movement, whose musicians even made it a condition for their music to be nonvirtuosic and accessible to all in the 1970s. Groups who had been entirely excluded from music revelled in opportunities to create. This led to a sense of novelty and empowerment in and beyond the music sphere.
options: ① Shift in Music for the Gifted Few
② Simpler Sounds Make Listening Easier
③ The Pros and Cons of the Popularization of Music
④ When Music Took Off Its Tuxedo and Joined the Crowd
⑤ How Musical Instruments Have Developed in the Late Twentieth Century?
questions.explanation: 20세기 후반 대중음악의 폭발과 함께 음악 제작이 전문적인 영역에서 누구나 참여할 수 있는 포괄적이고 접근하기 쉬운 영역으로 변화했음을 설명하고 있습니다. '음악이 턱시도를 벗고 군중과 합류했을 때'는 격식을 차린 소수만의 예술에서 대중의 예술로 변화한 과정을 비유적으로 잘 나타냅니다.
options_translation: ① 재능 있는 소수를 위한 음악의 변화
② 더 단순한 소리가 청취를 더 쉽게 만든다
③ 음악 대중화의 장단점
④ 음악이 턱시도를 벗고 군중과 합류했을 때
⑤ 20세기 후반 악기들이 어떻게 발전해 왔는가?

questions.question: 8. 다음 글의 내용과 일치하지 않는 것은? [3.4점]
questions.passage: It is a common assumption that most vagrant birds are ultimately doomed, aside from the rare cases where individuals are able to reorientate and return to their normal ranges. In turn, it is also commonly assumed that vagrancy itself is a relatively unimportant biological phenomenon. This is undoubtedly true for the majority of cases, as the most likely outcome of any given vagrancy event is that the individual will fail to find enough resources, and/or be exposed to inhospitable environmental conditions, and perish. However, there are many lines of evidence to suggest that vagrancy can, on rare occasions, dramatically alter the fate of populations, species or even whole ecosystems. Despite being infrequent, these events can be extremely important when viewed at the timescales over which ecological and evolutionary processes unfold. The most profound consequences of vagrancy relate to the establishment of new breeding sites and migration routes. Each of these can occur through different mechanisms, and at different frequencies, and they each have their own unique importance.
options: ① It is generally believed that vagrancy holds little importance in biological phenomenon.
② Most vagrancy events result in birds successfully adapting to new environments.
③ Some vagrancy events can dramatically influence entire populations or ecosystems.
④ Vagrancy can lead to the formation of new breeding sites and migration routes.
⑤ New breeding sites and migration routes may emerge through different processes and at different rates.
questions.explanation: 지문에서 대부분의 미조(vagrant birds)는 자원을 찾지 못하거나 열악한 환경에 노출되어 죽는다고(perish) 언급되어 있으므로, 대부분의 미조 사건이 새로운 환경에 성공적으로 적응한다는 ②번은 본문 내용과 일치하지 않습니다.
options_translation: ① 길을 잃은 상태(vagrancy)는 생물학적 현상에서 중요성이 거의 없다고 일반적으로 믿어진다.
② 대부분의 미조 사건은 새들이 새로운 환경에 성공적으로 적응하는 결과를 낳는다.
③ 일부 미조 사건은 전체 개체군이나 생태계에 극적으로 영향을 미칠 수 있다.
④ 길을 잃는 것은 새로운 번식지와 이동 경로의 형성으로 이어질 수 있다.
⑤ 새로운 번식지와 이동 경로는 서로 다른 과정과 속도를 통해 나타날 수 있다.

questions.question: 9. [3.7점] 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 어법상 틀린 것을 고르시오.
questions.passage: Commitment is <u>① the glue holding together human forms</u> of social life. Commitments <u>make individuals' behavior predictable</u> in the face of fluctuations in their desires and interests, <u>② facilitated the planning and coordination of joint actions</u> involving multiple agents. Moreover, commitments make people willing to perform actions <u>③ that they would not otherwise perform</u>. For example, a taxi driver picks up his clients and transports them to their desired destination because they are committed to paying him afterwards for the service, and a construction worker performs her job every day because her employer <u>④ has made a credible commitment to pay her</u> at the end of the month. Indeed, the taxi driver and the construction worker are willing to accept money as payment only because a network of other agents (notably the central bank) <u>⑤ is committed to taking various measures</u> to sustain the currency in question. Thus, social objects and institutions such as jobs, money, government, scientific collaborations and marriage depend for their origin and stability upon the credibility of commitments.
questions.explanation: ②번의 facilitated는 주어인 Commitments의 동작을 보충 설명하는 분사구문 자리로, 뒤에 목적어(the planning and coordination...)가 오고 있으므로 능동의 의미를 가진 현재분사 facilitating으로 고쳐야 합니다.

questions.question: 10. [3.7점] 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 어법상 틀린 것을 고르시오.
questions.passage: Empathy is frequently listed as one of the most desired skills in an employer or employee. What it actually means, however, <u>① is often left unspecified</u>. Some businesses stress cognitive empathy, emphasizing the need for leaders to understand the perspective of employees and customers <u>② when making decisions as well as negotiating deals</u>. Others stress affective empathy and empathic concern, <u>③ emphasizing the leaders' ability to gain trust</u> from employees and customers by treating them with real concern and compassion. When some consultants argue that successful companies foster empathy, <u>④ what that translate to is that companies should conduct good market research</u>. In other words, an "empathic" company understands the needs and wants of its customers and <u>⑤ seeks to fulfill those needs and wants</u>. When some people speak of design with empathy, they mean that companies should take into consideration the specific needs of different populations - the blind, the deaf, the elderly, non-English speakers, the color-blind, and so on - when designing products.
questions.explanation: ④번의 what절 내에서 주어는 대명사 that이며, 이는 단수 취급하므로 동사 translate를 3인칭 단수형인 translates로 고쳐야 합니다.

questions.question: 11. [3.6점] 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 어법상 틀린 것을 고르시오.
questions.passage: Dancers often push themselves to the limits of their physical capabilities. But that push is misguided if it is <u>① directed toward accomplishing something physically</u> impossible. For instance, a tall dancer with long feet may wish to perform repetitive vertical jumps to fast music, pointing his feet while in the air and <u>② lower</u> his heels to the floor between jumps. That may be impossible <u>③ no matter how strong</u> the dancer is. But a short-footed dancer may have no trouble! Another dancer may be struggling to complete a half-turn in the air. Understanding the connection between a rapid turn rate and the alignment of the body <u>④ close</u> to the rotation axis tells her how to accomplish her turn successfully. In both of these cases, understanding and working within the constraints imposed by nature and described by physical laws <u>⑤ allows</u> dancers to work efficiently, minimizing potential risk of injury.
questions.explanation: ②번의 lower는 문맥상 분사구문 pointing과 병렬 구조를 이루어야 합니다. 즉, '공중에서 발끝을 세우고(pointing) ... 뒤꿈치를 바닥으로 내리면서(lowering)'의 의미가 되어야 하므로 lowering으로 고쳐야 합니다.

questions.question: 12. [3.9점] 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 어법상 틀린 것을 고르시오.
questions.passage: In order to bring the ever-increasing costs of home care for elderly and needy persons under control, managers of home care providers have introduced management systems. These systems specify tasks of home care workers and the time and budget available to perform these tasks. Electronic reporting systems require home care workers to report on their activities and the time spent, <u>① thus making the distribution of time and money controllable as well as visible</u>, in the perception of managers. This, in the view of managers, has contributed to the resolution of the problem. The home care workers, on the other hand, <u>② may perceive their work not as a set of separate tasks to be performed as efficient as possible</u>, but as a service to be provided to a client with whom they may have developed a relationship. This <u>③ includes having conversations with clients and enquiring about the person's well-being</u>. Restricted time and the requirement to report <u>④ may be perceived as obstacles that make it impossible to deliver the service which is needed</u>. If the management systems are too rigid, <u>⑤ this may result in home care workers becoming overloaded and demotivated</u>.
questions.explanation: ②번에서 efficient는 동사 perform을 수식하는 부사 자리입니다. '가능한 한 효율적으로 수행되어야 할'이라는 의미이므로 형용사 efficient를 부사 efficiently로 고쳐야 합니다.

questions.question: 14. [3.7점] 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것을 고르시오.
questions.passage: The concept of ecosystem states should be familiar to anyone with a home vegetable garden. The garden is a small ecosystem that the grower attempts to keep in a specific state, namely the ①<u>maximization</u> of fruit and vegetable production. To achieve this, the grower is almost always intervening in the dynamics of the ecosystem: they ②<u>eliminate</u> unwanted plants that begin to grow and perhaps spray insecticides and fence off the patch to stop insects and other animals from consuming the vegetables. Since maximizing vegetable growth is an inherently unstable state for the ecosystem, the grower is effectively ③<u>keeping</u> an unstable ecosystem for high vegetable yield. If the grower stops intervening, even for a day, the ecosystem, that small patch of ground, will naturally begin to shift to a ④<u>less</u> stable state. Vegetables may still grow, but yield will almost certainly be ⑤<u>dim인ished</u> as other plants crowd out the vegetables and wildlife consume the produce.
questions.explanation: 인위적으로 유지되는 채소밭은 생태학적으로 불안정한 상태입니다. 따라서 관리자의 개입이 멈추면 생태계는 자연적인 균형을 향해 나아가므로 '더' 안정적인(more stable) 상태로 변하게 됩니다.

questions.question: 16. 다음 글의 빈칸 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은? [3.6점]
questions.passage: Since their start in the early 1950s U.S. television sitcoms have (A)______ many of the social conflicts in U.S. society: civil rights, women's rights in the home and in the workplace, children's rights, immigration and multiculturalism, as well as evolving conceptions of the family. Each of these issues has been addressed through humour in a way that has helped to make more progressive values more (B)________ than previously. Often a character, usually someone marked as a bigot, resisted one or more of these developments and was then made to appear ridiculous. They were cut down either through their own stupidity, a brief scolding from others, or both. In this way, the humour of sitcoms acted as a costeffective means to encourage (C)________ of a more pluralistic and tolerant society.
options: ① depicted ...... embraceable ...... approval
② depicted ...... embraceable ...... resistance
③ intensified ...... embraceable ...... resistance
④ intensified ...... intolerable ...... resistance
⑤ depicted ...... intolerable ...... approval
questions.explanation: 시트콤은 사회적 갈등을 '묘사(depict)'해왔고, 유머를 활용해 진보적 가치를 더 '수용 가능한(embraceable)' 것으로 만들었으며, 이를 통해 다원적이고 관용적인 사회에 대한 '승인/수용(approval)'을 장려했습니다.
options_translation: ① 묘사했다 ...... 수용할 수 있는 ...... 승인
② 묘사했다 ...... 수용할 수 있는 ...... 저항
③ 강화했다 ...... 수용할 수 있는 ...... 저항
④ 강화했다 ...... 참을 수 없는 ...... 저항
⑤ 묘사했다 ...... 참을 수 없는 ...... 승인

questions.question:
17.다음 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것을 고르시오.
 [3.5점]
questions.passage: There are reasons why science is not fully trusted and why healthy skepticism and critical thinking are essential. In spite of professional standards, claims of objectivity, and the peer review process, the conduct of science can be biased. All experts are not the same, nor do they submit their work to the same scrutiny. Knowing the source of funding can be important in evaluating scientific claims. For example, the Harvard researchers who made claims in the late 1960s about the problems with dietary fat, leading the nation away from perceiving sugar as one of the main causes in health problems, were funded in part by the sugar industry. The authors did not reveal their funding source to the New England Journal of Medicine, where their influential article appeared. Their article shaped a generation of changes in eating patterns that appears to have encouraged higher use of sugar, now widely implicated as a source of the rise in obesity and diabetes. Stories such as this one fuel suspicion – but also lead to further safeguards in the scientific process. Funding disclosures, although not required five decades ago, have since been made ________.
options: ① competitive
② mandatory
③ intangible
④ elective
⑤ political
questions.explanation: 설탕 산업의 자금 지원을 받은 하버드 연구원들이 연구의 편향성을 보인 사례를 언급하며, 과학적 연구에서 편향성을 방지하기 위한 안전장치로서 자금 출처 공개(funding disclosures)가 이제는 과거와 달리 '의무(mandatory)'가 되었다는 흐름이 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 경쟁적인
② 의무적인

questions.question:
18. 다음 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것을 고르시오.
 [3.8점]
questions.passage: We are the only species that seasons its food, deliberately altering it with the highly flavored plant parts we call herbs and spices. It's quite possible that our taste for spices has an evolutionary root. Many spices have antibacterial properties – in fact, common seasonings such as garlic, onion, and oregano inhibit the growth of almost every bacterium tested. And the cultures that make the heaviest use of spices – think of the garlic and black pepper of Thai food, the ginger and coriander of India, the chili peppers of Mexico – come from warmer climates, where bacterial spoilage is a bigger issue. In contrast, the most lightly spiced cuisines – those of Scandinavia and northern Europe – are from cooler climates. Our uniquely human attention to flavor, in this case the flavor of spices, turns out to ________.
options: ① focus on the beauty of cooking styles
② show how strong flavors can be harmful
③ reflect a deeper adaptive strategy for survival
④ result from globalization and cultural exchange
⑤ contradict the natural behaviors of most animals
questions.explanation: 향신료가 박테리아의 성장을 억제하는 항균 특성이 있으며, 박테리아에 의한 부패가 발생하기 쉬운 더운 기후에서 향신료 사용량이 더 많다는 점을 통해 인간의 향신료 선호가 생존을 위한 진화적 전략(adaptive strategy for survival)임을 설명하고 있습니다.
options_translation: ① 요리 스타일의 아름다움에 집중한다
② 강한 맛이 어떻게 해로울 수 있는지 보여준다
③ 생존을 위한 더 깊은 적응 전략을 반영한다
④ 세계화와 문화 교류의 결과이다
⑤ 대부분 동물들의 자연스러운 행동과 모순된다

questions.question: 20. 다음 글의 흐름으로 보아, 주어진 문장이 들어가기에 가장 적절한 곳은? [2.8점]
questions.passage: Technologists are always on the lookout for quantifiable metrics. ( ① ) Measurable inputs to a model are their lifeblood, and like a social scientist, a technologist needs to identify concrete measures, or "proxies," for assessing progress. ( ② ) But simple metrics can take us further away from the important goals we really care about, which may require complicated metrics or be extremely difficult, or perhaps impossible, to reduce to any measure. ( ③ ) And when we have imperfect or bad proxies, we can easily fall under the illusion that we are solving for a good end without actually making genuine progress toward a worthy solution. ( ④ ) The problem of proxies results in technologists frequently substituting what is measurable for what is meaningful. ( ⑤ ) As the saying goes, "Not everything that counts can be counted, and not everything that can be counted counts."
questions.insertion_sentence: This need for quantifiable proxies produces a bias toward measuring things that are easy to quantify.
questions.explanation: 제시된 문장은 정량화 가능한 대용물(proxies)의 필요성이 수치화하기 쉬운 것들을 측정하려는 편향을 낳는다고 설명합니다. ②번 앞 문장에서 기술자가 진척 상황을 평가하기 위해 대용물을 확인할 필요성을 언급했고, ②번 뒷 문장에서는 '단순한 지표(simple metrics)'가 중요한 목표로부터 멀어지게 할 수 있다는 한계를 지적하고 있으므로, 그 원인인 편향을 설명하는 제시 문장은 ②번에 들어가는 것이 가장 자연스럽습니다.

questions.question: 21. 다음 글에서 전체 흐름과 관계 없는 문장은? [2.7점]
questions.passage: The most prevalent problem kids report is that they feel like they need to be accessible at all times. Because technology allows for it, they feel an obligation. ① <u>It's easy for most of us to relate – you probably feel the same pressure in your own life!</u> ② <u>It is really challenging to deal with the fact that we're human and can't always respond instantly.</u> ③ <u>People often overlook the pressure to respond immediately, even though they want to maintain positive relationships.</u> ④ <u>For a teen or tween who's still learning the ins and outs of social interactions, it's even worse.</u> ⑤ <u>Here's how this behavior plays out sometimes: Your child texts one of his friends, and the friend doesn't text back right away.</u> Now it's easy for your child to think, "This person doesn't want to be my friend anymore!" So he texts again, and again, and again – "blowing up" their phone." This can be stress-inducing and even read as aggressive. But you can see how easily this could happen.
questions.explanation: 이 글은 항상 연락 가능해야 한다는 압박감과 그로 인해 발생하는 즉각적인 답장에 대한 집착을 다루고 있습니다. ③번 문장은 사람들이 긍정적인 관계를 유지하고 싶어 함에도 불구하고 즉각적으로 응답해야 한다는 압박감을 '간과한다'고 기술하고 있는데, 이는 글 전체의 흐름인 '압박감을 느끼고 그로 인해 문제가 발생한다'는 내용과 상충되며 논점을 벗어납니다.

questions.question: 22. [2.9점] 주어진 글 다음에 이어질 글의 순서로 가장 적절한 것을 고르시오.
questions.passage: The fast-growing, tremendous amount of data, collected and stored in large and numerous data repositories, has far exceeded our human ability for understanding without powerful tools. As a result, data collected in large data repositories become "data tombs" – data archives that are hardly visited.
ordered_passages: (A) However, this procedure is likely to cause biases and errors and is extremely costly and time consuming. The widening gap between data and information calls for the systematic development of tools that can turn data tombs into "golden nuggets" of knowledge.

(B) Important decisions are often made based not on the information-rich data stored in data repositories but rather on a decision maker's instinct, simply because the decision maker does not have the tools to extract the valuable knowledge hidden in the vast amounts of data.
(C) Efforts have been made to develop expert system and knowledge-based technologies, which typically rely on users or domain experts to manually input knowledge into knowledge bases.
questions.explanation: 주어진 글에서 방대한 데이터가 이해 능력을 초과하여 '데이터 무덤'이 된다고 설명합니다. (B)에서는 도구의 부재로 인해 데이터 대신 직관에 의존하는 결정을 내리는 문제 상황을 구체화합니다. (C)에서는 이를 해결하기 위해 전문가 시스템 등을 개발하려는 노력을 설명하고, (A)에서 'However'를 통해 수동 입력 방식의 한계를 지적하며 지식의 '황금 덩어리'로 바꿔줄 도구의 체계적 개발 필요성을 역설하며 마무리하는 것이 자연스럽습니다.

questions.question: 23. [3.0점] 주어진 글 다음에 이어질 글의 순서로 가장 적절한 것을 고르시오.
questions.passage: If you had wanted to create a "self-driving" car in the 1950s, your best option might have been to strap a brick to the accelerator. Yes, the vehicle would have been able to move forward on its own.
ordered_passages: (A) This once-distant dream now seems within our reach. It is much the same story in medicine. Two decades ago, we were still taping bricks to accelerators. Today, we are approaching the point where we can begin to bring some appropriate technology to bear in ways that advance our understanding of patients as unique individuals.

(B) In fact, many patients are already wearing devices that monitor their conditions in real time, which allows doctors to talk to their patients in a specific, refined, and feedback-driven way that was not even possible a decade ago.

(C) It could not, however, slow down – nor could it stop, nor turn to avoid barriers. Obviously not ideal. But does that mean the entire concept of the self-driving car is not worth pursuing? No, it only means that at the time we did not yet have the tools we now possess to help enable vehicles to operate both autonomously and safely.
questions.explanation: 주어진 글에서 1950년대 자율주행차(가속기에 벽돌 올리기)의 한계를 언급합니다. (C)에서 'It could not, however'를 통해 그 방식의 구체적 한계(감속 불가 등)를 지적하고, 현대의 기술적 가능성을 언급합니다. (A)에서 이러한 발전이 의학 분야에도 적용됨을 비유를 통해 설명하고, (B)에서 실시간 모니터링 장치 등 의학 분야의 구체적인 현대적 적용 사례를 제시하며 마무리됩니다.

questions.question: 24. [3.5점] 다음 글의 내용을 한 문장으로 요약하고자 한다. 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것을 고르시오.
questions.passage: If the brain has already stored someone's face and name, why do we still end up remembering one and not the other? This is because the brain has something of a two-tier memory system at work when it comes to retrieving memories, and this gives rise to a common yet infuriating sensation: recognising someone, but not being able to remember how or why, or what their name is. This happens because the brain differentiates between familiarity and recall. To clarify, familiarity is when you encounter someone or something and you know you've done so before. But beyond that, you've got nothing; all you can say is this person/thing is already in your memories. Recall is when you can access the original memory of how and why you know this person: recognition is just flagging up the fact that the memory exists.
questions.summary_sentence: Because the brain handles familiarity and recall (A)_______, we can recognize someone without (B)_________ their name.
options: ① distinctly ...... recalling
② distinctly ...... overlooking
③ identically ...... forgetting
④ identically ...... remembering
⑤ differently ...... neglecting
questions.explanation: 지문은 뇌가 '친숙함(familiarity)'과 '회상(recall)'을 서로 다른 시스템(two-tier memory system)으로 처리한다고 설명합니다. 따라서 뇌는 두 과정을 (A) 별개로/다르게(distinctly) 처리하기 때문에, 이름 등을 (B) 회상(recalling)하지 못하더라도 얼굴을 알아보는(친숙함) 일이 발생한다는 요약이 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 별개로 ...... 회상하는 것
② 별개로 ...... 간과하는 것
③ 동일하게 ...... 잊어버리는 것
④ 동일하게 ...... 기억하는 것
⑤ 다르게 ...... 방치하는 것

questions.question: 25. [3.5점] 다음 글의 내용을 한 문장으로 요약하고자 한다. 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: For years, many psychologists have held strongly to the belief that the key to addressing negative health habits is to change behavior. This, more than values and attitudes, is the part of personality that is easiest to change. Ingestive habits such as smoking, drinking and various eating behaviors are the most common health concerns targeted for behavioral changes. Process-addiction behaviors (workaholism, shopaholism, and the like) fall into this category as well. Mental imagery combined with power of suggestion was taken up as the premise of behavioral medicine to help people change negative health behaviors into positive ones. Although this technique alone will not produce changes, when used alongside other behavior modification tactics and coping strategies, behavioral changes have proved effective for some people. What mental imagery does is reinforce a new desired behavior. Repeated use of images reinforces the desired behavior more strongly over time.
questions.summary_sentence: To help people improve their health habits, psychologists emphasize (A)_______ , supported by techniques like mental imagery, which reinforce(s) (B)__________ over time.
options: ① behavior modification …… habitual thinking
② attitude adjustments …… long-term memory
③ behavioral changes …… desired behavior
④ mental visualization …… physical endurance
⑤ emotional regulation …… coping mechanisms
questions.explanation: 이 글은 부정적인 건강 습관을 해결하기 위해 '행동 변화(behavioral changes)'가 중요함을 강조하고 있으며, '정신적 이미지(mental imagery)' 기법이 '바람직한 행동(desired behavior)'을 강화하는 데 도움을 준다고 설명하고 있다. 따라서 (A)에는 behavioral changes, (B)에는 desired behavior가 들어가는 것이 가장 적절하다.
options_translation: ① 행동 수정 …… 습관적 사고
② 태도 조정 …… 장기 기억
③ 행동 변화 …… 바람직한 행동
④ 정신적 시각화 …… 신체적 인내력
⑤ 정서 조절 …… 대처 기제

questions.question: 26. [3.8점] 다음 글의 내용을 한 문장으로 요약하고자 한다. 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Emotion socialization - learning from other people about emotions and how to deal with them - starts early in life and plays a foundational role for emotion regulation development. Although extra-familial influences, such as peers or media, gain in importance during adolescence, parents remain the primary socialization agents. For example, their own responses to emotional situations serve as a role model for emotion regulation, increasing the likelihood that their children will show similar reactions in comparable situations. Parental practices at times when their children are faced with emotional challenges also impact emotion regulation development. Whereas direct soothing and directive guidance of what to do are beneficial for younger children, they may invade adolescents' autonomy striving. In consequence, adolescents might pull away from, rather than turn toward, their parents in times of emotional crisis, unless parental practices are adjusted. More suitable in adolescence is indirect support of autonomous emotion regulation, such as through interest in, as well as awareness and nonjudgmental <u>acceptance</u> of, adolescents' emotional experiences, and being available when the adolescent wants to talk.
questions.summary_sentence: Emotional socialization is an interactive process (in which younger children learn,) mainly according to their parents' reactions, about how to (A)_________ their emotional displays (while adolescents are unwilling to comply with straightforward emotional directives from their parents,) therefore, it is wise for parents to sustain a(n) (B)_________ attitude toward their adolescents' emotions.
options: ① manipulate …… incurable
② regulate …… receptive
③ deceive …… uncritical
④ conceal …… accepting
⑤ control …… offensive
questions.explanation: 지문은 어린 시절 부모의 반응을 통해 감정을 '조절(regulate)'하는 법을 배우지만, 청소년기에는 직접적인 지시보다는 부모가 수용적이고 간접적인 지원을 해주는 것이 중요하다고 설명한다. 요약문의 (A)에는 감정을 조절한다는 의미의 regulate(또는 control)가 적절하며, (B)에는 청소년의 감정에 대해 수용적인 태도를 가져야 한다는 의미의 receptive(또는 accepting)가 적절하다. 4번의 conceal(숨기다)은 문맥상 어색하므로 2번이 정답이다.
options_translation: ① 조작하다 …… 치유할 수 없는
② 조절하다 …… 수용적인
③ 속이다 …… 무비판적인
④ 숨기다 …… 수용하는
⑤ 통제하다 …… 불쾌한

questions.question: 27. 윗글의 주제로 가장 적절한 것은? [3.2점]
questions.passage: Great scientists are (a)<u>scarcely</u> one-hit wonders. Newton is a prime example: beyond the Newtonian mechanics, he developed the theory of gravitation, calculus, laws of motion, and optimization. In fact, well-known scientists are often involved in multiple discoveries, a phenomenon potentially explained by the Matthew effect. Indeed, an initial success may offer a scientist legitimacy, improve peer perception, provide knowledge of how to score and win, enhance social status, and attract resources and quality collaborators, each of these (b)<u>rewards</u> further increasing her odds of scoring another win. Yet, there is an appealing alternative explanation: Great scientists have multiple hits and consistently succeed in their scientific (c)<u>procrastinations</u> simply because they’re exceptionally talented. Therefore, future success again goes to those who have had success earlier, not because of (d)<u>gains</u> offered by the previous success, but because the earlier success was indicative of a hidden talent. The Matthew effect posits that success alone increases the future probability of success, raising the question: Does status dictate outcomes, or does it simply reflect an (e)<u>hidden</u> talent or quality? In other words, is there really a Matthew effect after all?
options: ① the best way to become an all-round scientist
② the merits of having ingenious disciples in science
③ the impact of vicious cycle leading to academic failure
④ suspicion of whether early success guarantees future success
⑤ a direct relationship between appropriate rewards and future success
questions.explanation: 글의 후반부에서 마태 효과(초기 성공이 미래 성공을 보장한다는 이론)에 대한 대안적 설명으로, 미래의 성공은 이전 성공으로 인한 보상 때문이 아니라 그저 숨겨진 재능의 지표일 뿐이라는 점을 언급하며 마태 효과의 실제 존재 여부에 대해 의문을 제기하고 있습니다. 따라서 ④ '초기 성공이 미래의 성공을 보장하는지에 대한 의구심'이 주제로 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 다재다능한 과학자가 되는 가장 좋은 방법
② 과학 분야에서 독창적인 제자를 두는 것의 장점
③ 학문적 실패로 이어지는 악순환의 영향
④ 초기 성공이 미래의 성공을 보장하는지에 대한 의구심
⑤ 적절한 보상과 미래 성공 사이의 직접적인 관계

questions.question: 1. 밑줄 친 ⓐ~ⓔ 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은? [2.7점]
questions.passage: Let's start with the path of ⓐ <u>avoidance</u>. The boy waits for his dad and concentrates hard. When the ball comes flying across the net rapidly, he ⓑ <u>misses</u> it completely. He puts his hands on his knees and sighs. "Never mind," says his dad, "Try again. Practice makes perfect." When the boy serves the ball, it returns with full force, hitting and bruising his elbow. The boy is having ⓒ <u>much</u> fun. He sets the paddle on the table, saying, "I have had enough," and leaves for his room. His dad asks for another game the next week, but (A) <u>the boy</u> still has some pain in his elbow and just does not feel like taking up the challenge. When his mom suggests playing against his older brother, he ⓓ <u>turns down</u> her suggestion because his brother is tough. "No, thanks," sighs the boy. "He's going to be better than me anyway. In his eyes, challenges are merely barriers that ⓔ <u>hinder</u> progress, and he holds onto the belief that they are best avoided.
questions.explanation: 지문에서 소년은 공에 맞고 팔꿈치에 멍이 들었으며, "그만하겠다(I have had enough)"라고 말하며 방으로 들어갔습니다. 또한 다음 주 아빠의 제안이나 형과의 시합도 거절하고 있으므로, 소년이 매우 즐거운(much fun) 시간을 보내고 있다는 표현은 문맥상 적절하지 않습니다. 소년은 전혀 즐거워하지 않는 상황이므로 ⓒ는 문맥에 어긋납니다.

questions.question: 2. 밑줄 친 (A) the boy에게 <아래>의 Jack Canfield가 할 말로 적절한 것은? [3.5점]
