vocabulary_box: Jack Canfield is a motivational speaker, author, and success coach best known for co-authoring Chicken Soup for the Soul. He emphasizes the power of persistence, positive thinking, and taking responsibility for one's success. He encourages people to set clear goals and take consistent action. His teachings highlight the importance of overcoming fear, learning from failures, and maintaining a success-oriented mindset. Through stories and practical strategies, he inspires individuals to chase their dreams with confidence and resilience.
options: ① Don't worry about chances you miss when you don't try.
② If you're not moving toward your goal, accept that it's not meant for you.
③ When you don't fail, you save time, energy, and resources for what truly matters.
④ Every setback is a setup for a comeback. Learn from it, grow, and keep moving forward.
④ Some of the greatest achievements come from careful planning, not from trial and error.
questions.explanation: <아래>의 박스 글에 따르면 잭 캔필드는 끈기, 긍정적 사고, 실패로부터의 학습, 그리고 회복력(resilience)을 강조합니다. 본문의 소년은 패배에 대한 두려움과 작은 부상 때문에 도전을 회피하고 있으므로, 모든 좌절(setback)을 재기의 발판으로 삼고 계속 나아가라는 ④번 조언이 잭 캔필드의 철학과 가장 잘 부합합니다.
options_translation: ① 시도하지 않을 때 놓치는 기회에 대해 걱정하지 마라.
② 만약 목표를 향해 나아가고 있지 않다면, 그것이 당신의 운명이 아님을 받아들여라.
③ 실패하지 않을 때, 정말 중요한 것을 위해 시간, 에너지, 자원을 아낄 수 있다.
④ 모든 좌절은 재기를 위한 준비 과정이다. 그것으로부터 배우고, 성장하며 계속 전진하라.
⑤ 위대한 업적 중 일부는 시행착오가 아니라 세심한 계획에서 나온다.

questions.question: 3. 밑줄 친 table tennis가 다음 글에서 의미하는 바로 가장 적절한 것은? [2.8점]
questions.passage: You may have the idea that this is simply a fictional tale. However, this is the true story of Matthew Syed, a former member of the British national table-tennis team. His tale shows how an ordinary boy developed his passion for table tennis and eventually became the national champion. Because he had a growth mindset, he tried something new, discovered what he truly desired, and then became tough when he faced a difficult task. How about you? Do you see yourself in the story? You, too, can find your own <u>"table tennis.<u>" It might be a hobby, a career, or a personal goal. What is important is that you embrace the challenge and never give up on what you want to achieve. Go out there and achieve your goal!
options: ① a great victory or achievement
② a piece of advice for your development
③ a challenge only talented people can overcome
④ a temptation that distracts you from your goals
⑤ a pursuit you chase with dedication and resilience
questions.explanation: 글에서 "table tennis"는 단순히 탁구라는 스포츠를 넘어 소년이 열정을 가지고 성취하고자 했던 목표를 상징한다. 필자는 독자들에게도 자신만의 "table tennis"(취미, 경력, 개인적 목표 등)를 찾으라고 권유하고 있으므로, ⑤번 '헌신과 회복 탄력성을 가지고 추구하는 일'이 가장 적절하다.
options_translation: ① 위대한 승리 혹은 업적
② 당신의 발전을 위한 조언의 한 조각
③ 재능 있는 사람들만이 극복할 수 있는 도전
④ 당신의 목표로부터 당신을 산만하게 하는 유혹
⑤ 헌신과 회복 탄력성을 가지고 당신이 추구하는 일

questions.question: 4. 밑줄 친 ⓐ~ⓔ 중, 가리키는 대상이 같은 것을 모두 고른 것은? [2.5점]
questions.passage: Let's rewind to the point when the boy first faces ⓐ <u>his</u> dad across the net. His first attempt does not go any better, and he still gets hit on the elbow on his second try. However, ⓑ <u>he</u> picks up the ball and tries again anyway. An hour later, his dad still keeps winning easily, but the boy is learning from the experience. Every now and then, he even surprises ⓒ <u>him</u> with a decent return, almost hitting the ball past his dad. The boy later on decides to challenge his older brother. His brother is better than expected. ⓓ <u>He</u> moves with confidence and precision as a skilled and experienced player. However, the boy likes the idea that he can work even harder. In ⓔ <u>his</u> eyes, challenges are opportunities to grow.
questions.explanation: ⓐ 'his dad'의 his는 소년(the boy)을 가리킨다. ⓑ 'he picks up'의 he는 소년을 가리킨다. ⓒ 'surprises him'에서 소년의 리턴에 놀라는 대상은 아빠(his dad)이다. ⓓ 'He moves'에서 숙련된 선수처럼 움직이는 대상은 소년의 형(his older brother)이다. ⓔ 'In his eyes'에서 도전을 기회로 보는 것은 소년의 관점이므로 his는 소년을 가리킨다. 따라서 ⓐ, ⓑ, ⓔ가 소년으로 일치한다.

questions.question: 5. 다음 ( B )는 ( A ) 속 'the boy'가 자신의 경험을 회상하는 회고록이다. ( A )에서는 드러나지 않고 ( B )를 통해서만 알 수 있는 내용은? [2.9점]
questions.passage:
( A ) The boy learns from his repeated mistakes and develops new skills by practicing. He practices hard after school, on weekends, and on holidays, ultimately securing a place on the regional team. Eventually, he participates in the national championship and makes it all the way to the finals. He finds his opponent to be skillful and smart, but he plays hard. He finds himself at match point, and the audience holds its breath. He realizes how far he has come. For years he has gotten up early to practice and has loved the challenge of improving his game. He serves for the match and sneaks the ball past his opponent. <u>He punches the air in triumph.</u> He has become truly awesome!

( B ) I still remember the boy I once was-① <u>the kid who kept making mistakes</u>, missing shots and wondering if I'd ever be good enough. But each failure taught me something. I realized that it wasn't talent but consistent, focused practice that truly mattered. ② <u>So I trained-after school, on weekends, and during holidays.</u> While others relaxed, I was at the table, drilling the same shots over and over. Slowly, my game improved. ③ <u>I earned a spot on the regional team, and eventually, I made it to the national championship.</u> In the finals, I faced a smart, skilled opponent. The match was tight. Then, match point. ④ <u>As I stood ready to serve, I thought of all the early mornings spent practicing</u> and the determination that brought me here. I served, the ball slipped past my opponent, and I won. ⑤ <u>I punched the air, not just for the victory, but for everything it represented-hard work and resilience.</u>
options: ① the kid who kept making mistakes, missing shots and wondering if I'd ever be good enough
② So I trained-after school, on weekends, and during holidays.
③ I earned a spot on the regional team, and eventually, I made it to the national championship.
④ As I stood ready to serve, I thought of all the early mornings spent practicing and the determination that brought me here.
⑤ I punched the air, not just for the victory, but for everything it represented-hard work and resilience.
questions.explanation: (A)에서는 소년이 승리 후 주먹을 휘두른 외적 동작만을 묘사하고 있으나, (B)의 ⑤번 문장에서는 그 행위가 단순한 승리뿐 아니라 그동안의 노력과 회복 탄력성을 상징한다는 소년의 내면적인 성찰과 의미 부여를 담고 있다. 다른 선택지들의 내용은 (A)에서도 언급되거나 충분히 유추 가능하다.

questions.question: 7. 글의 내용과 일치하는 것은? [3.1점]
questions.passage: Teenage life on social media might seem fun and easy, but being a real teenager presents its own set of challenges, both big and small. So why can some people handle tough times and become stronger while others remain unchanged and helpless? The answer lies in resilience-the ability to adapt to challenging experiences, such as unexpected events or personal difficulties. The good news is that humans can recover from pressure and hardship and you can develop this skill. However, having resilience does not mean you will never feel stressed or anxious; it is perfectly normal to feel down every now and then. Resilience will not prevent problems, but it will help you face and overcome them. Think of it like building your body's immune system. Just as you need to be exposed to germs to build immunity, you must experience difficulties to build resilience. In simple terms, resilience is not about being emotionless: Resilience means you experience. You feel. You fail. You hurt. You fall. But you keep going. It is like working out to build your muscles; it takes time and effort to enhance your resilience.
options: ① Some teenagers grow stronger through adversity, whereas others fail to adapt and remain vulnerable.
② It is resilience that makes people recover from difficult times, and it cannot be strengthened.
③ Having resilience guarantees immunity from stress and anxiety; emotional struggles are no longer a normal part of life.
④ Exposure to germs gives you the chance to build mental strength, emotional balance, and the confidence to get through tough times.
⑤ In contrast to the gradual process of building physical strength, psychological resilience can emerge rapidly in response to a single event.
questions.explanation: 본문에서 일부 사람들은 힘든 시기를 견디고 더 강해지는 반면, 다른 사람들은 변하지 않거나 무기력한 상태로 남는다고 언급되어 있으므로 ①번이 가장 적절합니다. ②번은 회복탄력성이 강화될 수 있다고 했으므로 틀렸고, ③번은 스트레스나 불안을 느끼지 않는 것이 아니라고 했으므로 틀렸으며, ④번은 세균 노출은 신체 면역력의 예시일 뿐이고, ⑤번은 회복탄력성도 근육을 키우는 것처럼 시간과 노력이 필요하다고 했으므로 틀렸습니다.
options_translation: ① 일부 십 대들은 역경을 통해 더 강해지지만, 다른 이들은 적응에 실패하고 취약한 상태로 남는다.
② 사람들이 어려운 시기에서 회복하게 만드는 것은 회복탄력성이며, 그것은 강화될 수 없다.
③ 회복탄력성을 갖는 것은 스트레스와 불안으로부터의 면역을 보장하며, 정서적 고충은 더 이상 삶의 정상적인 부분이 아니다.
④ 세균에 노출되는 것은 정신적 힘, 정서적 균형, 그리고 힘든 시기를 이겨낼 자신감을 기를 기회를 제공한다.
⑤ 신체적 힘을 기르는 점진적인 과정과 대조적으로, 심리적 회복탄력성은 단일한 사건에 반응하여 빠르게 나타날 수 있다.

questions.question: 8. 글의 내용을 한 문장으로 요약하고자 한다. 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은? [2.7점]
questions.passage: Teenage life on social media might seem fun and easy, but being a real teenager presents its own set of challenges, both big and small. So why can some people handle tough times and become stronger while others remain unchanged and helpless? The answer lies in resilience-the ability to adapt to challenging experiences, such as unexpected events or personal difficulties. The good news is that humans can recover from pressure and hardship and you can develop this skill. However, having resilience does not mean you will never feel stressed or anxious; it is perfectly normal to feel down every now and then. Resilience will not prevent problems, but it will help you face and overcome them. Think of it like building your body's immune system. Just as you need to be exposed to germs to build immunity, you must experience difficulties to build resilience. In simple terms, resilience is not about being emotionless: Resilience means you experience. You feel. You fail. You hurt. You fall. But you keep going. It is like working out to build your muscles; it takes time and effort to enhance your resilience.
questions.summary_sentence: Although real teenage life often comes with (A) _________, they can (B) _________ resilience—the ability to adapt, recover, and grow stronger—through experience and steady effort.
options: ① adversity ... enhance
② comfort ... destroy
③ adversity ... weaken
④ comfort ... strengthen
⑤ adversity ... overcome
questions.explanation: 십 대의 삶이 역경(adversity)을 동반할지라도, 경험과 꾸준한 노력을 통해 회복탄력성을 강화(enhance)할 수 있다는 요약이 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 역경 ... 향상시키다
② 안락함 ... 파괴하다
③ 역경 ... 약화시키다
④ 안락함 ... 강화하다
⑤ 역경 ... 극복하다

questions.question: 9. 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 어법상 틀린 것은? [4.1점]
questions.passage: Our skin conducts electricity more or less efficiently, ① <u>depending</u> on our emotions. We know that when we're emotionally stimulated — stressed, sad, any intense emotion, really — our bodies sweat a tiny bit, so little we might not even notice. And when those tiny drops of sweat appear, our skin gets more electrically conductive. This change in sweat gland activity happens completely without your conscious mind ② <u>has</u> much say in the matter. If you feel emotionally intense, you're going to notice an increase in sweat gland activity. This is particularly useful from a scientific viewpoint, because it allows us ③ <u>to put</u> an objective value on a subjective state of mind. We can actually measure your emotional state by tracking how your body ④ <u>subconsciously</u> sweats, by running a bit of electricity through your skin. We can then turn the subjective, subconscious experience of emotional intensity into an objective number by ⑤ <u>figuring</u> out how good your skin gets at transferring an electrical current.
questions.explanation: ②번이 포함된 문장에서 'without your conscious mind' 뒤에는 전치사 without의 목적어 역할을 하는 동명사가 와야 합니다. 따라서 'has'를 'having'으로 고쳐야 하며, 'your conscious mind'는 동명사 having의 의미상 주어 역할을 합니다.

questions.question: 10. 글에서 전체 흐름과 관계 없는 문장은? [3.0점]
questions.passage: Let's assume at least some animals are capable of thinking despite lacking a language. ① This doesn't necessarily mean that they possess concepts, for some forms of thought may be nonconceptual. ② We can imagine, for instance, a squirrel who is planning how to get from the branch she's currently standing on to a branch from the tree in front. ③ Leaping from one tree branch to another can be a challenging task for him, especially when the branches are far apart or unstable. To do this, in principle she doesn't need a concept of branch nor a concept of tree. ④ It might be enough for her to have, for example, the ability to think in images; to make a mental map of the tree where she can imagine and try out different routes. ⑤ This doesn't imply that squirrels lack concepts, simply that they don't need them for this concrete form of thinking. For us to be able to say that an animal has concepts, we have to show not just that she's capable of thinking, but also that she has certain specific abilities.
questions.explanation: 이 글의 핵심 내용은 동물이 언어가 없어도 비개념적 사고(이미지, 정신적 지도 등)를 통해 사고할 수 있다는 것입니다. ③번 문장은 단순히 나무 사이를 뛰는 것이 육체적으로 어려운 작업이라는 점을 언급하고 있으므로 글의 주제인 '사고 방식과 개념의 유무'와는 관련이 없습니다.

questions.question: 11. 글의 제목으로 가장 적절한 것은? [2.7점]
questions.passage: In the course of trying to solve a problem with an invention, you may encounter a brick wall of resistance when you try to think your way logically through the problem. Such logical thinking is a linear type of process, which uses our reasoning skills. This works fine when we're operating in the area of what we know or have experienced. However, when we need to deal with new information, ideas, and viewpoints, linear thinking will often come up short. On the other hand, creativity by definition involves the application of new information to old problems and the conception of new viewpoints and ideas. For this you will be most effective if you learn to operate in a nonlinear manner, that is, use your creative brain. Stated differently, if you think in a linear manner, you'll tend to be conservative and keep coming up with techniques which are already known. This, of course, is just what you don't want.
options: ① Ways of Improving Thinking Skills
② Creative Thinking Beyond the Limits of Logic
③ Differences Between Conservation and Innovation
④ Techniques for Faster and More Effective Thinking
⑤ How to Change Thinking from Linear to Nonlinear
questions.explanation: 글은 논리적인 선형적 사고가 아는 범위 내에서는 유용하지만, 새로운 문제나 아이디어를 다룰 때는 한계가 있다고 설명합니다. 따라서 비선형적인 방식, 즉 창의적 사고를 활용해야 한다는 것이 핵심이므로 '논리의 한계를 넘어서는 창의적 사고'인 ②번이 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 사고 능력을 향상시키는 방법들
② 논리의 한계를 넘어서는 창의적 사고
③ 보수와 혁신의 차이점들
④ 더 빠르고 효과적인 사고를 위한 기술들
⑤ 사고를 선형에서 비선형으로 바꾸는 방법

questions.question: 12. 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은? [3.6점]
questions.passage: What does it mean for a character to be a hero as opposed to a villain? In artistic and entertainment descriptions, it's essential for the author to establish a positive relationship between a protagonist and the audience. In order for tragedy or misfortune to draw out an emotional response in viewers, the character must be adjusted so as to be recognizable as either friend or enemy. Whether the portrayal is fictional or documentary, we must feel that the protagonist is someone whose actions benefit us; the protagonist is, or would be, a worthy companion or valued ally. Violent action films are often filled with dozens of incidental deaths of minor characters that draw out little response in the audience. In order to feel strong emotions, the audience must ____________________________________________.
options: ① understand the characters' motivation
② perceive the characters as real figures
③ be emotionally engaged with the characters
④ recognize the deeper message behind the story
⑤ see how they benefit emotionally from the story
questions.explanation: 이 글은 관객이 등장인물(특히 주인공)에게 강한 감정적 반응을 보이기 위해서는 그 인물과 긍정적인 관계를 맺고 그를 친구나 아군으로 인식해야 한다고 설명하고 있습니다. 단순히 많은 죽음이 일어나는 액션 영화에서 감정적 동요가 적은 이유는 그 인물들과의 정서적 유대가 없기 때문입니다. 따라서 빈칸에는 관객이 등장인물과 정서적으로 교감해야 한다는 내용이 들어가는 것이 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 등장인물의 동기를 이해하다
② 등장인물을 실제 인물로 인식하다
③ 등장인물과 정서적으로 교감하다
④ 이야기 뒤에 숨겨진 더 깊은 메시지를 인식하다
⑤ 그들이 이야기로부터 어떻게 감정적으로 이득을 얻는지 보다

questions.question: 13. 글의 주장하는 바로 가장 적절한 것은? [2.9점]
questions.passage: There is a wealth of evidence that when parents, teachers, supervisors, and coaches are perceived as involved and caring, people feel happier and more motivated. And it is not just those people with power — we need to feel valued and respected by peers and coworkers. Thus, when the need for relatedness is met, motivation and internalization are fueled, provided that support for autonomy and competence are also there. If we are trying to motivate others, a caring relationship is a crucial basis from which to begin. And when we are trying to motivate ourselves, doing things to enhance a sense of connectedness to others can be crucial to long-term persistence. So exercise with a friend, call someone when you have a difficult decision to make, and be there as a support for others as they take on challenges.
options: ① When people care about us, we feel ready to try more.
② Strong minds don't need soft hearts to win the race.
③ Hard times make you better if you keep walking alone.
④ Push your way forward and leave your feelings behind you.
⑤ Success comes when you close your heart and open your eyes.
questions.explanation: 이 글은 타인(부모, 교사, 동료 등)과의 유대감과 보살핌을 받는다는 느낌이 행복감과 동기 부여에 중요한 역할을 한다고 설명하고 있습니다. 특히 타인을 동기 부여하거나 자기 자신을 동기 부여할 때 '보살핌의 관계'나 '연결감'이 핵심적인 기초가 된다고 강조하므로, 사람들이 우리를 아껴줄 때 더 많은 것을 시도할 준비가 된다는 ①번이 가장 적절한 주장입니다.
options_translation: ① 사람들이 우리를 아낄 때, 우리는 더 시도할 준비가 된 기분을 느낀다.
② 강한 정신은 경주에서 이기기 위해 부드러운 마음을 필요로 하지 않는다.
③ 고난은 당신이 혼자 계속 걸어간다면 당신을 더 낫게 만든다.
④ 당신의 길을 밀고 나아가고 감정은 뒤로 하라.
⑤ 성공은 당신이 마음을 닫고 눈을 뜰 때 온다.

questions.question: 14. 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은? [3.7점]
questions.passage: As you listen to your child in an emotional moment, be aware that sharing simple observation usually works better than asking questions to get a conversation rolling. You may ask your child "Why do you feel sad?" and she may not have a clue. As a child, she may not have an answer on the tip of her tongue. Maybe she's feeling sad about her parents' arguments, or because she feels overtired, or she's worried about a piano recital. But she may or may not be able to explain any of this. And even when she does come up with an answer, she might be worried that the answer is not good enough to justify the feeling. Under these circumstances, a series of questions can just make a child silent. It's better to simply reflect what you notice. You can say, "You seem a little tired today," or, "I noticed that you frowned when I mentioned the recital," and wait for her response. In conclusion, ___________________________.
options: ① simple observations work better than asking why
② showing no emotion helps children calm down
③ parents should stay quiet until their child starts talking
④ emotional children need clear answers more than listening
⑤ talking about something else is better during emotional time
questions.explanation: 이 글은 자녀가 감정적인 순간에 있을 때 '왜?'라고 질문을 던지는 것이 자녀를 침묵하게 만들 수 있음을 경고하며, 대신 부모가 관찰한 바를 단순히 언급(reflection)하는 것이 대화를 이끌어내는 데 더 효과적이라고 조언하고 있습니다. 따라서 결론 부분에는 질문하는 것보다 단순한 관찰이 더 효과적이라는 ①번이 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 단순한 관찰이 이유를 묻는 것보다 더 효과적이다.
② 감정을 보이지 않는 것이 아이들이 진정하는 데 도움이 된다.
③ 부모는 아이가 말을 시작할 때까지 조용히 있어야 한다.
④ 감정적인 아이들은 듣는 것보다 명확한 대답을 필요로 한다.
⑤ 감정적인 시간 동안 다른 것에 대해 이야기하는 것이 더 낫다.

questions.question: 15. 다음 ⓐ~ⓔ의 밑줄 친 부분 중에서 어법의 쓰임이 틀린 문장의 개수는? [4.5점]
questions.passage:
Certain artists are so closely linked with particular places that it is hard to separate them. Arles and Van Gogh are like that. Arles is located five hours southeast of Paris and is well known for its magical light and colorful landscape. ⓐ <u>The most famous dweller of this town was Vincent van Gogh.</u> Leaving behind the gray skies of Paris, he arrived in Arles in 1888. ⓑ <u>The town was inspired an explosion of creativity.</u> Vincent claimed, "The whole future of art is to be found in the south of France." He worked enthusiastically and produced nearly 200 paintings in just fifteen months. ⓒ <u>None of Vincent's works are left in Arles now, but today you can see a number of them have recreated in street-side panels.</u>

Arles is an ancient city dating back to Roman times. Many Roman buildings remain, including an arena that was built in 90 A.D. 이 경기장은 한때 다양한 오락 행사를 보러 가곤 했던 2만 명 이상의 사람들을 수용하곤 했다. Vincent sometimes went to the bullfights that were held in the arena every Sunday. He particularly liked to watch the colorful crowds. ⓓ <u>He told a friend that he found the crowds charming.</u> They inspired the painting Arena at Arles. The arena is in the top right corner of the painting and is barely visible. Below, there is a faint image of two bulls. However, Vincent paid lots of attention to the people and their colorful clothes. ⓔ <u>Some of the people are chatting with friends, others are cheering on the bulls, and the entire painting has a powerful energy.</u>
options: ① 1개
② 2개
③ 3개
④ 4개
⑤ 5개
questions.explanation: ⓑ 'The town was inspired an explosion of creativity'에서 아를이라는 마을이 창의성의 폭발을 '고무시켰다'는 능동의 의미가 되어야 하므로 'was inspired'를 'inspired'로 고쳐야 합니다. ⓒ 'see a number of them have recreated'는 지각동사 see의 목적격 보어 자리이므로, '그것들(작품들)이 재현된' 것이라는 수동의 의미를 나타내기 위해 'recreated' 또는 'being recreated'가 적절하며 'have recreated'는 문법적으로 틀립니다. 따라서 틀린 문장은 ⓑ, ⓒ 총 2개입니다.

questions.question: 17. 글을 읽고 [A]~[E] 학생이 <보기>와 같이 대화하였다.글의 주장과 일치하는 의견을 말한 학생은? [3.8점]
questions.passage: Assuming gene editing in humans proves to be safe and effective, it might seem logical, even preferable, to correct disease causing mutations at the earliest possible stage of life, before harmful genes begin causing serious problems. Yet once it becomes possible to transform an embryo's mutated genes into "normal" ones, there will certainly be temptations to upgrade normal genes to superior versions. Should we begin editing genes in unborn children to lower their lifetime risk of heart disease or cancer? What about giving unborn children beneficial features, like greater strength and increased mental abilities, or changing physical characteristics, like eye and hair color? The pursuit for perfection seems almost natural to human nature, but if we start down this slippery slope, we may not like where we end up.
vocabulary_box: [A] : Some people might want to use gene editing to improve their child's physical characteristics, and I think they should have the right to choose. As long as it's safe, it could give people better lives.
[B] : In today's world, everything is so competitive. If gene editing can help a child become smarter or stronger, I think it makes sense for parents to want the best for their kids.
[C] : I think gene editing sounds helpful for preventing serious diseases, but if we start using it to make 'better' babies, like with higher intelligence, it could become really dangerous.
[D] : If we have the technology to make people healthier, smarter, or even more talented, I think it would be a waste not to use it. It could help humanity reach a new level.
[E] : I want my baby to be strong and very smart. If we can do that, we should do it. Everyone wants the best for their child, so using gene editing to help them succeed makes sense to me.
options: ① [A]
② [B]
③ [C]
④ [D]
⑤ [E]
questions.explanation: 이 글은 유전자 편집이 질병 예방을 넘어 지능 향상이나 신체적 특징 강화와 같은 목적으로 사용되는 것에 대해 '미끄러운 경사길(slippery slope)'에 비유하며 비판적인 우려를 표하고 있습니다. 학생 [C]는 질병 예방에는 긍정적이지만, 지능을 높이는 등 더 나은 아기를 만드는 데 사용하는 것은 위험할 수 있다고 말하여 글의 태도와 일치하는 의견을 제시하고 있습니다.

questions.question: 18. 고흐의 그림 Café Terrace at Night에 대한 윗글의 내용과 일치하지 않는 것은? [2.6점]
questions.passage: Art and the City Arles, the City of Light and Art Certain artists are so closely linked with particular places that it is hard to separate them. Arles and Van Gogh are like that. Arles is located five hours southeast of Paris and is well known for its magical light and colorful landscape. The most famous resident of this town was Vincent van Gogh. Leaving behind the gray skies of Paris, he arrived in Arles in 1888. The town inspired an explosion of creativity. Vincent claimed, “The whole future of art is to be found in the south of France.” He worked enthusiastically and produced nearly 200 paintings in just fifteen months. None of Vincent’s works are left in Arles now, but today you can see a number of them have been recreated in street-side panels. Let’s follow Vincent’s traces that remain in Arles. The Roman Arena Arles is an ancient city dating back to Roman times. Many Roman buildings remain, including an arena that was built in 90 A. D. The arena used to seat over 20,000 people who would go to watch various entertaining events. Vincent sometimes went to the bullfights that were held in the arena every Sunday. He particularly liked to watch the colorful crowds. He told a friend that he found the crowds fascinating. They inspired the painting Arena at Arles. The arena is in the top right corner of the painting and is barely visible. Below, there is a faint image of two bulls. However, Vincent paid lots of attention to the people and their colorful clothes. Some of the people are chatting with friends, others are cheering on the bulls, and the entire painting has a powerful energy. Café van Gogh Vincent painted the world-famous Café Terrace at Night in September 1888. He created this work while sitting outside the Café van Gogh at night. This was unusual because most painters did their night scenes from memory and worked during the daytime. As such, they used a lot of black paint. Vincent, however, believed that night scenes contained diverse and vibrant colors. Indeed, the Café Terrace at Night has such a rich harmony of yellows, blues, and oranges that Vincent did not have to use a single drop of black paint. Even today, there is still a café at the site of Vincent’s painting. It was renovated in the 1990s and painted yellow to look like the café in the painting. However, it is uncertain whether the color of the original café was yellow or not. The reason is that Vincent painted the wall of the café yellow to show the lamp light. Former Arles Hospital In December 1888, Vincent suffered from a mental illness and was sent to the hospital in Arles. He stayed there for five months. During this time, his mental stability improved, and the doctors allowed him to paint outdoors. Vincent took advantage of this freedom and produced several beautiful landscapes, such as The Garden of the Hospital in Arles. The picture illustrates a spring garden filled with flowers and trees with different colors and tones. The flowers are in full bloom, and the small trees are leafy. The big trees, however, have few leaves. This is rather odd given that the season is spring. Perhaps this contrast reflects the painter’s complex feelings during the most difficult time of his life. The hospital closed in the 1980s, and the building reopened as a library and exhibition space, with a café and gift shops. The garden was renovated to resemble Vincent’s painting as much as possible. Arles and its provincial countryside inspired Vincent to create brighter, more exciting landscapes. He had searched for brighter colors and softer light in Paris. In Arles, he found them. Today, more than 200 years later, this beautiful city remains just as attractive. The combination of Roman historic sites and Vincent’s story creates a unique mood that will inspire you just as the city had inspired Vincent.
options: ① 고흐가 1888년 9월에 그린 그림이다.
② 고흐가 밤에 카페 반 고흐 야외에 앉아서 그렸다.
③ 노란색, 파란색, 주황색의 풍부한 조화를 가진 그림이다.
④ 그림 속 카페 반 고흐의 벽은 실제 카페의 벽과 같이 노란색이었다.
⑤ 램프의 불빛을 보여주기 위해 고흐는 그림 속 카페의 벽을 노란색으로 칠했다.
questions.explanation: 지문의 마지막 부분에 'it is uncertain whether the color of the original café was yellow or not(원래 카페의 색이 노란색이었는지는 불확실하다)'라고 명시되어 있습니다. 고흐가 카페 벽을 노란색으로 칠한 이유는 실제 색이 그래서가 아니라 램프의 불빛을 표현하기 위함이었습니다.

questions.question: 19. 어법에 맞게 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 것으로 적절한 것은? [2.9점]
questions.passage:
Vincent painted the world-famous Café Terrace at Night in September 1888. He created this work while sitting outside the Café van Gogh at night. This was unusual (A) [ because of / because ] most painters did their night scenes from memory and worked during the daytime. As such, they used a lot of black paint. Vincent, however, believed that night scenes contained diverse and vibrant colors. Indeed, the Café Terrace at Night has (B) [ such / so ] a rich harmony of yellows, blues, and oranges that Vincent did not have to use a single drop of black paint.
Even today, there is still a café at the site of Vincent's painting. It was renovated in the 1990s and painted yellow to look like the café in the painting. However, it is uncertain (C) [ whether / if ] the color of the original café was yellow or not. The reason is that Vincent painted the wall of the café yellow to show the lamp light.
options: ① because, so, whether
② because, such, whether
③ because of, such, whether
④ because, so, if
⑤ because of, so, if
questions.explanation: (A) 뒤에 'most painters did...'와 같이 주어와 동사를 갖춘 절이 오므로 접속사인 because가 적절합니다. (B) 'such a + 형용사 + 명사'의 어순을 따르므로 such가 적절합니다. (C) uncertain의 목적어로 쓰여 '~인지 아닌지'의 의미를 나타내는 명사절 접속사 자리이며, 뒤에 'or not'과 호응하므로 whether가 가장 적절합니다.

questions.question: 20. 윗글의 밑줄 친 부분 중 어법상 틀린 곳을 모두 고른 것은? [3.1점]
questions.passage: Sunlight offers numerous health benefits. In small amounts, it boosts vitamin D levels, makes the bones stronger, prevents diseases, and heals skin conditions. Sunlight also affects mental health. Natural light causes the release of serotonin, a natural chemical the brain <u>ⓐ producing</u> to promote happiness and pleasure and reduce depression and anxiety. On the other hand, reductions in sunlight <u>ⓑ are linked</u> to panic attacks and anxiety-related disorders. However, the impact of light extends beyond sunlight. Colors <u>ⓒ created</u> by artificial light can cause different emotions and have other effects on the body. Blue and white light energize us, but they can also disturb sleep patterns by lowering levels of melatonin, a chemical made in the brain that regulates night-and-day cycles and sleep-wake cycles. The brain has the most sensitivity to blue light. In contrast, red light and yellow light <u>ⓓ are</u> the least likely to impact our bodies. Exposure to red light in the evening can improve mental health by increasing the release of melatonin, <u>ⓔ from which</u> leads to better sleep at night. This improves people's cognitive abilities and overall mental health.
questions.explanation: ⓐ는 목적격 관계대명사가 생략된 관계사절 내에서 주어 'the brain'의 동사가 필요한 자리이므로 현재분사 'producing'을 현재형 동사인 'produces'로 고쳐야 합니다. ⓔ는 콤마(,) 뒤에서 선행사(앞 문장의 내용 혹은 melatonin의 분비)를 부연 설명하는 주격 관계대명사가 필요한 자리이므로 'from which'를 'which'로 고쳐야 'leads to'의 주어 역할을 할 수 있습니다.

questions.passage: Plants can communicate, although not in the same way we do. Some express their discontent through scents. You know that smell that hangs in the air after you've mowed the lawn? Yeah, that's actually an SOS. Some plants use sound. Yes, sound, though at a frequency that we can't hear. Researchers experimented with plants and microphones to see if they could record any trouble calls. They found plants produce a high-frequency clicking noise when (A) _________ (stress) and can make different sounds for different stressors. The sound a plant makes when it's not getting watered differs from the one it'll make when a leaf is cut. However, it's worth noting that experts don't think plants are crying out in pain. It's more likely that these reactions are knee-jerk survival actions. Plants are (B) _________ (live) organisms, and their main objective is to survive. Scents and sounds are their tools for defending against things that might harm them.

questions.passage: Make Your World a Better Place Young Change-Makers Shaping the Future There are a lot of things that fill us with hope for the future: technology, science, accountable leaders, and nonprofit organizations committed to doing good. However, few things give us more hope for the future than young people. Some young people are already working toward solutions for the problems their communities and the world are facing. Let’s look at three inspirational examples of these young people. Combating Online Hate with Re Think Trisha Prabhu, a young computer scientist from the U. S., is fighting cyberbullying with her innovative application Re Think. Re Think is a virtual keyboard that uses artificial intelligence to detect potentially hurtful text messages before they are sent and prompts young people to pause and reconsider their words. When a user types a message that contains potentially offensive language, such as “I hate you,” Re Think prompts: “Hold on! Are you sure you want to say that?” or “Remember. You are what you type!” In 2014, when Trisha was just thirteen years old, she read the tragic news of a twelve-year-old girl who had been cyberbullied for over a year and a half. Shocked at the story, she decided to prevent cyberbullying by using technology and created Re Think. Re Think has been used by schools and organizations worldwide and has successfully raised awareness on cyberbullying. It has helped young people make better decisions in digital space where people could easily be unkind toward each other. In fact, it has been found that when using Re Think, adolescents change their minds 93% of the time and decide not to post offensive messages. Inventing with Discarded Electronic Parts Kelvin Doe, a self-taught inventor and engineer from Sierra Leone, has been fascinated with electronics since childhood. He would often do experiments with discarded electronics he found in trash cans to create his own inventions. In 2009, at the young age of thirteen, Kelvin built his own FM radio station by using a transmitter he made from discarded electronic parts. In 2014, during the time when an Ebola outbreak affected Africa, Kelvin’s radio station proved to be invaluable. With schools closed, his radio station provided educational programs to students over the radio. This was especially important in his country, where the radio was the main source of media. Kelvin also improved the lives of people around him by providing affordable resources. He invented a battery capable of powering homes and small businesses, designed a generator that runs on salt water, and constructed a windmill to supply electricity to his community. Helping Homeless People Rebuild Their Lives John Michael Stagliano is a young social activist from the U. S. who founded Home Again in 2016. It is a nonprofit organization that offers furniture and household essentials to families and individuals transitioning from homelessness to stable housing. He says, “For people who have lived in their cars, in and out of shelters, and in the woods, to be home again is a triumph, a sense of peace, and something to be celebrated.” John’s journey began in 2015. At the age of twelve, he volunteered at a local shelter where people in need were staying. He learned that many of the shelter residents worked hard to rent houses and trailers but faced difficulties in furnishing their new homes upon moving in. This prompted John to decide to do something for those transitioning out of homelessness. Needing donations to gather essential items to help them, John reached out to his family, friends, and neighbors. As word of his efforts spread, donations began to rush in. So John was able to help more people get settled. He said, “I never knew the impact that a simple couch or a kitchen table could have. Furniture can restore the dignity of a family.” Trisha Prabhu, Kelvin Doe, and John Michael Stagliano are all examples of young social activists who have made significant contributions to society. Their innovative efforts to solve social problems demonstrate the power of technology, commitment, and individual initiative. Their stories serve as an inspiration for young people around the world to pursue their passions and make a difference in their communities. As young innovators and social activists keep appearing, they will undoubtedly make the world a better place. Reading about Technology Appropriate Technology Appropriate technology refers to technological solutions that are designed to suitably meet the specific needs of a community. Such technologies typically utilize locally available resources, so they reduce costs and promote local industries. These technologies are environmentally sustainable because they rely on renewable resources. Additionally, their designs are easy to use, which allow local communities to maintain the technologies without specialized training. The Warka Tower is one good example of appropriate technology. This tower helps with the lack of clean water in many regions. It employs natural processes to deliver 100 liters of clean water daily. It gathers rainwater in a pot at its base. Additionally, the tower captures fog and changes it into water drops that collect on nets, and then the water drops fall into the pot. One of the tower’s strengths is that it is simple. A small team can construct it in just one day by using eco-friendly materials like soil, wood, and natural fiber nets. Truly, the Warka Tower demonstrates how appropriate technology can solve local issues in a way that is affordable, effective, and eco-friendly.

③ Trisha, who had endured cyberbullying for over a year and a half, came across the story of a girl facing the same struggle.
④ ReThink, the AI-powered keyboard adopted globally, guides young people toward more thoughtful choices in online interactions.
⑤ It has been revealed that when using ReThink, more than nine out of ten adolescents reconsider and modify their initial communicative intentions.

questions.question: 9. <보기>의 (A)~(E) 중, 윗글의 내용을 바탕으로 답할 수 있는 질문의 개수는? [4.1점]
questions.passage: From Tradition to Trend K-Delivery, Speedy and Reliable In Korea, nearly anything can be delivered within twenty-four hours. Delivery is not limited to Korea; however, a unique culture has developed around the Korean delivery industry. People in Korea can order whatever they want whenever they want and have it delivered wherever they want. Delivery apps rank stores by various standards: review scores, popularity, price, delivery fee, and distance, to name a few. The speedy delivery of purchased items to your house is literally at the tips of your fingers. What is the history behind this culture? In 1768, Hwang Yun-seok, a scholar, made a diary entry after taking the gwageo, a public service entrance exam. He wrote that he and his friends had ordered a delivery of naengmyeon for lunch. Hwang’s diary is the first historical document indicating Koreans have been delivering food for at least two and a half centuries. During the Joseon period, specialized people called jeonin delivered letters for a fee. In the days before the modern address systems, letters were delivered by name and place of residence, so a jeonin had to know the local areas like the back of his hand. Service prices were determined by schedule and distance. During the Japanese colonial period, Seoul’s streets were filled with delivery professionals called “messengers,” most working for a company named Yongdalsa. Many used bikes to speed up delivery. When customers contacted Yongdalsa, a messenger went to pick up the item and then delivered it. Delivery mistakes were rare. Messengers were sometimes charged with carrying large bundles of cash, but they were unfailingly honest and accurate. Customers trusted the messengers so much that they often did not check the items they received. This messenger service was unique to Korea and was based on a culture of mutual trust and a hunger for speed. It is possible that this paved the way for modern motorcycle delivery. After Korea’s liberation from colonial rule, it was divided into two. Then came the Korean War (1950-1953). During this series of upheavals, Korea’s delivery system fell apart. It was during the 1960s that delivery services grew again thanks to urbanization. As economic development progressed, people flocked to urban areas, where labor became concentrated. This boosted the demand for delivery services. Deliveries of newspapers and milk quickly became popular. During lunchtime, city centers were filled with restaurant workers delivering trays full of food, stacked on top of each other. In the late 1980s and 1990s, caterers delivered homemade lunches in cloth bags to urban offices and returned later to collect empty dishes. The delivery area grew rapidly. In 1992, taekbae service, an express home delivery service through which a person receives an ordered item in at least a day or two was introduced. On the first day, there were just two deliveries. Now, millions of items are delivered daily. On average, a South Korean uses taekbae sixty-five times per year. It was the development of digital and information technology that enabled the remarkable growth of taekbae. Logistics automation, GPS maps, and mobile applications have extended the range and scale of delivery services while keeping prices reasonable. The phenomenal growth of e-commerce has driven the need for delivery services. A rule of thumb for taekbae is next-day delivery; if a person orders something today, it should arrive tomorrow. Taekbae is changing so rapidly that now more and more items are delivered on the same day they are ordered. It is also possible to choose a specific date and time for delivery. Taekbae services, beginning from foot-powered delivery, have grown by leaps and bounds thanks to advancements in technology. Moreover, the services will likely be developed further due to continuing technological upheavals. Drones and autonomous robots are being used to deliver items by logistics companies in foreign countries. In Korea, companies are testing the possibility of using advanced equipment such as autonomous vehicles, delivery robots, and drones for deliveries. It is fair to say that modern Korean life cannot function as it does without its delivery services. To maintain trust with customers, the Korean delivery industry prioritizes rapid, safe, and affordable transportation. These persistent efforts for reliability and the adoption of advanced delivery technology will continue being the driving forces that will move Korean delivery forward well into the future. Reading about Culture Dabbawalas: The Lunch Box Delivery Men in India Mumbai, India’s largest and busiest city, has a unique tradition in which people enjoy home-cooked lunches delivered from their homes. This service is carried out by dedicated people known as dabbawalas. The delivery process begins early in the morning when lunch boxes are collected by dabbawalas from homes around Mumbai by 9:00 a.m. They are then taken to the nearest train station. Each lunch box is carefully placed on the right train heading in various directions. By 12:30 p.m., the lunches have reached their destinations in Mumbai, where they are distributed to offices. The empty lunch boxes are gathered by 5:00 p.m. and returned to their original homes by following the same route in reverse. Today, about 5,000 dabbawalas work in and around Mumbai and manage about 400,000 lunch box deliveries daily. This operation runs with remarkable accuracy, achieving a 99.99% success rate, which means just one error in every six million deliveries. Dabbawalas have a simple but effective color-coding system to ensure each lunch box reaches its planned destination. Dabbawalas owe their success to an efficient organization and a strong sense of work. Accuracy is key, and their cooperation and communication allow them to function as efficiently as a well-organized machine.

(B) How were letters delivered before Korea had a modern address system?
(C) How long did it take for a jeonin to deliver a letter in the 18th century?
(D) What cultural values shaped Korea's delivery system?
(E) Which modern Korean delivery company is the most successful?

② 2개
③ 3개
④ 4개
⑤ 5개

questions.question: 16. 글의 내용을 올바르게 정리하지 않은 것은? [3.6점]
questions.passage: A morally good person is one who does morally bad actions significantly less often than most and does morally good ones significantly more often than most. In judging a person not only her actions but also her intentions and motives are relevant. A morally good person must intend to do morally good actions and intend to avoid morally bad ones. A person who unintentionally prevents harm to others and does not harm them simply because things do not turn out as she intends is not morally good. Although this kind of situation generally occurs only in slapstick movies, it is worth mentioning to avoid the false impression that it is the actual consequences of a person’s actions that count toward her being judged morally good or bad. But actual consequences are important. A person who always tries to prevent harm but never does, is not generally thought of as morally good. Of such a person, it may be said that she means well; but, contrary to Kant, some results are necessary before she is regarded as morally good.

questions.question: 18. 글에 관한 내용으로 적절하지 않은 것은? [4.5점]
questions.passage: From Tradition to Trend K-Delivery, Speedy and Reliable In Korea, nearly anything can be delivered within twenty-four hours. Delivery is not limited to Korea; however, a unique culture has developed around the Korean delivery industry. People in Korea can order whatever they want whenever they want and have it delivered wherever they want. Delivery apps rank stores by various standards: review scores, popularity, price, delivery fee, and distance, to name a few. The speedy delivery of purchased items to your house is literally at the tips of your fingers. What is the history behind this culture? In 1768, Hwang Yun-seok, a scholar, made a diary entry after taking the gwageo, a public service entrance exam. He wrote that he and his friends had ordered a delivery of naengmyeon for lunch. Hwang’s diary is the first historical document indicating Koreans have been delivering food for at least two and a half centuries. During the Joseon period, specialized people called jeonin delivered letters for a fee. In the days before the modern address systems, letters were delivered by name and place of residence, so a jeonin had to know the local areas like the back of his hand. Service prices were determined by schedule and distance. During the Japanese colonial period, Seoul’s streets were filled with delivery professionals called “messengers,” most working for a company named Yongdalsa. Many used bikes to speed up delivery. When customers contacted Yongdalsa, a messenger went to pick up the item and then delivered it. Delivery mistakes were rare. Messengers were sometimes charged with carrying large bundles of cash, but they were unfailingly honest and accurate. Customers trusted the messengers so much that they often did not check the items they received. This messenger service was unique to Korea and was based on a culture of mutual trust and a hunger for speed. It is possible that this paved the way for modern motorcycle delivery. After Korea’s liberation from colonial rule, it was divided into two. Then came the Korean War (1950-1953). During this series of upheavals, Korea’s delivery system fell apart. It was during the 1960s that delivery services grew again thanks to urbanization. As economic development progressed, people flocked to urban areas, where labor became concentrated. This boosted the demand for delivery services. Deliveries of newspapers and milk quickly became popular. During lunchtime, city centers were filled with restaurant workers delivering trays full of food, stacked on top of each other. In the late 1980s and 1990s, caterers delivered homemade lunches in cloth bags to urban offices and returned later to collect empty dishes. The delivery area grew rapidly. In 1992, taekbae service, an express home delivery service through which a person receives an ordered item in at least a day or two was introduced. On the first day, there were just two deliveries. Now, millions of items are delivered daily. On average, a South Korean uses taekbae sixty-five times per year. It was the development of digital and information technology that enabled the remarkable growth of taekbae. Logistics automation, GPS maps, and mobile applications have extended the range and scale of delivery services while keeping prices reasonable. The phenomenal growth of e-commerce has driven the need for delivery services. A rule of thumb for taekbae is next-day delivery; if a person orders something today, it should arrive tomorrow. Taekbae is changing so rapidly that now more and more items are delivered on the same day they are ordered. It is also possible to choose a specific date and time for delivery. Taekbae services, beginning from foot-powered delivery, have grown by leaps and bounds thanks to advancements in technology. Moreover, the services will likely be developed further due to continuing technological upheavals. Drones and autonomous robots are being used to deliver items by logistics companies in foreign countries. In Korea, companies are testing the possibility of using advanced equipment such as autonomous vehicles, delivery robots, and drones for deliveries. It is fair to say that modern Korean life cannot function as it does without its delivery services. To maintain trust with customers, the Korean delivery industry prioritizes rapid, safe, and affordable transportation. These persistent efforts for reliability and the adoption of advanced delivery technology will continue being the driving forces that will move Korean delivery forward well into the future. Reading about Culture Dabbawalas: The Lunch Box Delivery Men in India Mumbai, India’s largest and busiest city, has a unique tradition in which people enjoy home-cooked lunches delivered from their homes. This service is carried out by dedicated people known as dabbawalas. The delivery process begins early in the morning when lunch boxes are collected by dabbawalas from homes around Mumbai by 9:00 a.m. They are then taken to the nearest train station. Each lunch box is carefully placed on the right train heading in various directions. By 12:30 p.m., the lunches have reached their destinations in Mumbai, where they are distributed to offices. The empty lunch boxes are gathered by 5:00 p.m. and returned to their original homes by following the same route in reverse. Today, about 5,000 dabbawalas work in and around Mumbai and manage about 400,000 lunch box deliveries daily. This operation runs with remarkable accuracy, achieving a 99.99% success rate, which means just one error in every six million deliveries. Dabbawalas have a simple but effective color-coding system to ensure each lunch box reaches its planned destination. Dabbawalas owe their success to an efficient organization and a strong sense of work. Accuracy is key, and their cooperation and communication allow them to function as efficiently as a well-organized machine.
options: ① Dabbawalas collect the empty lunch boxes by 5:00 p.m. and deliver them back home.
② About 5,000 dabbawalas handle roughly four hundred thousand deliveries each day.
③ Dabbawalas cook the lunch boxes at home before delivering them.
④ The delivery system achieves a 99.99% success rate, with only one mistake per 6,000,000 deliveries.
⑤ Color-codes are used to make sure each lunch box reaches its destination.

questions.question: 12. 다음 글의 내용을 요약하고자 한다. 빈칸 ⓐ, ⓑ, ⓒ에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은? [4.3점]
questions.passage: The concept of ecosystem states should be familiar to anyone with a home vegetable garden. The garden is a small ecosystem that the grower attempts to keep in a specific state, namely the maximization of fruit and vegetable production. To achieve this, the grower is almost always intervening in the dynamics of the ecosystem: they remove unwelcome plants that begin to grow and perhaps spray insecticides and fence off the patch to stop insects and other animals from consuming the vegetables. Since maximizing vegetable growth is an inherently unstable state for the ecosystem, the grower is effectively keeping the ball on a slope. If the grower stops intervening, even for a day, the ecosystem, that small patch of ground, will naturally begin to shift to a more stable state. Vegetables may still grow, but yield will almost certainly be lower as other plants crowd out the vegetables and wildlife consume the produce.
questions.summary_sentence: A home vegetable garden is an example of an ecosystem where the grower constantly ⓐ_______ - by removing weeds, using insecticides, or adding fences - to keep it in a productive state. However, this state is ⓑ________ , and without regular care, the garden will naturally shift to a more stable but ⓒ________ productive condition, with lower yields due to competing plants and animals.
options: ① observes ... stable ... less
② intervenes ... stable ... more
③ manages ... stable ... less
④ intervenes ... unstable ... less
⑤ manages ... unstable ... more

questions.question: 13. 다음 글의 요지로 가장 적절한 것은? [4.5점]
questions.passage: The prominence of the social dimension in food writing might suggest that the flavor of food is taking a back seat. I suspect that most people view flavor as of secondary importance in social settings where food is served. Although our social gatherings coalesce around food, the meaning of these gatherings does not seem to depend on flavor. Flavor assists with the narrow purpose of filling the belly, and once that is accomplished it provides the backdrop for whatever social dynamics characterize the gathering. These can be understood independently of the flavor of the food on offer, the appreciation of which is understood to be personal and subjective. According to this conventional wisdom, the ceremonies and rituals around food, the social events that supply food with its meaning, do not depend on the quality of sensations provided by the food. To focus excessively on flavor is to miss the larger significance of these social relations. * coalesce: 모이다 ** backdrop: 배경
options: ① People are highly focused on the latest food trends.
② The flavor of food determines the success of social events.
③ Food is an important element for satisfying hunger and providing energy.
④ People perceive the flavor of food objectively regardless of their mood or social context.
⑤ Social gatherings come together around food, but the flavor of food is subordinate to its social meaning.
questions.explanation: 글의 중심 내용은 음식을 중심으로 한 사회적 모임에서 음식의 맛(flavor)은 부차적인 중요성을 가지며, 모임의 진정한 의미는 음식의 감각적 품질보다는 사회적 관계와 역동성에 있다는 것입니다. 따라서 맛은 사회적 의미에 종속된다는 5번이 가장 적절합니다.

② 음식의 맛이 사교 행사의 성공을 결정한다.
③ 음식은 배고픔을 해결하고 에너지를 제공하는 중요한 요소이다.
④ 사람들은 기분이나 사회적 맥락에 상관없이 음식의 맛을 객관적으로 인지한다.
⑤ 사교 모임은 음식을 중심으로 모이지만, 음식의 맛은 그 사회적 의미보다 하위의(부차적인) 것이다.

questions.question: 14. ‘Commitment’에 대한 설명으로 올바른 것을 모두 고르면? [3.5점]
questions.passage: Commitment is the glue holding together characteristically human forms of social life. Commitments make individuals' behavior predictable in the face of fluctuations in their desires and interests, thereby facilitating the planning and coordination of joint actions involving multiple agents. Moreover, commitments make people willing to perform actions that they would not otherwise perform. For example, a taxi driver picks up his clients and transports them to their desired destination because they are committed to paying him afterwards for the service, and a construction worker performs her job every day because her employer has made a credible commitment to pay her at the end of the month. Indeed, the taxi driver and the construction worker are willing to accept money as payment only because a network of other agents (notably the central bank) is committed to taking various measures to sustain the currency in question. Thus, social objects and institutions such as jobs, money, government, scientific collaborations and marriage depend for their origin and stability upon the credibility of commitments.
vocabulary_box: ⓐ Commitment helps individuals act consistently even when their desires or interests change.
ⓑ Commitment primarily functions to fulfill personal desires rather than to maintain social order.
ⓒ Commitment is mostly relevant in financial transactions, not in broader social institutions like marriage or government.
ⓓ Commitment helps people perform actions and maintain systems that rely on trust and shared expectations.
ⓔ Commitment increases unpredictability in social interactions and institutions.
ⓕ Commitment helps make individuals' behavior predictable, which supports planning and cooperation.
questions.explanation: 지문은 헌신(Commitment)이 개인의 욕구나 흥미의 변화에도 불구하고 행동을 예측 가능하게 하며(ⓐ), 이를 통해 공동 행동의 계획과 조정을 돕고(ⓕ), 돈이나 정부, 결혼과 같은 신뢰와 기대를 바탕으로 하는 사회적 제도들의 기원과 안정성을 뒷받침한다고 설명하고 있다(ⓓ). 반면 개인적 욕구 충족이 우선이라거나(ⓑ), 금융 거래에만 관련된다는 점(ⓒ), 또는 예측 불가능성을 높인다는 점(ⓔ)은 본문의 내용과 상반된다.

They knew that a glitch in power supply would bring their operations to a halt-and that a lot of glitches might well mean bankruptcy. Sometimes, humour can _______________. The history of US television sitcoms provides a clear example. Since their inception in the early 1950s they have charted many of the social conflicts in US society: civil rights, women's rights in the home and in the workplace children's rights, immigration and multiculturalism, as well as evolving conceptions of the family. Each of these issues has been addressed through humour in a way that has helped to make more progressive values more acceptable than hitherto.
