questions.question: 17. 글의 흐름으로 보아 주어진 문장이 들어가기에 가장 적절한 곳은? [4.7점]
questions.passage:
The more connections a specific memory has, and the "stronger" (more active) the synapse is, the easier it is to access, in the same way that it's easier to travel to somewhere with multiple roads and transport links than to an abandoned barn in the middle of a wilderness. The name and face of your long-term partner, for example, is going to occur in a great deal of memories, so it will always be at the forefront of your mind. ( ① ) But if the brain has already stored someone's face and name, why do we still end up remembering one and not the other? ( ② ) This is because the brain has something of a two-tier memory system at work when it comes to retrieving memories, and this gives rise to a common yet infuriating sensation: recognizing someone, but not being able to remember how or why, or what their name is. ( ③ ) This happens because the brain differentiates between familiarity and recall. To clarify, familiarity (or recognition) is when you encounter someone or something and you know you've done so before. ( ④ ) But beyond that, you've got nothing; all you can say is this person/thing is already in your memories. ( ⑤ ) Recall is when you can access the original memory of how and why you know this person: recognition is just flagging up the fact that the memory exists.

*atypical: 이례적인
**synapse: 시냅스 <신경 세포의 자극 전달부>
questions.insertion_sentence: Other people aren't going to get this treatment (unless your relationships are rather more atypical), so remembering their names is going to be harder.
questions.explanation: 제시된 문장은 '다른 사람들은 이런 대우를 받지 못할 것이므로(당신의 관계가 다소 이례적이지 않는 한), 그들의 이름을 기억하는 것은 더 어려울 것이다'라는 내용입니다. 여기서 'this treatment'는 바로 앞 문장에서 언급된 '장기적인 파트너의 이름과 얼굴이 수많은 기억 속에 나타나 항상 마음의 최전선에 있게 되는 것'을 가리킵니다. 따라서 파트너에 대한 예시 바로 뒤인 ①번 위치가 가장 적절합니다. 이후 문장(②번 앞)부터는 왜 얼굴은 기억나는데 이름은 기억나지 않는지에 대한 뇌의 이중 기억 시스템(친숙함 vs 회상)에 대한 설명으로 이어집니다.

questions.question: 18. 글을 읽고 빈칸 (A)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은? [3.9점]
questions.passage:
Dictionaries are relatively good resources for anyone interested in finding out what a word means. Using one set of words to define another word is called a lexical definition. But it's important to understand the limits of dictionary definitions. More often than not, (A) ________________. In other words, a dictionary functions in many cases as a cross-reference or translator between words one knows and words that one doesn't yet know. Even the most obscure words in a dictionary, say, for example, "pulchritudinous" or "kalokagathia," must be defined using words that the reader already knows and understands. Otherwise, the dictionary isn't very helpful.
*lexical: 어휘적인 **robust: 탄탄한 ***obscure: 난해한
options: ① the definition of a dictionary is not always accurate
② dictionaries are essential tools for learning a new language
③ the method of using dictionaries is obscure for some readers
④ dictionaries presuppose that readers have prior knowledge of the language
⑤ dictionaries have limitations on the number of words they can include
questions.explanation: 이 글은 사전 정의의 한계에 대해 설명하고 있습니다. 사전은 이미 알고 있는 단어를 사용하여 모르는 단어를 정의하므로, 독자가 그 언어에 대한 사전 지식을 가지고 있어야만 유용하다는 것이 핵심 내용입니다. 따라서 빈칸 (A)에는 '사전은 독자가 해당 언어에 대한 사전 지식을 가지고 있다는 것을 전제로 한다'는 내용이 들어가는 것이 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 사전의 정의가 항상 정확한 것은 아니다
② 사전은 새로운 언어를 배우는 데 필수적인 도구이다
③ 사전 사용 방법이 일부 독자들에게는 난해하다
④ 사전은 독자가 해당 언어에 대한 사전 지식을 가지고 있음을 전제로 한다
⑤ 사전은 포함할 수 있는 단어의 수에 한계가 있다

questions.question: [서답형(단답형) 6] 다음 글 ⓐ ~ ⓔ 중 어법상 틀린 문장을 모두 고르시오. [3.0점]
questions.passage: ⓐ The explosion of popular music in the second half of the twentieth century as well as the global circulation and dissemination of music by the creative industries propelled a new understanding of accessibility in relation to music. ⓑ Suddenly, in the 1950s, anyone could pick up spoons, a couple of pans, a secondhand guitar and start a band. ⓒ This led to specific genres such as skiffle, but also, more generally, reflecting a much more relaxed and inclusive attitude to music making. ⓓ While ordinary people had always sung and made music, the popular music movement was driven by a spirit of rebellion and freedom. ⓔ This approach led to the punk movement, whose musicians even made it a condition for their music to non-virtuosic and accessible to all in the 1970s. ⓕ Groups who had entirely excluded from music revelled in opportunities to create. ⓖ This led to a sense of novelty and empowerment in and beyond the music sphere.
questions.explanation:
ⓒ: 'led to'의 목적어인 specific genres와 병렬 구조를 이루어야 하므로 'reflecting'을 명사구 형태인 'reflected'나 절의 형태로 고쳐야 어색하지 않지만, 문맥상 led to에 걸리는 목적어 역할을 하려면 reflected (동사)가 아니라 reflection (명사) 또는 'it reflected'와 같은 완전한 절이 되어야 합니다. 하지만 가장 자연스러운 수정은 'led to ~ but also reflected ~'와 같이 동사가 병렬되는 것입니다.
ⓔ: 'made it a condition for their music to' 뒤에는 동사원형이 와야 하므로 'to be non-virtuosic'으로 수정해야 합니다.
ⓕ: 그룹이 배제된 것이므로 수동태인 'had been entirely excluded'가 되어야 합니다.

questions.question: [서답형(단답형) 7] 다음 글의 요약문을 완성하고자 한다. 빈칸 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 단어들을 <보기>에서 골라 <조건>에 부합하도록 쓰시오. [3.0점]
questions.passage: The governments of virtually every country on the planet attach great importance to achieving food security and a wide variety of mechanisms have been developed to realize this goal. The first issue governments face in achieving national food security is the problem of insuring that adequate amounts of food are available to the resident population. Some governments have set goals of food self-sufficiency, which means most if not all of the food available in a country comes from the domestic farming system. However, food security does not require food self-sufficiency because countries can import food items not easily produced within the country. Agricultural products are, after all, highly sensitive to climatic, soil and other conditions that tend to vary around the world. Even countries with extremely productive agricultural sectors are not fully self-sufficient in all food items. The United States, for example, depends on imports for its supply of coffee, tea, bananas and other tropical products. In general, the problem of assuring adequate food supplies is solved by relying on both domestic production and imports.
questions.summary_sentence: Governments emphasize food security by ensuring the (A)_________ of sufficient food through (B) _________ production and imports, as food self-sufficiency is not essential. Since agricultural productivity depends on climate and soil conditions, even highly productive countries rely on (C) ________ sources for certain food items.
subjective_conditions: 1. <보기>의 주어진 표현만을 사용하시오.
2. 빈칸에 한 단어만 사용하시오.
3. 중복해서 사용하지 마시오.
4. 필요한 경우 주어진 표현의 형태를 변형하시오. 단 형태를 변형할 때, 다른 단어를 덧붙이지 마시오.
vocabulary_box: nation, foreign, available
questions.explanation:
(A) 'ensuring the (A) of sufficient food'에서 관사 the와 전치사 of 사이에 명사형이 필요하므로 available을 availability로 변형하여 사용합니다.
(B) 'domestic production and imports'의 지문 내용을 요약문에서 'production and imports'로 표현하고 있으므로 domestic과 동의어인 national(nation의 형용사형)을 사용합니다.
(C) 자국에서 생산되지 않는 품목을 해외에서 들여와야 하므로 foreign(외국의/외부의)이 적절합니다.

questions.question: [서답형(서술형) 8] 밑줄 친 (A)를 <보기>에 주어진 표현들을 모두 활용하여 <조건>에 부합하도록 쓰시오. [5.0점]
questions.passage: Fans who are inclined to spend a lot of time thinking about what athletes owe them as fans should also think about the corresponding obligations that fans might have as fans. One who thinks only about what they are entitled to receive from their friends without ever giving a moment's thought to what they owe their friends is, to put it mildly, not a very good friend. Similarly, fans who only think about what athletes owe them without ever thinking about what they owe to athletes have failed to take the fan/athlete relationship all that seriously. As in nearly every other area of human life, whatever special rights fans may possess are limited by a corresponding set of obligations, and <u>(A) 어떻게 하면 더 나은 팬이 될 수 있을지 생각하는 팬들은 자신의 의무를 다하고 있는 것이다.</u>
subjective_conditions: 1. <보기>의 주어진 표현만을 모두 사용하시오.
2. 중복해서 사용하지 마시오.
3. 필요한 경우 주어진 표현의 형태를 변형하시오. 단 형태를 변형할 때, 다른 단어를 덧붙이지 마시오.
vocabulary_box: fans / fulfilling / who / of / can be / the bargain / about / thinks / fans / better / how / is / they / their end /
questions.answer: the fan who thinks about how they can be better fans is fulfilling their end of the bargain
questions.explanation: 주어 부분인 '어떻게 하면 더 나은 팬이 될 수 있을지 생각하는 팬들은'은 'the fan who thinks about how they can be better fans'로 영작할 수 있으며, 동사 부분인 '자신의 의무를 다하고 있는 것이다'는 'is fulfilling their end of the bargain'으로 표현할 수 있습니다. <보기>의 단어 중 think를 thinks로, fan을 fans(또는 fan)으로, be를 can be의 구조에 맞게 활용하고 fulfill을 fulfilling으로 변형하여 문장을 완성합니다.

questions.question: [서답형(서술형) 9] 빈칸에 들어갈 한 문장을 <조건>에 부합하도록 완성하시오. [5.0점]
questions.passage:
Research shows that we all engage in "gestural foreshadowing," in which ________________________________________. When we realize we've said something in error and we pause to go back to correct it, for example, we stop gesturing a couple of hundred milliseconds before we stop speaking. Such sequences suggest the startling notion that our hands "know" what were going to say before our conscious minds do, and in fact this is often the case. Gesture can mentally prime a word so that the right term comes to our lips. When people are prevented from gesturing, they talk less fluently; their speech becomes halting because their hands are no longer able to supply them with the next word, and the next. Not being able to gesture has other deleterious effects: without gesture to help our mental processes along, we remember less useful information, we solve problems less well, and we are less able to explain our thinking. Far from tagging along as speech's clumsy companion, gesture represents the leading edge of our thought.
*foreshadowing: 전조
subjective_conditions: 1. <보기>의 주어진 표현만을 사용하시오.
2. <보기>의 주어진 표현을 모두 사용하시오.
3. 중복해서 사용하지 마시오.
4. 필요한 경우 주어진 표현의 형태를 변형하시오. 단, 형태를 변형할 때, 다른 단어를 덧붙이지 마시오.
vocabulary_box: about / anticipate / be / hands / our / say / to / we / what /
questions.answer: our hands anticipate what we are about to say
questions.explanation: 지문은 제스처가 언어보다 앞서서 생각을 표현하고 돕는 역할을 한다는 내용을 다루고 있습니다. 'gestural foreshadowing'의 정의로 빈칸을 채워야 하므로, <보기>의 단어들을 활용하여 '우리의 손이 우리가 말하려는 것을 예측한다'라는 의미의 문장을 구성해야 합니다. 'be about to(막 ~하려고 하다)' 구문을 활용하여 'our hands anticipate what we are about to say'로 완성하는 것이 적절합니다. <조건>에 따라 'be'를 'are'로 변형하여 사용합니다.

questions.question: 1. 다음 글의 제목으로 가장 적절한 것은? [3.4점]
questions.passage: Now let's turn our attention to ourselves, Homo sapiens. How have we managed to survive for so long? Neanderthals existed together with Homo sapiens until about 40,000 years ago, and they were known to be intelligent and physically superior to Homo sapiens. Neanderthals were able to make tools and fire and had strong bodies with well-developed muscles and broad shoulders. Despite these attributes, however, it was Homo sapiens who ultimately survived and thrived. One possible explanation is that our ancestors lived in larger communities that promoted cooperation and the free exchange of knowledge, while Neanderthals tended to live in smaller groups. These social differences may have given Homo sapiens a competitive advantage over Neanderthals, allowing them to adapt to an ever-changing environment.
options: ① Degeneration of Physically Superior Homo sapiens
② The insignificance of Cooperation in Human Evolution
③ Social Cooperation: The Key to Homo Sapiens' Dominance
④ Athletic Strength and Evolution: Why Muscles Matter Most
⑤ Neglected Toolmaking Skills of Ancient Humans and Their Decline
questions.explanation: 이 글은 신체적으로 우월했던 네안데르탈인보다 호모 사피엔스가 생존할 수 있었던 이유가 더 큰 공동체 내에서의 사회적 협력과 지식 교환 덕분이었다는 점을 설명하고 있으므로 제목으로 ③번이 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 신체적으로 우월한 호모 사피엔스의 퇴화
② 인류 진화에서 협력의 무의미함
③ 사회적 협력: 호모 사피엔스 지배의 핵심
④ 운동 능력과 진화: 근육이 가장 중요한 이유
⑤ 고대 인류의 방치된 도구 제작 기술과 그들의 쇠퇴

questions.question: 2. 다음 글의 주제로 가장 적절한 것은? [4.2점]
questions.passage: The rate of speed at which one is traveling will greatly determine the ability to process detail in the environment. In evolutionary terms, human senses are adapted to the speed at which humans move through space under their own power while walking. Our ability to distinguish detail in the environment is therefore ideally suited to movement at speeds of perhaps five miles per hour and under. The fastest users of the street, motorists, therefore have a much more limited ability to process details along the street -- a motorist simply has little time or ability to appreciate design details. On the other hand, pedestrian travel, being much slower, allows for the appreciation of environmental detail. Joggers and bicyclists fall somewhere in between these polar opposites; while they travel faster than pedestrians, their rate of speed is ordinarily much slower than that of the typical motorist.
options: ① how technology is transforming modern transportation
② the advantages of biking over driving in urban settings
③ the impact of social interactions on pedestrian behavior
④ the role of urban planning in enhancing pedestrian safety
⑤ the correlation between travel speed and environmental detail perception
questions.explanation: 이 글은 이동 속도가 빠를수록 주변 환경의 세부 사항을 파악하는 능력이 떨어지고, 속도가 느릴수록 더 잘 파악하게 된다는 점을 설명하고 있습니다. 따라서 이동 속도와 환경 세부 사항 지각 사이의 상관관계인 ⑤번이 주제로 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 기술이 현대 교통수단을 어떻게 변화시키고 있는가
② 도시 환경에서 운전보다 자전거 타기의 장점
③ 사회적 상호작용이 보행자 행동에 미치는 영향
④ 보행자 안전을 강화하는 데 있어 도시 계획의 역할
⑤ 이동 속도와 환경 세부 사항 지각 사이의 상관관계

questions.question:
3. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 어법상 맞는 것을 고르시오.
 [4.4점]
questions.passage: I'll give you another example of how friendliness ①<u>relate</u> to survival. D. Hare and his colleagues designed an experiment with chimpanzees and bonobos. Although the two are genetically similar, they are different in nature. To study their cooperative behavior, Dr. Hare's team set up a device which required two individuals ②<u>pull</u> both ends of a rope at the same time in order to access food on a board. When ③<u>placing</u> with partners that the chimpanzees knew, they were able to work together to get the food. However, when paired with new partners, the chimpanzees usually failed ④<u>getting</u> the food, and when they occasionally succeeded, they did not share the food with their partner. The bonobos, on the other hand, got along much better than the chimpanzees. They solved the problem regardless of which individual they were paired with, and they were also more willing to share the food. This research shows that bonobos have a cooperative and friendly nature. Experts suggest that their nature has helped their species survive. ⑤<u>But for</u> these characteristics, they could have faced extinction.
questions.explanation: ① 주어가 friendliness(단수)이므로 relates가 되어야 함. ② require A to-v 구문이므로 to pull이 적절함. ③ 분사구문에서 주어(they)와의 관계가 수동(놓여졌을 때)이므로 placed가 되어야 함. ④ fail은 to부정사를 목적어로 취하므로 to get이 적절함. ⑤ 'But for + 명사'는 '...이 없었더라면'의 뜻으로 가정법 과거완료(could have faced)와 함께 올바르게 쓰임.

questions.question:
4. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 어법상 맞는 것을 고르시오.
 [4점]
questions.passage: When I arrived at Auntie's place, I was ①<u>shocking</u> to see how thin Nani Tama was. “Look, Nani,” I said. “I'm not taking you anywhere. You could die on me!” Nani looked at me in anger. “You want me to die here in this room? Looking at these four walls? When the whakapapa is not yet finished?” The old man ②<u>was held</u> on tightly to the side of the bed and cried out as he stood up. Every slow, painful step ③<u>hurt</u> him, but he tried to walk. I could not help but ④<u>carrying</u> him to the car, and we set off with Auntie. We traveled all night, mostly in silence, listening to Nani chanting in the darkness. It was strange but wonderful to hear him. Sometimes, he burst into a song that he had taught Auntie. They sang together, ⑤<u>lifted</u> up their voices to send the song flying like a bird through the sky.
questions.explanation: ① 내가 놀라움을 느낀 것이므로 shocked가 되어야 함. ② 노인이 침대 옆을 직접 붙잡은 능동의 상황이므로 held가 되어야 함. ③ hurt는 과거형도 hurt이며 '모든 걸음이 그를 아프게 했다'는 문맥에서 정동사로 올바르게 사용됨. ④ 'cannot help but + 동사원형' 구문이므로 carry가 되어야 함. ⑤ 두 사람이 목소리를 높이며 노래한 것이므로 능동의 분사구문인 lifting이 적절함.

questions.question: 6. 다음 글에서 전체 흐름과 관계 없는 문장을 고르시오. [4.2검]
questions.passage: When we think of leaders, we may think of people such as Abraham Lincoln or Martin Luther King, Jr. ① If you consider the historical importance and far-reaching influence of these individuals, leadership might seem like a noble and high goal. ② But like all of us, these people started out as students, workers, and citizens. ③ They possessed ideas about how some aspect of daily life could be improved on a larger scale. ④ Due to the lack of experience, sufficient networks, adequate leadership skills, societal barriers, and confidence, ordinary people often find it nearly impossible to become pivotal leaders in society. ⑤ Through diligence and experience, they improved upon their ideas by sharing them with others, seeking their opinions and feedback and constantly looking for the best way to accomplish goals for a group. Thus we all have the potential to be leaders at school, in our communities, and at work, regardless of age or experience.
questions.explanation: 이 글의 주제는 '위대한 리더들도 처음에는 우리와 같은 평범한 사람들이었으며, 누구나 리더가 될 수 있는 잠재력을 가지고 있다'는 내용입니다. 1~3번 문장은 리더십이 거창해 보일 수 있지만 위대한 인물들도 평범하게 시작하여 개선 아이디어를 가졌음을 설명합니다. 반면, ④번 문장은 평범한 사람들이 경험 부족이나 사회적 장벽 때문에 리더가 되는 것이 거의 불가능하다는 부정적인 제약을 언급하고 있어, 글 전체의 핵심 주장(누구나 리더가 될 수 있다)과 정반대되는 흐름을 보입니다. ⑤번 문장은 다시 ③번에서 언급한 평범한 사람들이 어떻게 아이디어를 발전시켜 나갔는지를 설명하며 자연스럽게 결론으로 이어집니다.

questions.question: 8. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것을 고르시오. [4.1점]
questions.passage: The mind has parts that are known as the conscious mind and the subconscious mind. The subconscious mind is very fast to act and doesn't deal with emotions. It deals with memories of your ① <u>responses</u> to life, your memories and ② <u>recognition</u>. However, the conscious mind is the one that you have more control over. You think. You can choose whether to carry on a thought or to add emotion to it and this is the part of your mind that lets you down frequently because <u>③ fueled</u> by emotions you make the wrong decisions time and time again. When your ④ <u>judgment</u> is clouded by emotions, this puts in biases and all kinds of other negativities that hold you back. Scared of spiders? Scared of the dark? There are reasons for all of these fears, but they ⑤ <u>cease</u> in the conscious mind. They only become real fears when the subconscious mind records your reactions.
questions.explanation:
이 글은 의식적인 마음(conscious mind)과 잠재의식적인 마음(subconscious mind)의 차이와 공포가 형성되는 과정을 설명하고 있습니다. 필자는 거미나 어둠에 대한 공포가 의식적인 마음에서 '시작되거나 발생하며', 이것이 잠재의식에 기록될 때 진정한 공포가 된다고 설명하고 있습니다. 따라서 '그치다, 중단되다'라는 의미의 ⑤ cease는 문맥상 적절하지 않으며, '시작되다(start / begin)'와 같은 단어로 고쳐야 문맥이 자연스럽습니다.

[오답 분석]
① responses: 잠재의식이 삶에 대한 '반응'의 기억을 다룬다는 표현은 적절합니다.
② recognition: 기억과 '인식'을 다룬다는 표현은 잠재의식의 기능을 설명하기에 적절합니다.
③ fueled: 감정에 의해 '부채질 되는(에너지를 얻는)' 결정이 잘못된 판단으로 이어진다는 흐름상 적절합니다.
④ judgment: 감정에 의해 '판단'이 흐려진다는 표현은 논리적으로 타당합니다.

questions.question: 10. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것을 고르시오. [4.3점]
questions.passage: In our competitive society, many people believe that only the biggest or the strongest can survive and ① <u>thrive</u>. However, I propose an alternative view: kindness is the key to success. Isn't that a ② <u>indifferent</u> thought? We can use the power of our natural kindness to ③ <u>communicate</u> and cooperate with different individuals. We can all benefit from this instead of trying to be better than others. I'd like to end this talk with a message. Think of our society as a bouquet. Just as each flower adds to the beauty when it ④ <u>harmonizes</u> with the others, each person can contribute to a more beautiful world when they cooperate. By being kind and working together, we can truly ⑤ <u>flourish</u>. Thank you for your attention.
questions.explanation:
이 글은 무한 경쟁 사회에서 강자만이 살아남는다는 통념 대신, '친절과 협력'이 성공의 핵심이라는 긍정적인 대안을 제시하고 있습니다. 필자가 제안한 '친절이 성공의 열쇠'라는 생각은 독자들에게 매력적이거나 멋진 생각으로 다가가야 하므로, '무관심한, 냉담한'이라는 의미의 ② indifferent는 문맥상 적절하지 않습니다. 이를 '멋진(wonderful)', '매력적인(appealing)' 또는 '고무적인(inspiring)'과 같은 긍정적인 단어로 바꾸어야 합니다.

[오답 분석]
① thrive: 경쟁 사회에서 강자만이 '번성한다'는 믿음을 설명하므로 적절합니다.
③ communicate: 친절을 통해 타인과 '소통하고' 협력한다는 흐름상 적절합니다.
④ harmonizes: 꽃들이 서로 '조화를 이룰 때' 아름다움이 더해진다는 비유는 협력의 중요성을 잘 나타냅니다.
⑤ flourish: 친절과 협력을 통해 우리 사회가 진정으로 '번창할' 수 있다는 결론으로 적절합니다.

questions.question: 11. (A), (B), (C)의 각 괄호 안에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것을 고르시오. [4.4점]
questions.passage: The tongue was mapped into (A) [ separate / integrate ] areas where certain tastes were registered: sweetness at the tip, sourness on the sides, and bitterness at the back of the mouth. Research in the 1980s and 1990s, however, demonstrated that the “tongue map” explanation of how we taste was, in fact, totally wrong. As it turns out, the map was a misinterpretation and mistranslation of research conducted in Germany at the turn of the twentieth century. Today, leading taste researchers believe that taste buds are not grouped according to (B) [ specialty / conformity ]. Sweetness, saltiness, bitterness, and sourness can be tasted everywhere in the mouth, although they may be perceived at a little different intensities at different sites. Moreover, the (C) [ mechanism / fragmentation ] at work is not place, but time. It’s not that you register that perception first.
options: ① separate - conformity - fragmentation
② separate - specialty - mechanism
③ separate - specialty - fragmentation
④ integrate - conformity - mechanism
⑤ integrate - specialty - fragmentation
questions.explanation: (A) 혀 지도가 특정 맛이 등록되는 구역으로 나뉘어 있다고 여겨졌으므로 '분리된(separate)'이 적절합니다. (B) 미뢰가 특정 맛 전담 구역인 '전문성(specialty)'에 따라 분류되지 않는다는 내용이 와야 합니다. (C) 맛을 지각하는 '기제(mechanism)'가 장소가 아니라 시간이라는 설명이 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 분리된 - 일치 - 파편화
② 분리된 - 전문성 - 기제
③ 분리된 - 전문성 - 파편화
④ 통합된 - 일치 - 기제
⑤ 통합된 - 전문성 - 파편화

questions.question: 12. (A), (B), (C)의 각 괄호 안에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것을 고르시오. [4.4점]
questions.passage: Assuming gene editing in humans proves to be safe and effective it might seem logical, even preferable, to correct disease-causing mutations at the earliest possible stage of life. Before (A) [ hilarious / harmful ] genes begin causing serious problems, Yet once it becomes possible to transform an embryo’s mutated genes into “normal” ones, there will certainly be temptations to (B) [ upgrade / downgrade ] normal genes to superior versions. Should we begin editing genes in unborn children to lower their lifetime risk of heart disease or cancer? What about giving unborn children beneficial features, like greater strength and increased mental abilities, or changing physical characteristics, like eye and hair color? The pursuit for (C) [ imperfection / perfection ] seems almost natural to human nature, but if we allow genetic alterations to upgrade humans, we may not like where we end up.
options: ① harmful - upgrade - imperfection
② hilarious - upgrade - perfection
③ harmful - upgrade - perfection
④ hilarious - downgrade - imperfection
⑤ harmful - downgrade - imperfection
questions.explanation: (A) 질병을 일으키는 유전자는 '해로운(harmful)' 유전자입니다. (B) 정상 유전자를 더 우수한 버전으로 만드는 것은 '업그레이드(upgrade)'하는 것입니다. (C) 인간 본성에 가깝게 느껴지는 추구는 '완벽(perfection)'에 대한 추구입니다.
options_translation: ① 해로운 - 업그레이드 - 불완전함
② 아주 우스광스러운 - 업그레이드 - 완벽함
③ 해로운 - 업그레이드 - 완벽함
④ 아주 우스광스러운 - 다운그레이드 - 불완전함
⑤ 해로운 - 다운그레이드 - 불완전함

questions.question: 13. 다음 글의 내용과 일치하지 않는 것은? [4.5점]
questions.passage: The responsive behavior of dogs also caught the attention of an evolutionary anthropologist, Brian Hare. He conducted an experiment to see how dogs would respond to human gestures compared to wolves, who share the same common ancestor. He placed two cups on the ground with food hidden under only one of them. When he pointed to the cup with the food, the dogs found it easily. The wolves, however, struggled and chose cups at random, paying no attention to his gestures. Dr. Hare concluded that the dogs’ ability to read human gestures allowed them to perform better than the wolves. He explained that dogs, unlike wolves, have developed communicative skills with humans and a sense of friendliness. This explanation sounds reasonable according to several evolutionary biologists. They say that from the common ancestors of these two species, those that acted friendly toward humans evolved into dogs, and those that didn’t became wolves. Furthermore, Dr. Hare suggested that the friendly nature of dogs probably provided them a survival advantage that allowed their population to grow larger than that of wolves.
options: ① An experiment was conducted to find out how dogs react to human gestures compared to wolves.
② The wolves, uninterested in human gestures, struggled and chose cups randomly.
③ It was concluded that the dogs’ ability to read human gestures enabled them to perform better than wolves.
④ Dogs have developed communication skills and a sense of closeness with humans, consistent with wolves.
⑤ It was suggested that the friendly nature of dogs probably provided them with a survival advantage.
questions.explanation: 지문에서 개는 늑대와 달리(unlike wolves) 인간과의 의사소통 기술과 친밀감을 발달시켰다고 설명하므로, 늑대와 일관된다(consistent with wolves)는 4번 설명은 내용과 일치하지 않습니다.
options_translation: ① 늑대와 비교하여 개가 인간의 몸짓에 어떻게 반응하는지 알아내기 위한 실험이 수행되었다.
② 인간의 몸짓에 관심이 없는 늑대들은 고전하며 무작위로 컵을 선택했다.
③ 개의 인간 몸짓 읽기 능력이 늑대보다 더 나은 성과를 낼 수 있게 했다고 결론지어졌다.
④ 개는 늑대와 일관되게 인간과의 의사소통 기술과 친밀감을 발달시켜 왔다.
⑤ 개의 우호적인 성격이 아마도 그들에게 생존 우위를 제공했을 것이라고 제안되었다.

questions.question: 14. 다음 글의 내용과 일치하는 것은? [4.5점]
questions.passage: For some time, my grandfather had been busy writing down the village genealogy, known as the whakapapa. The whakapapa had been in his old house. But then came the night of the fire, which ran through the house and destroyed our past. In only one night everything we knew was gone. Nani Tama, in despair, went to stay with his daughter, my Auntie Hiraina. Trying to find a way out of the ashes of the past, Nani began to write the whakapapa again with his shaky hands. He chanted the names of the ancestors, joining the past to the present once more. The village went quiet and listened to his chanting. His voice traveled along the lines of our genealogy, searching back across the centuries. Sometimes, there were lines that were difficult to remember. Then his voice suddenly stopped in the middle of the chant. The village waited in worried silence until the next name burst out of his mouth. It took Nani Tama almost two years to gather most of the whakapapa, but there were still missing names he needed to fill in. Now, he wanted me to drive him to Murupara to finish his work.
options: ① For a while, my grandfather, in shock, refused to write the genealogy of the village.
② The fire accidentally started by my grandfather ignited at midnight, consuming the house and the past.
③ Unable to find the way from the ashes of the past, my grandfather was frustrated in reality.
④ At times, there were lines that were tough to retain, causing his voice to unexpectedly stop in the middle of the chant.
⑤ To complete his work, my grandfather had to go to Murupara, regardless of his own will.
questions.explanation: 지문에서 'Sometimes, there were lines that were difficult to remember. Then his voice suddenly stopped in the middle of the chant.'라고 언급되었으므로 4번이 일치합니다.
options_translation: ① 한동안 나의 할아버지는 충격을 받아 마을의 족보를 쓰는 것을 거부했다.
② 할아버지에 의해 실수로 시작된 불이 한밤중에 붙어 집과 과거를 집어삼켰다.
③ 과거의 재 속에서 길을 찾지 못한 할아버지는 현실에서 좌절했다.
④ 때때로 기억하기 힘든 구절들이 있었고, 그것은 그의 목소리가 노래 도중에 예기치 않게 멈추게 만들었다.
⑤ 그의 작업을 완료하기 위해, 할아버지는 자신의 의지와 상관없이 Murupara로 가야만 했다.

questions.question: 15. 다음 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 적절하지 않은 것은? [4.3점]
questions.passage: Crop rotation is the process in which farmers change the crops they grow in their fields in a special order. For example, if a farmer has three fields, he or she may grow carrots in the first field, green beans in the second, and tomatoes in the third. The next year, green beans will be in the first field, tomatoes in the second field, and carrots will be in the third. In year three, the crops will rotate again. By the fourth year, the crops will go back to their original order. Each crop enriches the soil for the next crop. This type of farming is sustainable ____________________.
options: ① as the soil is consistently barren.
② because the soil maintains its vitality.
③ thanks to the soil's persistent fertility.
④ since the soil remains rich in nutrients.
⑤ owing to the ongoing fertility of the soil.
questions.explanation: 윤작(crop rotation)이 지속 가능한 이유는 토양을 비옥하게(enrich) 유지하기 때문입니다. 1번의 'barren'은 '척박한, 불모의'라는 뜻이므로 문맥상 적절하지 않습니다.
options_translation: ① 토양이 지속적으로 척박하기 때문에.
② 토양이 활력을 유지하기 때문에.
③ 토양의 지속적인 비옥함 덕분에.
④ 토양이 풍부한 영양분을 유지하기 때문에.
⑤ 토양의 계속되는 비옥함 덕분에.

questions.question: 17. [4점] 다음 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것을 고르시오.
questions.passage:
Working around the whole painting, rather than concentrating on one area at a time, will mean you can stop at any point and the painting can be considered "finished." Artists often find it difficult to know when to stop painting, and it can be tempting to keep on adding more to your work. It is important to take a few steps back from the painting from time to time to assess your progress. Putting too much into a painting can spoil its impact and leave it looking overworked. If you find yourself struggling to decide whether you have finished, take a break, and come back to it later with fresh eyes. Then you can decide ____________________.
Ultimately, upon the completion of all these tasks, you will strategically pause at the appropriate moment to bring the work to its final form, which represents the completed painting.
options: ① to sell it immediately without considering any changes.
② it could be crafted into a sculpture instead of remaining as a painting.
③ to invite critiques from as many people as possible before finalizing.
④ whether any parts of your painting could benefit from additional refinement.
⑤ to explore various techniques, other than artistic techniques, and their effects on treating psychological issues.
questions.explanation: 작업 중 잠시 멈추고 새로운 눈으로 돌아와서 결정해야 하는 것은 그림이 완성되었는지 혹은 추가적인 수정이 필요한지 여부입니다. 따라서 4번이 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 어떠한 변화도 고려하지 않고 즉시 그것을 팔기로
② 그것이 그림으로 남는 대신 조각으로 만들어질 수 있을지
③ 최종 마무리 전에 가능한 많은 사람들에게 비평을 요청하기로
④ 그림의 어떤 부분에 추가적인 보완이 도움이 될 수 있을지 여부
⑤ 예술적 기술 외에 심리적 문제를 다루는 데 있어 다양한 기술과 그 효과를 탐구하기로

questions.question: 18.다음 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것을 고르시오.
questions.passage: Improving your gestural communication involves more than just knowing when to nod or shake hands. It's about using gestures to complement your spoken messages, adding layers of meaning to your words. Open-handed gestures, for example, can indicate honesty, creating an atmosphere of trust. You invite openness and collaboration when you speak with your palms facing up. This simple yet powerful gesture can make others feel more comfortable and willing to engage in conversation. But be careful of the trap of over-gesturing. Too many hand movements can distract from your message, drawing attention away from your words. Imagine a speaker whose hands move quickly like birds, their message lost in the chaos of their gestures. Balance is key. Your gestures should ____________________ not overshadow them.
options: ① highlight your words
② be used in the chaos
③ represent body language
④ be used more powerfully
⑤ differentiate between comfort and discomfort
questions.explanation: 이 글은 몸짓 의사소통이 언어적 메시지를 보완하고 의미의 층을 더해야 한다고 설명하고 있습니다. 너무 과한 몸짓은 메시지를 방해할 수 있으므로, 몸짓은 말을 가리는(overshadow) 것이 아니라 말을 돋보이게(highlight) 해야 한다는 흐름이 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 당신의 말을 강조해야(한다)
② 혼란 속에서 사용되어야(한다)
③ 바디 랭귀지를 나타내야(한다)
④ 더 강력하게 사용되어야(한다)
⑤ 편안함과 불편함을 구분해야(한다)

questions.question: 19. 다음 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것을 고르시오. [4.9점]
questions.passage: In many sports, people realized ____________________ participating fully in many adult sport environments. They found the road to success for young children is unlikely if they play on adult fields, courts or arenas with equipment that is too large, too heavy or too fast for them to handle while trying to compete in adult-style competition. Common sense has prevailed: different sports have made adaptations for children. As examples, baseball has T ball, football has flag football and junior soccer uses a smaller and lighter ball and (sometimes) a smaller field. All have junior competitive structures where children play for shorter time periods and often in smaller teams. In a similar way, tennis has adapted the court areas, balls and rackets to make them more appropriate for children under 10. The adaptations are progressive and relate to the age of the child.
options: ① the cultural significance of traditional sports
② the legal regulations governing professional sports
③ the financial benefits of adult leagues for children
④ the historical evolution of adult sports competitions
⑤ the difficulties and even impossibilities of young children
questions.explanation: 이 글은 어린아이들이 성인용 경기장이나 장비를 사용할 때 겪는 어려움 때문에 다양한 스포츠에서 아동용으로 변형(adaptations)을 가하고 있다는 내용입니다. 따라서 빈칸에는 아이들이 성인 환경에 완전히 참여하는 것이 어렵거나 불가능하다는 것을 깨달았다는 내용이 들어가는 것이 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 전통 스포츠의 문화적 중요성
② 프로 스포츠를 규제하는 법적 규정
③ 아이들을 위한 성인 리그의 경제적 혜택
④ 성인 스포츠 경기의 역사적 진화
⑤ 어린 아이들의 어려움 그리고 심지어 불가능함

questions.question:
21. 주어진 글 다음에 이어질 글의 순서로 가장 적절한 것은? [3.4점]

A number of research studies have shown how experts in a field often experience difficulties when introducing newcomers to that field.
questions.passage: A number of research studies have shown how experts in a field often experience difficulties when introducing newcomers to that field.
ordered_passages: (A) Furthermore, Her participants even underestimated how long it had taken themselves to acquire that skill in an earlier session.

(B) Therefore, Knowing that experts forget how hard it was for them to learn, we can understand the need to look at the learning process through students' eyes, rather than making assumptions about how students <u>'should be'</u> learning.

(C) For example, in a genuine training situation, Dr Pamela Hinds found that people expert in using mobile phones were remarkably less accurate than novice phone users in judging how long it takes people to learn to use the phones.

(D) Experts can become insensitive to how hard a task is for the beginner, an effect referred to as the 'curse of knowledge'. Dr Hinds was able to show that as people acquired the skill, they then began to underestimate the level of difficulty of that skill.
questions.explanation: 주어진 글은 전문가가 초보자를 가르칠 때 겪는 어려움에 대해 언급합니다. (C)에서 Pamela Hinds 박사의 연구 사례를 'For example'로 시작하여 구체적인 실험 내용을 제시합니다. (D)에서 실험 결과인 '지식의 저주' 현상과 기술 습득 후 난이도를 과소평가한다는 점을 설명합니다. (A)에서 'Furthermore'를 통해 자기 자신이 기술을 배우는 데 걸렸던 시간도 과소평가했다는 추가 결과를 제시합니다. 마지막으로 (B)에서 'Therefore'를 사용하여 이러한 사실을 통해 학생의 눈으로 학습 과정을 바라봐야 한다는 결론을 도출합니다.

questions.question: 22. [3.9점] 글의 흐름으로 보아, 주어진 문장이 들어가기에 가장 적절한 곳을 고르시오.
questions.passage: It's good to see you, everyone! I'm Dr. Edward Wilson, an evolutionary biologist. Thank you for inviting me here today. ( ① ) On my way, I had trouble locating this room. ( ② ) Luckily, a friendly student came up to me and walked me here. ( ③ ) Now, this raises some interesting questions: where does our friendliness come from, and why is it important? ( ④ ) To answer these questions, I'd like to tell you about my childhood companion dog, Sparky. ( ⑤ ) When we played with a ball, I noticed that he responded well to my gestures.
questions.insertion_sentence: It's fascinating how, in situations like this, we want to help someone in need.
questions.explanation: 주어진 문장은 '이와 같은 상황에서 어려움에 처한 누군가를 돕고 싶어 한다는 점이 흥미롭다'는 내용이다. ②번 뒤 문장에서 학생이 길을 잃은 화자를 도와준 구체적인 '상황'이 언급되었고, ③번 뒤 문장에서 '이것(this)'이 질문을 불러일으킨다고 했으므로, 주어진 문장은 ③번에 들어가는 것이 가장 적절하다.

questions.question: 24. 다음 글의 내용을 요약하고자 한다. 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은? [4.9점]
questions.passage: One of the most striking characteristics of a sleeping animal or person is that they do not respond normally to environmental stimuli. If you open the eyelids of a sleeping mammal the eyes will not see normally - they are functionally blind. Some visual information apparently gets in, but it is not normally processed as it is shortened or weakened; same with the other sensing systems. Stimuli are registered but not processed normally and they fail to wake the individual. Perceptual disengagement probably serves the <u>function of protecting sleep</u>, so some authors do not count it <u>as part of the definition of sleep itself</u>. But as sleep would be impossible without it, it seems essential to its definition. Nevertheless, many animals (including humans) use the intermediate state of drowsiness to derive some benefits of sleep without total perceptual disengagement.
questions.summary_sentence: Sleeping animals and humans exhibit reduced responses to stimuli, remaining functionally blind, which protects sleep and seems (A) _________ to its definition, while they can derive some benefits of sleep from drowsiness (B) _________ full perceptual.
options: ① abstract ...... rehabilitation
② integral ...... detachment
③ temporary ...... interaction
④ irrational ...... reconciliation
⑤ unpredictable ...... integration
questions.explanation: 본문에서 지각적 이탈(perceptual disengagement)은 잠의 정의에 필수적(essential)이라고 했으므로 (A)에는 integral(필수적인)이 적절하다. 또한 마지막 문장에서 완전한 지각적 이탈 없이 졸음 상태에서도 잠의 이점을 얻을 수 있다고 했으므로, (B)에는 detachment(분리, 이탈)가 들어가는 것이 적절하다. (full perceptual detachment = total perceptual disengagement)
options_translation: ① 추상적인 ...... 복구
② 필수적인 ...... 분리
③ 일시적인 ...... 상호작용
④ 비이성적인 ...... 화해
⑤ 예측 불가능한 ...... 통합

questions.question: 10. [4.3점] 다음 글의 주제로 가장 적절한 것을 고르시오.
questions.passage: The explosion of popular music in the second half of the twentieth century as well as the global circulation and dissemination of music by the creative industries propelled a new understanding of accessibility in relation to music. Suddenly, in the 1950s, anyone could pick up spoons, a couple of pans, a second-hand guitar and start a band. This led to specific genres such as skiffle, but also, more generally, reflected a much more relaxed and inclusive attitude to music making. While ordinary people had always sung and made music, the popular music movement was driven by a spirit of rebellion and freedom. This approach led to the punk movement, whose musicians even made it a condition for their music to be non-virtuosic and accessible to all in the 1970s. Groups who had been entirely excluded from music revelled in opportunities to create. This led to a sense of novelty and empowerment in and beyond the music sphere.
options: ① increased accessibility of music-making due to the rise of popular music
② restriction of music production and performance to trained musicians
③ influence of Western classical composers on punk and skiffle music
④ decline of global music interest due to explosion of music in 1950s
⑤ popularity of mainstream music limiting personal musical creativity
questions.explanation: 20세기 후반 대중음악의 폭발적 성장이 음악 제작에 대한 접근성을 높이고, 비전문가들도 음악 창작에 참여할 수 있는 포용적인 문화를 만들었다는 내용이므로, ① '대중음악의 부상으로 인한 음악 제작 접근성의 증가'가 주제로 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 대중음악의 부상으로 인한 음악 제작의 접근성 증가
② 훈련된 음악가들에게만 한정된 음악 제작 및 공연의 제한
③ 서양 고전 작곡가들이 펑크와 스키플 음악에 미친 영향
④ 1950년대 음악의 폭발로 인한 글로벌 음악 관심의 하락
⑤ 개인의 음악적 창의성을 제한하는 주류 음악의 인기

questions.question: 19. 주어진 글 다음에 이어질 글의 순서로 가장 적절한 것을 고르시오. [4.1점]
questions.passage: When we realize we've said something in error and we pause to go back to correct it, we stop gesturing a couple of hundred milliseconds before we stop speaking.
ordered_passages: (A) When people are prevented from gesturing, they talk less fluently; their speech becomes halting because their hands are no longer able to supply them with the next word, and the next.

(B) Not being able to gesture has other deleterious effects: without gesture to help our mental processes along, we remember less useful information, we solve problems less well, and we are less able to explain our thinking. Far from tagging along as speech's clumsy companion, gesture represents the leading edge of our thought.

(C) Such sequences suggest the startling notion that our hands "know" what we're going to say before our conscious minds do, and in fact this is often the case. Gesture can mentally prime a word so that the right term comes to our lips.
questions.explanation: 주어진 글에서 말하기 전에 제스처가 먼저 멈춘다는 사실을 언급한다. (C)에서 이러한 순서(Such sequences)가 손이 뇌보다 먼저 안다는 것을 암시하며 제스처가 단어를 준비시킨다고 설명한다. (A)에서는 제스처를 못 하게 하면 말이 덜 유창해진다는 부작용을 언급하고, (B)에서 '다른 해로운 효과(other deleterious effects)'를 추가로 나열하며 제스처가 사고의 첨단임을 강조하며 마무리한다.

questions.question: 20. (A), (B), (C)의 각 괄호 중 문맥상 알맞은 표현으로 가장 적절한 것은? [4점]
questions.passage: The concept of ecosystem states should be familiar to anyone with a home vegetable garden. The garden is a small ecosystem that the grower attempts to keep in a specific state, namely the maximization of fruit and vegetable production. To achieve this, the grower is almost always (A) [ controlling / ignoring ] the dynamics of the ecosystem; they remove unwanted plants that begin to grow and perhaps spray insecticides and fence off the patch to stop insects and other animals from consuming the vegetables. Since maximizing vegetable growth is an inherently (B) [ stable / unstable ] state for the ecosystem, the grower is effectively keeping the ball on a slope. If the grower stops getting involved, even for a day, the ecosystem, that small patch of ground, will naturally begin to shift to a more stable state. Vegetables may still grow, but yield will almost certainly be (C) [ higher / lower ] as other plants crowd out the vegetables and wildlife consume the produce.
options: ① ignoring - stable - higher
② ignoring - stable - lower
③ controlling - unstable - lower
④ controlling - unstable - higher
⑤ controlling - stable - higher
questions.explanation: (A) 정원사가 잡초를 뽑고 살충제를 뿌리는 행위는 생태계의 역동성을 '통제(controlling)'하는 것이다. (B) 채소 성장을 극대화하는 것은 생태계 입장에서 자연스럽지 않으므로 '불안정한(unstable)' 상태이며, 이는 공을 비탈길 위에 두는 것과 같다고 비유된다. (C) 인간의 개입이 멈추면 다른 식물들이 채소를 밀어내므로 수확량은 '더 낮아질(lower)' 것이다.
options_translation: ① 무시하는 - 안정적인 - 더 높은
② 무시하는 - 안정적인 - 더 낮은
③ 통제하는 - 불안정한 - 더 낮은
④ 통제하는 - 불안정한 - 더 높은
⑤ 통제하는 - 안정적인 - 더 높은

questions.question: 1. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 어법상 어색한 것은? [3.7점]
questions.passage: Welcome to a new season of High School Magazine. To start off the new school year on the right foot, we asked some of our recent graduates ① <u>to give us tips</u> on how to succeed in the coming year and beyond. In high school, everyone told me ② <u>how talented an artist I was,</u> so I dreamed of becoming an illustrator. In university, though, everyone seemed much more talented than me, and they all worked so hard ③ <u>which</u> I felt small in comparison. I thought about giving up my dream of ④ <u>becoming</u> an artist. Then one day, I happened to see a drawing ⑤ <u>that</u> I had won an award for from middle school on the kitchen wall. I was embarrassed because it wasn't very good.
questions.explanation: ③번 문장은 'so + 형용사/부사 + that 절' 구문이 필요한 자리입니다. 앞에 worked so hard가 있으므로 관계대명사 which가 아닌 접속사 that이 와서 결과를 나타내는 부사절을 이끌어야 적절합니다.

questions.question: 2. 다음 글의 내용을 한 문장으로 요약하고자 한다. 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은? [3.4점]
questions.passage: People say you shouldn't compare apples to oranges, and they're right. That's why it doesn't make sense to compare yourself to Internet personalities or even people in your real life. Maybe they had an advantage, or even a disadvantage, that you didn't. If you are going to compare yourself to anyone, the only fair comparison is "yesterday-you." Only you know where you started and how much effort you've put in. I couldn't see the progress in my ability when I only compared myself to others. Everyone develops differently. I'm able to see now the drawing in the kitchen was full of mistakes that I no longer make. It is empowering to see how I have improved rather than to envy the success of others. Your competition isn't the person next door or the influencer on social media: it's you.
questions.summary_sentence: Compare (A) _________ to who you were yesterday and focus on your own (B) _________ .
options: ① yourself ...... growth
② influencer ...... effort
③ others ...... change
④ yourself ...... mistakes
⑤ influencer ...... performance
questions.explanation: 지문의 핵심 내용은 타인과 자신을 비교하지 말고 어제의 자신과 오늘의 자신을 비교하라는 것입니다. 따라서 (A)에는 자신(yourself)을 어제의 모습과 비교하라는 내용이 들어가야 하며, (B)에는 타인을 부러워하기보다 자신의 향상(improved)된 모습, 즉 성장(growth)에 집중하라는 내용이 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 당신 자신 ...... 성장
② 인플루언서 ...... 노력
③ 타인 ...... 변화
④ 당신 자신 ...... 실수
⑤ 인플루언서 ...... 성과

questions.question: 3. 윗글의 제목으로 가장 적절한 것은? [3.3점]
questions.passage: Do you share your opinion in class discussions, or do you just (a) <u>remain</u> silent and keep it to yourself? Like many of you, I often found myself in the second group. A little black hole inside of me (b) <u>swallowed</u> my voice when I considered speaking up. The consequences of being ridiculed or being wrong were always on my mind. Then, after a particularly heated conversation in class, I asked myself, "What am I afraid of?" I was scared that bad things would happen, but I never thought about good things. When I noticed others taking risks, I knew that I needed to do the same in order to (c) <u>take part</u>. Many people are scared to speak up, but a lot of them do it anyway because they think it's (d) <u>worth</u> it. So I left my comfort zone and started to speak up. I grew intellectually and socially by expressing myself more (e) <u>vaguely</u>. I got closer to friends who liked how open I was with them. Now I have more people with whom I can talk, share my ideas, and learn new things. Remember, taking the risk of expressing yourself can be extremely rewarding in unexpected ways.
options: ① The Powers of Speaking up
② Why Silence Can Be Smart
③ The Dangers of Being Honest
④ How to Win All The Arguments
⑤ The Risk of Speaking Your Mind
questions.explanation: 글의 전반적인 내용은 침묵을 지키던 화자가 용기를 내어 자신의 의견을 말하기 시작하면서 지적, 사회적으로 성장했다는 내용을 담고 있습니다. 따라서 '말하기의 힘' 혹은 '의견을 말하는 것의 긍정적 효과'를 의미하는 ①번이 가장 적절한 제목입니다.
options_translation: ① 목소리를 내는 것의 힘
② 침묵이 영리할 수 있는 이유
③ 정직해지는 것의 위험성
④ 모든 논쟁에서 이기는 방법
⑤ 당신의 생각을 말하는 것의 위험

questions.question: 4. 윗글의 밑줄 친 (a)~(e) 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은? [3.7점]
questions.passage: Do you share your opinion in class discussions, or do you just (a) <u>remain</u> silent and keep it to yourself? Like many of you, I often found myself in the second group. A little black hole inside of me (b) <u>swallowed</u> my voice when I considered speaking up. The consequences of being ridiculed or being wrong were always on my mind. Then, after a particularly heated conversation in class, I asked myself, "What am I afraid of?" I was scared that bad things would happen, but I never thought about good things. When I noticed others taking risks, I knew that I needed to do the same in order to (c) <u>take part</u>. Many people are scared to speak up, but a lot of them do it anyway because they think it's (d) <u>worth</u> it. So I left my comfort zone and started to speak up. I grew intellectually and socially by expressing myself more (e) <u>vaguely</u>. I got closer to friends who liked how open I was with them. Now I have more people with whom I can talk, share my ideas, and learn new things. Remember, taking the risk of expressing yourself can be extremely rewarding in unexpected ways.
options: ① (a)
② (b)

questions.explanation: (e) 화자는 자신을 더 개방적으로(open) 드러냄으로써 성장했다고 했으므로, 'vaguely(모호하게)'가 아니라 'openly(공공연하게)' 혹은 'clearly(명확하게)' 같은 단어가 문맥상 적절합니다.

questions.question: 5. 주어진 글 (A)에 이어질 내용을 순서에 맞게 배열한 것으로 가장 적절한 것은? [3.5점]
questions.passage: As I worked through my second year into my third in college, I had more difficulties (a) <u>balance</u> school and personal life. I would get excited, anxious, worried, and bored all at once and then separately. I would get exhausted when I had to write a report for my courses, mediate a disaster between friends, and respond to the comments on my online journal.
ordered_passages: (B) By wasting less energy on my circle of concern, I was able to invest more energy into things that mattered. I no longer worry about what my friends think, and I focus on my own actions. I don't get anxious over what might be on the test, and instead I put in every effort to understand the concepts (b) <u>itself</u>. Now, I only put my mental and physical energy into my circle of influence: eating healthy, staying in shape, and working hard.

(C) I was drowning in a sea of responsibilities, concerns, and anxieties, and that was when I read an article with a simple insight. The article advised me to draw two big circles, with myself in the center. The smaller circle is my circle of influence, and I have direct control over the things inside it: what I eat and drink, (c) <u>the way</u> I behave, or what I do after school.

(D) The bigger circle (d) <u>called</u> my circle of concern: things I worry about but have no direct control over. For example, I have no direct control over how my professor will react to my report, but I do have control over the amount of research I do for it. Believing that everything (e) <u>were</u> in my circle of influence left me stressed out and constantly exhausted.
questions.explanation: (A)에서 여러 가지 일로 지친 상황을 설명하고, (C)에서 이를 해결해 준 기사를 만난 시점을 언급하며 두 개의 원 중 작은 원(영향력의 원)을 소개합니다. (D)에서는 큰 원(관심의 원)을 설명하며 모든 것을 영향력의 원 안에 있다고 믿는 것이 스트레스의 원인임을 밝힙니다. 마지막으로 (B)에서 관심의 원에 에너지를 덜 씀으로써 중요한 일에 더 집중하게 되었다는 결과로 마무리되는 것이 가장 자연스럽습니다.

questions.question: 6. 윗글의 밑줄 친 (a)~(e) 중, 어법상 옳은 것은? [4.2점]
questions.passage:
(A)
As I worked through my second year into my third in college, I had more difficulties (a) <u>balance</u> school and personal life. I would get excited, anxious, worried, and bored all at once and then separately. I would get exhausted when I had to write a report for my courses, mediate a disaster between friends, and respond to the comments on my online journal.

(B)

I don't get anxious over what might be on the test, and instead I put in every effort to understand the concepts (b) <u>itself</u>. Now, I only put my mental and physical energy into my circle of influence: eating healthy, staying in shape, and working hard.

(C)
I was drowning in a sea of responsibilities, concerns, and anxieties, and that was when I read an article with a simple insight. The article advised me to draw two big circles, with myself in the center. The smaller circle is my circle of influence, and I have direct control over the things inside it: what I eat and drink, (c) <u>the way</u> I behave, or what I do after school.

(D)
The bigger circle (d) <u>called</u> my circle of concern: things I worry about but have no direct control over. For example, I have no direct control over how my professor will react to my report, but I do have control over the amount of research I do for it. Believing that everything (e) <u>were</u> in my circle of influence left me stressed out and constantly exhausted.
options: ① (a)
② (b)
③ (c)
④ (d)
⑤ (e)
questions.explanation:
(a) have difficulty (in) -ing 구문이므로 balancing이 되어야 합니다.
(b) concepts가 복수이므로 themselves가 되어야 합니다.
(c) the way 또는 how 중 하나만 쓰거나 the way that/in which를 쓰는 것은 옳습니다. (c)는 단독으로 the way를 썼으므로 어법상 옳습니다.
(d) 문맥상 '큰 원은 ~라고 불린다'는 수동의 의미이므로 is called 또는 called(분사로서 원을 수식할 경우)가 되어야 하지만 문장의 술어 동사 자리가 필요하므로 is called가 적절합니다.
(e) Believing이 주어인 동명사구 내의 that절 주어 everything은 단수 취급하므로 was가 되어야 합니다.
