I was drowning in a sea of responsibilities, concerns, and anxieties, and that was when I read an article with a simple insight. The article advised me to draw two big circles, with myself in the center. The smaller circle is my circle of influence, and I have direct control over the things inside it: what I eat and drink, (c) <u>the way</u> I behave, or what I do after school.

(D)
The bigger circle (d) <u>called</u> my circle of concern: things I worry about but have no direct control over. For example, I have no direct control over how my professor will react to my report, but I do have control over the amount of research I do for it. Believing that everything (e) <u>were</u> in my circle of influence left me stressed out and constantly exhausted.
options: ① The speaker got weary when dealing with so many tasks.
② The speaker felt various emotions simultaneously and separately.
③ The speaker was told by the article to draw two large circles and place herself in the edge.
④ The speaker used less energy on things she couldn't control and focused more on what was important.
⑤ The speaker cannot control the professor's response to the report, but she can control how much research she does.
questions.explanation: (C) 단락에 따르면, 기사는 자신을 원의 가장자리(edge)가 아니라 중심(center)에 두라고 조언했습니다.
options_translation: ① 화자는 너무 많은 일들을 처리할 때 피곤함을 느꼈다.
② 화자는 다양한 감정을 동시에 그리고 따로따로 느꼈다.
③ 화자는 기사로부터 두 개의 큰 원을 그리고 자기 자신을 가장자리에 두라는 말을 들었다.
④ 화자는 통제할 수 없는 일에 에너지를 덜 쓰고 중요한 것에 더 집중했다.
⑤ 화자는 보고서에 대한 교수의 반응을 통제할 수 없지만, 그녀가 하는 연구의 양은 통제할 수 있다.

questions.question: 8. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 어법상 어색한 것은? [3.4점]
questions.passage: You order a nice, juicy hamburger with some fries. What’s next? Of course you (a) <u>have to</u> have ketchup with your fries, right? Well, (b) <u>not</u> for some people. In fact, some people prefer (c) <u>eating</u> fries with mayonnaise, chili sauce, or even steak sauce. (d) <u>Whereas</u> ketchup with fries may seem quite ordinary, other combinations may seem rather odd. Read on to learn about some popular dishes that (e) <u>has</u> flavor combinations that you may not have thought of.
options: ① (a)
② (b)
③ (c)
④ (d)
⑤ (e)
questions.explanation: (e)가 포함된 관계대명사 절의 선행사는 'some popular dishes'로 복수 명사입니다. 따라서 관계대명사 that 뒤의 동사는 단수형 has가 아니라 복수형 have가 되어야 적절합니다.

questions.question: 9. 다음 글의 내용과 일치하지 않은 것은? [3.6점]
questions.passage: Some people love this combination, while others can’t seem to stand it. It can even cause quite heated arguments. If you haven’t guessed already, it’s the tasty or nasty—depending on your taste—ham and pineapple pizza. The man who created this pizza was neither Italian nor Hawaiian. A Greek immigrant from Canada, Sam Panopoulos did not want to stick to the usual ingredients on pizzas, like pepperoni and mushrooms. He spread canned pineapple and sliced ham onto a pizza and called it “the Hawaiian” because that’s which was written on the pineapple can. Little did he know that he had created a classic combination. In Italy, however, most people find pineapple on pizza distasteful.
options: ① Most Italians think pineapple on pizza tasteless.
② The person who made this pizza was not Italian, but Hawaiian.
③ The same pizza may be tasty or nasty depending on your taste.
④ The man sprinkled pineapple and ham on the pizza, which became classic pizza.
⑤ The immigrant named the pizza after the word written on the pineapple can.
questions.explanation: 본문에서 하와이안 피자를 만든 샘 파노풀로스(Sam Panopoulos)는 이탈리아인도 하와이인도 아닌 '캐나다에 거주하는 그리스 이민자(A Greek immigrant from Canada)'라고 설명하고 있으므로 ②번은 틀린 내용입니다.
options_translation: ① 대부분의 이탈리아인들은 피자 위의 파인애플이 맛없다고 생각한다.
② 이 피자를 만든 사람은 이탈리아인이 아니라 하와이인이었다.
③ 같은 피자라도 취향에 따라 맛있거나 형편없을 수 있다.
④ 그 남자는 피자 위에 파인애플과 햄을 뿌렸고, 그것은 고전적인 피자가 되었다.
⑤ 그 이민자는 파인애플 통조림에 적힌 단어를 따서 피자 이름을 지었다.

questions.question: 10. 다음 글에서 전체 흐름과 관계 없는 문장은? [3.8점]
questions.passage: Why is the Hawaiian pizza so divisive? The combination is not that odd. ① Pineapple and ham is not the only fruit and meat pairing in kitchens around the world. ② In France, duck is paired with a sweet orange sauce, and American Thanksgiving turkey dinner would not be complete without cranberry sauce. ③ People often avoid combining sweet fruits with warm dishes because they believe fruits should only be eaten cold or fresh. ④ In Italy, people sometimes add sweet fruits like apples or raisins to meat dishes, enjoying the mix of sweet and salty flavors. ⑤ Many people enjoy salty and sweet flavor combinations, whereas some others prefer to keep those tastes as far from each other as possible.
questions.explanation: 글의 전체적인 흐름은 과일과 고기를 조합하여 먹는 사례들이 전 세계적으로 흔하다는 내용인데, ③번은 과일을 따뜻한 요리와 함께 먹는 것을 피한다는 반대되는 내용을 서술하고 있어 흐름에서 벗어납니다.

questions.question: 11. 다음 글의 제목으로 가장 적절한 것은? [3.4점]
questions.passage: A very popular dessert in Thailand is sweet, sticky rice topped with fresh mango and coconut milk. Mango with sticky rice is a dish that is extremely hard not to love. Rice is one of the world’s most consumed grains, so it should not be surprising that it can be combined with other interesting ingredients. One of those ingredients is fruit, which is nutritious, sweet, and plentiful in many parts of the world. The combination of fruit and rice may seem unusual, but it’s actually quite common.
options: ① Grains and Their Health Benefits
② Uses of Coconut Milk in Desserts
③ Nutritious Fruits Around the World
④ The Global popularity of Rice Dishes
⑤ A Perfect combination: Mango and sticky Rice
questions.explanation: 이 글은 태국의 인기 디저트인 망고 찰밥을 소개하며 과일과 쌀의 조합이 실제로는 꽤 흔하고 훌륭한 조합임을 설명하고 있으므로 ⑤번이 가장 적절한 제목입니다.
options_translation: ① 곡물과 그것의 건강상 이점
② 디저트에서 코코넛 밀크의 용도
③ 전 세계의 영양가 있는 과일들
④ 쌀 요리의 세계적 인기
⑤ 완벽한 조합: 망고와 찰밥

questions.question: 12. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은? [3.5점]
questions.passage: What kind of snack is nutritious, full of energy, and simple to make? This is the ① <u>genius</u> of peanut butter and banana sandwiches. No one could have predicted that the sweet taste of bananas ② <u>coupled</u> with salty, nutty peanut butter would become an American comfort food. This sandwich can be a ③ <u>healthy</u> choice for breakfast or lunch because its combination of protein and fiber helps you feel full, while the carbohydrates provide sustained energy. The best thing about this sandwich is that the ingredients are readily available and ④ <u>affordable</u>. Some people, however, like to take things to another level. Imagine a regular peanut butter and banana sandwich, and then add fried bacon to it. It has been said that the famous singer Elvis Presley loved this sandwich, which is why it’s called, “The Elvis.” Even though you may not want to eat the Elvis every day, there are many fans of this ⑤ <u>conventional</u> combination.
questions.explanation: 문맥상 베이컨을 추가한 'The Elvis' 샌드위치는 일반적인 조합이 아니라 특이하거나 독특한 조합이므로 'conventional(전통적인, 관습적인)'보다는 'unconventional' 또는 'unique'와 같은 낱말이 적절합니다.

questions.question: 13. 다음 글의 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 어법상 가장 적절한 것은? [3.5점]
questions.passage: The world is a big place, and everyone should eat. Eating the same thing every day can get quite (A)[boring / bored]. Sometimes all you need is to combine some ingredients in novel ways to create a new flavor. But if you think it’s odd, it’s probably (B)[because of / because] you haven’t tried it before. Considering how diverse the world is, there are probably more food combinations that seem odd than seem “normal”. Maybe odd is just something you haven’t experienced yet. They are just new experiences waiting for you (C)[discovering / to discover].
options: ① boring ........ because ........ to discover
② boring ........ because of ........ discovering
③ boring ........ because of ........ to discover
④ bored ........ because ........ to discover
⑤ bored ........ because ........ discovering
questions.explanation: (A) 주어인 Eating the same thing이 지루함을 유발하므로 현재분사 boring이 적절합니다. (B) 뒤에 주어(you)와 동사(haven't tried)를 갖춘 절이 오므로 접속사 because가 적절합니다. (C) waiting for you (의미상 주어) 뒤에 experiences를 수식하거나 목적을 나타내는 형용사적 용법의 to 부정사인 to discover가 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 지루하게 하는 ........ ~때문에 ........ 발견하기 위해/발견할
② 지루하게 하는 ........ ~때문에(전치사) ........ 발견하는 것
③ 지루하게 하는 ........ ~때문에(전치사) ........ 발견하기 위해/발견할
④ 지루함을 느끼는 ........ ~때문에 ........ 발견하기 위해/발견할
⑤ 지루함을 느끼는 ........ ~때문에 ........ 발견하는 것

questions.question: 14. 다음 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것을 고르시오. [3.6점]
questions.passage: According to the Tourism Authority of Thailand, neither mango nor sticky rice is native to Thailand. Mangoes are native to Myanmar and India, and sticky rice is commonly eaten in Laos, which shares a border with Thailand. This suggests that the roots of the dish are probably a result of the mixing of cultures in Southeast Asia. Rice is usually thought of a food ___________________________ but its use as a dessert shows how simple ingredients can create innovative, wonderful treats.
options: ① that is consumed as a meal
② which is eaten as a substitute for sticky rice
③ that is consumed as a special celebratory food
④ which is eaten as the best dessert for the holidays
⑤ which is eaten only in combination with tropical fruits
questions.explanation: 글의 흐름상 쌀이 보통 '식사(meal)'로 여겨지지만, 디저트로 사용됨으로써 혁신적인 간식이 될 수 있음을 보여준다는 내용이 자연스럽습니다.
options_translation: ① 식사로 소비되는
② 찰밥의 대체물로 먹히는
③ 특별한 축하 음식으로 소비되는
④ 휴일을 위한 최고의 디저트로 먹히는
⑤ 열대 과일과 조합해서만 먹히는

questions.question: 18. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 어법상 어색한 것은? [3.8점]
questions.passage: Assuming gene editing in humans (a) <u>proves</u> to be safe and effective, it might seem logical, even preferable, to correct disease-causing mutations at the earliest possible stage of life, before harmful genes begin causing serious problems. Yet once it becomes possible (b) <u>transform</u> an embryo’s mutated genes into “normal” ones, there will certainly be temptations to upgrade normal genes to superior versions. Should we begin (c) <u>editing</u> genes in unborn children to lower their lifetime risk of heart disease or cancer? What about (d) <u>giving</u> unborn children beneficial features, like greater strength and increased mental abilities, or changing physical characteristics, like eye and hair color? The pursuit for perfection seems almost (e) <u>natural</u> to human nature, but if we start down this slippery slope, we may not like where we end up.
options: ① (a)
② (b)
③ (c)
④ (d)
⑤ (e)
questions.explanation: (b)가 포함된 문장에서 'it'은 가주어이며, 뒤에 진주어가 와야 합니다. 동사 transform은 명사적 용법으로 쓰이기 위해 to부정사인 'to transform'으로 바뀌어야 문법적으로 적절합니다.

questions.question: 19. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은? [3.7점]
questions.passage: Our skin conducts electricity more or less efficiently, depending on our emotions. We know that when we're emotionally ① <u>stimulated</u> — stressed, sad, any intense emotion, really — our bodies sweat a tiny bit, so little we might not even notice. And when those tiny drops of sweat appear, our skin gets more ② <u>electrically</u> conductive. This change in sweat gland activity happens completely without your conscious mind having much say in the matter. If you feel emotionally ③ <u>intense</u>, you're going to notice an increase in sweat gland activity. This is particularly useful from a scientific viewpoint, because it allows us to put an ④ <u>objective</u> value on a subjective state of mind. We can actually measure your emotional state by tracking how your body ⑤ <u>consciously</u> sweats, by running a bit of electricity through your skin. We can then turn the subjective, subconscious experience of emotional intensity into an objective number by figuring out how good your skin gets at transferring an electrical current.
questions.explanation: 지문에서 땀샘 활동의 변화는 의식적인 마음의 간섭 없이(without your conscious mind having much say) 일어난다고 설명하고 있으며, 마지막 문장에서도 'subconscious experience(잠재의식적 경험)'라고 언급하고 있습니다. 따라서 신체가 '의식적으로(consciously)' 땀을 흘리는 것이 아니라 '무의식적으로(subconsciously/automatically)' 흘린다고 하는 것이 문맥상 적절합니다.

questions.question: 20.[4.1점] 다음 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것을 고르시오.
questions.passage:
Some researchers believe that numbers are the most neutral and accurate way to describe the world. However, turning human lives into numbers doesn't necessarily lead to better understanding. Numbers, while useful in certain areas like census-taking or income analysis, often remove valuable information. For example, students' futures can depend on test scores, but these numbers don't reflect their learning environments, support systems, or emotional state like test anxiety. Moreover, statistics can emotionally distance us from real human suffering. Numbers about crime, homelessness, or disease tell us nothing about people's pain. We see them as distant facts and feel less disturbed. In the end,
statistics are people "with the tears wiped off." Quantify with caution. In short, we must remember that numbers, despite their usefulness, can sometimes _________
options: ① reveal deeper meanings through logical analysis
② replace the need for moral and social awareness
③ help us solve emotional problems more effectively
④ hide the reality behind people's lives and emotions
⑤ reflect people's suffering more accurately than words
questions.explanation: 지문은 숫자가 세상을 설명하는 중립적인 수단처럼 보일 수 있지만, 실제 인간의 삶과 고통을 담아내지 못하고 감정적으로 소외시킨다는 점을 강조합니다. 따라서 숫자가 '사람들의 삶과 감정 뒤에 숨겨진 현실을 가릴 수 있다'는 내용이 빈칸에 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 논리적 분석을 통해 더 깊은 의미를 드러낼 수 있다
② 도덕적, 사회적 의식의 필요성을 대체할 수 있다
③ 우리가 정서적 문제를 더 효과적으로 해결하도록 도와준다
④ 사람들의 삶과 감정 뒤에 숨겨진 현실을 숨길 수 있다
⑤ 말보다 더 정확하게 사람들의 고통을 반영할 수 있다

questions.question: 22. [4.2점] 다음 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것을 고르시오.
questions.passage: The idea of altering a baby's genes to prevent diseases seems like a remarkable advancement, potentially eliminating the risk of serious illnesses before birth. However, this capability opens the door to questions about how far we should go. While correcting faulty genes is one thing, what if we could enhance a baby's genetic makeup beyond just preventing diseases? Imagine the possibility of modifying a child's DNA to reduce their likelihood of developing heart disease or cancer. Would such interventions be ethically acceptable? Furthermore, what about enhancements that go beyond health, such as increasing physical strength or cognitive abilities? Could we even reach a point where we alter traits like eye or hair color based on preference? The desire to give our children the best possible start in life is natural, but the prospect of genetically engineering "perfect" individuals raises complex ethical questions. If we begin altering genes for enhancement purposes, it becomes difficult to define acceptable limits. This path could lead to unforeseen and potentially undesirable consequences, _________
options: ① blurring the line between medical treatment and genetic enhancement
② creating a perfect society where every individual's traits can be controlled
③ offering an opportunity to solve all the ethical dilemmas related to genetic editing
④ making genetic editing universally accepted as a standard practice for all babies
⑤ ensuring that everyone has equal access to the technology for genetic enhancement
questions.explanation: 질병 예방을 넘어 신체적, 인지적 능력 강화나 외모 선택까지 유전 공학이 확장될 경우, 어디까지가 치료이고 어디서부터가 강화인지 그 경계가 모호해진다는 윤리적 문제를 지적하고 있습니다. 따라서 '의료적 치료와 유전적 강화 사이의 경계를 흐리게 한다'는 내용이 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 의료적 치료와 유전적 강화 사이의 경계를 흐리게 하며
② 모든 개인의 특성이 통제될 수 있는 완벽한 사회를 만들며
③ 유전자 편집과 관련된 모든 윤리적 딜레마를 해결할 기회를 제공하며
④ 유전자 편집을 모든 아기들에게 표준 관행으로 보편적으로 받아들이게 만들며
⑤ 모든 사람이 유전적 강화를 위한 기술에 동등하게 접근할 수 있도록 보장하며

questions.question: 23. 다음 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것을 고르시오.[3.8점]
questions.passage: In the course of trying to solve a problem with an invention, you may encounter a brick wall of resistance when you try to think your way logically through the problem. Such logical thinking is a linear type of process, which uses our reasoning skills. This works fine when we're operating in the area of what we know or have experienced. However, when we need to deal with new information, ideas, and viewpoints, linear thinking will often come up short. On the other hand, creativity by definition involves the application of new information to old problems and the conception of new viewpoints and ideas. For this you will be most effective ____________________; that is, use your creative brain. Stated differently, if you think in a linear manner, you'll tend to be conservative and keep coming up with techniques which are already known. This, of course, is just what you don't want.
options: ① if you improve your illogical skills
② if you try to change linear process
③ if you learn to operate in a nonlinear manner
④ if you learn to the traditional way of thinking
⑤ if you have to deal with conservative thinking rules
questions.explanation: 글의 중반부 이후 창의성(creativity)의 정의를 언급하며 새로운 관점과 아이디어를 위해서는 선형적 사고에서 벗어나야 함을 강조하고 있습니다. 따라서 '비선형적인 방식으로 작동하는 법을 배울 때' 효과적이라는 흐름이 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 만약 당신이 비논리적인 기술을 향상시킨다면
② 만약 당신이 선형적인 과정을 바꾸려 노력한다면
③ 만약 당신이 비선형적인 방식으로 작동하는 법을 배운다면
④ 만약 당신이 전통적인 사고방식을 배운다면
⑤ 만약 당신이 보수적인 사고 규칙을 다루어야 한다면

questions.question: 24. 다음 글에서 전체의 흐름과 관계 없는 문장은? [3.4점]
questions.passage: Plants can communicate, although not in the same way we do. ① Some express their discontent through scents. You know that smell that hangs in the air after you've mowed the lawn? Yeah, that's actually an SOS. Some plants use sound. Yes, sound, though at a frequency that we can't hear. ② Dark green leaves allow plants to get as much energy as possible, but some plants have leaves that are multicolored. ③ Researchers experimented with plants and microphones to see if they could record any trouble calls. They found that plants produce a high-frequency clicking noise when stressed and can make different sounds for different stressors. ④ The sound a plant makes when it's not getting watered differs from the one it'll make when a leaf is cut. However, it's worth noting that experts don't think plants are crying out in pain. ⑤ It's more likely that these reactions are knee-jerk survival actions. Plants are living organisms, and their main objective is to survive. Scents and sounds are their tools for defending against things that might harm them.
questions.explanation: 이 글은 식물이 소리나 냄새를 통해 의사소통을 하거나 생존을 위한 반응을 보인다는 내용입니다. ②번 문장은 잎의 색깔과 에너지 흡수에 관한 내용으로, 식물의 의사소통이라는 주제와 무관합니다.

questions.question: 26. 주어진 글 다음에 이어질 글의 순서로 가장 적절한 것을 고르시오. [3.8점]
questions.passage: Routines enable athletes to evaluate competition conditions. For example, bouncing a ball in a volleyball service routine supplies the server with information about the ball, the floor, and the state of her muscles.
ordered_passages: (A) This information can then be used to properly prepare for her serve. Routines also enable athletes to adjust and fine-tune their preparations based on those evaluations or in pursuit of a particular competitive goal.
(B) Just like adjusting a race-car engine to the conditions of the track, air temperature, and weather, routines adjust all competitive components to achieve proper performance.
(C) This adaptation can involve adjustment to the conditions, rivals, competitive situation, or internal influences that can affect performance.
questions.explanation: 주어진 문장에서 배구 서브 루틴을 통해 정보를 얻는다는 예시가 나왔으므로, (A)의 'This information'이 이를 가리키며 연결됩니다. (A) 끝부분의 'adjust and fine-tune'이 (C)의 'This adaptation'으로 구체화되며, 마지막으로 (B)에서 경주용 자동차 엔진 조절에 비유하며 전체 내용을 요약 정리합니다.

questions.question: 27.주어진 글 다음에 이어질 글의 순서로 가장 적절한 것을 고르시오. [3.6점]
questions.passage: The rise of air-conditioning accelerated the construction of sealed boxes, where the building's only airflow is through the filtered ducts of the air-conditioning unit.
ordered_passages: (A) They built with thick walls and white roofs and transoms over doors to encourage airflow. Anyone who has ever spent a few minutes in a mudbrick house in Tucson, or walked on the narrow streets of old Seville, knows how well these construction methods work.

(B) But all this wisdom about how to deal with heat, accumulated over centuries of practical experience, is all too often ignored. In this sense, air-conditioning is not just a technology of personal comfort; it is also <u>a technology of forgetting.

(C) It doesn't have to be this way. Look at any old building in a hot climate, whether it's in Sicily or Marrakesh or Tehran. Architects understood the importance of shade, airflow, light colors. They oriented buildings to capture cool breezes and block the worst heat of the afternoon.
questions.explanation: 주어진 문장은 에어컨의 도입으로 밀폐된 건물 구조가 확산되었음을 설명합니다. (C)에서는 '꼭 이럴 필요는 없다'며 대안으로 더운 기후의 오래된 건축물들을 제시하고, (A)에서 그 구체적인 건축 방식(두꺼운 벽, 하얀 지붕 등)을 설명합니다. 마지막으로 (B)에서 이러한 지혜가 현대에 와서 잊혀지고 있음을 지적하며 에어컨을 '망각의 기술'로 정의하며 마무리하는 것이 논리적으로 가장 적절합니다.

questions.question: 1. 다음 글에서 필자가 주장하는 바로 가장 적절한 것은? [3.3점]
questions.passage: Magic is what we all wish for to happen in our life. Do you love the movie Cinderella like me? Well, in real life, you can also create magic. Here's the trick. Write down all the real-time challenges that you face and deal with. Just change the challenge statement into positive statements. Let me give you an example here. If you struggle with getting up early in the morning, then write a positive statement such as "I get up early in the morning at 5:00 am every day." Once you write these statements, get ready to witness magic and confidence. You will be surprised that just by writing these statements, there is a shift in the way you think and act. Suddenly you feel more powerful and positive.
options: ① Put your thoughts into action immediately if you want to achieve your goal.
② To gain confidence, turn difficulties into positive statements.
③ Ask for help from people around you to solve a difficult problem.
④ Learn magic from time to time to improve your confidence in your daily life.
⑤ Don't shy away from the challenges you face in real life.
questions.explanation: 필자는 직면한 도전 과제들을 긍정적인 문장으로 바꾸어 써봄으로써 마법 같은 변화와 자신감을 얻을 수 있다고 주장하고 있습니다. 따라서 '자신감을 얻기 위해 어려움을 긍정적인 진술로 바꾸어라'는 내용의 ②번이 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 목표를 달성하고 싶다면 당신의 생각을 즉시 실행에 옮기세요.
② 자신감을 얻기 위해, 어려움들을 긍정적인 진술로 바꾸세요.
③ 어려운 문제를 해결하기 위해 주변 사람들에게 도움을 요청하세요.
④ 일상생활에서 자신감을 향상시키기 위해 때때로 마법을 배우세요.
⑤ 현실 세계에서 직면하는 도전들을 피하지 마세요.

questions.question: 2. 다음 글의 주제로 가장 적절한 것은? [2.8점]
questions.passage:
It would be hard to overstate how important <u>meaningful work</u> is to human beings - work that <u>provides a sense of fulfillment and empowerment</u>. Those who have found deeper meaning in their careers find their days much more energizing and satisfying, and to count their employment as one of their greatest sources of joy and pride. Sonya Lyubomirsky, professor of psychology at the University of California, has conducted numerous workplace studies showing that when people are more <u>fulfilled</u> on the job, they not only produce higher quality work and a greater output, but also generally earn <u>higher incomes</u>. Those most satisfied with their work are also much more likely to be happier with their lives overall. For her book Happiness at Work, researcher Jessica Pryce-Jones conducted a study of 3,000 workers in seventy-nine countries, finding that those who took <u>greater satisfaction from their work were 150 percent more likely to have a happier life overall</u>.
*numerous: 수많은
options: ① how to increase one's pride in one's job
② factors that contribute to a sense of fulfillment in life
③ the relationship between work environments and performance
④ importance of employee empowerment in work performance
⑤ effect of meaningful work on fulfillment and happiness
questions.explanation: 이 글은 의미 있는 일(meaningful work)이 인간에게 성취감을 제공하고 전반적인 삶의 행복에 긍정적인 영향을 미친다는 점을 여러 연구 결과를 통해 설명하고 있습니다. 따라서 주제로 가장 적절한 것은 ⑤번입니다.
options_translation: ① 직업에 대한 자부심을 높이는 방법
② 삶의 성취감에 기여하는 요인들
③ 업무 환경과 성과 사이의 관계
④ 업무 성과에 있어서 직원 권한 부여의 중요성
⑤ 의미 있는 일이 성취감과 행복에 미치는 영향

questions.question: 3. 다음 글의 제목으로 가장 적절한 것은? [3.3점]
questions.passage: Marilyn and her three-year-old daughter, Sarah, took a trip to the beach, where Sarah built her first sandcastle. Moments later, an enormous wave destroyed Sarah's castle. In response to the loss of her sandcastle, tears streamed down Sarah's cheeks and her heart was broken. She ran to Marilyn, saying she would never build a sandcastle again. Marilyn said, "Part of the joy of building a sandcastle is that, in the end, we give it as a gift to the ocean." Sarah loved this idea and responded with enthusiasm to the idea of building another castle - this time, even closer to the water so the ocean would get its gift sooner!
options: ① The More, The Better
② The True Charm of Travel
③ You Will Never Forget Your First
④ Everything Depends on How You Look At It
⑤ Childlike Innocence Has Flown Away With Time
questions.explanation: 사라가 모래성이 파괴되어 슬퍼할 때, 엄마가 그것을 바다에 주는 선물이라고 관점을 바꾸어 설명해주자 사라가 다시 즐겁게 모래성을 쌓게 되었다는 내용입니다. 상황을 어떻게 보느냐에 따라 태도가 달라질 수 있음을 보여주므로 제목으로 ④번이 적합합니다.
options_translation: ① 많을수록 좋다
② 여행의 진정한 매력
③ 당신의 첫 경험을 절대 잊지 못할 것이다
④ 모든 것은 당신이 그것을 어떻게 보느냐에 달려 있다
⑤ 어린아이 같은 순수함은 시간과 함께 사라졌다

questions.question: 4. 다음 글의 내용과 일치하지 않는 것은? [3점]
questions.passage:
When we think of leaders, we may think of people such as Abraham Lincoln or Martin Luther King, Jr. If you consider the historical importance and far-reaching influence of these individuals, leadership might seem like a noble and high goal. But like all of us, <u>these people started out as students, workers, and citizens who possessed ideas about how some aspect of daily life could be improved on a larger scale</u>. Through diligence and experience, they improved upon their ideas by sharing them with others, seeking their opinions and feedback and constantly looking for the best way to accomplish goals for a group. Thus we all have the potential to be leaders at school, in our communities, and at work, regardless of age or experience.
*diligence: 근면
options: ① 아브라함 링컨과 마틴 루터 킹 주니어는 종종 모범적인 지도자로 여겨진다.
② 리더십은 훌륭한 능력으로 보일 수 있다.
③ 아브라함 링컨과 마틴 루터 킹 주니어와 같은 상징적인 인물들은 어렸을 때 일반 사람들과는 특별하고 달랐다.
④ 아브라함 링컨과 마틴 루터 킹 주니어와 같은 지도자들은 다른 사람들의 피드백을 요청하고 집단 목표를 달성하기 위한 가장 효과적인 방법을 계속 모색함으로써 그들의 아이디어를 다듬었다.
⑤ 누구나 나이나 이전 경험에 상관없이 리더가 될 수 있다.
questions.explanation: 본문에서 이 위대한 지도자들도 우리 모두와 마찬가지로 일상생활의 개선에 대한 아이디어를 가진 학생, 노동자, 시민으로 시작했다고 언급하고 있습니다. 따라서 그들이 어렸을 때 일반 사람들과 특별히 달랐다는 ③번의 진술은 본문 내용과 일치하지 않습니다.

questions.question: 5. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 어법상 틀린 것은? [3.6점]
questions.passage:
No respectable boss would say, “I make it a point to discourage my staff from speaking up, and I maintain a culture that ① <u>prevents</u> disagreeing viewpoints from ever getting aired.” If anything, most bosses even say that they are pro-dissent. This idea can be found throughout the series of conversations with corporate, university, and nonprofit leaders, ② <u>publishing</u> weekly in the business sections of newspapers. In the interviews, the ③ <u>featured</u> leaders are asked about their management techniques, and regularly claim to continually encourage internal protest from more junior staffers. As Bot Pittman remarked in one of these conversations: “I want us to listen to these dissenters because they may intend to tell you why we can't do something, but if you listen hard, ④ <u>what they're really</u> telling you ⑤ <u>is</u> what you must do to get something done.”
*dissent: 반대
questions.explanation: ②번의 publishing은 문맥상 주간 비즈니스 섹션에 '발표되는(게재되는)'의 수동 의미를 가져야 하므로 현재분사가 아닌 과거분사 published가 되어야 어법상 적절하다.

questions.question: 6. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 어법상 틀린 것은? [3.4점]
questions.passage:
Working around the whole painting, rather than ① <u>concentrating</u> on one area at a time, will mean you can stop at any point and the painting can ② <u>be considered</u> “finished.” Artists often find it difficult to know when to stop painting, and it can be tempting to keep on ③ <u>adding</u> more to your work. It is important to take a few steps back from the painting from time to time ④ <u>to assess</u> your progress. Putting too much into a painting can spoil its impact and leave it looking overworked. If you find yourself struggling to decide whether you have finished, ⑤ <u>taking</u> a break and come back to it later with fresh eyes. Then you can decide whether any areas of your painting would benefit from further refinement.
*tempting: 유혹하는 **refinement: 정교하게 꾸밈
questions.explanation: ⑤번이 포함된 문장은 명령문 형태가 되어야 하며, 'taking a break'와 'come back'이 병렬 구조를 이루어야 하므로 taking을 동사 원형인 take로 고쳐야 한다.

questions.question: 7. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은? [3.7점]
questions.passage:
A number of research studies have shown how experts in a field often experience difficulties when introducing newcomers to that field. For example, in a genuine training situation, Dr Pamela Hinds found that people expert in using mobile phones were remarkably ① <u>less</u> accurate than novice phone users in judging how long it takes people to learn to use the phones. Experts can become ② <u>insensitive</u> to how hard a task is for the beginner, an effect referred to as the 'curse of knowledge'. Dr Hinds was able to show that as people acquired the skill, they then began to ③ <u>underestimate</u> the level of difficulty of that skill. Her participants even underestimated how long it had taken themselves to acquire that skill in an earlier session. Knowing that experts forget how ④ <u>hard</u> it was for them to learn, we can understand the need to look at the learning process through ⑤ <u>masters'</u> eyes, rather than making assumptions about how students 'should be' learning.
*novice: 초보
questions.explanation: 글 전체의 맥락은 전문가들이 초보자의 어려움을 이해하지 못하는 '지식의 저주'에 대해 설명하고 있다. 따라서 학습 과정을 전문가의 시각이 아닌, 초보자의 시각으로 보아야 한다는 내용이 적절하므로 ⑤번의 masters'를 beginners' 혹은 novices'와 같은 단어로 바꾸어야 한다.

questions.question: 8. 다음 글의 빈칸 ⓐ, ⓑ에 들어갈 알맞은 말로 연결된 것은? [3.5점]
questions.passage:
Consider the seemingly simple question How many senses are there? Around 2,370 years ago, Aristotle wrote that there are five, in both humans and animals - sight, hearing, smell, taste, and touch. ⓐ __________ according to the philosopher Fiona Macpherson, there are reasons to doubt it. For a start, Aristotle missed a few in humans: the perception of your own body which is different from touch and the sense of balance which has links to both touch and vision. Other animals have senses that are even harder to categorize. Many vertebrates have a different sense system for detecting odors. Some snakes can detect the body heat of their prey. These examples tell us that “senses cannot be clearly divided into a limited number of specific kinds,” Macpherson wrote in The Senses. ⓑ __________ trying to push animal senses into Aristotelian buckets, we should study them for what they are.
*vertebrate: 척추동물 **odor: 냄새
options: ① Similarly - Instead
② However - Instead of
③ Similarly - Otherwise
④ However - because of
⑤ As a result - Otherwise
questions.explanation: ⓐ 앞 문장은 아리스토텔레스가 감각이 5개라고 주장한 내용이고, 뒤 문장은 이를 의심할 이유가 있다는 반대 내용이므로 However가 적절하다. ⓑ 뒤에는 동명사 형태인 trying이 오고 있으며, '아리스토텔레스식 분류에 억지로 집어넣으려 하는 대신에'라는 의미가 되어야 하므로 전치사구인 Instead of가 적절하다.
options_translation: ① 마찬가지로 - 대신에
② 그러나 - ~대신에
③ 마찬가지로 - 그렇지 않으면
④ 그러나 - ~때문에
⑤ 결과적으로 - 그렇지 않으면

questions.question: 9. 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은? [3.4점]
questions.passage:
Every species has certain climatic requirements - what degree of heat or cold it can endure, for example. When the climate changes, the places that satisfy those requirements change, too. Species are forced to follow. All creatures are capable of some degree of movement. Even creatures that appear immobile, like trees and barnacles, are capable of dispersal at some stage of their life - as a seed, in the case of the tree, or as a larva, in the case of the barnacle. A creature must get from the place it is born - often occupied by its parent - to a place where it can survive, grow, and reproduce. From fossils, scientists know that even creatures like trees __________ with surprising speed during past periods of climate change.
*barnacle: 따개비 **dispersal: 분산 ***fossil: 화석
options: ① grew
② moved
③ evolved
④ reproduced
⑤ disappeared
questions.explanation: 글의 앞부분에서 기후 변화에 따라 생물 종들이 서식지를 이동해야 하며(Species are forced to follow), 움직이지 않는 것처럼 보이는 나무도 씨앗 단계에서 분산(dispersal)을 통해 이동 능력이 있다고 설명하고 있다. 따라서 과거 기후 변화기에 나무조차 놀라운 속도로 '이동했다(moved)'는 결론이 가장 적절하다.
options_translation: ① 자랐다
② 이동했다
③ 진화했다
④ 번식했다
⑤ 사라졌다

questions.question: 10. 주어진 글 다음에 이어질 글의 순서로 가장 적절한 것은? [3.3점]
questions.passage: Crop rotation is the process in which farmers change the crops they grow in their fields in a special order.
ordered_passages: (A) Each crop enriches the soil for the next crop. This type of farming is sustainable because the soil stays healthy.
(B) For example, if a farmer has three fields, he or she may grow carrots in the first field, green beans in the second, and tomatoes in the third.

(C) The next year, green beans will be in the first field, tomatoes in the second field, and carrots will be in the third. In year three, the crops will rotate again. By the fourth year, the crops will go back to their original order.
questions.explanation: 주어진 글에서 윤작(crop rotation)을 소개하고, (B)에서 구체적인 예시로 세 가지 밭에 세 가지 작물을 심는 경우를 듭니다. (C)에서 다음 해와 3년 차, 4년 차에 작물이 어떻게 순환되는지 설명한 뒤, (A)에서 이러한 방식이 토양을 비옥하게 하고 지속 가능하게 한다는 결론으로 마무리하는 것이 자연스럽습니다.

questions.question: 11. 글의 흐름으로 보아, 주어진 문장이 들어가기에 가장 적절한 곳을 고르시오. [2.8점]
questions.passage: One of the most striking characteristics of a sleeping animal or person is that they do not respond normally to environmental stimuli. If you open the eyelids of a sleeping mammal the eyes will not see normally - they are functionally blind. ( ① ) Some visual information apparently gets in, but it is not normally processed as it is shortened or weakened; same with the other sensing systems. ( ② ) Stimuli are registered but not processed normally and they fail to wake the individual. ( ③ ) Perceptual disengagement probably serves the function of protecting sleep, so some authors do not count it as part of the definition of sleep itself. ( ④ ) Nevertheless, many animals (including humans) use the intermediate state of drowsiness to derive some benefits of sleep without total perceptual disengagement. ( ⑤ )
questions.insertion_sentence: But as sleep would be impossible without it, it seems essential to its definition.
questions.explanation: ③번 문장에서 지각적 이탈(Perceptual disengagement)이 잠을 보호하는 기능을 하지만 일부 저자들은 그것을 잠의 정의로 간주하지 않는다고 언급합니다. 주어진 문장의 'it'은 지각적 이탈을 가리키며, 하지만 그것(지각적 이탈) 없이는 잠이 불가능하므로 잠의 정의에 필수적인 것처럼 보인다는 역접의 내용이 이어지는 ④번 자리가 가장 적절합니다. 그 뒤 ⑤번 문장 앞의 Nevertheless는 완전한 지각적 이탈이 없는 상태에 대한 보충 설명을 이어줍니다.

questions.question: 12. 다음 글의 내용을 한 문장으로 요약하고자 한다. 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은? [3.4점]
questions.passage: The rate of speed at which one is traveling will greatly determine the ability to process detail in the environment. In evolutionary terms, human senses are adapted to the speed at which humans move through space under their own power while walking. Our ability to distinguish detail in the environment is therefore ideally suited to movement at speeds of perhaps five miles per hour and under. The fastest users of the street, motorists, therefore have a much more limited ability to process details along the street - a motorist simply has little time or ability to appreciate design details. On the other hand, pedestrian travel, being much slower, allows for the appreciation of environmental detail. Joggers and bicyclists fall somewhere in between these polar opposites; while they travel faster than pedestrians, their rate of speed is ordinarily much slower than that of the typical motorist.
questions.summary_sentence: Because our capability to process detail in the environment is affected by the (A) _________ of our movement and our senses have developed based on walking speed, drivers, who travel much more rapidly than walkers, have a(n) (B) _________ capability in appreciating features in the environment.
options: ① velocity limited
② course excellent
③ route restricted
④ pace outstanding
⑤ speed appropriate
questions.explanation: 본문은 이동 속도(speed/velocity)가 주변 환경의 세부 사항을 처리하는 능력에 영향을 준다고 설명합니다. 인간의 감각은 걷는 속도에 최적화되어 있으므로, 보행자보다 훨씬 빠르게 이동하는 운전자들은 환경의 특징을 감상하는 능력이 더 제한적(limited/restricted)이라는 결론이 도출됩니다.
options_translation: ① 속도 - 제한된
② 경로 - 우수한
③ 경로 - 제한된
④ 속도 - 뛰어난
⑤ 속도 - 적절한

questions.question: 14. 다음 글에서 do so가 다음 글에서 의미하는 바로 가장 적절한 것은? [3.5점]
questions.passage: "To grow into a better version of ourselves, we should not stay as we are." That was the first thing our teacher said to us on the first day of school. She wanted us to start the semester by pushing ourselves out of our comfort zones and learning more about ourselves. To help us <u>do so</u>, she gave us an assignment to challenge ourselves in three different ways. The three challenges could involve hobbies, exercise, our studies, or even our relationships. The important part was trying something new for each one. She told us that we should share our experiences with our classmates when we finished the challenges.
options: ① 자신만의 안전지대를 설정하고 벗어나지 않기 위해 노력하기
② 안전지대를 벗어나고 자신에 대해 더 배우면서 학기를 시작하기
③ 자신의 도전과제를 설정하고 이루기 위해 노력한 내용을 발표하기
④ 새 학기 첫 날 새로운 친구를 사겨고 다양한 주제에 대해 대화 나누기
⑤ 자신의 현재 상태에 대해 객관적으로 바라보고 관찰한 내용 기록하기
questions.explanation: 본문에서 'do so'는 앞 문장에 언급된 'start the semester by pushing ourselves out of our comfort zones and learning more about ourselves'를 의미하므로 ②번이 정답이다.

questions.question: 15. 다음 인터뷰의 주제로 가장 적절한 것은? [3.7점]
questions.passage:
Host Oh, so that was the beginning of it. Could you explain to us how the Friendship Bench program works?

Dr. Chibanda Certainly. The program was created as a way to provide accessible mental health services. It offers talk therapy sessions to people dealing with issues such as depression or anxiety. The sessions are free and are provided by respected elderly women from the community. These women, called "grandmothers," volunteer to sit with patients at the benches, listen to their stories, and provide them with emotional support.

Host What a wonderful idea! How did these amazing grandmothers become a part of your program?

Dr. Chibanda Grandmothers were chosen for our program because they are deeply connected to the community. Moreover, they have all the qualities of a counselor, such as excellent listening skills, empathy, and the ability to engage in meaningful discussions. They are also very reliable, which is important for our efforts to support mental health. At the beginning, we started with only fourteen volunteer grandmothers. But today, there are thousands of grandmothers who have been trained to provide Friendship Bench therapy in Zimbabwe.
options: ① the mystery of traditional remedy in Zimbabwe
② meaningful discussions to help grandmothers
③ skills to give emotional supports to teenagers
④ how to deliver reliable communication with people
⑤ grandmothers as mental healers in the counseling program
questions.explanation: 이 대화는 Friendship Bench 프로그램에서 할머니들이 상담가로서 정신 건강 서비스를 제공하는 역할과 그 중요성에 대해 설명하고 있으므로 ⑤번이 가장 적절하다.
options_translation: ① 짐바브웨 전통 치료법의 신비
② 할머니들을 돕기 위한 의미 있는 토론
③ 십대들에게 정서적 지원을 제공하는 기술
④ 사람들과 신뢰할 수 있는 소통을 전달하는 방법
⑤ 상담 프로그램에서 정신적 치유자로서의 할머니들

questions.question: 16. Grandma Moyo에 관한 다음 인터뷰의 내용과 일치하는 것은? [3.5점]
questions.passage:
Host Now let's hear from one of the grandmothers who volunteers for the program. Can you introduce yourself and tell us how you got involved with the Friendship Bench program?

Grandma Moyo Hello, my name is Judith Moyo, but people call me Grandma Moyo. I'm 76 years old, and I have been volunteering for the Friendship Bench program for about eight years. I joined the program because many people in my community struggle with mental health problems, and I wanted to do something about it. I knew that I could help heal their wounded hearts by supporting them.

Host That's very kind of you. Can you tell us about your experience as a grandmother for the Friendship Bench program?

Grandma Moyo It's been wonderful. Seeking help for mental health problems is nothing to be ashamed of. I've seen how it can make a difference in people's lives. One patient of mine, a nineteen-year-old girl, was going through a difficult time after her mom passed away. I counseled her and helped her begin her recovery journey. Now her life is back on track, and she has even started her own business! Cases like this make me so proud to be part of the program. It is such a rewarding experience to help people make positive changes in their lives.
options: ① 현재 나이는 67세이다.
② Friendship Bench 프로그램에서 대략 8년째 봉사활동 중이다.
③ 자신의 정신건강 문제로 프로그램을 시작했다.
④ 정신건강 문제가 있는 사람을 잘 돌볼 수 있다는 확신은 없었다.
⑤ 9살 소녀 환자를 돌보며 수많은 좌절을 경험했다.
questions.explanation: 지문에서 Grandma Moyo는 76세이며, 8년 동안 봉사해 왔다고 언급했으므로 ②번이 일치한다. ①은 나이가 틀리고, ③은 지역사회의 문제를 돕기 위해 시작한 것이며, ④는 정반대로 도울 수 있다는 확신이 있었고, ⑤는 19세 소녀 환자를 도운 긍정적인 경험을 이야기하고 있다.

questions.question: 17. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 어법상 틀린 것은? [3.4점]
questions.passage: These days, I tend to watch movies on streaming services. However, if I go to the theater, I usually watch an action or science fiction movie with my friends or family. ① <u>Those</u> are the kinds of movies they enjoy. I ② <u>had never been</u> to the theater by myself before. So, for the first challenge, I decided to give it a try. It was nice ③ <u>to choose</u> the movie and the seat on my own. I didn't have to worry about anyone else's preferences. I saw the experience as a good opportunity to watch something different, so I chose a historical drama that I had been curious about. At first, it felt a bit awkward and lonely to sit in the theater by myself. But once the movie started, it was so ④ <u>satisfied</u> because I could focus on the movie itself. There was nothing to distract me! This experience made me realize that I sometimes enjoy doing things alone. After the movie, I promised myself ⑤ <u>that</u> I would try to make my own choices more often and enjoy more activities by myself in the future.
questions.explanation: 주어인 'it'(혼자 영화를 보는 경험)이 사람들에게 만족감을 주는 주체이므로, 감정의 원인을 나타내는 현재분사 'satisfying'이 와야 한다. 'satisfied'는 사람이 감정을 느낄 때 사용한다.

questions.question: 18. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은? [3.5점]
questions.passage: Buildings began to be constructed as sealed boxes, with airflow occurring only through the filtered ducts of air-conditioning units. This trend ① <u>accelerated</u> with the rise of air-conditioning. However, it doesn't have to be this way. Look at any old building in a hot climate, whether it's in Sicily or Marrakesh or Tehran. Architects understood the importance of shade, airflow, light colors. They oriented buildings to ② <u>capture</u> cool breezes and block the worst heat of the afternoon. They built with thick walls and white roofs and transoms over doors to ③ <u>discourage</u> airflow. Anyone who has ever spent a few minutes in a mud brick house in Tucson, or walked on the narrow streets of old Seville, knows how well these construction methods work. But all this wisdom about how to deal with heat, ④ <u>accumulated</u> over centuries of practical experience, is all too often ignored. In this sense, air-conditioning is not just a technology of personal comfort; it is also the ⑤ <u>loss</u> of tradition.
questions.explanation: 과거 더운 기후의 건축가들은 공기 흐름의 중요성을 이해하고 있었으며, 두꺼운 벽, 흰색 지붕, 문 위의 가로창(transoms) 등을 활용하여 공기 흐름을 장려(encourage)하거나 촉진하려 했으므로 '방해하다, 막다'라는 의미의 discourage는 문맥상 적절하지 않습니다.

questions.question: 19. 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은? [3.6점]
questions.passage: Ever since I was a child, I've always been afraid of water. I have never enjoyed water activities or felt comfortable while doing them. So, for the second challenge, I decided to try to ______________. However, I wasn't sure what to do at first. One day, I came across a video clip of my cousin surfing at an indoor pool on social media. It looked fun, and I liked the fact that it took place in a shallow pool, not in the ocean. I messaged my cousin about it. She assured me that it wasn't too hard, so I signed up for a beginner course. At the beginning of the lesson, it was hard just to stand up on the board. After some help from the instructor, however, I learned how to balance properly and even managed to surf a few waves! It gave me such a rush of excitement. Being in the water wasn't as bad as I had thought. While the experience didn't completely change my mind about water sports, it did help me discover my sense of adventure.
options: ① keep my daily routine
② intensify fake feeling inside me
③ overcome this uncomfortable feeling
④ practice how to give hidden messages
⑤ make truthful pictures on social media
questions.explanation: 필자는 어릴 때부터 물을 무서워했고 수중 활동을 즐기지 못했으므로, 두 번째 도전으로 이러한 '불편한 감정을 극복하기(overcome this uncomfortable feeling)' 위해 노력하기로 결정했다는 내용이 문맥상 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 나의 일상을 유지하기
② 내 안의 가짜 감정을 강화하기
③ 이 불편한 감정을 극복하기
④ 숨겨진 메시지를 전달하는 법을 연습하기
⑤ 소셜 미디어에 진실된 사진을 올리기

questions.question: 20. 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은? [3.4점]
questions.passage: There is a wealth of evidence that when parents, teachers, supervisors, and coaches are perceived as involved and caring, people feel happier and more motivated. And it is not just those people with power - we need to feel valued and respected by peers and coworkers. Thus, when the need for relatedness is met, motivation and internalization are fueled, provided that support for autonomy and competence are also there. If we are trying to motivate others, a caring relationship is a crucial basis from which to begin. And when we are trying to motivate ourselves, doing things to enhance ______________ can be crucial to long-term persistence. So exercise with a friend, call someone when you have a difficult decision to make, and be there as a support for others as they take on challenges.
options: ① a sense of connectedness to others
② the value of leadership in the group
③ the belief of risk-taking activity in new ways
④ the tendency of being kind within community
⑤ the act of doing selfish things as much as we can
questions.explanation: 글의 전반부에서 타인(부모, 교사, 동료 등)과의 유대감, 보살핌, 가치 인정 등이 동기 부여와 행복에 중요하다고 강조하고 있습니다. 따라서 스스로를 동기 부여할 때도 '타인과의 연결감(a sense of connectedness to others)'을 높이는 활동을 하는 것이 장기적인 지속성에 중요하다는 결론이 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 타인과의 연결감
② 집단 내 리더십의 가치
③ 새로운 방식으로 위험을 감수하는 활동에 대한 믿음
④ 공동체 내에서 친절하려는 경향
⑤ 우리가 할 수 있는 한 이기적인 일을 하는 행위

questions.question: 21. 다음 글에서 전체 흐름과 관계 없는 문장은? [2.8점]
questions.passage: Of all the challenges I chose for myself, the third one made me the most nervous: changing my hairstyle. ① For many years, I had kept the same hairstyle because I had been worried about my large forehead. ② Since I was feeling confident after the first two challenges, I went to a hair salon and talked to the stylist to find a shorter hairstyle that suited me. ③ The next day at school, my classmates were a bit surprised, however, the reactions were mostly positive. ④ The most important thing in my life has always been spending time with my friends and I sometimes give up many things because of them. ⑤ I realized that trying a different look wasn't as difficult as I thought it would be. In fact, it made me feel more confident about myself. I didn't expect that stepping out of my comfort zone would have such a positive effect on how I felt about myself!
questions.explanation: 전체 글은 자신의 콤플렉스를 극복하기 위해 새로운 헤어스타일에 도전하고 자신감을 얻었다는 내용입니다. 하지만 ④번 문장은 친구와 시간을 보내는 것의 중요성과 그들을 위해 희생한다는 내용으로, 헤어스타일 도전 및 자신감 획득이라는 주제와 관련이 없습니다.

questions.question: 22. 다음 글에서 전체 흐름과 관계 없는 문장은? [3.4점]
questions.passage: As you listen to your child in an emotional moment, be aware that usually works better sharing simple observation than asking questions to get a conversation rolling. You may ask your child "Why do you feel sad?" and she may not have a clue. ① As a child, she may not have an answer on the tip of her tongue. ② On the other hand, answering some questions sometimes makes her feel relieved because she thinks it is also emotional caring. ③ Maybe she may or may not be able to come up with answers because she might be worried that the answer is not good enough to justify the feeling. ④ Under these circumstances, a series of questions can just make a child silent. ⑤ It's better to simply reflect what you notice. You can say, "You seem a little tired today," or, "I noticed that you frowned when I mentioned the recital," and wait for her response.
questions.explanation: 이 글의 핵심은 아이가 정서적으로 격앙된 순간에 질문을 던지는 것보다 관찰한 내용을 단순히 말해주는 것이 대화를 이끌어내는 데 더 효과적이라는 것입니다. 따라서 질문에 답하는 것이 정서적 돌봄으로 느껴져 아이를 안도하게 한다는 내용의 ②번 문장은 전체적인 흐름과 상반됩니다.

questions.question: 23. 주어진 글 다음에 이어질 글의 순서로 가장 적절한 것은? [3.3점]
questions.passage: Our skin conducts electricity more or less efficiently, depending on our emotions.
ordered_passages: (A) We know that when we're emotionally stimulated-stressed, sad, any intense emotion, really our bodies sweat a tiny bit, so little we might not even notice. And when those tiny drops of sweat appear, our skin gets more electrically conductive.

(B) Therefore, it means that we can actually measure your emotional state by tracking how your body subconsciously sweats, by running a bit of electricity through your skin. We can then turn the subjective, subconscious experience of emotional intensity into an objective number by figuring out how good your skin gets at transferring an electrical current.

(C) This change in sweat gland activity happens (completely) without your conscious mind having much say in the matter. If you feel emotionally intense you're going to notice an increase in sweat gland activity. This is particularly useful from a scientific viewpoint, because it allows us to put an objective value on a subjective state of mind.
questions.explanation: 주어진 문장에서 감정에 따른 피부 전도율 변화를 제시합니다. (A)에서 감정 자극 시 땀이 나면서 전도율이 높아진다는 구체적인 원리를 설명하고, (C)에서 이러한 변화가 무의식적으로 일어나며 과학적으로 객관적 수치를 부여할 수 있게 해준다고 부연합니다. 마지막으로 (B)에서 'Therefore'를 통해 이를 활용해 감정 상태를 객관적인 숫자로 측정하고 변환할 수 있다는 결론을 맺습니다.

questions.question: 24. 글의 흐름으로 보아, 주어진 문장이 들어가기에 가장 적절한 곳은? [3.4점]
questions.passage: Promotion deals with consumer psychology. We can't force people to think one way or another, and the clever marketer knows that promotion is used to provide information in the most clear, honest, and simple fashion possible. ( ① ) By doing so, the possibility of increasing sales goes up. ( ② ) Gone are the days when promotions were done in order to fool the consumer into purchasing something. ( ③ ) The long-term effect of getting a consumer to buy something they did not really want or need wasn't good. ( ④ ) In fact, consumers fooled once can do damage to sales as they relate their experience to others. ( ⑤ ) Therefore, marketers must know where the potential consumers are, and how to reach them.
questions.insertion_sentence: Instead, marketers now know that their goal is to identify the consumers who are most likely to appreciate a good or service, and to promote that good or service in a way that makes the value clear to the consumer
questions.explanation: 이 글은 소비자를 속여서 구매하게 하던 과거의 방식에서 정직하게 정보를 전달하는 방식으로 마케팅이 변화했음을 설명합니다. ④번 문장까지는 소비자를 속였을 때 발생하는 장기적인 악영향(매출 타격 등)에 대해 기술하고 있습니다. 주어진 문장은 '대신에(Instead)'로 시작하여, 이제 마케터들이 제품의 가치를 알아줄 소비자를 찾아내어 가치를 명확히 전달하는 것을 목표로 삼는다는 대안적 전략을 제시하므로 ④번 문장 뒤인 ⑤번 위치가 가장 적절합니다. 그 뒤의 'Therefore' 문장은 이러한 타겟팅의 필요성에 대한 결론으로 자연스럽게 이어집니다.

questions.question:
【서답형 3번】
다음 글의 내용을 한 문장으로 요약한 아래 문장에서 빈칸 (A), (B), (C) 에 들어갈 가장 적절한 단어를 본문에서 찾아 어형을 변형할 필요가 있는 단어가 있다면 변형하여 쓰시오 (6점, 각 2점)
questions.passage:
In many sports, people realized the difficulties and even impossibilities of young children participating fully in many adult sport environments. They found the road to success for young children is unlikely if they play on adult fields, courts or arenas with equipment that is too large, too heavy or too fast for them to handle while trying to compete in adult-style competition. Common sense has prevailed: different sports have made some adjustments for children. As examples, baseball has T ball, football has flag football and junior soccer uses a smaller and lighter ball and (sometimes) a smaller field. All have junior competitive structures where children play for shorter time periods and often in smaller teams. In a similar way, tennis has modified the court areas, balls and rackets to make them more suitable for children under 10. The adjustments are progressive and relate to the age of the child.
* prevail: 널리 퍼지다
questions.summary_sentence: Sports have (A) _________ equipment and rules to (B) _________ young children's abilities and age for their (C) _________ (in many sport environments).
questions.explanation: 본문의 내용을 바탕으로 요약문을 완성하면 다음과 같습니다. (A) 테니스 사례에서 언급된 'modified'를 사용하여 스포츠가 장비와 규칙을 수정해왔음을 나타냅니다. (B) 본문의 'suitable'을 동사형인 'suit'로 변형하여 아이들의 능력과 연령에 맞춘다는 의미를 전달합니다. (C) 본문 첫 문장의 'participating'을 명사형인 'participation'으로 변형하여 아이들의 참여를 위한 것임을 명시합니다.

questions.question: 5. 다음 글의 주제로 가장 적절한 것은? [3.4점]
questions.passage: Fans who are inclined to spend a lot of time thinking about what athletes owe them as fans should also think about the corresponding obligations that fans might have as fans. One who thinks only about what they are entitled to receive from their friends without ever giving a moment's thought to what they owe their friends is, to put it mildly, not a very good friend. Similarly, fans who only think about what athletes owe them without ever thinking about what they owe to athletes have failed to take the fan/athlete relationship all that seriously. As in nearly every other area of human life, whatever special rights fans may possess are limited by a corresponding set of obligations, and fans who never think about how they can be better fans even as they confidently opine about what athletes owe them are hardly fulfilling their end of the bargain.
options: ① various elements that create good sportsmanship
② similarities and differences between fans and athletes
③ the influence of fans' positive comments on their players
④ necessity of fans' fulfillment of their responsibilities to athletes
⑤ the reason why athletes meet the expectations of their fans
questions.explanation: 이 글은 팬들이 운동선수에게 기대하는 권리만큼이나 팬으로서 운동선수에게 가져야 할 책임과 의무를 다하는 것의 중요성을 강조하고 있습니다. 따라서 주제로 가장 적절한 것은 ④번 '팬들이 선수들에 대한 책임을 이행해야 할 필요성'입니다.
options_translation: ① 훌륭한 스포츠맨십을 만드는 다양한 요소들
② 팬들과 운동선수들 사이의 유사점과 차이점
③ 팬들의 긍정적인 언급이 선수들에게 미치는 영향
④ 팬들이 선수들에 대한 책임을 이행해야 할 필요성
⑤ 운동선수들이 팬들의 기대에 부응하는 이유

questions.question: 6. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은? [3.5점]
questions.passage: When we realize we've said something in error and we pause to go back to ① <u>correct</u> it, we stop gesturing a couple of hundred milliseconds before we stop speaking. Such sequences ② <u>suggest</u> the startling notion that our hands "know" what we're going to say before our conscious minds do, and in fact this is often the case. Gesture can mentally prime a word so that the right term comes to our lips. When people are ③ <u>prevented</u> from gesturing, they talk less fluently; their speech becomes halting because their hands are no longer able to supply them with the next word, and the next. Not being able to gesture has other deleterious effects: without gesture to ④ <u>help</u> our mental processes along, we remember less useful information, we solve problems less well, and we are less able to explain our thinking. Far from tagging along as speech's clumsy companion, gesture ⑤ <u>conceals</u> the leading edge of our thought.
questions.explanation: 글의 흐름상 손동작은 우리가 무엇을 말할지 의식적인 마음보다 먼저 알고, 언어적 표현을 돕고 사고를 이끌어가는 역할을 한다고 설명하고 있습니다. 따라서 제스처가 사고의 최첨단을 '숨긴다(conceals)'는 표현은 문맥상 어색하며, '구성한다' 혹은 '이끈다'와 같은 표현이 적절합니다.

questions.question: 10. 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은? [4점]
questions.passage: Dictionaries are relatively good resources for anyone interested in finding out what a word means. Using one set of words to define another word is called a lexical definition. But we need to ____________________. More often than not, a definition in a dictionary requires readers to have a fairly robust understanding of the language already at their disposal. In other words, a dictionary functions in many cases as a cross-reference or translator between words one knows and words that one doesn't yet know. Even the most obscure words in a dictionary, say, for example "pulchritudinous" or "kalokagathia," must be defined using words that the reader already knows and understands. Otherwise, the dictionary isn't very helpful.
options: ① recognize that dictionary definitions can have limitations
② characterize features of languages through scientific methods
③ know that layouts of modern dictionaries improve reading fluency in learners
④ accept that mastering English can only be accomplished by analyzing dictionaries
⑤ admit that dictionaries bridge the gap between spoken and written language for learners
questions.explanation: 지문은 사전의 정의가 독자가 이미 알고 있는 언어 능력을 바탕으로 한다고 설명하며, 모르는 단어를 설명하기 위해 이미 아는 단어를 사용해야 한다는 점을 강조합니다. 즉, 사전적 정의는 사용자의 기존 언어 지식에 의존한다는 한계가 있음을 시사하므로 ①이 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 사전적 정의에 한계가 있을 수 있음을 인식하다
② 과학적 방법을 통해 언어의 특징을 규정하다
③ 현대 사전의 배치가 학습자의 읽기 유창성을 향상시킨다는 것을 알다
④ 영어 마스터는 사전을 분석함으로써만 성취될 수 있음을 받아들이다
⑤ 사전이 학습자를 위해 구어와 문어 사이의 간극을 메워준다는 점을 인정하다

questions.question: 13. (A), (B), (C)의 괄호 안에서 문맥에 맞는 낱말로 가장 적절한 것은? [3.3점]
questions.passage: Quite often the interaction between groups is socially (A) [equal / unequal], and this is reflected in the fact that in many cases borrowing of words or constructions goes mostly or entirely in one direction, from the more powerful or prestigious group to the less favored one. The languages of socially subordinated groups may from quite an early period of contact provide terminology for objects or practices with which speakers of the more powerful group were previously (B) [familiar / unfamiliar], but the effects of contact in that direction may not progress any further than this. In some cases, as with the Dharug language of Sydney, Australia, the source of some of the earliest loans from Indigenous Australian languages into English, the fate of the language system is extinction after the obliteration of many of its speakers. The remainder shifted to varieties of English, the language of the people who had (C) [supported / suppressed] them.
options: ① unequal familiar suppressed
② unequal unfamiliar suppressed
③ unequal unfamiliar supported
④ equal familiar supported
⑤ equal unfamiliar suppressed
questions.explanation: (A) 뒤의 내용에서 단어의 차용이 더 강력한 집단에서 덜 선호되는 집단으로 일방향으로 일어난다고 했으므로 사회적으로 '불평등한(unequal)' 상호작용임을 알 수 있다. (B) 하위 집단의 언어가 상위 집단이 이전에는 '익숙하지 않았던(unfamiliar)' 사물이나 관습에 대한 용어를 제공할 수 있다는 흐름이 자연스럽다. (C) 원주민 언어가 멸종하고 그들이 자신들을 '억압했던(suppressed)' 사람들의 언어로 전환했다는 문맥이 적절하다.
options_translation: ① 불평등한 익숙한 억압한
② 불평등한 익숙하지 않은 억압한
③ 불평등한 익숙하지 않은 지지한
④ 평등한 익숙한 지지한
⑤ 평등한 익숙하지 않은 억압한

questions.question: 14. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은? [3.6점]
questions.passage: As a general rule, it's better if your definition corresponds as closely as possible to the way in which the term is ordinarily used in the kinds of debates to which your claims are pertinent. There will be, however, occasions where it is appropriate, even necessary, to ① <u>coin</u> special uses through what philosophers call stimulative definition. This would be the case where the current lexicon is not able to make ② <u>distinctions</u> that you think are philosophically important. For example, we do not have a term in ordinary language that describes a memory that is not necessarily a memory of something the person having it has experienced. Such a thing would occur, for example, if I could somehow ③ <u>erase</u> your memories: I would have a memory-type experience, but this would not be of something that I had actually experienced. To call this a memory would be ④ <u>misleading</u>. For this reason, philosophers have coined the special term 'quasi-memory' to ⑤ <u>refer</u> to these hypothetical memory-like experiences.
questions.explanation: 글의 맥락상 본인이 직접 경험하지 않은 기억(타인의 기억 등)을 갖게 되는 상황을 설명하고 있다. 따라서 필자가 상대방의 기억을 '지우는(erase)' 것이 아니라, 상대방의 기억을 '이식받거나(transplant/transfer)' 공유하는 상황이어야 내가 직접 경험하지 않은 것에 대한 기억을 가지게 된다는 예시가 성립한다.

questions.question: 16. 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은? [4.2점]
questions.passage: If the brain has already stored someone's face and name, why do we still end up remembering one and not the other? This is because the brain has something of a two-tier memory system at work when it comes to retrieving memories, and this gives rise to a common yet infuriating sensation: recognising someone, but not being able to remember how or why, or what their name is. This happens because ________________________________. To clarify, familiarity (or recognition) is when you encounter someone or something and you know you've done so before. But beyond that, you've got nothing; all you can say is this person/thing is already in your memories. Recall is when you can access the original memory of how and why you know this person; recognition is just flagging up the fact that the memory exists.
options: ① unlike recall, every human brain can access recognition
② the brain treats familiarity and recall as two separate processes
③ reconstruction of <u>contextual information</u> demands an active process
④ memory retrieval failures are primarily caused by frustrating states
⑤ cognitive overload during social interactions often suppresses name recollection
questions.explanation: 글 전체에서 기억의 인출 과정을 '친숙함(재인)'과 '회상'이라는 두 가지 단계(two-tier system)로 나누어 설명하고 있으며, 이 둘을 별개의 것으로 취급하여 이름은 기억나지 않지만 얼굴은 낯익은 상황이 발생한다고 설명하므로 ②가 가장 적절하다.
options_translation: ① 회상과 달리 모든 인간의 뇌는 재인에 접근할 수 있다
② 뇌는 친숙함과 회상을 두 개의 분리된 과정으로 취급한다
③ 맥락 정보의 재구성은 능동적인 과정을 요구한다
④ 기억 인출 실패는 주로 좌절감을 주는 상태에 의해 발생한다
⑤ 사회적 상호작용 중의 인지적 과부하는 종종 이름 기억을 억제한다

questions.question: 17. What is the most appropriate thing that the writer argues in the next text? [4.1점]
questions.passage: Too many times people, especially in today's generation, expect things to just happen overnight. When we have these false expectations, it tends to discourage us from continuing to move forward. Because this is a high tech society, everything we want has to be within the parameters of our comfort and convenience. If it doesn't happen fast enough, we're tempted to lose interest. So many people don't want to take the time it requires to be successful. Success is not a matter of mere desire; you should develop patience in order to achieve it. Have you fallen prey to impatience? Great things take time to build.
options: ① To succeed, you need to build up patience.
② To keep interested, you have to do what you like.
③ You must respond quickly to the pace of social change.
④ Rather than waiting for opportunities, we must act positively.
⑤ Rather than seeking comfort, you should challenge your limits.
questions.explanation: 글의 후반부에서 'Success is not a matter of mere desire; you should develop patience in order to achieve it.'라고 언급하며 성공을 위해서는 인내심을 길러야 한다고 명시적으로 주장하고 있습니다.
options_translation: ① 성공하기 위해서는 인내심을 길러야 한다.
② 흥미를 유지하려면 좋아하는 일을 해야 한다.
③ 사회 변화의 속도에 빠르게 대응해야 한다.
④ 기회를 기다리기보다 긍정적으로 행동해야 한다.
⑤ 안락함을 찾기보다 한계에 도전해야 한다.

questions.question: 18. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은? [3.7점]
questions.passage: The most prevalent problem kids report is that they feel like they need to be <u>①reachable</u> at all times. Because technology allows for it, they feel an obligation. It's easy for most of us to relate-you probably feel the same pressure in your own life. It is really challenging to <u>②cope with</u> the fact that we're human and can't always respond immediately. For a teen or tween who's still learning the <u>③ins and outs</u> of social interactions, it's even worse. Here's how this behavior <u>④plays out</u> sometimes: Your child texts one of his friends, and the friend doesn't text back right away. Now it's easy for your child to think, "This person doesn't want to be my friend anymore!" So he texts again, and again, and again- "blowing up their phone." This can be <u>⑤unstressful</u> and even read as aggressive. But you can see how easily this could happen.
questions.explanation: 친구가 즉시 답장하지 않을 때 계속 문자를 보내는 행위("blowing up their phone")는 스트레스가 없는(unstressful) 것이 아니라 스트레스를 주는(stressful) 일이며 공격적으로 비춰질 수 있다는 문맥이 되어야 합니다.

questions.question: 19. 다음 글의 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 말로 알맞은 것끼리 연결된 것은? [3.8점]
questions.passage: We tend to overrate the impact of new technologies in part because older technologies have been absorbed into the furniture of our lives, so as to be almost invisible. Take the baby bottle. Here is a simple implement that has transformed a fundamental human experience for vast numbers of infants and mothers, yet it finds no place in our histories of technology. This technology might be ( A ) of as a classic time-shifting device, as it enables mothers to exercise more control over the timing of feeding. It can also function to save time, as bottle feeding allows for someone else to ( B ) the mother's time. Potentially, therefore, it has huge implications for the management of time in everyday life, yet it is entirely overlooked in discussions of high-speed society.
options: ① seen ······ replace
② viewed ······ eliminate
③ looked upon ······ destroy
④ thought ······ remove
⑤ regarded ······ waste
questions.explanation: (A) 뒤에 전치사 of가 있으므로 'thought of as(~로 생각되다)'가 어법상 가장 적절합니다. 다른 선택지인 seen, viewed, regarded, looked upon 등은 'as'와 직접 연결되거나 다른 전치사가 필요합니다. (B)의 경우 젖병 수유가 어머니의 시간(노동)을 대신하거나 덜어주는 역할을 한다는 내용이므로 'remove'가 흐름상 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 보이다 ······ 대체하다
② 보이다 ······ 제거하다
③ 간주되다 ······ 파괴하다
④ 생각되다 ······ 제거하다(덜어주다)
⑤ 간주되다 ······ 낭비하다

questions.question: 20. 다음 글에서 전체 흐름과 관계 없는 문장은? [3.7점]
questions.passage: The explosion of popular music in the second half of the twentieth century as well as the global circulation and dissemination of music by the creative industries propelled a new understanding of accessibility in relation to music. Suddenly, in the 1950s, anyone could pick up spoons, a couple of pans, a second-hand guitar and start a band. This led to specific genres such as skiffle, but also, more generally, reflected a much more relaxed and inclusive attitude to music making. ① While ordinary people had always sung and made music, the popular music movement was driven by a spirit of rebellion and freedom. ② This approach led to the punk movement, whose musicians even made it a condition for their music to be non-virtuosic and accessible to all in the 1970s. ③ Many music festivals during the 1970s were held outdoors and attracted large crowds regardless of the weather conditions. ④ Groups who had been entirely excluded from music revelled in opportunities to create. ⑤ This led to a sense of novelty and empowerment in and beyond the music sphere.
questions.explanation: 이 글은 대중음악의 발달이 음악 제작에 대한 접근성과 포용성을 높였다는 내용입니다. 1970년대 음악 축제가 야외에서 열리고 날씨와 상관없이 군중을 모았다는 ③번 문장은 음악 제작의 접근성이라는 전체 주제와 무관합니다.

questions.question: 21. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ⓐ~ⓔ문장 중에서 어법상 틀린 것의 개수는? [3.7점]
questions.passage: ⓐ <u>The governments of virtually every country on the planet attach great importance to achieving food security and a wide variety of mechanisms have been developed to realize this goal.</u> The first issue governments face in achieving national food security is the problem of insuring that adequate amounts of food are available to the resident population. ⓑ <u>Some governments have set goals of food self-sufficiency, which means most if not all of the food available in a country come from the domestic farming system.</u> ⓒ <u>However, food security does not require food self-sufficiency because countries can import food items not easy produced within the country.</u> Agricultural products are, after all, highly sensitive to climatic, soil and other conditions that tend to vary around the world. Even countries with extremely productive agricultural sectors are not fully self-sufficient in all food items. ⓓ <u>The United States, for example, depends on imports for its supply of coffee, tea, bananas and other tropical products.</u> ⓔ <u>In general, the problem of assuring adequate food supplies is solving by relying on both domestic production and imports.</u>
options: ① 5개
② 4개
③ 3개
④ 2개
⑤ 1개
questions.explanation: 틀린 문장은 ⓑ, ⓒ, ⓔ로 총 3개입니다. ⓑ: 'most... of the food'가 주어이므로 단수 동사인 comes가 와야 합니다. ⓒ: produced를 수식하는 부사 easily가 필요합니다. ⓔ: 문맥상 식량 공급을 확보하는 문제가 '해결된다'는 수동의 의미이므로 is solved가 적절합니다.

questions.question: 22. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ⓐ~ⓔ 중, 어법상 틀린 것의 개수는? [3.5점]
questions.passage: ⓐ <u>Dancers often push themselves to the limits of their physical capabilities.</u> But ⓑ <u>that push are misguided it is directed toward accomplishing something physically impossible.</u> For instance, ⓒ <u>a tall dancer with long feet may wish to perform repetitive vertical jumps to fast music, pointing his feet while in the air and lowered his heels to the floor between jumps.</u> That may be impossible no matter how strong the dancer is. But a short-footed dancer may have no trouble! Another dancer may be struggling to complete a half-turn in the air. ⓓ <u>Understanding the connection between a rapid turn rate and the alignment of the body close to the rotation axis tells her how to accomplish her turn successfully.</u> In both of these cases, ⓔ <u>understanding and working within the constraints imposed by nature and described by physical laws allows dancers work efficiently, minimizing potential risk of injury.</u>
options: ① 없음
② 1개
③ 2개
④ 3개
⑤ 4개
questions.explanation: 틀린 문장은 ⓑ, ⓒ, ⓔ로 총 3개입니다. ⓑ: 주어 push가 단수이므로 is가 와야 하며, 접속사 if가 빠져 있습니다. ⓒ: pointing과 병렬 구조를 이루어야 하므로 lowering이 적절합니다. ⓔ: allow는 목적격 보어로 to-부정사를 취하므로 to work가 되어야 합니다.

questions.question: 24. 다음 글의 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 말로 가장 알맞은 것은? [3.9점]
questions.passage: We are the only species that seasons its food, deliberately altering it with the highly flavored plant parts we call herbs and spices. It's quite possible that our taste for spices has an evolutionary root. Many spices have antibacterial properties-( A ), common seasonings such as garlic, onion, and oregano inhibit the growth of almost every bacterium tested. And the cultures that make the heaviest use of spices-think of the garlic and black pepper of Thai food, the ginger and coriander of India, the chili peppers of Mexico-come from warmer climates, where bacterial spoilage is a bigger issue. ( B ), the most lightly spiced cuisines-those of Scandinavia and northern Europe-are from cooler climates. Our uniquely human attention to flavor, in this case the flavor of spices, turns out to have arisen as a matter of life and death.
options: ① Hence ∙∙∙∙∙∙ In fact
② In constant ∙∙∙∙∙∙ As a matter of fact
③ What is more ∙∙∙∙∙∙ As a result

questions.question: 1. 위 글의 주제로 가장 적절한 것은? [3.0점]
questions.passage:
My grandparents sell their delicious organic jam at the local market every weekend. I went to help them last weekend. (A) ________, they had already sold all of their jam! They didn't have enough strawberries to make any more jam. That evening, I sat by the window and stared out at the empty field behind their house. Suddenly, I got an idea. The field would be the perfect place for a larger greenhouse. Then they could grow more strawberries! I immediately started searching for a way, and I found the perfect solution. I would start a crowdfunding campaign! My grandparents were thrilled when I told them my idea. With the help of investors, we could build a large greenhouse and grow a lot more strawberries. (B) ________, we could reward the investors for their help by sending them jars of organic jam! With this plan in mind, the next step was to figure out the details.
Before beginning your campaign, be sure to plan all the production details. How many products will you make? How long will it take to make the product? This planning is important because your potential investors will want to see a clear schedule. Once your plan is complete, remember to set your funding goal. It should be enough to complete the project and fulfill the rewards for the investors. Consider all the necessary costs before deciding on the amount. After doing some calculations, we decided on an 8 by 12 foot greenhouse. We thought it would cost approximately $4,000. Once it was built, we could fill it with strawberry plants and expect a harvest within about four months. Then it would take a few weeks to turn the strawberries into delicious jam. We decided to set our funding goal at $5,000 to cover all the costs. Also, we planned to run the campaign for three months. I was really excited when I filled out the form to launch the campaign. In less than a week, our application was accepted and funding began!

questions.question: 5. Adolescent anger에 관한 다음 글의 내용과 일치하는 것은? [3.0점]
questions.passage: Do you ever find yourself suddenly feeling angry? One moment you're fine, and the next moment you're slamming doors or rolling your eyes at your parents. Some people may think you just have a bad attitude or are getting too upset about a small problem. However, these feelings don't simply come from stress about everyday life. As a teen, you may feel like an adult, but your brain is still growing. In your brain, there is a part that is responsible for solving problems and controlling your emotions. In your teen years, this part is still in development. The changes in your brain lead you toward independence, social engagement, and creativity. At the same time, however, you may feel confused about who you are. You may also be more sensitive to unfairness. Furthermore, your body is flowing with hormones. This significantly affects your mood. The combination of these factors intensifies your strong emotions.

② 문을 쾅 닫거나 눈을 치켜떠야 화가 풀린다.
③ 대부분 일상생활에서 오는 스트레스가 원인이다.
④ 청소년의 뇌는 화가 나는 경우 이를 제어하는 부분이 없다.
⑤ 청소년의 기분은 호르몬의 영향을 크게 받는다.

questions.question: 7. 밑줄 친 <u>the other way around</u>가 다음 글에서 의미하는 바로 가장 적절한 것은? [3.2점]

questions.question: 8. 다음 글의 제목으로 가장 적절한 것은? [3.1점]
questions.passage: The rate of speed at which one is traveling will greatly determine the ability to process detail in the environment. In evolutionary terms, human senses are adapted to the speed at which humans move through space under their own power while walking. Our ability to distinguish detail in the environment is therefore ideally suited to movement at speeds of perhaps five miles per hour and under. The fastest users of the street, motorists, therefore have a much more limited ability to process details along the street — a motorist simply has little time or ability to appreciate design details. On the other hand, pedestrian travel, being much slower, allows for the appreciation of environmental detail. Joggers and bicyclists fall somewhere in between these polar opposites; while they travel faster than pedestrians, their rate of speed is ordinarily much slower than that of the typical motorist.
