questions.passage: Every species has certain climatic requirements - what degree of heat or cold it can endure, for example. When the climate changes, the places that satisfy those requirements change, too. Species are forced to follow. All creatures are capable of some degree of movement. Even creatures that appear immobile, like trees and barnacles, are capable of dispersal at some stage of their life - as a seed, in the case of the tree, or as a larva, in the case of the barnacle. A creature must get from the place it is born - often occupied by its parent - to a place where it can survive, grow, and reproduce. From fossils, scientists know that even creatures like trees moved with surprising speed during past periods of climate change.
options: ① 생물들은 이동할 때마다 새로운 종으로 진화한다.
② 생물들이 이동하는 속도는 기후 변화에 따라 달라진다.
③ 기후 변화에 따라 종들은 새로운 환경을 찾아 이동해야 한다.
④ 생물들은 새로운 환경 변화에 적응하지 않고, 정체된 채로 살아간다.
⑤ 기후 변화에 대한 대응으로 생물들이 적응하는 방식에 대한 연구가 중요하다.
questions.explanation: 지문은 모든 종이 특정한 기후 요구 조건을 가지고 있으며, 기후가 변화하면 그 조건을 충족하는 장소로 이동해야 한다는 점을 설명하고 있다. 나무나 따개비처럼 움직이지 않는 것처럼 보이는 생물들도 생애의 어느 단계에서는 분산과 이동을 통해 새로운 환경을 찾아간다는 내용이 핵심이므로 ③번이 정답이다.

questions.question: [9~11] 다음 글의 요지로 가장 적절한 것을 고르시오.
questions.passage: The mind has parts that are known as the conscious mind and the subconscious mind. The subconscious mind is very fast to act and doesn't deal with emotions. It deals with memories of your responses to life, your memories and recognition. However, the conscious mind is the one that you have more control over. You think. You can choose whether to carry on a thought or to add emotion to it and this is the part of your mind that lets you down frequently because - fueled by emotions - you make the wrong decisions time and time again. When your judgment is clouded by emotions, this puts in biases and all kinds of other negativities that hold you back. Scared of spiders? Scared of the dark? There are reasons for all of these fears, but they originate in the conscious mind. They only become real fears when the subconscious mind records your reactions.
options: ① 당신의 어떤 생각에 감정을 더하면 세웠던 목표를 슬그머니 접어 두게 된다.
② 모든 부정적 사고와 편견이 자리잡는 이면에는 두려움이 도사리고 있다.
③ 거미와 어두움을 두려워하는 것은 보편적인 것이며 타당한 이유가 있다.
④ 무의식적 마음의 기억과 인식의 축적은 의식적 마음의 판단과 관계가 없다.
⑤ 의식적 마음이 인식한 생각과 감정이 잠재의식적 마음에 축적되어 실제 두려움을 형성한다.
questions.explanation: 지문은 의식적 마음에서 감정이 더해진 생각이나 판단이 내려지고, 이러한 반응을 잠재의식적 마음(무의식)이 기록할 때 비로소 실제적인 두려움(fear)이나 편견이 형성된다고 설명하고 있다. 따라서 ⑤번이 글의 요지로 가장 적절하다.

questions.question: [9~11] 다음 글의 요지로 가장 적절한 것을 고르시오.
questions.passage: Plato argued that when you see something that strikes you as beautiful, you are really just seeing a partial reflection of true beauty, just as a painting or even a photograph only captures part of the real thing. True beauty, or what Plato calls the Form of Beauty, has no particular color, shape, or size. Rather, it is an abstract idea, like the number five. You can make drawings of the number five in blue or red ink, big or small, but the number five itself is none of those things. It has no physical form. Think of the idea of a triangle, for example. Although it has no particular color or size, it somehow lies within each and every triangle you see. Plato thought the same was true of beauty. The Form of Beauty somehow lies within each and every beautiful thing you see.
options: ① Photographs and paintings capture reality exactly as it is.
② True beauty exists as an abstract concept, not as a physical property.
③ Beauty is a relative concept that is perceived differently by each person.
④ True beauty can be fully experienced through the physical features of beautiful objects.
⑤ Mathematical concepts are generally considered to be unrelated to any form of artistic beauty.
questions.explanation: 플라톤은 진정한 아름다움(아름다움의 형상)이 특정한 색상, 모양, 크기가 없는 추상적인 관념(abstract idea)이라고 주장했다. 우리가 보는 개별적인 아름다운 사물들은 그 진정한 아름다움의 부분적인 반영일 뿐이므로, ②번이 가장 적절한 요지이다.
options_translation: ① 사진과 그림은 현실을 있는 그대로 포착한다.
② 진정한 아름다움은 물리적 특성이 아닌 추상적 개념으로 존재한다.
③ 아름다움은 사람마다 다르게 인식되는 상대적인 개념이다.
④ 진정한 아름다움은 아름다운 물체의 물리적 특징을 통해 충분히 경험될 수 있다.
⑤ 수학적 개념은 일반적으로 어떠한 형태의 예술적 아름다움과도 관련이 없는 것으로 간주된다.

questions.question: 다음 글의 주제로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: In many sports, people realized the difficulties and even impossibilities of young children participating fully in many adult sport environments. They found the road to success for young children is unlikely if they play on adult fields, courts or arenas with equipment that is too large, too heavy or too fast for them to handle while trying to compete in adult-style competition. Common sense has prevailed: different sports have made adaptations for children. As examples, baseball has T ball, football has flag football and junior soccer uses a smaller and lighter ball and (sometimes) a smaller field. All have junior competitive structures where children play for shorter time periods and often in smaller teams. In a similar way, tennis has adapted the court areas, balls and rackets to make them more appropriate for children under 10. The adaptations are progressive and relate to the age of the child.
options: ① how sports change to fit players' needs
② creating child-friendly sports adjustments
③ sports modifications to suit grown-up athletes
④ physiological arrangements for children's growth
⑤ the road to academic success for young children
questions.explanation: 이 글은 성인용 경기장이나 장비가 아이들에게 부적합하다는 점을 인식하여, 아이들의 연령과 신체 조건에 맞게 경기 방식, 장비, 경기장 크기 등을 조정한 사례들(티볼, 플래그 풋볼, 주니어 테니스 등)을 설명하고 있다. 따라서 주제는 '아이 친화적인 스포츠 조정안의 마련'인 ②번이 가장 적절하다.
options_translation: ① 선수들의 필요에 맞게 스포츠가 변화하는 방식
② 어린이 친화적인 스포츠 조정안 만들기
③ 성인 운동선수들에게 맞춘 스포츠 수정
④ 아이들의 성장을 위한 생리적 배치
⑤ 어린 아이들의 학업적 성공으로 가는 길

questions.question: 밑줄 친 'curse of knowledge'가 다음 글에서 의미하는 바로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: A number of research studies have shown how experts in a field often experience difficulties when introducing newcomers to that field. For example, in a genuine training situation, Dr Pamela Hinds found that people expert in using mobile phones were remarkably less accurate than novice phone users in judging how long it takes people to learn to use the phones. Experts can become insensitive to how hard a task is for the beginner, an effect referred to as the <u>'curse of knowledge'</u>. Dr Hinds was able to show that as people acquired the skill, they then began to underestimate the level of difficulty of that skill. Her participants even underestimated how long it had taken themselves to acquire that skill in an earlier session. Knowing that experts forget how hard it was for them to learn, we can understand the need to look at the learning process through students' eyes, rather than making assumptions about how students 'should be' learning.
options: ① the difficulty novices face in understanding expert explanations
② experts' natural advantage in learning new information quickly
③ the tendency of novices to acquire skills much more slowly than experts
④ experts' awareness to recognize the challenges of explaining their knowledge
⑤ the tendency of experts not to be aware of the difficulty of a skill for novices
questions.explanation: 지문은 전문가가 자신이 가진 지식 때문에 초보자가 겪는 어려움을 과소평가하거나 인지하지 못하는 현상을 설명하고 있습니다. 따라서 'curse of knowledge'는 전문가들이 초보자에게 어떤 기술이 얼마나 어려운지 인식하지 못하는 경향을 의미합니다.
options_translation: ① 전문가의 설명을 이해하는 데 초보자가 겪는 어려움
② 새로운 정보를 빠르게 학습하는 데 있어 전문가가 갖는 타고난 이점
③ 초보자가 전문가보다 훨씬 더 느리게 기술을 습득하는 경향
④ 자신의 지식을 설명하는 데 따르는 어려움을 인식하는 전문가의 자각
⑤ 전문가가 초보자에게 어떤 기술의 난이도를 인지하지 못하는 경향

questions.question: 다음 글의 제목으로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: A group of psychologists studied individuals with severe mental illness who experienced weekly group music therapy, including singing familiar songs and composing original songs. The results showed that the group music therapy improved the quality of participants' life, with those participating in a greater number of sessions experiencing the greatest benefits. Focusing on singing, another group of psychologists reviewed articles on the efficacy of group singing as a mental health treatment for individuals living with a mental health condition in a community setting. The findings showed that, when people with mental health conditions participated in a choir, their mental health and wellbeing significantly improved. Group singing provided enjoyment, improved emotional states, developed a sense of belonging and enhanced self-confidence.
options: ① The Benefits That Wellbeing Brings Us
② The Kinds of Treatments for Mental Illnesses
③ How to Improve One's Life? Music Is the Answer!
④ New Findings to Overcome Mental Health Conditions
⑤ The Group Music Therapy Effective For Mental Illness
questions.explanation: 지문은 집단 음악 치료(노래 부르기, 작곡 등)가 정신 질환을 앓고 있는 사람들의 삶의 질과 정신 건강, 웰빙을 향상시킨다는 연구 결과를 다루고 있습니다. 따라서 '정신 질환에 효과적인 집단 음악 치료'가 가장 적절한 제목입니다.
options_translation: ① 웰빙이 우리에게 가져다주는 혜택
② 정신 질환 치료의 종류
③ 삶을 개선하는 방법? 음악이 정답이다!
④ 정신 건강 상태를 극복하기 위한 새로운 발견들
⑤ 정신 질환에 효과적인 집단 음악 치료

questions.question: 다음 글에서 필자가 주장하는 바로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: No two animals are alike. Animals from the same litter will display some similar features but will not be exactly the same as each other; therefore, they may not respond in exactly the same way during a healing session. Environmental factors can also determine how an animal will respond to treatment. For instance, a cat in a rescue center will respond very differently from a cat in a domestic home environment. In addition, animals receiving healing for physical illness will react differently from those receiving healing for emotional distress. With this in mind, every healing session needs to be approached differently, and each healing treatment should be adjusted to suit the specific needs of the animal. You will learn as you go; healing is a constant learning process.
options: ① Animals born from the same litter should be treated using the same method.
② An appropriate environment should be created to suit each individual animal.
③ Physical illnesses and emotional distress factors in animals should be quickly eliminated.
④ Customized treatment should be provided according to the specific needs of each individual animal.
⑤ Animals in rescue shelters are vulnerable to disease and should be raised in a home environment.
questions.explanation: 지문은 동물마다 개별적인 특징, 환경적 요인, 질환의 종류가 다르기 때문에 각 동물의 구체적인 요구에 맞추어 치료 방식이 조정되어야 한다고 강조하고 있습니다.
options_translation: ① 같은 배에서 태어난 동물들은 동일한 방법으로 치료되어야 한다.
② 각 개별 동물에 맞게 적절한 환경이 조성되어야 한다.
③ 동물의 신체적 질병과 정서적 고통 요인은 빠르게 제거되어야 한다.
④ 각 개별 동물의 구체적인 필요에 따라 맞춤형 치료가 제공되어야 한다.
⑤ 구조 센터의 동물들은 질병에 취약하므로 가정 환경에서 길러져야 한다.

questions.question: 다음 글의 내용과 일치하지 않는 것은? [3.3점]
questions.passage: Our skin conducts electricity more or less efficiently, depending on our emotions. We know that when we're emotionally stimulated - stressed, sad, any intense emotion, really - our bodies sweat a tiny bit, so little we might not even notice. And when those tiny drops of sweat appear, our skin gets more electrically conductive. This change in sweat gland activity happens completely without your conscious mind having much say in the matter. If you feel emotionally intense, you're going to notice an increase in sweat gland activity. This is particularly useful from a scientific viewpoint, because it allows us to put an objective value on a subjective state of mind. We can actually measure your emotional state by tracking how your body subconsciously sweats, by running a bit of electricity through your skin. We can then turn the subjective, subconscious experience of emotional intensity into an objective number by figuring out how good your skin gets at transferring an electrical current.
options: ① 감정적으로 자극을 받을 때, 우리 몸은 미세한 양의 땀을 분비한다.
② 땀이 나면 피부의 전기 전도성이 증가한다.
③ 땀샘 활동의 변화는 우리의 의식적인 통제와 상관없이 발생한다.
④ 피부에 전기를 흘려보내 어떻게 땀을 흘리는지를 추적하여 사람의 감정 상태를 측정할 수 있다.
⑤ 우리는 감정의 강도를 객관적인 경험에서 주관적인 수치로 변환할 수 있다.
questions.explanation: 지문의 마지막 문장에서 주관적인 경험(subjective experience)을 객관적인 수치(objective number)로 바꿀 수 있다고 했으므로, 5번의 '객관적인 경험에서 주관적인 수치로'라는 진술은 반대로 되어 있어 일치하지 않습니다.

questions.question:
[20~22] 다음 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것을 고르시오.

[3.3점]
questions.passage: In the course of trying to solve a problem with an invention, you may encounter a brick wall of resistance when you try to think your way logically through the problem. Such logical thinking is a linear type of process, which uses our reasoning skills. This works fine when we're operating in the area of what we know or have experienced. However, when we need to deal with new information, ideas, and viewpoints, linear thinking will often come up short. On the other hand, creativity by definition involves the application of new information to old problems and the conception of new viewpoints and ideas. For this you will be most effective if you learn _______________________________________; that is, use your creative brain. Stated differently, if you think in a linear manner, you'll tend to be conservative and keep coming up with techniques which are already known. This, of course, is just what you don't want.
options: to use linear thinking
to hold a step-by-step approach
to operate in a nonlinear manner
to take a predictable and organized formula
to keep a logical, sequential way of thinking
questions.explanation: 지문은 발명에서 문제를 해결할 때 기존의 논리적이고 선형적인 사고방식은 이미 알고 있는 영역에서는 효과적이지만, 새로운 정보나 아이디어를 다루는 창의성이 필요할 때는 한계가 있다고 설명합니다. 따라서 창의적인 뇌를 사용한다는 것은 선형적인 방식에서 벗어난 '비선형적인 방식(nonlinear manner)'으로 사고하는 법을 배우는 것을 의미합니다.
options_translation: ① 선형적 사고를 사용하는 것
② 단계별 접근 방식을 유지하는 것
③ 비선형적인 방식으로 작동하는 것
④ 예측 가능하고 체계적인 공식을 취하는 것
⑤ 논리적이고 순차적인 사고 방식을 유지하는 것

questions.question:
[20~22] 다음 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것을 고르시오.

[3.4점]
questions.passage: Plants can communicate, although not in the same way we do. Some express their discontent through scents. You know that smell that hangs in the air after you've mowed the lawn? Yeah, that's actually an SOS. Some plants use sound. Yes, sound, though at a frequency that we can't hear. Researchers experimented with plants and microphones to see if they could record any trouble calls. They found that plants produce a high-frequency clicking noise when stressed and can make different sounds for different stressors. The sound a plant makes when it's not getting watered differs from the one it'll make when a leaf is cut. However, it's worth noting that experts don't think plants are crying out in pain. It's more likely that these reactions are knee-jerk survival actions. Plants are living organisms, and their main objective is to survive. Scents and sounds are their tools _______________________________________
options: to safeguard against excessive growth
to shield themselves from external hazards
to establish dominance over other nearby plants
to consciously deliver psychological pain to objects
to disregard their distress through conscious signaling
questions.explanation: 식물이 내뿜는 냄새나 소리는 감정적인 고통의 표현이 아니라 생존을 위한 본능적인 반응(knee-jerk survival actions)이라고 설명되어 있습니다. 생물의 주요 목표가 생존이라는 점을 고려할 때, 이러한 통신 수단은 외부의 위험이나 위협(external hazards)으로부터 자신을 보호하기 위한 도구로 쓰인다는 내용이 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 과도한 성장에 대비하여 방어하기 위해
② 외부 위험으로부터 자신을 보호하기 위해
③ 근처의 다른 식물들에 대한 우위를 확립하기 위해
④ 대상에게 의식적으로 심리적 고통을 전달하기 위해
⑤ 의식적인 신호 전달을 통해 그들의 고통을 무시하기 위해

questions.question: 글의 흐름으로 보아, 주어진 문장이 들어가기에 가장 적절한 곳은? [3.3점]
questions.passage: Routines enable athletes to evaluate competition conditions. ( ① ) For example, bouncing a ball in a volleyball service routine supplies the server with information about the ball, the floor, and the state of her muscles. ( ② ) Routines also enable athletes to adjust and fine-tune their preparations based on those evaluations or in pursuit of a particular competitive goal. ( ③ ) This adaptation can involve adjustment to the conditions, rivals, competitive situation, or internal influences that can affect performance. ( ④ ) Just like adjusting a race-car engine to the conditions of the track, air temperature, and weather, routines adjust all competitive components to achieve proper performance. ( ⑤ )
questions.insertion_sentence: This information can then be used to properly prepare for her serve.
options: ①
②
③
④
⑤
questions.explanation: 주어진 문장의 'This information'은 ① 뒤의 문장에서 언급된 배구 서버가 공을 튀기면서 얻는 '공, 바닥, 근육 상태에 대한 정보'를 의미합니다. 정보를 얻었다는 내용 바로 뒤에 그 정보가 어떻게 사용되는지(서브를 적절히 준비하는 데 사용됨)가 이어지는 것이 논리적이므로 ②가 가장 적절한 위치입니다.

questions.question: 주어진 글 다음에 이어질 글의 순서로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: One of the most striking characteristics of a sleeping animal or person is that they do not respond normally to environmental stimuli.
ordered_passages: (A) Stimuli are registered but not processed normally and they fail to wake the individual. Perceptual disengagement probably serves the function of protecting sleep, so some authors do not count it as part of the definition of sleep itself.

(B) But as sleep would be impossible without it, it seems essential to its definition. Nevertheless, many animals (including humans) use the intermediate state of drowsiness to derive some benefits of sleep without total perceptual disengagement.

(C) If you open the eyelids of a sleeping mammal the eyes will not see normally - they are functionally blind. Some visual information apparently gets in, but it is not normally processed as it is shortened or weakened; same with the other sensing systems.
questions.explanation: 주어진 문장에서 수면 중인 동물의 환경 자극에 대한 반응 부족을 언급한 후, (C)에서 눈을 뜬 포유류의 예시를 통해 구체적인 감각 차단을 설명합니다. (A)에서 이러한 자극이 처리되지 않아 잠을 보호하는 '지각적 단절(Perceptual disengagement)'의 기능을 설명하고, (B)에서 'it(지각적 단절)'이 수면의 정의에 필수적임을 역설하며 마무리하는 것이 자연스럽습니다.

questions.question: 28. 주어진 글 다음에 이어질 글의 순서로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: The tongue was mapped into separate areas where certain tastes were registered: sweetness at the tip, sourness on the sides, and bitterness at the back of the mouth.
ordered_passages: (A) Moreover, the mechanism at work is not place, but time. It's not that you taste sweetness at the tip of your tongue, but rather that you register that perception first.

(B) Research in the 1980s and 1990s, however, demonstrated that the "tongue map" explanation of how we taste was, in fact, totally wrong. As it turns out, the map was a misinterpretation and mistranslation of research conducted in Germany at the turn of the twentieth century.

(C) Today, leading taste researchers believe that taste buds are not grouped according to specialty. Sweetness, saltiness, bitterness, and sourness can be tasted everywhere in the mouth, although they may be perceived at a little different intensities at different sites.
questions.explanation: 주어진 글에서 언급한 혀의 특정 부위에 따른 맛의 지도가 잘못되었음을 (B)에서 연구 결과를 통해 제시하고, (C)에서 모든 부위에서 모든 맛을 느낄 수 있다는 현재의 연구 결과를 설명하며, 마지막으로 (A)에서 장소가 아닌 시간의 메커니즘이 작용함을 추가 설명하는 순서가 가장 적절합니다.

questions.question:
[29~30] 다음 글의 내용을 한 문장으로 요약하고자 한다. 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것을 고르시오.

29.
questions.passage: It would be hard to overstate how important meaningful work is to human beings - work that provides a sense of fulfillment and empowerment. Those who have found deeper meaning in their careers find their days much more energizing and satisfying, and count their employment as one of their greatest sources of joy and pride. Sonya Lyubomirsky, professor of psychology at the University of California, has conducted numerous workplace studies showing that when people are more fulfilled on the job, they not only produce higher quality work and a greater output, but also generally earn higher incomes. Those most satisfied with their work are also much more likely to be happier with their lives overall. For her book Happiness at Work, researcher Jessica Pryce-Jones conducted a study of 3,000 workers in seventy-nine countries, finding that those who took greater satisfaction from their work were 150 percent more likely to have a happier life overall.
questions.summary_sentence: Meaningful work significantly (A)____ job satisfaction, productivity, and income, (B)______ a greater sense of overall life fulfillment and happiness, as evidenced by research.
options: ① boosts ..... hindering
② elevates ..... fostering
③ enhances ..... preventing
④ diminishes ..... promoting
⑤ undermines ..... supporting
questions.explanation: 의미 있는 일은 직무 만족도, 생산성 및 수입을 향상시키며(elevates), 전반적인 삶의 만족감과 행복을 촉진한다(fostering)는 내용이 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 강화하다 ..... 방해하는
② 높이다 ..... 촉진하는
③ 향상시키다 ..... 예방하는
④ 줄이다 ..... 증진하는
⑤ 약화시키다 ..... 지지하는

questions.question:
[29~30] 다음 글의 내용을 한 문장으로 요약하고자 한다. 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것을 고르시오.

30.
questions.passage: Piaget put the same amount of water into two different glasses: a tall narrow glass and a wide glass, then asked kids to compare two glasses. Kids younger than six or seven usually say that the tall narrow glass now holds more water, because the level is higher. And when they are ready, they figure out the conservation of volume for themselves just by playing with cups of water. Piaget argued that children's understanding of morality is like their understanding of those water glasses: we can't say that it is inborn or kids learn it directly from adults. Rather, kids naturally construct their understanding as they play with other kids. Taking turns in a game is like pouring water back and forth between glasses. Once kids have reached the age of five or six, then playing games and working things out together will help them learn about fairness far more effectively than any teaching from adults.
questions.summary_sentence: Piaget proposed that children's understanding of fairness, much like their understanding of the conservation of volume in the water glasses experiment, is not (A)____ or directly taught by adults, but instead is self-constructed through peer (B)____ and collaborative play.
options: ① innate ..... arguments
② acquired ..... negotiations
③ innate ..... depressions
④ acquired ..... supports
⑤ innate ..... interactions
questions.explanation: 피아제는 공정성에 대한 아이들의 이해가 타고난(innate/inborn) 것이 아니라, 또래와의 상호작용(interactions) 및 놀이를 통해 스스로 구성된다고 주장했습니다.
options_translation: ① 타고난 ..... 논쟁
② 습득된 ..... 협상
③ 타고난 ..... 우울
④ 습득된 ..... 지지
⑤ 타고난 ..... 상호작용

questions.question: 12. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것을 고르시오. [3.5점]
questions.passage: Have you ever heard of the "Eiffel Tower Effect?" When the Eiffel Tower was first built, the iron tower was very ① <u>distinct</u> from all the other architecture in Paris, which was mainly made of stone. Many local people ② <u>objected</u> to the tower and protested that it would ruin the beauty of Paris. Nevertheless, as the locals became familiar with the tower due to exposure, they became more and more ③ <u>attached</u> to it, referring to it as the Tower of Love. This effect, also called the "Mere Exposure Effect," is found with people, too. Psychologist Robert Zajonc and his colleagues showed university students pictures of several faces. Some pictures were shown 25 times while others were shown only once or twice. Then, the students were shown a picture and asked to express how much they liked that person. The students liked the people they had seen less frequently ④ <u>more</u> than those they had seen more often! This shows that the more we are exposed to something, the more ⑤ <u>positively</u> we view it.
questions.explanation: 단순 노출 효과(Mere Exposure Effect)에 따르면 자주 본 것일수록 더 좋아하게 되므로, 적게 본 사람을 자주 본 사람보다 '더(more)' 좋아했다는 내용은 실험 결과와 일치하지 않는다. '덜(less)' 혹은 반대의 의미가 되어야 한다.

questions.question: 23. 글의 흐름으로 보아, 주어진 문장이 들어가기에 가장 적절한 곳은? [2.6점]
questions.passage: People wear tuxedos when a formal dress code is required, like for the opera, dinner parties, or awards shows. The tuxedo likely got its name from Tuxedo Park, one of the first gated communities in New York. In the late 19th century, men usually wore jackets with long tails that reached their knees on formal occasions. ( ① ) The male guests who stayed there were fascinated by the new jacket and started to wear the same style. ( ② ) Later, more people asked their tailors to make them a jacket "like the one worn in Tuxedo Park." ( ③ ) At first, this style of jacket was considered less formal than one with long tails. ( ④ ) As more and more men wore the shorter style, it eventually replaced the longer version. ( ⑤ ) Now men's formal wear is the tuxedo.
questions.insertion_sentence: One evening, a man showed up with a short black jacket without tails in Tuxedo Park.
questions.explanation: 주어진 문장은 턱시도 파크에 꼬리가 없는 짧은 자켓을 입은 남자가 나타났다는 내용입니다. ①번 뒷문장에서 '그곳에 머물던 남성 손님들이 그 새로운 자켓에 매료되었다'는 내용이 이어지므로, 새로운 자켓(주어진 문장의 short black jacket)이 처음 등장한 시점인 ①번 위치가 가장 적절합니다.

questions.question: 2. 다음 글의 주제로 가장 적절한 것을 고르시오. [2.9점]
questions.passage: The governments of virtually every country on the planet attach great importance to achieving food security and a wide variety of mechanisms have been developed to realize this goal. The first issue governments face in achieving national food security is the problem of insuring that adequate amounts of food are available to the resident population. Some governments have set goals of food self-sufficiency, which means most if not all of the food available in a country comes from the domestic farming system. However, food security does not require food self-sufficiency because countries can import food items not easily produced within the country. Agricultural products are, after all, highly sensitive to climatic, soil and other conditions that tend to vary around the world. Even countries with extremely productive agricultural sectors are not fully self-sufficient in all food items. The United States, for example, depends on imports for its supply of coffee, tea, bananas and other tropical products. In general, the problem of assuring adequate food supplies is solved by relying on both domestic production and imports.
options: ① challenges of food supplies in the United States
② dangers of overreliance on domestic production
③ unsolvable problems countries face in obtaining palatable food
④ strategies of the governments to guarantee national food security
⑤ necessity of food self-sufficiency to maintain enough amounts of food
questions.explanation: 정부가 국가 식량 안보를 달성하기 위해 식량 자급자족뿐만 아니라 수입을 활용하는 등 다양한 전략적 메커니즘을 사용한다는 내용의 글이므로 주제는 ④번이 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 미국의 식량 공급의 어려움
② 국내 생산에 대한 과도한 의존의 위험성
③ 맛있는 음식을 얻는 데 있어 국가들이 직면하는 해결 불가능한 문제들
④ 국가 식량 안보를 보장하기 위한 정부의 전략들
⑤ 충분한 양의 식량을 유지하기 위한 식량 자급자족의 필요성

questions.question: 3. 다음 글의 주제로 가장 적절한 것을 고르시오.[2.8점]
questions.passage: When we realize we've said something in error and we pause to go back to correct it, we stop gesturing a couple of hundred milliseconds before we stop speaking. Such sequences suggest the startling notion that our hands "know" what we're going to say before our conscious minds do, and in fact this is often the case. Gesture can mentally prime a word so that the right term comes to our lips. When people are prevented from gesturing, they talk less fluently; their speech becomes halting because their hands are no longer able to supply them with the next word, and the next. Not being able to gesture has other deleterious effects: without gesture to help our mental processes along, we remember less useful information, we solve problems less well, and we are less able to explain our thinking. Far from tagging along as speech's clumsy companion, gesture represents the leading edge of our thought.
options: ① gesture as a catalyst for our thought
② how our mind dominates our hands
③ limitations of nonverbal communication
④ evolution of language and its components
⑤ cognitive drawbacks of nonverbal communication
questions.explanation: 이 글은 제스처가 언어보다 앞서서 사고를 촉진하고 돕는 역할을 한다는 내용을 담고 있으므로 주제로 ①번 '우리의 사고를 위한 촉매제로서의 제스처'가 가장 적절하다.
options_translation: ① 우리 사고의 촉매제로서의 제스처
② 우리 정신이 손을 지배하는 방식
③ 비언어적 의사소통의 한계
④ 언어와 그 구성 요소의 진화
⑤ 비언어적 의사소통의 인지적 단점

questions.question: 5. 밑줄 친 <u>recall threshold</u>가 다음 글에서 의미하는 바로 가장 적절한 것은? [3.3점]
questions.passage: Sometimes our brain has already stored someone's face and name but we end up remembering just his or her face. It's intensely annoying for us, who regularly have to make small talk with people we're certain we know but can't actually recall right now. That's the part most people can relate to, and in brain terms, we're stuck in the state of 'recognition' (just knowing the memory exists). There is a point where this recognition turns to full-on recall so that we finally come to 'recall' the original memory of how and why we know this person. Some scientists describe the point as a <u>recall threshold</u>. The desired memory has several other memories linked to it, and these are being triggered and cause a sort of peripheral or low-level stimulation of the target memory, like a darkened house being lit by a neighbor's fireworks display. But the target memory won't actually activate until it is stimulated above a specific level, or threshold. You've heard the phrase "it all came flooding back," or you would have recognized the sensation of a quiz answer being "on the tip of your tongue" and it suddenly occurred to you. That's what's happening here.
options: ① the moment when one achieves the explosive development of memory capacity
② the step where our brain remembers someone's face but fails to recall his or her name
③ the confusing transition that people go through in the process of taking in new information
④ the state where our brain is taking a break and has difficulty in getting stimulation from outside
⑤ the crucial level at which associated memories become increasingly familiar and the original memory is activated
questions.explanation: recall threshold는 단순한 인지(recognition) 상태에서 목표 기억이 특정 자극 수준 이상으로 활성화되어 온전한 회상(recall)으로 넘어가는 지점을 의미하므로 ⑤번이 가장 적절하다.
options_translation: ① 기억 용량의 폭발적인 발전을 달성하는 순간
② 우리 뇌가 누군가의 얼굴은 기억하지만 이름은 기억하지 못하는 단계
③ 사람들이 새로운 정보를 받아들이는 과정에서 겪는 혼란스러운 전이
④ 우리 뇌가 휴식을 취하고 외부 자극을 받는 데 어려움을 겪는 상태
⑤ 연관된 기억들이 점점 더 익숙해지고 원래의 기억이 활성화되는 결정적인 수준

questions.question: 12.다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것을 고르시오.[2.8점]
questions.passage: Why is the discovery of mirror neurons important? Mirror neurons play a crucial role in our understanding of the people around us. Mirror neurons provide us with a genuine comprehension of what it means to ①<u>empathize</u> with others. In other words, if it were not for the actions of mirror neurons, people would ②<u>struggle</u> more to comprehend the feelings of those around them. It is widely recognized that infants respond positively when their parents smile at them, while they react negatively to expressions of ③<u>dissatisfaction</u>. When a baby sees the facial expressions and body postures of others, mirror neurons ④<u>impede</u> the similar internal responses. Then their muscles ⑤<u>reflect</u> the same emotions. Children later grasp the feelings of others through mirror neurons and learn how to behave in an emotionally appropriate manner.
questions.explanation: 거울 뉴런은 타인의 행동이나 표정을 볼 때 관찰자 내부에서 유사한 반응을 이끌어내어 공감을 가능하게 합니다. 따라서 타인의 표정을 볼 때 거울 뉴런이 유사한 반응을 '방해(impede)'하는 것이 아니라 '활성화(activate)'하거나 '유발(trigger)'한다는 내용이 문맥상 적절합니다.

questions.question: 14.다음 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것을 고르시오. [3.1점]
questions.passage: In many instances, the borrowing of words or constructions flows primarily or wholly in one direction, from the more prestigious or powerful group to the less favored one. This is a reflection of ____________________ that frequently characterizes interactions between groups. Even though the languages of socially subordinated groups may offer vocabulary for things or practices that were previously unfamiliar with from a very early stage of contact, the impacts of contact in that direction may not go farther than this. In some cases, as with the Dharug language of Sydney, Australia, the source of some of the earliest loans from Indigenous Australian languages into English, the fate of the language system is extinction after the obliteration of many of its speakers. The remainder shifted to varieties of English, the language of the people who had suppressed them.
options: ① fear and anxiety
② the social inequality
③ thought and language
④ the reciprocal arrangement
⑤ the dominant market position
questions.explanation: 지문은 언어적 차용이 주로 권력이나 위계가 높은 집단에서 낮은 집단으로 흐른다는 점을 설명하며, 이는 집단 간의 상호작용에서 흔히 나타나는 '사회적 불평등'의 반영임을 나타내고 있습니다. 억압받는 집단의 언어가 소멸하거나 억압자의 언어로 대체되는 현상 또한 이러한 불평등을 뒷받침합니다.
options_translation: ① 공포와 불안
② 사회적 불평등
③ 사고와 언어
④ 호혜적 배열
⑤ 지배적인 시장 지위

questions.question: 16.다음 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것을 고르시오. [3.3점]
questions.passage: There are valid reasons for the lack of complete trust in science and the importance of healthy skepticism and critical thinking. Despite established professional standards, claims of objectivity, and the peer review process, scientific conduct can still be influenced by bias. All experts are not the same, nor do they submit their work to the same scrutiny. Knowing the source of funding can be important in evaluating scientific claims. For example, the Harvard researchers who made claims in the late 1960s about the problems with dietary fat, leading the nation away from perceiving sugar as one of the main causes in health problems, were funded in part by the sugar industry. The authors did not reveal their funding source to the New England Journal of Medicine, where their influential article appeared. Their article shaped a generation of changes in eating patterns that appears to have fostered higher use of sugar, now widely implicated as a source of the rise in obesity and diabetes. Such cases breed suspicion but also encourage the implementation of additional safeguards in the scientific process. The disclosures of funding source, although not required five decades ago, __________________________
options: ① have been deemed optional
② have been rendered obligatory
③ have been overlooked in practice
④ have been left to individual discretion
⑤ have been excluded from compulsory measures
questions.explanation: 글의 맥락상 과거에는 자금 출처 공개가 요구되지 않았지만, 설탕 산업의 자금 지원을 받은 하버드 연구진의 사례와 같은 문제가 의혹을 불러일으키고 과학 과정에서의 추가적인 안전장치(safeguards) 도입을 장려했다는 내용이 나옵니다. 따라서 빈칸에는 자금 출처 공개가 '의무화되었다'는 내용이 들어가는 것이 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 선택적인 것으로 간주되어 왔다
② 의무적인 것으로 만들어졌다
③ 실제 관행에서 간과되어 왔다
④ 개인의 재량에 맡겨져 왔다
⑤ 강제적인 조치에서 제외되어 왔다

questions.question: 18. 다음 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것을 고르시오.[3.4점]
questions.passage: As a general rule, it's better if your definition corresponds as closely as possible to the way in which the term is ordinarily used in the kinds of debates to which your claims are pertinent. There will be, however, occasions where it is appropriate, even necessary, to coin special uses through what philosophers call <u>stimulative definition</u>. This would be the case where the current lexicon __________________________ . For example, we do not have a term in ordinary language that describes a memory that is not necessarily a memory of something the person having it has experienced. Such a thing would occur, for example, if I could somehow share your memories: I would have a memory-type experience, but this would not be of something that I had actually experienced. To call this a memory would be misleading. For this reason, philosophers have coined the special term 'quasi-memory' to indicate these hypothetical memory-like experiences.
options: ① is used by both the general public and scholars
② has its origin from a specific academic context in the distant past
③ is able to represent the philosophical concepts that many cultures share
④ provides different meanings depending on the situations where it is used
⑤ cannot refer to something that needs to be philosophically differentiated
questions.explanation: 철학자들이 '약정적 정의(stimulative definition)'를 통해 특별한 용어를 만들어내는 상황은 현재의 어휘목록이 '철학적으로 구별될 필요가 있는 무언가를 지칭할 수 없을 때'입니다. 예시에서 '직접 경험하지 않은 기억'을 지칭할 일반적인 용어가 없어 '유사 기억(quasi-memory)'이라는 용어를 만든 것이 이를 뒷받침합니다.
options_translation: ① 일반 대중과 학자들 모두에 의해 사용된다
② 먼 과거의 특정 학문적 문맥에서 기원한다
③ 많은 문화권이 공유하는 철학적 개념을 표현할 수 있다
④ 사용되는 상황에 따라 다른 의미를 제공한다
⑤ 철학적으로 차별화되어야 할 무언가를 지칭할 수 없다

questions.question: 20.다음 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것을 고르시오. [3.4점]
questions.passage: It is crucial to understand that science is a creative process even though it follows rules. A conjecture is a philosophical invention that is mystically created by the mind through what is known as attentive contemplation. However, the hypothesis is merely information that represents speculation and is not yet truly knowledge until it is tested against reality. Knowledge is information that has demonstrated its usefulness. It is ___________________________. A sort of "learning loop" known to statisticians as Bayesian updating arises as scientists test their theories and adjust their models in response to fresh and unexpected facts. Based on the Bayes' Rule, which was created by the English statistician and philosopher Thomas Bayes in the seventeenth century, Bayesian updating is a mathematical procedure that involves repeatedly testing rival versions of an accepted theory or predictive model in order to increase its accuracy.
options: ①what remains after incorrect theories have been ruled out by rounds of experimental testing
②something scientists or mathematicians are reluctant to engage in because of its process
③merely a hypothesis based on guesswork without any mental calculations
④completely eliminated by a scientific procedure based on rules
⑤the way we differentiate between science and art
questions.explanation: 지문에서 지식은 유용성이 증명된 정보이며, 베이즈 업데이트(Bayesian updating)를 통해 이론을 테스트하고 수정하며 정확성을 높인다고 설명합니다. 따라서 지식은 반복적인 실험 테스트를 통해 잘못된 이론들이 배제된 후 남는 것(what remains after incorrect theories have been ruled out...)이라는 ①번이 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ①수차례의 실험 테스트를 통해 잘못된 이론들이 배제된 후 남는 것
②과학자들이나 수학자들이 그 과정 때문에 참여하기를 꺼리는 것
③어떠한 정신적 계산도 없이 추측에만 기반한 단순한 가설
④규칙에 기반한 과학적 절차에 의해 완전히 제거되는 것
⑤우리가 과학과 예술을 구분하는 방법

questions.question: 23. 주어진 글 다음에 이어질 글의 순서로 가장 적절한 것을 고르시오. [2.9점]
questions.passage: The prominence of the social dimension in food writing might suggest that the flavor of food is taking a back seat.
ordered_passages: (A) Once the hunger is satisfied, it creates the backdrop for whatever social dynamics characterize the gathering. These can be understood independently of the flavor of the food on offer, the appreciation of which is understood to be personal and subjective.

(B) In other words, the description in food writing indicates that people regard flavor as of secondary importance in social settings where food is served. It seems that the significance of our social gatherings is not influenced by flavor, despite the fact that our gatherings usually coalesce around food. Flavor serves the specific function of filling the belly.

(C) According to such perception about social meetings and food, the social events that supply food with its meaning, as well as the ceremonies and rituals around food, do not depend on the quality of sensations provided by the food. To focus excessively on flavor is to overlook these social relations' greater value.
questions.explanation: 주어진 글에서 음식 글쓰기에서 사회적 차원의 중요성이 맛의 중요성을 뒤로 밀어낼 수 있음을 시사한다. (B)에서 'In other words'를 사용하여 맛이 부차적임을 구체적으로 설명하며, 맛은 단지 배를 채우는 기능을 한다고 언급한다. (A)에서는 배가 채워진 후 사회적 역동성이 형성되며, 맛은 개인적이고 주관적인 것으로 이해된다고 덧붙인다. 마지막으로 (C)에서 'According to such perception'을 통해 음식의 의미를 부여하는 것은 감각적 품질(맛)이 아니라 사회적 사건과 관계임을 정리하며 마무리하는 것이 자연스럽다.

questions.question: 25. 글의 흐름으로 보아, 주어진 문장이 들어가기에 가장 적절한 곳을 고르시오. [2.7점]
questions.passage: Great scientists rarely achieve success with just a single breakthrough. A prime example is Isaac Newton, who, in addition to formulating Newtonian mechanics, also developed the theory of gravitation, calculus, the laws of motion, and optimization. ① In fact, well-known scientists are often involved in multiple discoveries, a phenomenon potentially explained by the Matthew effect. ② Indeed, an initial success may offer a scientist legitimacy, improve peer perception, provide knowledge of how to score and win, enhance social status, and attract resources and quality collaborators, each of these payoffs further increasing her odds of scoring another win. ③ Yet, there is an intriguing alternative explanation: Great scientists have multiple hits and consistently succeed in their scientific endeavors simply because they’re exceptionally talented. ④ In conclusion, the Matthew effect posits that success alone increases the future probability of success, raising the question: Does status dictate outcomes, or does it simply reflect an underlying talent or quality? ⑤ In other words, is there really a Matthew effect after all?
questions.insertion_sentence: Therefore, future success again goes to those who have had success earlier, not because of advantages offered by the previous success, but because the earlier success was indicative of a hidden talent.
questions.explanation: 주어진 문장은 이전의 성공이 숨겨진 재능의 지표였기 때문에 미래의 성공이 초기 성공을 거둔 사람들에게 돌아간다는 내용이다. 이는 ③번 문장에서 제시된 '재능 때문'이라는 대안적 설명을 구체화하는 문장이다. ④번 문장 뒤에서 마태 효과(성공이 성공을 부름)와 재능(성공이 능력을 반영함) 사이의 질문을 던지는 결론으로 이어지므로, 주어진 문장은 ④번 위치에 들어가는 것이 가장 적절하다.

questions.question: 1. 다음 글에서 'I'가 겪은 심경의 변화로 가장 적절한 것은? [2.4점]
questions.passage: I was sweating as I walked up to the front of the class. My heart was racing so fast that I thought it might fly out of my chest. I could feel my face turn red. I didn't know where to look. I blanked out. I just stood there silently. Ms. Harper tried to help me out. "Start by telling us a bit about your grandmother, Logan." I spoke about what kind of work my grandmother used to do, but I quickly ran out of words to say. Then Ms. Harper said, "How about telling us a bit about why you admire her so much?" Her question suddenly sparked memories of all the wonderful things I wanted to share. As I began describing her kindness, wisdom, and the important life lessons she taught me, my nervousness melted away and I found my voice growing stronger. Looking around at my classmates' interested faces, I realized I was actually enjoying sharing these precious memories of someone I loved so dearly.
options: ① discouraged → satisfied
② embarrassed → bored
③ nervous → annoyed
④ excited → nervous
⑤ comforted → anxious
questions.explanation: 글의 초반부에서 주인공은 발표를 앞두고 땀을 흘리고 심장이 뛰며 얼굴이 붉어지는 등 매우 긴장하고 당황한 상태였으나(nervous/embarrassed), 할머니에 대한 이야기를 나누며 마음이 편안해지고 즐거움을 느끼게 되는 과정(satisfied/enjoying)을 묘사하고 있습니다. 따라서 답은 '낙담한/낙심한(긴장한) → 만족한'의 흐름을 나타내는 ①번이 가장 적절합니다. (다만 nervous → relaxed 계열의 선택지가 없으므로, 초기 당황 상태에서 발표를 마친 후의 만족감으로 해석함)
options_translation: ① 낙담한 → 만족한
② 당황한 → 지루해하는
③ 긴장한 → 짜증난
④ 흥분한 → 긴장한
⑤ 위로받은 → 불안한

questions.question: 2. 다음 글의 요지로 가장 적절한 것은? [2.8점]
questions.passage: Whose story it is affects what the story is. Change the main character, and the focus of the story must also change. If we look at the events through another character's eyes, we will interpret them differently. We'll place our sympathies with someone new. When the conflict arises that is the heart of the story, we will be praying for a different outcome. Consider, for example, how the tale of Cinderella would shift if told from the viewpoint of an evil stepsister. Gone with the Wind is Scarlett O'Hara's story, but what if we were shown the same events from the viewpoint of Rhett Butler or Melanie Wilkes?
options: ① Conflicts within a story make it more interesting.
② Successful stories always have various characters.
③ Readers need to empathize with characters in a story.
④ Every story has characters who lead to main conflicts.
⑤ A main character of a story determines the flow of the story.
questions.explanation: 이야기의 주인공이 누구냐에 따라 이야기의 내용, 초점, 해석, 공감의 대상 등이 달라진다는 내용입니다. 따라서 소설의 주인공이 이야기의 흐름(flow)이나 내용을 결정한다는 ⑤번이 가장 적절한 요지입니다.
options_translation: ① 이야기 내의 갈등은 이야기를 더 흥미롭게 만든다.
② 성공적인 이야기는 항상 다양한 캐릭터를 가지고 있다.
③ 독자들은 이야기 속 캐릭터들에게 공감할 필요가 있다.
④ 모든 이야기에는 주요 갈등으로 이끄는 캐릭터들이 있다.
⑤ 이야기의 주인공이 이야기의 흐름을 결정한다.

questions.question: 3. 다음 글의 제목으로 가장 적절한 것은? [3.2점]
questions.passage: The rise of air-conditioning accelerated the construction of sealed boxes, where the building's only airflow is through the filtered ducts of the air-conditioning unit. It doesn't have to be this way. Look at any old building in a hot climate, whether it's in Sicily or Marrakesh or Tehran. Architects understood the importance of shade, airflow, light colors. They oriented buildings to capture cool breezes and block the worst heat of the afternoon. They built with thick walls and white roofs and transoms over doors to encourage airflow. Anyone who has ever spent a few minutes in a mudbrick house in Tucson, or walked on the narrow streets of old Seville, knows how well these construction methods work. But all this wisdom about how to deal with heat, accumulated over centuries of practical experience, is all too often ignored. In this sense, air-conditioning is not just a technology of personal comfort; it is also a technology of forgetting.
options: ① Centuries of Heat Management Wisdom Forgotten in Air-conditioning
② The Environmental Drawbacks of Modern Air-conditioning Systems
③ White Roofs and Thick Walls: The Science of Natural Cooling
④ Sealed Boxes: The Evolution of Modern Building Design
⑤ Air-conditioning: Lessons from Hot Climate Regions
questions.explanation: 현대의 에어컨 시스템이 보급되면서 수 세기 동안 축적되어 온 자연 냉각 방식의 지혜(그늘, 환기, 두꺼운 벽 등)가 무시되고 잊히게 되었다는 내용을 담고 있습니다. 에어컨이 '망각의 기술'이라고 표현된 점을 미루어 볼 때 ①번이 가장 적절한 제목입니다.
options_translation: ① 에어컨 속에서 잊힌 수 세기의 열 관리 지혜
② 현대 에어컨 시스템의 환경적 단점들
③ 하얀 지붕과 두꺼운 벽: 자연 냉각의 과학
④ 밀폐된 상자: 현대 건축 디자인의 진화
⑤ 에어컨: 더운 기후 지역으로부터의 교훈

questions.question: 4.다음 글의 주제로 가장 적절한 것을 고르시오. [2.9점]
questions.passage: If you want the confidence that comes from achieving what you set out to do each day, then it's important to understand how long things are going to take. Over-optimism about what can be achieved within a certain time frame is a problem. So work on it. Make a practice of estimating the amount of time needed alongside items on your 'things to do' list, and learn by experience when tasks take a greater or lesser time than expected. Give attention also to fitting the task to the available time. There are some tasks that you can only set about if you have a significant amount of time available. There is no point in trying to gear up for such a task when you only have a short period available. So schedule the time you need for the longer tasks and put the short tasks into the spare moments in between.
options: ① difficulty in discriminating between the important and the trivial
② how to predict and schedule tasks to reach daily goals
③ importance of confidence in successful achievement
④ participating in some form of competitive activities
⑤ developing some new leisure interests
questions.explanation: 매일 목표한 일을 달성하여 자신감을 얻기 위해서는 각 업무에 소요되는 시간을 정확히 추정하고, 가용 시간에 맞춰 계획을 세워야 한다는 내용입니다. 따라서 일일 목표 달성을 위해 업무를 예측하고 일정을 짜는 방법인 ②번이 정답입니다.
options_translation: ① 중요한 것과 사소한 것을 구별하는 것의 어려움
② 일일 목표 달성을 위해 업무를 예측하고 일정을 짜는 방법
③ 성공적인 성취에 있어서 자신감의 중요성
④ 어떤 형태의 경쟁 활동에 참여하기
⑤ 새로운 여가 관심사를 개발하기

questions.question: 5.다음 글의 주제로 가장 적절한 것을 고르시오. [2.8점]
questions.passage: Community mapping helped deal with the impact of Hurricane Sandy, one of the most destructive hurricanes to hit the United States. One of its main effects was energy failures. Residents in affected areas would wait for hours in line at gas stations, sometimes only to learn that they were out of gasoline. In response to this problem, a group of high school students in New Jersey worked together to create an online community map, publishing information on open gas stations with available fuel. The students gathered information from personal observations, calls to local gas stations, and updates from other social media users. The live data streams filled a significant community information gap.
options: ① the importance of communication skills for high school students
② the role of social media in providing useful information during difficult situations
③ volunteering at gas stations during an energy crisis resulting from Hurricane Sandy
④ using community mapping to solve local problems in the consequence of Hurricane Sandy
⑤ the need for faster recovery from the damages from Hurricane Sandy through government support
questions.explanation: 이 글은 허리케인 샌디로 인해 발생한 에너지 부족 문제(주유소 대기 시간 등)를 해결하기 위해 뉴저지의 고등학생들이 커뮤니티 매핑을 사용하여 연료가 있는 주유소 정보를 공유한 사례를 다루고 있습니다. 따라서 주제는 허리케인 샌디의 결과로 발생한 지역 문제를 해결하기 위해 커뮤니티 매핑을 사용하는 것인 ④번이 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 고등학생들에게 의사소통 기술의 중요성
② 어려운 상황에서 유용한 정보를 제공하는 소셜 미디어의 역할
③ 허리케인 샌디로 인한 에너지 위기 동안 주유소에서의 자원봉사
④ 허리케인 샌디의 여파로 지역 문제를 해결하기 위해 커뮤니티 매핑을 사용하는 것
⑤ 정부 지원을 통한 허리케인 샌디 피해의 빠른 복구 필요성

questions.question: 6. 밑줄 친 <u>a case in point</u>가 다음 글에서 의미하는 바로 가장 적절한 것은? [3.3점]
questions.passage: Mapping can also rally community members around the assets of their community such as libraries, community centers, and parks. Heritage and cultural attractions, like landmarks, museums, and public artworks, are also good sources for community mapping. Through marking assets on a map, people become aware of the strengths and resources of their own community and build a strong bond with it. Also, these maps can provide valuable data to be used for tourism or urban design. The mapping project Where in Wally (short for Walthamstow, UK) is <u>a case in point</u>. A team of architects undertook the project to find out what spots were loved by the locals. People told the team about their treasured places and the reasons why these places were special to them. The team then added the places to an online map and marked them in the real world with yellow tags. The map and tags invited people to go on a treasure hunt and told them colorful stories about the corners of Walthamstow.
options: ① a commercial strategy to attract tourists through cultural marketing
② an example of how community mapping fosters local engagement
③ a typical case of government-led renovation of neglected neighborhoods
④ an experimental use of community mapping to renovate underused urban areas
⑤ a symbolic case where community mapping preserves personal memories for future generations
questions.explanation: 문맥상 'a case in point'는 앞서 설명한 내용(커뮤니티 매핑을 통해 지역 사회 자산을 표시하고 유대감을 쌓는 것)의 '적절한 사례'를 의미합니다. 'Where in Wally' 프로젝트는 지역 주민들이 사랑하는 장소를 공유하고 표시함으로써 지역 사회의 참여를 이끌어낸 사례이므로 ②번이 정답입니다.
options_translation: ① 문화 마케팅을 통해 관광객을 유치하기 위한 상업적 전략
② 커뮤니티 매핑이 어떻게 지역 사회의 참여를 촉진하는지에 대한 예시
③ 방치된 이웃에 대한 정부 주도의 전형적인 개조 사례
④ 활용도가 낮은 도시 지역을 개조하기 위한 커뮤니티 매핑의 실험적 사용
⑤ 커뮤니티 매핑이 미래 세대를 위해 개인의 기억을 보존하는 상징적인 사례

questions.question: 7. 밑줄 친 <u>Statistics are human beings with the tears wiped off.</u>가 의미하는 바로 가장 적절한 것은? [3.6점]
questions.passage: While useful for specific purposes (e.g. census taking, income distribution), numbers eliminate information of enormous value. For example, the future lives of young students are tied to their scores on national tests. In effect, whether they can continue with their education, where, and at what cost depends importantly on a handful of numbers. These numbers do not account for the quality of schools they have attended, whether they have been tutored, have supportive parents, have test anxiety, and so on. Finally, putting aside the many ways in which statistical results can be manipulated, there are ways in which turning people's lives into numbers is morally insulating. Statistics on crime, homelessness, or the spread of a disease say nothing of people's suffering. We read the statistics as reports on events at a distance, thus allowing us to escape without being disturbed. <u>Statistics are human beings with the tears wiped off.</u> Quantify with caution.
options: ① Statistical analysis helps researchers maintain necessary emotional distance from their subjects.
② Mere numbers remove the emotional and suffering aspects of human experience.
③ Human beings can be properly understood through quantitative data analysis.
④ Tears are irrelevant when conducting proper scientific research with human subjects.
⑤ Statistical methods are deliberately designed to dehumanize research subjects.
questions.explanation: 밑줄 친 부분은 통계가 사람들의 삶을 숫자로 변환하면서 그 속에 담긴 고통이나 개별적인 감정적 맥락을 제거해 버린다는 것을 비유적으로 표현한 것입니다. 따라서 '단순한 숫자가 인간 경험의 감정적이고 고통스러운 측면을 제거한다'는 ②번이 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 통계 분석은 연구자들이 피실험자와 필요한 정서적 거리를 유지하는 데 도움을 준다.
② 단순한 숫자는 인간 경험의 감정적이고 고통스러운 측면을 제거한다.
③ 인간은 양적 데이터 분석을 통해 적절하게 이해될 수 있다.
④ 인간 피실험자를 대상으로 적절한 과학적 연구를 수행할 때 눈물은 무관하다.
⑤ 통계적 방법은 연구 대상을 비인격화하기 위해 의도적으로 설계되었다.

questions.question: 8. 다음 글의 내용과 일치하지 않는 것은? [3점]
questions.passage: When we think of leaders, we may think of people such as Abraham Lincoln or Martin Luther King, Jr. If you consider the historical importance and far-reaching influence of these individuals, leadership might seem like a noble and high goal. But like all of us, these people started out as students, workers, and citizens who possessed ideas about how some aspect of daily life could be improved on a larger scale. Through diligence and experience, they improved upon their ideas by sharing them with others, seeking their opinions and feedback and constantly looking for the best way to accomplish goals for a group. Thus we all have the potential to be leaders at school, in our communities, and at work, regardless of age or experience.
options: ① Leadership seems to be only <u>achievable</u> for those who have exceptional leadership skills.
② Famous leaders began as ordinary people with ideas about improving aspects of daily life.
③ Leadership is an innate quality that cannot be fostered through diligence and experience.
④ Leadership skills can be improved <u>through</u> sharing ideas with others and seeking their feedback.
⑤ All individuals possess leadership capability in their communities regardless of their background.
questions.explanation: 지문에서 위대한 지도자들도 처음에는 평범하게 시작했으며, '근면과 경험을 통해(Through diligence and experience)' 아이디어를 개선해 나갔다고 설명하고 있습니다. 따라서 리더십이 근면과 경험을 통해 길러질 수 없는 타고난 자질이라는 ③번은 글의 내용과 일치하지 않습니다.
options_translation: ① 리더십은 뛰어난 리더십 기술을 가진 사람들에게만 달성 가능한 것처럼 보인다.
② 유명한 지도자들은 일상생활의 측면을 개선하려는 아이디어를 가진 평범한 사람들로 시작했다.
③ 리더십은 근면과 경험을 통해 육성될 수 없는 타고난 자질이다.
④ 리더십 기술은 다른 사람들과 아이디어를 공유하고 피드백을 구함으로써 향상될 수 있다.
⑤ 모든 개인은 배경에 상관없이 자신의 지역 사회에서 리더십 능력을 보유하고 있다.

questions.question: 9. 'I'에 관한 다음 글의 내용과 일치하지 않는 것은? [2.8점]
questions.passage: A few days later, Ms. Harper talked about how to deliver a good speech. This reminded me that it wasn't just a writing assignment, but a speech I would have to give in front of my classmates! The thought of standing in front of the entire class made my palms sweat. I'm too shy to raise my hand in class even when I know the answer. How on earth can I speak in front of everyone? I couldn't sleep at all that night. The big day for the speech finally arrived, and I felt more anxious than ever. I had spent the previous week imagining how my classmates would react to my speech. I was still mostly thinking about what my classmates might think. I wasn't putting much thought into what I was actually going to say. I figured I could just speak off the top of my head. After all, I was going to talk about my grandmother. I didn't need any notes.
options: ① A conversation with Ms. Harper made me think about a speech to give in front of classmates.
② I find it difficult to raise a hand in class even when knowing the answer.
③ The closer the day of the presentation came, the more nervous I became.
④ I prepared thoroughly by writing a script and practicing the speech several times.
⑤ I would improvise the speech without any notes.
questions.explanation: 지문에서 주인공은 무엇을 말할지에 대해 많은 생각을 하지 않았으며, 즉석에서(off the top of my head) 말할 수 있을 것이라 생각하며 노트를 준비하지 않았다고 언급하고 있습니다. 따라서 원고를 쓰고 여러 번 연습하며 철저히 준비했다는 ④번 내용은 글의 내용과 일치하지 않습니다.
options_translation: ① Harper 선생님과의 대화는 반 친구들 앞에서 할 발표에 대해 생각하게 만들었다.
② 나는 답을 알고 있을 때조차 교실에서 손을 드는 것이 어렵다는 것을 알았다.
③ 발표 날이 다가올수록 나는 더 긴장되었다.
④ 나는 대본을 쓰고 발표를 여러 번 연습함으로써 철저히 준비했다.
⑤ 나는 노트 없이 즉흥적으로 연설을 할 것이었다.

questions.question: 10. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 어법상 틀린 것을 고르시오.[3.5점]
questions.passage: There is a wealth of evidence that ① when parents, teachers, supervisors, and coaches are perceived as involved and caring, people feel happier and more motivated. And it is not just those people with power - we need to feel ② <u>valued</u> and respected by peers and coworkers. Thus, when the need for relatedness is met, motivation and internalization are fueled, ③ <u>provided</u> that support for autonomy and competence are also there. If we are trying to motivate others, a caring relationship is a crucial basis ④ <u>which</u> we begin. And when we are trying to motivate ourselves, doing things to enhance a sense of connectedness to others can be crucial to long-term persistence. So exercise with a friend, call someone when you have a difficult decision ⑤ <u>to make</u>, and be there as a support for others as they take on challenges.
questions.explanation: ④번이 포함된 문장에서 a crucial basis는 뒤에 이어지는 관계절의 수식을 받는데, '우리는 그 기초 위에서 시작한다'는 의미가 되어야 하므로 전치사 on이 필요합니다. 따라서 which를 'on which' 또는 'from which' 등으로 고쳐야 하며, 관계대명사 단독으로는 뒤에 전치사의 목적어가 비어있는 불완전한 문장이 와야 하는데 뒤에 we begin은 자동사로 쓰여 완전한 구조를 이루고 있으므로 틀린 표현입니다.

questions.question: 11. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 어법상 틀린 것을 고르시오.[3.4점]
questions.passage: A couple of weeks later, the class was ① <u>given</u> another speech assignment. I didn't want to drop the ball like the first time. So this time, I was determined to practice ② <u>delivering</u> the speech. I used cue cards that contained key phrases about important facts, making sure I wouldn't lose track of my points. I rehearsed how I would stand, how I would make eye contact with the audience, and even when I would pause to let my words sink in. To be used to ③ <u>speaking</u> in front of others, I even practiced in front of my family. My little sister giggled a few times, but my parents gave me helpful feedback, ④<u>encouraged</u> me to speak more clearly and confidently. I felt nervous again when the big day finally arrived. But when the teacher called my name, I noticed ⑤<u>that</u> my nerves had actually calmed down a bit. I felt way better than the last time, for sure!
questions.explanation: ④번은 문장의 주동사(gave)가 이미 존재하므로, 추가적인 동사 형태가 올 수 없으며 부수적인 상황을 나타내는 분사구문 자리입니다. 부모님이 피드백을 주면서 나를 '격려하는' 능동의 관계이므로 과거분사 encouraged가 아니라 현재분사인 encouraging으로 고쳐야 합니다.

questions.question: 12.주어진 글 다음에 이어질 글의 순서로 가장 적절한 것을 고르시오. [3.5점]
questions.passage: In the course of trying to solve a problem with an invention, you may encounter a brick wall of resistance when you try to think your way logically through the problem. Such logical thinking is a linear type of process, which uses our reasoning skills.
ordered_passages: (A) On the other hand, creativity by definition involves the application of new information to old problems and the conception of new viewpoints and ideas. For this you will be most effective if you learn to operate in a nonlinear manner.

(B) This works fine when we're operating in the area of what we know or have experienced. However, when we need to deal with new information, ideas, and viewpoints, linear thinking will often come up short.

(C) That is, use your creative brain. Stated differently, if you think in a linear manner, you'll tend to be conservative and keep coming up with techniques which are already known. This, of course, is just what you don't want.
questions.explanation: 주어진 글에서 논리적 사고(선형적 과정)를 언급했습니다. (B)에서 '이것(선형적 사고)'이 아는 영역에서는 잘 작동하지만 새로운 정보에는 부족하다는 한계를 지적합니다. (A)에서 '반면에'를 통해 창의성(비선형적 방식)의 필요성을 제시하고, (C)에서 이를 '창의적 뇌를 사용하라'고 재진술하며 마무리하는 구조가 자연스럽습니다.

questions.question: 13. 주어진 글 다음에 이어질 글의 순서로 가장 적절한 것을 고르시오.[3.5점]
questions.passage: The most noticeable human characteristic projected onto animals is that they can talk in human language.
ordered_passages: (A) Despite this evolution toward naturalism, however, human-like animals still consistently use their front legs like human hands. (for example, lions can pick up and lift small objects with one paw)

(B) Physically, animal cartoon characters and toys modeled after animals are also typically deformed to resemble humans more closely. This human-like transformation extends beyond speech to include fundamental physical alterations in media and entertainment.

(C) Specifically, these human-like appearances are achieved by giving animals humanlike facial features and deliberately modifying their front legs to resemble human hands. More recent animated movies have begun showing a trend toward depicting animals in a more "natural" way.
questions.explanation: 주어진 글은 동물의 언어 능력을 언급합니다. (B)에서 언어 외에 '신체적' 변형도 일어난다고 확장하며, (C)에서 구체적으로 얼굴 특징과 앞다리 변형을 설명한 후 최근의 '자연스러운' 묘사 경향을 소개합니다. (A)에서 '그러나 이러한 자연주의로의 진화에도 불구하고' 여전히 앞다리를 손처럼 사용한다는 예시로 마무리됩니다.

questions.question: 14. 글의 흐름으로 보아, 주어진 문장이 들어가기에 가장 적절한 곳을 고르시오.[3.2점]
questions.passage: Promotion deals with consumer psychology. We can't force people to think one way or another, and the clever marketer knows that promotion is used to provide information in the most clear, honest, and simple fashion possible. By doing so, the possibility of increasing sales goes up. ( ① ) Gone are the days when promotions were done in order to fool the consumer into purchasing something. ( ② ) The long-term effect of getting a consumer to buy something they did not really want or need wasn't good. ( ③ ) In fact, consumers fooled once can do damage to sales as they relate their experience to others. ( ④ ) They promote that good or service in a way that makes the value clear to the consumer. ( ⑤ ) Therefore, marketers must know where the potential consumers are, and how to reach them.
questions.insertion_sentence: Instead, marketers now know that their goal is to identify the consumers who are most likely to appreciate a good or service
questions.explanation: 주어진 문장의 'Instead(대신에)'는 앞선 내용(소비자를 속여서 사게 하는 방식의 부정적 결과)과 대조를 이룹니다. ④번 뒤의 'They'가 주어진 문장의 'marketers'를 지칭하며, 고객이 가치를 명확히 알 수 있게 홍보한다는 내용이 연결되므로 ④번이 가장 적절합니다.

questions.question: 15.글의 흐름으로 보아, 주어진 문장이 들어가기에 가장 적절한 곳을 고르시오. [3.3점]
questions.passage: A community mapping project doesn't have to be ambitious in scale. If the idea of mapping overwhelms you, start small. Here is an idea. Although it may seem that you know all about the routes to school, students have different information from one another due to different experiences. How about making a map with your classmates? Each of you can trace routes that you frequently use and mark how comfortable or safe you feel on those routes. ( ① ) With group participation and feedback, an informative visual map of safe routes to school can be constructed. ( ② ) You can provide the map to local district officials to help identify school safety problems. ( ③ ) The process is defined by the community itself, depending on what issues are raised and how the community members decide to deal with them. ( ④ ) The most important thing in the process is that you have to willingly work with others. ( ⑤ ) Remember that, by its very nature, community mapping is a collective experience.
questions.insertion_sentence: There isn't just one reason for, nor one method of, carrying out community mapping.
questions.explanation: 주어진 문장은 커뮤니티 매핑의 이유나 방법이 단 하나가 아니라는 일반적 진술입니다. ③번 뒤의 문장에서 'The process is defined by the community itself(그 과정은 커뮤니티 자체에 의해 정의된다)'는 내용이 주어진 문장의 '방법이 하나가 아니다'라는 내용을 구체적으로 뒷받침하므로 ③번 위치가 적절합니다.

questions.question: 16.다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것을 고르시오. [3.5점]
questions.passage: The major philosophical shift in the idea of selling came when industrial societies became more affluent, more competitive, and more geographically spread out during the 1940s and 1950s. This forced business to develop closer relations with buyers and clients, which in turn made business realize that it was not enough to produce a quality product at a reasonable price. In fact, it was important to produce what customers needed. Henry Ford produced his best-selling T-model Ford in one color only (black) in 1908, but in modern societies this was no longer possible. The modernization of society led to a marketing revolution that destroyed the view that ________________________________________. Customers, and the desire to meet their diverse and often complex needs, became the focus of business.
options: ① manufacturing items without considering customer needs would guarantee sales
② technological advances would eliminate the need for any marketing
③ advertising alone would determine the success of every product
④ offering limited choices would satisfy most customer demands
⑤ customers would naturally adapt to the products available
questions.explanation: 지문은 산업 사회가 발전하면서 고객의 요구를 충족시키는 것이 중요해졌다고 설명합니다. 따라서 마케팅 혁명은 '고객의 요구를 고려하지 않고 물건을 제조하는 것이 판매를 보장할 것'이라는 과거의 관점을 파괴했다는 내용이 빈칸에 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 고객의 요구를 고려하지 않고 제품을 제조하는 것이 판매를 보장할 것이다
② 기술적 진보가 어떠한 마케팅의 필요성도 없앨 것이다
③ 광고만이 모든 제품의 성공을 결정할 것이다
④ 제한된 선택권을 제공하는 것이 대부분의 고객 요구를 충족시킬 것이다
⑤ 고객들이 이용 가능한 제품에 자연스럽게 적응할 것이다

questions.question: 17.다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것을 고르시오. [3.3점]
questions.passage: There is no law that forces you to say Thank you. But if people don't say Thank you in these cases it is marked. People expect that you will say it. You become responsible. Failing to say it will be both surprising and worthy of criticism. Not knowing the norms of another community is the central problem of cross-cultural communication. To continue the Thank you example, even though another culture may have an expression that appears translatable (many don't), there may be different norms for its usage, for example, such that you should say Thank you only when ________________________________________. In such a case it would sound ridiculous (i.e., unexpected, surprising, and worthy of criticism) if you were to thank someone for something so minor as holding a door open for you.
options: ① the social interaction requires maintaining mutual respect
② the sacrifice or effort someone has made is significant
③ the cultural ritual of expressing gratitude is formalized
④ the verbal agreement follows universal social rules
⑤ the gesture deserves explicit verbal recognition
questions.explanation: 지문 뒤쪽에서 문을 열어주는 것과 같은 사소한 일에 감사하다고 하는 것이 우스꽝스럽게 들릴 수 있는 상황을 예로 들고 있습니다. 따라서 빈칸에는 감사를 표하는 기준이 엄격한 상황, 즉 '누군가가 한 희생이나 노력이 상당할 때'만 감사 인사를 해야 한다는 규범이 들어가는 것이 문맥상 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 사회적 상호작용이 상호 존중을 유지할 것을 요구한다
② 누군가가 한 희생이나 노력이 상당하다
③ 감사를 표현하는 문화적 의례가 공식화되어 있다
④ 구두 합의가 보편적인 사회적 규칙을 따른다
⑤ 그 제스처가 명시적인 언어적 인정을 받을 만하다

questions.question: 18.다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것을 고르시오. [3.2점]
questions.passage: The science we learn in grade school is a collection of certainties about the natural world - the earth goes around the sun, DNA carries the information of an organism, and so on. Only when you start to learn the practice of science do you realize that each of these "facts" was hard won through a succession of logical inferences based upon many observations or experiments. The process of science is less about collecting pieces of knowledge than it is about ________________________________________. Our uncertainties can be greater or lesser for any given piece of knowledge depending upon where we are in that process - today we are quite certain of how an apple will fall from a tree, but our understanding of the turbulent fluid flow remains a work in progress after more than a century of effort.
options: ① establishing permanent scientific truths through observation
② memorizing and categorizing established scientific principles
③ shrinking the zones of uncertainty in our understanding
④ documenting a series of scientific discoveries over time
⑤ proving the certainties we learn in grade school
questions.explanation: 과학은 지식의 파편을 수집하는 것이 아니라 불확실성을 줄여가는 과정이라는 것이 글의 핵심입니다. 마지막 문장에서 특정 지식에 대한 우리의 불확실성이 과정에 따라 커지거나 작아질 수 있다고 언급하고 있으므로 빈칸에는 '우리의 이해에서 불확실성의 영역을 줄이는 것'이 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 관찰을 통해 영구적인 과학적 진리를 확립하는 것
② 확립된 과학적 원리를 암기하고 분류하는 것
③ 우리의 이해에서 불확실성의 영역을 줄이는 것
④ 시간에 따른 일련의 과학적 발견을 기록하는 것
⑤ 초등학교에서 배우는 확실성들을 증명하는 것

questions.question: 19. 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것을 고르시오. [3.5점]
questions.passage: Assuming gene editing in humans proves to be safe and effective, it might seem logical, even preferable, to correct disease-causing mutations at the earliest possible stage of life, before harmful genes begin causing serious problems. Yet once it becomes possible to transform an embryo's mutated genes into "normal" ones, there will certainly be ________________________. Should we begin editing genes in unborn children to lower their lifetime risk of heart disease or cancer? What about giving unborn children beneficial features, like greater strength and increased mental abilities, or changing physical characteristics, like eye and hair color? The pursuit for perfection seems almost natural to human nature, but if we start down this slippery slope, we may not like where we end up.
options: ① ethical debates about correcting genetic abnormalities only in serious medical cases
② requirements that all embryos undergo genetic screening for potential health issue
③ scientific concerns about the safety of even therapeutic genetic modifications
④ legal restrictions preventing any modification beyond medical necessity
⑤ urges to advance regular genetic profiles to elite versions
questions.explanation: 지문은 배아의 유전자 편집이 질병 치료를 넘어 지능 향상이나 외모 변경과 같은 완벽을 향한 추구(The pursuit for perfection)로 이어질 수 있는 위험성(slippery slope)을 경고하고 있습니다. 따라서 빈칸에는 유전적 프로필을 엘리트 버전으로 향상시키려는 욕구가 생길 것이라는 내용이 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 심각한 의료 사례에서만 유전적 이상을 수정하는 것에 대한 윤리적 논쟁
② 모든 배아가 잠재적인 건강 문제를 위해 유전자 검사를 받아야 한다는 요구 사항
③ 치료 목적의 유전자 변형조차도 그 안전성에 대한 과학적 우려
④ 의료적 필요성을 넘어서는 어떠한 수정도 금지하는 법적 제한
⑤ 일반적인 유전적 프로필을 엘리트 버전으로 발전시키려는 충동

questions.question: 20. 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것을 고르시오.[3.6점]
questions.passage: We tend to feel safe and secure in numbers when we decide how to act, particularly when faced with uncertain conditions. To help decide what's risky and what's safe, who's trustworthy and who's not, we look for social evidence. From an evolutionary view, following the group is almost always positive for our prospects of survival. "If everyone's doing it, it must be a sensible thing to do," explains psychologist and best selling writer of Influence, Robert Cialdini. While we can frequently see this today in product reviews, even subtler cues within the environment can signal trustworthiness. Consider this: when you visit a local restaurant, are they busy? Is there a line outside or is it easy to find a seat? It is a hassle to wait, but a line can be a powerful cue that the food's tasty, and these seats are in demand, which means the restaurant is safe and worth visiting. More often than not, it's good to adopt the practices that ________________________.
options: ① copy the actions of others to fit in and conform to what's considered right
② observe collective wisdom while maintaining a healthy skepticism about majority opinions
③ carefully evaluate social trends before making independent decisions based on personal values
④ balance social awareness with critical thinking to determine the most beneficial course of action
⑤ trust instinctive reactions to social situations rather than following established group behaviors
questions.explanation: 이 글은 불확실한 상황에서 다수의 행동을 따르는 것(사회적 증거)이 생존과 안전 확보에 도움이 된다는 내용을 담고 있습니다. 따라서 빈칸에는 타인의 행동을 모방하여 순응하는 관습을 따르는 것이 좋다는 내용이 들어가야 합니다.
options_translation: ① 어울리고 옳다고 여겨지는 것에 순응하기 위해 타인의 행동을 모방하는 것
② 다수의 의견에 대해 건강한 회의론을 유지하면서 집단 지성을 관찰하는 것
③ 개인적 가치에 기반한 독립적인 결정을 내리기 전에 사회적 트렌드를 신중하게 평가하는 것
④ 가장 유익한 행동 과정을 결정하기 위해 비판적 사고와 사회적 인식을 균형 있게 맞추는 것
⑤ 확립된 집단 행동을 따르기보다 사회적 상황에 대한 본능적인 반응을 신뢰하는 것

questions.question: 21. 다음 글에서 전체 흐름과 관계 없는 문장은? [3.1점]
questions.passage: One of the most striking characteristics of a sleeping animal or person is that they do not respond normally to environmental stimuli. If you open the eyelids of a sleeping mammal the eyes will not see normally - they are functionally blind. ① Some visual information apparently gets in, but it is not normally processed as it is shortened or weakened: same with the other sensing systems. ② Stimuli are registered but not processed normally and they fail to wake the individual. ③ Perceptual disengagement probably doesn't serve the function of protecting sleep, so some authors count it as part of the definition of sleep itself. ④ As sleep would be impossible without it, perceptual disengagement seems essential to the definition of sleep. ⑤ Nevertheless, many animals (including humans) use the intermediate state of drowsiness to derive some benefits of sleep without total perceptual disengagement.
questions.explanation: 글 전체는 잠자는 동안 환경 자극에 반응하지 않는 '지각적 차단(perceptual disengagement)'이 수면의 필수적인 특성임을 설명하고 있습니다. 하지만 ③번 문장은 지각적 차단이 수면을 보호하는 기능을 하지 않는다는 부정적인 진술을 하고 있어 전체 흐름과 어긋납니다.

questions.question: 23.다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것을 고르시오. [3.1점]
questions.passage: All carbohydrates are basically sugars. Complex carbohydrates are the good carbohydrates for your body. These complex sugar compounds are very ① <u>hard</u> to break down and can trap other nutrients like vitamins and minerals in their chains. As they don't break down ② <u>slowly</u>, the other nutrients are also released into your body. Also, they can ③ <u>supply</u> you with fuel for a number of hours. Bad carbohydrates, on the other hand, are simple sugars. Since their structure is not complex, they are easy to break down and hold ④ <u>few</u> nutrients for your body other than the sugars from which they are made. Your body breaks down these carbohydrates rather quickly and what it cannot use is ⑤ <u>transformed</u> into fat and stored in the body.
questions.explanation: 복합 탄수화물은 분해되기 어렵기 때문에(hard to break down) '천천히' 분해됩니다. 따라서 'don't break down slowly'가 아니라 'break down slowly' 혹은 'don't break down quickly'가 되어야 문맥이 성립합니다.

questions.question: 24. 다음 글의 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 어법상 바르게 짝지어진 것은? [3.5점]
questions.passage: The next day when I met Ms. Harper after school, we talked about the speech. I said, "I'm embarrassed about the speech, I (A) [must / should] have looked like a fool. I know I could have done better." "It's quite all right to fall short of your own expectations as long as you learn something from it," she said in a warm voice. "What was bothering you the most while you prepared for the speech?" "I was afraid the other students would laugh at me if my speech wasn't good enough." She replied, "You certainly can't control (B) [what / which] others think about your speech. That means you should be focusing on the one thing that you can control - how you give your speech." That woke me up from the depths of despair. Of course, that was it! I wouldn't have been able to make my classmates (C) [like / to like] what I wanted to say. I really should have focused on my performance.
options: ① should ... which ... to like
② should ... what ... to like
③ must ... what ... to like
④ must ... which ... like
⑤ must ... what ... like
questions.explanation: (A) 과거에 틀림없이 그랬을 것이라는 강한 추측을 나타내므로 'must have p.p.'가 적절합니다. (B) 타동사 think의 목적어 역할을 하며 선행사가 없으므로 관계대명사 'what'이 적절합니다. (C) 사역동사 make의 목적격 보어 자리이므로 원형 부정사인 'like'가 적절합니다.

questions.question: 25. 윗글의 제목으로 가장 적절한 것은? [3.1점]
questions.passage: Lewis Carroll's Through the Looking-Glass is filled with whimsical yet thought-provoking moments, one of which introduces a peculiar idea about constant effort and competition. In the story, the Red Queen takes Alice on a race through the countryside. They run and they run, but then Alice discovers that they're still under the same tree that they started from. The Red Queen explains to Alice: "here, you see, it takes all the running you can do, to keep in the same place." This strange concept, at first glance (a) <u>nonsensical</u>, has found relevance beyond the world of fiction. Biologists sometimes use this Red Queen Effect to explain an (b) <u>evolutionary</u> principle. If foxes evolve to run faster so they can catch more rabbits, then only the fastest rabbits will live long enough to make a new generation of bunnies that run even faster - in which case, of course, only the fastest foxes will catch enough rabbits to (c) <u>thrive</u> and pass on their genes. Over countless generations, this arms race continues, with each species adapting in response to the other. Even though they might run, the two species just (d) <u>stay</u> in place, never gaining a permanent advantage over the other. This phenomenon isn't limited to the animal kingdom: it has been observed in fields as diverse as business, technology, and even international relations, where constant adaptation is (e) <u>unnecessary</u> just to maintain one's position in a rapidly changing world; standing still is not an option.
options: ① The Never-Ending Chase: How Competition Fuels Evolution
② Escaping the Race: How to Win Without Competing
③ The Secret to Staying Ahead of the Game
④ Why Running Faster Guarantees Success
⑤ When Competition Comes to an End
questions.explanation: 이 글은 한 종의 진화가 다른 종의 진화를 자극하여 끊임없이 경쟁하지만 제자리에 머물게 되는 '붉은 여왕 효과'를 설명하고 있으므로, 경쟁이 진화를 부추기는 끝없는 추격이 제목으로 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 끝나지 않는 추격: 경쟁이 어떻게 진화를 부추기는가
② 경주에서 탈출하기: 경쟁하지 않고 이기는 방법
③ 게임에서 앞서 나가는 비결
④ 더 빨리 달리는 것이 성공을 보장하는 이유
⑤ 경쟁이 끝날 때

questions.question: 26. 밑줄 친 (a)~(e) 중에서 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은? [3.2점]

questions.question: 27. 위 글의 주제로 가장 적절한 것은? [3.1점]
questions.passage: Everyone has unique experiences, but many people remain disconnected from what goes on outside their lives. As a result, there can be a (a) <u>lack</u> of connection between people with different experiences. Community mapping helps people look outside of themselves, connect with other members of their communities, and share (b) <u>invaluable</u> experiences. Since it involves collaboration rather than individual effort, it is more effective. It (c) <u>enables</u> members of a community to map details of the places where they live and other places they know about. This allows people to share important information not just about the areas they live in, but also other places they are familiar with. Through this process, people are able to understand different perspectives and (d) <u>erode</u> stronger bonds within their communities by sharing diverse experiences. Community mapping is a collective process. Community mapping is also a unique and valuable tool as it can be used in diverse ways. In this way, community mapping has become an essential tool that can be (e) <u>applied</u> in various situations.
options: ① connecting the isolated to the world through the means of community mapping
② exploring the role of technology in overcoming barriers to community mapping
③ why people become more disconnected in a rapidly changing world
④ understanding human isolation by joining community mapping
⑤ sharing personal stories as a key to building an inclusive society
questions.explanation: 이 글은 커뮤니티 매핑을 통해 사람들이 서로 연결되고 경험을 공유하며 유대감을 형성하는 과정을 설명하고 있으므로, 커뮤니티 매핑을 수단으로 하여 고립된 이들을 세상과 연결한다는 내용이 주제로 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 커뮤니티 매핑이라는 수단을 통해 고립된 이들을 세상과 연결하기
② 커뮤니티 매핑의 장벽을 극복하는 데 있어 기술의 역할 탐색
③ 급변하는 세상에서 사람들이 왜 더 단절되는가
④ 커뮤니티 매핑에 참여함으로써 인간의 소외를 이해하기
