questions.question: 31. 윗글에 관한 내용으로 적절하지 않은 것은? [3.2점]
questions.passage:
(A)
The phrase 'the curse of knowledge' was coined in 1989 by economists Camerer, Lowenstein and Weber and it refers to a cognitive bias where individuals assume other people know what they know. This can include knowledge and understanding of key terms, concepts or background information that someone (a)erroneously assumes others have.
(B)
The curse of knowledge within education doesn't just (b)apply to students' learning. Anyone delivering professional learning to their colleagues, or others, should be keenly aware of the curse of knowledge before using technical terms, acronyms or concepts that may not be familiar to the audience.
(C)
This educational paradox presents a significant challenge for teachers: the greater their subject knowledge, the more difficult it becomes to effectively communicate with novice learners. It is something all teachers should be aware of and mindful of when planning, designing, and delivering lessons. The curse of knowledge can create issues with communication and ultimately become a (c)barrier to effective teaching and learning.
(D)
Authors Chip and Dan Heath explain, "Once we know something, we find it hard to imagine what it was like not to know it. Our knowledge has 'cursed' us. And it becomes difficult for us to share our knowledge with others, because we (d)can't readily re-create our listeners' state of mind". This curse <u>can make it difficult for experts to explain and teach content or concepts to novices, making the curse of knowledge</u> especially (e)rare within education.
options: ① The curse of knowledge means a cognitive bias where people assume others possess the same knowledge they have.
② When teaching colleagues, people should carefully remember that they might know things their audience doesn't know.
③ Teachers face a strange contradiction when they teach beginners.
④ Our knowledge facilitates our sharing of complex ideas with novice learners.
⑤ The curse of knowledge makes it challenging for knowledgeable people to imagine what it's like not to know something.
questions.explanation: 글의 핵심 내용은 지식의 저주 때문에 알고 있는 지식이 오히려 초보자에게 복잡한 아이디어를 전달하는 것을 어렵게(difficult) 만든다는 것이다. ④번의 '지식이 초보 학습자와 복잡한 아이디어를 공유하는 것을 용이하게 한다(facilitates)'는 내용은 본문의 내용과 정반대이다.
options_translation: ① 지식의 저주는 사람들이 다른 이들도 자신과 같은 지식을 가지고 있다고 가정하는 인지적 편향을 의미한다.
② 동료를 가르칠 때, 사람들은 청중이 모르는 것을 자신이 알고 있을 수 있음을 신중히 기억해야 한다.
③ 교사들은 초보자를 가르칠 때 묘한 모순에 직면한다.
④ 우리의 지식은 초보 학습자들과 복잡한 아이디어를 공유하는 것을 용이하게 한다.
⑤ 지식의 저주는 지식이 있는 사람들이 무언가를 알지 못한다는 것이 어떤 것인지 상상하는 것을 어렵게 만든다.

questions.question: 2.글의 흐름으로 보아, 주어진 문장이 들어가기에 가장 적절한 곳을 고르시오. [3.8점]
questions.passage: Dictionaries are relatively good resources for anyone interested in finding out what a word means. ( ① ) Using one set of words to define another word is called a lexical definition. ( ② ) More often than not, a definition in a dictionary requires readers to have a fairly robust understanding of the language already at their disposal. ( ③ ) In other words, a dictionary functions in many cases as a cross-reference or translator between words one knows and words that one doesn’t yet know. ( ④ ) Even the most obscure words in a dictionary, say, for example, "pulchritudinous" or "kalogathia," must be defined using words that the reader already knows and understands. ( ⑤ ) Otherwise, the dictionary isn’t very helpful.
questions.insertion_sentence: But it’s important to understand the limits of this kind of definition used in dictionaries.
questions.explanation: 주어진 문장은 사전에서 사용되는 정의의 한계를 이해하는 것이 중요하다고 언급합니다. ①번 뒤에서 '어휘 정의'를 설명한 후, ②번 자리에서 그 한계(독자가 이미 해당 언어에 대한 이해가 있어야 함)를 설명하는 내용이 이어지므로 ②번이 가장 적절합니다.

questions.question: 4.글의 흐름으로 보아, 주어진 문장이 들어가기에 가장 적절한 곳을 고르시오. [4.1점]
questions.passage: Quite often, the interaction between groups is socially unequal, and this is reflected in the fact that in many cases, borrowing of words or constructions goes mostly or entirely in one direction, from the more powerful or prestigious group to the less favored one. ( ① ) The languages of socially subordinated groups may, from quite an early period of contact, provide terminology for objects or practices with which speakers of the more powerful group were previously unfamiliar. ( ② ) These borrowed words often describe things or cultural practices new to the dominant group, such as tools, foods, or customs. ( ③ ) However, the effects of language contact in that direction may not progress any further than this limited exchange of words or ideas. ( ④ ) In some cases, as with the Dharug language of Sydney, Australia, the source of some of the earliest loans from Indigenous Australian languages into English, the fate of the language system is extinction after the obliteration of many of its speakers. ( ⑤ ) Those who survived were forced to give up their language and culture, and they eventually shifted to using forms of English spoken by the people who had suppressed them.
questions.insertion_sentence: This means that dominant groups often take from weaker groups, but the exchange is not balanced and rarely benefits the weaker side equally.
questions.explanation: 주어진 문장은 지배적인 집단이 약한 집단으로부터 (언어적 요소를) 취하지만 그 교환이 균형 잡히지 않았음을 설명하고 있습니다. 첫 번째 문장에서 집단 간의 상호작용이 사회적으로 불평등하며 언어적 차용이 한 방향으로만 일어난다는 내용을 제시한 후, 그 의미를 구체화하는 문장으로 ①번 위치가 가장 적절합니다. 그 뒤의 내용은 약한 집단에서 강한 집단으로 전달되는 단편적인 용어들에 대한 사례와 한계를 설명합니다.

questions.question: 12. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것을 고르시오.[3.5점]
questions.passage: Great scientists are ①<u>seldom</u> one-hit wonders. Newton is a prime example: beyond the Newtonian mechanics, he developed the theory of gravitation, calculus, laws of motion, and optimization. In fact, well-known scientists are often involved in ②<u>multiple</u> discoveries, a phenomenon potentially explained by the Matthew effect. Indeed, an initial success may offer a scientist legitimacy, improve peer perception, provide knowledge of how to score and win, enhance social status, and attract resources and quality collaborators, each of these payoffs further ③<u>decreasing</u> her odds of scoring another win. Yet, there is an appealing alternative explanation: Great scientists have several hits and consistently succeed in their scientific endeavors simply because they're exceptionally ④<u>talented</u>. Therefore, future success again goes to those who have had success earlier, not because of advantages offered by the previous success, but because the earlier success was indicative of a hidden talent. The Matthew effect posits that success alone increases the future probability of ⑤<u>success</u>, raising the question: Does status dictate outcomes, or does it simply reflect an underlying talent or quality? In other words, is there really a Matthew effect after all?
questions.explanation: 맥락상 초기 성공이 주는 다양한 이점(정당성, 동료의 인식 개선, 지식, 사회적 지위 향상, 자원 및 협력자 유인 등)은 다음 성공을 거둘 확률을 '줄이는(decreasing)' 것이 아니라 '높이는(increasing)' 것이 되어야 자연스럽습니다.

questions.question: 14.다음 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것을 고르시오. [3.4점]
questions.passage: The prominence of the social dimension in food writing might suggest that the flavor of food is taking a back seat. I suspect that most people view flavor as of secondary importance in social settings where food is served. Although our social gatherings coalesce around food, the meaning of these gatherings does not seem to depend on flavor. Flavor assists with the narrow purpose of filling the belly, and once that is accomplished it provides the backdrop for whatever social dynamics characterize the gathering. These can be understood independently of the flavor of the food on offer, the appreciation of which is understood to be personal and subjective. According to this conventional wisdom, the ceremonies and rituals around food, the social events that supply food with its meaning, do not __________. To focus excessively on flavor is to miss the larger significance of these social relations.
options: ① focus on the act of social interaction itself
② make a contribution to the sustainability of society
③ depend on the quality of sensations provided by food
④ overlook the joy that comes from the quality of food
⑤ attract people more easily than events not centered on food
questions.explanation: 지문은 음식의 사회적 측면이 강조됨에 따라 음식의 '맛'이나 '풍미'는 부차적인 것이 되었음을 설명합니다. 따라서 빈칸에는 사회적 행사나 의례가 '음식이 제공하는 감각의 질(풍미)에 의존하지 않는다'는 내용이 들어가는 것이 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 사회적 상호작용 행위 자체에 집중한다
② 사회의 지속 가능성에 기여한다
③ 음식이 제공하는 감각의 질에 의존한다
④ 음식의 질에서 오는 즐거움을 간과한다
⑤ 음식을 중심으로 하지 않는 행사보다 사람들을 더 쉽게 끌어들인다

questions.question: 17. 주어진 글 다음에 이어질 글의 순서로 가장 적절한 것을 고르시오.[4.2점]
questions.passage: It is important to understand that even though science follows rules, it is also a very creative process. Scientists do not just follow steps — they also need to think deeply and creatively. A conjecture, which is a kind of guess or idea, is made by the mind during a time of deep thinking. It is a philosophical idea, like a new thought that comes from imagination and thought, not from testing.
ordered_passages: (A) To become knowledge, a hypothesis must go through many tests. During this time, scientists remove ideas that are not true. The ideas that remain are the ones that have passed the tests. This is how science moves forward — by keeping what works and leaving behind what doesn't.

(B) However, a hypothesis, which is another word for a scientific guess, is not real knowledge until it is tested. Before testing, it is only information that shows someone's thoughts or beliefs. It may seem true, but it is still just speculation. True knowledge is something different. It comes only after careful testing.

(C) This process, a kind of "learning loop," is also called Bayesian updating by statisticians. Based on Bayes' rule, developed by 18th-century English statistician and philosopher Thomas Bayes — Bayesian updating refers to a numerical process in which a theory or hypothesis becomes more accurate through repeated testing and comparison with alternative ideas.
questions.explanation: 주어진 글에서 과학적 추측(conjecture)이 창의적인 사고 과정임을 설명한다. (B)에서 'However'를 사용하여 이러한 추측이나 가설이 테스트 전까지는 실제 지식이 아님을 역설하고, (A)에서 테스트를 통과해야만 지식이 된다는 구체적 과정을 설명한다. (C)에서 이러한 과정(테스트를 통한 정확성 향상)을 'Bayesian updating'이라는 용어로 정의하며 마무리한다.

questions.question: 20.다음 글에서 전체 흐름과 관계 없는 문장을 고르시오. [4.0점]
questions.passage: The governments of virtually every country on the planet attach great importance to achieving food security and a wide variety of mechanisms have been developed to realize this goal. The first issue governments face in achieving national food security is the problem of insuring that adequate amounts of food are available to the resident population. ① Some governments have set goals of food self-sufficiency, which means most if not all of the food available in a country comes from the domestic farming system. ② However, food security does not require food self-sufficiency because countries can import food items not easily produced within the country. ③ Even countries without extremely productive agricultural sectors are fully self-sufficient in all food items. ④ The United States, for example, depends on imports for its supply of coffee, tea, bananas and other tropical products. ⑤ In general, the problem of assuring adequate food supplies is solved by relying on both domestic production and imports.
questions.explanation: 식량 안보를 달성하기 위해 국가들이 자급자족을 목표로 하기도 하지만, 수입을 통해서도 이를 달성할 수 있다는 내용이다. ③번 문장은 농업 생산성이 높지 않은 국가들도 모든 식량 품목에서 완전 자급자족한다는 내용으로, 수입의 필요성을 강조하는 문맥과 정반대이며 현실과도 맞지 않는다.

questions.question: 8. 다음 글의 주제로 가장 적절한 것은? [3.0점]
questions.passage: Plants can communicate, although not in the same way we do. Some express their discontent through scents. You know that smell that hangs in the air after you've mowed the lawn? Yeah, that's actually an SOS. Some plants use sound. Yes, sound, though at a frequency that we can't hear. Researchers experimented with plants and microphones to see if they could record any trouble calls. They found that plants produce a high-frequency clicking noise when stressed and can make different sounds for different stressors. The sound a plant makes when it's not getting watered differs from the one it'll make when a leaf is cut. However, it's worth noting that experts don't think plants are crying out in pain. It's more likely that these reactions are knee-jerk survival actions. Plants are living organisms, and their main objective is to survive. Scents and sounds are their tools for defending against things that might harm them.
options: ① elements affecting the survival of plants
② various ways required for plants to reproduce
③ how plants communicate with other organisms
④ some examples of plants using different defense mechanisms
⑤ how plants communicate stresses through scents and sounds as a survival mechanism
questions.explanation: 이 글은 식물이 향기(냄새)와 소리(고주파 클릭 소음)를 통해 자신이 처한 스트레스 상황을 알리며, 이것이 생존을 위한 반응이자 방어 도구라는 점을 설명하고 있습니다. 따라서 주제로 '생존 기제로서 향기와 소리를 통해 식물이 스트레스를 소통하는 방식'인 ⑤번이 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 식물의 생존에 영향을 미치는 요소들
② 식물이 번식하기 위해 필요한 다양한 방법들
③ 식물이 다른 생명체와 소통하는 방법
④ 다른 방어 기제를 사용하는 식물의 몇 가지 예시들
⑤ 생존 기제로서 향기와 소리를 통해 식물이 스트레스를 전달하는 방식

questions.question: 9. 다음 글의 제목으로 가장 적절한 것을 고르시오. [2.9점]
questions.passage: In the course of trying to solve a problem with an invention, you may encounter a brick wall of resistance when you try to think your way logically through the problem. Such logical thinking is a linear type of process, which uses our reasoning skills. This works fine when we're operating in the area of what we know or have experienced. However, when we need to deal with new information, ideas, and viewpoints, linear thinking will often come up short. On the other hand, creativity by definition involves the application of new information to old problems and the conception of new viewpoints and ideas. For this you will be most effective if you learn to operate in a nonlinear manner; that is, use your creative brain. Stated differently, if you think in a linear manner, you'll tend to be conservative and keep coming up with techniques which are already known. This, of course, is just what you don't want.
options: ① The Psychological Barriers to Logical Problem Solving
② Enhancing Decision-Making Through Traditional Methods
③ The Merits of Human Reasoning in Familiar Contexts
④ How Linear Thinking Supports Innovation in Known Fields
⑤ The Need for Creative Thinking in Overcoming the Limitations of Logical Thinking
questions.explanation: 이 글은 논리적이고 선형적인 사고가 익숙한 분야에서는 잘 작동하지만, 새로운 정보나 관점을 다룰 때는 한계가 있음을 지적합니다. 따라서 문제 해결을 위해 비선형적 방식인 '창의적 사고'를 사용해야 한다는 점을 강조하고 있으므로, 제목으로 가장 적절한 것은 ⑤번입니다.
options_translation: ① 논리적 문제 해결에 대한 심리적 장벽
② 전통적 방법을 통한 의사 결정 강화
③ 익숙한 맥락에서 인간 추론의 장점
④ 알려진 분야에서 선형적 사고가 혁신을 지원하는 방법
⑤ 논리적 사고의 한계를 극복하기 위한 창의적 사고의 필요성

questions.question: 10. 다음 글의 제목으로 가장 적절한 것을 고르시오. [3.4점]
questions.passage: Our skin conducts electricity more or less efficiently depending on our emotions. We know that when we're emotionally stimulated - stressed, sad, any intense emotion, really - our bodies sweat a tiny bit, so little we might not even notice. And when those tiny drops of sweat appear, our skin gets more electrically conductive. This change in sweat gland activity happens completely without your conscious mind having much say in the matter. If you feel emotionally intense, you're going to notice an increase in sweat gland activity. This is particularly useful from a scientific viewpoint, because it allows us to put an objective value on a subjective state of mind. We can actually measure your emotional state by tracking how your body subconsciously sweats, by running a bit of electricity through your skin. We can then turn the subjective, subconscious experience of emotional intensity into an objective number by figuring out how good your skin gets at transferring an electrical current.
options: ① How Physical Activities Govern Our Emotional State
② Skin Conductivity Reveals One of Our Physical Characteristics
③ How to Evaluate Our Skin Health by Running an Electrical Current
④ The Variation of Emotional Intensity Determines Our Subconscious Mind
⑤ Measuring Emotions through the Connection Between Skin Conductivity and Emotional Intensity
questions.explanation: 이 글은 감정적 자극이 땀샘 활동을 변화시켜 피부의 전기 전도성을 높인다는 점을 설명합니다. 이를 통해 주관적인 감정 상태를 객관적인 수치로 측정할 수 있다는 내용이 핵심이므로, 제목으로 가장 적절한 것은 ⑤번입니다.
options_translation: ① 신체 활동이 우리의 감정 상태를 지배하는 방법
② 피부 전도도가 우리의 신체적 특징 중 하나를 드러낸다
③ 전류를 흘려보내 피부 건강을 평가하는 방법
④ 감정 강도의 변화가 우리의 잠재의식을 결정한다
⑤ 피부 전도도와 감정 강도 사이의 연결을 통한 감정 측정

questions.question: 13. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 어법상 옳은 것을 고르시오.[3.6점]
questions.passage: Spoken languages <u>①view</u> as incomplete devices for capturing precise differences. Some researchers think numbers represent the most <u>neutral</u> language of description. However, when our language of description is changed to numbers, we do not move toward greater accuracy. Numbers are no more appropriate ‘pictures of the world’ than words, music, or painting. While <u>②usefully</u> for specific purposes (e.g. census taking, income distribution), they eliminate information of enormous value. For example, the future lives of young students are tied to their scores on national tests. In effect, the ability to continue their education — along with where they can go and how much it will cost — largely <u>③depend</u> on a handful of numbers. These numbers do not account for the quality of schools they have attended, whether they have been tutored, have supportive parents, have test anxiety, and so on. Finally, putting aside the many ways in which statistical results can be manipulated, there are ways in which turning people’s lives into numbers <u>④is</u> morally insulating. Statistics on crime, homelessness, or the spread of a disease say nothing of people’s suffering. We read statistics as reports on events at a distance, thus allowing us <u>⑤escape</u> without being disturbed. Statistics are human beings with the tears wiped off. Quantify with caution.
questions.explanation: ① 언어는 간주되는 것이므로 수동태 are viewed가 되어야 합니다. ② While (they are) useful 형태의 분사구문/접속사 생략 구문이므로 형용사 useful이 필요합니다. ③ 주어가 the ability이므로 단수 동사 depends가 되어야 합니다. ④ turning people's lives into numbers라는 동명사구가 주어이므로 단수 동사 is는 적절합니다. ⑤ allow + 목적어 + to부정사 구조이므로 to escape가 되어야 합니다.

questions.question: 14. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절한 것을 고르시오. [3.5점]
questions.passage: The advent of air-conditioning accelerated the trend of constructing tightly sealed buildings, where air enters only through the system's filtered ducts. But this approach isn't the only option. Traditional buildings in hot regions like those in Sicily, Marrakesh, or Tehran ① <u>disguise</u> how well older architectural techniques handled heat. Builders used strategies like ② <u>minimizing shade</u>, promoting natural airflow, and using light-colored materials. They positioned structures to catch cool breezes while avoiding the harsh afternoon sun, and incorporated thick walls, white roofs, and transoms to enhance ventilation. Anyone who's visited a mudbrick home in Tucson or strolled through the narrow, <u>shaded</u> alleys of old Seville has experienced how ③ <u>unproductive</u> these time-tested methods can be. Yet much of this accumulated wisdom about <u>heat management</u> has been ④ <u>overlooked</u>. In this way, air-conditioning isn't just a tool for staying cool — it also represents a ⑤ <u>preservation</u> of historical knowledge.
questions.explanation: 전통적인 건축 방식의 지혜가 에어컨의 등장으로 인해 잊히거나 무시되고 있다는 문맥이므로, 'overlooked(간과된)'가 문맥상 적절합니다. ① disguise → demonstrate/show, ② minimizing → maximizing, ③ unproductive → effective/productive, ⑤ preservation → loss/erasure 등이 문맥에 적합합니다.

questions.question: 18. 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것을 고르시오.[3.4점]
questions.passage: There is a wealth of evidence that when parents, teachers, supervisors, and coaches are perceived as involved and caring, people feel happier and more motivated. And it is not just those people with power — we need to feel valued and respected by peers and coworkers. Thus, when the need for relatedness is met, motivation and internalization are fueled, provided that support for autonomy and competence are also there. If we are trying to motivate others, a caring relationship is a crucial basis from which to begin. And when we are trying to motivate ourselves, doing things to enhance a <u>sense of connectedness</u> to others can be crucial to long-term persistence. So exercise with a friend, call someone when you have a difficult decision to make, and ____________________.
options: ① try to find out your life goal
② give yourself the space to think back
③ maintain your motivation as long as possible
④ stand by other as they navigate their difficulties
⑤ allow others time for their own independent thinking
questions.explanation: 글의 핵심 주제는 타인과의 관계(relatedness, sense of connectedness)가 동기부여와 지속성에 중요하다는 것입니다. 빈칸 앞 문장에서 친구와 운동하고 누군가에게 전화를 하라는 등 타인과 연결되는 예시를 들고 있으므로, 타인이 어려움을 겪을 때 곁에 있어 주는 ④번이 문맥상 가장 적절한 연결입니다.
options_translation: ① 당신의 인생 목표를 찾으려 노력하라
② 스스로에게 되돌아볼 공간을 주어라
③ 가능한 한 오래 동기를 유지하라
④ 타인이 어려움을 헤쳐 나갈 때 곁에 있어 주어라
⑤ 타인에게 독립적인 사고를 할 시간을 주어라

questions.question: 20.주어진 글 다음에 이어질 글의 순서로 가장 적절한 것을 고르시오. [2.8점]
questions.passage: Routines enable athletes to evaluate competition <u>conditions.</u>
ordered_passages: (A) This routine allows the player to make small adjustments to their shooting form or focus based on the game situation, crowd noise, or physical state.

(B) For example, a basketball player's <u>free-throw</u> routine like dribbling a certain number of times, setting their feet, and taking a deep breath helps them assess the grip of the ball, the <u>condition of</u> the court, and their own muscle tension or fatigue.
(C) Much like tuning a musical instrument to suit the acoustics of a concert hall, the routine ensures every element is aligned for optimal performance.
questions.explanation: 주어진 문장에서 루틴이 운동선수들로 하여금 경기 조건을 평가하게 한다고 언급한 후, (B)에서 농구 선수의 자유투 루틴을 구체적인 예시로 들어 공의 그립감, 코트 상태 등을 평가함을 설명한다. (A)의 'This routine'은 (B)에서 설명한 루틴을 가리키며, 이를 통해 조정을 할 수 있음을 덧붙인다. 마지막으로 (C)에서 이를 악기 조율에 비유하며 최적의 수행을 위해 정렬된다고 결론짓는 순서가 가장 자연스럽다.

questions.question: 24. 다음 글의 내용을 한 문장으로 요약하고자 한다. 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은? [3.5점]
questions.passage: Assuming gene editing in humans proves to be safe and effective, it might seem logical, even preferable, to correct disease-causing mutations at the earliest possible stage of life, before harmful genes begin causing serious problems. Yet once it becomes possible to transform an embryo's mutated genes into "normal" ones, there will certainly be temptations to upgrade normal genes to superior versions. Should we begin editing genes in unborn children to lower their lifetime risk of heart disease or cancer? What about giving unborn children beneficial features, like greater strength and increased mental abilities, or changing physical characteristics, like eye and hair color? The pursuit for perfection seems almost natural to human nature, but if we start down this slippery slope, we may not like where we end up.
questions.summary_sentence: The potential for safe and effective gene editing in humans raises ethical questions about whether we should modify embryos not only to correct diseases but also to (A) _________ desirable traits, leading to concerns about the implications of pursuing genetic (B) _________ .
options: ① replace ...... mutation
② analyze ...... disorder
③ enhance ...... perfection
④ interrupt ...... diversity
⑤ exclude ...... variation
questions.explanation: 본문은 유전자 편집이 질병 치료를 넘어 바람직한 특성을 강화(enhance)하고 우월한 버전을 추구하는 유전적 완벽(perfection)에 대한 욕구로 이어질 수 있다는 윤리적 우려를 다루고 있다. 따라서 (A)에는 enhance, (B)에는 perfection이 적절하다.
options_translation: ① 교체하다 ...... 돌연변이
② 분석하다 ...... 질환
③ 강화하다 ...... 완벽
④ 방해하다 ...... 다양성
⑤ 제외하다 ...... 변화

questions.question:
[단답형 1]
다음 글을 읽고 밑줄친 ① ~ ⑤ 중 어법상 틀린 것을 2개 찾아 번호를 쓰고, 바르게 고치시오. [총 2.0점]
questions.passage: Let’s start with the path of avoidance. The boy waits for his dad and concentrates hard. When the ball comes flying across the net rapidly, he misses it ① <u>complete</u>. He puts his hands on his knees and sighs. “Never mind,” says his dad, “Try again. Practice makes perfect.” When the boy serves the ball, it returns with full force, ② <u>hitting</u> his elbow. The boy is not having much fun. He sets the paddle on the table, saying, “I have had enough,” and leaves for his room. His dad asks for ③ <u>other</u> game the next week, but the boy still has some pain in his elbow and does not feel like taking up the challenge. When his mom suggests ④ <u>playing</u> against his older brother, he turns down her suggestion because his brother is very tough. “No, thanks,” sighs the boy. “He’s going to be better than me anyway.” In his eyes, challenges are nothing more than obstacles, and he holds onto the belief that they ⑤ <u>are</u> best avoided.
subjective_conditions: 1. 정답 작성 시 반드시 빈칸 번호를 함께 표기할 것
2. 수정 부분을 포함하여 밑줄 친 부분을 반드시 쓸 것
questions.answer:
번호①: complete -> completely
번호③: other -> another
questions.explanation:
① 동사 misses를 수식해야 하므로 부사 형태인 completely가 적절하다.
③ 단수 명사인 game 앞에는 another를 사용해야 한다(other는 뒤에 복수 명사가 옴).

questions.question:
[단답형 2]
다음 글의 빈칸 ①~④에 문맥상 가장 알맞은 말을 <조건>에 맞게 쓰시오. [4.0점]
questions.passage:
Arles is an ancient city dating back to Roman times. Many Roman buildings remain, including an arena that was built in 90 A.D. The arena used to ①________ over 20,000 people who would go to watch various entertaining events. Vincent sometimes went to the bullfights that were held in the arena every Sunday. He particularly liked to watch the colorful crowds. He told a friend that he found the crowds ②________ . They inspired the painting Arena at Arles. The arena is in the top right corner of the painting and is barely visible. Below, there is a faint image of two bulls. However, Vincent paid lots of attention to the people and their colorful clothes. Some of the people are chatting with friends, others are cheering on the bulls, and the entire painting has a powerful energy.
Vincent painted the world-famous Café Terrace at Night in September 1888. He created this work while sitting outside the Café van Gogh at night. This was unusual because most painters did their night scenes from ③__________ and worked during the daytime. As such, they used a lot of black paint. Vincent, however, believed that night scenes contained diverse and vibrant colors. Indeed, the Café Terrace at Night has such a rich harmony of yellows, blues, and oranges that Vincent did not have to use a single drop of black paint. Even today, there is still a café at the site of Vincent's painting. It was renovated in the 1990s and painted yellow to look like the café in the painting. However, it is ④__________ whether the color of the original café was yellow or not. The reason is that Vincent painted the wall of the café yellow to show the lamp light.
subjective_conditions: 1. 정답 작성 시 반드시 빈칸 번호를 함께 표기할 것
2. <보기>의 단어만 활용하여 한 단어로만 쓸 것 (단어 추가하지 않음)
3. 각 단어를 한 번씩만 활용할 것 (중복 표기 금지)
4. 형태를 변형할 것
vocabulary_box: shrug / memorable / intimate / seating / majestic / make / certainty / fascinate
questions.answer:
① seat
② fascinating
③ memory
④ uncertain
questions.explanation:
① used to 다음에는 동사 원형이 와야 하므로 seating을 seat로 변형하여 사용합니다. (≈수용하다)
② find + 목적어 + 목적격 보어 구조에서 군중들이 매력적이라는 형용사 표현이 필요하므로 fascinate를 fascinating으로 변형합니다.
③ from(전치사) 다음에는 명사가 와야 하므로 memorable을 memory로 변형합니다.
④ 문맥상 확실하지 않다는 형용사가 필요하므로 certainty를 uncertain으로 변형합니다.

questions.question:
[서술형 1] 다음 글을 읽고 <조건>에 맞게 질문에 답하시오. [4.0점]
Q: Choose all the marketing strategies from the above examples that are appropriate based on the passage.
(A) _________ are the appropriate marketing strategies because they _________ (B) _________
questions.passage:
Promotion deals with consumer psychology. We can't force people to think one way or another, and the clever marketer knows that promotion is used to provide information in the most clear, honest, and simple fashion possible. By doing so, the possibility of increasing sales goes up. Gone are the days when promotions were done in order to fool the consumer into purchasing something. The long-term effect of getting a consumer to buy something they did not really want or need wasn't good. In fact, consumers fooled once can do damage to sales as they relate their experience to others. Instead, marketers now know that their goal is to identify the consumers who are most likely to appreciate a good or service, and to promote that good or service in a way that makes the value clear to the consumer. Therefore, marketers must know where the potential consumers are, and how to reach them.

< Examples of Marketing Strategies >
① Creating urgency through countdown timers and "limited time only" language, even when supply is stable.
② Promoting a product with vague claims like "the best on the market," without providing evidence or context.
③ Partnering with influencers to showcase products, even if the influencers have no real experience using them.
④ Analyzing consumer values and promoting a product transparently to a segment whose needs match the product's benefits.
⑤ Setting artificially high original prices to make discounts appear more appealing during sales promotions.
⑥ Using exaggerated claims like "miracle results overnight" to grab consumer attention quickly.
⑦ Identifying a group of consumers whose needs align with the product and clearly communicating its value and benefits.
⑧ Highlighting only the positive features of a product while hiding potential downsides.
⑨ Targeting random audiences on social media to increase exposure, regardless of their actual interest.
⑩ Creating fake positive reviews to build trust and boost initial sales.
subjective_conditions: (A) 번호로만 쓸 것
(B) 지문에 있는 단어만 사용하여 7단어 이상으로 작성할 것
questions.answer:
(A) ④, ⑦
(B) identify the consumers who are most likely to appreciate a good or service
questions.explanation: 지문은 현대의 마케팅이 소비자를 속이는 것이 아니라, 제품의 가치를 알아줄 소비자를 식별하고 가치를 명확하게 전달하는 것이라고 설명합니다. 따라서 ④(투명한 홍보)와 ⑦(적합한 소비자 그룹 식별 및 가치 전달)이 적절한 전략입니다. (B)의 경우 지문에 제시된 'identify the consumers who are most likely to appreciate a good or service' 혹은 'promote that good or service in a way that makes the value clear to the consumer' 등을 사용하여 조건(7단어 이상)을 충족할 수 있습니다.

questions.question:
[서술형 2]
다음 글의 빈칸에 가장 적절한 말을 <조건>에 맞게 쓰시오. [6.0점]
questions.passage: Piaget put the same amount of water into two different glasses: a tall narrow glass and a wide glass, then asked kids to compare two glasses. Kids younger than six or seven usually say that the tall narrow glass now holds more water, because the level is higher. And when they are ready, they figure out the conservation of volume for themselves just by playing with cups of water. Piaget argued that children's understanding of morality is like their understanding of those water glasses: we can't say that it is innate or kids learn it directly from adults. Rather, it is self-constructed as kids play with other kids. Taking turns in a game is like pouring water back and forth between glasses. When children turn five or six, they learn about (A) _________ better (B) _________ than (C) _________ .
subjective_conditions: 1. <보기>의 단어를 한 번씩만 모두 사용할 것
2. 필요시 형태를 변형할 것
vocabulary_box: with / fair / adults / teach / by / cooperate / through / lessons / peers
questions.answer:
(A) fairness by cooperating
(B) with peers
(C) through lessons taught by adults
questions.explanation: 이 글은 피아제의 인지 발달 이론과 도덕성 발달의 유사점을 설명하고 있습니다. 아이들이 물의 보존 개념을 스스로 터득하듯, 도덕성 역시 성인의 직접적인 가르침보다는 또래와의 상호작용을 통해 스스로 구성한다는 내용입니다. 따라서 (A)에는 협력을 통한 공정함(fairness by cooperating), (B)에는 또래들과 함께(with peers), (C)에는 성인에 의해 교육되는 교훈(through lessons taught by adults)을 통한 것보다 더 잘 배운다는 내용이 오는 것이 적절합니다.

questions.question: 1. 다음 글의 주제로 가장 적절한 것은? [3.1점]
questions.passage: Stress not only affects physical disease but also the very structure of our brains, making us even more likely to experience a drained brain. A number of studies have been done to reveal what happens in healthy people's brains when they go through something stressful. One study demonstrated a link between a smaller hippocampus and people who had experienced long-lasting stress. Why does this matter? This part of the brain helps you remain resilient in the face of stress and is involved in mood regulation. It also helps you to monitor the safety of your environment and store dangerous images in your long-term memory so you can avoid them in the future. It does all these things as part of its duties of regulating your sympathetic and parasympathetic nervous systems. But chronic stress can confuse the hippocampus and lead to turning signals for cortisol “on” instead of “off,” which can trap you in a constant state of fight, flight, or freeze.
options: ① brain flexibility in coping with chronic stress
② cumulative effects of persistent stress on physical health
③ structural and neurological consequences of prolonged stress on the brain
④ the vulnerability and resilience of human brain networks in memory
⑤ cognitive decline caused by a brain exposed to sudden, intense stress
questions.explanation: 이 글은 지속적인 스트레스가 뇌의 구조(해마의 크기 감소 등)와 신경학적 조절 기능(코르티솔 신호 체계 교란 등)에 미치는 부정적인 영향을 설명하고 있으므로 주제로 가장 적절한 것은 ③번입니다.
options_translation: ① 만성 스트레스에 대처하는 뇌의 유연성
② 지속적인 스트레스가 신체 건강에 미치는 누적 효과
③ 장기간의 스트레스가 뇌에 미치는 구조적 및 신경학적 결과
④ 기억에 있어서 인간 뇌 네트워크의 취약성과 회복력
⑤ 갑작스럽고 강렬한 스트레스에 노출된 뇌에 의해 유발된 인지적 저하

questions.question: 12.다음 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것을 고르시오. [3.2점]
questions.passage: The prominence of the social dimension in food writing might suggest that the flavor of food is taking a back seat. I suspect that most people view flavor as of secondary importance in social settings where food is served. Although our social gatherings coalesce around food, the meaning of these gatherings does not seem to depend on flavor. Flavor assists with the narrow purpose of filling the belly, and once that is accomplished it provides the backdrop for whatever social dynamics characterize the gathering. These can be understood independently of the flavor of the food on offer, the appreciation of which is understood to be personal and subjective. According to this conventional wisdom, the ceremonies and rituals around food, the social events that supply food with its meaning, do not depend on the quality of sensations provided by the food. To focus excessively on flavor is ____________________.
options: ① not to appreciate the aesthetic values at play
② to overlook the social meaning behind the dish
③ not to understand the cultural context of the cuisine
④ to prioritize these social relations over culinary taste
⑤ to underscore the larger significance of these social relations
questions.explanation: 지문은 음식의 풍미보다 사교적 차원과 모임의 의미가 더 중요하게 여겨진다는 통념을 설명하고 있습니다. 이러한 관점에 따르면, 풍미에 과도하게 집중하는 것은 음식 뒤에 숨겨진 '사회적 의미'를 간과하는 것이 되므로 ②번이 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 작용하는 미적 가치를 감상하지 않는 것이다
② 요리 뒤에 숨겨진 사회적 의미를 간과하는 것이다
③ 요리의 문화적 맥락을 이해하지 못하는 것이다
④ 요리 맛보다 이러한 사회적 관계를 우선시하는 것이다
⑤ 이러한 사회적 관계의 더 큰 중요성을 강조하는 것이다

questions.question: 17.다음 글의 내용을 아래와 같이 요약하고자 한다. 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것을 고르시오. [3.4점]
questions.passage: Great scientists are seldom one-hit wonders. Newton is a prime example: beyond the Newtonian mechanics, he developed the theory of gravitation, calculus, laws of motion, and optimization. In fact, well-known scientists are often involved in multiple discoveries, a phenomenon potentially explained by the Matthew effect. Indeed, an initial success may offer a scientist legitimacy, improve peer perception, provide knowledge of how to score and win, enhance social status, and attract resources and quality collaborators, each of these payoffs further increasing her odds of scoring another win. Yet, there is an appealing alternative explanation: Great scientists have multiple hits and consistently succeed in their scientific endeavors simply because they're exceptionally talented. Therefore, future success again goes to those who have had success earlier, because of advantages offered by the previous success, but because the earlier success was indicative of a hidden talent. The Matthew effect posits that success increases the future probability of success, raising the question: Does status dictate outcomes, or does it simply reflect an underlying talent or quality?
questions.summary_sentence: The text examines whether great scientists achieve multiple discoveries due to advantages gained from early (A)________ or because their (B)________ enables consistent achievement.
options: ① collaboration ...... creativity
② experiments ...... methodology
③ recognition ...... acquired skills
④ achievement ...... inherent traits
⑤ experience ...... persistence
questions.explanation: 글은 위대한 과학자들이 반복적인 성공을 거두는 이유로 두 가지 가능성을 제시한다. 하나는 초기 성공(마태 효과)으로 얻은 이점 때문이고, 다른 하나는 그들이 가진 뛰어난 재능 때문이다. 요약문의 (A)는 초기 성공에서 얻은 이점인 'achievement(업적/성취)'가 적절하며, (B)는 일관된 성취를 가능하게 하는 'inherent traits(내재적 특성/재능)'가 적절하다.
options_translation: ① 협력 ...... 창의성
② 실험 ...... 방법론
③ 인정 ...... 습득된 기술
④ 성취 ...... 내재적 특성
⑤ 경험 ...... 끈기

questions.question: 18. 글의 흐름으로 보아, 주어진 문장이 들어가기에 가장 적절한 곳을 고르시오.[3.0점]
questions.passage: In 1900, at the close of the first decade in which electric systems had become a practical alternative for manufacturers, less than 5 percent of the power used in factories came from electricity. But the technological advances of suppliers made electric systems and electric motors ever more affordable and reliable, and the suppliers’ intensive marketing programs also sped the adoption of the new technology. ( ① ) Further accelerating the shift was the rapid expansion in the number of skilled electrical engineers, who provided the expertise needed to install and run the new systems. ( ② ) Factories continued to build their own power supply systems on their own premises, and few manufacturers considered buying electricity from the small central stations. ( ③ ) Designed to supply lighting to local homes and shops, the central stations had neither the size nor the skill to serve the needs of big factories. ( ④ ) And the factory owners, having always supplied their own power, were not willing to assign such a critical function to an outsider. ( ⑤ ) They knew that a glitch in power supply would bring their operations to a halt — and that a lot of glitches might well mean bankruptcy.
questions.insertion_sentence: Electric power went from exotic to commonplace in no time, but one thing didn’t change.
questions.explanation: 주어진 문장의 'one thing didn’t change(한 가지는 변하지 않았다)'는 내용은 ②번 뒤의 'Factories continued to build their own power supply systems(공장들은 계속해서 자신들의 전력 공급 시스템을 구축했다)'는 내용과 자연스럽게 연결됩니다. 그 앞부분까지는 전력이 어떻게 널리 보급되었는지 설명하고 있으며, ②번부터는 그럼에도 불구하고 공장들이 자체 전력을 사용하던 관습을 유지했다는 흐름으로 전환됩니다.

questions.question: 19.글의 흐름으로 보아, 주어진 문장이 들어가기에 가장 적절한 곳을 고르시오. [2.9점]
questions.passage: Quite often the interaction between groups is socially unequal. ( ① ) This is reflected in the fact that in many cases borrowing of words or constructions goes mostly or entirely in one direction, from the dominant group to the less favored one. ( ② ) The languages of socially subordinated groups may from quite an early period of contact provide terminology for objects or practices with which speakers of the powerful group were previously unfamiliar. ( ③ ) In some cases, as with the Dharug language of Sydney, Australia, the source of some of the earliest loans from Indigenous Australian languages into English, the language system vanished after the obliteration of many of its speakers. ( ④ ) This pattern can be seen in words like kangaroo and boomerang, borrowed from the Dharug language, which has since become extinct. ( ⑤ ) The remainder shifted to varieties of English, the language of the people who had suppressed them.
questions.insertion_sentence: However, the effects of contact in that direction may not develop any further than this.
questions.explanation: 주어진 문장의 'that direction'은 ②번 문장에서 언급된 '사회적으로 하위 그룹의 언어가 지배적인 그룹에게 용어를 제공하는 방향'을 의미하며, 'any further than this(이보다 더 발전하지 못할 수도 있다)'라는 내용은 ③번 이후에 나오는 해당 언어가 소멸해버린 상황과 논리적으로 연결됩니다.

questions.question: 21. 주어진 글 다음에 이어질 내용을 순서에 맞게 배열한 것으로 가장 적절한 것을 고르시오.[2.9점]
questions.passage: When we realize we’ve said something in error and we pause to go back to correct it, we stop gesturing a couple of hundred milliseconds before we stop speaking.
ordered_passages: (A) When people are prevented from gesturing, they talk less fluently; their speech becomes halting because their hands are no longer able to supply them with the next word, and the next. Not being able to gesture has other deleterious effects.

(B) Such sequences suggest the startling notion that our hands “know” what we’re going to say before our conscious minds do, and in fact this is often the case. Gesture can mentally prime a word so that the right term comes to our lips.

(C) Without gesture to help our mental processes along, we remember less useful information, we solve problems less well, and we are less able to explain our thinking. Far from tagging along as speech’s clumsy companion, gesture represents the leading edge of our thought.
questions.explanation: 주어진 글에서 말하기 전에 제스처가 먼저 멈춘다는 순서를 언급했으므로, 이러한 순서가 손이 의식보다 먼저 안다는 것을 시사한다는 (B)가 가장 먼저 와야 합니다. (B)의 마지막 부분에서 제스처가 단어를 준비시킨다고 했으므로, 제스처를 못하게 하면 유창함이 떨어진다는 (A)가 이어지는 것이 자연스럽습니다. 마지막으로 제스처의 부재가 기억과 문제 해결 능력에도 악영향을 미친다는 추가적인 효과를 설명하는 (C)로 마무리되는 것이 적절합니다.

questions.question: 24. 다음 글에서 전체 흐름과 관계 없는 문장은? [3.0점]
questions.passage: There are reasons why science is not fully trusted and why healthy skepticism and critical thinking are essential. In spite of professional standards, claims of objectivity, and the peer review process, the conduct of science can be biased. ① All experts are not the same, nor do they submit their work to the same scrutiny. ② Knowing the source of funding can be important in evaluating scientific claims. ③ The absence of continued funding in scientific research has received limited attention, despite growing concerns about maintaining sustained progress. ④ For example, in the mid-20th century, tobacco companies secretly funded research to cast doubt on the link between smoking and cancer, delaying public health action and eroding trust in scientific integrity. ⑤ Stories such as this one fuel suspicion — but also lead to further safeguards in the scientific process. Funding disclosures, although not required five decades ago, have since been made compulsory.
questions.explanation: 이 글은 과학 연구에서 연구 자금의 출처가 연구 결과에 편향을 일으킬 수 있으며, 그에 따른 비판적 사고의 중요성을 강조하고 있습니다. ③번 문장은 과학 연구의 지속적인 발전과 관련된 '연구 자금의 지속적 부족'에 대해 언급하고 있으므로, 글의 핵심 주제인 '자금 출처에 따른 편향성 및 그로 인한 불신'과는 흐름상 관계가 없습니다.

questions.question: 6. 밑줄 친 <u>acting as a silent enforcer of the power dynamic</u> 부분이 다음 글에서 의미하는 바로 가장 적절한 것은? [3.4점]
questions.passage: Historically, palaces weren't just homes; they were carefully constructed stages designed to impress and intimidate. While stone symbolized permanence and strength, glass offered something equally powerful: visibility. The introduction of large windows in palaces allowed rulers to literally look down upon their subjects, emphasizing their elevated position. Conversely, it also allowed subjects to gaze up at their leaders, creating a sense of awe and distance. Consider the Palace of Versailles: its Hall of Mirrors, lined with reflective surfaces, not only magnified the grandeur of the space but also placed the king at the center of a dazzling display, reinforcing his absolute authority. The use of glass in palaces wasn't merely aesthetic; it was strategic. Open sightlines allowed for better surveillance and control, ensuring the safety and security of the ruling family. Courtiers and visitors were constantly aware of being observed, contributing to an atmosphere of careful obedience and respect. The very architecture dictated social behavior, with glass <u>acting as a silent enforcer of the power dynamic</u>.
options: existing as a bridge linking the throne and the public
subtly acting as an implicit regulator for upholding hierarchy
opening the ruler's eyes to the invisible hardships of the ruled
serving as the lens through which the ruler contemplates himself
standing as a thin, brittle, invisible ceiling in a fragile social hierarchy
questions.explanation: 글의 문맥상 궁전의 유리(창문, 거울 등)는 단순히 미적인 용도가 아니라, 지배자가 피지배자를 감시하고 권위를 과시하며 사람들에게 관찰당하고 있다는 인식을 심어주어 복종을 이끌어내는 전략적 도구로 쓰였습니다. 따라서 '권력 역학의 침묵의 집행자'라는 말은 계급 질서를 유지하기 위한 암묵적인 규제자 역할을 한다는 의미인 2번이 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 왕좌와 대중을 연결하는 다리로서 존재함
② 계층 구조를 유지하기 위한 암묵적인 규제자로서 미묘하게 작용함
③ 피지배층의 보이지 않는 고난에 대해 통치자의 눈을 뜨게 함
④ 통치자가 자신을 성찰하는 렌즈 역할을 함
⑤ 취약한 사회적 계층 구조 내에서 얇고 깨지기 쉬운 투명 천장으로 서 있음

questions.question: [7~9] 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것을 고르시오. 8. [3.4점]
questions.passage: Within liberal culture, the preservation of the family's integrity is ① <u>outweighed</u> by the value of fair equality of opportunity for individuals. In contrast, in Confucian culture, the family assumes a fundamental role in human flourishing, and living within a family institution is considered the essential way of life, while seeking fair equality of opportunity for individuals is important. The familial role of individuals ② <u>precedes</u> their civil status as state citizens. Therefore, for Confucians, the family possesses inherent value that should never be ③ <u>abandoned</u>, even if it fails to prevent certain societal inequalities. Some cultures, like the liberal one, may choose to impose increasing ④ <u>restrictions</u> on the role of families and implement more egalitarian government programs for education, healthcare, and other positive rights in society in the pursuit of fair equality of opportunity. On the other hand, other cultures, like Confucian cultures, may primarily assign welfare to the family, rarely ⑤ <u>accepting</u> resulting inequalities as long as basic rights are safeguarded by the state.
questions.explanation: 유교 문화권에서는 가족의 역할을 근본적으로 중시하며, 설령 그것이 사회적 불평등을 방지하지 못하더라도 가족의 가치를 저버리지 않는다고 설명하고 있습니다. 따라서 마지막 문장에서 유교 문화권은 기본권이 보호되는 한 결과적인 불평등을 '받아들인다'는 내용이 되어야 하므로 'rarely accepting(거의 수용하지 않는)'은 문맥상 어색합니다.

questions.question: 14. 다음 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것을 고르시오. [3.1점]
questions.passage: Prioritizing a moment of intentional mental activity midday is _________________________________________. Imagine pausing in the middle of a busy day to refresh your mind and recharge your energy. This power of a midday break is, however, often underestimated. Breaking away from routine, especially with activities designed to stimulate your brain, effectively prevents cognitive tiredness and enhances productivity for the rest of the day. Neurobic exercises—simple yet effective—are perfect for such strategic pauses. They target different areas of your brain, keeping it agile and alert, thereby creating a mental oasis that refreshes and prepares you for the afternoon's challenges. This brief, strategic pause is more than just a break; it actively boosts your cognitive capabilities, ensuring your mind remains sharp and focused. For instance, even briefly experimenting with neurobic exercises during lunch, such as using your non-dominant hand for routine tasks like writing or eating, challenges your brain, activating pathways that aren't typically engaged and promoting greater flexibility in thinking.
options: vital for preserving intellectual vigor and maximizing work output
always counterproductive to achieving short-term operational targets
often considered an outdated and ineffective management technique
solely beneficial for reducing interpersonal conflict and emotional burnout
a necessary requirement for the standardized formalization of office hours
questions.explanation: 이 글은 하루 중 정오에 잠깐의 시간을 내어 의도적인 정신 활동(뉴로빅 운동 등)을 하는 것이 인지적 피로를 방지하고 오후의 생산성을 높이며 뇌의 기민함을 유지시켜 준다고 설명하고 있습니다. 따라서 이러한 활동은 지적 활력을 보존하고 작업 생산성을 극대화하는 데 필수적이라는 내용인 1번이 정답입니다.
options_translation: ① 지적 활력을 보존하고 작업 생산성을 극대화하는 데 필수적이다
② 단기적인 운영 목표를 달성하는 데 항상 역효과를 낸다
③ 종종 구식이고 비효과적인 관리 기법으로 간주된다
④ 대인 관계 갈등과 정서적 소진을 줄이는 데에만 유익하다
⑤ 근무 시간의 표준화된 공식화를 위한 필수 요구 사항이다

questions.question: 15. [3.3점] 다음 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Viewing time as a purchasable and consistent product cemented artificial views on time into our psyche, but every now and again we ______________________. On twenty six occasions in the last fifty years, a second has been added to everyone's day to adjust for the Earth wobbling and the rate of its spin changing. For instance, when El Niño, a climatic system in the Pacific, causes wind speed to change dramatically, it can slow the rotation of the Earth slightly. Indeed, the Earth's spin is generally slowing because the moon's gravity is acting as a drag, so days are getting longer by about 1.7 milliseconds per century. Such events disturb the similarity between manmade time and more flexible time based on the Earth's naturally occurring rotation. When events like this happen, a bunch of humans make the decision to add a small slice of time to your day, without your knowledge. We try to force our fixed, manmade view of time on to nature in the false hope that it will yield. It doesn't.
options: ① are compelled to make our flexible sense of time rigid
② acknowledge that nature does not conform to our manmade time
③ are forced to acknowledge the standardization of our concept of time
④ end up confronting the reality that time is entirely under human agency
⑤ find ourselves realizing that we have been taking every minute of time for granted
questions.explanation: 이 글은 인간이 시간을 구매 가능하고 일관된 제품으로 보며 인위적인 시간 관념을 고착시켰지만, 실제로는 지구의 자전 속도 변화(윤초 추가 등)로 인해 인간이 만든 시간이 자연의 유연한 시간과 일치하지 않는 사례들을 설명하고 있습니다. 마지막 문장에서 우리가 고정된 인위적인 시간 관념을 자연에 강요하려 하지만 자연은 굴복하지 않는다고 언급하고 있으므로, 빈칸에는 우리가 만든 시간에 자연이 순응하지 않는다는 것을 인정하게 된다는 내용이 들어가는 것이 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 우리의 유연한 시간 감각을 경직되게 만들 수밖에 없다
② 자연이 우리가 만든 시간에 부합하지 않는다는 점을 인정한다
③ 시간 개념의 표준화를 인정하도록 강요받는다
④ 시간이 전적으로 인간의 통제하에 있다는 현실에 직면하게 된다
⑤ 우리가 시간의 매 순간을 당연하게 여겨왔다는 것을 깨닫게 된다

questions.question: 16. [3.1점] 다음 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.passage: Experiments testify to science's embrace of ignorance. Arguably the worst thing a scientist can do is to suppose they know what will happen in a given scenario without bothering to check. The rise of the experimental philosophy coincided with ______________________. For all that experimental science today is often assumed to be supported by a philosophical framework and an approved methodology ("state your hypothesis and then test it"), the fact is that, as philosopher of science Ian Hacking says, "One can conduct an experiment simply out of curiosity to see what will happen." Indeed, in the view of Charles Darwin's son, the astronomer George Darwin, once in a while one should do a completely crazy experiment, even if it is most likely to prove fruitless. You never know until you try.
options: ① the liberation of curiosity as a valuable rather than a questionable quality
② the validation of systematic observation over spontaneous experimentation
③ the suppression of speculative inquiry in favor of evidence-based methodology
④ the requirement that all scientific inquiries begin with clear practical applications
⑤ the establishment of rigorous hypotheses as prerequisites for legitimate experimentation
questions.explanation: 이 글은 과학이 무지를 포용하고, 단순히 어떤 일이 일어날지 보기 위해 호기심에서 실험을 수행하는 것의 중요성을 강조하고 있습니다. 가설을 세우고 검증하는 정해진 방법론보다도, 때로는 결과가 없을 것 같은 '미친 실험'조차도 해볼 가치가 있다는 조지 다윈의 견해를 통해 호기심 자체가 과학에서 중요한 동력임을 알 수 있습니다. 따라서 실험 철학의 부상이 호기심을 의심스러운 것이 아닌 가치 있는 자질로 해방시킨 것과 시기적으로 일치했다는 ①번이 정답입니다.
options_translation: ① 의심스러운 자질이기보다는 가치 있는 자질로서 호기심의 해방
② 자발적인 실험보다 체계적인 관찰의 검증
③ 증거 기반 방법론을 선호하여 추측적 탐구를 억제함
④ 모든 과학적 탐구가 명확한 실용적 응용에서 시작되어야 한다는 요구 사항
⑤ 정당한 실험의 전제 조건으로서 엄격한 가설의 수립

questions.question: 17. 다음 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은? [3.1점]
questions.passage: Waste has historically been seen as a necessary driver of the economy. Sales are tied to the amount of a product supplied, which is directly dependent on the demand for that product. Therefore, if you design the product to eventually be wasted, you can ensure that the demand for more products will be sustained. Many strategies have been incorporated into product design and use to ensure that waste is inevitable, such as planned obsolescence, limited access to tools for repairs, and use of cheap materials. All these strategies ensure that the consumer will have limited access to the product in use and will eventually require a replacement. Those who supported the idea that waste is necessary to drive demand failed to realize that __________. Through this setup, companies simply lease out products that were once sold directly to the customer: products as a service. With this transition of ownership, companies maintain profit by offering maintenance and repair services and are encouraged to develop long-lasting products.
options: longer-lasting products would inevitably decrease total market demand
waste reduction strategies ultimately decrease overall economic growth and consumer spending
the circular economy model requires government subsidies to compensate for reduced product sales
consumers prefer disposable products over repairable ones due to convenience and lower initial costs
emphasizing the prevention of disposal by restoration and rebuilding establishes a new type of market demand
questions.explanation: 이 글은 과거에는 경제 성장을 위해 폐기물을 의도적으로 발생시키는 전략(계획적 구식화 등)을 사용했으나, 제품을 서비스로 제공하고 유지보수 서비스를 통해 수익을 창출하는 모델(products as a service)이 등장하면서 폐기를 방지하는 것이 오히려 새로운 시장 수요를 창출할 수 있음을 설명하고 있습니다. 따라서 빈칸에는 폐기 방지 및 복원을 통한 새로운 수요 창출을 간과했다는 내용인 5번이 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 더 오래 지속되는 제품은 필연적으로 전체 시장 수요를 감소시킬 것이다
② 낭비 감소 전략은 궁극적으로 전반적인 경제 성장과 소비자 지출을 감소시킨다
③ 순환 경제 모델은 감소된 제품 판매를 보상하기 위해 정부 보조금을 필요로 한다
④ 소비자들은 편리함과 낮은 초기 비용 때문에 수리 가능한 제품보다 일회용 제품을 선호한다
⑤ 복원과 재건에 의한 폐기 방지를 강조하는 것이 새로운 유형의 시장 수요를 창출한다

questions.question: [20~21] 다음 글에서 전체 흐름과 관계 없는 문장을 고르시오. 21. [3.0점]
questions.passage: Just as an expert in the taste and colour of wine will gain much by being aware of the chemistry that underlies those qualities, so each perspective on the body can potentially enhance the others. And yet every scientific tool, from microscopes to mathematics, and every aspect of the body, from the brain to the microorganism, requires such depth of expertise that this tends not to happen. 1 We tend to study the human body in silos, each community separated from the others by its own specialised vocabulary. 2 Research communities may be dedicated to one type of scientific tool or a specific component of the body, such as one type of cell: how different types of cell communicate with one another becomes its own specialist topic. 3 Even simple forms of life on Earth are now rarely studied as a whole, and the human body is evidently much more complex. 4 The body's cells function as an integrated network, where specialized cells in various tissues and organs depend on continuous interaction to sustain life. 5 As long ago as 1890, a newspaper commented that knowledge 'had already become too vast to be manageable'; today, nobody is an expert in the whole of anything.
questions.explanation: 이 글은 지식이 너무 방대해짐에 따라 신체에 대한 연구가 각자의 전문 분야(silos)로 나뉘어 단절된 채로 이루어지고 있으며, 전체적인 관점에서 통합적으로 연구되기 어렵다는 점을 설명하고 있습니다. 4번 문장은 신체의 세포가 통합된 네트워크로서 상호작용하며 생명을 유지한다는 '신체의 생물학적 특성'에 대해 설명하고 있으므로, 연구의 전문화와 지식의 단절을 다루는 전체 흐름에서 벗어납니다.

questions.question: 22. 글의 흐름으로 보아, 주어진 문장이 들어가기에 가장 적절한 곳을 고르면? [3.1점]
questions.passage: As a political researcher in Germany, Noelle-Neumann observed that during election campaigns, certain views seemed to get more play than others, and sometimes people muted their opinions rather than talking about them, especially if those opinions were perceived to be unpopular. ( ① ) Noelle-Neumann calls this the spiral of silence, which occurs when individuals who perceive that their opinions are popular express them. ( ② ) This process occurs in a spiral. ( ③ ) One side of an issue ends up with considerable publicity and the other side with very little. ( ④ ) In everyday life, people express their opinions in a variety of ways: they talk about them, they wear buttons, they put bumper stickers on their cars, and they post their views on social media. ( ⑤ ) According to this theory, people are more apt to do these kinds of things when they perceive that others share their opinions.
questions.insertion_sentence: Conversely, those who do not think their opinions are popular remain quiet due to a fear of social isolation.
questions.explanation: 주어진 문장은 자신의 의견이 주류가 아니라고 생각하는 사람들이 소외에 대한 두려움으로 인해 침묵을 지킨다는 내용을 담고 있습니다. ②번 앞 문장에서 자신의 의견이 대중적이라고 생각하는 사람들이 의견을 표명한다는 '침묵의 소용돌이'의 한 축을 설명했으므로, 대조를 나타내는 'Conversely'로 시작하며 나머지 한 축(비주류 의견의 침묵)을 설명하는 주어진 문장이 들어가는 것이 가장 적절합니다. 이후 문장에서 이러한 과정이 소용돌이처럼 일어난다고 결론짓습니다.

questions.question: [23~24] 주어진 글 다음에 이어질 내용을 순서에 맞게 배열한 것으로 가장 적절한 것을 고르시오. 23. [3.0점]
questions.passage: We can discard or replace a scientific theory only if we have a better way of explaining the evidence that supports it. The theories of Newton and Einstein offer great examples.
ordered_passages: (A) Some scientists today are seeking a theory of gravity that will go beyond Einstein's. If any new theory ever gains acceptance, it will have to match all the successes of Einstein's theory as well as work in new realms where Einstein's theory does not.

(B) Still, the many successes of Newton's theory could not be ignored, and Einstein's theory would not have gained acceptance if it had not been able to explain these successes equally well. It did, and that is why we now view Einstein's theory as a broader theory of gravity than Newton's theory.

(C) A vast body of evidence supports Newton's theory of gravity, but by the late nineteenth century scientists had begun to discover cases where its predictions did not perfectly match observations. Only when Einstein developed his general theory of relativity, which was able to match the observations, were these discrepancies explained.
questions.explanation: 주어진 글에서 뉴턴과 아인슈타인의 이론을 예시로 제시합니다. (C)에서 먼저 뉴턴 이론의 성공과 관찰 결과 사이의 불일치, 그리고 이를 해결한 아인슈타인의 상대성 이론을 언급합니다. (B)에서는 아인슈타인의 이론이 뉴턴의 성공 사례들을 똑같이 잘 설명해냈기 때문에 더 넓은 범위의 중력 이론으로 받아들여졌음을 설명합니다. 마지막으로 (A)에서 현재 과학자들이 아인슈타인을 넘어선 새로운 이론을 찾고 있다는 흐름으로 이어지는 것이 자연스럽습니다.

questions.question: 1. <u>밑줄 친 the same was true of beauty가</u> 다음 글에서 의미하는 바로 가장 적절한 것은? (3.2점)
questions.passage: Plato argued that when you see something that strikes you as beautiful, you are really just seeing a partial reflection of true beauty, just as a painting or even a photograph only captures part of the real thing. True beauty, or what Plato calls the Form of Beauty, has no particular color, shape, or size. Rather, it is an abstract idea, like the number five. You can make drawings of the number five in blue or red ink, big or small, but the number five itself is none of those things. It has no physical form. Think of the idea of a triangle, for example. Although it has no particular color or size, it somehow lies within each and every triangle you see. Plato thought <u>the same was true of beauty.</u> The Form of Beauty somehow lies within each and every beautiful thing you see.
options: ① beauty was innate
② beauty lay in perfection
③ beauty was found only in nature
④ beauty existed beyond any visible shape
⑤ beauty was rooted in simplicity and clarity
questions.explanation: 본문에서 플라톤은 숫자 '5'나 '삼각형'의 개념처럼 진정한 아름다움(Form of Beauty)은 구체적인 색상, 모양, 크기가 없는 추상적인 관념이며, 물리적 형태를 가지지 않는다고 설명합니다. 따라서 '아름다움에 대해서도 마찬가지이다'라는 밑줄 친 부분은 아름다움이 눈에 보이는 어떤 구체적인 형태 너머에 존재한다는 의미입니다.
options_translation: ① 아름다움은 타고난 것이었다
② 아름다움은 완벽함 속에 있었다
③ 아름다움은 자연에서만 발견되었다
④ 아름다움은 가시적인 형태 너머에 존재했다
⑤ 아름다움은 단순함과 명료함에 뿌리를 두고 있었다

questions.question: 2. 다음 글의 요지로 가장 적절한 것은? (2.6점)
questions.passage: No respectable boss would say, "I make it a point to discourage my staff from speaking up, and I maintain a culture that prevents disagreeing viewpoints from ever getting aired." If anything, most bosses even say that they are pro-dissent. This idea can be found throughout the series of conversations with corporate, university, and nonprofit leaders, published weekly in the business sections of newspapers. In the interviews, the featured leaders are asked about their management techniques, and regularly claim to continually encourage internal protest from more junior staffers. As Bot Pittman remarked in one of these conversations: "I want us to listen to these dissenters because they may intend to tell you why we can't do something, but if you listen hard, what they're really telling you is what you must do to get something done."
options: ① No responsible leader must underestimate the danger of setting clear guidance.
② Strong leaders not only provide strategic guidance but also unite their teams under it.
③ Great leaders are those who remain confident and composed in times of uncertainty.
④ Respected leaders would never overlook the value of dissent, as it is crucial for problem-solving.
⑤ Effective leaders never cease to invest in their own growth, recognizing that personal development is key to leading others.
questions.explanation: 글의 내용은 훌륭한 리더들이 반대 의견(dissent)을 장려하며, 특히 마지막 부분에서 반대자들의 의견을 경청하는 것이 문제를 해결하고 일을 완수하기 위해 무엇을 해야 하는지 알려주는 가치가 있음을 강조하고 있습니다.
options_translation: ① 어떤 책임감 있는 리더도 명확한 지침을 설정하는 위험을 과소평가해서는 안 된다.
② 강력한 리더는 전략적 지침을 제공할 뿐만 아니라 그 아래에서 팀을 결속시킨다.
③ 위대한 리더는 불확실한 시기에 자신감 있고 침착함을 유지하는 사람들이다.
④ 존경받는 리더는 반대 의견의 가치를 결코 간과하지 않는데, 그것이 문제 해결에 중요하기 때문이다.
⑤ 유능한 리더는 자기 계발이 타인을 이끄는 열쇠임을 인식하고 자신의 성장에 투자를 멈추지 않는다.

questions.question: 3. 다음 글의 주제로 가장 적절한 것은? (3.3점)
questions.passage: Assuming gene editing in humans proves to be safe and effective, it might seem logical, even preferable, to correct disease-causing mutations at the earliest possible stage of life, before harmful genes begin causing serious problems. Yet once it becomes possible to transform an embryo's mutated genes into "normal" ones, there will certainly be temptations to upgrade normal genes to superior versions. Should we begin editing genes in unborn children to lower their lifetime risk of heart disease or cancer? What about giving unborn children beneficial features, like greater strength and increased mental abilities, or changing physical characteristics, like eye and hair color? The pursuit for perfection seems almost natural to human nature, but if we start down this slippery slope, we may not like where we end up.
options: ① how genetic engineering techniques are shaping the future of disease prevention
② potential risks associated with advancements in gene editing technology

questions.question: 4. 다음 글의 제목으로 가장 적절한 것을 고르시오.(2.6점)

questions.question: 5. 다음 글의 제목으로 가장 적절한 것을 고르시오. (3.4점)
questions.passage: In many sports, people realized the difficulties and even impossibilities of young children participating fully in many adult sport environments. They found the road to success for young children is unlikely if they play on adult fields, courts or arenas with equipment that is too large, too heavy or too fast for them to handle while trying to compete in adult-style competition. Common sense has prevailed; different sports have made adaptations for children. As examples, baseball has T ball, football has flag football and junior soccer uses a smaller and lighter ball and (sometimes) a smaller field. All have junior competitive structures where children play for shorter time periods and often in smaller teams. In a similar way, tennis has adapted the court areas, balls and rackets to make them more appropriate for children under 10. The adaptations are progressive and relate to the age of the child.

questions.question: 6. 다음 글의 제목으로 가장 적절한 것을 고르시오. (2.8점)
questions.passage: Our skin conducts electricity more or less efficiently, depending on our emotions. And when those tiny drops of sweat appear, our skin gets more electrically conductive. This change in sweat gland activity happens completely without your conscious mind having much say in the matter. If you feel emotionally intense, you're going to notice an increase in sweat gland activity. This is particularly useful from a scientific viewpoint, because it allows us to put an objective value on a subjective state of mind. We can actually measure your emotional state by tracking how your body subconsciously sweats, by running a bit of electricity through your skin. We can then turn the subjective, subconscious experience of emotional intensity into an objective number by figuring out how good your skin gets at transferring an electrical current.

② Emotional Detection Using Skin Conductivity
③ Inside the Mind: Where Feelings Are Born
④ Mastering the Mind through Meditation
⑤ Sweat: The Body's Cooling System

questions.question: 7.다음 글의 제목으로 가장 적절한 것을 고르시오.  (2.6점)
questions.passage: In the course of trying to solve a problem with an invention, you may encounter a brick wall of resistance when you try to think your way logically through the problem. Such logical thinking is a linear type of process, which uses our reasoning skills. This works fine when we're operating in the area of what we know or have experienced. However, when we need to deal with new information, ideas, and viewpoints, linear thinking will often come up short. On the other hand, creativity by definition involves the application of new information to old problems and the conception of new viewpoints and ideas. For this you will be most effective if you learn to operate in a nonlinear manner; that is, use your creative brain. Stated differently, if you think in a linear manner, you'll tend to be conservative and keep coming up with techniques which are already known. This, of course, is just what you don't want.
options: ① Think Outside the Line
② The Trap of the Unfamiliar
③ Creativity Starts with Logic
④ Relying on Reason in Uncertain Times

questions.question: 8. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 어법상 틀린 것을 있는 대로 고르시오. (3.6점)
questions.passage: Working around the whole painting, rather than concentrating on one area at a time, will mean you can stop at any point and the painting can ⓐ <u>be thought of as completing</u>. questions.question: 9. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 어법상 틀린 것을 있는 대로 고르시오.(4.2점)
questions.passage: Every species has certain climatic requirements, including ⓐ <u>what</u> level of heat or cold it is able to endure, for example. When the climate changes, the locations that satisfy those requirements change, too. All creatures are capable of some degree of movement. Even creatures that appear immobile like a tree and a barnacle ⓒ <u>is</u> capable of dispersal at some stage of their life - as a seed, in the case of the tree, or as a larva, in the case of the barnacle. A creature must get from the place it is born - often ⓓ <u>inhabited</u> by its parent - to a place ⓔ <u>in which</u> allows it to withstand, thrive, and reproduce. From fossils, scientists found out that even creatures like trees, ⓕ <u>migrating</u> with surprising speed during past periods of climate change, adapted to changing environments.

questions.question: 10. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 어법상 틀린 것을 있는 대로 고르시오.(4.0점)

The results showed that the group music therapy improved the quality of participants' life, with those attending a greater number of sessions ⓑ <u>derived</u> the greatest benefits. ⓒ <u>Highlighting</u> singing as the primary focus, another group of psychologists reviewed articles on the efficacy of group singing as a mental health treatment for individuals ⓓ <u>coping with</u> mental health issues in a community setting. questions.question: 11. (3.5점)
questions.passage: While listening to your child during an emotional moment, be aware that simply sharing observations, rather than asking questions, ⓐ <u>tend</u> to work better in getting a conversation started. Even if she does manage to respond, she might fear that her answer isn't sufficient ⓓ <u>to justify</u> feeling that way. In such situations, asking multiple questions may cause her to become silent. It is often more effective to reflect the observation ⓔ <u>what</u> you have made, such as saying, "You seem a little tired today," or "I noticed that you frowned when the recital was mentioned." questions.question: 12. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 어법상 틀린 것은? (2.7점)
questions.passage: The rise of air-conditioning accelerated the construction of sealed boxes, ① <u>where</u> the building's only airflow is through the filtered ducts of the air-conditioning unit. Architects understood the importance of shade, airflow, light colors. They oriented buildings to capture cool breezes and block the worst heat of the afternoon. They built with thick walls and white roofs and transoms over doors ③ <u>to encourage</u> airflow. Anyone who has ever spent a few minutes in a mudbrick house in Tucson, or walked on the narrow streets of old Seville, ④ <u>know</u> how well these construction methods work. ② whether

questions.question: 13.다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것을 고르시오. (3.3점)
questions.passage: Improving your gestural communication involves more than just knowing when to nod or shake hands. This simple yet powerful gesture can make others feel more ③ <u>reluctant</u> to engage in conversation. But be careful of the trap of over-gesturing. questions.question: 14.다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것을 고르시오. (3.2점)
questions.passage: A number of research studies have shown how experts in a field often experience difficulties when introducing newcomers to that field. For example, in a genuine training situation, Dr. Pamela Hinds found that people expert in using mobile phones were surprisingly ① <u>less</u> precise than novice phone users in judging how long it takes people to learn to use the phones. Experts may become ② <u>unaware</u> of the difficulty a task presents to beginners, an effect referred to as the 'curse of knowledge'. questions.question: 15. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것을 고르시오.(4.1점)
questions.passage: What does it mean for a character to be a hero as opposed to a villain? questions.question: 16.다음 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것을 고르시오. (3.4점)
