options_translation: ① 더 강한 소속감과 상호 지원을 기르는
② 시간 관리 능력을 향상시키고 명확한 우선순위를 설정하는
③ 타인과 거리를 두고 성찰을 위한 감정적 공간을 만드는
④ 개인적 도전을 극복하기 위한 인내와 회복력을 증진하는
⑤ 신체적 지구력과 전반적인 운동 성과를 향상시키는

questions.question: 17. 다음 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것을 고르시오.(3.5점)
questions.passage: The rate of speed at which one is traveling will greatly determine the ability to process detail in the environment. In evolutionary terms, human senses are adapted to the speed at which humans move through space under their own power while walking. Our ability to distinguish detail in the environment is therefore ideally suited to movement at speeds of perhaps five miles per hour and under. The fastest users of the street, motorists, therefore have a much more limited ability to process details along the street — a motorist simply has little time or ability to appreciate design details. Conversely, pedestrians, who move at a much slower pace, ____________________. Joggers and bicyclists fall somewhere in between these polar opposites: while they travel faster than pedestrians, their rate of speed is ordinarily much slower than that of the typical motorist.
options: ① rely primarily on side vision for navigation
② experience difficulty in recognizing street features
③ gain a heightened awareness of their surroundings
④ focus more on movement proficiency than on details
⑤ struggle to perceive small details in the environment
questions.explanation: 글은 이동 속도가 환경의 세부 사항을 처리하는 능력에 큰 영향을 미친다고 설명합니다. 보행자는 자동차 운전자보다 훨씬 느리게 이동하므로, 운전자와 반대로 환경의 세부적인 부분들을 더 잘 인식할 수 있습니다. 따라서 '주변 환경에 대한 향상된 인식을 갖게 된다'는 의미의 ③번이 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 내비게이션을 위해 주로 측면 시야에 의존한다
② 도로의 특징을 인식하는 데 어려움을 겪는다
③ 주변 환경에 대한 고조된 인식을 얻는다
④ 세부 사항보다 움직임의 숙달에 더 집중한다
⑤ 환경의 작은 세부 사항을 인지하는 데 고군분투한다

questions.question: 18. 다음 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것을 고르시오.(4.1점)
questions.passage:
Promotion deals with consumer psychology. We can't force people to think one way or another, and the clever marketer knows that promotion is used to provide information in the most clear, honest, and simple fashion possible. By doing so, the possibility of increasing sales goes up. Gone are the days when promotions were done in order to fool the consumer into purchasing something. The long-term effect of getting a consumer to buy something they did not really want or need wasn't good. In fact, consumers fooled once can do damage to sales as they relate their experience to others. Instead, marketers now know that their goal is to ____________________, allowing the true worth of products or services to resonate clearly in their mind. Therefore, marketers must know where the potential consumers are, and how to reach them.
*resonate: 반향을 불러일으키다
options: ① set consumers' desire on fire
② appeal primarily to consumers' emotions
③ unlock doors consumers didn't know existed
④ identify gaps in the market to push products aggressively
⑤ target those whose needs are aligned with the product's value
questions.explanation: 현대의 마케팅은 소비자를 속이는 것이 아니라 정직한 정보를 제공하여 제품의 진정한 가치가 전달되게 하는 것입니다. 따라서 마케터의 목표는 제품의 가치와 필요가 일치하는 사람들을 찾아내는 것입니다.
options_translation: ① 소비자의 욕구에 불을 지핀다
② 주로 소비자의 감정에 호소한다
③ 소비자가 존재 여부를 몰랐던 문을 연다
④ 제품을 공격적으로 밀어붙이기 위해 시장의 틈새를 식별한다
⑤ 제품의 가치와 요구가 일치하는 사람들을 목표로 삼는다

questions.question: 19. 다음 글에서 전체 흐름과 관계 없는 문장은? (2.7점)
questions.passage: The science we learn in grade school is a collection of certainties about the natural world—the earth goes around the sun, DNA carries the information of an organism, and so on. ① Only when you start to learn the practice of science do you realize that each of these "facts" was hard won through a succession of logical inferences based upon many observations or experiments. ② The process of science is more focused on minimizing uncertainties in our knowledge than simply gathering pieces of knowledge. ③ Our degree of uncertainty regarding a particular piece of knowledge depends on how far we have progressed in understanding it. ④ Science has already eliminated ambiguity surrounding the natural world, leaving no room for uncertainty—therefore, scientific inquiry is now nothing more than mere repetition. ⑤ Today we are quite certain of how a ball will roll down a slope, but our understanding of how high-temperature superconductors work remains a work in progress after more than a century of effort.
questions.explanation: 이 글은 과학이 불확실성을 줄여가는 과정임을 설명하고 있습니다. 하지만 ④번은 과학이 이미 모든 모호성을 제거하여 불확실성이 전혀 남아있지 않으며 단순한 반복일 뿐이라고 주장하고 있으므로 글의 전체 흐름과 상반됩니다.

questions.question: 20. 주어진 글 다음에 이어질 글의 순서로 가장 적절한 것은? (3.6점)
questions.passage: Consider the seemingly simple question How many senses are there? Around 2,370 years ago, Aristotle wrote that there are five, in both humans and animals—sight, hearing, smell, taste, and touch.
ordered_passages: (A) Other animals have senses that are even harder to categorize. Many vertebrates have a different sense system for detecting odors. Some snakes can detect the body heat of their prey.

(B) However, according to the philosopher Fiona Macpherson, there are reasons to doubt it. For a start, Aristotle missed a few in humans: the perception of your own body which is different from touch and the sense of balance which has links to both touch and vision.

(C) These examples tell us that "senses cannot be clearly divided into a limited number of specific kinds," Macpherson wrote in The Senses. Instead of trying to push animal senses into Aristotelian buckets, we should study them for what they are.
questions.explanation: 주어진 글에서 아리스토텔레스의 5감설을 언급한 후, (B)에서 '그러나'를 사용하여 인간에게도 다른 감각이 있음을 보여주며 이 이론에 의문을 제기합니다. 이어 (A)에서 '다른 동물들'의 사례를 추가로 들고, 마지막으로 (C)에서 이러한 사례들을 종합하여 감각을 특정 종류로 명확히 나눌 수 없다는 결론을 내리는 것이 자연스럽습니다.

questions.question: 21. 글의 흐름으로 보아, 주어진 문장이 들어가기에 가장 적절한 곳을 고르시오.(2.8점)
questions.passage: During the past few decades, scientists have begun to find more and more similarities between octopuses and humans. One of the most interesting ones is intelligence. Octopuses are smart. The best evidence is their ability to camouflage themselves. ( ① ) An octopus can change its color, pattern, and texture, and the changes are carried out almost instantly. ( ② ) In terms of speed and the diversity of change, no other animal can rival octopuses. ( ③ ) The main purpose of these changes is to avoid detection by their hunters or their prey. ( ④ ) When an octopus comes across its hunter or prey, it must swiftly determine the appropriate color, pattern, and texture to display. ( ⑤ ) To acquire knowledge and put it to use for a particular purpose is a sure sign of intelligence.
questions.insertion_sentence: Such a decision implies that it has gained sufficient knowledge of the surrounding animals and applies it to survive.
questions.explanation: 주어진 문장의 'Such a decision'은 ④번 문장에서 언급한 '적절한 색상, 패턴, 질감을 신속하게 결정해야 하는 상황'을 가리킵니다. 또한 문장의 내용(지식을 습득하고 생존을 위해 적용함)이 ⑤번 다음 문장인 지능의 확실한 징표라는 결론으로 자연스럽게 이어집니다.

questions.question: 22. 글의 흐름으로 보아, 주어진 문장이 들어가기에 가장 적절한 곳을 고르시오.(3.2점)
questions.passage: One of the most striking characteristics of a sleeping animal or person is that they do not respond normally to environmental stimuli. (①) If you open the eyelids of a sleeping mammal the eyes will not see normally — they are functionally blind. (②) Some visual information apparently gets in, but it is not normally processed as it is either reduced or weakened, just like other sensory systems. (③) Stimuli are perceived but not fully processed, so they do not awaken the individual. (④) Perceptual disengagement probably serves the function of protecting sleep, so some researchers exclude it from the definition of sleep itself. (⑤) Nonetheless, many animals (including humans) use the intermediate state of drowsiness to derive some benefits of sleep without total perceptual disengagement.
questions.insertion_sentence: However, since sleep cannot occur without it, it appears to be a crucial aspect of the definition of sleep.
questions.explanation: 주어진 문장의 'it'은 앞 문장의 'Perceptual disengagement(지각적 이탈)'를 가리킵니다. ④번 뒤 문장에서 일부 연구자들이 지각적 이탈을 수면의 정의에서 제외한다는 내용이 나오고, 주어진 문장에서 '하지만 그것(지각적 이탈) 없이는 수면이 일어날 수 없으므로 수면 정의의 중요한 측면으로 보인다'는 반박이 이어지는 것이 자연스럽습니다. ⑤번 뒤 문장은 '그럼에도 불구하고(Nonetheless)'로 시작하며 완전한 지각적 이탈 없이도 이득을 얻는 중간 상태에 대해 설명하며 논의를 보충합니다.

questions.question: 23. Octopuses에 관한 다음 글의 내용과 일치하지 않는 것은? (2.7점)
questions.passage: Another sign of the intelligence of the octopus is its use of tools. In the lab, octopuses use tools to get food rewards. In the wild, they use stones to create walls to protect the entrances to their homes. They use not only stones but anything they can find to protect themselves. The most impressive example of octopuses using tools came in 2009 in Indonesia. A few octopuses were found to collect coconut shells. They cleaned the shells with bursts of water, carried them to a new location, and piled them as a shelter. Traveling with the shells under their bodies forced them to walk slowly along the sea floor. This made the octopuses more exposed to predators. But it seems that they were willing to take that risk for greater future protection. The scientists who discovered the behavior argue that this is clear evidence of octopuses using tools.
options: ① They have been observed using tools to obtain food rewards in laboratory settings.
② In the natural environment, they employ stones to construct barriers that guard the entrances to their homes.
③ They make use of stones and whatever they discover to keep themselves safe.
④ The octopuses found in Indonesia cleaned coconut shells with jets of water and carried them to a different spot.
⑤ Since carrying the shells made them more vulnerable to predators, they rarely took the risk for their future safety.
questions.explanation: 지문에서 문어는 포식자에게 노출될 위험이 있음에도 불구하고 미래의 더 큰 보호를 위해 기꺼이 그 위험을 감수했다고(willing to take that risk) 기술되어 있으므로, 위험을 거의 감수하지 않았다는 ⑤번은 일치하지 않습니다.
options_translation: ① 그들은 실험실 환경에서 먹이 보상을 얻기 위해 도구를 사용하는 것이 관찰되었다.
② 자연 환경에서, 그들은 집 입구를 지키는 장벽을 만들기 위해 돌을 사용한다.
③ 그들은 스스로를 안전하게 지키기 위해 돌뿐만 아니라 발견하는 무엇이든 활용한다.
④ 인도네시아에서 발견된 문어들은 물줄기로 코코넛 껍질을 닦고 다른 장소로 옮겼다.
⑤ 껍질을 운반하는 것이 포식자에게 더 취약하게 만들었기 때문에, 그들은 미래의 안전을 위해 위험을 거의 감수하지 않았다.

questions.question: 24. 다음 글의 내용과 일치하지 않는 것은? (2.8점)
questions.passage: With no horses available, the Inca empire excelled at delivering messages on foot. The messengers were stationed on the royal roads to deliver the Inca king's orders and reports coming from his lands. Called Chasquis, they lived in groups of four to six in huts, placed from one to two miles apart along the roads. They were all young men and especially good runners who watched the road continuously in both directions. If they caught sight of another messenger coming, they hurried out to meet them. The Inca built the huts on high ground, in sight of one another. When a messenger neared the next hut, he began to call out and repeated the message three or four times to the one who was running out to meet him. The Inca empire could relay messages 1,000 miles (1,610 km) in three or four days under good conditions.
options: ① Chasquis were positioned along the royal roads in groups of four to six, living in huts placed one to two miles apart.
② Chasquis were all young men who were exceptional runners, and constantly kept an eye on the road in both directions.
③ Away from elevated areas were the huts, where Chasquis resided, to avoid being seen by others.
④ When a messenger approached another hut, they would call out and repeat the message several times to the next runner.
⑤ The Inca empire was capable of transmitting messages with a range of 1,000 miles within three or four days in ideal conditions.
questions.explanation: 지문에서 잉카인들은 서로 시야를 확보하기 위해 오두막을 높은 지대(high ground)에 지었다고 명시되어 있습니다. 따라서 지대가 높은 곳에서 멀리 떨어진 곳에 집을 지었다는 ③번은 내용과 반대됩니다.
options_translation: ① 차스키는 왕의 도로를 따라 4~6명씩 무리를 지어 배치되었으며, 1~2마일 간격으로 배치된 오두막에서 살았다.
② 차스키는 모두 뛰어난 달리기 선수인 젊은 남성들이었으며, 끊임없이 양방향으로 도로를 주시했다.
③ 차스키가 거주하는 오두막은 다른 사람들에게 보이는 것을 피하기 위해 높은 지역에서 떨어진 곳에 있었다.
④ 메신저가 다른 오두막에 가까워지면 소리를 질러 다음 주자에게 메시지를 여러 번 반복했다.
⑤ 잉카 제국은 이상적인 조건 하에서 3~4일 이내에 1,000마일 범위의 메시지를 전달할 수 있었다.

questions.question: 25. 다음 글을 읽고, 답할 수 없는 질문은? (3.3점)
questions.passage: Octopuses' use of tools can be found in their love of toys and puzzles, too. They are curious about new objects, and do not like getting bored. That is why aquariums try to come up with ideas to keep their octopuses busy. Some aquariums hide food inside a big doll and let the octopus break up the toy to get the food. Others offer plastic building blocks for their octopuses to play with. Our knowledge about the octopus is still very limited. Thanks to the efforts of scientists, however, it is expanding year by year. One of the most impressive new findings about the octopus is that it seems to have feelings. Of course, it is impossible for us to know exactly what they feel, but a few of their changes in skin color seem to be linked to their feelings. For example, a giant Pacific octopus that turns red seems to be excited, while it is white when it is relaxed. An octopus presented with a difficult puzzle often undergoes several rapid changes in color. The octopus seems to be worried that it may not solve the problem.
options: ① Why do aquariums provide toys and plastic building blocks for octopuses?
② What is one challenge we face when trying to understand octopuses' emotions?
③ How do we believe octopuses express their feelings?
④ How does an octopus react when given a challenging puzzle?
⑤ Are octopuses more likely to use tools when they are stressed or anxious?
questions.explanation: 지문에서 문어가 도구를 사용하는 것과 감정을 느끼는 것에 대한 언급은 있지만, 스트레스나 불안을 느낄 때 도구를 더 많이 사용하는지에 대한 정보는 없습니다.
options_translation: ① 왜 수족관은 문어에게 장난감과 플라스틱 조립 블록을 제공하는가?
② 문어의 감정을 이해하려고 할 때 우리가 직면하는 한 가지 어려움은 무엇인가?
③ 우리는 문어가 그들의 감정을 어떻게 표현한다고 믿는가?
④ 어려운 퍼즐이 주어졌을 때 문어는 어떻게 반응하는가?
⑤ 문어는 스트레스를 받거나 불안할 때 도구를 사용할 가능성이 더 높은가?

questions.question:
29. 다음 글을 읽고 작성한 감상평으로 가장 적절하지 않은 것은?
(3.6점)
questions.passage: Let's assume that at least some animals are capable of thinking despite lacking a language. This doesn't necessarily mean that they possess concepts, for some forms of thought may be nonconceptual. We can imagine, for instance, a squirrel who is planning how to get from the branch she's currently standing on to a branch from the tree in front. To do this, in principle she doesn't need a concept of branch nor a concept of tree. It might be enough for her to have, for example, the ability to think in images; to make a mental map of the tree where she can imagine and try out different routes. This doesn't imply that squirrels lack concepts, simply that they don't need them for this concrete form of thinking. For us to be able to say that an animal has concepts, we have to show not just that she's capable of thinking, but also that she has certain specific abilities.
options: ① The passage helped me understand that thinking doesn't always require language or concepts. The squirrel example clearly showed how an animal could plan using mental images.

② After reading about the squirrel, I thought about how I sometimes imagine routes in my head when I walk home. I don't name every street or object, but I still know where to go. Maybe that's similar to <u>conceptual thinking</u>.

③ The passage first says animals might think without language, and then it explains how. I liked that the author supported the idea with a clear example. It made me see that thought doesn't always need words or definitions.

④ I used to think that thinking always involved language, but now I see that mental images can also guide decisions. The squirrel imagining routes made sense to me. It shows that thought can be visual, not just verbal.
⑤ The writer says that even if animals don't have concepts, they might still think. I found this point convincing because the squirrel example shows actual planning without using words.
questions.explanation: 지문에서는 다람쥐가 구체적인 개념(concept) 없이도 이미지나 정신적 지도를 통해 생각할 수 있다는 '비개념적 사고(nonconceptual thought)'를 설명하고 있습니다. ②번의 경우, 이름을 붙이지 않고 경로를 떠올리는 것은 비개념적 사고에 가깝기 때문에 이를 '<u>conceptual thinking</u>(개념적 사고)'이라고 표현한 것은 적절하지 않습니다.
options_translation: ① 이 글은 사고가 항상 언어나 개념을 필요로 하는 것은 아니라는 점을 이해하는 데 도움이 되었습니다. 다람쥐 예시는 동물이 어떻게 정신적 이미지를 사용하여 계획을 세울 수 있는지 명확하게 보여주었습니다.
② 다람쥐에 관한 글을 읽고 나서, 집으로 걸어갈 때 머릿속으로 경로를 상상하는 방식에 대해 생각해보았습니다. 모든 거리나 물체의 이름을 명명하지는 않지만, 여전히 어디로 가야 할지 압니다. 아마 그것이 <u>개념적 사고</u>와 비슷할 것입니다.
③ 이 글은 먼저 동물이 언어 없이 생각할 수 있다고 말한 뒤, 그 방법을 설명합니다. 저자가 명확한 예시로 그 아이디어를 뒷받침한 것이 좋았습니다. 사고가 항상 단어나 정의를 필요로 하는 것은 아니라는 점을 알게 해주었습니다.
④ 사고에는 항상 언어가 포함된다고 생각했었지만, 이제는 정신적 이미지도 결정을 내리는 데 지침이 될 수 있다는 것을 알았습니다. 경로를 상상하는 다람쥐의 모습이 이해가 되었습니다. 이는 사고가 단어뿐만 아니라 시각적일 수도 있음을 보여줍니다.
⑤ 작가는 비록 동물이 개념을 가지고 있지 않더라도 여전히 생각할 수 있다고 말합니다. 다람쥐 예시가 단어를 사용하지 않고도 실제로 계획하는 모습을 보여주기 때문에 이 점이 설득력 있다고 생각했습니다.

questions.question: 30. 다음 글을 읽고 작성한 감상문의 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은? (4.3점)
questions.passage: Plants can communicate, although not in the same way we do. Some express their discontent through scents. You know that smell that hangs in the air after you've mowed the lawn? Yeah, that's actually an SOS. Some plants use sound. Yes, sound, though at a frequency that we can't hear. Researchers experimented with plants and microphones to see if they could record any trouble calls. They found that plants produce a high-frequency clicking noise when stressed and can make different sounds for different stressors. The sound a plant makes when it's not getting watered differs from the one it'll make when a leaf is cut. However, it's worth noting that experts don't think plants are crying out in pain. It's more likely that these reactions are knee-jerk survival actions. Plants are living organisms, and their main objective is to survive. Scents and sounds are their tools for defending against things that might harm them.
questions.summary_sentence: Reading this passage gave me a whole new perspective on something I've always taken for granted - the smell of freshly cut grass. I used to think of it as just a pleasant sign of spring, but now I see it as a (A) _________ from the plants. It's fascinating to realize that plants, though they can't speak or move like animals, still find ways to communicate distress through scents and even sounds. What struck me most is how these signals are not random - they're survival strategies. This reminds me that the basic goal of all living organisms, including plants, is (B) _________. Everything they do, even releasing a scent or making a tiny sound, is ultimately aimed at protecting themselves. It's incredible how much complexity and intention can exist in something we usually overlook.
options: ① renewal sign ------ growth
② cry for rescue ------ survival
③ breath of fresh air ------ reproduction
④ pleasant side effect ------ cooperation
⑤ warning sign to insects ------ balance
questions.explanation: 지문에서 갓 깎은 풀 냄새가 실제로는 식물의 'SOS' 신호라고 설명하고 있으며, 식물의 반응은 생존(survival)을 위한 자동적인 작용이라고 언급하고 있습니다. 따라서 (A)에는 '구조를 위한 외침(cry for rescue)', (B)에는 '생존(survival)'이 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 재생의 신호 ------ 성장
② 구조를 위한 외침 ------ 생존
③ 신선한 공기의 호흡 ------ 번식
④ 즐거운 부작용 ------ 협력
⑤ 곤충에 대한 경고 신호 ------ 균형

questions.question: 1. 밑줄 친 (a)~(e) 중에서 어법상 틀린 것은? [3.4점]
questions.passage: In high school, everyone told me how talented an artist I was, so I dreamed of becoming an illustrator. In university, though, everyone seemed (a) <u>much</u> more talented than me, and they all worked so hard that I felt small in comparison. I thought about giving up my dream of becoming an artist. Then one day, I happened to see a drawing I (b) <u>had won</u> an award for from middle school on the kitchen wall. I was embarrassed because it wasn't very good. People say you shouldn't <u>compare apples to oranges</u>, and they're right. That's why it doesn't make sense to compare yourself to Internet personalities or even people in your real life. Maybe they had an advantage, or even a disadvantage, that you didn't. If you are going to compare yourself to anyone, the only fair comparison is "yesterday-you." Only you know where you started and how much effort you've put in. I couldn't see the progress in my ability when I only compared myself to others. Everyone develops (c) <u>differently</u>. I'm able to see now the drawing in the kitchen was full of mistakes (d) <u>what</u> I no longer make. It is empowering to see how I have improved rather than (e) <u>to envy</u> the success of others. Your competition isn't the person next door or the influencer on social media: it's you.
questions.explanation: (d)의 what은 앞에 선행사(mistakes)가 있으므로 관계대명사 that 또는 which로 고쳐야 문법적으로 옳습니다.

questions.question: 2. 밑줄 친 <u>compare apples to oranges</u>가 위의 글에서 의미하는 바로 가장 적절한 것은? [3.5점]
questions.passage: In high school, everyone told me how talented an artist I was, so I dreamed of becoming an illustrator. In university, though, everyone seemed (a) <u>much</u> more talented than me, and they all worked so hard that I felt small in comparison. I thought about giving up my dream of becoming an artist. Then one day, I happened to see a drawing I (b) <u>had won</u> an award for from middle school on the kitchen wall. I was embarrassed because it wasn't very good. People say you shouldn't <u>compare apples to oranges</u>, and they're right. That's why it doesn't make sense to compare yourself to Internet personalities or even people in your real life. Maybe they had an advantage, or even a disadvantage, that you didn't. If you are going to compare yourself to anyone, the only fair comparison is "yesterday-you." Only you know where you started and how much effort you've put in. I couldn't see the progress in my ability when I only compared myself to others. Everyone develops (c) <u>differently</u>. I'm able to see now the drawing in the kitchen was full of mistakes (d) <u>what</u> I no longer make. It is empowering to see how I have improved rather than (e) <u>to envy</u> the success of others. Your competition isn't the person next door or the influencer on social media: it's you.
options: ① judge unrelated things by the same standard
② resist the temptation to become an influencer
③ try more fruits beyond just oranges and apples
④ develop the talents you possess to succeed in life
⑤ find common ground between fundamentally different things
questions.explanation: '사과와 오렌지를 비교하다'라는 표현은 서로 근본적으로 다른 조건이나 상황에 처한 대상을 동일한 기준으로 비교하는 오류를 지칭합니다.
options_translation: ① 관련 없는 것들을 같은 기준으로 판단하다
② 인플루언서가 되고 싶은 유혹에 저항하다
③ 단지 오렌지와 사과 너머의 더 많은 과일을 시도하다
④ 인생에서 성공하기 위해 소유한 재능을 계발하다
⑤ 근본적으로 다른 것들 사이에서 공통점을 찾다

questions.question: 3. 다음 글의 요지로 가장 적절한 것은? [2.9점]
questions.passage: Promotion deals with consumer psychology. We can't force people to think one way or another, and the clever marketer knows that promotion is used to provide information in the most clear, honest, and simple fashion possible. By doing so, the possibility of increasing sales goes up. Gone are the days when promotions were done in order to fool the consumer into purchasing something. The long-term effect of getting a consumer to buy something they did not really want or need wasn't good. In fact, consumers fooled once can do damage to sales as they relate their experience to others. Instead, marketers now know that their goal is to identify the consumers who are most likely to appreciate a good or service, and to promote that good or service in a way that makes the value clear to the consumer. Therefore, marketers must know where the potential consumers are, and how to reach them.
options: ① Consumers need to be aware of consumer psychology to avoid being fooled by marketers.
② Consumers keep good relationships with marketers to stay informed about their purchases.
③ People are misled or tricked by promotions but are eventually satisfied with the products.
④ Marketers should identify the right consumers and promote products transparently to highlight their value.
⑤ Promotion targets consumers to encourage purchases without concern for the costs of goods or services.
questions.explanation: 이 글은 현대의 마케팅이 소비자를 속이는 것이 아니라, 제품의 가치를 알아줄 적절한 소비자를 찾아 투명하고 정직하게 정보를 제공하여 가치를 분명히 전달해야 함을 강조하고 있습니다.
options_translation: ① 소비자들은 마케터들에게 속지 않기 위해 소비자 심리를 인식할 필요가 있다.
② 소비자들은 그들의 구매에 대해 정보를 유지하기 위해 마케터들과 좋은 관계를 유지한다.
③ 사람들은 홍보에 의해 오도되거나 속지만 결국 제품에 만족한다.
④ 마케터들은 적절한 소비자를 식별하고 제품의 가치를 강조하기 위해 투명하게 홍보해야 한다.
⑤ 홍보는 제품이나 서비스의 비용에 대한 걱정 없이 구매를 장려하기 위해 소비자를 목표로 한다.

questions.question: 5. 다음 글의 제목으로 가장 적절한 것을 고르시오.[2.9점]
questions.passage: Improving your gestural communication involves more than just knowing when to nod or shake hands. It's about using gestures to complement your spoken messages, adding layers of meaning to your words. Open-handed gestures, for example, can indicate honesty, creating an atmosphere of trust. You invite openness and collaboration when you speak with your palms facing up. This simple yet powerful gesture can make others feel more comfortable and willing to engage in conversation. But be careful of the trap of over-gesturing. Too many hand movements can distract from your message, drawing attention away from your words. Imagine a speaker whose hands move quickly like birds, their message lost in the chaos of their gestures. Balance is key. Your gestures should highlight your words, not overshadow them.
options: ① Mastering the Art of Interpreting Gestures
② The Dominance of Verbal Language Over Gestures
③ Elevating Communication Through the Art of Gestures
④ Why Repetition Is Key to Effective Communicative Gestures
⑤ Exploring Hand Movements That Build Trust and Connection
questions.explanation: 이 글은 제스처를 사용하여 구어 메시지를 보완하고 의사소통의 의미를 더하는 방법과 균형 잡힌 제스처의 중요성에 대해 설명하고 있으므로, '제스처의 기술을 통한 의사소통의 격상'이 가장 적절한 제목입니다.
options_translation: ① 제스처 해석의 기술 마스터하기
② 제스처에 대한 언어적 언어의 지배력
③ 제스처의 기술을 통한 의사소통의 격상
④ 효과적인 의사소통 제스처에 반복이 핵심인 이유
⑤ 신뢰와 연결을 구축하는 손동작 탐구하기

questions.question: 6.다음 글의 제목으로 가장 적절한 것을 고르시오. [3.4점]
questions.passage: There is a wealth of evidence that when parents, teachers, supervisors, and coaches are perceived as involved and caring, people feel happier and more motivated. And it is not just those people with power -- we need to feel valued and respected by peers and coworkers. Thus, when the need for relatedness is met, motivation and internalization are fueled, provided that support for autonomy and competence are also there. If we are trying to motivate others, a caring relationship is a crucial basis from which to begin. And when we are trying to motivate ourselves, doing things to enhance a sense of connectedness to others can be crucial to long-term persistence. So exercise with a friend, call someone when you have a difficult decision to make, and be there as a support for others as they take on challenges.
options: ① Boosting Your Motivation by Imitating Peers
② Related to Others: The Key Factor in Motivation
③ What Is the Role of Motivation in Decision Making?
④ Cooperating with Others: A Path to Greater Happiness
⑤ The Link Between Motivation and Dependence on Others
questions.explanation: 글의 핵심 내용은 타인과의 관계성(relatedness)이나 연결감(connectedness)이 충족될 때 동기부여가 잘 이루어진다는 것이므로, '타인과의 관계: 동기부여의 핵심 요소'가 제목으로 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 동료를 모방하여 동기부여 증진하기
② 타인과의 관계: 동기부여의 핵심 요소
③ 의사 결정에서 동기부여의 역할은 무엇인가?
④ 타인과 협력하기: 더 큰 행복으로 가는 길
⑤ 동기부여와 타인에 대한 의존 사이의 연결 고리

questions.question: 9. 다음 글의 내용과 일치하지 않는 것은? [3.6점]
questions.passage: An octopus's average life is about a year, which ends after reproducing. One day, eight months after meeting her, I found her with another octopus. It was bittersweet knowing her final moments were approaching even though she would bear young. After mating, she didn't come out of her den. There would be no feeding or hunting. She was timing her final moments for the hatching of her eggs. After the eggs hatched, she died. A few months later, my son found a little octopus. We believe her story continues on. I fell in love with an octopus and the amazing wildness she represented. I built a relationship with her and witnessed her life up to the final moments. I saw her from a perspective that I could not have had without this experience. She was smart, sensitive, and strong, often going through rough and tough days just like humans do. Eventually, she committed herself to protecting the birth of her young before she died. As a human being, I found something noble in that sacrifice. She was not simply an octopus; she was a part of this world just as I am a part of it now, and in that sense, we all have our own stories to tell.
options: ① The life of an octopus comes to an end after breeding.
② The author denies that the octopus's story continues beyond her death.
③ The author developed a close bond with the octopus and remained by her side until the very end of her life.
④ Like humans, the octopus endured hard times with strength.
⑤ The author thought the octopus showed amazing wildness and noble sacrifice.
questions.explanation: 지문에서 작가는 'A few months later, my son found a little octopus. We believe her story continues on.'라고 언급하며 문어가 죽은 뒤에도 그 이야기가 계속된다고 믿고 있습니다. 따라서 작가가 이를 부정(denies)한다는 ②번은 내용과 일치하지 않습니다.
options_translation: ① 문어의 삶은 번식 후에 끝이 난다.
② 작가는 문어의 이야기가 그녀의 죽음 이후에도 계속된다는 것을 부정한다.
③ 작가는 문어와 밀접한 유대감을 형성했고 그녀의 생이 끝날 때까지 곁에 머물렀다.
④ 인간처럼, 그 문어는 강인함으로 힘든 시간을 견뎌냈다.
⑤ 작가는 그 문어가 놀라운 야생성과 고귀한 희생을 보여주었다고 생각했다.

questions.question: 10. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 어법상 틀린 것을 고르시오.[3.5점]
questions.passage: I returned to the Cape of Good Hope, South Africa, where I had spent my childhood, after over 20 years of movie-making. I went diving in the cold sea off the coast of the Cape, and it was among the dense seaweed forests ①<u>where</u> I met an octopus. I saw a fish peacefully ②<u>swim</u> near a heap of shells. Suddenly, an octopus sprang from the heap and grabbed the fish. ③<u>Amazed</u> at the cleverness of the octopus, I swam a little closer, but it disappeared. In fact, it had lifted a piece of seaweed, wrapped it around itself, and was staring at me out of a little gap. What an extraordinary creature! I wondered what would happen if I kept ④<u>to watch</u> it. To see the world from the octopus's perspective, I left a camera near the den and started visiting regularly. I even mapped the environment around the den. ⑤<u>Expecting</u> some drama to come, I waited.
questions.explanation: keep 동사는 목적어로 동명사를 취하므로, to watch를 watching으로 고쳐야 합니다.

questions.question: 11. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 어법상 틀린 것을 고르시오.[3.5점]
questions.passage: One of the persistent myths of mainstream society is that the knowledge we study in schools ①<u>is</u> factual and neutral. Yet we know that knowledge evolves over time and is dependent on the moment in history and the cultural reference/point of the society that accepted ②<u>them</u>. Thinking critically involves more than just acquiring new information so as to ③<u>determine</u> which facts are true and which false. It also involves determining the social, historical, and political meaning given to those facts. This determination includes assessing the investment various groups may have in furthering or challenging those meanings in any particular historical moment. For example, there was a time ④<u>when</u> it was not widely understood that the Earth is round. Common sense might tell us that it is flat, and anyone looking out over a vast landscape would have this sense confirmed. Yet when scientific reasoning and more accurate technological methods for measuring the Earth emerged, the knowledge or "fact" ⑤<u>that</u> the Earth is flat was rewritten.
questions.explanation: ②번의 them이 지칭하는 대상은 불가산 명사인 knowledge이므로 단수 대명사인 it으로 고쳐야 합니다.

questions.question: 15. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것을 고르시오.[3.3점]
questions.passage: The rise of air-conditioning accelerated the construction of sealed boxes, where the building's only airflow is through the filtered ducts of the air-conditioning unit. It doesn't have to be this way. Look at any old building in a hot climate, whether it's in Sicily or Marrakesh or Tehran. Architects understood the importance of shade, airflow, light colors. They ① <u>adjusted</u> buildings to capture cool breezes and block the worst heat of the afternoon. They built with thick walls and white roofs and transoms over doors to ② <u>discourage</u> airflow. Anyone who has ever spent a few minutes in a mudbrick house in Tucson, or walked on the narrow streets of old Seville, knows how well these construction methods ③ <u>function</u>. But all this wisdom about how to deal with heat, accumulated over centuries of practical experience, is all too often ④ <u>disregarded</u>. In this sense, air-conditioning is not just a technology of personal comfort; it is also a technology of ⑤ <u>forgetting</u>.
questions.explanation: 과거의 건축가들은 공기 흐름(airflow)의 중요성을 이해하여 건물을 설계했습니다. 문맥상 시원한 바람을 포착하고 열을 차단하기 위해 문 위의 채광창(transoms) 등을 설치한 것이므로, 공기 흐름을 '막는(discourage)' 것이 아니라 '장려하거나 촉진하는(encourage)' 것이 적절합니다.

questions.question: 16.다음 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것을 고르시오. [3.8점]
questions.passage: I was drowning in a sea of responsibilities, concerns, and anxieties, and that was when I read an article with a simple insight. The article advised me to draw two big circles, with myself in the center. The smaller circle is my circle of influence, and I have direct control over the things inside it: what I eat and drink, how I behave, or what I do after school. The bigger circle is called my circle of concern: things I worry about but have no direct control over. For example, I have no direct control over how my professor will react to my report, but I do have control over the amount of research I do for it. Believing that everything was in my circle of influence________________. By wasting less energy on my circle of concern, I was able to invest more energy into things that mattered. I no longer worry about what my friends think, and I focus on my own actions.
options: ① left my friends feeling exhausted and annoyed
② empowered me with the energy to reach my goals
③ made me feel overwhelmed and mentally worn out
④ led people to avoid discussing important matters with me
⑤ filled me with confidence and pride in my capabilities
questions.explanation: 필자는 통제할 수 없는 일(관심의 원)에 에너지를 낭비하며 불안해하다가, 통제 가능한 일(영향력의 원)에 집중하라는 조언을 받았습니다. 빈칸이 포함된 문장은 과거에 모든 것이 자신의 영향력 안에 있다고 믿었을 때의 부정적인 상태를 설명해야 하므로 '압도당하고 정신적으로 지치게 만들었다'는 내용이 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 내 친구들을 기진맥진하고 짜증나게 만들었다
② 내 목표에 도달할 수 있는 에너지를 내게 부여했다
③ 나를 압도당하고 정신적으로 지치게 만들었다
④ 사람들이 나와 중요한 문제를 논의하는 것을 피하게 만들었다
⑤ 내 능력에 대한 자신감과 자부심으로 나를 채웠다

questions.question: 23. 글의 흐름으로 보아, 주어진 문장이 들어가기에 가장 적절한 것을 고르시오. [2.8점]
questions.passage: Plants can communicate, although not in the same way we do. Some express their discontent through scents. You know that smell that hangs in the air after you’ve mowed the lawn? Yeah, that’s actually an SOS. Some plants use sound. Yes, sound, though at a frequency that we can’t hear. ( ① ) Researchers experimented with plants and microphones to see if they could record any trouble calls. ( ② ) They found that plants produce a high-frequency clicking noise when stressed and can make different sounds for different stressors. ( ③ ) The sound a plant makes when it’s not getting watered differs from the one it’ll make when a leaf is cut. ( ④ ) It’s more likely that these reactions are knee-jerk survival actions. ( ⑤ ) Plants are living organisms, and their main objective is to survive. Scents and sounds are their tools for defending against things that might harm them.
questions.insertion_sentence: However, it’s worth noting that experts don’t think plants are crying out in pain.
questions.explanation: ④번 앞 문장까지는 식물이 스트레스 상황에서 소리를 낸다는 연구 결과를 설명하고 있습니다. 주어진 문장은 전문가들이 이를 '고통의 울부짖음'으로 보지 않는다는 내용이며, ④번 뒤의 '이러한 반응은 무릎 반사적인 생존 행동일 가능성이 더 크다'는 설명과 자연스럽게 연결됩니다.

questions.question: 25.글의 흐름으로 보아, 주어진 문장이 들어가기에 가장 적절한 것을 고르시오. [2.9점]
questions.passage: In the course of trying to solve a problem with an invention, you may encounter a brick wall of resistance when you try to think your way logically through the problem. ( ① ) Such logical thinking is a linear type of process, which uses our reasoning skills. ( ② ) This works fine when we’re operating in the area of what we know or have experienced. ( ③ ) To address this issue, you will be most effective if you learn to operate in a nonlinear manner when dealing with new ideas; that is, use your creative brain. ( ④ ) Stated differently, if you think in a linear manner, you’ll tend to be conservative and keep coming up with techniques which are already known. ( ⑤ ) This, of course, is just what you don’t want.
questions.insertion_sentence: However, when we need to deal with new information, ideas, and viewpoints, linear thinking will often come up short.
questions.explanation: ②번 문장까지는 선형적(논리적) 사고가 익숙한 영역에서는 잘 작동한다고 설명합니다. 주어진 문장은 '새로운 정보나 아이디어를 다룰 때 선형적 사고는 부족해진다'는 내용이므로, 대조를 이루는 ③번에 들어가야 하며, 뒤이어 나오는 '이 문제를 해결하기 위해 비선형적 방식(창의적 뇌)을 사용하라'는 조언과 연결됩니다.

questions.question: 26. 주어진 글 다음에 이어질 글의 순서로 가장 적절한 것을 고르시오.[3.2점]
questions.passage: Do you share your opinion in class discussions, or do you just stay silent and keep it to yourself?
ordered_passages: (A) So I left my comfort zone and started to speak up. I grew intellectually and socially by expressing myself more clearly. I got closer to friends who liked how open I was with them. Now I have more people with whom I can talk, share my ideas, and learn new things. Remember, taking the risk of expressing yourself can be extremely rewarding in unexpected ways.

(B) Then, after a particularly heated conversation in class, I asked myself, “What am I afraid of?” I was scared that bad things would happen, but I never thought about good things. When I noticed others taking risks, I knew that I needed to do the same in order to participate. Many people are scared to speak up, but a lot of them do it anyway because they think it’s worth it.

(C) Like many of you, I often found myself in the second group. A little black hole inside of me swallowed my voice when I considered speaking up. The consequences of being ridiculed or being wrong were always on my mind.
questions.explanation: 주어진 글에서 제시한 두 가지 선택지 중 필자는 (C)에서 '두 번째 그룹(침묵하는 그룹)'에 속한다고 답하며 시작합니다. 이후 (B)에서 특정 사건을 계기로 자신의 두려움을 직시하고 태도를 바꾸기로 결심하며, (A)에서 그로 인한 긍정적인 변화와 교훈을 전달하며 마무리하는 것이 논리적입니다.

questions.question: 27. 주어진 글 다음에 이어질 글의 순서로 가장 적절한 것을 고르시오.[3.4점]
questions.passage: Danger in the form of pyjama sharks, the area's biggest predators, came with little warning in the sea. The octopus was moving around near the edge of the seaweed forest, and I saw a shark tracking her.
ordered_passages: (A) In an instant, she swam into a crack to escape, but the shark was faster. The shark had taken a bite of one of her arms and was waiting for her. I wanted to save my friend, but in this environment, I could only observe. She managed to get deeper into the crack, but she was bleeding.

(B) The next day, I was relieved to see that she had survived. She was weak, and her colors were not as bright. I checked on her every day, wondering if that day would be the last. It was emotionally painful to witness these things happening to her.

(C) After a while, the shark lost interest, and the octopus used the opportunity to get back to her den, without one of her arms. She was in serious danger because her arms function like the hands, legs, nose, and eyes of humans.
questions.explanation: 주어진 글에서 상어가 문어를 추적하는 긴박한 상황이 제시됩니다. (A)에서 상어의 공격과 문어의 도피 시도가 이어지고, (C)에서 상어가 물러난 뒤 문어가 다리 하나를 잃고 은신처로 돌아가는 상황이 묘사됩니다. 마지막으로 (B)에서 'The next day'라는 시간의 흐름과 함께 문어의 생존 확인과 필자의 안도감이 나타나는 흐름이 적절합니다.

questions.question: 28. 주어진 글 다음에 이어질 글의 순서로 가장 적절한 것을 고르시오.[3.0점]
questions.passage: Piaget put the same amount of water into two different glasses: a tall narrow glass and a wide glass, then asked kids to compare two glasses.
ordered_passages: (A) Once kids have reached the age of five or six, then playing games and working things out together will help them learn about fairness far more effectively than any teaching from adults.

(B) Piaget argued that children's understanding of morality is like their understanding of those water glasses: we can't say that it is innate or kids learn it directly from adults. Rather, it is self-constructed as kids play with other kids. Taking turns in a game is like pouring water back and forth between glasses.

(C) Kids younger than six or seven usually say that the tall narrow glass now holds more water, because the level is higher. And when they are ready, they figure out the conservation of volume for themselves just by playing with cups of water.
questions.explanation: 주어진 글에서 피아제의 물 컵 실험이 제시됩니다. (C)에서 실험의 구체적인 결과와 아이들이 부피 보존 개념을 스스로 깨닫는 과정이 나옵니다. (B)에서는 이러한 물 컵 실험의 원리를 도덕성 이해에 비유하여, 도덕성 또한 아이들이 놀이를 통해 스스로 구성하는 것이라고 설명합니다. 마지막으로 (A)에서 5~6세 연령대를 언급하며 놀이를 통한 공정성 학습의 효과를 강조하며 마무리합니다.

questions.question: 29.다음 글의 내용을 한 문장으로 요약하고자 한다. 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것을 고르시오. [2.7점]
questions.passage:
The science we learn in grade school is a collection of certainties about the natural world — the earth goes around the sun, DNA carries the information of an organism, and so on. Only when you start to learn the practice of science do you realize that each of these "facts" was hard won through a succession of logical inferences based upon many observations or experiments. The process of science is less about collecting pieces of knowledge than it is about reducing the uncertainties in what we know. Our uncertainties can be greater or lesser for any given piece of knowledge depending upon where we are in that process — today we are quite certain of how an apple will fall from a tree, but our understanding of the turbulent fluid flow remains a work in progress after more than a century
of effort.
questions.summary_sentence: Science is an ongoing journey of (A) __________ uncertainties through observations and experiments, with some facts well-established and others still uncertain, rather than merely (B)__________ a fixed set of facts.
options: ① reducing ...... discarding
② neglecting ...... exploring
③ increasing ...... gathering
④ expanding ...... confronting
⑤ minimizing ...... accurnulating
questions.explanation: 글의 핵심 내용은 과학이 단순히 지식을 수집하는 것이 아니라 관찰과 실험을 통해 불확실성을 줄여가는 과정이라는 것입니다. 요약문에서 (A)에는 불확실성을 '줄이는(minimizing/reducing)' 과정이 들어가야 하며, (B)에는 단순히 지식을 '축적하는(accumulating)' 것이 아니라는 내용이 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 줄이는 ...... 버리는
② 무시하는 ...... 탐구하는
③ 늘리는 ...... 모으는
④ 확장하는 ...... 직면하는
⑤ 최소화하는 ...... 축적하는

questions.question: 6.다음 글의 요지로 가장 적절한 것을 고르시오. [3.5점]
questions.passage: When we realize we've said something in error and we pause to go back to correct it, we stop gesturing a couple of hundred milliseconds before we stop speaking. Such sequences suggest the startling notion that our hands "know" what we're going to say before our conscious minds do, and in fact this is often the case. Gesture can mentally prime a word so that the right term comes to our lips. When people are prevented from gesturing, they talk less fluently: their speech becomes halting because their hands are no longer able to supply them with the next word, and the next. Not being able to gesture has other deleterious effects: without gesture to help our mental processes along, we remember less useful information, we solve problems less well, and we are less able to explain our thinking. Far from tagging along as speech's clumsy companion, gesture represents the leading edge of our thought.
options: ① Restricting gestures enables speakers to focus more intently on lexical precision and logical articulation.
② Gestures serve as cognitive facilitators that not only precede but actively shape verbal expression and mental processing.
③ The primary function of gestures lies in capturing listeners' attention rather than contributing to the speaker's thought formation.
④ While gestures may enhance expressiveness, they remain supplementary and are dispensable for coherent verbal communication.
⑤ Gestures are incidental physical movements that accompany speech without significantly influencing linguistic or cognitive functions.
questions.explanation: 제스처가 말보다 앞서 나타나며, 단어를 떠올리게 하거나 인지적 과정을 돕는 등 사고의 최첨단 역할을 한다는 내용이므로 ②가 가장 적절하다.
options_translation: ① 제스처를 제한하면 화자가 어휘적 정밀도와 논리적 표현에 더 집중할 수 있게 해준다.
② 제스처는 언어적 표현과 정신적 처리에 앞설 뿐만 아니라 이를 적극적으로 형성하는 인지적 조력자 역할을 한다.
③ 제스처의 주요 기능은 화자의 사고 형성 기여보다는 청자의 주의를 끄는 데 있다.
④ 제스처가 표현력을 향상시킬 수는 있지만, 일관된 언어적 의사소통에 있어 보충적이며 없어도 되는 것이다.
⑤ 제스처는 언어적 또는 인지적 기능에 큰 영향을 미치지 않으면서 말을 수반하는 부수적인 신체 움직임이다.

questions.question: 12.다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 어법상 틀린 것을 고르시오.[3.4점]
questions.passage: In 1900 at the close of the first decade ① <u>when</u> electric systems had become a practical alternative for manufacturers, less than 5 percent of the power used in factories came from electricity. But the technological advances of suppliers made electric systems and electric motors ever more affordable and reliable, and the suppliers' intensive marketing programs also sped the adoption of the new technology. Further accelerating the shift was the rapid expansion in the number of skilled electrical engineers ② <u>whose</u> expertise enabled them to install and run the new systems. In short order, electric power had gone from exotic to commonplace. But one thing didn't change. Factories continued to build their own power-supply systems on their own premises. Few manufacturers considered buying electricity from the small central stations. ③ <u>Designed</u> to supply lighting to local homes and shops, the central stations had neither the size nor the skill to serve the needs of big factories. And the factory owners, having always supplied their own power, were loath to assign such a critical function to an outsider. They knew that a glitch in power supply would bring their operations to a halt — and ④ <u>what</u> a lot of glitches might well mean bankruptcy. As the new century began, a survey found that there were already 50,000 private electric plants in operation, far ⑤ <u>surpassing</u> the 3,600 central stations.
questions.explanation: ④번의 what은 뒤에 'a lot of glitches(주어) might well mean(동사) bankruptcy(목적어)'라는 완전한 문장이 이어지므로 접속사 that으로 바뀌어야 합니다. (and 뒤에 병렬로 연결된 명사절 접속사)

questions.question: 13. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은? [3.8점]
questions.passage: Organisms thrive through teamwork, beginning with genes. Each gene is selected for its capacity to cooperate with other genes in the way that ① <u>expedites</u> adaptive responses crucial to survival, thereby enhancing the survivability of both the individual organism and the species. Groups of ② <u>synergistic</u> genes naturally arise. For instance, genes that determine the size, speed, and coloring of a predatory animal like a snow leopard blend together to maximize the survivability and reproductive potential of the whole animal where the animal lives. Most of the snow leopard's offspring will carry genes that reflect the same positive attributes and traits their parents have. In a harsh and challenging environment where organisms constantly ③ <u>contend</u> for limited resources, offspring that lack favorable genes are less likely to survive. That's how nature determines winners and losers in a never-ending process of aimless self-organization. Those with the most advantageous genetic traits are ④ <u>outcompeted</u>. Individual organisms whose genes happen to be poorly matched to their environments starve, get eaten, or die without mating. This brutal truth ⑤ <u>manifests</u> what is meant by "survival of the fittest."
questions.explanation: ④번의 outcompeted는 '경쟁에서 밀려나다/지다'라는 의미입니다. 문맥상 가장 유리한 유전적 특질을 가진 개체들은 살아남는 '승자(winners)'가 되어야 하므로, 경쟁에서 이기거나 선택되어야 합니다. 따라서 'selected' 또는 'favored'와 같은 단어가 적절하며, outcompete(경쟁에서 이기다)를 수동태로 쓴 outcompeted는 '패배한' 자들에게 어울리는 표현입니다.

questions.question: 14. (A), (B), (C) 각 네모 안에서 문맥에 맞는 어휘를 골라 짝지은 것으로 가장 적절한 것은? [3.6점]
questions.passage: The prominence of the social dimension in food writing might suggest that the flavor of food is taking a back seat. Accordingly I think that most people view flavor as of (A) [utmost / subordinate] importance in social settings where food is served. Although our social gatherings coalesce around food, the meaning of these gatherings does not seem to depend on flavor. Flavor assists with the narrow purpose of filling the belly, and once that is accomplished it provides the (B) [pivot / periphery] for whatever social dynamics characterize the gathering. These can be understood independently of the flavor of the food on offer, the appreciation of which is understood to be personal and subjective. According to this conventional wisdom, the ceremonies and rituals around food, the social events that supply food with its meaning, aren't (C) [contingent on / extraneous to] the quality of sensations provided by the food. To focus excessively on flavor is to miss the larger significance of these social relations.
options: ① subordinate ... periphery ... contingent on
② subordinate ... periphery ... extraneous to
③ subordinate ... pivot ... extraneous to
④ utmost ... periphery ... contingent on
⑤ utmost ... pivot ... extraneous to
questions.explanation: (A) 문맥상 음식의 맛이 '뒷전(taking a back seat)'이라는 표현이 나오므로, 맛은 사회적 환경에서 '부차적인(subordinate)' 중요성을 갖는 것으로 간주됩니다. (B) 맛은 배를 채우는 좁은 목적을 돕고, 그것이 달성되면 사회적 역학의 '주변부(periphery)'를 제공합니다. (C) 이러한 통념에 따르면, 음식의 의미를 제공하는 의례나 행사들은 음식에 의해 제공되는 감각의 질에 '의존하지(contingent on)' 않는다는 것이 문맥상 적절합니다. (원문에서는 'aren't contingent on'이 '맛에 좌우되지 않는다'는 의미로 쓰임)
options_translation: ① 부차적인 ... 주변부 ... ~에 의존하는
② 부차적인 ... 주변부 ... ~와 관계없는
③ 부차적인 ... 중심점 ... ~와 관계없는
④ 최고의 ... 주변부 ... ~에 의존하는
⑤ 최고의 ... 중심점 ... ~와 관계없는

questions.question: 15.다음 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것을 고르시오. [3.5점]
questions.passage: If the brain has already stored someone's face and name, why do we still end up remembering one and not the other? This is because the brain has something of a two-tier memory system at work when it comes to retrieving memories, and this gives rise to a common yet infuriating sensation: recognising someone, but not being able to remember how or why, or what their name is. This happens because the brain differentiates between familiarity and recall. To clarify, familiarity (or recognition) is when you encounter someone or something and you know you've done so before. But beyond that, you've got nothing; all you can say is this person/thing is already in your memories. Recall is when you can access the original memory of how and why you know this person; recognition is just ______________________.
options: ① assuming the memory has been distorted
② constructing a new version of the memory
③ analyzing the emotional impact of the memory
④ imagining a scenario based on past experiences
⑤ pointing out that the memory is stored somewhere
questions.explanation: 글의 맥락에서 'recognition(인지/친숙함)'은 이전에 본 적이 있다는 것만 알고 그 이상의 세부 정보(어떻게, 왜 아는지 등)는 떠올리지 못하는 상태를 설명하고 있습니다. 따라서 'recognition'은 단지 그 기억이 어딘가에 저장되어 있다는 사실을 가리키는 것뿐이라는 내용의 ⑤번이 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 기억이 왜곡되었다고 가정하는 것
② 기억의 새로운 버전을 구성하는 것
③ 기억의 정서적 영향을 분석하는 것
④ 과거 경험을 바탕으로 시나리오를 상상하는 것
⑤ 기억이 어딘가에 저장되어 있음을 지적하는 것

questions.question: 17. 다음 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것을 고르시오. [3.2점]
questions.passage: It is important to recognize that although science is a rule-based procedure, it is very much a creative process. A conjecture is a philosophical invention, cooked up rather mystically by the mind through the mental computation we call careful contemplation. However, until the hypothesis is tested against reality, it is not yet truly knowledge; it is just information that represents speculation. Knowledge is information that has demonstrated its usefulness. It is what is left over after cycles of experimental testing have eliminated false theories. As scientists continually test their hypotheses and modify their models to account for new and surprising data, a kind of "learning loop" emerges that statisticians call Bayesian updating. Based on Bayes' Rule, developed by eighteenth-century English statistician and philosopher Thomas Bayes, Bayesian updating refers to a mathematical process whereby an accepted theory or predictive model gets increasingly accurate through the repetitive testing of competing variants of that theory. In this way, ____________ in science is continuously earned, not assumed, through repeated confrontation with evidence.
options: ① fortuity
② vulnerability
③ legitimacy
④ accusation
⑤ contradiction
questions.explanation: 지문은 과학적 지식이 단순히 추측에 머무는 것이 아니라, 반복적인 실험과 증거와의 대면을 통해 그 유용성을 입증하고 점진적으로 정확해지는 과정을 설명하고 있습니다. 따라서 과학에서의 '정당성(legitimacy)' 또는 타당성은 당연하게 가정되는 것이 아니라 끊임없이 획득되는 것이라는 의미가 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 우연성
② 취약성
③ 정당성(타당성)
④ 비난
⑤ 모순

questions.question: 20.다음 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것을 고르시오. [3.9점]
questions.passage: There are reasons why science is not fully trusted and why healthy skepticism and critical thinking are essential. In spite of professional standards, claims of objectivity, and the peer review process, the conduct of science can be biased. All experts are not the same, nor do they submit their work to the same scrutiny. ________________ is crucial in evaluating scientific claims, and knowing the source of funding plays a key role in that process. For example, the Harvard researchers who made claims in the late 1960s about the problems with dietary fat, leading the nation away from perceiving sugar as one of the main causes in health problems, were funded in part by the sugar industry. The authors did not reveal their funding source to the New England Journal of Medicine, where their influential article appeared. Their article shaped a generation of changes in eating patterns that appears to have fostered higher use of sugar, now widely implicated as a source of the rise in obesity and diabetes. Stories such as this one fuel suspicion - but also lead to further safeguards in the scientific process. Funding disclosures, although not required five decades ago, have since been made compulsory.
options: ① Promoting collaborative scientific efforts
② Ensuring the innovative use of resources
③ Detecting underlying conflicts of interest
④ Developing vital skills for experimental inquiry
⑤ Exposing the channels of illegal financial flow

questions.question: 21.다음 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것을 고르시오. [3.6점]
questions.passage: As a general rule, it's better if your definition corresponds as closely as possible to the way in which the term is ordinarily used in the kinds of debates to which your claims are pertinent. There will be, however, occasions where it is appropriate, even necessary, to coin special uses through what philosophers call stimulative definition. This would be the case where ____________________. For example, we do not have a term in ordinary language that describes a memory that is not necessarily a memory of something the person having it has experienced. Such a thing would occur, for example, if I could somehow share your memories: I would have a memory-type experience, but this would not be of something that I had actually experienced. To call this a memory would be misleading. For this reason, philosophers have coined the special term 'quasi-memory' to refer to these hypothetical memory-like experiences.
options: ① terms should be defined broadly to prevent any potential confusion in academic discourse
② natural language is deficient for articulating philosophically meaningful differences
③ the philosophical terms you use should match those found in dictionaries
④ language is constantly evolving so that there's no need to coin new terms
⑤ any invented term must be immediately accepted by the general public
questions.explanation: 이 글은 일상적인 언어 사용이 철학적으로 의미 있는 구분을 명확히 표현하기에 부족할 때, 철학자들이 '약정적 정의(stimulative definition)'를 통해 새로운 용어를 만들어낸다는 점을 설명하고 있다. 예시로 든 '준기억(quasi-memory)'은 우리가 경험하지 않은 것에 대한 기억을 일상어로 표현할 수 없기 때문에 만들어진 용어이다. 따라서 빈칸에는 자연어가 철학적 차이를 설명하기에 불충분하다는 내용이 들어가야 한다.
options_translation: ① 학술적 담론에서 잠재적인 혼란을 방지하기 위해 용어는 광범위하게 정의되어야 한다
② 자연어는 철학적으로 의미 있는 차이를 명확하게 표현하기에 부족하다

questions.question: 22. 다음 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것을 고르시오.. [3.5점]
questions.passage: Dictionaries are relatively good resources for anyone interested in finding out what a word means. Using one set of words to define another word is called a lexical definition. But it's important to understand the limits of dictionary definitions. More often than not, a definition in a dictionary requires readers to ____________________. In other words, a dictionary functions in many cases as a cross-reference or translator between words one knows and words that one doesn't yet know. Even the most obscure words in a dictionary, say, for example, "pulchritudinous" or "kalokagathia," must be defined using words that the reader already knows and understands. Otherwise, the dictionary isn't very helpful.
options: ① bridge gaps in comprehension with existing assets
② grasp the significance based on cultural perspectives
③ rely on intuition rather than adhering to societal norms
④ clarify the usage of language in the context of narratives
⑤ translate words into another language using digital tools
questions.explanation: 이 글은 사전이 모르는 단어를 설명하기 위해 독자가 이미 알고 있는 단어들을 사용해야 한다는 점을 강조하고 있다. 즉, 사전의 정의는 독자가 가진 기존의 지식(이미 아는 단어들)을 활용하여 이해의 간극을 메우는 방식으로 작동한다. 따라서 ① '기존 자산(지식)으로 이해의 간극을 메우다'가 가장 적절하다.
options_translation: ① 기존의 자산(지식)을 가지고 이해의 간극을 메우다
② 문화적 관점에 기초하여 의미를 파악하다
③ 사회적 규범을 따르기보다 직관에 의존하다
④ 이야기의 맥락 안에서 언어의 사용을 명확히 하다
⑤ 디지털 도구를 사용하여 단어를 다른 언어로 번역하다

questions.question: 24.다음 글에서 전체 흐름과 관계 없는 문장을 고르시오. [3.4점]
questions.passage: Since their start in the early 1950s U.S. television sitcoms have charted many of the social conflicts in U.S. society: civil rights, women's rights in the home and in the workplace, children's rights, immigration and multiculturalism, as well as evolving conceptions of the family. ① Discussions to resolve social conflicts must be approached from multiple angles, with the role of a mediator being crucial in facilitating fair, objective solutions and fostering trust between conflicting parties. ② Each of these issues has been addressed through humour in a way that has helped to make more progressive values more acceptable than previously. ③ Often a character, usually someone marked as a bigot, resisted one or more of these developments and was then made to appear ridiculous. ④ They were cut down either through their own stupidity, a brief scolding from others, or both. ⑤ In this way, the humour of sitcoms acted as an effective means to encourage acceptance of a more pluralistic and tolerant society.
questions.explanation: 이 글은 미국의 시트콤이 유머를 통해 사회적 갈등을 다루고 진보적인 가치를 수용하도록 돕는 역할을 했다는 내용이다. ①번 문장은 일반적인 사회적 갈등 해결을 위한 중재자의 역할에 대해 설명하고 있으므로 시트콤의 사회적 역할이라는 주제와 관련이 없다.

questions.question: 26. 글의 흐름으로 보아, 주어진 문장이 들어가기에 가장 적절한 곳은? [3.5점]
questions.passage: Great scientists are seldom one-hit wonders. Newton is a prime example: beyond the Newtonian mechanics, he developed the theory of gravitation, calculus, laws of motion, and optimization. ( ① ) In fact, well-known scientists are often involved in multiple discoveries, a phenomenon potentially explained by the Matthew effect. ( ② ) Indeed, an initial success may offer a scientist credibility, improve peer perception, provide knowledge of how to score and win, enhance social status, and attract resources and quality collaborators, each of these payoffs further increasing her odds of scoring another win. ( ③ ) Therefore, future success again goes to those who have had success earlier, not because of advantages offered by the previous success, but because the earlier success was indicative of a hidden talent. ( ④ ) The Matthew effect posits that success alone increases the future probability of success, raising the question: Does status dictate outcomes, or does it simply reflect an underlying talent or quality? ( ⑤ ) In other words, there is really a Matthew effect after all?
questions.insertion_sentence: Yet, there is an appealing alternative explanation: Great scientists have multiple hits and consistently succeed in their scientific endeavors simply because they're exceptionally talented.
questions.explanation: 주어진 문장은 앞선 '매튜 효과(성공이 성공을 낳는다)'에 대한 대안적 설명(재능이 뛰어나서 계속 성공한다)을 제시하고 있습니다. ③번 앞부분까지는 이전 성공이 가져다주는 이점(매튜 효과)을 설명하고 있고, ③번 뒤의 'Therefore' 이하 문장은 매튜 효과 때문이 아니라 '이전의 성공이 숨겨진 재능의 지표였기 때문(indicative of a hidden talent)'에 성공이 이어진다고 결론짓고 있으므로, 재능에 기반한 대안 설명을 도입하는 주어진 문장은 ③에 들어가는 것이 가장 적절합니다.

questions.question: 6. 윗글의 밑줄 친 ⓐ ~ ⓔ중, 어법상 틀린 것은? [4점]
questions.passage:
The famous German musician Johann Sebastian Bach once said, "Without my morning coffee, I'm just like a dried-up piece of goat." Today this sentiment is shared by many, with coffee shops springing up on almost every street corner, and it is common to see city residents ⓐ <u>walking around</u> with a cup of coffee in hand. According to the International Coffee Organization (ICO), approximately 10 billion tons of coffee was consumed worldwide between 2020 and 2021, and Koreans made a significant contribution to this huge total, consuming 150,780 tons of coffee. This means that every Korean adult drank an average of one cup of coffee every day throughout the year. Clearly, for Koreans and other world citizens, coffee is not just a drink but a(n) (A) _________.

The world's widespread love of coffee comes at a substantial environmental cost, as the extraction process generates significant waste. Only 0.2 percent of a coffee bean is used ⓑ <u>to make</u> coffee, with the remaining 99.8 percent disposed of as waste. As a result, the vast quantity of coffee consumed worldwide ⓒ <u>producing</u> millions of tons of coffee waste each year.

So, what happens to all the waste from the coffee extraction process? Spent coffee grounds (SCGs) are classified as general waste and sent to landfills. There they break down, releasing methane, a greenhouse gas ⓓ <u>that</u> is approximately 25 times more potent than CO2. Some SCGs are incinerated instead of being buried, but this releases a lot of CO2: 338 kg per ton. However, neither of these waste management options takes into account the potential value of coffee grounds. Although the grounds contain valuable organic compounds and minerals, ⓔ <u>they</u> are simply destroyed.

Fortunately, thanks to increased awareness of the coffee waste problem, companies, organizations, and governments around the world are working hard to improve the environmental impact of the coffee industry through circular economy measures. A circular economy promotes the reuse of resources for as long as possible, reducing waste and environmental costs.
options: ① ⓐ
② ⓑ
③ ⓒ
④ ⓓ
⑤ ⓔ
questions.explanation: ⓒ는 'As a result, the vast quantity... produces...'와 같이 주어(the vast quantity)에 맞는 동사가 필요하므로, producing을 produces로 고쳐야 한다.

questions.question: 8. 주어진 문장을 윗글의 내용에 맞게 알맞은 순서대로 배열한 것은? [4.3점]
questions.passage:
An example of a circular economy in action occurs when a chain of coffee shops collaborates with an organization to collect spent coffee grounds from its shops. These grounds are processed to remove impurities and dried out. The resulting SCGs are sold to fertilizer companies, where they are transformed into organic fertilizer. This fertilizer is later sold back to the coffee shop chain. The chain provides the fertilizer to local eco-friendly farmers, who then sell their produce back to the chain. The farm produce can be used to create various food items, such as rice chips and dried sweet potatoes, which are sold in the chain's coffee shops. By repurposing coffee grounds in this manner, related businesses and local farmers can benefit both economically and environmentally.
Recycled coffee grounds have a wide range of uses, including coffee logs, fabrics for clothing and shoes, and reusable cups. Coffee logs, for instance, generate more heat and burn for a longer time than wood. Fabric made from coffee grounds absorbs sweat, dries quickly, and provides UV protection. Reusable cups from coffee grounds [A] <u>시각적으로 매력적인 외관을 가지고 있을 뿐만 아니라 커피의 풍미도 간직하고 있다</u>.

b. Spent coffee grounds are collected from coffee shops.
c. Spent coffee grounds are sold to fertilizer companies.
d. A coffee chain provides organic fertilizer to local farmers.
options: ① a-b-c-d
② b-c-d-a
③ b-d-c-a
④ c-b-a-d
⑤ c-d-b-a

문장의 주어인 'Reusable cups from coffee grounds(복수)'에 이어지는 동사구를 영작하는 문제입니다.

questions.question: 13. 윗글에 대한 설명으로 적절하지 않은 것은? [4.8점]
questions.passage:
Just before noon, we arrived at a small town called Murupara. "Where do we go now?" I asked Nani. He did not reply, but he was searching inside himself, staring at the small houses. Then, at a street corner, he told us to turn. After turning the corner, we saw an old man standing in front of a house. He welcomed Nani Tama with a gentle smile, but in his eyes, I saw the message, "We must hurry."
Now that day seems like a dream to me. I remember the two old men sitting at the table and the soft sounds of the Maori words as they talked. All through the quiet afternoon and into the evening, they recalled missing names. I had a strange feeling that there were other people in the room. I felt as if ⓐ ____________________ to see if the work was correct.
Finally, they stopped. It was done. After a moment of silence, the old man whispered to Nani, "Goodbye, friend." Crying, they pressed their noses together to say goodbye.
It was early morning and still dark when we returned to Auntie's place. All the lights were on, and the village people were waiting for us. Smiling, Nani Tama lifted up the whakapapa and offered it to the village. Our hearts were full because ⓑ ____________________.

Our Nani Tama smiled again. His smile grew tired.
He sighed. "At last, I may go now."
Then, he closed his eyes.
"No, Dad!" Auntie Hiraina cried.
The sun burst across the hills.
options: ① The events were presented in the order they happened.
② Some expressions in the novel imply the grandfather's death at the end of the story.

questions.question: 1. 윗글에 대한 설명으로 적절하지 않은 것은? [5.5점]
questions.passage: You and I Become "We" The Power of Friendliness: Soft but Strong It’s good to see you, everyone! I’m Dr. Edward Wilson, an evolutionary biologist. Thank you for inviting me here today. On my way, I had trouble locating this room. Luckily, a friendly student came up to me and walked me here. questions.question: 6. 윗글의 밑줄 친 an alternative view에 대한 설명으로 적절하지 않은 것은? [4.7점]
questions.passage: You and I Become "We" The Power of Friendliness: Soft but Strong It’s good to see you, everyone! I’m Dr. Edward Wilson, an evolutionary biologist. Thank you for inviting me here today. On my way, I had trouble locating this room. Luckily, a friendly student came up to me and walked me here. It’s fascinating how, in situations like this, we want to help someone in need. Now, this raises some interesting questions: where does our friendliness come from, and why is it important? To answer these questions, I’d like to tell you about my childhood companion dog, Sparky. When we played with a ball, I noticed that he responded well to my gestures. The responsive behavior of dogs also caught the attention of an evolutionary anthropologist, Brian Hare. He conducted an experiment to see how dogs would respond to human gestures compared to wolves, who share the same common ancestor. He placed two cups on the ground with food hidden under only one of them. When he pointed to the cup with the food, the dogs found it easily. The wolves, however, struggled and chose cups at random, paying no attention to his gestures. Dr. Hare concluded that the dogs’ ability to read human gestures allowed them to perform better than the wolves. He explained that dogs, unlike wolves, have developed communicative skills with humans and a sense of friendliness. This explanation sounds reasonable according to several evolutionary biologists. They say that from the common ancestors of these two species, those that acted friendly toward humans evolved into dogs, and those that didn’t became wolves. Furthermore, Dr. Hare suggested that the friendly nature of dogs probably provided them a survival advantage that allowed their population to grow larger than that of wolves. I’ll give you another example of how friendliness is related to survival. Dr. Hare and his colleagues designed an experiment with chimpanzees and bonobos. Although the two are genetically similar, they are different in nature. To study their cooperative behavior, Dr. Hare’s team set up a device which required two individuals to pull both ends of a rope at the same time in order to access food on a board. When placed with partners that the chimpanzees knew, they were able to work together to get the food. However, when paired with new partners, the chimpanzees usually failed to get the food, and when they occasionally succeeded, they did not share the food with their partner. The bonobos, on the other hand, got along much better than the chimpanzees. They solved the problem regardless of which individual they were paired with, and they were also more willing to share the food. This research shows that bonobos have a cooperative and friendly nature. Experts suggest that their nature has helped their species survive. Without these characteristics, they could have faced extinction. Now let’s turn our attention to ourselves, Homo sapiens. How have we managed to survive for so long? Neanderthals existed together with Homo sapiens until about 40,000 years ago, and they were known to be intelligent and physically superior to Homo sapiens. Neanderthals were able to make tools and f ire and had strong bodies with well-developed muscles and broad shoulders. Despite these attributes, however, it was Homo sapiens who ultimately survived and thrived. One possible explanation is that our ancestors lived in larger communities that promoted cooperation and the free exchange of knowledge, while Neanderthals tended to live in smaller groups. These social differences may have given Homo sapiens a competitive advantage over Neanderthals, allowing them to adapt to an ever-changing environment. In our competitive society, many people believe that only the biggest or the strongest can survive and thrive. However, I propose an alternative view: kindness is the key to success. Isn’t that a comforting thought? We can use the power of our natural kindness to communicate and cooperate with different individuals. We can all benefit from this instead of trying to be better than others. I’d like to end this talk with a message. Think of our society as a bouquet. Just as each flower adds to the beauty when it harmonizes with the others, each person can contribute to a more beautiful world when they cooperate. By being kind and working together, we can truly flourish. Thank you for your attention.
options: ① It goes against the common belief about success.
② It is based on the important role of communication and cooperation in success.
③ To support the view, the author uses a metaphorical expression.
④ From this view, people don't have to compete with each other for benefits.
⑤ It considers each individual to be more important than the group as a whole.

questions.passage: Promotion deals with consumer psychology. We can’t force people to think one way or another, and the clever marketer knows that promotion is used to provide information in the most clear, honest, and simple fashion possible. questions.passage: Our skin conducts electricity more or less efficiently, depending on our emotions. We know that when we’re emotionally stimulated — stressed, sad, any intense emotion, really—our bodies sweat a tiny bit, so little we might not even notice. And when those tiny drops of sweat appear, our skin gets more electrically conductive. This change in sweat gland activity happens completely without your conscious mind having much say in the matter. If you feel emotionally intense, you’re going to notice an increase in sweat gland activity. This is particularly useful from a scientific viewpoint, because it allows us to put an objective value on a subjective state of mind. We can actually measure your emotional state by tracking how your body subconsciously sweats, by running a bit of electricity through your skin. We can then turn the subjective, subconscious experience of emotional intensity into an objective number by figuring out how good your skin gets at transferring an electrical current.

② sweat gland activity --- scientific measure
③ emotional intensity --- electrical current
④ conductivity of skin --- emotional intensity

questions.question: 13. 윗글의 노이즈캔슬링 헤드폰 속 회로가 하는 역할로 가장 적절한 것은? [4.7점]
questions.passage: Free Yourself with Science Tuning Out: The Science of Noise-Cancellation Which is the better environment for studying: a noisy place or a quiet place? Rarely do people want to put up with a lot of noise because it can be unpleasant and distracting. Fortunately, scientists have invented noise-cancelling technology, which is now being used across various fields to reduce unwanted noise. What is the scientific principle behind this achievement? To understand this, let’s examine how sound travels. The Principle of Sound Waves and Interference Sound is produced through vibrations that occur from a sound source, when the strings of a guitar are played, for instance. The vibrations of the sound source cause the air to vibrate and the sound to travel as waves, similar to the ripples created in a lake when you throw a stone. When these sound waves reach our ears, the brain interprets them as sound. Just as different ripples in water might overlap if you throw two stones, sound waves can also interfere with each other when they meet. There are two types of interference: constructive and destructive. Constructive interference occurs when the peaks of two waves overlap, resulting in a bigger wave and a louder sound. Destructive interference, on the other hand, occurs when a peak of one wave overlaps with a valley of another wave, so they cancel each other out and produce a quieter sound, or no sound at all. The Science Behind Noise-Cancelling Headphones Destructive interference is used in the noise-cancelling feature of headphones when we listen to music. Inside the headphones are microphones and noise-cancelling circuitry. The microphones pick up sounds from the outside, and the circuitry analyzes them to produce opposite sound waves. For example, if outside noise has a value of +1, the circuitry will generate an opposite noise of –1 and transmit it to the speakers. This cancels out the unwanted sound even in noisy surroundings, so you can hear the music sound clearly without turning up the volume. However, it is not easy to entirely eliminate external noise with this technology. To achieve full noise cancellation, the circuitry must convert the noise into digital data and instantly transmit the opposite sound to the speakers as soon as the noise reaches the microphones. Therefore, this noise-cancellation technology is effective for predictable sounds like those of car engines and subways that occur regularly or over a period of time. However, it’s relatively less effective for inconsistent sounds such as those of people talking close to you. Exploring the Technology and Its Applications Noise-cancelling technology is not only used in music devices. Other fields also take advantage of this technology, such as ticket offices at tourist attractions which are often very noisy. Microphones are installed in ticket offices to detect external noise, and an opposite sound wave is generated and transmitted through a speaker, enabling the ticket agent to hear the customer’s voice clearly. Another area in which this technology is used is drive-through fast-food restaurants and coffee shops. They use noise-cancelling headsets to improve communication between employees and customers by eliminating vehicle noise. These noise-cancelling headsets help drive-through employees take orders accurately. The same technology is also used for cars, whose audio systems generate waves to cancel out unpleasant sounds such as engine, wind, and road noise. Thanks to noise-cancelling devices, it is possible for drivers to focus on driving without being disturbed by distracting noises. As technology advances, many people expect it will solve various social issues caused by noise pollution. A common source of these problems is noisy neighbors, as the noise they make can lead to conflict among residents. Noise-cancellation technology can help address these problems by reducing unwanted disturbances, allowing people to lead more peaceful and healthier lives.
options: ① to create vibrations and make the air vibrate as well
② to detect outside sounds and adjust music's tone to match them
③ to pick up external sounds and transmit them to the speakers
④ to analyze external noise and produce sound waves that cancel it out
⑤ to increase the volume of the music when external noise is detected
